On a fixed-anchor branch, the corrected map factors into chart transition, harmonic propagation, and inverse stereographic projection, yielding an explicit sensitivity Jacobian and a finite-triangle conditioning bound. Separately, we introduce a bounded five-parameter affine preconditioner over planar scale, translation, and anisotropy and evaluate candidates on the corrected spherical map. Across 30 genus-0 surfaces, it reduces median polar upper-tail log-condition and chord-angle distortion by $10.17\%$ and $10.97\%$, respectively, with both measures improving on every mesh. We also apply the framework to other spherical mapping methods including the conformalized mean-curvature flow and spherical density-equalizing maps. Altogether, our work highlights the importance of representation selection as a structural and practical component of spherical parameterization and downstream computation.

papers.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{T}_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal{A}$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Cesàro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Cesàro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.

papers.title: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields
papers.abstract: We classify the pairs $(q,n)$, where $q$ is a prime power, $n>1$, and $\gcd(n,q)=1$, for which every irreducible factor of $Φ_n(x)$ over $\F_q$ has exactly three nonzero terms. The positive support exponents of these factors have a common greatest common divisor, which gives a unique reduction by a power substitution. The reduced degree is two in odd characteristic and belongs to $\{2,3,4\}$ in characteristic two; the cubic and quartic cases arise by scalar substitution from the layers of orders $7$ and $15$. This yields necessary and sufficient arithmetic conditions on $(q,n)$ and explicit factorizations. Among the classified families, precisely those arising from quartic bases have a divisor layer containing an irreducible factor with more than three terms.

papers.title: The distribution of $απ$ modulo one in $\mathbb{F}q(T)$: beyond Matomäki's exponent
papers.abstract: Let $α$ be an element of $\Fq((1/T))$ which is not in $\Fq(T)$. We ask how small $\nrm{απ}$ can be made when $π$ runs over irreducible polynomials, and write $θ(α)$ for the largest exponent $θ$ such that $\nrm{απ}<|π|^{-θ}$ has infinitely many solutions. The analogue of Matomäki's exponent, $θ(α)\ge\frac13$, was proved by Baier and the author, and it is the natural limit of \chg{methods based on} the Riemann Hypothesis. In this paper we go beyond it. For odd characteristic $p$ and $q$ large in terms of $p$ and $θ$, we prove that $θ(α)\geθ$ for every $α$ and every $θ<\sqrt2-1=0.414\ldots$, and for every $θ<\frac12$ when $α$ has bounded partial quotients. The main tools are an exact count of points in affine subspaces of $\Fq[T]$, a splitting of these subspaces into long arithmetic progressions, and the results of Sawin and Shusterman on the Möbius function along such progressions.

papers.title: Hopf Algebra of Graphs for Operator Splitting Methods
papers.abstract: Motivated by combinatorial identities arising in the study of operator splitting methods and their description in terms of bipartite rooted trees, we establish a connection between operator splitting methods and the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras. We show that the inclusion-exclusion expansion of the elementary weight of a rooted tree over its rooted subforests can be interpreted as the antipode of Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs. This interpretation recovers known identities for operator splitting and partitioned Runge-Kutta methods from general properties of the antipode. We further show that adjoint operator splitting methods can be described algebraically through the antipode and the canonical involution of the original method. The resulting framework also yields new combinatorial identities and connects the analysis of geometric numerical integrators with the theory of incidence Hopf algebras.

papers.title: Erratum to "Linear representations of 3-manifold groups over rings"
papers.abstract: The fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by allowing only finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}_2(R),$ where $R$ is a finite commutative ring with identity. In a prior paper, "Linear representations of $3$-manifold groups over rings", we, together with two co-authors, gave an equivalent formulation of Luo's conjecture via faithful representations, investigated variants of the conjecture where the target group is of type $\mathrm{SL}_2, \mathrm{GL}_2, \mathrm{PSL}_2$, or $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ as in the original conjecture, and claimed to provide a $3$-manifold group which violated all four variants of the conjecture. We have discovered a flaw in the work, such that the existing proof is valid only for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Here, we provide a modified argument for the $\mathrm{PSL}_2$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2$ cases.

papers.title: Optimality of the $D_4$ lattice quantizer
papers.abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The minimum is $13/(120\sqrt{2})$. The proof reduces the problem to polynomial inequalities on three secondary cones. We derive the second-moment formulas geometrically and give explicit polynomial certificates that can be checked by coefficient comparison. We also derive a lower bound for lattice quantizers in every dimension at least two from the number of Voronoi facets, using a comparison with circular cones and concavity in the solid angle. This bound strictly improves the sphere bound and recovers the hexagonal value in dimension two.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the standard and the mass-lumped linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem. For the standard method, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of the discrete ground state up to sign for sufficiently small mesh sizes, which only requires the $H^1$-convergence of the discrete ground states. For both methods, we establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-norms for $1 \le p < \infty$. Under additional regularity assumptions on the potential, we further obtain an optimal convergence rate in the $W^{1,\infty}$-norm and an almost optimal convergence rate, up to a logarithmic factor, in the $L^\infty$-norm. Moreover, we prove that the discrete ground states superconverge to the Ritz projection of the exact ground state in the $W^{1,p}$-seminorm. The analysis is based on a perturbation argument. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

papers.title: Separating hash families with large universe II
papers.abstract: For fixed integers $t,k\ge 2$, put $N=(t-1)(k-1)+1$. We prove that the maximum universe size of a $t$-perfect hash family of length $N$ over an alphabet of size $q$ satisfies $ p_t(N,q)\ge q^{k-o(1)}$. Together with monotonicity in the length, this gives a positive answer to a question of Blackburn, Etzion, Stinson and Zaverucha for every choice of feasible parameters. Our proof combines the Nash--Williams--Tutte theorem, a graph-theoretic elimination argument, and a solution-free-set theorem established in our previous work.

papers.title: Nearly-Optimal Time-Sample Trade-off in Consensus Dynamics
papers.abstract: How does the number of sampled opinions affect the time required to reach consensus in distributed consensus dynamics? We study the synchronous $h$-Majority, in which every node independently samples $h$ nodes uniformly at random with replacement in each round and adopts a most frequent sampled opinion, breaking ties uniformly at random. We show that $h$-Majority achieves the nearly-optimal trade-off between the sample size and the consensus time, among a broad class of consensus dynamics. In particular, we prove the following results. For every sample size $h \ge 3$ and for every initial configuration, we prove that the process reaches consensus with high probability within $$\widetilde{O}\left(1+\min\left\{\frac{1}{\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\}},\frac{\sqrt{n}}{h}\right\}\right)$$ rounds, where $n$ is the number of nodes and $p_{\max}$ is the largest initial fraction of nodes supporting any single opinion. This is the first bound on the consensus time for $h$-Majority that holds for every $h\ge3$ and every initial configuration. When the initially most popular opinion has a sufficiently large lead over every other opinion, we show that all nodes adopt this opinion with high probability within $O(\log n/\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\})$ rounds. We establish a matching lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors for any fixed update rule that treats all opinions symmetrically and that selects either a sampled opinion or the node's current opinion.

papers.title: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
papers.abstract: We study antiferromagnetic spin systems on random regular graphs through the lens of the phase transitions characterized by the complex zeros of the partition function. Our motivating examples include the hardcore model and the antiferromagnetic Potts model (including proper $q$-colorings at $β=0$). For both models on random $d$-regular graphs, we establish, with high probability over the graph, zero-free regions throughout the interior of the replica-symmetric regime. Asymptotically, this regime extends up to tree occupation density $$α< α_{\mathrm{RSB}}(d) = (2\log d - 2\log\log d + 2 - 2\log 2 + o_d(1))/d$$ for the hardcore model and up to degree $$d < d_{\mathrm{RSB}}(q) = (2q-1)\log q - 2\log 2 + o_q(1)$$ for proper $q$-colorings. Leveraging the standard algorithmic implications of zero-freeness, we obtain deterministic polynomial-time algorithms that multiplicatively approximate the corresponding partition functions at fixed rational parameters throughout this regime, with high probability over the graph. Our algorithmic guarantees significantly improve upon prior work and extend beyond the parameter ranges reached by previously known search algorithms. As a key intermediate step, we establish the pointwise equivalence, away from the threshold, of three notions of replica symmetry: geometric (averaged pairwise correlation decay), thermodynamic (convergence to the Bethe free-energy prediction), and variational (nonpositivity of the Bethe functional). To establish zero-freeness, we develop reinforced small subgraph conditioning, lifting classical small subgraph conditioning to random holomorphic functions to control short-cycle fluctuations. We also use variational replica symmetry to obtain exponential planted overlap concentration. This enables a typical-graph truncation that controls complex second moments up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold.

papers.title: Differentiation and Shift Property Characterisations of the Group Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group
papers.abstract: Recently, Krukowski characterised the Euclidean Fourier transform in terms of its behaviour with respect to differentiation. For locally compact abelian groups, he obtained a characterisation based on the behaviour of the Fourier transform under translation. Each of these results assumed that the operator (to be characterised) is an integral transform (with a kernel satisfying suitable regularity conditions), paired with a normalisation. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Here, the differentiation property is formulated in terms of the behaviour of the group Fourier transform with respect to the left-invariant vector fields, and the shift property is on its behaviour under right translation. Both of these characterise the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group, once paired with a normalisation. Our results assume that the transform is continuous linear, and do not require it to be an integral transform a priori.

papers.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
papers.abstract: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

papers.title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
papers.abstract: For every prime $p$ and every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$, we prove that, for every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines an incidence matrix factorization with a projective-plane construction controlling line-intersection numbers modulo $p$. A separate geometric construction in characteristic two yields better explicit constants in certain cases, and also gives integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $Ω_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.

papers.title: Propagation of Sobolev Regularity for Integral-Invariant Weak Solutions of the Linear Transport Equation
papers.abstract: Previous work strengthened the time integrability of integral-invariant weak solutions from L^1 to L^\infty within a spatial L^2 framework.This paper studies the propagation of Sobolev regularity for integral-invariant weak solutions of the conservative linear scalar transport equation.We first derive a representation formula along the flow and a distributional equation from integral identities against adjoint-transported test functions on domains moving with the same characteristic flow,and relate the weak formulation in time, including an endpoint term for the initial data, to representatives satisfying the pointwise-in-time integral definition.We then give a unified proof for k=1,2:under u_0\in H^k(Ω_0)and Assumption \mathsf A_{k+1},the pullback of the solution belongs to C^1([0,T];H^k(Ω_0)),the material derivative has spatial $H^k$ regularity,and the Eulerian time derivative has spatial H^{k-1} regularity.The corresponding time continuity is understood after pullback to the fixed domain by the flow.In both cases, U\in H^1(Q);when k=2, we further obtain \nabla_xU\in H^1(Q;\R^d).The pullback differentiability and the spatial estimates for the material derivativeprovide information beyond first-order space-time Sobolev regularity alone.The proof combines estimates for the characteristic flow with Sobolev product and composition rules.Under the additional assumption that the zero extension of the initial data belongs to H^2(\R^d),we also establish $H^1(0,T;H^1(\R^d))$ regularity in the fixed ambient space.Counterexamples show that these results concern regularity propagation under additional assumptions: general L^2 initial data do not automatically yield spatial smoothing,and spatial regularity of the material derivative cannot replace the corresponding regularity of the Eulerian time derivative.

papers.title: Uniform estimates for the Erdős-Moser equation and its analogue in arithmetic progressions
papers.abstract: We study the Erdős-Moser equation in arithmetic progressions, $\sum i^k=m^k$, where $i$ runs over the positive integers $i<m$ with $i\equiv b \pmod q$. We prove that a solution has at most $\lfloor k/\log 2+3/2\rfloor$ terms for all $k<10^{55}$, and at most $k/\log 2+5/2$ terms in general; this linear bound is best possible for real solutions and replaces the previously known exponential bound $(k+1)2^{2k+1}$. For $k=3$ we obtain a complete classification: solutions with exactly $n$ terms exist if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5\}$, and in each case there are infinitely many primitive solutions. For even exponents there are no solutions with three terms, and there are no solutions at all for $k=4$, for every $k=2^s\ge 4$, and for every even $k$ with $4\le k\le 24$. The key analytic input is a uniform estimate for the classical equation $1^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$: the real exponent $κ_m$ for which $1^κ+\dots+(m-1)^κ=m^κ$ satisfies $κ_m=\log 2\,(m-3/2-γ_m/m)$ with $0<γ_m<1/(8\log 2)$ for every $m\ge 3$. The proofs rest on a method based on centres of mass, Steiner's parallel-axis theorem and what we call the half-mass principle. The same framework identifies the constants of a general class of balance equations through the moments of a mass distribution: $3/2$ is a Steiner quotient, and $25/12-3\log 2=1/12-f''(\log 2)/2$ with $f(λ)=λ/(e^λ-1)$, whose Bernoulli expansion explains why this constant is so small.

papers.title: Selection spectra and sharp perturbations of normal sequences
papers.abstract: For a bounded sequence $y=(y_n)\subset E^*$ and $p>0$, put $G_p(y)=\{x\in E:(y_n(x))\in\ell_p\}$ and call $y$ $p$-strongly normal when $G_p(y)$ is dense in $E$. We study the density spectra of the original sequence, its subsequences, and its normalized successive blocks. The possible subsequence and block spectra are exactly $\varnothing$, $(0,\infty)$, $(1,\infty)$, $[r,\infty)$, and $(r,\infty)$ for $r>1$, and their possible pairs are precisely the nested pairs. Every such pair has a normalized weakly null $1$-unconditional basic realization in $\ell_1(\mathfrak c)^*$, even with empty original-sequence spectrum. Without a basicness requirement, the possible original-sequence spectra are all upper subsets of $(0,\infty)$; each is realized in a separable Hilbert space. We determine the exact universal perturbation classes: $\ell_p$ for a fixed original-sequence exponent, $c_0$ for the subsequence spectrum, and $\ell_1$ for the block spectrum. The ideal-valued version holds for every proper solid permutation-invariant linear ideal $c_{00}\subset A\subsetneq c_0$, without a norm or completeness assumption. For the author's 2012 selection model, the bounded-run criterion extends to all proper symmetric quasi-Banach sequence ideals. In the unbounded-run case, a single norm-one projection annihilates the summability domains of any family of fewer than $\mathfrak b$ such ideals; the quotient by their closed linear span contains a $1$-complemented isometric copy of $\ell_\infty$. Such copies also occur in the left jump at every $q>1$ and in the right jump at every $q\ge1$ of the scale of closed summability domains. Thus the common density criterion coexists with two-sided complemented discontinuities.

papers.title: Phase-Space Realization of Stochastic Multivalued Dynamics with Gyroscopic Subdifferential Coupling
papers.abstract: We introduce a new framework for stochastic variational inequalities with oblique reflections generated by non-symmetric matrix coefficients. The loss of symmetry fundamentally changes the structure of the reflected dynamics: besides the dissipative component, it produces a genuinely gyroscopic component describing rotational effects that are invisible to the associated energy forms. To capture this hidden component, we consider planar obstacle problems and we lift the dynamics to an extended phase-space system, where the dissipative and gyroscopic mechanisms are naturally separated. This leads to a new notion of solution, for which we establish existence and uniqueness. The resulting framework allows for genuinely rotated reflections, which can lead to angle-controlled rotations.

papers.title: The K-property of equilibrium states for systems with non-uniform structure
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a general criterion for the K-property of equilibrium states within the Climenhaga-Thompson framework. Under suitable pressure-gap and non-uniform expansiveness assumptions, we show that the unique equilibrium state has the K-property, provided that the good collection of orbit segments satisfies an appropriate non-uniform specification property, as well as an appropriate non-uniform distortion control property for the potential function. These results do not require any additional lambda-decomposition structure and apply to a wide range of systems, including those with non-trivial central directions, such as the frame flow over closed rank-one manifolds with bunched nonpositive curvature. Moreover, we also construct several counterexamples to demonstrate that generally the assumptions in our criteria cannot be weakened while keeping the K-property.

papers.title: Geometric structures, orbit closures and invariant measures in moduli spaces
papers.abstract: Building on the seminal work of Eskin, Mirzakhani and Mohammadi in the context of dynamics on moduli spaces, we introduce linear loci and linear measures to provide a relatively basic description of orbit closures and invariant measures in strata of translation surfaces. We use this to discuss geometrical properties of orbit closures and invariant measures from the perspective of geometric structures.

papers.title: Different approach to certain problems in univalent function theory
papers.abstract: Using different approach we consider some problems for the class $\mathcal{S}_{ex}^{\star}$ defined by the condition $\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\prec e^{αz}$, $0<α\leq1.$ Our method is more simple than that used by Das and Sarkar in their work: \textit{Sharp coefficient estimates for the exponential starlike class $S^\star_{ex}$} (\cite{DS26}).

papers.title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
papers.abstract: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph records the extrema of its iterated basin and hill boundaries. Their unweighted counts need not satisfy Morse inequalities, and the reduction can change homology. We assign multiplicities using the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain every vertex with nonzero local homology. This modified reduction preserves both hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We give explicit formulas in low dimensions and for complete layered graphs. We also construct local Morse numbers for path homology and prove agreement with the reachability construction on complete layered graphs, including those without transitive arrows. Counterexamples distinguish the homology theories and show that local Morse degrees need not equal vertex depths. A comparison with discrete-gradient methods explains the role of auxiliary choices.

papers.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
papers.abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility throughout the parameter family and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.

papers.title: Pure Type-One Generalized Hypercomplex Structures in Dimension Four
papers.abstract: We classify untwisted generalized hypercomplex structures on four-manifolds whose entire sphere has type one. Their Poisson tensors determine a canonical line field, and their local geometry is described by Gauduchon--Tod coframes. On a closed manifold, the canonical foliation is automatically Riemannian: the non-Riemannian alternative would require a twisting three-form with a nonzero period. Without assuming a circle action, we classify the compact structures into four families, distinguished by their first Betti numbers \(b_1=1,2,3,4\): Berger quotients, flat axis quotients, nontrivial circle bundles over flat three-tori, and constant tori. The underlying manifolds are parallelizable and admit symplectic forms precisely when the intrinsic Gauduchon--Tod invariant vanishes. These results address the four-dimensional untwisted case of the intermediate-type problem posed by Fino and Grantcharov.

papers.title: Quadratic Returns for a Moving Water Tank: An Explicit Right Inverse and a Sylvester Representation
papers.abstract: Coron's return method established local nonlinear controllability of a moving water tank in sufficiently large time. The quadratic response at uniform equilibrium is studied in this work, where the acceleration input in the linearized model cannot excite the Fourier modes of the fluid with even indices. At three one-way wave crossings ($T=3$), the quadratic final-state map on a family of delayed controls that return the linearized state to zero is reduced to a scalar expression associated with a planar curve. A constant-level curve gives the return, and a tangential variation yields an explicit right inverse of the derivative of the quadratic final-state map. This inverse acts on all missing modes and maps mean-zero periodic $H^r$ targets to $H^r$ controls for every nonnegative integer $r$. A contraction argument also gives local exact solvability of the quadratic final-state equation. Finally, a time-dependent Sylvester equation provides an alternative representation of the coupling responsible for the second-order correction. The associated change of state coordinates involves one spatial derivative, while the control correction preserves regularity in appropriate Sobolev spaces. These results concern the first two variation equations only, while nonlinear controllability at this time remains open. Keywords: Controllability, control of partial differential equations, return method, Saint-Venant equations, Sylvester equations.

papers.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
papers.abstract: We provide sharp estimates on the number of vertices needed to approximate the Euclidean unit ball $B_d\subset\mathbb R^d$ with relative symmetric-difference volume error at most $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. We show that the minimum vertex budget $N_\varepsilon(d)$ satisfies $$\log N_\varepsilon(d)\asymp d\log\left(1+\frac1{\varepsilon\sqrt d}\right).$$ In particular, $\exp(O(\sqrt d/\varepsilon))$ vertices suffice for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and all sufficiently large $d$. We also prove that achieving a fixed error $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ requires at least $Ω\bigl((\tfrac{1+\varepsilon}{2\sqrt\varepsilon})^{d-1}\bigr)$ facets, an exponential number in $d$. We extend our vertex approximation result to Gaussian symmetric-difference error, and give a positive answer to the question of De, Nadimpalli, and Servedio about subexponential vertex complexity for approximating Euclidean balls. We also disprove a Macbeath-type extremality principle for unrestricted vertex approximation. Whereas the ball uniformly maximizes the inscribed approximation error among all convex bodies (Macbeath, 1951), we show that approximating the hypercube $[-1,1]^d$ to relative error $\varepsilon$, with $δ:=1-\varepsilon$, requires $N\ge\fracδ{2}\exp(Ω(δ^2d/\log^2(2/δ)))$ vertices whenever $d\ge16\log(2/δ)$. Thus, when $d$ is large, the cube is harder to approximate than the ball in this sense. Finally, we determine the sharp dimensional order of the classical Laguerre-Delone triangulation number, showing that $\mathrm{ldel}_{d-1}=Θ(d^{-1/2})$ as $d\to\infty$. This improves both the upper bound of Ludwig, Schütt, and Werner and the lower bound of Böröczky by a factor of order $\sqrt d$. By classical asymptotic approximation theorems (Ludwig, 1999), this improvement applies to every convex body in $\mathbb R^d$ with $C^2$ boundary and positive Gaussian curvature.

papers.title: Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Covers
papers.abstract: We give a conic upper bound on the asymptotic rank of every weighted graph tensor over every field. If $W$ is the logarithmic edge-weight matrix of its dimension matrix $Q$, then $$ \operatorname{MaxCut}(W)\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{WT}(Q))\le U_{\operatorname{CP}}^Δ(W). $$ Here $U_{\operatorname{CP}}^Δ(W)$ maximizes $\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}W_{i,j}P_{i,j}$ over nonnegative symmetric zero-diagonal matrices $P$ such that $J-2P$ is copositive and $P_{i,j}\le P_{i,k}+P_{k,j}$ for all distinct vertices. The matrix $J$ is all-one, and copositivity means nonnegativity of the quadratic form on nonnegative vectors. Our starting point extends OpenAI's polynomial multiplication method and its subsequent arbitrary-field developments from three tensor legs to arbitrary order. We prove $$ \left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor\le\log_2\operatorname{\widetilde R}_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{GT}_2(K_n))\le\frac{n^2}{4}. $$ The edge exponent is at most $n/(2(n-1))$ and tends to the optimal value $1/2$, improving the previous Coppersmith--Winograd bounds and answering Question 1.3.1 of Christandl, Vrana, and Zuiddam. The bounds coincide for every even $n$. For every odd $m\ge3$, the theorem gives $\log_2\widetilde R_{\mathbb F}(\operatorname{GT}_2(C_m))\le m-1+1/(m+1)$, improving the previous cycle bound with a gap of only $1/(m+1)$ above the maximum cut. On weighted triangles, the program recovers the rectangular matrix multiplication curve of Uznański and Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam. The CP and semidefinite programs, with or without path constraints, all have value $9/4$ on the unweighted triangle, giving this upper bound a natural conic interpretation. Further applications give explicit bounds for complete multipartite graphs, split graphs, and wheels, including new cases of maximum-cut equality.

papers.title: The Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of fixed even difference from a uniform zeta-ratios conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of every fixed positive even difference $h$ from a restricted uniform two-over-two zeta-ratios formula. The formula may have error $O_\varepsilon(U^{\vartheta+\varepsilon})$ for any fixed $1/2\le\vartheta<(39-\sqrt{177})/32$. The real parts of all four shifts lie in $[3/64,5/64]$; their imaginary parts need only have absolute value at most $U^ν$, for a fixed $0<ν\le1/4$. For a fixed real smooth weight supported in $(1,1+1/(25h))$, we obtain an error $O_{h,W,\varepsilon}(x^{-Δ(\vartheta)+\varepsilon})$ in the correlation sum with weight $W(n/x)^2/n$, where $Δ(\vartheta)=7/16-\vartheta+\vartheta/(3-\vartheta)>0$. Adding the Riemann hypothesis improves this error to $O_{h,W,\varepsilon}(x^{\vartheta-7/8+\varepsilon})$. The proof retains the crossed zero residues in Mellin inversion and estimates their mixed term with the logarithmic-derivative integral. Two nonnegative time weights have the same diagonal term and opposite coefficients for the difference $h$. We deduce the logarithmic asymptotic for the weighted prime-pair sum $B_h$ and an asymptotic for the second finite difference of integrals of squared increments of the truncated Chebyshev function. The latter is connected to a logarithmically weighted Möbius approximant in the Nyman-Beurling criterion by finite identities.

papers.title: A Linear Lower Bound for Convex Body Chasing in Every Norm
papers.abstract: We establish an $Ω(d)$ lower bound on the competitive ratio of convex body chasing in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with movement costs measured in any norm. Previously, the best known lower bound valid across all norms was $Ω(d^{1/6})$, established by Papazov (2023); stronger lower bounds were known for $\ell_p$ norms, where Bubeck, Klartag, Lee, Li, and Sellke (2019) had established a lower bound of $Ω(\max\{\sqrt{d}, d^{1-1/p}\})$. In particular, a linear lower bound was known only for the $\ell_\infty$ norm, realized by the standard construction of chasing faces of a hypercube. Our lower bound strictly improves on the prior universal and $\ell_p$ lower bounds for $p < \infty$ and shows that the functional Steiner point algorithm of Sellke (2023) - which has competitive ratio $O(d)$ - is asymptotically optimal for every norm. Our approach is based on the recursive construction of Bubeck, Coester, and Rabani (2023) for metrical service systems, which gives a lower bound of $Ω(r^2)$ for requests of size $O(r)$. We show that requests in their construction, each comprising a set of discrete points in a graph metric, can be mapped to the vertices of convex requests in a $(2r+1)$-dimensional $\ell_p$ vector space while approximately preserving movement costs up to a factor of $O(r)$; the general result then follows via Milman's (1985) quotient-of-a-subspace theorem.

papers.title: The Fundamental Semigroup and Associative Lifts of Topological Semigroups
papers.abstract: We introduce the fundamental semigroup $Λ(S)$ of a nonempty path-connected topological semigroup $S$, defined using right translations and change-of-basepoint isomorphisms on its fundamental group. We prove that this construction is closed under composition and independent of the chosen basepoint up to isomorphism. It is also invariant under homotopy equivalences that preserve multiplication up to homotopy. We characterize exactly when the fundamental semigroup is a group and identify that group with an inner automorphism group. For a connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected topological semigroup, we show that multiplication admits a continuous associative lift to the universal cover if and only if $Λ(S)$ contains an idempotent. Every such idempotent can be realized by an associative lift, and any two associative lifts are isomorphic over $S$ through a deck transformation. We obtain existence results when the fundamental group has finite inner automorphism group or contains no subgroup isomorphic to Thompson's group $F$, and when the underlying space is a finite-dimensional CW complex. In contrast, we construct a path-connected countable CW topological semigroup with cells in arbitrarily high dimensions whose multiplication admits no continuous associative lift to its universal cover.

papers.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
papers.abstract: Haussler's covering lemma (JCTA 1995) gives the sharp $(C/δ)^d$ metric-entropy bound for binary VC classes under normalized $\ell_1$ distance. We prove a sharp global dynamic analogue for bounded real-valued classes in normalized $\ell_p$, for every $1\le p<\infty$. Writing $d=\operatorname{sfat}_{\varepsilon/32}(\mathcal F)$, we obtain a global dynamic cover of size at most $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ for every horizon and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Here a single family of deterministic causal experts, fixed independently of the instance sequence, covers every target on every sequence. For $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, a matching worst-case lower bound $(c/\varepsilon)^{pd}$ holds already for binary classes on one fixed sequence, even with real-valued experts. The constants are universal, independent of $p$. For $p=2$, this resolves the horizon-independent sequential $\ell_2$ covering problem of Rakhlin, Sridharan, and Tewari (PTRF 2015) in a stronger global form. For $p=1$, it gives the sharp $(C/δ)^{\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal H)}$ global dynamic covering bound for binary classes, resolving questions of Alon, Ben-Eliezer, Dagan, Moran, Naor, and Yogev (STOC 2021) and Malliaris and Moran (Trans. AMS 2024). Our proof combines rank-decreasing correction schedules and accurate sampled prefixes with exact continuations after target identification. Shared-parent routing distributes these continuations among eligible prefixes, eliminating the logarithmic overhead.

papers.title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
papers.abstract: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We express the second variation of the energy by the index form and characterize the null space of the index form by Jacobi fields. Given a geodesic flow, we construct Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data along its flow lines; they are unique when the real line is a curve object for the space. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization; the latter result does not require the curve-object property and applies to mapping spaces such as free loop spaces of complete Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: A sharp weighted commutator inequality for rank-one matrices
papers.abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be positive definite Hermitian, where $n\ge 2$, and define $\|X\|_A^2=\mathrm{tr}(AX^*X)$ for all $X\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$. We determine the smallest constant $C_A$ for which $$ \|XY-YX\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le C_A\|X\|_A^2\|Y\|_A^2 $$ holds for all rank-one $X,Y\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, where $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. The constant depends only on the two smallest eigenvalues of $A$ and is determined by a strictly monotone scalar equation. This answers the sharp-constant question for rank-one matrices formulated by Fang and Cheng. We characterize all equality pairs. Also, we present an application to density matrices in quantum physics.

papers.title: The Art of Toda Brackets-A Journey through the Homotopy Groups of SO(n) in degrees 23-29
papers.abstract: This book has several fundamental aims, one of which is to serve as a reference book for computing unstable homotopy groups using methods of the Toda school. The Toda bracket serves the art of constructing homotopy liftings and extensions of maps. It plays a fundamental role in dealing with composition relations of homotopy classes. This book brings together in Appendix A.3 all known results on the $2$-primary components of unstable homotopy groups of spheres obtained using the art of Toda brackets as the principal tool, with explicit generators. It also explains in Appendix A.2 the conventions used to name the generators. The book mainly presents calculations of the $2$-primary components of the homotopy groups $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq 28$ and all $n,$ as well as some $π_{29}(\mathit{SO}(n)),$ with explicit generators, while retaining two possible group structures for $π_{28}(\mathit{SO}(11)).$ In degree $29,$ the cases $7\leq n\leq14$ remain under investigation. The odd-primary components of the homotopy groups $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ in the above range can be computed with little effort; these computations essentially amount to looking up the relevant entries in existing tables.

papers.title: Recent progress in the construction of Hadamard matrices
papers.abstract: A Hadamard matrix is a square matrix with entries $\pm 1$ whose rows are mutually orthogonal. Hadamard matrices are conjectured to exist at every order divisible by $4$; for approximately the last twenty years, the smallest open case of this conjecture was order 668. In August 2026, Alpöge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle announced Hadamard matrices at the twelve orders below $2000$ at which none was known. In this paper we verify and analyse the claimed matrices. We survey results on the existence of Hadamard matrices and list the $85$ orders up to $10\,000$ at which no Hadamard matrix is currently known. In pursuing this work we constructed Hadamard matrices at sixteen orders that were open in the published literature. We conclude with a list of open problems.

papers.title: The Wandering Must Continue: Pure Mathematicians as Rangers of the North
papers.abstract: Pure mathematics is an honest barometer of a civilization's scientific capacity, maintaining an unwritten culture of rigor, structural perception, and intellectual honesty whose primary service is not merely proving theorems, but cultivating human judgment. In an era of automated theorem generation and formal verification, this essay argues that establishing a result and understanding both why it holds and why it matters remain distinct achievements, and outlines concrete institutional mechanisms to protect the exploratory core of the discipline.

papers.title: Zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Bergman space of the unit ball
papers.abstract: In this paper, using local boundary factorizations of harmonic functions and singular-value estimates for Toeplitz products, we study the zero-product problem for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space of the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove that a finite product of such operators is zero only if one of the symbols is identically zero, provided that all the symbols are harmonic on the open unit ball and continuous on the closed unit ball.

papers.title: Large deviations for the largest eigenvalue of a polynomial in Gaussian matrices
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that the spectrum, the norm, and the largest eigenvalue of a self-adjoint polynomial $P$ in $k$ independent matrices from the GOE or the GUE satisfy a large deviation principle.

papers.title: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the Néron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$.

papers.title: Multiplicity Bounds for Contractible Closed Reeb Orbits on Prequantization Bundles
papers.abstract: We study the multiplicity of contractible closed Reeb orbits on prequantization circle bundles $(M^{2n+1},ξ)$ over closed symplectic manifolds $(B^{2n},ω)$. For even $n$, under suitable geometric hypotheses, we prove that every non-degenerate contact form supporting $ξ$ whose contractible closed orbits have nonzero mean index and whose good contractible closed orbits have nonzero Conley--Zehnder index carries at least $\frac{1}{2}χ(B)+\frac{1}{2}\dim H_n(B;\mathbb{Q})+1$ geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits. In dimension five, under the corresponding geometric hypotheses and assuming $H_1(B;\mathbb{Q})=0$, we prove the conjectural lower bound $\dim H_*(B;\mathbb{Q})$ for every non-degenerate supporting contact form whose simple contractible closed orbits have nonzero Conley--Zehnder index.

papers.title: Almost-optimal bulk regularity conditions in the CLT for G$β$E
papers.abstract: We consider linear statistics $\sum_{k=1}^N f(x_k)$ of a Gaussian $\b$-ensemble. Following the work of \cite{LaSo22}, which was concerned only with Wigner matrices, we extend their results for general $\b$. In particular, we show that the CLT holds for any $f \in H^{1/2 + \e}$. The novel input which was not used in \cite{LaSo22} is the Helffer-Sjöstrand representation for the covariance, first appearing the random matrix context in \cite{ErYa15}, coupled with characteristic flow estimates for DBM, first appearing in \cite{Bo22}.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
papers.abstract: This is the third paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. Here we study simplicity through two countable structures with simple unstable theories: the Rado graph, and the symplectic space of labels of Pauli strings of finite support, in which addition records the products of the strings and the symplectic form records their commutation. In the second structure, forking characterizes the logical errors of stabilizer codes: an error undetectable by the checks of a code is logical exactly when its type over the stabilizer labels and a complete set of logical-operator labels forks over the stabilizer labels, and the independence theorem becomes a rule for gluing syndromes. A two-valued relation between countable sets of labels defines a diagonal bipartite observable, whose real-valued theory describes Alice's probability mixtures of labels and their expected responses at Bob's probes. Mixing changes the classification: if the relation has the independence property, this theory has the tree property of the second kind. For the observable of the symplectic form, actual mixtures of checks witness this property for the response itself; for the observable of the Rado graph, every array that witnesses it for a quantifier-free formula in Bob's probe contains idealized preparations, which lie outside the original structure.

papers.title: Converses of Moreau's decomposition theorem
papers.abstract: We study when generalized metric projections generated by strongly quasiconvex functions are polarizable. The point of departure is Moreau's decomposition theorem, where the Euclidean metric projections onto two mutually polar closed convex cones form complementary retractions whose sum is the identity. This suggests the following fundamental question: when does a given retraction admit such a complementary polar retraction? We formulate this notion through polarizable retractions and then specialize it to generalized projections of the form $x\mapsto P_{\cal C}^\varphi(x)$, defined by minimizing $\varphi(x-y)$ with respect to $y$ over a closed convex set ${\cal C}$. After recalling basic properties of mutually polar retractions and first-order characterizations of generalized projections, we prove the main result: If $\varphi$ is strongly quasiconvex, the generalized projection $P_{\cal C}^\varphi$ is polarizable if and only if ${\cal C}$ is a closed convex cone. Thus, polarizability of the projection is characterized by the conic geometry of its range. Hence, this result can be considered as a converse of Moreau's decomposition theorem. As a consequence, a more specific converse of the same theorem is presented for the Euclidean norm.

papers.title: A universal framework for Hopf algebras in combinatorics
papers.abstract: A universal framework for Hopf algebras in combinatorics provides a unified understanding of combinatorial objects. To establish such a framework, we dualize the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras developed by Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile, obtaining the theory of rooted Hopf algebras. An object in this category is a graded connected Hopf algebra equipped with a group-like element, called a root, in its completion. These roots dualize the character theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras and provide a natural way to extend Bernstein and raising operators to other rooted Hopf algebras. The resulting constructions extend Schur, Hall--Littlewood, and Macdonald functions to rooted Hopf algebras. As an application, we develop these constructions for symmetric functions in noncommuting variables.

papers.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: For a one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operator with bounded nonconstant iid potential, we prove a unit-intensity Poisson limit for local eigenvalues unfolded by the integrated density of states. The limit holds at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. In particular, it holds for Bernoulli potentials at every fixed nonzero coupling. The proof uses auxiliary phase functions built from inverse stationary measures to obtain an exact IDS drift. Projective contraction then yields exponential crossing times, and a spatial subdivision argument gives independent Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows. At energies where the IDS has a finite positive derivative, the usual linear rescaling gives the same limit.

papers.title: Ball growth at all scales in universal covers of short metric graphs
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a connected metric graph of first Betti number $b\ge 2$, and let $Γ_b$ be a trivalent graph of the same Betti number with all edges of unit length. We show that if $\text{length}(Γ) \le λ\, \text{length}(Γ_b)$, then the universal cover of $Γ$ contains a vertex around which, at every radius $R\ge 0$, the ball is at least as long as the ball of radius $R$ in the trivalent tree whose edges all have length $3λ$. In particular, for $λ\le\frac13$, this ball is at least as long as the ball of the same radius in the universal cover of $Γ_b$, with no multiplicative loss. This improves an earlier theorem of the author, which gives the weaker lower bound $(1-3λ)$ times the ball in the universal cover of $Γ_b$, and only for $λ\le\frac16$. The proof rests on an elementary comparison principle. Among trees whose vertices have degree at least three and whose edges have length at most $c$, the trivalent tree with all edges of length $c$ has the smallest balls at every radius. As an application, we double the exponential growth rate in the author's earlier uniform lower bound for the area of balls in the universal cover of small-area surfaces of hyperbolic type, from $\ln 2$ to $2\ln 2$, beyond the hyperbolic rate. We also obtain explicit constants in the positive answer to Guth's question for surfaces. Finally, we conjecture the sharp, all-scale version of the minimal volume entropy inequality of Kapovich-Nagnibeda and Lim, and show that it would be optimal.

papers.title: Regularity lemma for Gaussian polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{é}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$. We apply the regularity lemma to obtain a short proof of the robust Borell inequality of Mossel and Neeman.

papers.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
papers.abstract: We answer, in the trace metric, a question of Kowalski and Untrau on Wasserstein distances of all orders between the distribution $μ_q$ of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and the Sato-Tate law $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$: we prove bounds for every order $s$ and show that their exponents are optimal for Katz-type moment bounds. In the trace metric we prove $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll_s q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s<3$, $W_3\ll q^{-1/3}(\log q)^{1/3}$, $W_s\ll_s q^{-1/4-1/(4s)}$ for $3<s<\infty$ and $W_\infty\ll q^{-1/4}$. In the angle metric we obtain bounds of every order, including $W_2\le 7q^{-1/3}$ and $W_\infty\ll q^{-1/6}$. These estimates follow from a general theorem for probability measures satisfying Katz-type Chebyshev moment bounds. Its proof combines an edge-sensitive discrepancy estimate with a new level-set bound for the distribution function and a quantile-displacement argument. We construct measures showing that the resulting exponents cannot in general be improved using moment bounds of this type alone, in the trace metric and in the angle metric for $s\le 2$ and $s\ge 6$ (up to logarithms); these constructions do not assert optimality for the Kloosterman measures themselves. A sharp comparison between Wasserstein distances and the Kolmogorov distance for the Sato-Tate law exhibits the same transition at $s=3$. Finally, using the exact third moment, we prove $W_1(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})>q^{-1/2}/10$ when $3\nmid q$.

papers.title: Compactness and essential norms for two-weight fractional Riesz transforms on curves
papers.abstract: We prove a compact two-weight $T1$ theorem for the $α$-fractional Riesz vector, $0\leqα<n$, when one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve $Γ$. The measures may have common point masses. Under the global boundedness assumptions, we give a two-sided estimate for the essential norm in terms of Muckenhoupt and testing constants computed after restricting both measures to small cubes. Compactness is equivalent to the uniform vanishing of these local bounds as the cube side length tends to zero. The smooth truncations have a unique weak operator limit and converge in operator norm in the compact case. For arclength measure and distance power weights, we determine the compactness ranges for Green gradients on bounded tubes and for Newtonian gradients and Biot--Savart fields on the whole space. The whole-space operators in these ranges are compact but are not Hilbert--Schmidt. When $α=n-1$ and both measures have positive continuous arclength densities $a,b$ on the same closed curve, we obtain the exact essential norm $πc_{n-1,n}\max_Γ\sqrt{ab}$.

papers.title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
papers.abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe equations of the form $i\partial_tu+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc\neq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. Under the additional assumption $e\neq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. Unlike the previous $H^1$ global theory based on Takaoka's periodic well-posedness estimates (2000), our result does not require any non-resonance condition on the coefficients. Our approach relies on the construction of modified higher-order energies, following the strategy developed for the generalized KdV equation by Planchon, Tzvetkov and Visciglia (2023) and for the generalized DNLS equation by Hayashi, Ozawa and Visciglia (2025). Motivated by higher-order modulation theory, we exploit the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow to establish Sobolev bounds uniform in the modulation parameter $\varepsilon$ on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$. This corresponds to physical times of order $\varepsilon^{-3}$, which is the natural time scale anticipated for the NLS-Dysthe approximation.

papers.title: Variance Bounds for Minimum Perfect Matching Problem by Random Walk on Multinomial Distribution
papers.abstract: We establish variance upper bounds for the minimum perfect matching problem in general metric spaces under a geometric partition condition. As a principal application, let $H_n$ be the minimum perfect matching cost of $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, where $n$ is even and $d\ge2$. We prove $$\operatorname{Var}(H_n)\le C d n^{1-2/d},$$ where $C$ is independent of $n$ and $d$. This removes the logarithmic losses in earlier upper bounds in every dimension (Talagrand, 1995); in particular, the variance remains bounded in dimension two, answering an open question (Rhee, 1994). The proof relies on constructing a rapidly mixing Markov process with a multinomial stationary distribution.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
papers.abstract: This is the second paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. For an observable of two independently prepared systems, Alice's and Bob's, we study its idealized responses: the expectation values of Alice's limiting preparations, as functions of Bob's preparations, which serve as probes, with Bob's system idealized first. We show that the observable is NIP, that is, no sequence of Alice's preparations lets Bob's probes realize every finite pattern of high and low values at a fixed positive gap, exactly when all idealized responses are of the first Baire class, pointwise limits of sequences of continuous functions; they then form a separable Rosenthal compactum. Because Alice can mix preparations, this compactum is convex, and hereditary separability forces it to be metrizable, so that NIP observables occupy three of the four topological classes defined by metrizability and Todorčević's trichotomy. Comparisons of photon numbers, of positions and of events in spacetime realize these three classes, and trees of preparations realize the seven minimal families of the Argyros--Dodos--Kanellopoulos heptachotomy. For the ferromagnetic transverse-field Ising model at positive temperature, the finite-volume magnetizations with offset longitudinal fields form a stable family when the spontaneous magnetization vanishes, and a family whose closure is first countable but not hereditarily separable when it does not.

papers.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
papers.abstract: We study whether global asymptotic stability (GAS) of the origin is decidable for homogeneous polynomial vector fields with rational coefficients. Our main technical contribution is showing that, for such vector fields of odd degree $d \geq 3$ in every sufficiently large dimension $n$, the problem of deciding GAS of the origin is many-one complete for the class of recursively enumerable sets (and hence undecidable). Using the tools we have built up, we also improve on some recent work by proving a similar result for Lyapunov stability instead of GAS. The proof of our main contribution splits naturally into two parts: - In the first part we give, for every fixed dimension $n$ and odd degree $2k+1$, a computable map which sends a homogeneous polynomial vector field of degree $2k+1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ to a homogeneous polynomial vector field of degree three on $\mathbb{R}^m$, where $m=\binom{n+k-1}{k}$, and preserves both GAS and Lyapunov stability. As a consequence, the problems of deciding whether the origin is GAS or Lyapunov stable for rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields of any degree, of any fixed odd degree $d \geq 3$, and of degree three are pairwise many-one equivalent. - In the second part we prove that there is a fixed dimension $n_*$ and a fixed odd degree $d_*$ such that the set of rational-coefficient homogeneous polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^{n_*}$ of degree $d_*$ whose origin is GAS is many-one complete. This is done by "transferring" many-one completeness between several different problems, starting from the solvability of a Diophantine equation and eventually arriving at our desired GAS decision problem.

papers.title: CutIGA with Least Squares Stabilized Nitsche Boundary Conditions: The Biharmonic Problem
papers.abstract: We propose a symmetric Nitsche method for the biharmonic Dirichlet problem on a smooth domain whose boundary may cut arbitrarily through the computational mesh. Bulk least-squares stabilization in a boundary strip and tangential boundary penalties control the consistency terms through an explicit lifting of the two Dirichlet traces. This gives coercivity on $H^4(Ω)$ without inverse inequalities and permits a fixed penalty independent of the cut configuration for sufficiently thin strips. Under suitable regularity assumptions, splines of degree $p\geq4$ give energy and $L^2$ error bounds of orders $h^{p-1}$ and $h^{p+1}$. We also analyze a face-stabilized extension to $C^1$ splines of degree $p=2$ and $C^2$ splines of degree $p=3$. Exact-ellipse experiments examine convergence, cut stability, and parameter sensitivity.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
papers.abstract: This is the first of three papers that read the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables, through their expectation functions on product states. Here we study stability: the independence of the expectation from the order in which the preparations of the two systems are idealized. We show that stability is characterized by weak compactness, by factorization through a reflexive Banach space, and by the uniform simulation of idealized preparations by finite mixtures of actual ones. A uniform version of stability, which bounds at every margin the finite staircases of responses, governs adaptive discrimination and the online prediction of thresholded expectations; for the swap test, Hong--Ou--Mandel coincidences and discrete equality tests, it yields bounds independent of dimension.

papers.title: Sparse domination modulo polynomials
papers.abstract: We develop a sparse domination theory that captures both local polynomial approximation and cancellation of the input below the scale of each sparse cube. Its coefficients are percentiles of localized smooth maximal functions of the input minus its local polynomial approximation, combining features of mean-oscillation sparse bounds and of the cancellative sparse bounds of Conde-Alonso, Lorist and Rey. Using wavelet representations, we characterize the Calderón-Zygmund operators whose derivatives admit these bounds by explicit polynomial testing conditions. In the homogeneous setting, the same conditions characterize weighted Hardy-Sobolev inequalities with linear dependence on the $A_\infty$ characteristic. This quantitative dependence detects the transition from BMO to $L^\infty$ testing conditions that Lerner found for pointwise bounds by Riesz potentials, a distinction that qualitative weighted estimates cannot recover. In the inhomogeneous setting, we prove corresponding weighted inequalities and show that they are strictly weaker than pointwise sparse domination from the second derivative order onward. Consequences include Hardy-Sobolev estimates below the Banach range, sharp weighted Sobolev inequalities, and pointwise bounds by Riesz potentials.

papers.title: Amenable C-sequences and ineffability in L
papers.abstract: We give a relative consistency counterexample to the conjecture of Inamdar and Rinot that every regular uncountable cardinal carrying no amenable C-sequence is ineffable in the constructible universe L. The existence of a $Π^2_1$-indescribable cardinal is equiconsistent with the existence of a $Π^2_1$-indescribable cardinal carrying no amenable C-sequence and not ineffable in L. For every ground-model C-sequence on a weakly compact cardinal $κ$, generalized Hechler forcing adds a club D with $D\capβ\subseteq C_β$ at stationarily many inaccessible indices. We use this capture theorem in an iteration of length $κ^+$ after Johnstone's local lottery preparation.

papers.title: Large Growth Happens: Gaussian Elimination with Partial Pivoting on Random Matrices
papers.abstract: We prove that the probability that Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting on $n \times n$ Gaussian random matrices has growth $ρ$ is at least inverse quasi-polynomial: $Ω\left(\exp\left(-c \log^2 \left(\fracρ{\sqrt{n}}\right)\log(n)\right)\right)$ for some constant $c > 0$. In particular, the probability of growth $ρ\ge n^{1/2 + ε}$ is at least $\exp(- O (ε^2 \log^3 (n) ))$. This lower bound breaks standard conjectures in the smoothed and average-case analysis of Gaussian elimination. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first non-trivial lower bound on the probability of large growth for Gaussian random matrices.

papers.title: When Hilbert functions determine generic initial ideals
papers.abstract: Over a field of characteristic zero, we characterize the Hilbert functions that determine the degree reverse lexicographic generic initial ideal among Artinian quotients of embedding dimension $n\ge2$ with the $(n-2)$-strong Lefschetz property. The criterion is a finite arithmetic test on successive positive differences of the Hilbert function. It uses recursively defined integer vectors and requires no construction of a monomial ideal. When uniqueness holds, the same vectors recover the common generic initial ideal degree by degree. The proof reduces uniqueness successively to uniqueness of lower sets of specified cardinalities in Borel orders. In four variables, the test simplifies to avoidance of explicitly computed integer intervals. We recover the quasi-symmetry criterion of Harima and Wachi and give infinite families beyond that criterion in every number of variables at least four.

papers.title: An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids
papers.abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) for approximately counting and uniformly sampling common bases of two matroids given by their independence oracles. Moreover, our algorithms generalize far beyond this to Hadamard products of two probability measures on the Boolean cube satisfying a simple nonnegative curvature condition. These algorithmic primitives have myriad applications in statistical physics, polyhedral combinatorics, the theory of quantum many-body systems, and beyond. The central difficulty is that the hard constraints imposed by the two input matroids (or the two input measures, more generally) obstruct traditional approaches based on local Markov chains. Relaxing these constraints can restore rapid mixing, but configurations that satisfy the original hard constraints may become exponentially rare if this is done naïvely. Our main contribution is a novel approach for approximate counting that marries Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) with convex programming to overcome these obstacles: - We relax the intersection by imposing an overlap penalty on the product measure formed by the two input measures. We prove, via an integrated Bochner-type method, that this "soft intersection" satisfies a Poincaré Inequality uniformly over all external fields. - We use samples from the relaxed distribution to solve a dual maximum entropy convex program inspired by the Gurvits capacity. This program reweights the soft intersection measure using external fields to boost the aggregate probability of configurations satisfying the hard intersection constraint, without changing their relative weights. We bound the success probability directly using the uniform Poincaré Inequality and smallness of the gradient norm. AI Disclosure: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra and GPT-6 Astra Ultra were heavily used to develop the ideas in this paper.

papers.title: Finite Stick Breaking Sequences
papers.abstract: In 1949, De Bruijn and Erdős considered infinite stick-breaking sequences. In this work, we consider finite sequences and prove that an infinite sequence that is due to De Bruijn, Erdős, and Toulmin is in some sense unique.

papers.title: Sharp Riesz capacity inequalities and the Pólya--Szegő conjecture
papers.abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $p\in(n-2,n)$, we prove that closed balls maximize the ratio of Riesz $p$-capacity to Newtonian capacity among all compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. This resolves the classical Pólya--Szegő capacity ratio conjecture and its higher-dimensional extensions. For $n\geq4$, a sharp inequality for the ratio of Newtonian capacity to logarithmic capacity is established. All equality cases are characterized.

papers.title: Infinitesimal Hilbertianity for manifolds with Sobolev regular Riemannian metrics through uniform lower capacity bounds
papers.abstract: We prove that metric measure spaces arising from $2$-manifolds equipped with Riemannian metrics $g$ such that $g, g^{-1} \in L^\infty_{\rm loc} \cap W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ are infinitesimally Hilbertian. Along the way, we establish uniform lower $1$-capacity bounds of several $1$-dimensional subsets of $\R^2$.

papers.title: A Lean~4 Framework for the Radii Polynomial Method
papers.abstract: Understanding nonlinear dynamics is central to many fields of study, yet most nonlinear systems are beyond the reach of closed-form solutions. Numerical simulation is then used to reveal dynamical structures before their existence can be established. This alone, however, leaves the validity of the computed solution unanswered. Rigorous numerical methods address this gap by combining computation with explicit analytic estimates. Among them, the radii polynomial approach, a Newton--Kantorovich type argument, turns a numerical approximation into a proof of existence and uniqueness of a true solution near that approximation. In previous practice, the verification of these inequalities relies on interval-arithmetic libraries and hand-derived algebraic bounds. In this paper, we present a framework for the radii polynomial method in the Lean~4, which turns numerical certificates into fully type-checked theorems about the true solution. A central challenge in this process is to manage the complexity of the formalization. Our approach begins with a family of problems and their common structure. The spaces in which the analysis takes place are developed through universal properties in suitable categories, with extension properties that characterize maps by their action on generators. These properties guide the design of a reusable interface such that problem-specific arguments concentrate on the numerical data and the algebraic bounds that distinguish one equation from another. We formalize a general radii polynomial theorem, develop weighted coefficient algebras and reusable operator estimates, connect finite computational checks to the hypotheses of the theorem, and establish the realization theorems that transport certified coefficient space zeros to analytic solutions of the original equations.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
papers.abstract: We reveal an unexpected connection between two interacting particle systems: Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. We first establish a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs: the mixing time of the $t$-particle process on any connected $d$-vertex graph is at most $O(\log d)$ times the corresponding single-particle mixing time, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ [KV26] to $O(n\log n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution. We then show that the twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace can be exactly encoded by a Markov chain on partitions, which naturally lifts to a parallel KMP chain on the complete graph. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions of the parallel Kac's walk suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in all $t$. Our main technical contribution is a new structural property of KMP-type dynamics: conditional product structure, which holds for both the standard KMP processes on general graphs and the parallel KMP processes on complete graphs. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the evolution of the labeled KMP process factorizes into independent single-particle updates. Combining this structure with an exact coupling, we remove the dependence on the number of particles from the mixing bounds for both unlabeled KMP models. This bypasses the $\log(π_{\min}^{-1})$ dependency from spectral-gap arguments, which is often prohibitively large for many-particle systems. Using this framework, we prove mixing bounds that are sharp up to logarithmic factors for both unlabeled KMP models.

papers.title: Universal Formulas for de Jonquières Loci and Equivariant Contact Problems
papers.abstract: Given a family of genus $g$ curves $f:Ψ\to S$ and a relative degree $d$ line bundle $L$ on $Ψ$ such that $f_*L$ is a vector bundle, the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ is stratified by relative de Jonquières loci, which parameterize sections of $L$ with prescribed vanishing orders. We give universal formulas for the classes of these loci in terms of the relative $O(1)$ on $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ and tautological classes pulled back from the universal Picard stack $\mathrm{Pic}_g^d$. When $f$ is the family of lines in $\mathbb{P}^r$, we use the universal polynomials to compute $\mathrm{GL}_{r+1}$-equivariant classes of loci of hypersurfaces and complete intersections admitting lines with prescribed contact orders.

papers.title: Critical semilinear damped wave equations beyond moduli of continuity
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear classical damped wave equations with general nonnegative nondecreasing nonlinearities, without imposing a modulus-of-continuity structure or convexity. A Dini-type integral condition expressed directly in terms of the nonlinearity gives small data global in-time existence and extends the nonlinear framework of Ebert--Girardi--Reissig [Math. Ann. 378 (2020), 1311--1326]. When this Dini-type integral diverges and the effective total mass of the initial data is positive, convergence of the Keller--Osserman tail integral is necessary and sufficient for finite-time blow-up of the maximal mild Sobolev solution, particularly, divergence of the tail integral gives global grow-up. The resulting integral criteria distinguish the contributions of the nonlinearity near zero and at infinity in governing small data global in-time existence with diffusion decay, global grow-up, and finite-time blow-up.

papers.title: Metric foundations of geometry
papers.abstract: A metric space is called all-set-homogeneous if every isometry between two of its subsets extends to an isometry of the whole space. We classify all-set-homogeneous length spaces: besides the classical examples, they include the universal metric trees of finite valence.

papers.title: Word Length and Diameter in Permutation Groups
papers.abstract: In the binary diameter problem, the input consists of explicitly given permutations generating a finite group $G$ and a binary-encoded number $k$, and the question is whether every element of $G$ is a product of at most $k$ of the given generators. In the binary length problem, the input additionally contains a permutation $g \in G$, and the question is whether $g$ is such a product. We show that the binary diameter problem is PSPACE-complete, thereby confirming a conjecture of Lohrey and Rosowski (2023). Moreover, we show that PSPACE-hardness already holds for solvable groups of derived length at most 3, whereas the problem is $Π_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete for 2-step nilpotent groups. For the binary length problem, we establish a sharp complexity threshold: the problem is NP-complete for 2-step nilpotent groups, which extends a result of Lohrey and Rosowski for abelian groups, and PSPACE-complete for groups that are simultaneously 3-step nilpotent and metabelian, which strengthens the main result of Jerrum (1985). Finally, we show that the unary diameter problem, where $k$ is encoded in unary, is $Π_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete for generating sets of the full symmetric group, confirming another conjecture of Lohrey and Rosowski.

papers.title: Descent along flat composed with radicalization
papers.abstract: We study the following general situation. Let $R\to S$ be a finite flat morphism of regular rings of zero (resp. prime) mixed or (equi)-characteristic. For $P\in Spec R$, put $A=R/P, C=S/PS,$ and $B=S/\sqrt{PS}=C_{\mathrm{red}}.$ The basic question is whether a property of $B$ forces the same property of $A$. The main point is that ordinary finite-flat descent applies naturally to $A\to C$, whereas the passage $C\to C_{\mathrm{red}}$ may (not) destroy nilpotent information.

papers.title: Vector Balancing in Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: The Komlós problem asks for signs $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^n$ with $\|A\varepsilon\|_\infty$ bounded by an absolute constant whenever the columns of $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ have Euclidean norm at most $1$. We give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem in the unit-cost real-RAM model. Our deterministic algorithm achieves discrepancy at most $8272$. As a consequence, we obtain a deterministic $O(\sqrt t)$-discrepancy algorithm for the Beck-Fiala problem on set systems in which each element belongs to at most $t$ sets. Our algorithm rounds a fractional coloring while keeping the row sums bounded. Its key idea is to keep the number of nearly tight row constraints small relative to the number of active coordinates. We achieve this through a spectral bound based on a weighted Gram matrix of squared row entries. We maintain the bound using a cubic spectral potential and negative-curvature updates that satisfy the required linear constraints.

papers.title: Isogeometric analysis for the Helmholtz transmission eigenvalue problem
