Its analysis combines preservation of the support in a fixed direction with contraction of the corresponding functional after renormalization. Crucially, the algorithm works directly with the input generators and does not use zonotope sparsification. We complement this result with a \emph{universal} $Ω(\sqrt{d/\log d})$ lower bound holding for \emph{all} full-dimensional zonotopes when the number of oracle queries is polynomial in $d$. Finally, we consider containment problems $\max\{s >0 : s K \subseteq Q\}$, for general convex bodies $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. A result of Nasz{ó}di on approximating $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ by a polytope implies a $Θ(d/\log d)$ approximation algorithm in polynomial time when the centroid of $K$ is the origin. We show the tightness of this approximation factor in the oracle model via a reduction to the circumradius computation. Our lower bound holds for centrally symmetric convex sets, implying that Barvinok's optimal $O(\sqrt{d})$-approximation of a centrally symmetric convex body by a polytope with a polynomial number of vertices cannot be computed in polynomial time.

papers.title: More on expressibility of satisfiability in submodels and extensions
papers.abstract: We study expressibility in infinitary languages of the modal operators associated with satisfiability of sentences of these languages in submodels and extensions of models. We give a syntactic criterion for expressibility in finitary predicate languages, show that in many cases infinitary languages are closed under the operator associated with submodels, and that this is so in any language with a purely monadic signature. Finally, we prove that in finitary or strongly compact languages, the operator associated with extensions, though can be inexpressible by a single sentence, is always expressible by a universal theory, in striking contrast with the submodel case.

papers.title: A Distributional Equation Approach to Front Propagation
papers.abstract: Travelling waves of mean-field particle systems are usually studied through the partial differential equation satisfied by the mean-field limit. We develop a different and entirely probabilistic set of tools. The wave profile is characterised as the solution of a distributional fixed-point equation for a tagged particle seen in the frame of the wave, and that equation is solved by relating it to a linear one --- a smoothing transform --- whose solutions are the martingale limits of a branching random walk. We apply this approach to a range of models, recover some known results and obtain a number of new ones. We first study models where particles evolve according to independent Lévy processes and, at Poisson epochs synchronise randomly selected pairs of particles (the lower of the two moves instantaneously to the position of the higher of the two). We characterise the speeds and travelling waves for all such models. In particular, this covers the case where the Lévy process is a continuous-time random walk with an arbitrary jump distribution; previously, only exponentially distributed jumps had been treated. We also consider a variant in which, instead of synchronising, the lower of the two particles jumps up by a random amount, drawn independently at each jump. This model is motivated by the so-called power-of-2 systems from queueing theory. Finally, we consider a new model where updates are given by the mixture of synchronisation and power-of-2: each update is a random value but the resulting position of the lower particle is capped by that of the higher one. In all cases, we characterise the speed, the travelling waves and their tail behaviour; the probabilistic nature of our approach makes the tail analysis particularly tractable.

papers.title: Efficient Receding Horizon Control for Stabilizing 2D Navier--Stokes Flows with Finitely Many Localized Actuators and POD Acceleration
papers.abstract: This paper develops and analyzes a computationally efficient receding horizon control (RHC) strategy for steering two-dimensional Navier--Stokes flows to prescribed reference trajectories. The control is represented by a finite linear combination of localized actuators supported within a prescribed control subdomain. At the continuous PDE level, we establish local exponential stabilization in the $L^2$-norm and suboptimality of the actuator-based RHC scheme for weak solutions. Direct implementation requires the repeated solution of high-dimensional finite-horizon optimal control problems. To reduce this computational cost, we combine RHC with model order reduction based on proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). A common POD space constructed from state snapshots reduces the state and adjoint equations and accelerates the online optimization, while the resulting controls are applied to the full-order discretized dynamics. Numerical experiments for two flow configurations of increasing complexity examine the influence of actuator layouts, prediction horizons, viscosity, and POD dimension. The numerical results demonstrate substantial reductions in computational cost while maintaining closed-loop stabilization in the tested configurations.

papers.title: Reconstruction of F-cohomological field theories on moduli of compact type
papers.abstract: We prove an analogue of Givental-Teleman reconstruction for F-cohomological field theories on the moduli space of compact type. We apply it to reconstruct the restriction of the extended $r$-spin classes to the extended direction and deduce relations between $κ$-classes (both in compact type).

papers.title: Large fringe trees for random trees with given vertex degrees
papers.abstract: This paper extends the study of fringe trees in random plane trees with a given degree statistic. While previous work established the asymptotic normality of the count of fringe trees isomorphic to a fixed tree, we investigate the case where the target tree grows with the size of the random tree. We consider three primary subtree counts: the number of fringe trees isomorphic to a specific growing tree, the number of fringe trees sharing a given growing degree statistic, and the number of fringe trees of a specific growing size. To establish our results, we employ and compare four distinct probabilistic frameworks: the method of moments with the Gao-Wormald theorem, Stein's method with coupling (to provide explicit error bounds in total variation distance), the Cai-Devroye method, and Stein's method with exchangeable pairs. Our findings provide conditions for Poisson and normal convergence for these subtree counts. Additionally, we provide a local limit theorem for sums of values obtained via sampling without replacement that may be of independent interest. Finally, our results and methods are also applied to conditioned critical Galton-Watson trees.

papers.title: Functoriality and the theta correspondence
papers.abstract: We study the functoriality of the local theta correspondence for classical $p$-adic groups. This is realized via the adaptation of the Adams conjecture to ABV-packets. We provide evidence for the conjecture, especially in the case of general linear groups.

papers.title: On the average-case complexity landscape for Tensor-Isomorphism-complete problems over finite fields
papers.abstract: In Grochow and Qiao (\emph{SIAM J. Comput.}, 2023), the complexity class Tensor Isomorphism (TI) was introduced and isomorphism problems for groups, algebras, and polynomials were shown to be TI-complete. In this paper, we study average-case algorithms for several TI-complete problems over finite fields, including algebra isomorphism, matrix code conjugacy, and $4$-tensor isomorphism. Our main results reveal a rich landscape of average-case complexities of Tensor Isomorphism problems, despite their equivalence in the worst-case setting. Over the finite field of order $q$, we devise (1) average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithms for algebra isomorphism and matrix code conjugacy that succeed for $1/Θ(q)$ fraction of inputs; (2) an average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithm for the $4$-tensor isomorphism that succeeds for $1/q^{Θ(1)}$ fraction of inputs; and (3) an average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithm for the orthogonal $3$-tensor isomorphism that succeed for $1-1/\poly(n)$ fraction of $n\times n\times n$ tensors. Our main technical contribution is to introduce the spectral properties of random matrices into algorithms for TI-complete problems. This leads to not only new algorithms but also new questions in random matrix theory over finite fields. To settle these questions, we need to extend both the generating function approach as in Neumann and Praeger (\emph{J. London Math. Soc.}, 1998) and the character sum method of Gorodetsky and Rodgers (\emph{Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.}, 2021).

papers.title: Towards European Hydrogen Market Design: Perspectives from Transmission System Operators
papers.abstract: Despite hydrogen being central to Europe's decarbonisation strategy, only a small share of renewable hydrogen projects reached final investment decision. A key barrier is uncertainty about how future hydrogen markets will be designed and operated, particularly under Renewable Fuels of Non-Biological Origin requirements. This study investigates the extent to which future hydrogen market design can be adapted from existing natural gas markets, and the challenges it must address. The analysis was based on a survey on future hydrogen market design targeting European gas transmission system operators, the stakeholder group responsible for operating the network and implementing the Network Codes. The survey provided an assessment of mechanism transferability and identified challenges for the early development of the hydrogen market. Core market design principles and trading frameworks are broadly transferable from natural gas markets, as entry-exit systems and virtual trading points. Capacity allocation requires targeted adaptation to improve coupling with electricity markets. Tariffs require adaptation through intertemporal cost allocation, distributing infrastructure costs over time to protect early adopters. Balancing regimes should be revisited to reflect hydrogen's physical characteristics and different linepack flexibility usages. Key challenges for early hydrogen markets include: temporal mismatches between variable renewable supply and expected relatively stable industrial demand, limited operational flexibility due to scarce storage and reduced pipeline linepack, fragmented regional hydrogen clusters, and regulatory uncertainty affecting long-term investment decisions. These findings provide empirical input to the hydrogen Network Codes and offer guidance to policymakers designing hydrogen market frameworks.

papers.title: Pruning for efficient deterministic global optimization over trained ReLU neural networks
papers.abstract: Neural networks are increasingly used as surrogates in optimization problems to replace computationally expensive models. However, embedding ReLU neural networks in mathematical programs introduces significant computational challenges, particularly for large networks. This work investigates how pruning techniques can accelerate the solution of optimization problems with embedded neural networks, focusing on the mechanisms underlying the computational gains. We show that, besides problem size reduction, both unstructured and structured pruning tightens preactivation bounds. We conduct a comprehensive empirical study spanning three morphologies and four complexity levels, comparing magnitude-based weight and node pruning with structured perspective regularization (SPR). We test on both an illustrative test function and a chemical process flowsheet surrogate, using a commercial and an open-source solver. Pruning consistently improves the accuracy-runtime trade-off, with speedups spanning one to four orders of magnitude depending on the complexity of the unpruned network. The gains are attributed to three factors: (i) reduction in problem size, (ii) decrease in the number of integer variables, and (iii) tightening of big-M bounds. Weight pruning and SPR occupy most of the accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier, the latter enabling faster convergence at the mildest sparsity considered. The mechanisms transfer from the test function to the engineering case study, although the preferred technique and sparsity level might vary with the case study, and should be selected as part of surrogate development.

papers.title: Terminal Fano 4-fold Hypersurfaces via Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We construct $46{,}992$ new families of Fano $4$-fold hypersurfaces $X_d\subset\mathbb(a_1,\ldots,a_6)$ of Fano index $1$ with $d>200$, whose general members have terminal singularities. Unlike the $11{,}617$ quasismooth families classified by Brown and Kasprzyk, these are nonquasismooth, for which determining terminality can require the analysis of hyperquotient singularities. An exhaustive search has classified all nonquasismooth families with $d\leq200$, but extending this classification to higher degrees becomes computationally prohibitive. We therefore exploit the sparsity and spatial clustering of terminal examples using two best-first searches over $\mathbb{Z}^6$: one with a fixed heuristic, and the other with a neural network trained online by deep reinforcement learning. Together, the searches reach degrees up to $3{,}234$. The neural network additionally discovers an average of $79$ hard-to-reach families per run. For the most isolated examples, our conservative distance-based model gives an estimated lower bound of nearly $40\%$ of the fixed search's total step budget to discover a single such family. An ablation study demonstrates that this advantage arises from the neural network rather than stochastic exploration alone. The complete list of families is publicly available.

papers.title: Edge-spectral supersaturation and stability: Resolving a problem on color-critical subgraphs
papers.abstract: Inspired by Mubayi's work on the supersaturation of color-critical subgraphs, we investigate its edge-spectral counterpart: determining the minimum number of copies of a color-critical subgraph in a graph whose spectral radius exceeds the corresponding extremal threshold. While earlier breakthroughs by Bollobás and Nikiforov, Ning and Zhai, and Li, Liu, and Zhang provided edge-spectral supersaturation results for the complete graph, the general problem for color-critical graphs has remained open. In this paper, we strengthen existing results by studying all color-critical graphs \(F\) with \(χ(F)=r+1\geq 4\). Specifically, we prove that if $ρ(G)\!>\!\sqrt{(1\!-\!1/r)2m}$, then the number of copies of \(F\) in \(G\) satisfies $N_F(G) \geq \bigl(γ_F-o(1)\bigr)m^{(|F|-2)/2},$ where both the order of magnitude and the leading constant \(γ_F\) are optimal. The above supersaturation statement is derived from a more general edge-spectral supersaturation and stability framework. Classically, a theorem of Erdős and Simonovits [Combinatorica, 1983] asserts that any $n$-vertex graph with edge density strictly exceeding the Turán density of $F$ must contain $Ω(n^{|F|})$ copies of $F$. By applying the progressive induction method to spectral extremal problems, we establish a comprehensive edge-spectral analogue of the Erdős--Simonovits theorem. Beyond obtaining the asymptotic upper bounds on the spectral radius $ρ(G)$ under the condition $N_F(G) = o(m^{|F|/2})$, we further establish a sharp stability result. Our work strengthens both the classical Erdős--Stone--Simonovits theorem and Nikiforov's spectral stability theorem by extending the setting from $F$-free graphs to graphs containing only a limited number of copies of $F$. We conclude with several open problems in spectral supersaturation.

papers.title: Clustering without geometry in sparse networks with independent edges
papers.abstract: The coexistence of sparsity and clustering (non-vanishing average fraction of triangles per node) is one of the few structural features that, irrespective of finer details, are ubiquitously observed across large real-world networks. This fact calls for generic models producing sparse clustered graphs. Earlier results suggested that sparse random graphs with independent edges fail to reproduce clustering, unless edge probabilities are assumed to depend on underlying metric distances that, thanks to the triangle inequality, naturally favour triadic closure. This observation has opened a debate on whether clustering implies (latent) geometry in real-world networks. Alternatively, recent models of higher-order networks can replicate clustering by abandoning edge independence. In this paper, we mathematically prove, and numerically confirm, that a sparse random graph with independent edges, recently identified in the context of network renormalization as an invariant model under node aggregation, produces finite clustering without any geometric or higher-order constraint. The underlying mechanism is an infinite-mean node fitness, which also implies a power-law degree distribution. Further, as a novel phenomenon that we characterize rigorously, we observe the breakdown of self-averaging of various network properties. Therefore, as an alternative to geometry or higher-order dependencies, node aggregation invariance emerges as a basic route to realistic network properties.

papers.title: The $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions of hyperelliptic curves: a generalization of Jacobi's elliptic functions and explicit solutions of a degenerate Krichever-Novikov equation
papers.abstract: The Jacobi elliptic functions $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{dn}$ and their ratios are expressed by Weierstrass's functions $\mathrm{al}_a=\sqrt{x-b_a}$ of an elliptic curve. For a hyperelliptic curve of genus $g$, Weierstrass's $\mathrm{al}_a$ functions generalize $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{cn}$ and $\mathrm{dn}$, and the modified Korteweg-de Vries and sine-Gordon equations stand behind them. In this paper we study the $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions, which are defined by the sigma function shifted by the sum of two half-periods and which, together with the ratios of the $\mathrm{al}_a$ functions, generalize the remaining Jacobi elliptic functions. We determine the exact lattice of periods of $\mathrm{al}_{12}$ and show that it is single-valued on the unramified double covering of the Jacobian corresponding to the double covering $\hat{w}^2=(x-b_1)(x-b_2)$ of the curve. We show that $\mathrm{al}_{12}$ is the Wronskian of the band-edge eigenfunctions $\mathrm{al}_1$ and $\mathrm{al}_2$, so that the half-period translations realize Darboux transformations. As the main result, $\mathrm{al}_{12}$, $\mathrm{al}_2/\mathrm{al}_1$ and $1/\mathrm{al}_{12}$ satisfy one and the same degenerate Krichever-Novikov equation, whose polynomial has the double roots $0$ and $\infty$, and the half-periods act on these solutions as the Möbius symmetries of the equation. Thus the Krichever-Novikov equation stands behind the $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions. In genus one these functions reduce to $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{ns}$ and $\mathrm{dc}$.

papers.title: On the de Rham flip-flopping in dual towers
papers.abstract: We prove a version of de Rham and Hyodo-Kato flip-flopping for dual towers of rigid analytic spaces including those coming from dual basic local Shimura varieties. The main tool are comparison theorems expressing the two cohomologies as pro-étale cohomology of corresponding relative period sheaves that, by definition, satisfy pro-étale descent. As an application, we show that de Rham and Hyodo-Kato cohomologies of finite level coverings of the Drinfeld space of any dimension $d$ over $K$ are admissible as representations of $\mathbb{GL}_{d+1}(K)$.

papers.title: The Pivotal Information Criterion
papers.abstract: The Bayesian and Akaike information criteria aim at finding a good balance between under- and over-fitting. They are extensively used every day by practitioners. Yet we contend they suffer from at least two afflictions: their penalty parameters $λ=\log n$ and $λ=2$ are too small, leading to many false discoveries, and their inherent (best subset) discrete optimization is infeasible in high dimension. We alleviate these issues with the pivotal information criterion: PIC is defined as a continuous optimization problem, and the PIC penalty parameter $λ$ is selected at the detection boundary (under pure noise). PIC's choice of $λ$ is an upper quantile of a statistic that we prove to be (asymptotically) pivotal, provided the loss function is appropriately transformed. As a result, simulations show a phase transition in the probability of exact support recovery with PIC, a phenomenon studied with no noise in compressed sensing. Applied to real data, for similar predictive performances, PIC selects the least complex model among state-of-the-art learners.

papers.title: Attainable forms of lower spectra
papers.abstract: Let $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\varphi\colon(0,1)\to[0,d]$. We prove there exists a set $F\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ whose lower spectrum $\operatorname{dim}^θ_{\mathrm{L}} F$ satisfies $(1-θ)\operatorname{dim}^θ_{\mathrm{L}} F = \varphi(θ)$ for all $θ\in(0,1)$ if and only if for all $λ,θ\in(0,1)$, \begin{equation*} \varphi(θ) \leq \varphi(λθ) - θ\varphi(λ) \leq (1-θ) d. \end{equation*} We also obtain a similar classification result for $\underline{\operatorname{dim}}^θ_{\mathrm{L}} F$. In contrast to the case for Assouad spectra, it is insufficient to consider homogeneous (or uniform) sets. Instead, we follow the approach introduced by Orgoványi--Rutar in arXiv:2510.07013 and proceed via a more general classification result for appropriate two-scale branching functions.

papers.title: On the non-uniformity of the 2026 FIFA World Cup draw
papers.abstract: The group stage of a sports tournament is often made more appealing by introducing additional constraints in the group draw that promote an attractive and balanced group composition. For example, the number of intra-regional group matches is minimised in several world championships. Under such constraints, the traditional draw procedure may become non-uniform, meaning that the feasible allocations of the teams into groups are not equally likely to occur. Our paper quantifies this non-uniformity of the 2026 FIFA World Cup draw for the official draw procedure, as well as for 47 reasonable alternatives implied by all permutations of the four pots and two group labelling policies. We show why simulating with a recursive backtracking algorithm is intractable, and propose a workable implementation using integer programming. The official draw mechanism is found to be optimal based on two of five non-uniformity measures, including the average distortion of the 771 non-zero assignment probabilities. Nonetheless, non-uniformity can be more than halved if the organiser aims to treat the best teams drawn from the first pot equally.

papers.title: Non-stationary normal coordinates on neighborhoods of Pesin stable manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct non-stationary normal coordinates in a neighborhood of Pesin stable manifolds \cite{Pesin}. This construction is a natural extension, via jets in the normal directions, of the non-stationary normal coordinates on stable manifolds introduced by Guysinsky and Katok. We emphasize that this extension provides a useful framework for describing the fractal geometric structures of stable and unstable foliations in smooth dynamical systems.

papers.title: On very weak solutions of certain elliptic systems with double phase growth
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a higher integrability result for very weak solutions of higher-order elliptic systems involving a double phase operator as the principal part. As a model case, we consider \begin{equation} \int_Ω \left( |D^m u|^{p-2}D^m u + a(x)|D^m u|^{q-2}D^m u \right) \cdot D^m \varphi = 0 \quad \text{for any } \varphi \in C_c^{\infty}(Ω), \end{equation} where $n,\,m \in \mathbb{N},\ n\ge 2,\,1 < p \le q < \infty,\,Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is an open set and $a:Ω\rightarrow [0,\infty)$ is a measurable function. We extend the result of Baasandorj, Byun and Kim (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2023) with respect to the derivative order, the coefficient class and the growth conditions. The proof is based on a construction of an appropriate test function by the Lipschitz truncation technique, a deduction of a reverse Hölder inequality and an application of Gehring's lemma. To this end, we establish estimates for weighted mean value polynomials and sharp Sobolev--Poincaré-type inequalities for the double phase operator.

papers.title: Path properties of Lévy driven mixed moving average processes
papers.abstract: We derive general sufficient conditions for the existence of càdlàg and continuous modifications of Lévy-driven mixed moving average processes. The conditions are explicit and easy to verify and applied to supOU, well-balanced supOU, trawl, and power-weighted supOU processes. In these examples, the conditions are shown to be close to optimal.

papers.title: Asymmetric conformal prediction with penalized kernel sum-of-squares
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) is a distribution-free method to construct reliable prediction intervals that has gained significant attention in recent years. Despite its success and various proposed extensions, a significant practical feature which has been overlooked in previous research is the potential skewed nature of the noise, or of the residuals when the predictive model exhibits bias. In this work, we leverage recent developments in CP to propose a new asymmetric procedure that bridges the gap between skewed and non-skewed noise distributions, while still maintaining adaptivity of the prediction intervals. We introduce a new statistical learning problem to construct adaptive and asymmetric prediction bands, with a unique feature based on a penalty which promotes symmetry: when its intensity varies, the intervals smoothly change from symmetric to asymmetric ones. This learning problem is based on reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and the recently introduced kernel sum-of-squares framework. First, we establish representer theorems to make our problem tractable in practice, and derive dual formulations which are essential for scalability to larger datasets. Second, the intensity of the penalty is chosen using a novel data-driven method which automatically identifies the symmetric nature of the noise. We show that consenting to some asymmetry can let the learned prediction bands better adapt to small sample regimes or biased predictive models.

papers.title: Exact Gaussian Moment Matching for Residual Networks: a Second-Order Method
papers.abstract: We study the problem of propagating the mean and covariance of a general multivariate Gaussian distribution through a deep (residual) neural network using layer-by-layer moment matching. We close a longstanding gap by deriving exact moment matching for the probit, GeLU, ReLU (as a limit of GeLU), Heaviside (as a limit of probit), and sine activation functions; for both feedforward and generalized residual layers. On large-variance random networks, median KL-divergence improvements over common baselines range from tens to thousands of times. On a variational Bayes neural network, we show that our method improves upon a state-of-the-art deterministic inference method by an order of magnitude in KL divergence from Monte Carlo ground truth. We also give a smooth-distance error bound showing that, under regularity assumptions, moment matching removes the leading low-variance errors and propagates higher-order local accuracy through the layers of a network.

papers.title: Asymptotically Strong Dual of Smooth Nonconvex Problems: A Smooth Shapley-Folkman Perspective
papers.abstract: In convex geometry, the Shapley-Folkman Lemma asserts that the nonconvexity of a Minkowski sum of $n$ dimensional bounded nonconvex sets does not accumulate once the number of summands exceeds the dimension $n$, and thus the sum becomes approximately convex. Originally published by Starr in the context of quasi-equilibrium in nonconvex market models in economics, the lemma has since found widespread use in optimization, particularly for estimating the duality gap of the Lagrangian dual of separable nonconvex problems. Given its foundational nature, we pose the following geometric question: Is it possible for the nonconvexity of the Minkowski sum of $n$-dimensional nonconvex sets to even diminish instead of just not accumulating as the number of summands increases, under some general conditions? We answer this affirmatively. First, we provide an elementary geometric proof of the Shapley-Folkman Lemma based on the facial structure of the convex hull of each set. This leads to refinement of the classical error bound derived from the lemma. Building on this new geometric perspective, we further show that when most of the sets satisfy a certain local smoothness condition which naturally arises in the epigraphs of smooth functions, their Minkowski sum converges directly to a convex set, with a vanishing nonconvexity measure. In optimization, this implies that the Lagrangian dual of block-structured smooth nonconvex problems with potentially additional sparsity constraints is asymptotically tight under mild assumptions, which contracts nonvanishing duality gap obtained via classical Shapley-Folkman Lemma.

papers.title: Spectral extrema on closed surfaces of fixed Euler genus
papers.abstract: We investigate a classical extremal problem in combinatorics and topological graph theory: determining the maximum spectral radius $spex(n,γ)$ of all $n$-vertex graphs embeddable on a closed surface of Euler genus $γ$. Building on seminal contributions by Boots and Royle, Cao and Vince, and Hong in the 1990s; Ellingham and Zha in 2000; Dvořák and Mohar in 2010; Tait and Tobin in 2017; and Liu, Ning, and Wang in 2026, we provide a complete characterization of spectral extremal graphs for any fixed Euler genus $γ$ and all sufficiently large $n$. The extremal graph attaining $\operatorname{spex}(n,γ)$ is unique, necessarily edge-extremal, and, roughly speaking, is constructed from the join $K_2 \nabla P_{n-2}$ by adding exactly $3γ$ edges. As a consequence, we derive asymptotically tight estimates for $\operatorname{spex}(n,γ)$, strengthening a classical bound due to Ellingham and Zha [J. Combin. Theory B, 2000]. We further characterize the extremal structures for the projective plane and torus, sharpening earlier bounds of Hong [J. Combin. Theory B, 1995]. For the planar case, we establish an explicit vertex threshold of $4.5\times 10^6$ for the Tait--Tobin theorem. Our approach combines extremal constructions of cellular embeddings, topological edge-switching techniques, and walk-counting estimates for large-scale substructures, revealing a bridge between spectral extremality and surface topology.

papers.title: Sharp quantitative Llarull's theorem and scalar-curvature rigidity with boundary
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp quantitative extension of Llarull's theorem to complete noncompact spin manifolds. Let $Φ:M\to\mathbf S^m$ be an area-decreasing map of nonzero degree that is locally constant at infinity, and assume that $\operatorname{scal}_{g_M}\geq m(m-1)$ on $\operatorname{supp}(dΦ)$. If $λ_1(M,g_M)=0$, then $\inf_M\operatorname{scal}_{g_M}<0$; if $λ_1(M,g_M)>0$, then \[ \inf_M\operatorname{scal}_{g_M}\leq -\frac{4m}{m-1}λ_1(M,g_M). \] The coefficient is sharp in every dimension, as shown by an explicit family of warped metrics. We also prove a boundary analogue under the same support-localized scalar-curvature hypothesis, without requiring the strict scalar-curvature positivity condition near the boundary used in Liu--Liu's doubling argument. Applications include a Geroch-type obstruction for connected sums with compact area-enlargeable manifolds and a Ricci-flat splitting theorem for complete metrics with nonnegative scalar curvature and mean-convex boundary.

papers.title: Non-linear traces of Choquet type on AF algebras
papers.abstract: We study non-linear traces of Choquet type on unital AF algebras. Building on the matrix-algebra theory of Nagisa--Watatani and the UHF setting considered by Sogame, we first establish the corresponding description for finite direct sums of matrix algebras and then pass to arbitrary unital AF algebras. We prove that the cone of Choquet traces on an AF algebra $A$ is isomorphic, as an ordered cone, to the cone of increasing maps $α:Γ(A)\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $α(0)=0$. On each finite-dimensional stage, the associated trace is given by an explicit Choquet formula involving spectral values and the classes of spectral projections.

papers.title: Optimal estimation of generalized causal effects in cluster-randomized trials with multiple outcomes
papers.abstract: Cluster-randomized trials (CRTs) are used to evaluate group-level interventions and can collect multiple outcomes capturing complementary dimensions of benefit and risk. Investigators typically seek a single global summary of treatment effect, yet existing methods largely focus on single-outcome estimands or rely on model-based procedures with unclear causal interpretation or limited robustness. We develop a unified potential outcomes framework for generalized treatment effects with multiple outcomes in CRTs, accommodating both non-prioritized and prioritized outcome settings. The proposed cluster-pair and individual-pair causal estimands are defined through pairwise contrast functions and explicitly account for informative cluster size. We establish nonparametric estimation via weighted clustered U-statistics and derive efficient influence functions to construct covariate-adjusted estimators that integrate debiased machine learning with U-statistics. The resulting estimators are consistent and asymptotically normal, attain semiparametric efficiency bounds under mild regularity conditions, and admit analytically tractable variance estimators that are consistent under cross-fitting. Simulations and an application to a CRT for chronic pain management illustrate the practical utility of our proposed methods.

papers.title: Quantification of Tail-trimming Effects for Interval CVaR Based Nonlinear Regression
papers.abstract: The tail trimming strategy is widely adopted for robustness against outlier contamination in statistical learning and operations research. However, it generally lacks the thorough understanding that to what extent the tail-trimming technique is effective for nonlinear regression. In this paper, we address the robust nonlinear regression based on the so-called interval conditional value-at-risk (In-CVaR), which is introduced to guard against outliers by trimming extreme losses. We first analyze the trimming effect of the In-CVaR based estimator under distributional perturbation. Our first finding is that the In-CVaR based estimator is qualitatively robust under distributional perturbation in terms of the Prokhorov metric if and only if the largest portion of losses is trimmed. Furthermore, under sample contamination, we derive a probably approximately correct (PAC) bound for the In-CVaR based estimator, showing that the preliminary covariate filtering that is customary in the literature is not needed for In-CVaR based regression. The nonconvexity of the In-CVaR objective, together with unboundedness of covariates, responses and parameter space create the technical challenges for our developed theory, and thus necessitate the new treatment of the qualitative robustness and PAC analysis. Overall, this study rigorously analyzes robustness properties of In-CVaR based nonlinear regression models, which illustrates to what extent the right tail-trimming of the loss by In-CVaR risk measure is essential and effective for robust nonlinear regression. These theoretical findings are further supported by numerical experiments.

papers.title: A boundary example for the Volterra decomposition of arithmetic error terms
papers.abstract: Let phi(n) denote the Euler totient function. We study the analytic part associated with the summatory function of sigma_1(n) and obtain explicit bounds under the Riemann Hypothesis. In particular, we establish an upper bound of order x^{delta'} exp((log x)/(log log x)), where delta' = max(1/2, delta).

papers.title: The 2-systole on compact Kähler surfaces with positive scalar curvature
papers.abstract: We study the 2-systole on compact Kähler surfaces of positive scalar curvature. For any such surface $(X,ω)$, we prove the sharp estimate $\min_X S(ω)\cdot\operatorname{sys}_2(ω)\le12π$, with equality if and only if $X=\mathbb P^2$ and $ω$ is the Fubini--Study metric. Using the classification of positive scalar curvature Kähler surfaces, we determine the optimal constant in the case that $X$ is rational or non-rational and describe the corresponding rigid models. When $X$ is a non-rational ruled surface, we also give an independent analytic proof, adapting Stern's level set method to the holomorphic fibration in the Kähler setting.

papers.title: Hierarchical filtrations of vector bundles and birational geometry
papers.abstract: We study chains of locally free subsheaves of equal rank whose successive quotients are nonzero divisorial torsion sheaves. Fixing the determinant of the initial term defines a normalized hierarchical depth. An ample intersection argument proves finiteness on every smooth projective variety. On an algebraically closed smooth projective curve, the depth equals the degree of the determinant difference precisely when that difference is effective; otherwise, no normalized filtration exists. For birational morphisms of smooth projective surfaces, reflexive pushforward contracts exactly those steps whose determinant divisors are entirely exceptional. This yields a comparison of filtration lengths without a commutativity assumption. Explicit examples show that pullback can strictly increase depth and compute a depth of twenty on a two-point blowup. Finally, we distinguish preservation of evaluation codes for genuinely descended bundles from removal of zero coordinates caused by exceptional fixed components. The coding statements use specified compatible fiber bases or the block Hamming metric.

papers.title: Convergence rate of $\ell^p$-relaxation on a graph to a $p$-harmonic function with given boundary values
papers.abstract: We study asynchronous $\ell^p$-energy minimization on finite connected graphs with prescribed boundary values. At each step, a uniformly chosen interior vertex updates its value to minimize the local energy. For initial values in $[0,1]$, we bound the expected time to approach the $p$-harmonic extension within $ε$ in supremum norm, for $0<ε\le1/2$. On graphs with $n$ vertices, the bound is $C_p n^{β_p}ε^{-(2-p)/(p-1)}$ for $1<p<2$ and $C_p n^{β_p}\log(n/ε)$ for $p\ge2$, where $C_p$ depends only on $p$ and $β_p=\max\{2p/(p-1),3\}$. Bounds incorporating average degree are jointly sharp in graph size, degree, and accuracy for $1<p<2$; for $p\ge2$, lower bounds match the polynomial dependence on size and degree at fixed accuracy. We also establish corresponding synchronous bounds and graph-dependent estimates for $p=2$.

papers.title: Recovering Geodesic Distances from Noisy Observations
papers.abstract: Let $(M,d,μ)$ be a nice geodesic probability space (such as a manifold) and $X=\{x_i\}_{i\in [N]} \subset M$ a finite $μ$-i.i.d. sample. Suppose we observe noisy distance random variables $d'(x_i,x_j)$. When can the true distances be recovered to small additive error? This question has attracted interest in two disparate fields: latent-space graph models and boundary-value inverse problems. We first show that, taking $N \asymp ε^{-2d-2}|\logε|$ and using runtime $O(N^{2.5+o_d (1)})$, we can recover all distances in $X$ to additive error $O(ε|\logε|)$ with high probability, assuming $\mathbb{E} d'(x_i, x_j) = F(d(x_i,x_j))$ for an unknown, increasing bilipschitz $F$ and with the $d'(x_i,x_j)$ allowed to be arbitrarily heterogeneous in their distribution as long as they are bounded in subgaussian norm. This generalizes existing work, which required $F$ to be known and made strict assumptions on the distribution of $d'(x_i, x_j)$. Achieving this generalization required a novel ``ruler-building'' procedure to learn $F$. We extend our results to a missing data case where we randomly lose access to noisy distances. Our second result uses ideas from the first to tackle a partial observability case: $X = Y \cup Z$ with $Z$ sampled from $M$ and $Y$ sampled from an observer subset satisfying visibility conditions that model the assumptions made on the boundary in boundary-value inverse problems. In this setting, we recover all pairwise distances in $Z$ to additive error $O(ε)$ with $|Z| \asymp ε^{-2d-2}|\logε|$, $|Y| \asymp ε^{-\max\{d_ν,4\}}$ with $d_ν$ determined by the volume-growth properties of the probability measure on the observer set, and runtime $O(|Z|^3)$. This is, to our knowledge, the first quantitative guarantee for this observer/observed split under noise, which complements existing stability results for boundary data.

papers.title: On Spectral Clustering in Algebraic Multigrid Methods
papers.abstract: We introduce a new direct multilevel method for solving general nonsingular complex square linear systems admitting a suitable block partition, using a regular smoother and an arbitrary but equal number of pre- and post-smoothings. Through careful analysis of the error propagation operator, we cluster the spectrum of this operator. This allows us to write a direct K-cycle version of the method.

papers.title: Verifying spiral minimal product structure through the Takahashi Theorem
papers.abstract: We verify the spiral minimal product structure through the Takahashi Theorem with full computational details which were omitted in [LZ].

papers.title: Gaussian Approximation for High-Dimensional Weighted and Two-Sample $U$-statistics with Size-Dependent Kernels
papers.abstract: We develop Gaussian approximations for high-dimensional vectors formed by second-order $U$-and $V$-statistics whose kernels depend on sample size. To accommodate weighted and two-sample $U$-and $V$-statistics within a unified framework, we establish our results under independent but not identically distributed (i.n.i.d.) sampling. The resulting theorems apply to a broad range of problems, including estimation in linear regression models with many covariates or many-weak instruments, variance component analysis, smoothed two-sample testing, and inference for separately exchangeable arrays, among others. Our results do not require either component of the Hoeffding decomposition to dominate, thereby covering both non-degenerate and degenerate regimes. In addition, we develop maximal inequalities for high-dimensional $U$-statistics with size-dependent kernels under the i.n.i.d.~setting, in a form that remains sharp across a broad range of applications, which may be of independent interest. Finally, applications to estimation and testing with many weak instrumental variables demonstrate that, our results are sharp enough to recover the corresponding fixed-dimensional rate conditions up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: A mathematical study of the excess growth rate
papers.abstract: The excess growth rate, defined as the gap in Jensen's inequality for the logarithm, is a fundamental functional in portfolio theory. In this paper, we present a mathematical study motivated by information theory. We begin by establishing its properties and showing that it has rich connections with information-theoretic concepts such as the Helmholtz free energy, L. Campbell's measure of average code length and large deviations. Our main results consist of three axiomatic characterization theorems of the excess growth rate, in terms of (i) the relative entropy, (ii) the gap in Jensen's inequality, and (iii) the logarithmic divergence that generalizes the Bregman divergence. Furthermore, we study maximization of the excess growth rate and compare it with Kelly's growth optimal portfolio. Our results not only provide theoretical justifications of the significance of the excess growth rate, but also establish new connections between information theory and quantitative finance.

papers.title: MAGDrop: Momentum Adaptive Gradient Dropout With Provable Generalization Guarantees
papers.abstract: Standard dropout applies a fixed, uniform noise rate to all units, ignoring available gradient information. We propose momentum adaptive gradient dropout (MAGDrop), a Bayesian linear layer that adapts per-unit weight noise by tracking an exponential moving average of gradient magnitudes. Units with large recent gradient magnitudes receive less noise to preserve learned features; units with below-average gradient magnitudes receive more noise to promote exploration. This adaptation transforms the classifier head into a data-dependent Bayesian predictor whose mean predictor has no additional inference cost. Our primary contribution is a certificate-aware low-rank posterior, MAGDrop-Subspace, that addresses the tension between strong accuracy and tight bounds from probably approximately correct (PAC)-Bayes theory. A full-head stochastic posterior incurs a Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence of approximately 8,625 nats. By confining the posterior to an $r$-dimensional subspace constructed from an independent prior-construction sample $S_0$ and certifying on an independent sample $S$ with $S_0\perp S$, MAGDrop-Subspace reduces KL by approximately a factor of 800 while keeping accuracy close to the baseline. On CIFAR-10 with a 13-layer convolutional neural network and $r=50$, MAGDrop-Subspace achieves a PAC-Bayes Gibbs-risk bound of 0.1882 at 90\% confidence using binary KL inversion, compared with 0.4439 for the full-head baseline. Mean-predictor accuracy is 82.31\%, compared with 83.74\% for the baseline. Complementary accuracy experiments on ImageNet-1K show that MAGDrop reaches top-1 accuracy similar to the strong baseline: 78.57\% compared with 78.51\% on the base Vision Transformer with $16\times16$ patches, and 82.14\% compared with 82.23\% on ConvNeXt-Base.

papers.title: Cohomology of vector bundles on the moduli space of parabolic connections on $\mathbb{P}^1$ minus $5$ points
papers.abstract: We study the moduli space of parabolic connections of rank two on the complex projective line $\mathbb{P}^1$ minus five points with fixed spectral data. We prove a cohomological vanishing theorem for tensor products of four natural vector bundles on the moduli stack of $ν$-${\mathfrak sl}_2$-parabolic connections. We also compute the cohomology of the structure sheaf and give an explicit geometric description of a compactification of this moduli space, using $ε$-connections and the birational geometry of $\mathbb{P}^2 \times (\mathbb{P}^2)^{\vee}$. As an application, we construct a universal family of twisted $D$-modules whose fibers satisfy an orthogonality property over a dense open subset. These results are motivated by Arinkin's approach to the tamely ramified geometric Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: Variational formulae for entropy-like functionals for states in von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: The paper presents variational formulae for entropy-like functionals, including Segal and Rényi entropies, for normal states on semifinite von Neumann algebras. The considered functionals are of the form $τ(f(h))$ where $τ$ is a normal faithful semifinite trace on this algebra, $h$ is a positive selfadjoint operator from $L^1(\mathscr{M},τ)$, and $f$ is an appropriate convex or concave function. The results cover both finite and semifinite algebras, and the obtained formulae generalise known results, in particular, those concerning relative entropy. Moreover, the connection between quantum entropies and the structure of abelian subalgebras is highlighted, providing new interpretations in the context of quantum information theory.

papers.title: Distribution of mixed character sums and extremal problems for Littlewood polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove distributional results for mixed character sums \begin{equation*}\sum_{n\le x }χ(n)e(nθ),\end{equation*} for fixed $θ\in [0,1]$ and random character $χ\pmod q$, as well as for a fixed character $χ$ and randomly sampled $θ\in [0,1].$ We present various applications of our results. For example, we construct Littlewood polynomials with large Mahler measure and $L_1$ norm, thus establishing new records in the Mahler and Newman problems. We also prove asymptotics for the $L_{2k}$ norms of well-known Turyn polynomials as $k\to\infty$, refuting a conjecture of Günther and Schmidt. An important ingredient in our work is a general way of dealing with "log-integrability" problems.

papers.title: On the Orthogonal Projections
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional algebra and $e$ a rigid presentation. We give an explicit formula for the left adjoint to the inclusion $\operatorname{rep}(e^\perp)\hookrightarrow \operatorname{rep}(A)$ and construct a bijection between presentations in $\operatorname{rep}(e^\perp)$ and presentations compatible with $e$. The induced bijection on weights preserves generic $\operatorname{E}$-invariants and canonical decompositions. If $A$ is Jacobian, the reduction algebra is Jacobian for every rigid $e$. We prove mutation formulas for the signed completions and for the dimension vectors of the simple objects of $\operatorname{rep}(e^\perp)$, enabling an algorithm to find the projected quiver with potential when $e$ is extended-reachable. Additionally, we introduce a modified projection for quivers with potentials that preserves general presentations. For applications to cluster algebras, we establish a connection to the stabilization functors.

papers.title: How deep is your network? Deep vs. shallow learning of transfer operators
papers.abstract: We introduce RaNNDy, a randomized neural network framework for learning transfer operators and their spectral decompositions. By fixing the weights of the hidden layers and training only the output layer, RaNNDy achieves significant reductions in computational costs -- often by two orders of magnitude -- with similar accuracy compared to state-of-the-art deep learning methods. The method is less sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and provides a closed-form solution for the output layer weights that directly represent eigenfunctions of the learned operator. Moreover, it is possible to estimate uncertainties associated with the computed spectral properties via ensemble learning. We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach using diverse benchmark problems, including stochastic dynamical systems and protein folding processes, highlighting the strengths but also weaknesses of RaNNDy.

papers.title: Elementary Real Analysis
papers.abstract: Preliminary version of a book on univariate real analysis, with 19 chapters and 6 appendices. 1. Prologue on functions and relations; 2. From ZFC formulas to natural numbers; 3. From natural numbers to integers; 4. From integers to fractions; 5. From fractions to extended reals; 6. From extended reals to real numbers; 7. Limits of real sequences; 8. Infinite series; 9. Limits of real functions. 10. Elementary functions; 11. Continuous functions; 12. Derivatives; 13. Mean value theorems; 14. Taylor polynomials; 15. Real analytic functions; 16. Newton integral; 17. Riemann integral; 18. Henstock-Kurzweil integral; 19. Applications of integrals; A. ZFC set theory; B. The equiconsistence of AC: Gödel; C. The equiconsistence of $\neg$AC: Cohen; D. From real numbers to complex numbers; E. Metric spaces; F. Solutions to exercises

papers.title: On the extremal functions of second order uncertainty principles: symmetry and symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: This paper focus on the symmetry and symmetry breaking about the second order Hydrogen Uncertainty Principle. \emph{Firstly}, by choosing a suitable test function, we give a negative answer to the conjecture presented by Cazacu, Flynn and Lam in [\emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{283} (2022), Paper No. 109659, 37 pp] for $N\in\{2,3\}$, and emphasizing the symmetry breaking phenomenon. \emph{Secondly}, we obtain a family of sharp weighted second order Hydrogen Uncertainty Principle, and prove the extremal functions are radial, which extends the work of Duong and Nguyen [The sharp second order Caffareli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality and stability estimates for the sharp second order uncertainty principle, arXiv:2102.01425].

papers.title: NP-Hardness and Additive Inapproximability of Deterministic Communication Complexity
papers.abstract: Given the full truth table of a Boolean function whose input is split between two players, we study the complexity of determining the minimum worst-case number of bits they must communicate to compute it. This is a basic meta-complexity question, posed by Yao in 1979. We prove NP-hardness of approximation within every fixed additive error for deterministic communication complexity, under deterministic polynomial-time reductions. The result holds both in the standard model and in Yao's original model, where the players alternate after every bit and only the receiver of the last bit must determine the answer. In particular, it resolves the exact computation question under Yao's original conventions. Earlier versions of this same paper established exact NP-hardness for the standard model, independently and concurrently with Hirahara, Ilango, and Loff. In both models, a polynomial-time estimator with any fixed additive error would yield a polynomial-time $3$-SAT algorithm, deterministic or bounded-error randomized according to the estimator. For the standard model, we also give quantitative implications for errors that grow with the number $T$ of table entries. A bounded-error randomized polynomial-time estimator with additive error $c\log T/\log\log T$, for any fixed $0\le c<1/8$, yields a bounded-error randomized $3$-SAT algorithm on $N$ variables and $O(N)$ clauses running in time $2^{O(N^α)}$ for every fixed $8c<α<1$. A deterministic polynomial-time estimator with additive error $c_*\log\log T$, for an effective absolute constant $c_*>0$, yields a deterministic algorithm running in time $2^{O((\log N)^2)}$ on such formulas.

papers.title: A lecture note on covering theory in representation theory of algebras
papers.abstract: Covering theory is an important tool in representation theory of algebras, however, the results and the proofs are scattered in the literature. We give an introduction to covering theory at a level as elementary as possible and in a more general way on some basic notions than the existing literature does.

papers.title: Unified Toolbox for Multipartite Entanglement Certification
papers.abstract: We present a unified framework for multipartite entanglement characterization based on the conditional gradient (CG) method, incorporating both fast heuristic detection and rigorous witness construction with numerical error control. Our method enables entanglement certification in quantum systems of up to ten qubits and applies to arbitrary entanglement structures. We demonstrate its power by closing the gap between entanglement and separability bounds in white-noise robustness benchmarks for a class of bound entangled states. Furthermore, the framework extends to entanglement robustness under general quantum noise channels, providing accurate thresholds in cases beyond the reach of previous algorithmic methods. These results position CG methods as a powerful tool for practical and scalable entanglement analysis in realistic experimental settings.

papers.title: Density of finitely supported invariant measures for automorphisms of compact abelian groups
papers.abstract: We study the structure of invariant measures for continuous automorphisms of compact metrizable abelian groups satisfying the descending chain condition. We show that the finitely supported invariant measures are weak-* dense in the space of all invariant probability measures, and that if the system is ergodic with respect to Haar measure, then the finitely supported ergodic invariant measures are also dense. A key ingredient in the proof is a variant of the specification property, which we establish for the ergodic systems in this class. Our results also yield the following two consequences: first, that every finitely generated group that is a semidirect product of $\mathbb{Z}$ with a countable abelian group $G$ is Hilbert-Schmidt stable; and second, a Livshitz-type theorem characterizing the uniform closure of coboundaries arising from continuous functions in terms of vanishing on periodic orbits. We also construct an example showing that, in general dynamical systems, the property of having dense finitely supported invariant measures does not pass to product systems.

papers.title: On a fuzzy Landau Equation: II. Solvability results
papers.abstract: This article is the second in a series of works on the fuzzy Landau equation, which describes particles interacting through delocalised Coulomb-type collisions. The spatial interaction is modulated by a kernel. We establish the existence of global-in-time H-solutions for exponentially decaying spatial kernels on the whole space and for kernels bounded above and below by positive constants, including periodised kernels on the torus. For the latter class, we further study the propagation of velocity moments and $L^p$-bounds.

papers.title: The superposition principle for the continuity equation with singular flux
papers.abstract: Representation results for absolutely continuous curves $μ:[0,T]\to \mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $p>1$, with values in the Wasserstein space $(\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d),W_p)$ of Borel probability measures in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite $p$-moment, provide a crucial tool to study evolutionary PDEs in a measure-theoretic setting. They are strictly related to the superposition principle for measure-valued solutions to the continuity equation. This paper addresses the extension of these results to the case $p=1$, and to curves $μ:[0,+\infty)\to\mathcal{P}_1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that are only of bounded variation in time: in the corresponding continuity equation, the flux measure $ν\in\mathcal{M}_{loc}([0,+\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^{d};\mathbb{R}^{d})$ thus possesses a non-trivial singular part w.r.t. $μ$ in addition to the absolutely continuous part featuring the velocity field. Firstly, we carefully address the relation between curves in ${\rm BV}_{loc}([0,+\infty);\mathcal{P}_1(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and solutions to the associated continuity equation, among which we select those with minimal singular (contribution to the) flux $ν$. We show that, with those distinguished solutions it is possible to associate an `auxiliary' continuity equation, in an augmented phase space, solely driven by its velocity field. For that continuity equation, a standard version of the superposition principle can be thus obtained. In this way, we derive a first probabilistic representation of the pair $(μ,ν)$ solutions by projection over the time and space marginals. This representation involves Lipschitz trajectories in the augmented phase space, reparametrized in time and solving the characteristic system of ODEs. Finally, for the same pair $(μ,ν)$ we also prove a superposition principle in terms of BV curves on the actual time interval, providing a fine description of their behaviour at jump points.

papers.title: Extracting Dual Analytic Geometries of Linear Transformations to Achieve Efficient Computation
papers.abstract: We generalize the Calderon-Zygmund methodology for operator analysis and the Rokhlin-Greengard fast multipole algorithms, in which the domain and range of an operator are jointly organized. Our methods analyze unstructured kernels by uncovering the joint hidden geometries of their domain and range. The main tool is the Questionnaire algorithm, an iterative procedure that constructs adaptive bi-hierarchical partition trees that reveal latent multiscale organization and local low-rank structure in the kernel. When the geometry is unknown, the iteration starts from any initial affinity, even a random one, and, with a stochastic flip perturbation and a spectral space-filling curve that fixes the left-right order of every tree, reorganizes the matrix into an image of the operator's "phase space": the joint space of its sources and sensors, in duality, as positions and frequencies are for the Fourier transform. This ordering gives the phase space an analytic structure on which any classical transform can be carried out; the resulting compression is direct evidence of that structure. Guided by these geometries, we obtain efficient factorizations and fast matrix-vector products in two ways: (1) the Butterfly algorithm, which exploits the learned bi-hierarchical localized low-rank structure; and (2) the adaptive eGHWT, which selects best tilings in space and sequency from all levels of generalized Haar-Walsh wavelet packets. We call the resulting algorithms the Questionnaire Factorization and Fast Transform (QFFT). Unlike classical approaches requiring prior knowledge of the geometry, QFFT is fully data-driven and applies to matrices from irregular or unknown distributions. We demonstrate it on heterogeneous oscillatory operators and on orthogonal eigenvector expansions with high multiplicity and random sampling, reducing storage from O(N^2) to O(N log N) and enabling fast, scalable computation.

papers.title: On the stationary Navier-Stokes equations in distorted pipes under energy-stable outflow boundary conditions
papers.abstract: The steady motion of a viscous incompressible fluid in distorted pipes, of finite length, is modeled through the Navier-Stokes equations with mixed boundary conditions: the inflow is given by an arbitrary member of the Lions-Magenes class with positive influx, and the fluid motion is subject to a directional do-nothing boundary condition on the outlet, together with the standard no-slip assumption on the remaining walls of the domain. Existence of a weak solution to such Navier-Stokes system is proved without any restriction on the data (that is, inlet velocity and external force) by means of the Leray-Schauder Principle, in which the required a priori estimate is obtained by a contradiction argument that employs Bernoulli's law for solutions of the stationary Euler equations, as well as some properties of harmonic divergence-free vector fields. Under a suitable smallness assumption on the data, we also prove the unique solvability of the boundary-value problem.

papers.title: Categorical foundations of discrete dynamical systems
papers.abstract: We develop categorical foundations of discrete dynamical systems, aimed at understanding how the structure of the system affects its dynamics. We introduce the notion of cycle sets to analyze attractors of a system, and use this to generalize multiple decomposition theorems of Kadelka, Veliz-Cuba, Murrugarra, and the last two authors from Boolean networks to arbitrary discrete dynamical systems.

papers.title: On the Dynamics of Invariant Graphs for Dissipative Twist Maps
papers.abstract: We study the persistence and internal dynamics of invariant graphs for dissipative twist maps. Explicit $C^1$ persistence and parameter estimates allow every real rotation number to be realized by varying either translation parameter, while arbitrarily small zero-mean analytic perturbations at fixed irrational horizontal parameters can yield analytic graphs with dynamics conjugate to rational rotations. With a fixed Brjuno horizontal parameter and fixed-strip analyticity, normally attracting $C^r$ graphs persist under perturbations of size $(1-λ)^γ$, for any $γ>0$ and prescribed finite $r$, as $λ\to1^-$. At the critical Lipschitz bound, the invariant graphs can carry Denjoy dynamics and have countably many nondifferentiable points, with perturbations smooth outside a null Cantor set and tending to zero in every Hölder norm of order less than one.

papers.title: Bounded Discrete Bridges
papers.abstract: In 2010 Banderier and Nicodeme consider the height of bounded discrete bridges and conclude to a limiting Rayleigh distribution. This result is correct although their proof is partly erroneous. They make asymptotic simplifications based upon dominance properties of the roots of the kernel of the walk within a disk centered at the origin, but these dominance properties apply only upon a positive real segment. However the very good agreement of simulations with their asymptotic expansion of the probability distribution in case of Łukasiewicz bridges let us think that their proof could be corrected. This is the scope of the present article which provides a proof using the dominance property only in its domain of validity. We also consider the case of periodic walks, a topic not considered in Banderier-Nicodeme2010..

papers.title: Scalable and adaptive prediction bands with kernel sum-of-squares
papers.abstract: Conformal Prediction (CP) is a popular framework for constructing prediction bands with valid coverage in finite samples, while being free of any distributional assumption. A well-known limitation of conformal prediction is the lack of adaptivity, although several works introduced practically efficient alternate procedures. In this work, we build upon recent ideas that rely on recasting the CP problem as a statistical learning problem, directly targeting coverage and adaptivity. This statistical learning problem is based on reproducible kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS) and kernel sum-of-squares (SoS) methods. First, we extend previous results with a general representer theorem and exhibit the dual formulation of the learning problem. Crucially, such dual formulation can be solved efficiently by accelerated gradient methods with several hundreds or thousands of samples, unlike previous strategies based on off-the-shelf semidefinite programming algorithms. Second, we introduce a new hyperparameter tuning strategy tailored specifically to target adaptivity through bounds on test-conditional coverage. This strategy, based on the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC), is introduced here to tune kernel lengthscales in our framework, but has broader applicability since it could be used in any CP algorithm where the score function is learned. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted to show how our method compares to related work. All figures can be reproduced with the accompanying code at \href{https://www.gitlab.com/drti/ksos-bands}{gitlab.com/drti/ksos-bands}.

papers.title: Riemannian EXTRA: Communication-efficient decentralized optimization over compact submanifolds with data heterogeneity
papers.abstract: We consider decentralized optimization over a compact Riemannian submanifold in a network of $n$ nodes, where each node $i$ owns a smooth nonconvex local objective $f_i$ defined by its private data, and the goal is to minimize the global objective $F(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)$ using only local communications. A naive Riemannian extension of EXTRA leaves the auxiliary normal-space error uncontrolled and does not inherit the Euclidean convergence guarantees. We develop projection-based Riemannian EXTRA (REXTRA) and a retraction-based counterpart that incorporate a normal correction into both the communicated variable and the auxiliary update, while using only one local-variable-sized message per optimization iteration. By jointly controlling consensus, tangent, and normal errors, our analysis interprets the update as a network-based Riemannian inexact-gradient step. For projection-based REXTRA, a sufficiently small constant stepsize and a local initialization yield vanishing consensus, stationary accumulation points, and an $\mathcal O(1/k)$ best-iterate stationarity--consensus bound. For the retraction-based method, we prove that its difference from the projection update is uniformly second order and establish the same convergence properties and rate under a local initialization. Numerical experiments on representative manifold-valued learning tasks demonstrate the communication efficiency of the REXTRA updates.

papers.title: On the $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator on higher-dimensional almost Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce $\mathcal{D}^+_J$, a generalization of $\partial\bar{\partial}$ operator on higher dimensional almost Kähler manifolds. Using the $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator, we investigate the $\bar{\partial}$-problem in almost Kähler geometry and explore the generalized Monge-Ampère equation on almost Kähler manifolds. We establish uniqueness up to an additive constant. We also prove a local existence theorem for this equation on almost Kähler four-manifold. At last, we find an elliptical system for $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator. As an application, we reorganize the result of Tosatti-Weinkove-Yau in \cite{TWY}.

papers.title: Topics in higher ramification theory I: ramification ideals
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the notion of ramification ideals in higher ramification theory. After general results on their computation for finite extensions, we discuss their connection with the possibly nontrivial defect of the extensions. We compute them for Artin-Schreier extensions and Kummer extensions of prime degree equal to the residue characteristic, which may or may not have nontrivial defect. We present an example that shows that nontrivial defect in an extension of degree $p^2$, $p$ a prime, may not imply the existence of a nonprincipal ramification ideal.

papers.title: The min-max width of spheres associated to the distance function
papers.abstract: What one obtains when the min-max methods for the distance function are applied on the space of pairs of points of a Riemannian two-sphere? This question is studied in details in the present article. We show that the associated min-max width do not always coincide with half of the length of a simple closed geodesic which is the union of two minimizing geodesics with the same endpoints. Therefore, it is a new geometric invariant. We study the structure of the set of minimizing geodesics joining a pair of points realizing the width, and relationships between this invariant and the diameter. The extrinsic case of an embedded Riemannian sphere is also considered.

papers.title: On the representability of actions of unital algebras
papers.abstract: Working in the setting of ideally exact categories, we investigate the representability of actions of unital non-associative algebras over a field. We show that, in general, such categories fail to be action representable: for instance, the category of all unital algebras is not even action accessible. We then consider this problem in the context of operadic, action accessible, unit-closed varieties. Using the construction of the external weak actor, we prove that for any algebra $X$ in such a variety $\mathcal{V}$, the canonical map into its external weak actor is an isomorphism if and only if $X$ is unital. Consequently, the ideally exact category $\mathcal{V}_1$ of unital algebras in $\mathcal{V}$ is action representable, and the actor of a unital algebra $X$ is $X$ itself. The action accessibility of $\mathcal{V}$ is not necessary for this conclusion: in characteristic zero, unital Jordan algebras form an action representable category, although the variety of all Jordan algebras is not action accessible. Finally, we prove action representability for the categories of unital Poisson algebras and unital commutative Poisson algebras.

papers.title: Path-Kernel Method for Differentiating Unstable Diffusions
papers.abstract: We derive and rigorously prove the path-kernel formula for the linear response of stochastic differential equations, namely, the derivative of averaged statistics with respect to a model parameter. The parameter may affect the diffusion coefficient, as well as the drift coefficient and initial condition. No hyperbolicity assumption is required. The proof introduces a single change of variables for the state path that transfers part of the unstable path perturbation to differentiation of the probability kernel. We also derive a pathwise Monte Carlo algorithm for estimating the response and demonstrate it on the 40-dimensional noisy Lorenz--96 system.

papers.title: Matching with Choice: Menu Design for Patient--Provider Assignment
papers.abstract: High-quality matches between patients and primary care providers improve downstream health outcomes, yet provider turnover breaks these matches and forces patients to be reassigned. Health systems facing this problem must decide not only which providers to recommend, but how much choice to offer. Direct assignment avoids competition for scarce provider capacity but relies on noisy estimates of patient preferences; broader choice allows patients to correct these estimates using private information but can create costly coordination failures. We study this tradeoff through the design of fixed, personalized menus from which patients choose providers. We show that constructing the optimal menu is NP-hard and establish an information-theoretic lower bound. We find that offering each patient a single provider matches this bound up to a constant factor, while unrestricted choice can perform arbitrarily poorly. However, we show that additional choice improves on single-provider assignment when the system cannot reliably distinguish among a patient's alternatives. We formalize this tradeoff through two forms of loss: menu loss, which arises when menus offer too few options, and coordination loss, which arises when scarce capacity is exposed to too much choice. Motivated by this decomposition, we develop the Scenario-Averaged Marginals (SAM) algorithm, which tailors menus based on provider shadow prices so choice is offered only when utility exceeds the capacity cost. We identify sufficient conditions which SAM's regret matches the lower bound, namely when patients have valuable alternatives and offered menus don't create competition for scarce capacity. In a semi-synthetic environment calibrated to a provider network using Medicare data, SAM improves total utility by up to 19% over single-provider assignment as preference uncertainty grows, while improving utility for the least-served ZIP codes.

papers.title: Boundary Blow-up Solutions of Second Order Quasilinear Equation on Infinite Cylinders
papers.abstract: This article studies large solutions, for a class of quasi-linear equations involving p-Laplacian on the infinite cylindrical domains. We study the wellposedness of weak large solutions on infinite cylinders by the convergence of large solutions on finite cylinders and observe that any such solution coincides with the large solution on its cross-section. Finally, the results are generalized to a class of operators involving non-linearity in the gradient.

papers.title: Curves on the torus with few intersections
papers.abstract: Aougab and Gaster [Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 174 (2023), 569-584] proved that any set of simple closed curves on the torus, where any two are non-homotopic and intersect at most k times, has a maximum size of $k+O(\sqrt{k}\log k)$. We determine the maximum size of such a set for every k. In particular, the maximum never exceeds k+6, and it does not exceed k+4 when k is large. As this quantity coincides with the maximal number of columns of a generic k-modular matrix with two rows, our result also settles the column number problem, a problem of interest in combinatorial optimization, for such matrices.

papers.title: $L^2$-Betti numbers of Dehn fillings
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of the $L^2$-Betti numbers of group-theoretic Dehn fillings. For a broad class of virtually special groups $G$, we prove that the $L^2$-Betti numbers of sufficiently deep Dehn fillings $\overline{G}$ are equal to those of $G$. As applications, we verify the Singer Conjecture for certain Einstein manifolds, establish a virtual fibering criterion for $\overline{G}$, obtain bounds on deficiency of $\overline{G}$, and provide new examples of hyperbolic groups with exotic subgroups that arise as Dehn fillings of any cusped arithmetic hyperbolic manifold of dimension at least four.

papers.title: Bayesian Nonparametric Global-local Clustering of High-dimensional Functions
papers.abstract: There is a rich literature on clustering functional data with applications to time-series modeling, trajectory data, and even spatiotemporal applications. Existing methods are classified into two categories of global clustering that assigns an identical membership over the whole domain, and local clustering that allows multiple memberships based on the sub-domains. Classical literature has typically focused on global clustering that may struggle with degenerate clustering or produce numerous spurious clusters for high-dimensional functions. In contrast, a limited number of local clustering approaches have been proposed that are not scalable to high-dimensional functions and have limited theoretical guarantees. Focusing on basis expansions for high-dimensional functions, we propose a novel global-local framework that partitions coefficients into exclusive subsets and imposes independent Dirichlet process priors on each subset. The proposed framework reduces the total number of possible clustering configurations compared to local clustering and therefore provides greater scalability, while simultaneously providing enhanced flexibility compared to global clustering by relaxing the assumption of identical clustering for all elements in the high-dimensional function. Moreover, the proposed method incorporates spatially correlated errors to provide better model fitting and shows posterior consistency properties that asymptotically recover the true density of random functions. An efficient Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm is developed for implementation. Extensive simulations involving images illustrate the improved scalability, clustering, and function estimation under the proposed method compared to classical approaches. We apply the proposed approach to a spatial transcriptomics application where the goal is to infer clusters of genes with distinct spatial patterns of expressions.

papers.title: Highest weight vectors, shifted topological recursion and quantum curves
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of topological recursion by considering Airy structures whose partition functions are highest weight vectors of particular $\mathcal{W}$-algebra representations. Such highest weight vectors arise as partition functions of Airy structures only under certain conditions on the representations. In the spectral curve formulation of topological recursion, we show that this generalization amounts to adding specific terms to the correlators $ ω_{g,1}$, which leads to a ``shifted topological recursion'' formula. We then prove that the wave-functions constructed from this shifted version of topological recursion are WKB solutions of families of quantizations of the spectral curve with $ \hbar$-dependent terms. In the reverse direction, starting from an $\hbar$-connection, we find that it is of topological type if the exact same conditions that we found for the Airy structures are satisfied. When this happens, the resulting shifted loop equations can be solved by the shifted topological recursion obtained earlier.

papers.title: Refining Concentration Bounds for Gaussian Quadratic Chaos with Applications
