papers.abstract: This paper studies concentration of measure for Gaussian quadratic chaos in the non-asymptotic regime. We begin by tightening the classic Hanson-Wright inequality, where we increase its absolute constant $κ$ from 0.125 to at least 0.1457 in the symmetric case. We present a sharper version of Laurent-Massart inequality (LMI), which increases $κ$ from the largest available value of $1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\approx 0.134$ to $\frac{9-\sqrt{17}}{32}\approx 0.152$ in the positive-semidefinite case. We develop a sequence of inequalities indexed by $m\ge1$ that involve Schatten norms of the underlying matrix. The case $m=1$ recovers HWI. The bounds undergo a phase transition in the sense that if the tail parameter is smaller than a critical threshold $τ_c$, then $m=1$ is the tightest, whereas if it is larger than $τ_c$, then $m=\infty$ is the tightest. This leads to a novel bound called the $m_\infty$ bound. All HWI, LMI and the $m_\infty$ inequality rely on Markov's inequality. By avoiding Markov's inequality, we introduce the strong and weak $χ^2$ inequalities. We provide a list of concentration bounds that depend only on the operator norm in the positive-definite case, namely, the $m_\infty$ bound, the weak $χ^2$ bound, relaxed versions of HWI and LMI, and the so-called large-deviations bound. The sharpest among these is shown to be always either the $m_\infty$ bound or the weak $χ^2$ bound. By utilizing conditioning, modified versions of $m_\infty$, $χ^2$, and HW inequalities of various orders are proposed, all of which can be significantly tighter than the original inequalities. By leveraging the Ruben-Kotz expansion for the distribution of a positive-definite quadratic form, we introduce the Ruben-Kotz inequalities (RKIs) for general symmetric quadratic forms. A key advantage of RKIs is that they provide an explicit upper bound on the approximation gap.

papers.title: Anticanonical divisor with good asymptotic base loci
papers.abstract: We characterize varieties of Fano type in terms of potentially log canonical pairs and birational Zariski decompositions. We also prove the existence of anticanonical minimal models of a potentially lc pair $(X,Δ)$ under the assumptions that no potentially log canonical centers are contained in the augmented base locus of $-(K_X+Δ)$ and that $-(K_X+Δ)$ is a big $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor admitting a birational Zariski decomposition with NQC positive part. This can be considered as an anticanonical analogue of the results by Birkar--Hu.

papers.title: Contextful Arrows via Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We introduce contextads and the Ctx construction, unifying various structures and constructions in category theory dealing with context and contextful arrows---comonads and their Kleisli construction, actegories and their Para construction, adequate triples and their Span construction. Contextads are defined in terms of Lack--Street wreaths, suitably categorified for pseudomonads in a tricategory of spans in a 2-category with display maps. The associated wreath product provides the Ctx construction, and by its universal property we conclude trifunctoriality. This abstract approach lets us work up to structure, and thus swiftly prove that, under very mild assumptions, a contextad equipped colaxly with a 2-algebraic structure produces a similarly structured double category of contextful arrows. We also explore the role contextads might play qua dependently graded comonads in organizing contextful computation in functional programming. We show that many side-effects monads can be dually captured by dependently graded comonads, and gesture towards a general result on the `transposability' of parametric right adjoint monads to dependently graded comonads.

papers.title: Répartition conjointe de trois nombres premiers et applications
papers.abstract: We prove asymptotic results for the singular series associated to the distribution of three primes. Assuming a quantitative version of Hardy and Littlewood's conjecture on prime 3-tuples, we deduce an asymptotic formula related to the joint distribution of three primes. This improves recent results of Kuperberg and completes results by Montgomery and Soundararajan. Following the Montgomery and Soundararajan approach, we derive conjectural applications to the distribution of primes in short intervals.

papers.title: Analysis of The Limiting Spectral Distribution of Large Random Matrices of The Marčenko-Pastur Type
papers.abstract: Consider the random matrix \(\bW_n = \bB_n + n^{-1}\bX_n^*\bA_n\bX_n\), where \(\bA_n\) and \(\bB_n\) are Hermitian matrices of dimensions \(p \times p\) and \(n \times n\), respectively, and \(\bX_n\) is a \(p \times n\) random matrix with independent and identically distributed entries of mean 0 and variance 1. Assume that \(p\) and \(n\) grow to infinity proportionally, and that the spectral measures of \(\bA_n\) and \(\bB_n\) converge as \(p, n \to \infty\) towards two probability measures \(\calA\) and \(\calB\). Building on the groundbreaking work of \cite{marchenko1967distribution}, which demonstrated that the empirical spectral distribution of \(\bW_n\) converges towards a probability measure \(F\) characterized by its Stieltjes transform, this paper investigates the properties of \(F\) when \(\calB\) is a general measure. We show that \(F\) has an analytic density at the region near where the Stieltjes transform of $\calB$ is bounded. The density closely resembles \(C\sqrt{|x - x_0|}\) near certain edge points \(x_0\) of its support for a wide class of \(\calA\) and \(\calB\). We provide a complete characterization of the support of \(F\). Moreover, we show that \(F\) can exhibit discontinuities at points where \(\calB\) is discontinuous.

papers.title: Common Noise by Random Measures: Constructing Mean-Field Equilibria for Competitive Investment and Hedging
papers.abstract: We construct Nash equilibria in mean-field portfolio games of optimal investment and hedging under relative performance concerns with exponential (CARA) utility preferences. Common noise dynamics are modeled by integer-valued random measures, for instance Poisson random measures, in addition to Brownian motions. Agents differ in individual risk aversions, competition weights, and initial capital endowments, while their contingent claim liabilities depend on both common and idiosyncratic risk factors. Mean-field equilibria are characterized by solutions to McKean-Vlasov backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, for which we prove existence and uniqueness of solutions, without assuming mean-field interaction to be small. Moreover, we show how the equilibrium can be constructed from the optimal strategy of a single-agent optimization problem (without mean-field interaction) via an appropriate projection. Using successive changes of measure, our derivation provides a decomposition of the equilibrium strategy into three components with clear interpretations. Finally, we show how a limiting mean-field game of quadratic (instead of utility-based) hedging with relative performance concerns arises for vanishing risk aversion.

papers.title: Dwork Motives, Monodromy and Potential Automorphy
papers.abstract: In this paper we study certain families of motives, which arise as direct summands of the cohomology of the Dwork family. We computationally find examples of interesting families with the following three properties. Firstly, their geometric monodromy group is Zariski dense in $\operatorname{SL}_n$. Secondly, they realise many different unipotent operators as the monodromy operator at $t = \infty$. Thirdly, all their Hodge numbers are $\leq 1$. This has consequences for Galois representations. Namely, if a nilpotent operator $N$ appears as the monodromy at $t = \infty$ in one of our families, we can construct potentially automorphic representations with $\ell$-adic monodromy given by $N$ at a fixed prime $p$. As another application, we obtain a new proof of some cases of the recent local-global compatibility theorem of Matsumoto.

papers.title: Power rate of convergence of discrete curves: framework and applications
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for power-law rates of convergence of random discrete curves to Schramm Loewner Evolution (SLE). We show that a power-law rate of convergence of a suitable martingale observable gives a power-law rate of convergence of the interface to SLE, provided the discrete curves satisfy the Kemppainen-Smirnov crossing condition; the proof uses known estimates on the derivative of the SLE map. We apply the framework to the exploration process of critical site percolation on the triangular lattice, obtaining a power-law rate of convergence to SLE$_6$.

papers.title: On the growth of the parameters of approximating ReLU neural networks
papers.abstract: This work focuses on the analysis of fully connected feed forward ReLU neural networks as they approximate a given, smooth function. In contrast to conventionally studied universal approximation properties under increasing architectures, e.g., in terms of width or depth of the networks, we are concerned with the asymptotic growth of the parameters of approximating networks. Such results are of interest, e.g., for error analysis or consistency results for neural network training. The main result of our work is that, for a ReLU architecture with state of the art approximation error, the realizing parameters grow at most polynomially. The obtained rate with respect to a normalized network size is compared to existing results and is shown to be superior in most cases, in particular for high dimensional input.

papers.title: On a Completion of Cohomological Functors Generalising Tate Cohomology I
papers.abstract: Tate cohomology has been generalised by several authors using different constructions that have applications in group theory, ring theory and homotopical algebra. Therefore, there is a need for a uniform account that explains why their underlying approaches all lead to the same conclusions. The key notion in such a uniform theory is a specific completion of cohomological functors that is constructed under mild assumptions. This completion takes Tate cohomology to settings where it has never been introduced such as in condensed mathematics. Through the latter, one can define Tate cohomology for any $T1$ topological group.

papers.title: On a general notion of a polynomial identity and codimensions
papers.abstract: Using the braided version of Lawvere's algebraic theories and Mac Lane's PROPs, we introduce polynomial identities for arbitrary algebraic structures in a braided monoidal category C as well as their codimensions in the case when C is linear over some field. The new cases include coalgebras, bialgebras, Hopf algebras, braided vector spaces, Yetter-Drinfel'd modules, etc. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate codimensions in some important particular cases.

papers.title: Quantitative Propagation of Chaos for Singular Interacting Particle Systems Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion
papers.abstract: We consider interacting systems particle driven by i.i.d. fractional Brownian motions, subject to irregular, possibly distributional, pairwise interactions. We show propagation of chaos and mean field convergence to the law of the associated McKean--Vlasov equation, as the number of particles $N\to\infty$, with quantitative sharp rates of order $N^{-1/2}$. Our results hold for a wide class of possibly time-dependent interactions, which are only assumed to satisfy a Besov-type regularity, related to the Hurst parameter $H\in (0,+\infty)\setminus \mathbb{N}$ of the driving noises. In particular, as $H$ decreases to $0$, interaction kernels of arbitrary singularity can be considered, a phenomenon frequently observed in regularization by noise results. Our proofs rely on a combinations of Sznitman's direct comparison argument with stochastic sewing techniques.

papers.title: The prime geodesic theorem for the modular orbifold
papers.abstract: We establish the prime geodesic theorem for the modular orbifold with exponent $\frac{9}{13} = 0.692307 \cdots$ in the error term. By periodicity and Heath-Brown's quadratic large sieve, we estimate the sixth moment of the error term in an approximation to the Zagier $L$-series at $s = 1$. The smooth explicit formula of Soundararajan and Young then leads to the stated exponent without recourse to subconvexity for quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions.

papers.title: Poisson transforms, the BGG complex, and discrete series representations of SU(n+1,1)
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to construct specific Poisson transforms mapping differential forms on the sphere $S^{2n+1}$ endowed with its natural CR structure to forms on complex hyperbolic space. These transforms have co-closed harmonic values, descend to the BGG (Rumin) complex, and intertwine the differential operators in that complex with the exterior derivative. Passing to the Poincaré ball model, we analyze boundary asymptotics, proving that the values of our transforms admit a continuous extension to the boundary in degrees $\leq n$. Finally, we show that composing the exterior derivative with the transform in degree $n$, one obtains an isomorphism between the kernel of the Rumin operator in degree $n$ and a dense subspace of the $L^2$-harmonic forms on complex hyperbolic space. This provides a realization of the disc rete series representations of $SU(n+1,1)$ with trivial infinitesimal character in spaces of differential forms on the compact manifold $S^{2n+1}$. These developments are motivated by a program of the third author to prove some instances of the Baum-Connes conjecture. The first part of the article is valid in a much more general setting, in particular, it is relevant for cases in which the conjecture is still open.

papers.title: Upper estimates of the lifespan for the fractional wave equations with time-dependent damping and a power nonlinearity of subcritical and critical Fujita exponent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Cauchy problem of the fractional wave equation with time-dependent damping and the source nonlinearity $f(u)\approx |u|^p$: $$ \begin{cases} \partial_t^2u(t,x)+(-Δ)^{σ/2} u(t,x)+b(t) \partial_t u(t,x) =f(u(t,x)),\ &(t,x)\ \in [0,T)\times \mathbb{R}^N,\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\ \partial_tu(0,x)=u_1(x),\ &x\ \in\ \mathbb{R}^N, \end{cases} $$ where the damping coefficient behaves as $b(t)\approx (1+t)^{-β}$. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of mild and strong solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces by deriving weighted Sobolev estimates for the linear propagators and overcoming the spatial-weight coupling in the nonlinearity through the Bessel potential estimates. Then, in the subcritical and critical cases $1<p\leq p_c:=1+\frac σN$, we derive the upper estimates of the lifespan for the fractional Laplacian with $0<σ<2$ and time-dependent damping $β\in [-1, 1)$ via the framework of ordinary differential inequalities. The blow-up results, together with the global existence in the supercritical case obtained in \cite{LI}, show that the critical exponent for the fractional wave equation is $p_c=1+\fracσ{N}$ for $0<σ<2$. Moreover, combining with the lower estimate of lifespan derived in \cite{LI}, we conclude that the estimate in this paper is sharp. Note that our result for the critical case is completely new even in the classical case $b(t)=1$. We also consider the case of $β=1$, and obtain the upper estimate of the lifespan.

papers.title: Fundamental groups, coregularity, and low dimensional klt Calabi-Yau pairs
papers.abstract: In this article, we study how the absolute coregularity of a projective log pair reflects on its fundamental group. More precisely, we conjecture that for a projective klt log pair $(X,D)$ of absolute coregularity $c$ (and arbitrary dimension) the fundamental group $π_1^{\rm reg}(X,D)$ admits a normal abelian subgroup of finite index and rank at most $2c$. We prove this conjecture in the cases $0 \leq c \leq 3$, building on the almost abelianity of the fundamental groups of klt Calabi-Yau pairs of dimension $\leq 3$. In the cases $c \in \{0,1,2\}$ and fixed dimension, we can furthermore bound the index of a solvable normal subgroup. In dimension three, we are able to prove almost abelianity of the fundamental group of the regular locus for projective klt Calabi-Yau pairs.

papers.title: Connected Dominating Sets in Triangulations
papers.abstract: A dominating set of a graph $G$ is \emph{connected} if it induces a connected graph in $G$. For planar triangulations, it has been known since 1990 that every $n$-vertex triangulation with $n\ge4$ admits a connected dominating set of size at most $n/2 - 1$, and no improvement to this bound was known for over three decades. We break this longstanding barrier by showing that every $n$-vertex triangulation has a connected dominating set of size at most $10n/21$. Equivalently, every triangulation admits a spanning tree with at least $11n/21$ leaves. This result has graph drawing applications, establishing a bound for one-bend free sets and improving the known bound for simultaneous planar embeddings. The connected dominating set results extend readily to show that an $n$-vertex triangulation of a surface of Euler genus $g$ has a connected dominating set of size at most $10n/21+O(\sqrt{gn})$.

papers.title: Systems of affine equations, their L-functions, t-holonomic sequences, non-commutative determinants
papers.abstract: The authors defined in their previous paper ''$h^1\ne h_1$ for Anderson t-motives'' the notion of an affine equation associated to a t-motive. We study in the present paper general affine equations and their systems. We define L-functions of an affine equation. We show that its local factor is an algebraic function; we state a problem to prove an analog of the Lefschetz trace formula for the global L-function. We define t-holonomic sequences which are solutions of any affine equations. We state some conjectures and open questions related to t-holonomic sequences, for example formulas of their asymptotic growth. We show that some of the properties of t-holonomic sequences are analogous to the properties of the classical holonomic sequences, for example the closure properties. Further, we show that systems of affine equations can be reduced to one equation by a process analogous to the elimination of variables in a system of linear equations; this gives us a notion of non-commutative determinants. Finally, we consider some explicit examples of affine equations that come from Drinfeld modules, their duals and some other t-motives.

papers.title: Homology with the theme of Matlis
papers.abstract: Matlis proved a lot of homological properties of the fraction field of an integral domain. In this paper, we simplify and extend some of them from 1-dimensional (resp. rank one) cases to the higher dimensional (resp. finite rank) cases. For example, we study the weakly co-torsion property of Ext$(-,\sim)$, and use it to present splitting criteria. These are equipped with several applications. For instance, we compute the projective dimension of $\widehat{R}$ and present some non-noetherian versions of Grothendieck's localization problem. We construct a new class of co-Hopfian modules and extend Matlis' decomposability problem to higher ranks. In particular, this paper deals with the basic properties of Matlis' quadric $(Q,Q/R, \widehat{R},\overset{\sim}R).$

papers.title: $P=W$ via $\mathcal{H}_2$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_2$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial Hamiltonian vector fields on the symplectic plane. Let $X$ be the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles of fixed relatively prime rank and degree, or more generally the moduli space of stable parabolic Higgs bundles of arbitrary rank and degree for a generic stability condition. Let $H^*(X)$ be the cohomology with rational coefficients. Using the operations of cup-product by tautological classes and Hecke correspondences we construct an action of $\mathcal{H}_2$ on $H^*(X)[x,y]$, where $x$ and $y$ are formal variables. We show that the perverse filtration on $H^*(X)$ coincides with the filtration canonically associated to $\mathfrak{sl}_2\subset \mathcal{H}_2$ and deduce the $P=W$ conjecture of de Cataldo-Hausel-Migliorini.

papers.title: The Collatz Conjecture & Non-Archimedean Spectral Theory -- Part II -- $\left(p,q\right)$-Adic Fourier Analysis and Wiener's Tauberian Theorem
papers.abstract: This paper gives an overview of $\left(p,q\right)$-adic Fourier theory - the Fourier theory of functions from the $p$-adic numbers to the $q$-adic numbers, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes - which we then use to prove a novel $\left(p,q\right)$-adic generalization of Norbert Wiener's celebrated Tauberian Theorem. Letting $K$ be a metrically complete, algebraically closed local field of residue characteristic $q$, letting $C\left(\mathbb{Z}_{p},K\right)$ be the Banach space of continuous functions $\mathbb{Z}_{p}\rightarrow K$, and letting $dμ$ be a $\left(p,q\right)$-adic measure (a continuous linear functional $C\left(\mathbb{Z}_{p},K\right)\rightarrow K)$, the $\left(p,q\right)$-adic Wiener Tauberian Theorem (WTT) we prove establishes that the density of the span of translates of $dμ$'s Fourier-Stieltjes Transform implies the non-vanishing of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of $dμ$ at all points in $\mathbb{Z}_{p}$ where the derivative exists in $K$.

papers.title: The virtual fundamental class for the moduli space of surfaces of general type
papers.abstract: We prove that the moduli stack of index-one covers of semi-log-canonical surfaces of general type is isomorphic to the KSBA moduli stack of stable general type surfaces. Using the index-one covering Deligne-Mumford stack of a semi-log-canonical surface, we define the $\lci$ cover. The $\lci$ cover, as a Deligne-Mumford stack, has only locally complete intersection singularities. We then construct the moduli stack of $\lci$ covers so that it admits a proper map to the moduli stack of surfaces of general type. The smoothing of lci covering Deligne-Mumford stacks can not control all the non lci slc singularities. Thus, we construct the moduli stack of birational lci enhancement Deligne-Mumford stacks for all non lci slc singularities. This moduli stack is in general nonseparated. We construct a separated {\em algebraic space} from this moduli stack. Next, we construct a perfect obstruction theory on each of these moduli stacks and a virtual fundamental class in the Chow group. We then pushforward the virtual fundamental class to the KSBA moduli space. Thus, our construction proves Donaldson's conjecture on the existence of a virtual fundamental class for KSBA moduli spaces. A tautological invariant is defined by integrating a power of the first Chern class of the CM line bundle over the virtual fundamental class. This serves as a generalization of the tautological invariants defined by integrating tautological classes over the moduli space $\overline{M}_g$ of stable curves to the moduli space of stable surfaces.

papers.title: A Note On Majorizing Norms on Majorized Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a new type of norm for ordered vector spaces majorized by a proper (convex) cone that generalizes the notions of order unit norm and base norm. Then we give sufficient conditions to ensure its completeness. In the case of normed Riesz spaces, we also present necessary completeness conditions and describe the completed norm. Finally, we define a particular family of well-behaving sets. Spaces majorized by the cone generated by these sets display surprisingly interesting structural properties. In particular, we generalize two famous standard results in Banach lattice theory. Namely, every principal ideal in a Banach lattice is an AM-space and every Banach lattice having a generating cone with a compact base admits an equivalent L-norm.

papers.title: Rotational symmetry of complete gradient Einstein-type manifolds with $α=0$ under vanishing conditions on several tensor fields
papers.abstract: To provide a unified framework for various geometric solitons, Catino, Mastrolia, Monticelli, and Rigoli introduced gradient Einstein-type manifolds, which include gradient Yamabe solitons, gradient almost Yamabe solitons, gradient $k$-Yamabe solitons and conformal gradient solitons. In this paper, we show that any nontrivial complete four-dimensional gradient Einstein-type manifold with $α=0$, nonnegative scalar curvature, and vanishing Bach tensor is rotationally symmetric. The Bach-flat condition arises naturally in four-dimensional geometry and physics. We prove the main theorem by exploiting the conformal invariance of Bach-flatness and establishing a relation between two functionals. We also provide classification results under vanishing conditions on the Weyl tensor, the Cotton tensor, and the Cao-Chen-type tensor.

papers.title: Hilbert's 16th problem through Morse theory
papers.abstract: We focus on the second part of Hilbert's 16th problem and provide an upper bound on the number of limit cycles that a polynomial, differential, planar system may have, depending exclusively on the degree $n$ of the system. Such a bound turns out to be a polynomial of degree $4$ in $n$. More specifically, if $H(n)$ indicates the maximum number of limit cycles among planar, differential, polynomial systems of degree $n$, then \begin{gather} H(n)\le \dfrac52 n^4-\dfrac{23}2 n^3+ \dfrac{43}2n^2-\dfrac{37}2n+7\,\,\,\, \mbox{if $n$ is even, and} \nonumber H(n)\le \dfrac52 n^4-\dfrac{23}2 n^3+ \dfrac{41}2n^2-\dfrac{33}2n+6\,\,\,\, \mbox{if $n$ is odd}.\nonumber \end{gather} For quadratic systems, we find $H(2)=4$. Our proof is entirely variational and utilizes in a fundamental way tools and facts from Morse theory, to the point that no particular expertise in dynamical systems is necessary or required. It is particularly interesting to compare our results with the ones for the same problem recently announced and made public by OpenAI as part of the solution of hundreds of important mathematical problems.

papers.title: Combining Determinism and Indeterminism
papers.abstract: Our goal is to construct mathematical operations that combine indeterminism measured from quantum randomness with computational determinism so that non-mechanistic behavior is preserved in the computation. Formally, some results about operations applied to computably enumerable (c.e.) and bi-immune sets are proven here, where the objective is for the operations to preserve bi-immunity. While developing rearrangement operations on the natural numbers, we discovered that the bi-immune rearrangements generate an uncountable subgroup of the infinite symmetric group (Sym$(\mathbb{N})$) on the natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$. This new uncountable subgroup is called the bi-immune symmetric group. We show that the bi-immune symmetric group contains the finitary symmetric group on the natural numbers, and consequently is highly transitive. Furthermore, the bi-immune symmetric group is dense in Sym$(\mathbb{N})$ with respect to the pointwise convergence topology. The complete structure of the bi-immune symmetric group and its subgroups generated by one or more bi-immune rearrangements is unknown.

papers.title: On the minimum bisection of random $3$-regular graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper we give new bounds on the bisection width of random 3-regular graphs on $n$ vertices. The main contribution is a new lower bound of $0.103295n$ based on a first moment method together with a structural analysis of the graph, thereby improving a 27-year-old result of Kostochka and Melnikov. We also give a complementary upper bound of $0.139822n$ by combining a result of Lyons with original combinatorial insights. Developping this approach further, we obtain a non-rigorous improved upper bound with the help of Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: Sharp Poincaré inequalities for the logarithmic smoothness of the Gauss map on hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We establish sharp lower bounds for two geometric functionals which evaluate the global variation of the Gauss map on the boundary of bounded open sets $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. These functionals arise as the endpoint case $s=0$ of the Gagliardo seminorm in $W^{s,p}(\partialΩ)$ of the normal vector field, for $p\in\{1,2\}$. We also show that balls are the unique minimizers. In addition, some applications to the fractional setting $s>0$ are given.

papers.title: Drinfeld J Presentation of Twisted Yangians
papers.abstract: We present a quantization of a Lie coideal structure for twisted half-loop algebras of finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebras. We obtain algebra closure relations of twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for all symmetric pairs of simple Lie algebras and for simple twisted even half-loop Lie algebras. We provide the explicit form of the closure relations for twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for the ${\mathfrak{sl}}_3$ Lie algebra.

papers.title: O-segments on topological measure spaces
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ be a finite non-atomic measure on a set $X$. A \emph{segment} for $μ$ is an increasing family $u(t)$, $t\in[0,1]$, of measurable sets with $u(0)=\emptyset$, $u(1)=X$ and $μ(u(t))=t\,μ(X)$; by a theorem of Fryszkowski, finitely many measures $f\,dμ$ admit a common segment. We study \emph{open segments}, i.e.\ segments consisting of open sets, when $X$ carries a topology. We show that weak outer regularity of $μ$ is equivalent to the approximability of measurable sets by open sets, and that it holds for every finite Borel measure on a metrizable space. Our main result states that if $μ$ is finite, non-atomic and weakly outer regular, then for all $f,g\in L^1(μ)$ with $(\int f\,dμ,\int g\,dμ)\neq(0,0)$ there is a common open segment for $f\,dμ$ and $g\,dμ$; in particular, for every $f\in L^1(μ)$ there is an open segment for $μ$ which is simultaneously a segment for $f\,dμ$. Relative versions allow one to prescribe an initial set. We also characterize open segments as upper semicontinuous functions with uniform distribution and show that on separable metrizable spaces a single measure admits such a function which is continuous.

papers.title: Multipliers and weighted d-bar estimates
papers.abstract: We study some size estimates for the solution of the equation d-bar u=f in one variable. The new ingredient is the use of holomorphic functions with precise growth restrictions in the construction of explicit solutions to the equation.

papers.title: Boundary phenomena for slow recurrences:finite and infinite critical sets
papers.abstract: For a second-order recurrence with positive integral coefficients, the slow length of an integer is the largest index at which it can occur when the initial terms range over positive integers. Spiro conjectured that, among a finite set of relatively prime recurrence pairs, a pair is slowest infinitely often precisely when its growth constant is strictly less than the square of the smallest growth constant. We study the equality case. For $T_m=\{(m-1,m),(m^2-1,m^2)\}$, the larger-growth pair attains the maximal slow length, with ties allowed, on $Θ_m(\log x)$ integers up to $x$ whenever $m\ge3$, whereas for $m=2$ its complete set of slowest integers is $\{1,2,25\}$. We give certificates for the infinite examples and prove a bounded-seed theorem that limits the possible initial pairs at each critical index.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree at least $750$ satisfies $χ(G)\le\max\{ω(G),Δ(G)-1\}$. The proof starts with a random partial colouring and completes it on large cliques using a list-colouring condition that remains valid as the rest of the graph is coloured. Disjoint stars provide the required colours. We estimate the number of stars that can be chosen after the clique colours have been exposed, while keeping their endpoint set fixed. A common exponential-moment argument reduces intervals of packing sizes to endpoint comparisons. More detailed neighbourhood estimates handle the remaining vertices. The final probability inequalities are verified by directed rational and interval arithmetic.

papers.title: Isosceles sets in Euclidean spaces of dimension nine to twenty-two
papers.abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erdős asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The answer was known for $d\le 8$, the last cases being due to Ionin. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le 21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre, and the number $\binom d2+3$ is attained. The proof combines Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets, for which we give a short self-contained proof (the key step is a special case of Gallai's theorem on edge colourings without rainbow triangles), with the recent determination of the maximum two-distance sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $9\le d\le22$ and with the known maximum sizes of spherical two-distance sets. In dimension nine this gives only $\mathrm{iso}(9)\le47$, and the exact value $46$ requires an additional argument about eight-dimensional two-distance sets with at least $44$ points. We also show that $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}$, where $g(23)$ is the largest size of a two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^{23}$, so that $278\le\mathrm{iso}(23)\le575$.

papers.title: A normalization issue in a transmitted form of Bloch's diamond formula: anti-invariant subgroup versus regulator quotient
papers.abstract: Bloch's identity $\int_γη(f,g)=D_E((f)\diamond(g))$, relating the regulator of a $K_2$-symbol on an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ to the elliptic dilogarithm of the diamond product of the divisors, is transmitted in the Mahler-measure literature with $γ$ generating the anti-invariant subgroup $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^-$ and factor $1$ (e.g. Lalin-Ramamonjisoa, Thm. 6). We observe that, when $E(\mathbb{R})$ has one connected component ($Δ<0$), this reading is incompatible with the published intersection-product normalization (Brunault, Proposition 19): the anti-invariant subgroup then has index $2$ in the regulator quotient $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})/H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^+$. The correct statement -- factor $1$ for the quotient generator, hence factor $ι(E)\in\{1,2\}$ for the subgroup generator, with $ι(E)=1\iffΔ>0$ -- follows from Brunault's formula by an elementary index computation. We document the phenomenon twice: on 11.a3 by proved values (a Siegel-unit anchor from [Zheng, arXiv:2609.26119]; the diamond side by Brunault and Bertin), and on 20.a4 by high-precision computation of both integrals against the $q$-series for $D_E$ (subgroup/quotient ratio $2$ to $13$ digits). We also show that Touafek's Theorem 2 (involving a $Δ<0$ curve) mixes two independent normalizations (subgroup versus quotient, and a $(2π)^{-1}$ prefactor versus the bare diamond value), and we identify the two-part reinterpretation making its printed formulas mutually compatible. In the cases we have checked, no Mahler-measure or $D_E$-identity is affected: the main theorem of Lalin-Ramamonjisoa (conductor $17$, $Δ>0$) and Bertin's proved exotic relations stand untouched, and Touafek's final $D_E$-relation is not contradicted and is numerically supported, though its printed derivation retains the gap described in the text. A systematic audit is beyond the scope of this note.

papers.title: On nearly Lefschetz fibrations and spinal open books
papers.abstract: We survey the recent development of spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations. The focus is on explaining past and new results regarding the detection of symplectic fillability and classification of symplectic fillings of contact 3-manifolds in light of the new machinery. We give many examples and a list of open questions. This can be considered as an additional chapter to the lecture notes by Ozbacgi and Wendl.

papers.title: Time to AC-t: When AC-transmission changes capacity expansion planning
papers.abstract: Capacity expansion models often dramatically simplify the physics of how power flows through a transmission network in order to preserve computational tractability. However, with the rapid growth of electrification, large loads, renewables, and storage, increased realism in planning future grids is imperative. We extend the open-source capacity expansion model GenX with AC optimal power flow physics, and analyze generation, storage, and transmission investment decisions for 20-zone, hourly models of Germany and Texas. We compare our results against those using two common approximations, the transport model and DC optimal power flow. We find that total costs and emissions largely agree across all formulations. However, we find substantial differences in outputs related to transmission, generation siting, storage, and reactive-power support between the approximate formulations and the true AC physics formulation. We identify where AC physics changes planning decisions and discuss how to potentially capture these effects without the full computational cost.

papers.title: Bounds for Orthogonal Expansion Coefficients via Weighted Primitives
papers.abstract: For trigonometric and polynomial orthogonal expansions, we present coefficient bounds with an explicit numerator determined by the total variation of the function and the largest cumulative signed area of the weighted basis element. This area, denoted by $M_n$, is the sharp constant in the corresponding weighted integral estimate. We calculate or bound $M_n$ for several classical systems, thereby obtaining quantitative inequalities beyond an asymptotic statement of coefficient decay. Integration between consecutive zeros gives a geometric interpretation of the estimate. The comparison includes Chebyshev polynomials of the first three kinds, Legendre, Jacobi, Gegenbauer, and ordinary Laguerre polynomials, with normalization and boundary conditions stated explicitly. Classical estimates and their elementary consequences are organized as Fourier analysis in inequalities. In the controlled distortion application, ideal curves have selected coefficients absent, and restrictions on the variation, corridor width, and number of extrema of admissible departures give explicit guarantees for those coefficients.

papers.title: Adaptive data-driven reduced-order models for reciprocal MIMO port-Hamiltonian dynamical systems
papers.abstract: Port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems provide a general framework for modeling a broad class of physical dynamical systems, including systems with dissipation. Constructing accurate and robust data-driven reduced-order models for general pH systems is challenging. In this work, we focus on an important subclass of pH systems satisfying reciprocity, a property arising naturally in a variety of models. Rather than seeking to preserve the full pH structure, we exploit the additional symmetry provided by reciprocity to develop an efficient data-driven reduced-order modeling approach. We show that every minimal realization of a reciprocal system is self-adjoint with respect to a generally indefinite inner product and can, up to a similarity transformation preserving the pH structure, be represented in a Krein space with a signature inner product. This observation motivates a Galerkin projection onto a tangential rational Krylov subspace with respect to the corresponding indefinite inner product. Although the resulting projection involves full-order state solutions and the unknown inner product, we show that its reduced mass and stiffness matrices can be constructed directly from transfer-function data through a Loewner formulation. We then propose a greedy data-driven procedure that adaptively selects both interpolation frequencies and tangential directions. At every iteration, the frequency is chosen according to the largest transfer-function approximation error, while the tangential direction is selected from a dominant singular direction of the corresponding matrix-valued residual. Numerical experiments for wave propagation in lossy media demonstrate improved approximation efficiency compared with block adaptive interpolation. We further apply the method to spectral mass gauging of a three-dimensional propellant tank to provide an accurate estimate of the tank volume through Weyl's law.

papers.title: Minimax signal detection in regression under differential privacy
papers.abstract: We establish minimax separation rates across sparsity levels for regression signal detection under $(ε, δ)$-central differential privacy, considering linear regression with an unknown error distribution and generalised linear models (GLMs) with an unknown intercept. Without sparsity restrictions, the separation rates for linear regression and GLMs with binary responses match the private Gaussian mean testing rate up to polylogarithmic factors. For GLMs with more than two possible response outcomes, additional information in the marginal response distribution permits faster detection of sufficiently small signals when the dimension exceeds the sample size $n$. Our upper bounds are based on a reduction to private mean testing, tests of dependence between the response and sparse covariate projections, and a response-only test that is adjusted for the unknown intercept. The resulting procedure adapts to unknown sparsity and matches our lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. We also construct polynomial-time tests that attain these rates when $ε\gtrsim n^{-1/2}$, and compare their numerical performance with existing private procedures.

papers.title: StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Policy Selection under Stream Dependence
papers.abstract: Learn-then-Test (LTT) provides a general framework for certifying deployment policies against a prescribed risk target, but its standard formulation targets a fixed population risk estimated from calibration losses. In sequential deployment, losses may instead be dependent and nonstationary, so the risk of a fixed policy can evolve with the observed history. We introduce StreamLTT, which replaces this fixed population risk with average predictable risk, defined by conditioning each decision's loss on the information available before its outcome is revealed. Conditional centering turns empirical deviations from this target into a martingale sum, enabling both a test that adapts to predictable variance and a finite-sample Hoeffding alternative. Combined with family-wise error rate control, StreamLTT yields a simultaneously certified policy region that supports subsequent deployment selection. Across seven forecasting datasets and seven deployment risks, StreamLTT places the certified frontier substantially closer to the prescribed risk target than IID, robust-variance, block-bootstrap, and concentration-based alternatives, while empirical family-wise error closely follows the prescribed level. A finite-sample ablation further shows that the predictable-risk formulation drives the tighter risk frontier, while adaptation to predictable variance makes more effective use of the available family-wise error budget. StreamLTT therefore extends risk-certified policy selection to dependent deployment streams by addressing both what risk should be certified and how it should be tested.

papers.title: Revisiting the Upper Bild of Quaternionic Numerical Ranges
papers.abstract: The upper bild of the quaternionic numerical range provides a convex representative of the generally nonconvex quaternionic numerical range. Although its convexity is known, the geometry of the upper bild is difficult to describe explicitly, even for 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices. In this paper, we revisit the upper bild of quaternionic numerical ranges from both algebraic and geometric viewpoints. We first point out gaps in Kumar's proof. We then investigate several special classes of 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices and describe their shapes and boundary structures in the closed upper complex half-plane directly in terms of the standard eigenvalues and the off-diagonal entry of the Schur form. For the general 2-by-2 case, we use a different canonical form. Following So and Thompson, we prove the concavity of the upper-boundary function through the associated complex representation. For the lower boundary, we obtain a distance-to-a-disk representation and use convex optimization to prove its convexity. We also treat the degenerate cases. Together with the connectedness of the vertical sections, these results give an alternative proof of the convexity of the upper bild for arbitrary quaternionic matrices.

papers.title: A Review of Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control Algorithms: State of the Art and Research Opportunities
papers.abstract: Max-Pressure (MP) has emerged as a widely studied decentralized traffic signal control framework, thanks to its desirable theoretical properties and strong control performance. Early research on MP focused on improving control performance by exploring different variables of the traffic state for the definition of pressure. Subsequent studies expanded MP to incorporate the complexity of real-world transportation systems and emerging technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive review of these developments. The review first introduces the theoretical foundations of MP and examines early developments in movement weight definition. It then synthesizes major extensions for multimodal and multiscale network control, followed by recent developments in connected and automated vehicle (CAV) environments and the integration of MP with artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven methods. Beyond summarizing existing approaches, this review examines their underlying assumptions, data requirements, implementation considerations, and practical limitations. Based on this comprehensive review, key research gaps and future directions are identified, including remaining limitations in the theoretical foundations of MP and the underexplored integration of autonomous vehicle control with the MP framework. Overall, this review provides a structured perspective on the evolution and current state of MP control and highlights opportunities for developing more proactive, robust, and practically deployable MP-based traffic control methods.

papers.title: Fixed-grid schemes for fractional moving-boundary problems
papers.abstract: The Landau transformation xi = x/s(t) is the usual way to hold a moving boundary in place. It fails for fractional time derivatives because they have no chain rule: the transformed operator gains a nonlocal integral with a closed form only for self-similar fronts. We develop a sharp-interface finite-difference scheme for the conservation-consistent memory-flux fractional Stefan problem on a fixed grid, storing the memory limit h(x) = s^-1(x) as the time each node melts. The front is advanced using an integrated energy balance, with the singular source timed to the sub-step crossing instant. Against a known self-similar solution, the front constant is accurate to 0.02 to 0.11%, whereas competing formulations differ by 17 to 27% at alpha = 0.6. A remaining positivity violation follows from dt/t0 ~ s0^(1 - 2/alpha) and disappears on a front-locked time grid. We also derive two exact solutions with non-power-law fronts: a source-dominated solution and a Mittag-Leffler traveling wave, and verify the scheme against both. Neural-network solvers for moving boundaries are often trained in normalized coordinates; for alpha < 1, this silently changes the problem, while the change vanishes at alpha = 1, where checks are commonly performed. In the classical limit, our scheme is more accurate in 12 ms than a reimplemented moving-boundary network in 177 s.

papers.title: Hochschild cohomology of Temperley--Lieb algebras: a Kauffman diagram perspective
papers.abstract: We describe Hochschild cohomology of Temperley--Lieb algebras by explicit minimal-resolution coordinates and multilinear operations on Kauffman diagrams. For each doubled-line basic algebra, a finite four-term bimodule complex is verified by a signed-shuffle comparison and an augmented contracting homotopy. We compute cocycles and coboundaries and recover the known cup product and Gerstenhaber bracket in explicit representatives. Over $\mathbb C$, at nonzero root-of-unity loop parameters, we construct a tower-compatible derivation and the marked-circle two-cocycle. Their classes are nonzero on every nonsemisimple block; their cup products therefore represent all positive classes over the centre. Relative full twists give a compact expression for the derivation. Worked planar diagrams distinguish the cup product from insertion and strict cochain equalities from equalities of classes. A finite-lattice section interprets the marked-circle operation as loop-weight response, derives its planar Potts normalization, and exhibits a six-vertex realization. It also shows why passing to a deformable spin representation may annihilate the class with different coefficients. No thermodynamic conclusion is claimed, and the even-strand zero-parameter family remains separate.

papers.title: Automatic partition identities
papers.abstract: We encode certain sets of partitions by regular languages of boundary words, so that their generating functions become rational series in the quantum plane $RU=qUR$. An equality between two partition counts is certified by writing the difference of their series as $(1-U)a+b(1-R)$, with $a,b$ converging $q$-adically. We show that $a,b$ may be chosen as solutions of finite holonomic systems of $q$-difference equations computed from the automata, and describe finite certificates of their convergence, together with bounded searches for such certificates; the searches need not succeed, but a false identity is always detected. As an application, we prove the three-row, level-two case of Primc's conjecture, which equates counts of coloured partitions subject to local multiplicity conditions with counts of coloured partitions whose parts lie in prescribed residue classes modulo eight.

papers.title: Some instances of modularity for residually reducible representations in the mixed case
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field, abelian over $\Q$, in which an odd prime $p$ splits completely, and let $ρ:G_F\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_p)$ be an odd irreducible representation which is de Rham with distinct Hodge--Tate weights at the places above $p$ and whose residual representation is reducible. We consider the \emph{mixed} case of the Fontaine--Mazur conjecture, in which $ρ$ is reducible at some places above $p$ and irreducible at the others. This case is not covered by the work of Pan and Zhang. We prove some instances of modularity in this situation. Our main result is that $ρ$ is modular if it is non-split at every place above $p$ where it is reducible, by combining Zhang's pro-modularity theorem with a classicality criterion based on Emerton's ordinary parts. Together with a theorem of Zhao on local indecomposability, this gives the modularity of the $λ$-adic representations attached to abelian varieties of $\GL_2$-type in the mixed case, and, using a result of Snowden, of potentially modular representations of parallel weight two under a mild additional condition. It also gives the modularity of representations whose local type at every place above $p$ is of discrete series type, and, through a member of the compatible system with interchanged Hodge-Tate weights, of potentially modular representations of weight $(2,k)$ over real quadratic fields with Steinberg type at one place above $p$, under conditions on that member.

papers.title: Toward Quillen stratification for the odd primary Steenrod algebra
papers.abstract: Fix an odd prime $p$ and let $A$ be the mod $p$ Steenrod algebra. There is a normal sub-Hopf algebra $D$ of $A$, and we show that the cohomology of $A$ is $F$-isomorphic to the subalgebra of the cohomology of $D$ which is invariant under the $A$-action. We also show that the sub-Hopf algebras of $A$ with bounded profile function detect nilpotence in cohomology.

papers.title: Pseudo-Fredholm operators form a regularity on Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. We prove that the class of pseudo-Fredholm operators on $H$ is a regularity in the sense of Kordula and Müller. We also prove that the classes of left and right generalized Drazin invertible operators are regularities on $H$. Consequently, the generalized Kato spectrum and the corresponding generalized Drazin spectra satisfy the spectral mapping theorem. We construct an operator $T$ on a separable complex Banach space such that $T^2$ is right generalized Drazin invertible whereas $T$ is not pseudo-Fredholm. In particular, the power axiom need not hold for pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach spaces. Finally, we show that the accumulation sets of the approximate point and surjectivity spectra define regularities on Banach spaces, yielding another proof of the regularity of generalized Drazin invertible operators in $\B(X)$.

papers.title: Initial-Trace Insufficiency and Entropy-Accounting Separation in Finite-Volume Coarse Graining
papers.abstract: Coarse finite-volume information does not automatically define an exact pathwise closure for the restricted evolution of a fine-grid realization. We study two one-step information boundaries that are distinct from recursive predictive memory. First, we show that parent averages together with complete initial parent-interface trace pairs are sufficient for one forward-Euler finite-volume transition with a deterministic two-state numerical flux, but they do not generally determine a completed second-order strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta, equivalently Heun, transition. An explicit scalar upwind collision shows that hidden interior data can affect later stage traces and hence the completed parent update, even when initial traces and parent averages agree. Second, we show that exact conservative one-step closure is not the same as entropy-accounting closure. A parent entropy balance obtained from a cellwise numerical entropy balance contains a subcell Jensen gap, a realized entropy-flux difference, and residual dissipation. For a declared Burgers-Rusanov conservative flux and a declared Rusanov-type numerical entropy flux, we construct a sign-indexed finite family in which all branches have identical parent averages, identical conservative interface registers, and identical next parent averages, while the entropy-interface register distinguishes every branch. Under the uniform branch law, the conservative channel leaves nonzero deterministic squared-error floors for both the raw entropy register and its cyclic divergence. The results give a concise finite-volume information-sufficiency test for multistage interface data and entropy-side accounting.

papers.title: Balance in Inequality: Testing the Physical Equilibrium, Precession, and Structural Stability of Magic Gems
papers.abstract: A magic square exemplifies balance in inequality: its $n^2$ entries $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ are distinct, yet every row, column, and main diagonal sums to $μ_n=n(n^2+1)/2$. Lifting centred grid cells into $\mathbb{R}^3$ as radial vectors $\mathbf{p}_{ij}(λ)=(x_j,y_i,λz_{ij})$ and taking their convex hull---the Magic Gem $\mathcal{G}_λ(S)$---asks: when does line-sum equality suffice for equilibrium in 3D, and when a nonlinear realization breaks balance, how can an opposing inequality restore it? We test this across all $880$ order-$4$ magic squares in four regimes. For radial spokes from $O$, natural lengths balance identically, while unit spokes break equilibrium on all $832$ non-associative squares in 3D and on all squares in 2D, where the ring-radius ratio $r_2/r_1=\sqrt{5}$ bounds the resultant below by the Pell convergent $9/4\approx\sqrt{5}$. By length--weight duality, balance is restored via tip weights $\mathbf{w}^*>\mathbf{0}$ on $S^2$ or power-law spoke scaling ($r^{α^*}$ in 2D and $(\mathbf{V}_3)_z=0$ in 3D). In 3D rotation, equal point masses make every semi-magic square an axisymmetric top with spherical-top transition $λ_{\mathrm{iso}}=(n^2+1)^{-1/2}$, whereas entry masses $m_{ij}=s_{ij}$ expose the quadrupole $Q_{xy}=\sum z_{ij}x_jy_i$, triggering $180^\circ$ Dzhanibekov flips on $824$ squares. Passing to the uniform solid hull $\mathcal{G}_0(S)$ shifts the centroid off $O$ on $829$ squares; re-engaging the opposing core $\mathcal{G}_1(S)$ restores balance via two-density inclusions, nested wireframes, or the $K_{n^2}$ strut network, while all $880$ hulls unfold into non-overlapping nets with $f_0-1$ glue tabs. Finally, $λ=1/5$ stabilizes $74.5\%$ of facets on a table, and alternating $\mathcal{G}_λ(S)$ with its mirror twin $\mathcal{G}_λ(r^2\overline{S})=-\mathcal{G}_λ(S)$ locks chiral blocks into a vertical tower.

papers.title: Binomial Artin-Schelter Regular Algebras and Twisted Monoid Algebras
papers.abstract: We study four-dimensional binomial Artin-Schelter regular algebras and their connection with twisted monoid algebras. Starting with $23$ examples up to permutation of generators, we investigate the associated monoids of I-type and the structure of their groups of fractions. We determine the corresponding finite permutation groups and compute the second group cohomology $H^2(G(M),k^\times)$. These computations allow us to construct explicit families of four-dimensional Koszul Artin-Schelter regular algebras through cocycle twists. We illustrate this construction for some of these algebras.

papers.title: The first non-trivial Fučík curve for the sublinear Dirichlet Laplacian
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded open connected set, and let $q\in(1,2)$. We consider the sublinear $q$-eigenvalue problem for the Dirichlet Laplacian $-Δu=λ\|u\|_{L^q(Ω)}^{2-q}|u|^{q-2}u$, $u\in H^1_0(Ω)\setminus\{0\}$, whose first eigenvalue $λ_1(Ω)$ is simple, with eigenfunctions of constant sign. The definition of a second eigenvalue is not unique. Following the approach introduced by Molle and Passaseo for the linear Laplacian, we construct the first non-trivial curve of the corresponding Fučík spectrum, and show that it has a unique diagonal point $(γ(Ω),γ(Ω))$. The Fučík-selected second value $λ_2^F(Ω)=2^{1-\frac{2}{q}}γ(Ω)$ is strictly larger than $λ_1(Ω)$, admits a two-phase variational characterisation, and satisfies a sharp Hong-Krahn-Szegő inequality: among sets of given measure it is minimised by the union of two equal balls. The selected solution at the diagonal point is a classical $(2,q)$-eigenfunction exactly when its nodal $L^q$-masses are balanced. We finally show that on balls in dimensions $N\geq2$ every Fučík-selected solution is foliated Schwarz symmetric.

papers.title: Rings in which every semiprime left ideal is an intersection of prime left ideals
papers.abstract: We study rings over which every semiprime submodule of every module is an intersection of prime submodules. This holds if semiprime two-sided ideals satisfy ACC, if principal two-sided ideals are finitely generated as left ideals, or if the ring is PI. Over Jacobson PI rings, every finitely generated module is Jacobson: its prime submodules are intersections of maximal submodules. For affine PI algebras this extends the Amitsur-Procesi theorem to modules. In every ring with involution, real two-sided ideals are intersections of real prime two-sided ideals. The same holds for real submodules of modules over PI rings and hereditary Noetherian prime rings, but can fail for real left ideals in Noetherian domains. Formally real affine PI algebras need not be real Jacobson: their real prime two-sided ideals need not be intersections of real primitive ideals. We give a sufficient positivity criterion. Over real Jacobson PI rings, finitely generated modules are real Jacobson: their real prime submodules are intersections of real maximal submodules. Over finitely generated free associative algebras, every finitely generated semiprime submodule of a finite free module is a finite intersection of finitely generated prime submodules and an intersection of maximal submodules of finite codimension. Semiprime hulls of finitely generated submodules are finitely generated. Evaluation at finite-dimensional irreducible representations and nonzero vector tuples gives a Hilbert Nullstellensatz over arbitrary fields. For free algebras with involution, the corresponding real results are known over the real or complex numbers when the involution permutes the generators. We extend real prime decomposition to arbitrary fields and involutions, and give new algebraic proofs of the real Nullstellensatz and finite generation of real radicals, without the GNS construction or Groebner bases.

papers.title: Invariant random subgroups of the finitary special linear group over a finite field
papers.abstract: An invariant random subgroup of a discrete group is a conjugation-invariant probability measure on the space of its subgroups. We confirm a conjecture of Simon Thomas and classify the invariant random subgroups of the finitary special and general linear groups over a finite field. These are shown to be stabilizers of random tuples of vectors and functionals. The classification uses the character theory of the finitary special linear group established by Skudlarek and the theory of the invariant random subgroups of the finitary permutation group established by Vershik. In addition, we classify the invariant probability measures for several natural actions of these finitary groups.

papers.title: Mixing Time of the Random-Pair Monte Shuffle
papers.abstract: In the random-pair Monte shuffle on $n$ cards, each step chooses two positions independently and uniformly and exchanges their cards with probability $1/2$. The chosen positions are public; the decisions to exchange cards remain hidden. We prove that the mixing time in expected conditional total variation distance is $2n\log n+O(n)$, with an exact leading constant and an $O(n)$ cutoff window. To our knowledge, this is the first public-schedule Monte shuffle whose full-permutation mixing time has been determined up to an additive $O(n)$ term. The upper bound follows by comparing two executions with the same public schedule to a classical random-transposition walk. For the lower bound, we construct a schedule-dependent test function and estimate its variance using a matrix-averaging operator. Combined with the depth bound of Czumaj and Lingas, the mixing estimate gives public switching networks with at most $2n\log n+O(n)$ switches and $O(\log n)$ depth for fixed error and failure probabilities. The author obtained this result through interaction with GPT-6 Astra.

papers.title: Well-Covered Powers: Cartesian Products and Cayley Graphs
papers.abstract: We study graphs whose powers are well-covered, with an emphasis on Cartesian products and Cayley graphs. We first establish necessary conditions and sufficient criteria for Cartesian products, provide examples showing that a factor need not be well-covered and that two noncomplete factors can have the well-covered powers property, and classify several structured product families. In particular, we construct graphs satisfying the well-covered powers property for arbitrarily large diameters. We then show that the Cartesian square of a connected abelian Cayley graph is well-covered exactly when the graph is complete. We classify the well-covered-power graphs among connected circulant graphs of degree at most four. For Cartesian products of any number of complete graphs, we also prove that the recursive alphabet-size inequalities in the final conjecture are sufficient for all powers to be well-covered, prove partial converses for arbitrarily many factors, and give explicit obstructions for every binary prefix followed by one complete factor.

papers.title: Discontinuities in optimal transport between nonconvex domains
papers.abstract: We develop a new approach to studying discontinuity sets of measure-preserving convex gradient maps between nonconvex domains. Such maps optimize the Euclidean distance squared. Our idea is to introduce a new `phantom' optimal transport problem, that transports the missing mass from the convex hull of the target to the `excess' Monge--Ampère measure of the minimal convex extension of the Brenier potential. We show that the closure of the discontinuity set of the original map contains the support of this phantom target. Moreover, inside a planar source domain these two sets actually coincide; on $n$-dimensional domains they coincide $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$-a.e. The Hausdorff exponent $n-1$ is sharp in every dimension $n\geq3$. For planar polygonal targets, we establish a quantitative global length bound for the closure of the discontinuity set depending only on the target geometry, valid for bounded positive densities.

papers.title: The Complexity of KKT Points of Quadratic Programs with Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
papers.abstract: Computing a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point of a quadratic polynomial over the unit hypercube is known to be $CLS$-complete, when the coefficients of the polynomial are encoded in binary. We prove that the problem remains $CLS$-complete even when the coefficients are encoded in unary. This is the first problem proven to remain $CLS$-hard when the input is given in unary.

papers.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over sextic fields
papers.abstract: We determine all the groups that appear as the torsion group of an elliptic curve over a number field of degree $6$. Apart from the $44$ groups that occur infinitely often, which were determined by Derickx and Sutherland, exactly four groups occur: $\mathbb{Z}/25\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/12\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$. The first three were known to occur, while the group $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ is new. We also show that, up to isomorphism, each of the groups $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ is the torsion group of a single elliptic curve over a single sextic field. The methods build on those developed by Derickx and Najman for quartic fields and by the author for quintic fields. Among the new ingredients are a formal immersion criterion at the prime $2$ which uses the Cartier operator, and arguments with several diamond operators and with cuspidal divisor classes on quotients of modular curves.

papers.title: Markovian Lifts and Multifactor Approximations for Weighted Sub-fractional Brownian Motion
papers.abstract: We construct a Hilbert-space Markovian lift of weighted sub-fractional Brownian motion for $0<b<2$, including the logarithmic case $b=1$. A Laplace factorization represents the process as the boundary value of a forward curve. In the weighted Sobolev space with derivative weight $r^γ/(1+r)^2$, $0<γ<1$, right translation is strongly continuous and the noise operator is Hilbert--Schmidt if and only if $b+γ>1$. The state norm bounds the total variation of initial curves on compact intervals. For locally bounded deterministic temporal weights, this bound allows the driven scalar equation to be restarted from every lifted state. Under spatial Lipschitz assumptions, with additional time and derivative regularity in the Young case, the solution and forward curve form a time-inhomogeneous Markov process with $C_b$-Feller transitions; both coefficients may have linear growth. Discretization of the Laplace variable gives independent Ornstein--Uhlenbeck factors coupled to the original process through the same Gaussian noise. The nonlinear approximations converge uniformly in time in every finite $L^p$. For uniform spectral partitions with balanced cutoffs, the solution rate is $M^{-(b-1)/3}$ for $1<b<2$, while the uniform driver rate is $M^{-b/4}\sqrt{\log(2+M)}$ for $0<b\le1$. Under stronger coefficient assumptions, we derive error bounds for Young solutions and for the fully discrete scheme, retaining the dependence on the spectral cutoff and specifying joint mesh conditions.

papers.title: A Hardy space approximation supporting zero-free half-planes for the $ζ$-function
papers.abstract: By a theorem of Bagchi, the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if $E(s) = 1/s$ belongs to the closed linear span of $G_k(s) = (k^{-s} - k^{-1})ζ(s)/s$, $k \geq 2$, in the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{C}_{1/2})$, where $\mathbb{C}_α$ is the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s) > α$. The formal Möbius expansion $E = \sum_{k \geq 2} μ(k) G_k$ diverges on the critical line, by a theorem of Báez-Duarte. We study it in the scale of spaces $H^2(\mathbb{C}_α)$, where its convergence forces $ζ$ to be zero-free in $\mathbb{C}_α$. We prove that the partial sums $S_n$ converge to $E$ in $H^2(\mathbb{C}_α)$ for every $α> 1$, and that a single zero of $ζ$ in $\mathbb{C}_α$ keeps the best-approximation error $d_n(α)^2$ uniformly away from zero. We express the Möbius error $s_n(α) = \|S_n - E\|^2_α$ as a series with elementary terms, free of $ζ$, and compute it for $n \leq 10^6$: $s_n(1/2)$ oscillates without decaying, whereas for $α> 1/2$ it decays at a rate close to $n^{1-2α}$, much faster than the bound known under RH. On the critical line, $d_n(1/2)^2$ behaves like $0.046/\log n$ for $100 \leq n \leq 5120$, in agreement with earlier computations by Báez-Duarte, Balazard, Landreau and Saias.

papers.title: The finite basis problem for varieties modulo x^3=0
papers.abstract: We prove that any variety of associative algebras over a Noetherian commutative ring with unity satisfying the identity x^3=0 is finitely based. This property has been known for the varieties satisfying the identity x^2=0. On the other hand, there are varieties satisfying the identity x^6=0 that are not finitely based.

papers.title: Rényi mixing bounds for kinetic samplers via $L^2$ hypocoercivity
papers.abstract: We study convergence in Rényi divergence of order two for underdamped Langevin dynamics, the bouncy particle sampler, and the Zigzag sampler, for a target $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb R^d$ that satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality, with $\nabla^2U$ bounded below by a possibly negative constant and, for the Zigzag sampler, also bounded above. For initial laws whose Rényi divergence from equilibrium is at most $R$, we show that it decays exponentially, at a rate that depends on $R$. With the friction or refreshment rate chosen according to $R$, the time needed to reach a fixed accuracy in total variation or in Rényi divergence is of order $\sqrt{R\log R}$ at fixed dimension and target parameters, improving the linear dependence obtained by directly converting exponential $L^2$ decay. The key idea is to use the logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the position target in place of the usual spatial spectral-gap estimate in the $L^2$ hypocoercivity argument. For the bouncy particle and Zigzag samplers, this order is sharp for the Rényi divergence on a one-dimensional Gaussian target, uniformly in the refreshment rate. For the Zigzag sampler in dimension at least two, Gaussian examples show that the mixing-time bound is sharp up to logarithmic factors in the worst case over strongly convex targets, in both the initial divergence and the upper Hessian bound; in particular, strong convexity alone does not give a uniform mixing bound.

papers.title: Exact penalty methods with adaptive discretization for nonsmooth semi-infinite optimization
papers.abstract: The paper considers a nonsmooth semi-infinite optimization problem in which the constraints are reformulated through a value function. Stationary points of the cutting surface approximations are studied, showing that stationarity is preserved in the limit under boundedness of the associated sequence of multipliers. Building on these results, an algorithm that combines the cutting surface approximations with a penalty scheme is devised, together with some proximal variants. An exact penalty result is established under suitable global conditions, and numerical results are reported to compare the methods with existing exact penalty and cutting surface algorithms.

papers.title: A probabilistic score estimation using the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula
papers.abstract: Score-learning methods generally lack pointwise supervision, which affects the training accuracy, particularly in regions where SDE trajectories are rare. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel method called \emph{BEL anchors}, which uses Monte Carlo score estimates at user-selected space-time query points. By combining a Feynman--Kac representation of the Fokker--Planck equation with the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula, our estimator requires neither closed-form transition densities, spatial discretization, nor derivatives of the initial density. We derive its asymptotic variance and use the anchors as sparse supervised targets for existing score-learning objectives. Experiments show that BEL anchors improve implicit score matching in poorly sampled regions, prevent score-PINN collapse, and enable accurate sample regeneration in several numerical examples.

papers.title: The Askey-Wilson Function is the Laplace Transform of a Positive Measure
papers.abstract: The Askey-Wilson function $φ(x, γ)$ is a meromorphic continuation of the Askey-Wilson polynomials in their spectral variable off the lattice $γ= \tilde{a} q^m, m \in \mathbb{Z}_+$. We show that the analytic part of the Askey-Wilson function $φ^{an}(x, \tilde{a} q^γ)$ is the Laplace transform of a positive measure of total measure $φ^{an}(x, s_0) < \infty$, under certain conditions on the parameters governing the function. We deduce log-convexity of this function, as well as positive-definiteness and an integral formula for a certain intertwining operator associated with the Askey-Wilson operator $L$. This offers a $q$-analogue of several results, in the trigonometric limit due to Sahi-McSwiggen, and in the rational (i.e. Dunkl) limit due to Rösler.

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring on Structured Graph Classes: Bounds, Exact Algorithms, and Hardness
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every non-isolated vertex has a neighbor whose color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood. We study this coloring on chordal and ordered bipartite graph classes. For well-partitioned chordal graphs, we prove the tight bound $ω(G)\leq\pcf(G)\leqω(G)+1$ and give an $O(n^2)$ construction from a partition tree. Every assignment of lists of at least $ω(G)+1$ colors also admits a PCF coloring that respects the lists. Deciding whether $ω(G)$ colors suffice is NP-complete, even when the partition tree is a star. This also proves NP-completeness on chordal graphs when the number of colors is part of the input. For interval graphs, we prove that lists of size $ω(G)+1$ always suffice, improving the previous ordinary-coloring bound of $ω(G)+2$. We use matchings to characterize when $ω(G)$ colors suffice and give an endpoint algorithm taking $2^{O(ω(G)^2)}n^{O(1)}$ time. We also characterize the exact value when the clique number is at most three and give a linear-time algorithm from sorted interval endpoints. For biconvex graphs, we prove a tight five-color bound and give a direct exact algorithm taking $O(n^{33})$ time. For bipartite permutation graphs, a smaller dynamic program gives an exact $O(n^{17})$ algorithm. Finally, if a bipartite graph is convex over an ordered shore $X$, we prove the sharp bound $\pcf(G)\leq\lceil\log_2(|X|+1)\rceil+3$ and construct a coloring in linear time from the order.

papers.title: Large time dynamics for non-autonomous weakly damped KdV-Burgers equations on the real line
papers.abstract: The large time dynamics of the weakly damped non-autonomous Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation \begin{equation*} u_t + u_{xxx}+ uu_x + λu - μu_{xx} = g(x,t) \end{equation*} in the phase space $L^2(\mathbb R)$ is investigated. Due to the low regularity of the initial data, the framework of Bourgain spaces is employed. We first obtain the existence of a unique pullback attractor $\{\mathcal A_μ(t)\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ in $L^2(\mathbb R)$ for each $μ\ge 0$. Then we show an optimal asymptotic smoothing effect of the equation, namely the pullback attractor is compact in $H^3(\mathbb R)$. These results are proved by using an energy equation method, splitting solutions into parts with low and high frequencies and exploiting a dispersive regularization. Furthermore, the attractors are shown to be upper semicontinuous as $μ\to 0$ and have finite fractal dimensions in $H^1(\mathbb R)$.

papers.title: Small Hankel operators on weighted Besov spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize bounded small Hankel operators from $B_p(\om)$ to $\overline{B_q(\om)}$ on the polydisc for $0<p,q<\infty$, under explicit conditions relating the kernel parameter to the weight. When $q<p$, boundedness is equivalent to a weighted Besov condition on the symbol; when $p\le q$, it is equivalent to a weighted supremum condition on a shifted radial derivative. In particular, the diagonal case is characterized by the product Bloch space. The proof combines weighted Bergman duality and atomic factorization with local kernel estimates and randomized atomic tests.

papers.title: Min-plus Bruhat decomposition
papers.abstract: We study min-plus Bruhat cells $B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$, where $B_{trop}^{(n)}$ denotes the set of all upper-triangular matrices over $\RR \cup \{\infty\}$, and $p$ is a permutation. It is proved that $\dim (B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p \odot B_{trop}^{(n)})= \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + l(p)$, where $l(p)$ is the length of $p$ in Coxeter generators. Also we provide an explicit description of the cell $B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR) \odot p_0\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR)$ (up to a subset of dimension less than $n^2$) for the highest in Bruhat order permutation $p_0$. Finally, it is shown that for a tropically non-singular matrix $A$ for at most one permutation $p_A$ it can hold $A\in B_{trop}^{(n)}\odot p_A\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$.

papers.title: A Tetration Distribution
papers.abstract: We introduce a one-parameter family of continuous distributions on the unit interval whose cumulative distribution functions are given by the odd-height power towers \(x\uparrow\uparrow n\) (\(n=1,3,5,\dots\)). The associated densities admit a simple recursive formula obtained by logarithmic differentiation. We prove that every such density is strictly positive on \((0,1)\) and integrates to one, thereby establishing that the construction yields a genuine probability distribution. Numerical investigation reveals a characteristic peak--dip--rise shape: a sharp mode lying just below \(e^{-e}\) for all examined heights, followed by a trough and a gradual recovery toward density value~1 at the right endpoint. We then identify the limiting distribution as the height tends to infinity through odd integers.

papers.title: Unital qubit channels are $3$-noisy
papers.abstract: The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated.
