papers.abstract: We construct, for each deterministic Turing machine that halts on all inputs, one polynomial vector field with rational coefficients that performs the same logical computation at unit Euler step, at every smaller or variable step in $(0,1]$ with divergent sum, and along the flow. This unifies discrete-time and continuous-time computation by polynomial dynamics, which earlier characterizations treated separately. For a machine making $T$ transitions in space $H$, a logical scale $h=2^{-s}$ with $s=O(H)$ suffices, with physical time $O(s(T+s))$, drift disturbances up to $h^{2K}$ for a fixed exponent $K$, and $2Ks+3$ fractional bits at unit step. On a fixed compact domain, polynomial time and robust eventual decision characterize P and PSPACE, respectively, with polynomial scale thresholds and no supplied stabilization horizon in the space case. Without sign, floor or conditional primitives, margin amplification at bounded speed, overlapping polynomial gates and interval-product estimates give the common realization, from which we derive shared logical traces, fixed-field PSPACE-complete prediction and a robust safety family with polynomial certificates common to all Euler steps and the flow.

papers.title: Arbitrary Dirichlet Eigenvalue Multiplicities on Smooth Star-Shaped Euclidean Domains
papers.abstract: In every fixed dimension \(N\ge3\), for any finite list of positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\), we construct smooth strictly star-shaped Euclidean domains whose first \(\ell+1\) distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues can have multiplicities \(1,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\) respectively. The condition "star-shaped" is almost optimal in the sense that this statement can not hold for bounded convex domains. In fact, we show that the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue of any bounded convex domain has multiplicity at most $(N-1)(k-1)+1$, and this bound $N$ for the second Dirichlet eigenvalue is sharp.

papers.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
papers.abstract: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.

papers.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and prove that every vector bundle of rank at least three admits smooth connected simply branched spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.

papers.title: Serre's conjectures for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$
papers.abstract: The present article proves (assuming GRH and a minor technical result) the veracity of Serre's conjectures for the field $\Q(\sqrt{13})$. In doing so, we prove a ``reduction to level 1'' result that holds for any real quadratic field with narrow class number one. However we can only establish the needed base cases for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$.

papers.title: Accelerating Nonlinear MPC by Behavior Cloning with Separated Timescales: Application to Nuclear Reactor Load-Following
papers.abstract: Behavior Cloning (BC) of expert controllers for multiscale dynamical systems is challenging: state variables evolving at widely separated timescales induce highly nonlinear couplings that a shared latent space may fail to adequately represent, degrading closed-loop generalization. We propose Structured Representation Learning for Behavior Cloning (SRLBC), an architecture designed to leverage the physical knowledge of multiscale systems in which slow state variables, fast (stiff) state variables, and predictable exogenous inputs evolve at different timescales. On 500 long-horizon roll-outs of a pressurized water reactor (PWR) load-following benchmark -a high-dimensional, stiff industrial system with challenging safety constraints -and across 20 training seeds, separated embeddings systematically outperform shared embedding baselines on cumulative cost, imitation accuracy and constraint satisfaction. The resulting standalone policies approach NMPC closed-loop performance at a computational cost 15 times lower on average. Since standalone policies still leave a few percent of trajectories infeasible, we embed the learned policies in a safety-augmented approximate NMPC framework, in which the optimizer is only called when the predicted input sequence is not certified as safe. This yields controllers still 6.8 times faster than the NMPC controller on average, with a feasibility (i.e., constraint satisfaction) of at least 99.8% for all architectures, SRLBC retaining the lowest closed-loop cost. Under distribution shift, standalone BC policies degrade sharply: SRLBC degrades the least, and once safety-augmented, it retains a feasibility above 98% with the lowest closed-loop cost. Beyond the quantitative results, Jacobian-based sensitivity analysis shows that the resulting controller relies on a sparse and less redundant set of latent features, each attributable to a single group of physical variables, and aligned with the physical timescale decomposition of the system.

papers.title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
papers.abstract: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $Π_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[ρ]\in H^3(BG,Π_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=Π_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.

papers.title: New inhomogeneous Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with large symmetry group
papers.abstract: We study compact non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds endowed with an automorphism group acting with cohomogeneity one. We prove that the Lie algebra of this group is isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ or $\mathbb R^2\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$, provided that the Bismut connection is not flat. In the first case, we explicitly describe all these structures up to homothety and biholomorphic isometry. We also construct explicit families of complete non-compact examples. The resulting non-Bismut-flat threefolds have non-constant scalar curvature and restricted Bismut holonomy $T^1\subset \mathrm{SU}(3)$, and include examples on $S^3\times S^3$ and complete examples on $S^3\times S^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$. Finally, we construct a smooth deformation of a Bismut-flat Samelson structure on $S^3\times S^3$ through non-Bismut-flat Bismut Hermitian-Einstein structures whose complex structures are not compatible with any Bismut-flat metric.

papers.title: The Andreadakis conjecture
papers.abstract: For $n\ge2$, let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, and let $\IA(F_n)$ be the group of automorphisms of $F_n$ acting trivially on its abelianization. Two natural filtrations of $\IA(F_n)$ are its lower central series $γ_c(\IA(F_n))$ and the Andreadakis filtration $\mathrm{I}_{c+1}\mathrm{A}(F_n)$, consisting of automorphisms acting trivially on $F_n/γ_{c+1}(F_n)$, $c \geq 1$. Andreadakis conjectured that these filtrations coincide. We prove that the conjectured equality fails for all $n\ge3$ and $c\ge4$.

papers.title: Deterministic Causal Quantization with Bounded Error: Adaptive Reconstruction and Entropy bounds
papers.abstract: We study compression of real-valued stationary sources under a deterministic error bound: every sample must be reconstructed within a prescribed tolerance $\varepsilon$ on every input sequence. Reconstructions are causal, depending only on present and past inputs. Rates are measured by the entropy of the quantizer output, which block entropy coding can approach, and compared with the minimum rate of unrestricted block quantization under the same error constraint. A uniform scalar quantizer with cells of width $2\varepsilon$ is within one bit per sample of this minimum whenever finite-entropy scalar quantization is possible, without density, independence, or mixing assumptions. Under entropy and Sobolev regularity conditions, the gap is at most $2\mathcal{J}\varepsilon^2/(π^2\ln 2)$, where $\mathcal{J}$ is the asymptotic Fisher information per sample. Thus the cost of causal reconstruction vanishes at a quadratic rate as the tolerance decreases. A uniform grid, however, cannot adapt to the source. We construct an adaptive quantizer whose encoder and decoder maintain a common finite set of reconstruction values, updated from the transmitted symbols alone; suitable initialization reproduces any uniform grid. When its initial values are at least $\varepsilon$ apart, its rate is within two bits per sample of the minimum for every such source. For sources uniform within separated intervals of width $2\varepsilon$, storing the interval centers attains the minimum and its Shannon lower bound. Such configurations can outperform every uniform grid of the same cell width: over sources with well-separated intervals, the best uniform grid's worst-case excess rate is $1/(2\ln 2)\approx 0.72$ bit per sample.

papers.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{η_1,\ldots,η_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $η_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{η_i,η_j\in S:η_i\neqη_j}|\mathcal N(η_i-η_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

papers.title: The effective mass of the Pauli-Fierz electron: a cutoff-independent lower bound and the breakdown of mass renormalization
papers.abstract: We study the effective mass of a spinless non-relativistic electron coupled to the quantized transverse electromagnetic field (the Pauli-Fierz model without external potential), with bare mass $m$, fine structure constant $α=e^2/4π$ and a sharp ultraviolet cutoff $Λ$. We define $1/(2m_{\rm eff}):=\limsup_{P\to0}(E(P)-E(0))/|P|^2$ for the fiber ground state energy $E(P)$; this agrees with the curvature mass whenever $E$ is twice differentiable at zero. By scaling, $h=m_{\rm eff}/m$ depends only on $α$ and $λ=Λ/m$. For all $α>0$ and $λ\ge1$ we prove $h\ge1+0.3441\,α/(1+0.2985\sqrtα+0.1252\,α)$, a bound independent of the cutoff; with the band extended to the cutoff, its first order coefficient in $α$ is the perturbative one of Hiroshima and Spohn. At fixed $α>0$ we further prove $h\geλ^{8/7-ε}$ for every $ε>0$ and all sufficiently large $λ$. Hence $ι_{\rm PF}(α):=\inf_{λ>0}h/λ>0$: at fixed coupling, a bare mass reproducing a prescribed physical mass $m_{\rm phys}$ can exist only if $Λ\le m_{\rm phys}/ι_{\rm PF}(α)$. This proves the obstruction to mass renormalization at fixed physical mass anticipated by Lieb and Loss (2002). The first bound uses a coherent translation of the field applied to the ground state as a trial state. The second uses the sharp self-energy asymptotics of a companion paper and a position estimator constructed from the local centre of a shallow level set of the photon cloud.

papers.title: The sharp leading asymptotics of the self-energy of the spinless Pauli-Fierz model
papers.abstract: We study the self-energy $E_0(α,Λ)$ of the spinless Pauli-Fierz model with a sharp ultraviolet cutoff $Λ$, retaining the vacuum contribution of the $A^2$ term (no normal ordering); $α=e^2/4π$ is the fine structure constant. Lieb and Loss proved lower and upper bounds of orders $α^{1/2}Λ^{3/2}$ and $α^{2/7}Λ^{12/7}$ for large $Λ$ and suggested that the upper bound, which comes from product states, gives the correct order. We prove that, for every fixed $α>0$, $E_0(α,Λ)=(1+o(1))\,c_α\,α^{2/7}Λ^{12/7}$, with an explicit constant $c_α=0.99338\ldots$, as $Λ\to\infty$. The same asymptotics hold uniformly in the joint limit $Λ/α\to\infty$, $α^{5/2}Λ\to\infty$, provided $\log(2+α)=o((Λ/α)^{1/21})$. The infimum of the energy over product states has the same leading asymptotics. The upper bound follows from a coherent state bound for the field energy in a fixed electron density. For the lower bound we combine a periodization of the field, a blockwise Born-Oppenheimer bound, and a lower bound on the magnetic Neumann Laplacian on a cube for band-limited fields. The magnetic estimate follows from a non-concentration bound for the vorticity of band-limited fields satisfying a weighted gradient condition.

papers.title: Failure of interior $L^p$ estimates for nonlocal elliptic equations with continuous kernels
papers.abstract: Let $0<σ<2$ and $1\leq p<\infty$. We construct a fixed linear nonlocal elliptic operator $L$ and functions $u_m\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ such that \[ \|u_m\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}+\|Lu_m\|_{L^p(B_2)}\longrightarrow0, \qquad \liminf_{m\to\infty}\|(-Δ)^{σ/2}u_m\|_{L^p(B_1)}>0. \] The kernel is symmetric in the increment variable, uniformly elliptic, and satisfies the standard bounds on its first two derivatives in that variable. Its dependence on $x$ has a uniform modulus of continuity of order $(\log(1/r))^{-1/2}$ as $r\downarrow0$. Moreover, $\|Du_m\|_{L^p(B_4)}\to0$ for $σ>1$, and these norms remain bounded for $σ=1$. Thus the interior $L^p$ estimates for translation-invariant operators do not extend to this class under mere continuity in $x$.

papers.title: On the Error Analysis of Triangular Transport Maps for Conditional Generation via MMD-based Objectives
papers.abstract: Conditional generative models parameterized by triangular transport maps are widely used for conditional sampling, yet theoretical guarantees on the quality of the conditional measures they produce remain scarce. We address this question for minimum divergence estimators of triangular maps. We use MMD-based objectives as a tractable setting in which the gap between joint and conditional errors can be analyzed precisely, and we measure performance through the average conditional estimation error, defined as the squared maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between the estimated and the true conditionals, averaged over the conditioning variable. We first show that the common practice of minimizing a joint MMD may fail to recover the conditionals: writing the joint and the conditional criteria as quadratic energies of the same conditional mean embedding residual, we prove that, for parametric classes, joint minimizers are generically inconsistent in the misspecified setting. We then analyze an estimator that directly minimizes the conditional criterion through a surrogate loss computable from joint target samples and reference samples. We prove a non-asymptotic error bound that decomposes the average conditional estimation error into approximation, estimation, and reference sampling errors, with fast rates independent of the ambient dimension in the parametric setting. Finally, for joint MMDs built from concentrating Gaussian kernels on the conditioning variable, we show that the joint criterion approximates a density-reweighted version of the conditional one, and we derive an error bound for the joint minimizer whose rate suffers from a curse of dimensionality in the conditioning variable. Our results suggest that training criteria for conditional generative models should target the conditional rather than the joint error, a principle that extends to other divergences and to dynamic transport.

papers.title: Who pays for urban environment management? The role of the third-party service provider
papers.abstract: The dominant contemporary paradigm of direct state-led urban environmental regulation entails significant risks, including high administrative burden, frequent conflicts with polluting entities, and economic vulnerabilities for those sources. To address these deficiencies, this paper integrates third-party service provider (TPSP) into China's existing management framework as a beneficial extension beyond conventional government intervention. Utilizing an evolutionary game approach, we compare two distinct institutional settings, a non-integration management mode and an integration management mode, and scrutinize the evolutionary dynamics across both two- and three-dimensional systems. To enhance system robustness, we embed a strategic behavior-based dynamic punishment mechanism that effectively eliminates the perturbing effects of varied penalty rules, thereby steering all stakeholders toward an ideal stable state. This comparative institutional analysis isolates the marginal contribution of third-party intermediation, specifies when outsourcing environmental services outperforms direct government enforcement, and reframes evolutionary game theory as a design device for institutional self-correction. Furthermore, a predefined variable importance analysis is conducted to highlight critical factors warranting attention in practical policy implementation. Extensive simulation experiments, carried out under diverse system-level and parameter-level conditions, validate the theoretical properties of our model. The findings offer concrete managerial insights to inform the formulation of more effective urban environmental supervision regulations.

papers.title: Leafrians, Frobenius splittings, and moduli spaces over Poisson surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Poisson surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, and let $s\in H^0(X,ω_X^{-1})$ be nonzero. We construct an anticanonical section associated to $s$, called the leafrian, on moduli spaces $M$ of stable objects on $X$, including the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons. The leafrian splits $M$ if and only if $s^{p-1}$ Frobenius splits the base. It is invariant under the Hamiltonian flows of Bottacin's Poisson structure on $M$, so every compatibly split subvariety of $M$ is a Poisson subvariety. Furthermore, the leafrian extends to an anticanonical section on the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$, and splits $\bar M$ under the same criterion. As a consequence, in characteristic zero, for $X$ a smooth projective Poisson surface with a smooth or empty anticanonical divisor and $ρ>0$ (positive leaf rank), the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$ satisfies Kodaira-type cohomology vanishing, including singular $\bar M$.

papers.title: Sharp Variational estimates for Schrödinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
papers.abstract: For $p\geq2$ and $r\geq 1$, we prove the sharp strong $r$-variation estimate for solutions to the free Schrödinger equation $$ \bigl\|V^r_{[0,1]}\{e^{itΔ}f\}\bigr\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)} \lesssim \|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^2)}. $$ The estimate holds if $s> s(p,r)$ and fails if $s< s(p,r)$, where $$s(p,r)=\max\left\{ \frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{p}-\frac12,\, \frac{2}{r}-\frac{2}{p},\, \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r},\, \frac{2}{p}-\frac13,\, 1-\frac{2}{p} \right\}.$$ In particular, $s(3,\infty)=1/3$. Thus our result yields a sharp variational extension of the two-dimensional Schrödinger maximal estimate of Du, Guth, and Li [{Ann. Math.}, 186, 607--640 (2017)]. The proof employs fractal restriction estimates to eliminate the regularity loss originating from the summation in the variation norm.

papers.title: Weyl Bounds for $\operatorname{GL}_2\times \operatorname{GL}_2$ Rankin--Selberg $L$-functions via Short Spectral Moments
papers.abstract: Let $f$ and $g$ be Hecke--Maass cusp forms of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with spectral parameters $t_f$ and $t_g$, respectively. Let $T$ be a large parameter and put $L = |T-t_g|.$ We prove the Lindelöf-on-average estimate \[ \sum_{ |t_f-T|\leq H} \left|L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right)\right|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon} T^{1+\varepsilon}H, \] uniformly in the range \[ T^{1/3+\varepsilon}\ll H,\qquad HT^\varepsilon\ll L\leq T. \] As an immediate consequence, in the generic range when both $|t_g|$ and $L$ are of size $T$, we obtain the Weyl bound \[ L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right) \ll_\varepsilon C(f\times g)^{1/6+\varepsilon}. \]

papers.title: Trace Inverse Estimates and Kernel-based Meshfree Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Interface Problems
papers.abstract: Kernel Galerkin methods allow meshfree trial spaces to be generated independently in each material subdomain and refined through their center sets, without generating an approximation mesh. We establish trace inverse estimates for products of Sobolev-kernel spaces on Lipschitz subdomains and use them to analyze symmetric Nitsche discretizations of linear elliptic interface problems. The estimates control gradient traces on subdomain boundaries by subdomain gradients, the interface jump, and an exterior boundary trace. Their conormal form supplies the flux control required for stability directly from the kernel and center assumptions, without a separate discrete flux hypothesis. For quasi-uniform center families with comparable fill distances and a fixed kernel scale, we obtain well-posedness for sufficiently large penalty parameters independent of refinement. We prove energy and $L^2$ error bounds of orders $h^{s-1}$ and $h^s$ for piecewise $H^s$ solutions, $2\le s\le m$, where $h$ is the maximum subdomain fill distance and $m$ is the kernel Sobolev order. The $L^2$ bound additionally requires piecewise $H^2$ regularity of the homogeneous adjoint interface problem. For kernels $Φ_m(\varepsilon\,\cdot)$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$, we derive a scale-explicit condition-number bound in the kernel-translate basis and an $O(h^{-2})$ bound in an $L^2$-orthonormal basis. The analysis assumes exact geometry and integration. Planar experiments examine convergence and kernel scaling, while a three-dimensional heat-conduction problem in a curved composite illustrates the method.

papers.title: From Inverse Vandermonde Matrices to the Shift Structure of the Dirichlet Eta and Beta Functions
papers.abstract: We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the inverse of Vandermonde matrices with nodes drawn from the quadratic sequences $u\_n = n^2$ and $u\_n = (n -1/2 )^2$. We derive new limiting formulas for the entries of the inverses, expressed through the even and odd central factorial numbers. These formulas are then used to study the asymptotic behavior of a ratio of determinants involving a modified Vandermonde matrix. For each node sequence, the corresponding determinant ratio converges uniformly on compact subsets of the complex plane to an explicit expression involving the Dirichlet eta or beta function. We then study a family of related functions and, using an inversion theorem, exhibit their shift structure: the shifted values of the eta and beta functions are recovered as finite linear combinations of the family, which yields an integral form of these values as integrals of polynomials related to the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials against generalized (half-)Clausen functions. A unified form of the shift representation, valid for an arbitrary base point z with Re(z) > 0, brings the eta and beta families under a single theorem. On the critical line the representation is unitary and the values on the two sides are complex conjugates.

papers.title: On the stabilizing effects of rotation on stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the half spaces in scale-critical spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier--Stokes equations with the Coriolis force in the half space with the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We show the existence of a unique small solution in the scale-critical Besov spaces. In particular, for any boundary data with a vanishing normal component, and for any external forces, we establish the well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary value problem when the speed of rotation is sufficiently large. In the proof, to exploit the stabilizing effect of the Coriolis term, we employ two explicit formulas depending on the relation between the horizontal frequency and the magnitude of the rotation speed.

papers.title: On quandles with isomorphic enveloping groups
papers.abstract: We give a method to construct two injective connected finite quandles of different cardinal with isomorphic enveloping groups.

papers.title: Rapid Mixing for Sampling Colorings of Random Graphs up to Tree Uniqueness Threshold
papers.abstract: We study the mixing time of the single-site Glauber dynamics for sampling proper $q$-colorings on sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)$. We prove that, whenever $q \ge (1 + o_d(1))d$, Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time with high probability over $\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. This improves the previous bound $q = (α^* + o_d(1))d$ where $α^* = 1.7632...$ is the unique solution of $x = \exp(1/x)$ on $[1, \infty)$ by Efthymiou, Hayes, Štefankovič, and Vigoda (SODA, 2018) and asymptotically matches the uniqueness threshold on infinite regular trees. Our proof has three main ingredients. First we establish logarithmic bounds on the spectral and coupling independence constants of the Gibbs distribution by extending the tree analysis of Chen, Liu, Mani, and Moitra (J. ACM, 2026). Second, we extend the entropy-factorization framework for two-spin systems on random graphs, developed by Bezáková, Galanis, Goldberg, and Štefankovič (TALG, 2024), to proper colorings by introducing a buffer around high-degree vertices. Finally, we compare the resulting heat-bath block dynamics with the single-site Glauber dynamics.

papers.title: Dg models for derived differential operators
papers.abstract: We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith--Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $\mathcal E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that this dg algebra fits into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer--Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$. In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg $\mathcal E_M$-modules and the derived category of \mbox{$D$-modules} on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra $\mathcal E_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.

papers.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
papers.abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by Pólya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

papers.title: Stationary Unit Roots and Inference in Softplus INGARCH Models
papers.abstract: A unit root makes linear count time series models such as the Poisson INGARCH(1,1) nonstationary. We show that a softplus link changes this. Weiß, Zhu and Hoshiyar (2022) introduced softplus INGARCH models and gave a sufficient condition for stationarity. For Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related versions of these models, we obtain the necessary and sufficient condition, which allows a unit root. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail, and the observations can have infinite variance or long memory. To our knowledge, this is the first stationary unit root established for an INGARCH-type count model. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is asymptotically normal both below and at the unit root, including cases with infinite variance. Two applications show that unit-root conclusions can depend on the softplus scale.

papers.title: Disproving two conjectures on the cospectrality of complete tripartite graphs
papers.abstract: The spectral distance between two non-isomorphic graphs of the same order is the lp-distance between their ordered adjacency spectra, and the cospectrality of a graph G on a family Gn is the minimum such distance from G to another graph in Gn. Abdollahi and Zakeri (Ars Math. Contemp. 22(1) (2022) P1.06) conjectured that, for every n >= 4 and for p in {1, 2}, the cospectrality of the complete tripartite graph Kn,n,n among all graphs on 3n vertices is attained exactly at Kn-1,n,n+1. We disprove both conjectures for every n >= 4. As a counterexample we use the graph Hn = (n - 1)K1 nabla (K1 union Kn,n), whose spectrum we determine. It yields cs(1)(Kn,n,n) <= 1 + o(1) and cs(2)(Kn,n,n) <= 1/2 + o(1) as n -> infinity, contrary to the conjectured values. We also study the cospectrality of Kn,n,n for p = 2, asymptotically, among complete multipartite graphs with possibly added isolated vertices. We conclude the paper by posing a conjecture that Hn is the unique graph nearest to Kn,n,n for p in {1, 2} and every n >= 3, and a problem asking whether every connected graph H with sigma(2)(Kn,n,n,H) < 2/3 has an adjacency matrix of rank at most 5.

papers.title: Near-boundary rigidity and strict maximum modulus for Neumann eigenfunctions on convex planar domains
papers.abstract: We develop a near-boundary rigidity theorem for arbitrary nonzero Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded convex planar domains. Precisely, if an eigenfunction $u$ with positive eigenvalue $μ$ has an interior maximum-modulus point $p$ satisfying $\sqrtμ\,\text{dist}(p,\partialΩ)\leπ/\sqrt3$, then $Ω$ must be a rectangle and $u$ must be a cosine of one coordinate, and $μ\ge4μ_2(Ω)$, with the factor $4$ being sharp. This shows that a scale-invariant distance condition at just one maximum-modulus point determines the geometry of the entire domain and the explicit form of the eigenfunction. We further prove that the maximum modulus of every second Neumann eigenfunction on a bounded convex planar domain is attained only on the boundary, without assuming boundary smoothness or eigenvalue simplicity. Moreover, we also prove strict boundary maximum modulus for higher Neumann eigenfunctions under suitable conditions, including all third Neumann eigenfunctions on arbitrary triangles.

papers.title: An application of the parameterization method to evolution flows associated to nonautonomous systems
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry. We consider a time-dependent vector field $X : \mathbb{R} \times M \to TM$ with $X_t:=X(t,\cdot) \in \mathfrak{X}^r(M)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies some further uniform continuity assumptions. We suppose that $X$ admits a globally defined integral curve $γ: \mathbb{R} \to M$. To any isolated subset $Ω$ of the Sacker-Sell spectrum of $t \mapsto \nabla X_t(γ(t))$, Sacker-Sell theory associates a subbundle $\mathscr{N}^Ω$ of $T_γM$ invariant under $\nabla X_t$. Under additional nonresonance conditions on $Ω$, we prove, by an application of the parameterization method (Cabré et al., 2003), the existence of an invariant topological submanifold $\mathscr{W}^Ω\subset \mathbb{R} \times M$ with $C^r$ fibers $W_t^Ω:= \mathscr{W}^Ω\cap \{t\} \times M$ that is unique in a sufficiently smooth subclass of invariant manifolds uniformly tangent to $\mathscr{N}^Ω$ (made precise later). We moreover show regularity of $\mathscr{W}^Ω$ with respect to parameters, and characterize the attraction towards $\mathscr{W}^Ω$ via a foliation in the case $Ω$ is the slowest part of the spectrum.

papers.title: CM fibers of Shimura parametrizations and thirteen proofs of the class number one theorem
papers.abstract: We determine thirteen entirely CM identity fibers of Shimura parametrizations attached to elliptic curves of rank two and conductor below $2000$. Each yields a proof of the imaginary quadratic class number one theorem. The argument combines the Gross--Zagier formula with the Ribet--Takahashi degree comparison to show that the fiber is completely explained by known CM points.

papers.title: Quantum integrals II: Dominated and almost uniform convergence
papers.abstract: One main aim of our paper is to formulate noncommutative versions of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem in the setting of quantum integration theory on von Neumann algebras. Our starting point is a reformulation of classical dominated convergence in terms of weak* convergence. Using our recent sequential-continuity theorem, we obtain dominated convergence formulations for sequentially normal states and, under domination by a fixed bounded integrable majorant, for sequentially normal weights. Integrable, possibly unbounded, majorants are treated first in the tracial setting, then for arbitrary von Neumann algebras using Haagerup's \(L^1\) space, and finally using normal semifinite weights and their GNS representations. For any faithful normal semifinite weight phi, weak* convergence of norm-bounded sequences is characterized by `integrating against' bounded positive integrable majorants. We also study noncommutative almost uniform and local almost uniform convergence, and make the relationship with the order convergence results of Chetcuti et al. explicit. In particular, for norm-bounded sequences, local phi-bilaterally almost uniform convergence implies weak* convergence and \(\|h^{1/2}(x_n-x)h^{1/2}\|_1\to0\) for every positive Haagerup L1 density h, without assuming \(σ\)-finiteness. We also prove a dominated convergence theorem in the predual: fixed positive order domination and Petz's almost uniform convergence imply convergence in the predual norm. We establish implications and equivalences among these convergence notions, connecting dominated convergence with tracial and nontracial integration.

papers.title: NP-hardness of additive approximation for generalized Turán problems
papers.abstract: Given a graph $T$ and a nonempty family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs, let $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{F}$-free subgraph of a host graph $G$. Alon and Shikhelman [Algorithmica, 2022] conjectured that if $e(T)> 0$ and no member of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$, approximating $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ within an additive error of $n^{v(T)-\varepsilon}$ is NP-hard for an input graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. Previous advances toward this conjecture include the resolution of the canonical case $T=K_2$ by Alon, Shapira, and Sudakov [Ann. of Math., 2009], as well as the case of $\operatorname{ex}(G,K_m,K_k)$ by Alon and Shikhelman. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for every bipartite graph $T$ and every clique $T$. Our proof reductions combine several techniques, including iterative leaf additions, symmetric rooted extensions, and random transversals. Together, they encode the optimal value of the NP-hard Max $r$-Colorable Subgraph problem into the objectives $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ for a suitably constructed graph $G$.

papers.title: QPTAS for Max Weight Independent Set in Graphs with Strongly Edge-Sublinear Separators
papers.abstract: A hereditary graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if, for some constant $0 \leqslant b < 1$, every graph in the class with $m$ edges admits a balanced separator of size $\mathcal O(m^b)$. We show that Max Weight Independent Set (MWIS) admits a deterministic quasipolynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS) on every such class. In particular, this applies to graphs excluding any fixed graph as an induced minor, by a separator theorem of Korhonen and Lokshtanov [SODA 2024]. Our theorem generalizes the QPTASes for axis-parallel rectangles [Adamaszek and Wiese, FOCS 2013] and polygons [Adamaszek, Har-Peled, and Wiese, JACM 2019], or equivalently for packing connected subgraphs of a planar graph [Pilipczuk, van Leeuwen, and Wiese, Algorithmica 2020]. It also generalizes the QPTAS for MWIS on hereditary classes with strongly sublinear separators measured in vertices [Dvořák, EJC 2018; Dvořák and Lahiri, ESA 2021], as well as the QPTASes for graphs excluding specific induced minors [Chudnovsky et al., arXiv 2025; Bonnet et al., SWAT 2026; Czyżewska et al., arXiv 2026].

papers.title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
papers.abstract: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. Call a division ring index-symmetric if every division subring with at least one finite index has equal finite indices. It has been a long-standing open question whether there exists an index-symmetric division ring that is infinite-dimensional over its center. We give the first such examples: using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. This applies to the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, to the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero, to quantum skew fields, to the quotient division rings of noetherian AS-regular Hopf domains, and to the quotient and degree-zero division rings of three- and four-dimensional elliptic Sklyanin algebras, which we show to be twisted Calabi--Yau. In particular, every division ring on Artin's list of noncommutative surfaces is index-symmetric.

papers.title: Campana strong approximation on generalized Markoff surfaces
papers.abstract: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.

papers.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube
papers.abstract: For a known finite-dimensional model subspace, classical Gaussian regression theory guarantees that least squares eventually attains the parametric rate, with prediction error scaling as the subspace dimension divided by the sample size. Yet subspaces with the same number of unknown coefficients can require very different sample sizes to reach this regime. For subspaces of polynomials on the Boolean cube, a fundamental question is how restrictions on degree and ambient dimension jointly determine this threshold. Our main result sharply characterizes the worst-subspace minimax sample threshold over a substantial parameter range, revealing an exponential dependence on degree and precisely quantifying the joint effects of degree, ambient dimension, and subspace dimension. A small modification of our lower-bound construction reveals a strong separation: a single subspace can admit noiseless recovery with optimal sample complexity independent of degree, yet require essentially the worst-case sample size, exponential in degree, to attain the noisy parametric rate. To establish the sampling lower bound, we sharpen the Polyanskiy-Samorodnitsky uncertainty principle (J. Funct. Anal., '19) to uniformly optimal precision and extend its concentration guarantee to large subspaces in which every function concentrates most of its energy on one shared Hamming ball. The sampling upper bound follows from the sharp moment bound of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, '21) combined with empirical-process bounds.

papers.title: Statistics of divisor functions over function fields
papers.abstract: Extending recent works on the restricted divisor function over integers, we consider an analogue of this function over the function field. We provide some exact and asymptotic formulas related to this function.

papers.title: Infinite Girth, Finite Quotients, and Nielsen Connectivity in Groups
papers.abstract: We develop new methods for studying infinite girth in finitely generated residually finite groups, particularly those containing no non-abelian free subgroups and satisfying no non-trivial group law. Our main contribution is a probabilistic Nielsen-component lifting principle, based on product replacement graphs, which provides a criterion for transferring suitable generation and word-avoidance properties of finite quotients to the ambient group. As an application, we prove that every finitely generated group admitting infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic non-abelian finite simple quotients has infinite girth, with extensions to quasisimple and, under additional hypotheses, almost-simple quotients. We further establish infinite girth for the B. H. Neumann group and the Bou-Rabee-Seward group, obtaining new results on the occurrence of non-abelian finite simple quotients and sections. By a different construction, we also prove that Alt_fin(Z) semidirect Z has infinite girth. Finally, we establish a marked finite-quotient characterization of infinite girth for finitely generated residually finite groups and prove that, for linear groups over fields of characteristic zero, large marked girth can be realized in congruence quotients. We conclude with several open questions and remarks arising from our results.

papers.title: Edge-Connectivity versus Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature
papers.abstract: We systematically explore the relationship between edge-connectivity and Lin--Lu--Yau curvature for graphs. The intuition is that a connected graph with large Lin--Lu--Yau curvature should also have large edge-connectivity, and vice versa under suitable conditions. We prove that the edge-connectivity of a connected graph is bounded lower by the product of its minimum degree, its Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and the constant $\frac{3}{2}$. We also provide two lower bounds on the edge-connectivity of a graph that guarantee positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature, and discuss the sharpness of these bounds.

papers.title: Fast Almost-Uniform Sampling of Random $k$-SAT Solutions
papers.abstract: We study approximately uniform sampling of satisfying assignments from random $k$-SAT formulas. Fix a constant $B>0$. For every $k\ge 2^{20}$ and density $0<α\le 2^k/k^{16}$, we prove that, with high probability over a random formula on $n$ variables, every accuracy $n^{-B}\le\varepsilon\le 1/2$ admits a sampler whose output distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the uniform distribution on satisfying assignments with expected running time $$\widetilde O_B\left(\mathrm{poly}(k,α+1)n^{2+η}\right),\quad 0<η\le 2^{16-k}.$$ In particular, the exponent of $n$ is $2+O(2^{-k})$ while the dependence on the width and density is polynomial with a universal degree. This improves the parameter-dependent polynomial exponent of the sampling algorithm of Chen, Lonkar, Wang, Yang, and Yin (STOC 2025) in the density regime $2^k/\mathrm{poly}(k)$. Our algorithm separates a high-degree core from the remaining variables. Every residual formula on the good variables is a deletion subformula of a common bounded-dependency formula. Adapting the rejection--repair framework of Liu, Wang, Yin, Zhang and Zhou (arXiv 2026), we construct an executable sampler for all such residual formulas using ordinary connected violation sets replacing weighted 2-tree witnesses and use it to simulate approximate block heat-bath updates on the core. To analyze the resulting core chain, we integrate out the good variables, represent the core marginal by an absolutely convergent polymer expansion and combine a component-swap variance comparison with an adaptive exploration bound. Absorbing single-component interactions into the local weights leaves interactions of cluster size at least two; retaining their additional decay gives a spectral gap of at least $1/(2s n^{2^{12-k}})$ where $s$ counts core components. Together with the residual sampler, this yields the stated running time.

papers.title: A curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form of a regular surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and its applications
papers.abstract: We study a Monge normal form of a surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ based on the principal axes of its curvature ellipse. The curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form is obtained using only Euclidean motions of the ambient space and local reparameterizations of the surface, and preserves the Euclidean invariants of the curvature ellipse, including its semi-axis lengths up to their ordering. We also give applications of this normal form to the $2$-jet geometry of surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and to the geometry of their orthogonal projections.

papers.title: Iwahori Gaiotto conjecture for cotangent type
papers.abstract: We study the Iwahori Gaiotto conjecture for cotangent types and its application to the representation theory of the (mixed, small, and Lusztig) quantum supergroups. Using local and global models and SW-Zastava spaces, we construct factorization functors and compare the Iwahori Gaiotto category with the category $O$ of the mixed quantum supergroup. We then study the images of intersection cohomology sheaves and the metaplectic Hecke action. In type A, we describe the finite and affine monodromic categories, the corresponding Yokonuma--Hecke actions, and their role in the Kazhdan--Lusztig algorithm. The last section treats the pointwise purity.

papers.title: Biased random walk on a locally infinite Galton-Watson tree
papers.abstract: We propose a new variant of a biased random walk on a Galton-Watson tree, in which some vertices have infinitely many children. These vertices induce a natural regeneration structure, which allows to study differentiability and also monotonicity of the speed of the random walk in the bias parameter. In particular, we give explicit examples of offspring distributions for which the speed is strictly monotone increasing. Additionally, we show that the speed in this model is the limit of the speed of random walks on appropriate locally finite trees.

papers.title: Model-Based Koopman-Galerkin Lifting for Guaranteed H-Infinity Output Feedback Control of Nonlinear Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a model-based Koopman-Galerkin framework for output-feedback control of nonlinear systems with known dynamics. With a suitable actuator augmentation, the finite-dimensional realization preserves the actuator dynamics and the constant input matrix. The approach is based on an exact decomposition of the lifted dynamics into an LTI system and a finite-order closure residual. It also applies to non-control-affine systems and allows dictionaries that do not span an invariant subspace. Regional bounds are derived for the closure residual, actuator-realization defect, and output-reconstruction error. We use these bounds to formulate a standard $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ output-feedback problem. The controller is linear and dynamic and is implemented using only the measured tracking error. Neither full-state measurements nor a separate state observer are required. Lifting is performed offline. With the state coordinates retained in the dictionary, we obtain explicit transient bounds on the original state and tracking error. A sufficient condition for regional containment is also given. Under this condition, the nonlinear closed loop is forward complete, and the state and tracking error are uniformly ultimately bounded. The cart-pendulum example illustrates the nonlinear closed-loop guarantees. The proposed output feedback gives lower RMSE and peak tracking error on average than Jacobian-based $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ feedback, full-state backstepping, and Koopman-based hybrid MPC.

papers.title: Diffusions with critical divergence-free drifts: Varadhan asymptotics and path-law singularity
papers.abstract: We study the Euclidean Varadhan formula (EVF) and path laws for diffusions with critical divergence-free drifts in dimension $d\geq2$. For drifts given by smooth bounded skew-symmetric stream matrices, we prove a quantitative lower bound under a sector condition with a lower-order term. Its constants depend only on the dimension and the sector condition data. By approximation, the locally uniform Euclidean lower bound holds for all divergence-free $L^\infty_t{\rm BMO}^{-1}_x$ drifts. However, a time-dependent counterexample shows that EVF can fail even for a drift in $L^\infty_tL^d_x$. A complementary upper bound is given under a structural decomposition condition. In particular, for every time-independent $L^{d,\infty}$ drift (without any smallness assumption), and the decoupled diffusion associated with the two-dimensional vorticity equation, the EVF holds. Finally, we construct a time-independent $L^d$ drift whose SDE has a unique strong solution from the origin and whose path law is mutually singular with the corresponding driftless Brownian law. The same diffusion satisfies EVF, showing that Brownian short-time endpoint costs can persist despite singularity of the path law.

papers.title: Dunkl--BMO functions representable in terms of generalized balayage of Carleson measures and an application
papers.abstract: We characterize compactly supported functions $f$ in Dunkl--BMO spaces as those that can be written as \begin{equation*} f=g+\widetilde{S}_{μ,\mathcal{P}}, \end{equation*} the sum of some bounded function $g$ and the generalized balayage $\widetilde{S}_{μ,\mathcal{P}}$ of a Carleson measure on $\mathbb{R}^{N}\times(0,\infty)$ associated with the Dunkl--Poisson semigroup. As a direct application of this representation of Dunkl--BMO functions, we establish a new characterization of the Hardy space in the Dunkl setting via a principal value integral related to $\widetilde{S}_{μ,\mathcal{P}}$. Moreover, analogous conclusions hold for the Dunkl--heat semigroup as well.

papers.title: Analyticity and tautness of smooth Dupin submanifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth immersed Euclidean submanifold is locally Nash if it satisfies the Dupin condition on the regular part of its unit normal bundle. This condition is equivalent to the Morse-Bott property of all squared distance functions and, for compact connected embedded submanifolds, to tautness over $\mathbb{Z}_2$. No local finiteness assumption on the regular locus, or regularity assumption on its complement, is required. We also prove that, in each fixed Euclidean space, every compact connected smooth taut submanifold can be joined to one of finitely many representatives by a Nash isotopy through taut embedded submanifolds. In each fixed intrinsic dimension, we also obtain only finitely many diffeomorphism types admitting taut embeddings in Euclidean spaces. We first treat hypersurfaces by combining a dimension-dependent degree bound on proper Dupin pieces with a continuation argument using finite jets and resultants. An analytic Hessian criterion then gives the Morse-Bott property, and small tubes extend the conclusions to arbitrary codimension. The degree bound also provides uniform semialgebraic complexity. Together with the semialgebraicity of tautness in parameter families and Nash triviality, this yields the finiteness and deformation results. Classical classification theorems give further topological restrictions.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Strong Roberson Conjecture
papers.abstract: We refute the Strong Roberson Conjecture, which asserts that adding any graph outside a graph class closed under minors and disjoint unions strictly increases the distinguishing power of homomorphism counts from that class. More precisely, we construct connected graphs $H$ for which homomorphism counts from graphs excluding $H$ as a minor determine the number of homomorphisms from $H$ to any target graph. We also refute the analogous conjecture with immersions in place of minors. The proof introduces a method for deriving exact homomorphism count dependence from modular equivalences. We obtain these modular equivalences for infinitely many primes using prime-order automorphisms and the corresponding orbit quotients. We complete the refutations by proving that suitable circulant graphs with two jump lengths and related cubic bipartite graphs exclude their corresponding orbit quotients as minors and immersions, respectively.

papers.title: QWEP stability under twisted crossed products
papers.abstract: We study the QWEP property of twisted crossed products and its relation to Fourier multiplier transference on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We show that QWEP is not preserved by crossed products of QWEP von Neumann algebras by hyperlinear groups. Our examples include trace-preserving actions of a torsion-free residually finite Kazhdan group on a diffuse abelian algebra and on the hyperfinite type II$_1$ factor. We also obtain non-QWEP crossed products with nontrivial scalar cocycles. For scalar twists, we prove that a finite trace-preserving crossed product is QWEP if and only if its ordinary crossed product and its twisted group von Neumann algebra are QWEP. In the positive direction, we establish a restriction theorem for scalar twists of regular wreath products. These results provide QWEP inputs for Fourier multiplier transference and identify a completely bounded multiplier norm obstruction to QWEP. Finally, operator-valued cocycles give finite QWEP crossed products whose acting groups are not hyperlinear.

papers.title: Fast Stochastic Post-Fault Replanning for Launch Vehicles under Persistent Parametric Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Post-fault ascent replanning for launch vehicles requires rapid joint trajectory-guidance replanning under uncertainty to maintain closed-loop constraint satisfaction. In particular, propulsion performance cannot be promptly and fully identified after a fault, leaving persistent parametric uncertainty throughout the remaining flight. A fast stochastic ascent replanning method is developed to address this problem. To efficiently account for the cross-time correlation induced by persistent parametric uncertainty, a fast system level synthesis formulation is developed with a Riccati-based solution structure. The resulting feedback synthesis is complemented by a task-oriented terminal weighting method that shapes terminal covariance according to post-injection correction demand. These components are integrated with nominal trajectory replanning, chance-constraint tightening, and online feedback realization to establish a real-time joint stochastic trajectory-guidance replanning framework for launch vehicles. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the proposed method effectively suppresses the influence of persistent parametric uncertainty and maintains stable convergence and high injection accuracy across parameter sweeps, with subsecond solution times. Compared with conventional ascent guidance, the empirical constraint-violation rate is substantially reduced.

papers.title: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses
papers.abstract: We introduce a technique for studying state preparation complexity in the quantum $p$-spin model on $n$ qubits, a disordered quantum spin system with random interactions on every set of $p$ qubits. We reduce the task of proving state preparation lower bounds to bounding the local profile complexity of the class, a quantity derived from the metric entropy of the set of vectors recording each state's expectation values against all weight-$p$ Pauli strings. We show that, for sufficiently large fixed $p$, any class with local profile complexity $O(n^2)$ remains separated from the ground-state energy by $Ω(\sqrt n)$, a gap on the leading energy scale. When the profile complexity is $o(n^2)$, we prove the stronger conclusion that the class cannot outperform a benchmark class of simpler states at leading order. Product states always provide such a benchmark. Our framework strengthens known bounds and covers classes beyond the reach of previous methods. These include examples where circuit lightcones extend across the entire system, preventing an application of standard arguments. We obtain an $Ω(n^2/\log n)$ gate lower bound for preparing near-ground states and depth--width tradeoffs, allowing arbitrary one- and two-qubit gates and arbitrarily many discardable ancillas. We also derive lower bounds on entanglement depth and matrix product state bond dimension, and energy obstructions for forward and reverse magic at every fixed level of Parham's magic hierarchy (arXiv:2504.19966). For Clifford circuits doped with $T$-gates, we obtain sharper energy comparisons using product stabilizer states as a more restrictive benchmark. The proof combines an adaptation of a nonsymmetric quantum de Finetti theorem (arXiv:1810.12197) with metric-entropy bounds for the Gaussian process indexed by the local profiles of states in the class.

papers.title: On the asymptotics of the Erdős-Rogers function
papers.abstract: The Erdős-Rogers function $f_{\ell,s}(n)$ is the largest order of a $K_\ell$-free induced subgraph guaranteed to exist in every $K_s$-free graph on $n$ vertices. While this function is well understood for $s=\ell+1$, the case where $s$ is much larger than $\ell$ has remained wide open. A long-standing lower bound of Sudakov states that $f_{\ell,s}(n)\geq n^{\frac{\ell}{2s}+O_\ell(s^{-2})}$, while a recent result of Bradač shows that $f_{\ell,s}(n)\leq n^{\frac{\ell-1}{s-1}+o(1)}$. In this paper, we close this gap asymptotically by proving that $f_{\ell,s}(n)= n^{\frac{\ell}{2s}+O_\ell(s^{-2})}$. More precisely, we prove that for all $2\leq \ell<s$, we have $f_{\ell,s}(n)\leq n^{\frac{\ell}{2s-\ell}+o(1)}$. Our proof builds on Bradač's recent tight construction for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, which can be viewed as the $\ell=2$ case of our result.

papers.title: Concurrent Strategies as Street Fibrations
papers.abstract: Concurrent games and strategies based on event structures are an established and expressive model of interactive computation. In this paper we revisit the problem of equipping this model with symmetry. Symmetry is essential for many applications, but it is also a source of mathematical complexity, not least because strategies with symmetry can be compared up to several distinct notions of equivalence. Our first contribution is a complete characterization of two classes of strategies for which composition admits an identity. For these two classes the identity laws hold, respectively, up to a "weak" and a "strong" notion of equivalence. The main result is that the weak class of strategies corresponds precisely to those inducing Street fibrations over the game. We also show how the established "thin" approach to symmetry also fits in this general framework. A second contribution is a formal connection between games and setoid-valued profunctors. This follows a long tradition of relating games and relational models, but here additionally includes a very general model of symmetries. Our characterization of strategies as Street fibrations makes the connection to profunctors significantly easier to establish.

papers.title: Real-rootedness and ultra log-concavity of rank-two matroid Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that the Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial of a rank-two matroid with exactly three parallel classes is real-rooted whenever its smallest parallel class has size at most three. This bound is sharp: the loopless rank-two matroids with parallel-class sizes $(4,561,600)$ and $(4,a,a+29)$, for all sufficiently large integers $a$, have $h^*$-polynomials that are not real-rooted. By matroid duality, these examples disprove Ferroni's real-rootedness conjecture even for cycle matroids of theta graphs. Nevertheless, every matroid of rank two or corank two has a positive $h^*$-coefficient sequence that is ultra log-concave of order equal to the polynomial's degree. In particular, the unimodality conjecture holds in both cases.

papers.title: Local stability of direct Mach configurations
papers.abstract: We investigate the local stability of direct Mach configurations for the two-dimensional steady compressible Euler equations. Given a piecewise constant direct Mach configuration with subsonic flow behind both the reflected shock and the Mach stem, we prove that under a transversality condition on the shock polar loops and a suitable condition on the truncation segment, every sufficiently small perturbation of the incoming flow gives rise to a Mach configuration that is a small perturbation of the background one, in the sense that the reflected shock, the Mach stem and the slip line, together with the downstream subsonic flow, stay close to their background counterparts. The triple point is fixed at the origin, and the domain is truncated at a finite distance. Euler--Lagrange coordinates are employed to transform the unknown contact discontinuity curve (slip line) into a fixed boundary and to write the full Euler system as a first-order elliptic system for the flow direction and pressure coupled to transport equations for the Bernoulli and entropy quantities. The key idea in dealing with the contact discontinuity is to solve a mixed boundary value problem, in divergence form with discontinuous coefficients, for a single elliptic equation, so that continuity of the scalar unknown and its conormal flux allows reconstruction of the flow direction and pressure with the required contact discontinuity conditions.

papers.title: Noncommutative Maximal Averages over Submanifolds and Variable Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We establish noncommutative maximal inequalities for averages over submanifolds in the $L^p$-spaces associated with semifinite von Neumann algebras. For every $1<p\leq\infty$, we prove local maximal bounds for smooth submanifolds of finite type at the parameter origin, and global bounds over all positive scales for polynomial parametrizations, without a finite-type assumption and with constants depending only on $p$, the degree and the dimensions. For variable hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq3$, satisfying a uniform rotational curvature condition, we obtain local maximal bounds for $p>n/(n-1)$. To our knowledge, these are the first such noncommutative inequalities for general lower-dimensional submanifolds and polynomial images. The key step is a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for a regularized auxiliary family adapted to non-isotropic dilations. The geometric kernels need not satisfy the pointwise smoothness or $L^2$-Dini conditions required by existing noncommutative Calderón--Zygmund theories. We combine a Calderón--Zygmund decomposition based on Cuculescu projections with integral regularity estimates, a non-isotropic Littlewood--Paley decomposition and Fourier decay to prove this endpoint estimate. Marcinkiewicz interpolation yields maximal $L^p$ bounds for the regularized averages, and interpolation with Fourier-based $L^2$ bounds recovers the original averages. The variable-hypersurface result uses oscillatory $TT^*$ estimates and localization. As applications, we obtain maximal ergodic inequalities for trace-preserving actions of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and, under additional assumptions, bilaterally almost uniform convergence results for the associated normalized averages.

papers.title: $p$-adic spectral zeta functions via the inverse Stieltjes transform
papers.abstract: Spectral zeta functions provide a standard tool for regularizing determinants of differential operators in quantum physics. In a previous paper (J. Math. Phys. 66: 083505, 2025), we introduced a $p$-adic spectral zeta function for discrete spectra via a locally analytic interpolation function. In this paper we extend the framework to continuous spectra using the inverse Stieltjes transform. Starting from the resolvent of a bounded operator, we construct a generalized distribution, called the $p$-adic spectral distribution, and define bosonic and fermionic zeta functions and functional determinants. We establish their analytic properties, special value formulas, and Stirling expansions, and show that our previous framework is embedded into the present one in the discrete case. In this approach, the bosonic and fermionic cases exhibit an interesting symmetry. As an application, we consider the position operator in $p$-adic quantum mechanics on an arbitrary compact subset of $\mathbb{C}_{p}$.

papers.title: The Hilbert Basis Theorem for Non-Associative Skew Power Series Rings and Non-Associative Skew Laurent Series Rings over a Non-Associative Coefficient Ring
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give conditions on a unital non-associative ring $R$ and additive map $σ: R\longrightarrow R$ so that the non-associative skew power series ring, denoted by $R[[X;σ]]$ and the non-associative skew Laurent series ring denoted by $R((X;σ))$ are left (resp. right) Noetherian, respectively. Consequently, we establish versions of Hilbert Basis Theorem of $R[[X;σ]]$ and $R((X;σ))$, respectively, for left (resp. right) Noetherianity . We also give a counterexample showing that the Hilbert Basis Theorem does not hold in general in the non-associative case. In establishing the Hilbert Basis Theorems for $R[[X;σ]]$ and $R((X;σ))$, we introduce and utilize the right (resp. left) quasi-associative property of $R$, which is equivalent to $rR$ (resp. $Rc$) being one-sided ideals for all $r\in R$ (resp. $c\in R$).

papers.title: Disproving Conjectures on the Davenport and Narkiewicz Constants
papers.abstract: The Davenport constant $\DD(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is a classical invariant arising from the arithmetic of ideal class groups of number fields. Closely related to the Davenport constant is the first Narkiewicz constant $\Nark_1(G)$, which arises in the quantitative study of algebraic integers and their factorizations. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured in 2006 that $\DD(G)\leq \sum_{i=1}^r n_i,$ while Narkiewicz and Śliwa conjectured in 1982 that $\Nark_1(G)=\sum_{i=1}^r n_i,$ where $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ are the invariant factors of $G$. Both are central conjectures concerning arithmetic invariants arising from the theory of number fields. In this paper, we disprove both conjectures. Moreover, we show that, for every fixed $r\geq5$, both $\DD(G)-\sum_{i=1}^r n_i$ and $\Nark_1(G)-\sum_{i=1}^r n_i$ are unbounded over finite abelian groups of rank $r$. We develop a probabilistic representation technique to establish a uniform upper bound for the Davenport constant: $$ \DD(G)\leq\frac{16}{5}\,\rr(G)\exp(G). $$ Our bound gives the first improvement of the classical van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk estimate: $\DD(G)\leq\exp(G) \left(1+\log\frac{|G|}{\exp(G)}\right) \leq\exp(G)\bigl(1+(\rr(G)-1)\log\exp(G)\bigr)$, by removing the logarithmic dependence on the exponent from this classical estimate, replacing it with the absolute constant $16/5$. Their bound stood unimproved since its establishment in 1969. The existence of $C=16/5$ also brings us closer to the most challenging conjecture on the Davenport constant, namely the Emde Boas--Kruyswijk Conjecture in 1969, which predicts that $\DD(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1.$ As a further application of our results, we disprove a conjecture of Girard in 2008 concerning cross numbers, an invariant with deep roots in the arithmetic of number fields and Krull monoids.

papers.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
papers.abstract: We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$. Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $α$ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{α}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_α^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.

papers.title: Uniqueness for the inverse Schrödinger problem in the plane with $L^p$ potentials, $p>1$
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded smooth domain. We prove that the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for $-Δ+V$ uniquely determines every complex-valued potential $V\in L^p(Ω)$, $p>1$, provided that zero is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue. This extends the previously known range $p>4/3$ to all $p>1$. The proof uses Bukhgeim's quadratic-phase solutions and an average of Alessandrini's identity over the phase center. After separating the Neumann-series tails, we show that each remaining Born term tends to zero. The fixed-order estimates combine bounds for the absolute kernels with oscillatory cancellation and a duality argument for the product of the two Cauchy transforms.

papers.title: Infinitely Many Binomial Coefficients of Deficiency One
papers.abstract: A binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$ is good if all its prime divisors exceed $k$, and its deficiency is the number of $k$-smooth integers in $(n-k,n]$. A short constructive proof of the existence of infinitely many good binomial coefficients with deficiency exactly one is given, which provides an answer to a problem of Erdős, Lacampagne, and Selfridge.

papers.title: $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the Bogomolov property for canonical heights
papers.abstract: We show that for any number field $K$ and any rational map $f$ in $K(x)$ of degree at least $2$ that is not conjugate to a power, (signed) Chebyshev or CM Lattès map, $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the strong Bogomolov property for the canonical height of $f$. Combined with former results of Amoroso-Zannier, Pottmeyer and Ratazzi, this implies that $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the Bogomolov property for canonical heights of any rational map of degree at least $2$. We also classify the pairs $(f,α)$ whose backward orbit contains infinitely many abelian points. This settles the Andrews--Petsche conjecture in the greater generality of rational maps over a number field and infinite abelian subsets of backward orbits. The authors were led to the main idea of the proof in conversation with \emph{Astra}. The key insight consists of applying Yuan's equidistribution results, followed by a classification of $(f,f)$-preperiodic curves due to Pakovich and Beaumont followed by an additional application of equidistribution on a parametrized preperiodic curve.

papers.title: Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras from Ševera bicomplexes
papers.abstract: A Ševera bicomplex is a bicomplex $(M,d_{0},d_{1})$ whose differentials $d_{i}$ are Grothendieck differential operators of order $\leq i$ with respect to a given $A$-module structure on $M$, where $A$ is a graded commutative algebra. One also requires that $(M,d_{0})$ admits a contracting homotopy $K$ that is a differential operator of the same order as $d_{0}$. Under suitable assumptions, the differential $d_{2}$ of the second page of the spectral sequence associated with $(M,d_{0},d_{1})$ is a Batalin-Vilkovisky operator on $E_{2}$, so that when $E_{2}$ is a free rank 1 $A$-module, the graded commutative algebra structure of $A$ is enhanced to a Gerstenhaber algebra structure, and the choice of a $d_{2}$-closed basis element for $E_{2}$ further enhances this to a Batalin-Vilkovisky algebra structure. The prototypical example of this construction is Ševera's description of the Batalin--Vilkovisky algebra structure on the algebra of smooth functions of an odd symplectic manifold. Throughout the whole article we look at Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras through the lenses of Cartan calculus. Indications of a generalization to derived Cartan calculus are briefly discussed in the concluding section.

papers.title: The category of nominal sets is locally monoidal closed
papers.abstract: The category Nom of nominal sets was proposed by Pitts and Gabbay as a setting for the semantics of abstract syntax with variable bindings. It is well-known that Nom is a topos, also known as the Schanuel topos, and in particular it follows that Nom is locally closed, i.e., every slice category Nom/X is cartesian-closed. In this paper, we show that Nom has a much stronger property: every monoidal (closed) structure on Nom induces a monoidal (closed) structure on all slice categories Nom/X. One monoidal closed structure of particular interest on Nom is the separated product A * B, whose right adjoint A -* B is called the separated function space. In particular, it follows that Nom is locally separatedly closed.

papers.title: Domain-decomposed Evolutional Deep Neural Network with Random Features for Transient Pressure Diffusion with Discontinuous and High-Contrast Coefficients
papers.abstract: Transient pressure diffusion in heterogeneous porous media becomes difficult to resolve efficiently when permeability is discontinuous and spans several orders of magnitude. In this paper, we develop a domain-decomposed random-feature evolutional deep neural network (DD RF-EDNN) that separates spatial approximation from temporal evolution. Permeability-informed random features are compressed into an orthonormal pressure space, and a conservative finite-volume operator is projected onto this space so that only the reduced coordinates are advanced in time.
