This formulation retains the dissipative structure of the discrete flow problem without repeated neural-network optimization. The analysis quantifies dictionary and singular-value truncation errors, proves contractivity under an energy-consistent dissipativity correction, and derives a conditional grid-level estimate for homogeneous dynamics and time-independent data admitting a steady lifting. Numerical experiments on low-permeability inclusions, high-conductivity blocks and channels, and three-dimensional grids assess the accuracy of the method across distinct coefficient configurations. The method reaches a final-time relative $L^2$ error of $9.54\times10^{-4}$ in the principal benchmark and maintains errors on the order of $10^{-2}$ at a permeability contrast of $10^3$. Numerical diagnostics further show that the observed error balance and temporal convergence are consistent with the analysis. These results support DD RF-EDNN as a structure-preserving and interpretable reduced formulation for transient simulations on prescribed heterogeneous media.

papers.title: Admissible qx+1 Sequences, Semiconvergents, and Rational Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract: Let $q\geq3$ be odd and put $m_r=\lfloor r\log_2q\rfloor$. We count parity sequences with exactly $r$ entries equal to $1$ for which the coefficient in the $qx+1$ iteration first drops below $1$ at step $m_r+1$. Their number $a_q(r)$ also counts the corresponding residue classes modulo $2^{m_r+1}$. By classifying increasing integer sequences according to the first index at which they exceed a prescribed bound, we obtain a recurrence which, for $q=3$, establishes the five- or six-term block pattern conjectured in 2015, allowing a shorter final block. We establish the sharp inequalities \[ \frac1r\binom{m_r-1}{r-1}\leq a_q(r)\leq\frac1r\binom{m_r}{r-1} \] Equality in the lower (respectively upper) bound occurs exactly when $\{r\log_2q\}$ is smaller (respectively larger) than all preceding fractional parts $\{j\log_2q\}$, $1\leq j<r$. These indices are characterized by denominators of convergents and semiconvergents from below and above; at these indices $r\geq2$, the values $a_q(r)$ are rational Catalan numbers. We also characterize the dependence on $q$ and prove, for each fixed odd $q\geq3$, that $a_q(r)=Θ_q(r^{-3/2}B_q^r)$, where $B_q=(\log_2q)^{\log_2q}/(\log_2q-1)^{\log_2q-1}$. For $q=3$, this proves Hikawa's conjectured polynomial factor for the number of finite binary words of given weight for which the length of every nonempty prefix is smaller than $\log_2 3$ times the number of its ones.

papers.title: The Face Lattice of any Simplicial Polytope is Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We show that the cover graph of the face lattice of every simplicial polytope admits a Hamilton cycle. Moreover, any two distinct facets can be prescribed as the neighbors of the full polytope on this cycle. By duality, the face lattice of every simple polytope is Hamiltonian as well. This proves the simplicial and simple cases of a conjecture of Behrooznia, Brenner, Merino, Mütze, Rieck, and Verciani (SODA26). The proof uses a line shelling in both directions. The forward shelling partitions the faces into Boolean intervals, whose cover graphs are cubes. The reverse shelling gives a second partition, on which we construct a perfect matching by adding or removing a fixed vertex in each interval. This matching connects the cubes of the first partition. A theorem of Gregor then completes it to a Hamilton cycle using only edges within these cubes. The same argument applies to shellable simplicial spheres, although without the prescribed neighbors of the full complex in this case. Using Chari's shelling construction of perfect matchings, we also obtain Hamiltonicity for polytopes with at most one facet that is not a simplex.

papers.title: A new family of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q$ and integer $n\ge1$, we give a single Kummer equation defining an $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $\mathcal X_{q,n}$. The family recovers the Hermitian curves for $n=1,2$, the Giulietti--Korchmáros curve for $n=3$, and the Beelen--Montanucci curves for odd $n\ge5$. For $q>2$ and even $n\ge4$, it gives new maximal curves of genus $(q^2-1)q^n/2$ that are not covered by the Hermitian curve over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$. We compute the genus for both parities of $n$ and give a uniform proof of maximality by counting rational places. For $q>2$ and odd $n\ge5$, we remove the Galois hypothesis from the known non-covering results for the Beelen--Montanucci and Garcia--Güneri--Stichtenoth curves. For even $n\ge4$, we determine the full automorphism group,of order $(q^n+1)q(q^2-1)$, and give explicit equations and genera for all Galois quotients, with closed-form equations for several classes of subgroups.

papers.title: Surjectivity of the Enots Wolley Sequence
papers.abstract: We prove that the Enots-Wolley sequence, a greedy sequence defined by local divisibility and coprimality conditions, contains every positive integer with at least two distinct prime divisors. This resolves an open conjecture by Shannon and Sloane. The only analytic number-theoretic inputs are the prime number theorem and Mertens' estimate for reciprocal primes.

papers.title: An explicit solution of the five-expert prediction PDE and the exact optimality set of COMB
papers.abstract: In this paper, we derive an explicit solution of the stationary prediction with expert advice PDE for five experts. The formula is given in three regions. In the first two regions, it is the four-expert solution plus a single integral with an elementary positive density. In the third region, it is a finite sum of hyperbolic products whose coefficients are determined by one scalar quadrature. Our formula establishes that the rank ordered adversary $(1,0,1,0,0)$ achieves the Hamiltonian maximum in the PDE everywhere in the ordered sector, while the COMB strategy $(1,0,1,0,1)$ is optimal only on a lower dimensional subset of the sector (where $x_1=x_2$ and $x_3=x_4$). The verification of the Hamiltonian inequalities is a tedious task, part of which is completed with a computer assisted proof. The verification reduces to 21 scalar inequalities, which we prove using 147 exact rational Bernstein polynomial certificates. The exact certificates and their independent arithmetic checks are included in a supplement to this paper, and a Lean 4 formalization machine-checks the verification and both main theorems, apart from the viscosity characterization.

papers.title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers I. Analytic Rigidity
papers.abstract: In 1984, Mahler asked whether a transcendental entire function can map the set of Liouville numbers $\mathscr{L}$ into itself. We answer this question in the negative by proving a local rigidity theorem for real-analytic functions. More precisely, if $U\subset\mathbb{R}$ is an open interval and $f:U\to\mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic with $f(\mathscr{L}\cap U)\subseteq\mathscr{L}$, then $f$ is the restriction to $U$ of a rational function in $\mathbb{R}(x)$. Quantitatively, there exists an absolute constant $τ>2$ such that, for every nonrational real-analytic function $f$ and every nonempty open subinterval $V\subset U$, the set of $ξ\in V\cap\mathscr{L}$ satisfying $μ(f(ξ))\leqτ$ contains a Cantor set. The proof combines a two-height counting estimate near analytic graphs with a nested-interval construction.

papers.title: Spatial Mixing and Deterministic Approximate Counting of Multi-spin Systems beyond Bounded Degree Graphs
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for deterministic approximate counting of multi-spin systems beyond bounded-degree graphs. The algorithm recursively constructs rational polytopes containing the true marginal vectors and uses linear-fractional programming to obtain certified bounds on marginal ratios. For positive interactions on graphs of polynomial connective constant $D$, we establish strong spatial mixing whenever $Dc<1$, where $c$ bounds the Birkhoff contraction coefficients of the interactions. Under the same condition, we also give a deterministic fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (\textbf{FPTAS}) for the partition function. We further extend the framework to proper colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs using recursion on permissive blocks. For every fixed $η\in(0,1)$, sufficiently large fixed $d$, and fixed integer $q\ge(2+η)d$, we obtain an \textbf{FPTAS} for counting proper $q$-colorings of $G\sim\mathcal G(n,d/n)$ with high probability over $G$. This improves the leading constant $3$ in the earlier counting guarantee of Yin and Zhang (APPROX/RANDOM, 2016) to $2$, and asymptotically matches the spatial mixing regime established by Yin (ICALP, 2014).

papers.title: Markov Chain CLTs: Resolving Open Problems
papers.abstract: Markov chain central limit theorems (CLTs) and their associated variances are very important for implementing Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms among other applications. Häggström and Rosenthal (2007) presented various results regarding the equality of different formulae for this variance and also posed seven open problems. We resolve all seven in this paper. Our main result is a general characterization of Markov chain CLTs: for stationary and ergodic Markov chains, we prove that the normalized partial sums satisfy a $\sqrt{n}$-CLT if and only if the Poisson equation admits a finite solution with square-integrable martingale differences whose second moment equals the CLT variance. In particular, this result does not require reversibility of the chain or square integrability of the function. It implies that Roberts' holding-probability condition always precludes a $\sqrt{n}$-CLT, and for reversible chains, whenever a $\sqrt{n}$-CLT holds, the variance limit is finite if the function is square-integrable, otherwise undefined. In addition, we develop a general principle that expresses Fourier coefficients as the autocovariances of an ergodic nonreversible Markov chain.

papers.title: Minimax Rate for Diffusion-Guided Local Intrinsic Dimension Estimation based on Fokker-Planck Equation
papers.abstract: Diffusion-guided methods have recently emerged as effective tools for probing the intrinsic geometry of high-dimensional data. Understanding their accuracy requires quantifying both (i) finite-scale approximation error relative to the true local intrinsic dimension (LID) and (ii) estimation error from finite samples. We address these two questions for the FLIPD field (Kamkari et al., 2024; arXiv:2406.03537), defined at the population level through the logarithmic scale derivative of a Gaussian-smoothed density and admitting a Fokker--Planck representation. For $α$-smooth densities on a regular $d$-dimensional manifold, we establish a uniform $O(σ^2)$ approximation bound relative to the manifold dimension $d$. Under expected integrated squared loss, we prove a minimax lower bound of order $(nσ^d)^{-1}$ for estimating the FLIPD field from $n$ observations when $n^{-1/(2α+d)}\leσ\leσ_0$. A plug-in FLIPD estimator based on the empirical denoising score matching (DSM) solution attains a matching upper bound. Thus the minimax rate is of order $(nσ^d)^{-1}$ and it becomes $n^{-2α/(2α+d)}$ at its smallest scale.

papers.title: On multiply induced characters
papers.abstract: We investigate finite group structures that yield complex irreducible characters induced simultaneously from two or more distinct subgroups. When such a group is realized as the Galois group of a Galois extension of number fields, this phenomenon implies that multiple subfields share the same Artin $L$-function.

papers.title: Proof of the generalized Chui conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Chui's conjecture on sums of Cauchy kernels. It states that among all configurations of Cauchy kernels on the unit disk, the equispaced one minimizes $L^1$ norm of the sum in the unit disk. Moreover, we obtain a generalization to a wider set of functionals, including weighted $L^p$ norms for $p > 1$ with radially symmetric weights.

papers.title: Permutative lifts of strictly ergodic subshifts
papers.abstract: Permutative sliding block codes - in the sense of Hedlund - give rise to finite-to- one extensions of subshifts. We provide criteria under which minimality and unique ergodicity are preserved by this 'lifting procedure'. These findings are illustrated by means of some nat- ural example families, which we use to obtain strictly ergodic finite-to-one extensions of sub- stitution subshifts (including the case of Fibonacci, Tribonacci, silver mean and noble means substitutions). We further study the interplay between permutative sliding block codes and Toeplitz flows. In particular, we find examples which demonstrate that a permutative lift of a strictly ergodic subshift may be minimal, but not uniquely ergodic - a phenomenon which cannot occur for primitive substitution subshifts.

papers.title: On the horizon problem over the product of self-similar fractals
papers.abstract: In this article, we first investigate the box dimension results for the graphs of continuous functions defined on $\mathfrak{F\times F}$, where $\mathfrak{F}$ is the self-similar fractal generated by an iterated function system (IFS) exhibiting the open set condition (OSC). Following this, we manifest the existence of a prevalent surface, defined by a continuous function on $\mathfrak{F\times F}$, that satisfies the horizon property in relation to the box dimension, i.e., the box dimension of the prevalent surface is greater than that of its horizon up to a constant $η$, where $η$ is the box dimension of the self-similar fractal $\mathfrak{F}$. Finally, we provide an example consolidating that the OSC on the underlying IFS of $\mathfrak{F}$ cannot be dropped.

papers.title: Carleson measures, Volterra integral operators and multipliers for $Q_K$ spaces
papers.abstract: We study embeddings and operators on the Möbius-invariant spaces $Q_K$ using two dyadic capacities. One capacity is defined by analytic packets; the other is defined by domination of positive semidefinite matrices. We prove that they are equivalent. They give criteria for bounded and compact embeddings $Q_K\to L^2(μ)$, bounded and compact Volterra operators, and pointwise multipliers. For the weights $K(t)=t^p/\log^β(e/t)$, $0<p<1$ and $β\ge1$, we prove $\mathcal M(Q_K)\subsetneq H^\infty\cap Q_K^{\log}.$ This disproves the logarithmic multiplier conjecture recorded in Bao and Wulan's 2021 survey.

papers.title: Pointwise function spaces over compacta are not weak Banach spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional real Banach space. We prove that there is no continuous bijection $h\colon C_p(K)\to E_w$ whose inverse is continuous at $h(0)$. Consequently, $C_p(K)$ and $C_w(L)$ are not homeomorphic for any infinite compact Hausdorff spaces $K$ and $L$. This settles Krupski's problem and its two-space version due to Krupski and Marciszewski, and answers a question of Kąkol, Leiderman, and Michalak concerning $C_p([0,1])$ and weak Banach spaces.

papers.title: A classification of nearly Gorenstein monomial ideals
papers.abstract: We classify nearly Gorenstein monomial ideals over an arbitrary field. In dimension zero, we compute the canonical trace ideal using a graph on the socle monomials. In positive dimension, we prove a dimension bound under unmixedness and a connectedness condition, with weaker assumptions on the canonical trace ideal.

papers.title: Dimension-Free Lipschitz Bounds for Brenier Maps to Compact Log-Concave Targets
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq1$, $Λ>0$, and $ρ\in\mathbb{R}$, let $μ=\mathcal{N}(0,Λ^{-1}\mathrm{Id})$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, where $\mathrm{Id}$ is the identity matrix, and let $ν$ be a probability measure whose support is a convex body $K$ of diameter $D=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and whose density is proportional to $e^{-W}$, where $\mathrm{D}^{2}W\succeq-ρ\mathrm{Id}$. We prove that the Brenier map $T$ from $μ$ to $ν$ has Lipschitz constant $\operatorname{Lip}(T)\leq\sqrt{Λ/(2π)}\int_{-D/2}^{D/2}e^{ρt^{2}/2}\,\mathrm{d}t$, which is sharp in every fixed dimension. For log-concave targets, the optimal coefficient of $\sqrtΛ\,D$ is $1/\sqrt{2π}$. For sources with finite second moment and density proportional to $e^{-V}$ for which $x\mapsto\frac12\langle Qx,x\rangle-V(x)$ is convex, where $Q$ is symmetric positive definite, and log-concave targets with compact support $K$, the Brenier potential $Φ$ satisfies $\partial_{vv}Φ\leq C_{1}\sqrt{\langle Qv,v\rangle}\,w_{K}(v)$ in the sense of distributions, where $w_{K}(v):=\sup_{y\in K}\langle y,v\rangle-\inf_{y\in K}\langle y,v\rangle$ is the width of $K$ along $v\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $C_{1}<0.463$. This removes Kolesnikov's $\sqrt d$ loss. For log-concave sources with $\mathrm{D}^{2}V\preceqΛ\mathrm{Id}$ and the target $ν$, the Brenier map $T$ satisfies $\operatorname{Lip}(T)^{2}\leqΛ\int_{0}^{D^{2}/4}e^{ρt}\,\mathrm{d}t$, so $\operatorname{Lip}(T)$ has the optimal exponential rate $1/8$ in $ρD^{2}$.

papers.title: Qualitative Analysis of a Two-Compartment Pharmacokinetic Model for Human Ethanol Metabolism and Its Generalization
papers.abstract: In this work, we revisit a continuous-time two-compartment pharmacokinetic model of human ethanol metabolism originally proposed by Levitt and Levitt. We first establish the positivity of the solutions, investigate the existence and uniqueness of a positive equilibrium, and analyze its local and global asymptotic stability. As a result, the global dynamics of the original ethanol metabolism model is characterized, thereby complementing and extending the analytical results reported in the original study. Second, building upon the foundational two-compartment model of Levitt and Levitt, we replace the Michaelis--Menten metabolism rate with a general class of nonlinear functions, including both monotone and nonmonotone forms. This generalization allows us to examine a wider range of physiologically motivated scenarios and reveals richer dynamical behavior. We then establish the positivity of the solutions, study the existence and asymptotic stability of equilibria, and analyze the long-term dynamics under different ethanol input conditions. In particular, for a specific nonmonotone family, we establish the occurrence of a nondegenerate saddle-node bifurcation through center-manifold analysis. Furthermore, we prove the absence of nonconstant periodic orbits in the generalized model without assuming monotonicity of the metabolic rate functions. These findings extend the qualitative analysis beyond equilibrium stability and provide further insights into the complex dynamics of human ethanol metabolism. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to illustrate the theoretical findings. The numerical results provide further support for the theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Universality in random graphs via optimal linking systems: trees and beyond
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for proving universality results in sparse random graphs. As a first application, we show that there exists an absolute constant $C>1$ such that, with high probability, for every fixed constant $Δ$, the binomial random graph $G(n,C\ln n/n)$ contains every $n$-vertex tree with maximum degree at most $Δ$. This answers a question of Montgomery (Advances in Mathematics, 2019). We also determine, for every $p$ satisfying $C\ln n/n\leq p=n^{-1+o(1)}$, the minimum girth $\ell$ (up to an absolute multiplicative constant) for which with high probability $G(n,p)$ contains all cycle factors of girth at least $Ω(\ell)$. In particular, with high probability $G(n,C\ln n/n)$ contains all cycle factors of girth at least $C\ln n/\ln\ln n$, which is optimal up to a constant factor. This extends an earlier result of Ferber, Kronenberg, and Luh (Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, 2019) and significantly improves a corollary of a deep result of Kahn, Lubetzky, and Wormald (Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics, 2017). One of the key ingredients in the proofs is establishing the optimal depth of linking systems in sparse random graphs.

papers.title: On Riemannian Geometry in Elastic Diffeology
papers.abstract: Blohmann's tangent functor makes the category of elastic diffeological spaces a Cartesian tangent category in the sense of Cockett and Cruttwell. We use this structure to develop Riemannian geometry on elastic diffeological spaces. Following Cockett and Cruttwell, with additional axioms for scalar multiplication, we introduce connections, covariant derivatives and curvature; for a Riemannian metric we prove a Koszul formula and the uniqueness of the Levi-Civita covariant derivative. Our main result is a variational characterization of geodesics: if a full connection whose vertical part is Levi-Civita admits a geodesic flow fixing the zero section, then the critical paths of the energy functional are exactly the paths satisfying the geodesic equation, and regular length-minimizing paths are geodesics after constant-speed reparametrization. On elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, completeness of the geodesic spray yields such a flow and uniqueness of geodesics. The results apply to quotients of complete Riemannian manifolds by free isometric actions of countable groups, such as irrational tori, and, under a tangent-commuting hypothesis, to mapping spaces from a closed manifold into elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, including free loop spaces of complete Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: The first chiral homology group in higher genus
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of the first chiral homology group of vertex algebras, developed by van Ekeren and Heluani for elliptic curves, to compact Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus. Our approach realizes a genus $g$ surface by iterated self-sewing of $g$ handles onto the Riemann sphere, each governed by a sewing parameter $ρ_i$ in a punctured disc. We construct an explicit complex computing the chiral homology groups $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_0$ and $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_1$ of a vertex algebra $V$ on a genus $g$ surface with $n$ marked points, and equip it with a projectively flat connection, with an explicit central-charge anomaly, over the $g$-dimensional space of sewing parameters. We prove a genus $g$ Fourier-space Borcherds identity for the associated modified vertex operators. We show that two finiteness assumptions 1) finite dimensionality of the first Poisson homology $\HP_1(R_V)$ of the Zhu $C_2$-algebra, and 2) finite generation of a certain Koszul homology of the associated graded algebra, imply finite dimensionality of $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_1(X,V)$ for every genus $g$ and every vertex algebra $V$. Using the degeneration $ρ_i \to 0$ together with the factorization theorem of Damiolini-Gibney-Tarasca, we relate the totally degenerate limit of $H_1^{\mathrm{ch}}$ to the Hochschild homology of an iterated construction on the Zhu algebra, and deduce vanishing of the first chiral homology group in every genus for rational vertex algebras.

papers.title: A multi-player optimal stopping game based on a spider Brownian motion
papers.abstract: This paper studies a multi-player non-zero-sum optimal stopping game driven by a spider Brownian motion. We study a specific, tractable family of games and the focus is on the existence and uniqueness of subgame-perfect Nash equilibria (SPNE). We begin by analyzing the two-player setting, in which the underlying process is a skew Brownian motion, and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of an SPNE. We then derive sufficient conditions for the uniqueness of the SPNE in the symmetric case, (where the skew Brownian motion reduces to a standard Brownian motion and both players have the same payoff structures). We also give examples which show that there can be multiple SPNE or no SPNE. We then extend the framework to the multi-player setting and provide sufficient conditions for the existence of an SPNE in this more general setting with a spider Brownian motion.

papers.title: Weight-constrained universal sequences
papers.abstract: In 2011/12, Ruskey, Sawada, Stevens and Williams showed that a binary universal sequence can be constructed containing all $n$-tuples of Hamming weight either $r$ or $r+1$ for every possible $r$, and no others. In this paper we examine extensions of this result that require choosing a weight-like function applying to $n$-tuples with symbols taken from an alphabet of arbitrary (finite) size. We consider three possible such weight functions, and in each case establish an analogous result to that of Ruskey, Sawada, Stevens and Williams.

papers.title: Generalised flip order on the faces of nestohedra
papers.abstract: Tamari lattices and weak Bruhat order are classical posets on the vertices of associahedra and permutohedra. These posets are particular instances of the \emph{flip order} on the vertices of graph associahedra. We present here a generalisation of the flip order to all the faces of nestohedra, encoded in terms of hypergraphs. For right-filled hypergraphs, we characterise our order in terms of generalised inversions. As an application, we describe shuffle products on faces of suitable nestohedra as sums over intervals in this order.

papers.title: On the diffusive-mean field limit of a kinetic weakly interacting particle system
papers.abstract: We study the joint diffusive-mean field limit for a system of weakly interacting kinetic Langevin dynamics, extending the results of Delgadino, Gvalani and Pavliotis (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 2021) to the hypoelliptic/hypocoercive case. We show that, in the absence of phase transitions, the two limits commute, and we calculate the covariance matrix of the limiting Brownian motion using the Green-Kubo/Kipnis-Varadhan formula. However, at low temperatures, and in the presence of phase transitions, the two limits may not commute. We demonstrate our findings by providing a detailed analysis of the diffusive-mean field limit for the $O(2)$ model in a magnetic field. Our analysis is based on the systematic use of recently developed hypocoercivity techniques, together with an appropriate linearization of the mean field McKean-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck partial differential equation.

papers.title: Propagation dynamics of an acid-mediated invasion model with degenerate tumor diffusion
papers.abstract: We investigate traveling wave fronts for an acid-mediated tumor invasion model with density-dependent degenerate diffusion. The model is a partially diffusive PDE--ODE system of Gatenby--Gawlinski type, in which the tumor diffusion coefficient $D(U)$ is allowed to be a general decreasing function satisfying $D(1)=0$. This degeneracy causes the traveling wave equation for the tumor component to lose uniform ellipticity near the healthy state, and hence standard arguments for nondegenerate reaction diffusion systems are not directly applicable. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce a nonlinear change of variables which removes the degeneracy from the highest-order term of the tumor equation. For each fixed admissible tumor profile, the acid profile is represented by a Green kernel, while the healthy-tissue profile is obtained from an explicit integral formula. The transformed tumor profile is then constructed as the stationary limit of a uniformly parabolic auxiliary problem. By combining comparison principles, local Schauder estimates, carefully chosen super- and sub-solutions, and the Schauder fixed-point theorem, we prove the existence of traveling wave fronts for every wave speed $θ\ge 2\sqrt{rD(0)}$. The resulting wave connects the tumor-dominant state $(0,1,1)$ at $z=-\infty$ to the healthy state $(1,0,0)$ at $z=+\infty$. We further establish strict pointwise bounds, monotonicity of all wave components, and one-sided exponential asymptotic estimates in both the transformed variable and the original traveling-wave variable.

papers.title: Compatibility of Martensitic Microstructures in Polycrystals
papers.abstract: The paper studies martensitic microstructures in polycrystals, focussing on their compatibility across grain boundaries. After a reduction to the case of a planar grain boundary, the case when the grain boundary separates two constant gradients of zero energy is considered. It is shown that for cubic-to tetragonal transformations such a configuration can occur when the relative grain rotation is not in the cubic group. Then the case when the grain boundary separates two simple laminates of zero energy is considered, it being shown using a computer-assisted symbolic calculation that in the cubic-to-tetragonal case compatibility is only possible for a closed set of measure zero in the manifold of grain boundary normals and relative grain rotations, and that a similar slightly weaker result holds for cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations. The results suggest why higher-order laminates are often observed for such transformations. The Taylor set of deformation gradients is defined and studied, this set having the property that any deformation whose gradient belongs to it corresponds to a zero-energy microstructure for the polycrystal independent of grain geometry and grain rotations. New upper bounds for the Taylor set are proved for cubic-to-tetragonal and cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations, generalizing those of Bhattacharya and Kohn using the geometrically linearized theory. We give a simple proof of a related result of Peigney characterizing the positive diagonal matrices in the quasiconvex hull of the energy wells for cubic-to-tetragonal transformations.

papers.title: Combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomial of fence posets
papers.abstract: Given a fence poset P , we define a new statistic on permutations, denoted by blP, that provides a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomial of P , answering a question of Ferroni, Morales, and Panova (2025). Using the fact that the base polytope of a lattice path matroid can be decomposed into order polytopes of fence posets, we also obtain a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial of the base polytope of Schubert matroids, answering a question of Stanley (1999). As an application of this statistic, we establish the first nontrivial lower bound for the linear coefficient of the Ehrhart polynomial of an order polytope. Finally, we conjecture generalizations of this statistic to skew-shape posets and circular fence posets.

papers.title: The Siegel-Weil formula in geometry and arithmetic
papers.abstract: The present paper is an extended version of the lecture notes of a course given by the first author at the summer school on Formulas of Siegel and Weil (Bielefeld, September 2025). We survey three perspectives on the Siegel-Weil formula: classical, geometric, and arithmetic. We first recall the Siegel-Weil formula for elliptic theta series arising from positive definite lattices. We next discuss the higher genus case for lattices of arbitrary signature from an adelic viewpoint. After introducing orthogonal Shimura varieties, we present the geometric Siegel-Weil formula, in which the generating series of volumes of special cycles is shown to be an Eisenstein series. We conclude with the (partly conjectural) arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula, relating degrees of special cycles in arithmetic Chow groups to central derivatives of Eisenstein series.

papers.title: Symmetric Spectral Reciprocity for $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Uniform Subconvexity
papers.abstract: We establish an explicit symmetric spectral reciprocity formula for twisted fourth moments of $\mathrm{GL}_{2}$ $L$-functions over an arbitrary number field. A Rankin--Selberg kernel gives a new analytic regularization of the formal Petersson identity for products of Eisenstein series, based on the rank decomposition $4=2+2$. The formula preserves the nonnegativity of the amplified fourth-moment spectral side at general levels. We further identify a new \emph{square-level concentration phenomenon}: after amplification, the dominant off-diagonal contribution comes from representations whose conductor is the square of a product of two distinct primes. Using square-level local test functions in the relative trace formula, we prove new hybrid subconvexity bounds for twisted $L$-functions. Combining these bounds with symmetric spectral reciprocity and amplification, we obtain the uniform estimate \begin{align*} L(1/2,π)\ll_{F,\varepsilon} C(π)^{\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{120}+\varepsilon} \end{align*} for every unitary cuspidal automorphic representation $π$ of $\mathrm{GL}_{2}/F$ with arbitrary central character. We also obtain stronger bounds for fixed central characters, a prime-level fifth-moment estimate, and applications to Rankin--Selberg and ring class $L$-functions.

papers.title: A Constructive Framework for Generalized Fourier Transforms via Truncate-and-Generalized Limits
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a constructive definition of generalized Fourier transforms based entirely on ordinary truncated Fourier integrals and ordered dual-domain limits, within the framework of improper Riemann integration and classical analysis. The proposed truncate-and-generalized-limit (t.g.l.) formulation does not require test-function spaces, Lebesgue measure theory, or duality pairings in its proofs: the forward and inverse transforms are defined directly through finite-domain truncation of the target function, followed by successive ordered limits in the time and frequency domains. As consequences of this constructive definition, the formulation provides a unified treatment of non-decaying, oscillatory, and locally singular functions beyond the classical L1(R) setting; reveals an inherent asymmetry between the forward transform, interpreted as a first-order generalized-limit family, and the inverse transform, which requires frequency-domain truncation to generate pointwise reconstruction through Dirichlet-type oscillatory localisation; and clarifies the distinction between the t.g.l. approach and distribution theory, where generalized Fourier transforms are introduced through duality pairings rather than constructed from ordinary integrals. The inversion formula is established rigorously for two concrete admissible classes using only the classical Dirichlet convergence theorem. Several examples confirm that the framework covers constants, polynomials, periodic functions, singular kernels, and chirp signals within a single constructive scheme.

papers.title: Fluctuations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy at critical temperature
papers.abstract: We consider the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model at the critical inverse temperature $β= 1$ with zero external field. We prove that the free energy $F_N = F_{N,β=1}$ of this model has variance \[ \mathrm{Var}(F_N) = \frac16 \log N + O(1)\,, \] confirming a physics prediction of Aspelmeier \cite{aspelmeier2008free}, and that the centered and scaled $F_N$ satisfies a Gaussian CLT. We also identify the critical two-replica overlap scale, proving \[ \mathbb{E} \langle R_{1,2}^2\rangle \asymp N^{-2/3}\,, \] as conjectured by Talagrand \cite{talagrand2011mean2}, together with a uniform exponential moment bound for $N^{1/3} |R_{1,2}|$. The key input is a critical reweighted moment method, in the spirit of the ``small subgraph conditioning'' technique from probabilistic combinatorics, but capable of capturing diverging fluctuations. Through this reweighting, we relate the critical SK model to the BBP critical edge, which determines the overlap and fluctuation scales.

papers.title: Avalanche homology of digraphs via sandpile dynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce avalanche homology as a new (di)graph homology theory, based on the dynamics of the sandpile model. Avalanche homology is the simplicial homology of the avalanche complex generated from the sets of unstable vertices at the time steps of the sandpile dynamics. In this work we focus on digraphs, and our main results give the homotopy types of the avalanche complex for directed paths and directed cycles for certain initial configurations of the sandpile dynamics. Even for such simple digraphs a wide range of topologies can arise, and we compare this to the directed flag complex and to the recently introduced burning homology. Furthermore, the dynamics yields very naturally a filtered simplicial complex, and hence persistent avalanche homology.

papers.title: A new perspective in linear Cauchy Elasticity: variational minimum principles for statics, dynamics, and heterogeneous materials
papers.abstract: A variational minimum principle for linear elastodynamics of a possibly heterogeneous material without a stored energy function is developed. It involves a change of variables to dual fields, and results in a degenerate elliptic Euler-Lagrange system, even when the primal elastodynamics is hyperbolic. Uniqueness assertions for the dual dynamic and static problems and implications of the degenerate ellipticity are sketched. Some implications pertaining to heterogeneous materials and ones with indefinite elastic moduli are discussed.

papers.title: Discrepancy for Random Linear Codes
papers.abstract: We show that random linear codes (RLCs) possess nearly optimal discrepancy-type properties in a broad range of settings. Our main results are two general discrepancy theorems: one controls all translates of a fixed test, and the other controls large families of Fourier-pseudorandom tests. Two motivating examples follow: First, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for list-decoding from errors above capacity. More precisely, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1 - \frac{1}{n}\log_q|B_ρ| + \varepsilon$, where $|B_ρ|$ is the volume of a radius-$ρ$ Hamming ball in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, satisfies $|C \cap B| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot |B|}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all radius-$ρ$ Hamming balls $B$ with high probability. This significantly strengthens the best prior results, which follow from work by Blinovsky (1987, 1990) and Levitin (1988) on the covering properties of RLCs. Second, over prime fields, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for zero-error list-recovery, and list-recovery from erasures, above capacity. More precisely, for a prime $q>2$ and input list size $2\leq \ell\leq q-1$, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1-\log_q \ell+\varepsilon$ will satisfy $|C \cap S| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot \ell^n}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all combinatorial rectangles $S=S_1\times S_2\times\cdots\times S_n$, where $|S_i|=\ell$ for all $i$, with high probability. An analogous result also holds when we can bound $|S_i|$ only for some of the $i$'s. We use this to show the abundance of locally leakage-resilient $n$-party linear ramp secret sharing schemes with any linear reconstruction threshold and sublinear threshold gap $O(n/\log n)$ over fields of polynomial size $q=Θ(n^γ)$ for a constant $γ\in(0,1/5)$. Prior work was stuck at reconstruction thresholds above $n/2$ for both threshold and ramp schemes.

papers.title: Cost of one-relator groups
papers.abstract: For any infinite one-relator group $Γ=\langle S \mid w^m\rangle$, we prove that $\mathrm{cost}(Γ)=|S|-\frac{1}{m}$. For such groups, this gives $β^{(2)}_1(Γ)=\mathrm{cost}(Γ) - 1$, answering a special case of Gaboriau's question on the relationship between cost and first $\ell^2$-Betti number.

papers.title: On finiteness properties of the unramified Iwasawa module of a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension with restricted ramification
papers.abstract: In the present article, we consider $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions defined by restrictions on ramification at $p$-adic primes. We study the finiteness, the existence of non-trivial finite submodules, and the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa modules of these $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions. In addition, we give a new sufficient condition for Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture with some non-trivial concrete examples.

papers.title: Magnetic cotangent groupoids
papers.abstract: We introduce magnetic cotangent groupoids on the cotangent bundle of a Lie groupoid using normalized cocycles, and characterize when magnetic symplectic forms are multiplicative on these groupoids. We show that $\mathbb{S}^1$-central extensions of Lie groupoids yield such structures via symplectic reduction. For a Kac--Moody extension, the resulting deformation connects the coadjoint and gauge action groupoids, which are not Morita equivalent.

papers.title: The five vertex model on a rectangle
papers.abstract: We derive a determinantal expression for the inhomogeneous asymmetric five vertex model in a rectangular geometry with arbitrary boundary conditions at the bottom and top. Standard non-intersecting lattice path, or free fermion, approaches are not applicable and the determinantal form thus is not immediate.

papers.title: Divided differences and complex variations of multiple zeta-star values
papers.abstract: Motivated by the known derived set $[1,+\infty)$ of multiple zeta-star values, we study finite multiple star harmonic sums and their infinite-depth limits. Divided differences give a cube-integral representation of their holomorphic interpolation on $\mathrm{Re}(s)>0$, which agrees with the Kawashima functions after reversal of the index. The finite-depth interpolations converge locally uniformly in $s$ as the depth tends to infinity, uniformly over all positive integer index sequences on compact subsets. For real $s>1$, these limits define a bijection from the infinite positive integer indices onto $(1,s]$. For each admissible infinite index, they tend to the corresponding multiple zeta-star limit as $\mathrm{Re}(s)\to+\infty$ with bounded imaginary part. For $\mathrm{Re}(s)>1$, we prove strict separation of every ordered pair of finite indices and of every ordered pair of infinite indices: either the difference or the difference divided by $s$ has positive real part throughout this half-plane, with the choice fixed by the pair. In particular, both index maps are injective. The proof uses a summation principle for functions with positive real part, established through positive integral representations and explicit kernel estimates.

papers.title: The existence of invariant sublinear expectations for $G$-SDEs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the existence of invariant sublinear expectations of Markovian semigroups on sublinear expectation spaces. To achieve this, we establish a complete metric space of sublinear expectations, on which we extend Harris' method to the nonlinear setting on the convergence of sublinear semigroups. We then explore two cases of $G\text{-}$diffusions by studying the Lyapunov function and the local Doeblin condition. One is the $G\text{-}$Brownian motion on the unit circle which is the case studied in Feng and Zhao(2021), but with the new method. Another is the multidimensional $G\text{-}$SDEs on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^d$. We establish, for the first time in the literature, the existence of the invariant sublinear expectation for $G\text{-}$SDEs under the non-degenerate and weakly dissipative assumption. For this, we prove that for a class of $G\text{-}$SDEs, the $G\text{-}$expectation can be represented as the supremum of the semigroup of a family of SDEs, of which the regularity is obtained by considering { oscillations and coupling of the nonlinear Markovian semigroup,} and the Denis-Hu-Peng representation for the distribution of $G\text{-}$Brownian motions.

papers.title: Integer points close to a transcendental curve: an algorithmic approach
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose an algorithmic approach to determine the integer points located near a transcendental curve. This approach is closely related to a celebrated work by Bombieri and Pila and to the so-called Coppersmith's method. We establish the underlying theoretical foundations, prove the algorithms, study their complexity and present practical experiments; we also compare our approach with previously existing ones. From a practical point of view, we focus on an instance of our general problem, called the Table Maker's Dilemma, whose solving makes it possible to evaluate a given function with correct rounding. Our experiments show a significant speedup. In particular, our results show that the development of a correctly rounded mathematical library for the binary128 format is now possible at a much smaller cost than with previously existing approaches.

papers.title: Entropy Bounds for Local Coordination and Graph Amenability
papers.abstract: We study local coordination on finite graphs, equivalently, the ability of randomized local protocols with independent private randomness to produce highly correlated outputs at neighboring vertices. Hutchcroft, Rospuskova, and Tamuz (2026) showed that if such local coordination can be achieved with low cost, then the graph admits a low-cost leader profile, or equivalently an appropriate bounded-radius decomposition, with a square-root loss in the cost. We substantially improve this bound for unbiased binary outputs. If the average disagreement is $\varepsilon$, we construct a leader profile of cost $O(\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon))$. The key ingredient is an information-theoretic influence measure: after fixing an ordering of the independent information sources, we assign to each binary output the increments of mutual information revealed along that ordering. For two outputs that disagree with probability $p$, the corresponding measures are within binary entropy $h(p)$ in total variation. Combined with a grand coupling theorem, this yields the improved bound. We also show that a universal linear bound is impossible. We construct graphs with binary local profiles of cost $O(\varepsilon)$ for which every leader profile has cost $$ Ω\!\left(\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}\right). $$ The construction uses weighted majority functions and can be implemented as an action-symmetric Nash equilibrium, giving a negative answer to the question of HRT whether leader equilibria are always optimal up to a constant factor. Finally, we show that the binary assumption is essential: for general real-valued outputs, the square-root dependence of the HRT theorem is sharp up to a universal constant.

papers.title: Accelerating Sinkhorn for Entropy-Regularized Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Entropy-regularized optimal transport is widely used to compare and align data distributions, but Sinkhorn can converge slowly at small regularization. We introduce Acc-Sinkhorn, a two-state Hessian-driven Nesterov iteration built on the dual mirror geometry of the row-reduced Sinkhorn map. The method combines momentum acceleration with an inexpensive descent safeguard, sta- ble log-domain evaluation, and a prescribed homotopy schedule requiring neither line search nor curvature estimation. We prove global linear convergence of the safeguarded method, rule out con- secutive restarts, and establish local accelerated convergence for fixed parameters without restarts through spectral analysis. Numerical comparisons with six methods on synthetic problems, color transfer, and bilingual word alignment show runtime speedups of up to about 26 over Sinkhorn, with additional rendering-accuracy comparisons for color transfer.

papers.title: On higher order Morrey's inequalities over CD{\boldmath$(K,N)$}-spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a higher order Morrey's inequality in the framework of $\mathsf{CD}(K,N)$-spaces for $K\in\mathbb{R}$ and $N\in\mathbb{N}$. We do so by first introducing an alternate version of second order Sobolev spaces in general metric measure spaces, which contains amply many functions even when $p>N$. These spaces contain the traditional $H^{2, p}(X)$ spaces on $\mathsf{RCD}(K, N)$-spaces.

papers.title: Excursion-dependent inverse-subordinator time changes of regenerative processes: Excursion structure and multiscale occupation-time limits
papers.abstract: We study an excursion-dependent generalization of inverse-subordinator time changes for recurrent regenerative processes. Subordinators from an independent family are assigned to measurable classes of excursions and to the distinguished state at which the process is regenerative, and the random clock is constructed from the corresponding occupation times. Although the time-changed process is not necessarily regenerative or Markovian, we show that its transformed excursion point process is again Poisson and is obtained from the original excursion point process by a marking-and-mapping procedure. We also identify the transformed stagnancy component, on the original local-time scale, as a subordinator independent of this point process. We use this representation to study occupation- and waiting-time asymptotics. Under regular variation assumptions on the tails of the Lévy measures of the cumulative excursion lifetimes and stagnancy components, we prove a multiscale joint occupation-time limit theorem, including generalized arcsine laws and Darling--Kac-type limits. We further obtain joint scaling limits for the last and next visit times to the distinguished state.

papers.title: Multicategorical Semantics for Untyped Effects
papers.abstract: Completeness proofs in categorical semantics usually proceed by building a syntactic category whose composition is given by substitution. For untyped effectful Call-by-Value languages, this runs into a basic obstacle: there is no canonical notion of simultaneous substitution of computations, since evaluation order is semantically meaningful. We address this by taking single computation substitutions, that is, binding steps, as primitive, and representing computation substitution by finite sequential lists composed by concatenation. We formalize this idea in a one-object Freyd-multicategorical setting. We introduce Freyd operads, separating a cartesian operad of values from a symmetric Ren-cartesian preoperad of computations, connected by a Freyd functor, and from any Freyd operad we construct a corresponding Freyd PROP of substitutions. We prove that this construction is representable and, in the strict one-object setting, left adjoint to restriction to codomain 1. Using the induced term model, we interpret untyped computational lambda-calculus with procedures and higher-order functions in weakly closed Freyd operads, and prove soundness, initiality, and completeness. This yields a categorical semantics tailored to untyped effectful computation and broad enough to encompass realizability-oriented models such as monadic combinatory algebras.

papers.title: Quantitative Soft-to-Hard Terminal Constraint Convergence for the Heat Equation
papers.abstract: We investigate an optimal control problem for the one-dimensional heat equation with a prescribed terminal state. To approximate the hard terminal constraint, we consider quadratic terminal penalization and analyze the convergence of the optimal controls and terminal states as the penalty parameter \(α\to\infty\). We develop a unified spectral treatment of terminal reachability, minimum-energy control, and quadratic-penalty convergence. Using modal decompositions, we characterize finite-energy admissible terminal targets and construct the corresponding minimum-energy hard-constrained control. For admissible targets, we establish strong convergence of penalized optimal controls and terminal states. Under suitable spectral summability conditions, we obtain regularity-dependent convergence estimates of order \(O(α^{-(1/2+θ)})\) for the terminal-state error, \(0\leθ\le1/2\), and \(O(α^{-θ})\) for the optimal-control error, \(0<θ\le1\). The analysis connects these results explicitly with classical Tikhonov regularization in the heat-equation setting. A finite-dimensional prototype illustrates the underlying projection structure, while companion numerical investigations provide supporting evidence for the predicted convergence behavior.

papers.title: Kernel-Gradient Drifting Models
papers.abstract: We propose kernel-gradient drifting, a one-step generative modeling framework that replaces the fixed Euclidean displacement direction in drifting models with directions induced by the kernel itself. Standard drifting is attractive because it enables fast, high-quality generation without distilling a large pretrained diffusion model, but its theory is currently understood mainly for Gaussian kernels, where the drift coincides with smoothed score matching and is identifiable. Our gradient-based reformulation exposes this score-based structure for general kernels: the resulting drift is the score difference between kernel-smoothed data and model distributions, yielding identifiability for characteristic kernels and a smoothed-KL descent interpretation of the smoothed drifting dynamics. Since kernel gradients are intrinsic tangent vectors, the same construction extends naturally to Riemannian manifolds and to discrete data via the Fisher-Rao geometry of the probability simplex. Across spherical geospatial data, promoter DNA and molecule generation, kernel-gradient drifting enables state-of-the-art one-step generation beyond the Euclidean setting without distillation. Code is available \href{https://github.com/jcarrascopollo/kgd_thesis}{here}.

papers.title: Generalization Error Bounds for Picard-Type Operator Learning in Nonlinear Parabolic PDEs
papers.abstract: Operator learning for partial differential equations (PDEs) aims to learn solution operators on infinite-dimensional function spaces from finite-resolution data. In this setting, it is important for the learned model to be discretization-invariant, or resolution-robust, and to reflect PDE-specific structure. It is therefore natural to ask how such structure should be encoded in the model architecture, hypothesis class, or learning procedure. In this paper, we study operator learning for solution operators of nonlinear parabolic PDEs based on Duhamel--Picard iteration. We formulate Picard iteration as an abstract state-transition model and present a theoretical framework for Picard-type operator learning. We derive implementation-agnostic generalization error bounds that separate the implementation error from the estimation error associated with the abstract state-transition model induced by Picard iteration. A key consequence is that increasing the Picard depth reduces the Picard truncation error without causing an unbounded growth of the entropy-based estimation error. We also extend the analysis to long-time prediction by rolling out the same learned local model over successive time blocks. Finally, we illustrate the theory for nonlinear heat equations on the torus using a Picard-type Fourier neural operator as a concrete implementation.

papers.title: On Enhancing the Dissipative Behavior of Active Flux Advection Schemes
papers.abstract: In this work, the traditional third-order Active Flux advection scheme is modified by reformulating the method and introducing four additional parameters R, S, T, and U that allow the numerical dissipation and dispersion of the scheme to be adjusted. The influence of these parameters is studied using Fourier analysis and parameter choices that lead to schemes with improved dissipative properties are identified. These improvements are validated by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Univalence without function extensionality
papers.abstract: It is a well-known theorem of homotopy type theory, originally due to Voevodsky, that function extensionality holds inside any univalent universe. We consider a weaker variant of the univalence axiom, asserting that the wild category formed by the universe is univalent, which we call categorical univalence. We show that categorical univalence does not imply function extensionality by an analysis of Von Glehn's polynomial model construction, which produces models of Martin-Löf type theory that always refute function extensionality. We find in particular that when the base model has a univalent universe, its polynomial model has a universe that is categorically univalent but lacks function extensionality.

papers.title: Identification to Subclasses of Chordal Graphs
papers.abstract: An identification of two vertices \(u\) and \(v\) in a graph replaces them with a new vertex that is made adjacent to every vertex of \(N(u)\cup N(v)\setminus \{u,v\}\). We study the \(\mathcal{H}\)-Identification problem, which is to decide whether a given graph \(G\) can be transformed (``identified'') to a graph in \(\mathcal{H}\) by applying at most \(k\) vertex identifications. We determine the classical and parameterized complexity of this problem for various subclasses \(\mathcal{H}\) of chordal graphs, obtaining an almost complete picture for two parameters: \(k\) and \(n-k\). We also consider the Identification problem, which is to test, for two given graphs \(G\) and \(H\), whether \(G\) can be identified to \(H\). We determine the parameterized complexity of this problem when \(H\) is a graph from one of our testbed classes, taking the number of simplicial vertices of \(H\) as the parameter.

papers.title: On the regularity index of the minimum distance function in projective nested Cartesian codes
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a projective nested product of fields and let $δ_X(d)$ be the minimum distance in degree $d\geq 1$ of the projective nested Cartesian code $C_X(d)$. The regularity index ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ of the minimum distance function $δ_X$ is the minimum integer $d_0\geq 0$ such that $δ_X(d)=1$ for $d\geq d_0$. We give a formula for ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ by determining an indicator function of least degree for each point of $X$ and using the fact that ${\rm reg}(δ_X)$ is the ${\rm v}$-number of the vanishing ideal $I_X$ of $X$. Then we give an arithmetical criterion that characterizes when $X$ is Cayley--Bacharach.

papers.title: Uniqueness and Mixing in the Low-Temperature Random-Cluster Model on Trees and Random Graphs
papers.abstract: We study the random-cluster model on trees and treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p\in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q\in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, approximately sampling from this model on graphs of degree at most $Δ$ is computationally hard. At parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf{u}}(q,Δ)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all bounded degree graphs. On typical graphs (e.g., random regular graphs), the same is predicted at $p > p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$, where $p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $Δ$-regular wired tree. Our first result establishes this non-uniqueness/uniqueness phase transition at $p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$ for all $q$ on the infinite $Δ$-regular wired tree, resolving a conjecture of H{ä}ggstr{ö}m (1996). For this, we establish weak spatial mixing at $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$ under sufficiently wired boundary conditions. We use this understanding of decay of correlations to show that on the wired tree on $n$ vertices, whenever $q>1$ and $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$, the mixing time of random-cluster Glauber dynamics is a near-optimal $n^{1+o(1)}$. We then extend these results on spatial and temporal mixing from the tree to treelike geometries with mostly wired boundaries and use them to show that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix rapidly on the random $Δ$-regular graph for all $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,Δ)$ as long as $q \ge C \log Δ$, providing an efficient sampling algorithm for both the random-cluster and Potts models in this context.

papers.title: Minimal $a$-numbers of Artin--Schreier covers of ordinary curves
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $d$ be a positive integer not divisible by $p$. We define a non-empty Zariski open subset $U$ of the space of polynomials of degree $d$, and for $f(x)\in U(k)$, we compute the $a$-number of the curve defined by $y^p-y=f(x)$. This $a$-number realizes a lower bound given by Booher and Cais, so the latter is tight. Our result also implies that the bound of Booher and Cais for minimal $a$-numbers of Artin-Schreier covers of ordinary curves is tight.

papers.title: Generalized Howe curves of genus 4, 5, and 6 with completely decomposable Jacobians
papers.abstract: Superspecial curves are important objects in number theory and algebraic geometry, and the existence of such a curve of genus $g \geq 4$ is an open problem, for general characteristics $p > 0$. As a computational approach to this problem, Kudo-Harashita-Howe (2020) showed that a superspecial curve of genus 4 exists in each characteristic $p$ with $7 < p < 20000$. Their method restricted attention to a specific class of curves, known as Howe curves, for which superspeciality is reduced to those of curves of genus at most 2. In this paper, we focus on a more specific class of curves, namely Howe curves whose Jacobians decompose into a product of four elliptic curves. By restricting our attention to such curves, the superspeciality reduces to the supersingularity of elliptic curves, which enables us to construct a superspecial curve of genus 4 more efficiently than Kudo-Harashita-Howe's method. As our first main result, we confirmed by computer the existence of such superspecial curves of genus 4 in characteristics $p$ with $20000 < p < 10^6$. Using a similar approach, we also propose constructions of superspecial curves of genera 5 and 6 from only supersingular elliptic curves. Furthermore, computational experiments establish the existence of superspecial curves of genus 5 (resp. genus 6) in characteristics $p$ with $13 < p < 10^5$ (resp. $7 < p < 10^5$).

papers.title: The Huang Algebra Ideal and the Diagonal Shift Property
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a grading-restricted vertex algebra and let $A^\infty(V )=U^\infty(V)/Q^\infty(V)$ be the associative algebra constructed by Huang, where $U^\infty(V)$ is the space of column-finite infinite matrices with entries in $V$ and $Q^\infty(V)$ is an ideal of a (nonassociative) algebra structure on $U^\infty(V)$ defined by Huang. Huang introduced families of elements in $Q^\infty(V)$ and conjectured that these elements generate $Q^\infty(V)$. We introduce the ``diagonal shift property" and prove that the elements that Huang conjectured as a generating set for $Q^\infty(V)$ satisfy this property. On the other hand, in the case that $V$ is the rank one Heisenberg vertex operator algebra, we construct infinitely many linearly independent elements in $Q^\infty(V)$ that do not satisfy the diagonal shift property. As a corollary, we disprove Huang's conjecture.

papers.title: Contraherent cosheaves of contramodules on Noetherian formal schemes
papers.abstract: There are two main results in this paper: the MGM equivalence between the conventional derived categories of abelian/exact categories, and the derived co-contra correspondence (i.e., an equivalence between the coderived and the contraderived category). Firstly, for any Noetherian formal scheme that is either of finite Krull dimension or semi-separated, we construct a triangulated equivalence between the conventional unbounded derived categories of the abelian category of quasi-coherent torsion sheaves and the exact category of contraherent cosheaves of contramodules. A natural dedualizing complex of quasi-coherent torsion sheaves is constructed and used for that purpose. Secondly, for any Noetherian formal scheme with a dualizing complex of quasi-coherent torsion sheaves, we construct a triangulated equivalence between the coderived category of quasi-coherent torsion sheaves and the contraderived category of contraherent cosheaves of contramodules. The exact category of contraherent cosheaves of contramodules on a locally Noetherian formal scheme, as well as the exact categories of locally contraherent cosheaves of contramodules (with respect to a given open covering) are defined and discussed in this paper. The exposition in the section of preliminaries in adic commutative algebra is worked out in the greater generality of arbitrary commutative rings with adic topologies (of finitely generated ideals).

papers.title: Statistical and Computational Limits for Cumulant Tensor Inference: A Regime in Which Efficient Detection Is Harder Than Efficient Estimation
papers.abstract: We study estimation and detection of high-order cumulant tensors from $n$ i.i.d. observations of a $p$-dimensional random vector, with performance measured in the tensor spectral norm. Under sub-Gaussianity, we show that the minimax rate for estimating the order-$d$ cumulant tensor is $\sqrt{p/n}\wedge 1$. In contrast to covariance estimation, the natural plug-in estimator obtained by replacing population moments in the moment--cumulant formula with sample moments, which we call the sample cumulant tensor, is generally not rate-optimal for $d\ge 3$, and we construct an estimator that attains the minimax rate. On the computational side, we study testing whether the $d$-th order cumulant tensor vanishes after whitening. We provide evidence, under a model-specific low-degree conjecture, that detection is computationally hard when $n\ll p^{d/2}$. At the same time, we identify a regime in which an efficiently computable estimator achieves error smaller than the separation at which polynomial-time tests can reliably distinguish the null from the alternative under the same conjecture. This reveals an unusual reverse detection--estimation gap: computationally efficient detection can be harder than computationally efficient estimation. The underlying reason is that the relevant loss, tensor spectral norm, is itself NP-hard to compute, creating a new form of computational--statistical gap.

papers.title: Stone Duality for Monads
papers.abstract: We introduce a contravariant idempotent adjunction between (i) the category of ranked monads on $\mathsf{Set}$; and (ii) the category of internal categories and internal retrofunctors in the category of locales. The left adjoint takes a monad $T$-viewed as a notion of computation, following Moggi-to its localic behaviour category $\mathsf{LB}T$. This behaviour category is understood as "the universal transition system" for interacting with $T$: its "objects" are states and the "morphisms" are transitions. On the other hand, the right adjoint takes a localic category $\mathsf{LC}$-similarly understood as a transition system-to the monad $Γ\mathsf{LC}$ where $(Γ\mathsf{LC})A$ is the set of $A$-indexed families of local sections to the source map which jointly partition the locale of objects. The fixed points of this adjunction consist of (i) hyperaffine-unary monads, i.e., those monads where term $t$ admits a read-only operation $\bar{t}$ predicting the output of $t$; and (ii) ample localic categories, i.e., whose source maps are local homeomorphisms and whose locale of objects are strongly zero-dimensional. The hyperaffine-unary monads arise in earlier works by Johnstone and Garner as a syntactic characterization of those monads with Cartesian closed Eilenberg-Moore categories. This equivalence is the Stone duality for monads; so-called because it further restricts to the classical Stone duality by viewing a Boolean algebra $B$ as a monad of $B$-partitions and the corresponding Stone space as a localic category with only identity morphisms.

papers.title: New Characterizations of Nonsmooth Convex Functions via Generalized Derivatives
papers.abstract: This paper studies the convexity properties of nonsmooth extended-real-valued weakly convex functions, a class of functions that is central to modern optimization and its applications. We establish new characterizations of convexity using second-order generalized derivative tools, including subgradient graphical derivatives, second subderivatives, and second-order subdifferentials. These tools allow us to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for convexity in the nonsmooth framework.

papers.title: $p$-Ordinary Part of Hyperbolic Cycles on Modular Curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study hyperbolic cycles in the first homology group of congruence subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with local coefficients. We prove that, for any prime number $p$, the $p$-ordinary part of the first homology group is generated by hyperbolic cycles.

papers.title: From cut sets to cube complexes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain an action on a cube complex from an action on a path-connected topological space with a system of divisions. In the settings of hyperbolic groups or relatively hyperbolic groups with no peripheral splittings, our result provides an alternate route to Sageev's construction of a cube complex action from a collection of (relatively) quasiconvex subgroups of a (relatively) hyperbolic group.

papers.title: A Simple Categorical Calculus of Interacting Processes
papers.abstract: We present a calculus that models a simple sort of process interaction. Our calculus consists of a collection of terms together with a rewrite relation, parameterised by an arbitrary multicategory whose morphisms we understand as non-interactive processes. We show that our calculus is confluent and terminating, and that terms modulo the induced convertibility relation form a virtual double category. We relate our calculus to the free cornering of a monoidal category, which is a double-categorical model of process interaction that is similar in spirit to the calculus presented herein. Precisely, we construct a functor from the virtual double category given by our calculus into the underlying virtual double category of the free cornering of the free monoidal category on the multicategory of non-interacting processes. If we think of the terms of our calculus as programs and the rewriting system as an operational semantics for these programs, this functor gives a sound denotational semantics for our calculus in terms of the free cornering.

papers.title: Fields with no everywhere good abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We extend methods of Fontaine, Abrashkin and Schoof to obtain criteria determining number fields K over which no non-zero abelian variety with everywhere good reduction exists. As an application, under the GRH, we find 26847 such fields of various degrees up to 16.

papers.title: Monoidal categories graded by partial commutative monoids
papers.abstract: Effectful categories have two classes of morphisms: pure morphisms, which form a monoidal category; and effectful morphisms, which can only be combined monoidally with central morphisms (such as the pure ones), forming a premonoidal category. This suggests seeing morphisms of an effectful category as carrying a grade that combines under the monoidal product in a partially defined manner. We axiomatize this idea with the notion of monoidal category graded by a partial commutative monoid (PCM). Monoidal categories arise as the special case of grading by the singleton PCM, and effectful categories arise from grading by a two-element PCM. Further examples include grading by powerset PCMs, modelling non-interfering parallelism for programs accessing shared resources, and grading by intervals, modelling bounded resource usage. We show that effectful categories form a coreflective subcategory of PCM-graded monoidal categories; introduce cartesian structure, recovering Freyd categories; and describe PCM-graded monoidal categories as monoids by viewing a PCM as a thin promonoidal category.

papers.title: Convex algebras on an interval with semicontinuous monotone operations
papers.abstract: In a recent work of Matteo Mio on compact quantitative equational theories (here compact means that all its consequences are derivable by means of finite proofs) convex algebras on the carrier set [0,1] whose operations are monotone and satisfy certain semicontinuity properties occurred. We fully classify those algebraic structures by giving an explicit construction of all possible convex operations on [0,1] possessing the mentioned properties. Our result thus describes exactly the range of theories to which Mio's theorem applies.

papers.title: A Known M-Curve of Degree 8 in OSCAR
papers.abstract: We show how the computer algebra system OSCAR can be used to retrace geometric constructions of plane algebraic curves and provide topologically correct and visually pleasing drawings. The approach is illustrated on Shustin's construction from 1987 of a particular M-curve of degree eight. We arrive at an explicit homogeneous trivariate polynomial with rational coefficients, and we provide a computational proof of all claimed properties of Shustin's original article.

papers.title: Design of Hierarchical Excitable Networks
papers.abstract: We provide a method to systematically construct vector fields for which the dynamics display transitions corresponding to a desired hierarchical connection structure. This structure is given as a finite set of directed graphs $\mathbf{G}_1,\dotsc,\mathbf{G}_N$ (the lower level), together with another digraph $\mathbfΓ$ on $N$ vertices (the top level). The dynamic realizations of $\mathbf{G}_1,\dotsc,\mathbf{G}_N$ are heteroclinic networks and they can be thought of as individual connection patterns on a given set of states. Edges in $\mathbfΓ$ correspond to transitions between these different patterns. In our construction, the connections given through $\mathbfΓ$ are not heteroclinic, but excitable with zero threshold. This describes a dynamical transition between two invariant sets where every $δ$-neighborhood of the first set contains an initial condition with $ω$-limit in the second set. Thus, we prove a theorem that allows the systematic creation of hierarchical networks that are excitable on the top level, and heteroclinic on the lower level. Our results modify and extend the simplex realization method by Ashwin & Postlethwaite.

papers.title: Approximation of invariant measures for stochastic functional differential equations with infinite delay via an explicit finite-memory scheme
papers.abstract: Owing to the intrinsic computational limitation that infinite memory cannot be stored numerically, the approximation of invariant probability measures (IPMs) for stochastic functional differential equations (SFDEs) with infinite delay remains an open problem. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing an explicit finite-memory truncated Euler-Maruyama scheme that combines memory and state truncation for such SFDEs. We establish strong convergence of the numerical segment process over any finite time horizon and obtain a convergence order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. We further prove that this numerical segment process admits a unique IPM and that its IPM converges to the exact counterpart under the $L^2$-Wasserstein metric as the step size vanishes, with an explicit convergence rate. The framework applies to both linear and superlinear coefficients.

papers.title: Complete Diagrammatic Axiomatisations of Relative Entropy
papers.abstract: Relative entropy is a fundamental class of distances between probability distributions, with widespread applications in probability theory, statistics, and machine learning. In this work, we study relative entropy from a categorical perspective, viewing it as a quantitative enrichment of categories of stochastic matrices. We consider two natural monoidal structures on stochastic matrices, given by the Kronecker product and the direct sum. Our main results are complete axiomatisations of Kullback-Leibler divergence and, more generally, of Rényi divergences of arbitrary order, for each such structure. Our axiomatic theories are formulated within the framework of quantitative monoidal algebra, using a graphical language of string diagrams enriched with quantitative equations.

papers.title: Geometry and biological processes
papers.abstract: We suggest a geometric approach to modeling biochemical processes, aiming at those processes that occur in humans with food sensitivities or chemical sensitivities.

papers.title: Zero Variance Portfolio
papers.abstract: When the number of assets is larger than the sample size, the minimum variance portfolio interpolates the training data, delivering pathological zero in-sample variance. We show that if the weights of the zero variance portfolio are learned by a novel ``Ridgelet'' estimator, in a new test data this portfolio enjoys out-of-sample generalizability. It exhibits the double descent phenomenon and can achieve optimal risk in the overparametrized regime when the number of assets dominates the sample size. In contrast, a ``Ridgeless'' estimator which invokes the pseudoinverse fails in-sample interpolation and diverges away from out-of-sample optimality. Extensive simulations and empirical studies demonstrate that the Ridgelet method performs competitively in high-dimensional portfolio optimization.

papers.title: Constrained Mean Field Games with Grushin type dynamics
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to a class of finite horizon deterministic mean field games with Grushin type dynamics, state constraints and nonlocal coupling. First, we consider the optimal control problem that each agent aims to solve when the evolution of the population is given and we establish some properties as: the existence of an optimal trajectory for any starting point $(x,t)$, the closed graph property for the multivalued map which associates to each point $(x,t)$ the set of optimal trajectories starting from that point, endowed with a suitable notion of convergence, the continuity of the value function. The main issue to overcome is due to the local interplay at boundary points between the set of state constraints and the degenerate dynamics. To this end, we shall point out two different sets of assumptions which are both sufficient for these properties. Afterwards, we tackle the mean field games; taking advantage of the aforementioned properties, we prove the existence of a relaxed equilibrium (which describes the evolution of the game in terms of a probability on the set of admissible trajectories) and derive the existence of a mild solution (which is a couple formed by the value function for the generic player and a family of time dependent measures on the state).

papers.title: Constructions of contractibility in finite subset spaces
papers.abstract: The space of all finite non-empty subsets of a topological space $X$, also known as the Ran space of $X$, is weakly contractible for $X$ path connected. We consider subspaces $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ of the Ran space given by all subsets of $X$ of size at most $n$, and their first homotopy groups. These groups are known to be trivial for $n\geqslant 3$, though the proofs are not constructive. We draw an explicit contraction in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 3}(S^1)$ of the generator of $π_1(S^1)$, which we then use to conclude that the induced maps $π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 2n+1}(X))$ and $π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n+2}(X))$ are trivial for all positive integers $n$. Pathological maps with infinitely many strata changes in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ are resolved via locally contractible neighbourhoods and exit paths. From this we conclude the triviality of $π_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X))$, for all $n\geqslant 3$.
