In the case of nontrivial discriminant actions, we show that such automorphisms only exist for finitely many deformation types and orders

papers.title: Embedding a Quantum Rank Two Quadric in a Quantum $\mathbb{P}^3$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we classify connected graded quadratic Artin-Schelter regular (AS-regular, henceforth) algebras of global dimension four that have a Hilbert series the same as that of the polynomial ring on four generators and that map onto a twisted homogeneous coordinate ring of a rank-two quadric. A twisted homogeneous coordinate ring is a construction that was defined by Artin, Tate, and Van den Bergh in \cite{ATV1, ATV2, AVdB1990} in the context of the classification of AS-regular algebras of global dimension three. In \cite{SV99,VVr}, the authors classified AS-regular algebras of global dimension four that map onto the twisted homogeneous coordinate ring of a rank-three and a rank-four quadric, respectively. We expand on their work to include the case of coordinate rings of a rank-two quadric.

papers.title: The rigidity of Doyle circle packings on the infinite hexagonal triangulation
papers.abstract: Peter Doyle conjectured that locally univalent circle packings on the hexagonal lattice only consist of regular hexagonal packings and Doyle spirals, which is called the Doyle conjecture. In this paper, we prove a rigidity theorem for Doyle spirals in the class of infinite circle packings on the hexagonal lattice whose radii ratios of adjacent circles have a uniform lower bound in one fixed lattice direction. This gives a partial answer to the Doyle conjecture. Based on a new observation that the logarithm of the radii ratio of adjacent circles is a weighted discrete harmonic function, we prove the result via the Liouville theorem for discrete harmonic functions. Moreover, we establish a Ring Lemma for locally univalent circle packings with bounded degree, assuming that their carrier surfaces are the universal covers of $\mathbb{C}-\{0\}$, and the visual angles of all circles viewed from the origin are uniformly bounded away from $π$. This provides a new geometric sufficient condition for the rigidity of Doyle spirals.

papers.title: Quasi-$F^e$-splittings and quasi-$F$-regularity
papers.abstract: We develop the theory of quasi-$F^e$-splittings, quasi-$F$-regularity, and quasi-$+$-regularity.

papers.title: Conic Multiview Varieties
papers.abstract: We present an algebraic study of projections of conics in space onto multiple images of pinhole cameras. We study the Zariski closures of the projection images, which we call conic multiview varieties. Extending previous work for point and line multiview varieties, we use back-projected cones to describe these varieties. For two views, we determine the defining ideals of conic multiview varieties and describe their singular loci. For any number of views, we characterize when the simplest possible set-theoretic description is achieved based on the geometry of the camera centers. Finally, we investigate the complexity of the associated triangulation problem and conjecture the Euclidean distance degree for the conic multiview variety for two cameras.

papers.title: Oscillatory free boundary problems in heterogeneous media
papers.abstract: We investigate a class of free boundary problems with oscillatory singularities within heterogeneous media. Our main result yields sharp regularity estimates along the free boundary, provided the power of the singularity varies in a Dini-continuous fashion below a certain threshold. We also reveal an interesting repelling estimate preventing the free boundary from touching the region where the singularity power oscillates above the threshold.

papers.title: Koopman Regularization and Independent Koopman Eigenfunction Approximation
papers.abstract: The geometry induced from a dynamical system dictates its latent structures, conservation laws, and intrinsic coordinates. This paper provides two procedures to extract the governing equations of a dynamical system from its samples, \acf{KR} and \acf{IKEA}. These procedures leverage the prior knowledge from the Koopman Eigenfunction Space. Both techniques extract a functionally independent set of Koopman Eigenfunctions, which are the intrinsic coordinates. Consequently, despite its finite cardinality, the governing equations are immaculately restored. Thus, the principle of parsimony is implemented. Samples can be taken either from a vector field or from orbits of the system. \acs{KR} extracts the governing law from samples of the vector field, and \acs{IKEA} extracts it from samples of trajectories of the system. Both algorithms are based on constrained optimization methods for learning the governing equations from sparse and corrupted samples of the vector field or trajectories. These procedures yield promising results in denoising, generalization, and dimensionality reduction and achieve better results than \acs{DMD}, \acs{EDMD}, \acs{PINN}, and \acs{SINDy} in dynamical system restoration.

papers.title: Finite translation orbits on double families of abelian varieties (with an appendix by E. Amerik)
papers.abstract: We study two families of $g$-dimensional abelian varieties, induced by distinct rational maps defined on a common variety $\overline{\mathcal A}$ and mapping to two bases $\overline{S}_1$ and $\overline{S}_2$. Two non-torsion sections induce birational fiberwise translations on $\overline{\mathcal A}$. We consider the action of a specific subset of the group generated by these translations. Under the assumption that $\operatorname{dim} \overline{S}_1 (= \operatorname{dim} \overline{S}_2) \leq g$, we prove that the points with finite orbit are contained in a proper Zariski closed subset. This subset is explicitly described to a certain extent. Our results generalize a theorem of Corvaja, Tsimermann, and Zannier to higher dimensions.

papers.title: Topological Anderson Insulators by homogenization theory
papers.abstract: A central property of (Chern) topological insulators is the presence of robust asymmetric transport along interfaces separating two-dimensional insulating materials in different topological phases. A Topological Anderson Insulator is an insulator whose topological phase is induced by spatial fluctuations. This paper proposes a mathematical model of perturbed Dirac equations and shows that for sufficiently large and highly oscillatory perturbations, the systems is in a different topological phase than the unperturbed model. In particular, a robust asymmetric transport indeed appears at an interface separating perturbed and unperturbed phases. The theoretical results are based on careful estimates of resolvent operators in the homogenization theory of Dirac equations and on the characterization of topological phases by the index of an appropriate Fredholm operator.

papers.title: The Complete Intersection Discrepancy of a Curve II: Families of Curves
papers.abstract: We study equisingularity of families of reduced curves over smooth parameter spaces of arbitrary positive dimension, using the difference between two analytic invariants of a curve singularity: the multiplicity of its Jacobian ideal and its complete intersection discrepancy. This difference provides a fiberwise multiplicity criterion for Whitney equisingularity. We prove that Whitney equisingularity (equivalently, strong simultaneous resolution) is characterized by equidimensionality of the fibers of the exceptional locus of either the relative conormal space or the relative Nash blowup. We further show that this condition is equivalent to the emptiness of the relative polar variety of smallest dimension. In addition, we establish that the Milnor number of a reduced curve is Zariski upper semicontinuous. As an application, we show that the constancy of the Milnor number in a family of reduced curves is equivalent to its topological equisingularity, under a natural assumption on the fibers.

papers.title: Biexact von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of biexactness for general von Neumann algebras, naturally extending the notion from group theory. We show that biexactness implies solidity for von Neumann algebras, and that many of the examples of solid von Neumann algebras contained in the literature are, in fact, biexact. We also give examples of certain crossed products arising from Gaussian actions that are solid but not biexact, and we give examples of certain $q$-Gaussian von Neumann algebras that are strongly solid but not biexact. The techniques developed involve studying a certain weak form of nuclear embeddings, and we use this setting to give a new description of weak exactness for von Neumann algebras, which allows us to answer several open problems in the literature about weakly exact von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Beating the average: how to generate profit by exploiting the inefficiencies of soccer betting
papers.abstract: In economy, markets are denoted as efficient when it is impossible to systematically generate profits which outperform the average. In the past years, the concept has been tested in other domains such as the growing sports betting market. Surprisingly, despite its large size and its level of maturity, sports betting shows traits of inefficiency. The anomalies indicate the existence of strategies which shift betting from a game of chance towards a game of skill. This article shows an example for an inefficiency detected in the German soccer betting TOTO 13er Wette, which is operated by state-run lottery agencies. Gamblers have to guess the outcome (win, draw, loss) of 13 soccer matches listed on a lottery tip. Applying stochastic methods, a recipe is presented to determine hit rates for single match outcomes. More important, the recipe provides the number of lottery tips required to achieve a specific number of strikes (number of correct match forecasts per lottery tip) for any given level of safety. An approximation is derived to cope with large numbers in hypergeometric distributions, valid under certain constraints. Overall, the strategy does lead to returns exceeding the aggregated lottery fees, resulting in moderate, but consistent profits. It is briefly discussed if lessons learned from soccer betting can be transferred back to financial markets, because gamblers and retail investors face similar challenges and opportunities.

papers.title: Consensus in label propagation on binomial random graphs
papers.abstract: Understanding how local update rules amplify small random fluctuations into global consensus is a central challenge in the study of network dynamics and decentralized processes. A prominent family of examples is given by label propagation algorithms, widely used heuristics for community detection whose analysis is complicated by the strong dependencies created as the process evolves. Despite the simplicity and practical success of this class of algorithms, a rigorous understanding of their convergence remains limited. In this paper, we study a specific variant, which we refer to as LPA, on the binomial random graph $\mathcal{G}(n,p)$ - a canonical null model with no planted community structure. We show that LPA reaches consensus asymptotically almost surely when $np\ge n^{5/8+\varepsilon}$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, thus breaking the current best $n^{3/4+\varepsilon}$ analytical barrier. More remarkably, we uncover a phase transition governing \emph{which} label survives: when $np\gg n^{2/3}$, the surviving label is asymptotically almost surely the smallest initial label, whereas for $n^{5/8+\varepsilon}\le np\ll n^{2/3}$, the surviving label is asymptotically almost surely not the smallest one. We further show that, in the critical window $np=Θ(n^{2/3})$, both outcomes have probability $Θ(1).$ Our analysis has several important ingredients. We analyze a staged exploration that progressively reveals information about the random graph while preserving some randomness needed to track the amplification of label advantages across multiple rounds. This analysis is complemented by novel coupling and decoupling arguments that control the dependencies inherent to the process. Along the way, we establish a monotonicity result for competing binomial random variables that we believe is of independent interest.

papers.title: Discrete two-generator subgroups of ${\rm PSL_2}$ over non-archimedean local fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field with residue field of characteristic $p$. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for a two-generator subgroup $G$ of ${\rm PSL_2}(K)$ to be discrete, where either $K=\mathbb{Q}_p$ or $G$ contains no elements of order $p$. We give a practical algorithm to decide whether such a subgroup $G$ is discrete. We also give practical algorithms to decide whether a two-generator subgroup of either ${\rm SL_2}(\mathbb{R})$ or ${\rm SL_2}(K)$ (where $K$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$) is dense. A crucial ingredient for this work is a structure theorem for two-generator groups acting by isometries on a $Λ$-tree.

papers.title: Harmonic analysis approach to the relative Riemann-Roch theorem on global fields
papers.abstract: In this paper we generalize and put in a new light part of ``Fouier analysis on Number fields and Hecke's zeta function''[14] by Tate. We express the relative Euler characteristic using purely adelic language. By using certain natural normalization of Haar measure on adeles we obtain the relative Riemann-Roch theorem. In particular we show that using our relative normalization of the Haar measure on adeles we can obtain the relative Riemann-Roch theorem from the adelic Poisson summation formulae. In addition, using our methods we define the relative 'size of cohomology' numbers, i.e. extract the $h^0$ and $h^1$ part of the relative Euler characteristic. Our theory not only covers both absolute and relative cases, but also the case of an arithmetic curve and a nonsingular, projective curve over a finite field.

papers.title: Parametrized Euler class and semicohomology theory
papers.abstract: Given a measurable cocycle with values in $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\mathbb{S}^1)$, we construct an $\mathrm{L}^\infty$-parametrized Euler class in bounded cohomology. We show that such a class vanishes if and only if the cocycle can be lifted to $\mathrm{Homeo}^+_{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{R})$ and it admits an equivariant family of points. We recall the notion of semicohomologous cocycles and we show that two measurable cocycles are semicohomologous if and only if they induce the same parametrized Euler class. Since for minimal cocycles, semicohomology boils down to cohomology, the parametrized Euler classes of minimal cohomologous cocycles are equal. We conclude by studying the vanishing of the real parametrized Euler class and we obtain some results about elementary cocycles.

papers.title: Balancing non-rectangular tables
papers.abstract: Balancing square and rectangular tables by rotation has been an interesting way to illustrate the intermediate value theorem. This article studies the same question for tables whose feet form a cyclic quadrilateral, following a conjecture of A.~Martin. In the idealised model behind this conjecture, the balancing act works for every such table and is a nice application of the ergodic theorem. For the actual rigid table on a Lipschitz terrain, the situation is more subtle. If the terrain is flattened enough, the table can be stabilised unless an idealised wobbling function vanishes identically, \ie unless the terrain is degenerate for the table. Even if this should happen, the tables whose feet are vertices of a regular polygon and which satisfy a non-degeneracy condition of their own can still be stabilised on every terrain with a small enough Lipschitz constant (\eg a halved regular hexagon as long as the slope is less than $3.7$\textdegree{}). On the other hand, there is an isosceles trapezoid and another table, which are shown to wobble at every angle on suitable terrains however small the Lipschitz constant is. These counterexamples are fragile: for every table, if the idealised wobbling function vanishes identically for every position of the rotation axis in a small disc, then, near the feet, the terrain is a plane or a paraboloid of revolution with a vertical axis; so in practice a slight move of the axis makes the terrain non-degenerate. The results are, with minor exceptions, formalised in Lean.

papers.title: Weighted inequalities in ergodic theory via transference
papers.abstract: We first extend Calderón's transfer principle to weighted weak type and strong type inequalities in various different settings including vector-valued setting. We show that our results can be used to prove a large class of inequalities in ergodic theory and ergodic $H^1$ spaces.

papers.title: Mass inflation and the $C^2$-inextendibility of spherically symmetric charged scalar field dynamical black holes
papers.abstract: It has long been suggested that the Cauchy horizon of dynamical black holes is subject to a weak null singularity, under the mass inflation scenario. We study in spherical symmetry the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations and \textit{while we do not directly show mass inflation}, we obtain a "mass inflation/ridigity" dichotomy. More precisely, we prove assuming (sufficiently slow) decay of the charged scalar field on the event horizon, that the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}= \mathcal{D} \cup \mathcal{S}$ for two (possibly empty) disjoint connected sets $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{S}$ such that: _$\mathcal{D}$ (the dynamical set) is a past set on which the Hawking mass blows up (mass inflation scenario). _$\mathcal{S}$ (the static set) is a future set isometric to a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon i.e.\ the radiation is zero on $\mathcal{S}$. As a consequence, we establish a novel classification of Cauchy horizons into three types: dynamical ($\mathcal{S}=\emptyset$), static ($\mathcal{D}=\emptyset$) or mixed, and prove that $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}$ is globally $C^2$-inextendible. Our main motivation is the $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture for a realistic model of spherical collapse in which charged matter emulates the repulsive role of angular momentum: in our case the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon system on one-ended space-times. As a result, we prove in spherical symmetry that: - two-ended asymptotically flat space-times are $C^2$-future-inextendible i.e. $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship is true for Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon, assuming the decay of the scalar field on the event horizon at the expected rate. - In the one-ended case, the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $C^2$-inextendible. This result suppresses the main obstruction to $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship in spherical collapse.

papers.title: Invariant Flags for Singularly Perturbed Logarithmic Systems of Rank Two
papers.abstract: We study rank-two differential systems $\hbar x \partial_x ψ+ A (x, \hbar) ψ= 0$ near a logarithmic pole, with coefficients that are holomorphic in $x$ and admit uniform factorial asymptotic expansions in the complex parameter $\hbar$. If the classical residue has distinct eigenvalues, then upon choosing an ordering and an admissible $\hbar$ direction, we transform this system to an upper-triangular form by a holomorphic gauge transformation with the same factorial asymptotic regularity on a sector in the $\hbar$-plane. Its diagonal is fully determined by the $\hbar \to 0$ and $x \to 0$ limits. This construction produces a canonical $(x,\hbar)$-dependent invariant flag. This flag specialises to the usual Levelt filtration for nonzero values of $\hbar$ on a narrower sector, and its associated graded converges to the eigenspaces of the residue as $x \to 0$ and of the leading-order matrix as $\hbar \to 0$. A Schrödinger example gives a uniform matching formula between the WKB data and the exact Frobenius exponent at a double pole.

papers.title: Positive scalar curvature on manifolds with fibered singularities
papers.abstract: A (compact) manifold with fibered $P$-singularities is a (possibly) singular pseudomanifold $M_Σ$ with two strata: an open nonsingular stratum $\mathring M$ (a smooth open manifold) and a closed stratum $βM$ (a closed manifold of positive codimension), such that a tubular neighborhood of $βM$ is a fiber bundle with fibers each looking like the cone on a fixed closed manifold $P$. We discuss what it means for such an $M_Σ$ with fibered $P$-singularities to admit an appropriate Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature, and we give necessary and sufficient conditions (the necessary conditions based on suitable versions of index theory, the sufficient conditions based on surgery methods and homotopy theory) for this to happen when the singularity type $P$ is either $\mathbb Z/k$ or $S^1$, and $M$ and the boundary of the tubular neighborhood of the singular stratum are simply connected and carry spin structures. Along the way, we prove some results of perhaps independent interest, concerning metrics on spin$^c$ manifolds with positive "twisted scalar curvature," where the twisting comes from the curvature of the spin$^c$ line bundle.

papers.title: Stability and instability of the sub-extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole interior for the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations in spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: We show non-linear stability and instability results in spherical symmetry for the interior of a charged black hole -approaching a sub-extremal Reissner-Nordström background fast enough at infinity- in presence of a massive and charged scalar field, motivated by the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in that setting : 1. Stability : We prove that spherically symmetric characteristic initial data to the Einstein-Maxwell- Klein-Gordon equations approaching a Reissner-Nordström background with a sufficiently decaying polynomial decay rate on the event horizon gives rise to a space-time possessing a Cauchy horizon in a neighbourhood of time-like infinity. Moreover if the decay is even stronger, we prove that the spacetime metric admits a continuous extension to the Cauchy horizon. This generalizes the celebrated stability result of Dafermos for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry. 2. Instability : We prove that for the class of space-times considered in the stability part, whose scalar field in addition obeys a polynomial averaged-L^2 (consistent) lower bound on the event horizon, the scalar field obeys an integrated lower bound transversally to the Cauchy horizon. As a consequence we prove that the non-degenerate energy is infinite on any null surface crossing the Cauchy horizon and the curvature of a geodesic vector field blows up at the Cauchy horizon near time-like infinity. This generalizes an instability result due to Luk and Oh for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry. This instability of the black hole interior can also be viewed as a step towards the resolution of the C^2 strong cosmic censorship conjecture for one-ended asymptotically initial data.

papers.title: Orientations for pseudoholomorphic quilts
papers.abstract: We construct orientations on moduli spaces of pseudoholomorphic quilts with seam conditions in Lagrangian correspondences equipped with relative spin structures and determine the effect of various gluing operations on the orientations. We also investigate the behavior of the orientations under composition of Lagrangian correspondences.

papers.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
papers.abstract: (Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.

papers.title: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory. The Kourovka Notebook
papers.abstract: This is a collection of open problems in group theory proposed by hundreds of mathematicians from all over the world. It has been published every 2--4 years since 1965. This is the 21st edition, which contains 150 new problems and a number of comments on problems from the previous editions. Problems with $\boldsymbol{\displaystyle{\sharp }}$ have AI-proposed solutions that are not yet confirmed by mathematicians and should be regarded as unsolved. Anyone interested is invited to look into such an AI solution and either confirm it or refute. Comments can be sent to the editors Evgeny Khukhro khukhro@yahoo.co.uk and Victor Mazurov mazurov@math.nsc.ru

papers.title: The set $\{\frac{(p+q)(p+q+1)}{2}+q: (p,q\in N)\wedge (\forall x_0,...,x_p\in N~\exists y_0,...,y_p\in\{0,...,q\}~\forall i,j,k\in \{0,...,p\}~((x_j+1=x_k => y_j+1=y_k)\wedge (x_i\cdot x_j=x_k => y_i\cdot y_j=y_k)))\}$ is not listable
papers.abstract: Let $F(x,n)$ denote the formula $$ \exists ab ~\forall i \leqslant n ~\exists swpq ~\forall jv ~\exists eg ~\{(s+w)^2+3w+s=2i ~\wedge ~\langle[j=w ~\vee ~v=q] $$ $$ \vee~[j=3i ~\wedge ~v=p+q] ~\vee ~[j=s ~\wedge ~(v=p ~\vee ~(i=n ~\wedge ~v=q+x))] $$ $$ \vee~[j=3i+1 ~\wedge ~v=pq] ~\Rightarrow ~a=v+e+ejb ~\wedge ~v+g=jb\rangle\} $$ from J. P. Jones' article in vol. 43 of J. Symbolic Logic. From the results of Jones' article, it follows that the set $J=\{n \in \mathbb{N}: \neg F(n,n)\}$ is co-recursively enumerable and not recursively enumerable. We prove that the set $$ W=\{\frac{1}{2}(p+q)(p+q+1)+q: (p,q\in \mathbb{N})~\wedge $$ $$ \forall (x_0,\ldots,x_p) \in \mathbb{N}^{p+1} ~~\exists (y_0,\ldots,y_p) \in \{0,\ldots,q\}^{p+1}$$ $$ ((\forall j,k \in \{0,\ldots,p\} ~(x_j+1=x_k \Rightarrow y_j+1=y_k))~\wedge $$ $$ (\forall i,j,k \in \{0,\ldots,p\} ~(x_i \cdot x_j=x_k \Rightarrow y_i \cdot y_j=y_k)))\} $$ is co-recursively enumerable and not recursively enumerable. Let $β:\mathbb{N}^3 \to \mathbb{N}$ denote Gödel's $β$ function. For $x_1,x_2,x_3 \in \mathbb{N}$, $β(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ equals the remainder after integer division of $x_1$ by $1+(x_3+1) \cdot x_2$. We prove that the set $W$ consists of all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $$ \forall u,v \in \mathbb{N} ~\exists a,b,p,q \in \mathbb{N} ~((2n=(p+q)(p+q+1)+2q) ~\wedge ~\forall i,j,k \in \{0,\ldots,p\} $$ $$ ((β(a,b,i) \leqslant q) ~\wedge ~(β(u,v,j)+1=β(u,v,k) \Rightarrow β(a,b,j)+1=β(a,b,k)) ~\wedge $$ $$ (β(u,v,i) \cdot β(u,v,j)=β(u,v,k) \Rightarrow β(a,b,i) \cdot β(a,b,j)=β(a,b,k)))) $$ We express the above formula in Peano arithmetic.

papers.title: On a property of plane curves
papers.abstract: Let $γ:[0,1]\to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a continuous curve with $γ(0)=(0,0)$ and $γ(1)=(1,1)$. We prove that if $γ(t)\in(0,1)^2$ for all $t\in(0,1)$, then for each $n\in \mathbb{N}$ there exist points $A_1,\dots,A_n$ on $γ$ such that, with $A_0=(0,0)$ and $A_{n+1}=(1,1)$, the horizontal increments $π_1(\overrightarrow{A_iA_{i+1}})$ and the vertical increments $π_2(\overrightarrow{A_iA_{i+1}})$, $0\le i\le n$, are positive and coincide up to order. More generally, the same conclusion holds as soon as $γ$ contains an arc that joins two points of the diagonal segment, lies on one side of the diagonal, and satisfies a mild one-sided boundary condition. This covers, for instance, the graph of every continuous function $f$ with $f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=1$, with no restriction on the range of $f$. In all cases the rearrangement can be taken to be a cyclic shift by one place of a block of consecutive increments. The main tool is a version of the mountain climbers' theorem in which one function is piecewise monotone and the other is an arbitrary continuous function. As an application, any two non-atomic probability measures on $[0,1]$ satisfying a mild condition admit, for each $n$, a partition of $[0,1]$ into $n+1$ consecutive intervals whose two lists of measures are rearrangements of each other.

papers.title: Uniqueness of scalar-flat ALE Kähler metrics
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness of scalar-flat Kähler metrics in a fixed Kähler class on an asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) Kähler manifold, assuming only differentiated $o(1)$ decay to a fixed Euclidean metric on the end. In complex dimension $n\geq2$, under suitable polynomial decay of the reference metric, we prove that the relative Mabuchi functional is finite, continuous, and convex along weak geodesics whose endpoint potentials satisfy $u=O(r^{-γ})$, $γ>2n-4$, together with the corresponding derivative estimates. Combining this convexity with the analysis of the Lichnerowicz operator in weighted spaces, we obtain uniqueness by a perturbation argument. Decay improvement and comparison of the asymptotic charts produce a global potential with the required decay for the difference of the two cohomologous scalar-flat Kähler forms. The argument also extends to asymptotically conical Kähler metrics approaching a fixed Ricci-flat Kähler cone under prescribed decay assumptions.

papers.title: Asymptotic Stability and $L^p$ Time-Decay Rates of Rarefaction Waves for Systems of Viscous Conservation Laws
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic stability and quantitative time-decay rates of rarefaction waves for one-dimensional $n\times n$ strictly hyperbolic systems of viscous conservation laws. While the nonlinear stability of rarefaction waves for $2\times 2$ systems was established by Xin \cite{Xin1988,Xin1989}, extending such results to general $n\times n$ systems presents additional difficulties arising from the possible coexistence of positive and negative transverse relative characteristic speeds and nonlinear interactions between distinct characteristic families. Moreover, establishing standalone $L^p$ energy estimates and explicit algebraic decay rates for general viscous systems without $L^1$ localization remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we establish both the global $H^2(\R)$ asymptotic stability and, for the first time, standalone physical-space $L^p$ energy estimates and explicit algebraic $L^p$ time-decay rates for weak rarefaction waves. Specifically, for every integer $p\ge 3$, we prove that the perturbation $U(t)-\bar{U}(t)$ around the smooth Burgers rarefaction profile $\bar{U}$ decays in $L^p(\R)$ at the rate \[ \|U(t)-\bar{U}(t)\|_{L^p}\le C_p\bigl(\|U_0-\bar{U}(0)\|_{H^2}^2+δ^3\bigr)^{1/2}(1+t)^{-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{p})}, \] where $δ$ denotes the wave strength. Our proof combines a diagonal characteristic weight matrix that yields coercive rarefaction damping in all characteristic modes with directed wave-interaction functionals that exploit the strict separation of characteristic speeds to control nonlinear coupling between distinct characteristic families. These estimates lead to a closed $L^p$ Lyapunov inequality, from which the algebraic time-decay rates follow by the one-dimensional Nash inequality.

papers.title: A High-Dimensional LM Test for Cross-Sectional Independence with Serially Correlated Data
papers.abstract: We develop a high-dimensional Lagrange multiplier (LM) test for cross-sectional independence in Gaussian panels with a common stationary, short-memory temporal covariance matrix. The statistic is based on the trace of the square of R, where R is the sample correlation matrix. When the cross-sectional and time dimensions grow proportionally, we derive explicit expansions for the null mean and variance in terms of temporal spectral moments. Random diagonal normalization produces a non-negligible centering correction, while squared sample correlations sharing a cross-sectional unit contribute an additional variance term. Both corrections vanish under temporal independence. We establish a central limit theorem under the null, consistency against fixed alternatives, and a Gaussian-shift limit with a detection boundary under local alternatives. Monte Carlo experiments examine the size and power of the oracle test and feasible versions that estimate the temporal spectral moments. The asymptotic theory applies to the oracle statistic; feasible procedures are evaluated numerically.

papers.title: Uniqueness of self-shrinking ends asymptotic to a cylindrical cone
papers.abstract: Let $C^m \subset \mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ be a regular embedded cone, where $n\geq 1$, and let $k\geq 1$. We prove that two smooth, connected, properly embedded self-shrinking ends whose blow-downs converge locally smoothly to the same cylindrical cone $C\times\mathbb{R}^k$ away from the axis $\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}^k$ must coincide. As a consequence, we obtain a rigidity result for complete self-shrinkers asymptotic to cylindrical cones. The proof uses Gaussian decay estimates and a sectorial Carleman estimate to establish backward uniqueness.

papers.title: The module structure of ideals in degree $p$ extensions of $p$-adic fields
papers.abstract: Let $L/K$ be a degree $p$ extension of $p$-adic fields. We shall provide a complete characterization for the freeness of any fractional ideal $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$, $h\in\mathbb{Z}$, of $L$ as a module over its associated order $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ in the only Hopf-Galois structure on $L/K$, and an explicit description of $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$. We show that there is no loss of generality in assuming that $0\leq h\leq p-1$ and that the normal closure of $L/K$ is totally ramified over $K$. If $L/K$ is maximally ramified, then $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ is the maximal $\mathcal{O}_K$-order in $H$ and $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$ is $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$-free. The remaining cases correspond to typical extensions. For these, we provide an $\mathcal{O}_K$-basis of $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ and a characterization for the condition that $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$ is $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$-free. In the non-exceptional cases, which had been partially studied in the Galois setting, the characterization depends on $h$ and the continued fraction expansion of $\frac{a}{p}$, where $a$ is the residue class mod $p$ of the (fractional) ramification jump $\ell$ of $L/K$. In the remaining exceptional case, where $L/K$ is almost maximally ramified and $a+1\leq h\leq p-1$, it consists in a numerical common minimizer condition.

papers.title: On the exponential Diophantine equation $\left(P_{n+1}^{(k)}\right)^{x}-\left(P_{n-1}^{(k)}\right)^{x}=2P_{m}^{(k)}$
papers.abstract: For the Pell numbers one has $P_{n+1}-P_{n-1}=2P_n$ and $P_{n+1}^2-P_{n-1}^2=2P_{2n}$. We look for all the solutions of $\big(P_{n+1}^{(k)}\big)^x-\big(P_{n-1}^{(k)}\big)^x=2P_m^{(k)}$ in positive integers $k\ge2$, $n$, $m$, $x$, where $P^{(k)}$ is the $k$-generalized Pell sequence. We prove that for $k=2$ the two identities above give all the solutions, and that for $k\ge3$ the only solutions are $(n,m,x)=(1,1,1),(1,2,2),(2,2,1)$. In contrast with the analogous equation for $k$-generalized Fibonacci numbers, there are no parametric families of solutions. The proof uses an auxiliary equation with Fibonacci numbers which does not depend on $k$, Matveev's lower bound for linear forms in logarithms, the reduction of Dujella and Pethő, and, for large $k$, the fact that the dominant root of $P^{(k)}$ is very close to $\varphi^2$.

papers.title: Improved criteria for geometric properties of confluent hypergeometric functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sufficient conditions for several geometric properties of confluent hypergeometric functions. Using differential subordination techniques, we derive parameter conditions ensuring lower bounds for the real part of the confluent hypergeometric function and sectorial subordination of its derivative. We also obtain criteria for strong convexity and strong starlikeness of prescribed order. In addition, we investigate the close-to-convexity and starlikeness of the confluent hypergeometric functions. Particular cases yield corresponding results for generalized Laguerre polynomials. The obtained criteria are compared with existing sufficient conditions, and their implications for the geometric theory of special functions are discussed.

papers.title: On the exponential Diophantine equation $\left(P_{n}^{(k)}\right)^{x}+\left(P_{r}^{(k)}\right)^{x}=P_{m}^{(k)}$
papers.abstract: The Pell numbers satisfy $P_n^2+P_{n+1}^2=P_{2n+1}$, and Bravo, Luca and Pomeo recently found all the cases in which the sum of the $x$-th powers of two consecutive $k$-generalized Pell numbers is again a $k$-generalized Pell number. We ask what happens when the two indices are arbitrary, that is, we solve $\big(P_n^{(k)}\big)^x+\big(P_r^{(k)}\big)^x=P_m^{(k)}$ in positive integers $k\ge2$, $n\ge r$, $m$ and $x$. The answer is that nothing new appears: apart from $1^x+1^x=2$, every solution has consecutive indices. The proof combines linear forms in logarithms with an auxiliary Fibonacci equation which does not depend on $k$, and, for large $k$, with the fact that the dominant root of the sequence is very close to $\varphi^2$. For the reduction step, the method of Dujella and Pethő fails for large indices and has to be replaced by a criterion of Legendre type.

papers.title: Two teams that cancel: a didactic analysis of a teaching progression for signed numbers from Grade 5 to Grade 7
papers.abstract: Signed numbers make learners revise what addition, subtraction and the minus sign meant for whole numbers. This paper presents the design rationale and a critical analysis of a three-level source progression for signed numbers (Grades 5-7, nominal ages 10-13), from which French-curriculum and International Baccalaureate chapters published at https://commeunjeu.org are assembled. One representation is presented first and taken up throughout: an integer is drawn as a collection of positive and negative units, a positive and a negative unit forming a zero pair that leaves nothing. An integer therefore has many drawings, which makes visible the construction of the integers as classes of pairs of natural numbers. The design hypothesis is that the gesture pupils perform with the units, inserting a zero in the form a + (-a), is shared by the subtraction of a negative number, by the worked examples that accompany the 2026 French programme, and by the derivation of the sign of a product of two negatives through distributivity; the progression does not model that product, it derives it from the zero pair, a derivation that holds only if distributivity is kept. The number line supports position, order and distance; contexts provide applications. The choices are related to the epistemological obstacles described by Glaeser, to studies of counter and number-line models, including a classroom comparison in which a path model gave better results than chips, immediately and five weeks later, and to the French and IB curricula. A block-level audit of the dated source documents found the representation absent from the first level, no exercise asking pupils to draw, and the decisive subtraction never drawn; the revisions made after the audit are recorded. No empirical evaluation is reported; hypotheses for one are stated.

papers.title: Small-time controllability of affine systems and quadratic Lie brackets
papers.abstract: We prove a new sufficient condition for small-time global exact controllability of finite-dimensional control-affine systems. It points out that, under a natural Lie algebra rank condition, quadratic Lie brackets are the only possible obstacles to controllability. This result extends to infinite-dimensional settings such as the global approximate controllability of diffeomorphisms. It also allows us to interpret recent results in PDE control theory.

papers.title: Monotonicity and bounded variation for harmonic mappings with applications to special functions
papers.abstract: We investigate sufficient conditions for the close-to-convexity and univalence of planar harmonic mappings. First, we establish a unified monotonicity criterion for harmonic mappings that incorporates the ordinary and odd harmonic cases. We then develop a criterion based on the total variation of successive coefficient differences. Unlike conventional monotonicity conditions, this approach allows the coefficient sequences to exhibit non-monotone behavior. Several previously established criteria for harmonic close-to-convexity are recovered as particular consequences. Applications are developed for harmonic mappings associated with Gaussian hypergeometric functions and Legendre polynomials, with explicit restrictions on their parameters.

papers.title: Unconditionally $L^2$-stable explicit--implicit--null filtered Runge--Kutta methods for general nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations
papers.abstract: We develop unconditionally $L^2$-stable explicit--implicit--null (EIN) filtered Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with space-, time-, state-, and gradient-dependent diffusion coefficients. The methods are linearly implicit in the sense that they evaluate nonlinear terms explicitly and require only linear solves. Unlike classical EIN methods that are direct applications of implicit--explicit (IMEX) RKs, our construction is built upon explicit RKs. The key ingredient is two-sided symmetric filtering applied at each RK stage: a high-order filter is applied both before and after evaluating the original nonlinear residual. It leads to a dissipation estimate independent of the time step and retains the underlying RK order formally. Assuming time-dependent splitting operators with stagewise pointwise coefficient bounds, we rigorously prove non-increasing $L^2$ norm for arbitrary time steps. A quadratic matrix criterion covers explicit RK-based methods with positive weights, while strong stability preserving (SSP) compositions yield exact energy identities and weighted dissipation estimates. We present SSP methods through fourth order and a method based on the classical RK4. The framework accommodates spatial discretizations with discrete gradient structures including continuous Galerkin, Bassi--Rebay 1, the method of Brezzi et al., and local discontinuous Galerkin. Compatible summation-by-parts discretizations with simultaneous approximation terms are also covered in their discrete mass norm.

papers.title: Near-Quadratic Error-Free Graph Matching above Otter's Threshold via Approximate Local Tree Correlation Testing
papers.abstract: This paper presents a near-quadratic-time algorithm that correctly matches almost all nodes of two correlated Erdős-Rényi graphs without any incorrect matches. Each graph has average degree $λ$ and its edges are subsampled from a common parent Erdős-Rényi graph with $n$ nodes, with subsampling probability $s$. The nodes of one graph are then relabeled by an unknown permutation. The algorithm is built on a test for correlated versus independent Galton-Watson trees with approximated likelihood ratios. For every constant $s>\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{Otter}}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{Otter}}\approx0.338$ is Otter's tree-counting constant, and every $λ=ω(1)$ with $λ=(\log n)^{O(1)}$, the algorithm outputs a partial matching of size $n-o(n)$ that contains no incorrect matches with high probability. If, in addition, $λs\ge(1+ε)\log n$ for a constant $ε>0$, a seeded completion step recovers the permutation exactly. In both cases, the time complexity of the algorithm is $n^{2+o(1)}$ with high probability, whereas previous polynomial-time algorithms with the same guarantees either have a time-complexity bound whose exponent goes to $\infty$ as $s$ approaches $\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{Otter}}}$ from above, or apply only when $s$ is close to $1$.

papers.title: Deterministic Polynomial-Time Primality Testing with a Single Binomial Congruence
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time primality test whose main verification is the congruence $(1+X)^n=1+X^n$ in $C_n[X]/(X^r-b(Y))$, where $C_n=(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})[Y]/(Φ_r(Y))$. Two identities in the coefficient ring normalize $b$ and ensure compatibility with the main congruence. A finite-field root count and a lattice bound show that an accepted input is a prime power; elementary preprocessing excludes nontrivial perfect powers. We construct $b$ deterministically using Jacobi sums and the uniform Dedekind-zeta zero-free theorem of Cureton and Thorner, which extends OpenAI's Hecke zero-free theorem. The total bit complexity is $L^{32+o(1)}$, where $L=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$, and verification after constructing $b$ costs $L^{6+o(1)}$. More generally, for a fixed real algebraic $1/2\leθ<1$, a common zero-free boundary $\Re s>θ$ for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions gives $L^{\max\{6,(1-θ)^{-1}\}+o(1)}$. This bound reaches $L^{6+o(1)}$ at $θ=5/6$, and hence under GRH. We state a fixed-base modification of Agrawal's conjecture for odd integers passing the base-$2$ Fermat test, using the modulus $X^r-2$ with $r$ the least positive integer not dividing $n(n-1)$.

papers.title: An affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality via information decay
papers.abstract: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ admits $S\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that $λ_1(SK)|K|^{2/n}\le Cn$, where $C$ is universal. For origin-symmetric bodies of volume one, the bound holds in maximal Gaussian measure position. The main step is the spectral estimate \[ λ_1(D)\le C(P)\bigl(n+\sqrt{n I(ν\midγ_n)}\bigr) \] for an even isotropic log-concave probability measure $ν$ supported on a symmetric convex body $D$, with Poincaré constant at most $P$ and finite relative Fisher information. A second-order Stein estimate and an information jump under convolution give entropy decay faster than $m^{-1}$ for normalised sums. Their supports control the Gaussian measure of dilates, and a Brownian bridge expansion gives the spectral estimate. A Gaussian-weighted ground state supplies a measure whose Fisher information is bounded in terms of $λ_1(K)$. The square-root dependence then gives the bound of order $n$.

papers.title: Overcoming Demand Censoring through Randomization for Risk-Sensitive Newsvendor Learning
papers.abstract: We study online newsvendor learning with bounded demand, censored observations, and convex nonlinear shortage costs. Because stockouts can conceal the shortage magnitudes needed by gradient-based algorithms, we use randomized ordering to construct unbiased subgradient estimates. We characterize admissible randomization distributions within this framework and develop an online inventory policy that combines the resulting subgradient estimates with gradient-based updates. Our regret analysis quantifies the cost of randomization via the estimation variance and an additional loss term. We characterize the randomization distributions that minimize this objective. For piecewise-linear shortage costs, the optimal distribution is computed through a linear-time recursion; for costs with bounded curvature density, it is characterized by a scalar ordinary differential equation. The policy achieves expected regret of $O(T^{2/3})$ against the best fixed order in hindsight over $T$ periods. Under independent demand and suitable curvature of expected losses, the bound improves to $O(\sqrt{T})$. Matching minimax lower bounds establish rate optimality over the corresponding classes with a fixed marginal-cost bound. Both rates extend to nonperishable inventory under uniformly positive conditional expected demand. Numerical experiments on synthetic and retail data show improvements over alternative policies using censored observations.

papers.title: Nonpathological submeasures and $F_σ$ ideals
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between nonpathological lower semicontinuous submeasures, $F_σ$ ideals on $ω$, and matrix summability ideals. First, we construct in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ a non-analytic ideal on $ω$ which is representable as an intersection of matrix summability ideals. Then, we show that an $F_σ$ ideal is nonpathological if and only if it can be represented as an intersection of summable ideals if and only if it can be represented as an intersection of matrix summability ideals. We also prove that the random graph ideal is pathological. Finally, we compute the exact degree of pathology of a certain submeasure related to a construction of Topsøe.

papers.title: The Non-Abelian X-Ray Transform on Simple Asymptotically Hyperbolic Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove a gauge equivalence result for the non-Abelian X-ray transform with connection and Higgs field on simple 2-dimensional asymptotically hyperbolic spaces. Our approach is based on the construction of holomorphic integrating factors. To construct these, we analyze the geodesic X-ray transform on functions on simple asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds of general dimension and prove polyhomogeneous mapping properties and a surjectivity result for the adjoint.

papers.title: Normality of closures of conormal bundles to Schubert cells for $\operatorname{GL}_n$
papers.abstract: We prove normality of closures of the conormal bundle to certain Schubert cells in the flag variety for $\operatorname{GL}_n$ coming from Grassmannians. Our argument uses a Zelevinsky-type resolution of singularities, and through a sequence of cohomological computations based on the Borel--Weil--Bott theorem, we reduce normality to a problem about Kronecker coefficients, which we solve by applying results of Knutson and Tao from honeycomb theory.

papers.title: Multiclass Classification with Rare Useful Features: Fundamental Limits and the Optimality of Diversity Pursuit Higher Criticism Thresholding
papers.abstract: We consider classification in high-dimensional feature spaces where only a vanishing fraction of features are useful and the number of classes may be large. While this rare-and-weak useful-feature regime is well understood in the binary setting, its multiclass version raises new questions: a feature can be useful for class discrimination without separating any specific pair of classes. We focus on a rare feature diversity model, in which most features are useless, but a small fraction promote discrimination among classes in a way that can be detected by a per-feature diversity test, such as one-way ANOVA or the Kruskal-Wallis test. For this setting, we propose Diversity Pursuit Higher Criticism Thresholding (DP-HCT), a feature-screening procedure that applies a higher-criticism threshold to the collection of p-values obtained from per-feature diversity tests. We justify DP-HCT under a Gaussian multiclass Rare-and-Weak Useful Feature model with class-mean contrasts of fixed magnitude in random directions, extending the binary model of Donoho and Jin (2008). When the number of classes is fixed, our model recovers the binary phase transition. When the number of classes grows logarithmically with the number of features, however, we derive a new and strictly harder phase transition, driven by the growing degrees of freedom and their effect on the useful-feature tail rate. We show that whenever classification beyond chance is possible, DP-HCT with ANOVA, followed by a simple classifier based on similarity to class means, achieves asymptotically perfect accuracy. Experiments on real multiclass classification benchmarks demonstrate substantial improvements, and numerical simulations confirm that the derived phase-transition curve accurately predicts the finite-sample behavior of DP-HCT in the growing-class regime.

papers.title: $P$-stationary structural equation modeling: Causal effect identification under temporally incomplete observations
papers.abstract: Causal modeling of discrete-time processes often involves the assumption that the modeled processes are stationary. A general class of linear causal models for discrete-time stationary processes are structural equation processes (SEP), which generalize the well known structural equation model for i.i.d. observations. In this paper, we extend the SEP model from stationary to $P$-stationary processes, which are non-stationary processes whose $P$-periodically sampled subprocesses are jointly stationary. We will use this model to approach the problem of causal effect identification under temporally incomplete observations from a graphical modeling perspective. To have a notion of generic identifiability, we restrict our analysis to $P$-stationary structural vector autoregressive (SVAR) processes, which are SVAR processes whose underlying coefficients can vary $P$-periodically over time. Our findings allow to detect, in any given temporally incomplete observational setting, if a certain set of instrumental processes qualifies to identify a causal effect between $P$-periodic subprocesses, and if this is the case, that effect admits an explicit expression as a rational function evaluated at the observational spectral density.

papers.title: How the eigenvalue region of standardized Laplacians leaves the 2005 polygon
papers.abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of $n\times n$ standardized Laplacian matrices, and let $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ be the polygon introduced in 2005, with upper vertices $λ_0=0,\dots,λ_{n-1}=1$. It is now known that $Λ_n=S_n$, and that $Λ_n$ is convex, if and only if $n\le4$. We study how $Λ_n$ leaves $S_n$ near an edge $[λ_m,λ_{m+1}]$, $2(m+1)<n$. First, we prove a switching law for matrices having a boundary point of $Λ_n$ as a simple eigenvalue: an explicit switching function on the arcs, built from the left and right eigenvectors and the outward normal, forces maximal weight where positive and zero weight where negative; intermediate weights occur only where it vanishes. Second, we perturb the weights of the arcs $k\to k+m+1$ in the circulant digraph (arcs $k\to k+s$, $1\le s\le m$, plus these arcs with weight $τ$) that realizes the point $λ_m+τ(λ_{m+1}-λ_m)$. At second order, the first Fourier harmonic of the perturbation moves the eigenvalue beyond the line of the edge if and only if $τ<τ^*_m=\sin(πm/n)/(2\cos(π/n)\sin(π(m+1)/n))$. For even $n$ and $m$, the point with $τ=τ^*_m$ is the vertex of $S_{n/2}$ lying on this edge, and digraphs with these arcs only at even $k$ give an explicit eigenvalue path that leaves $S_n$ at $λ_m$ and, in all computed cases, ends at this vertex. Third, we give a conjectural, numerically supported picture of $\partialΛ_5$: beyond each edge of $S_5$ not incident to $0$ or $1$, $Λ_5$ forms a cap bounded by four algebraic arcs, which leaves the edge tangentially at its endpoint adjacent to $0$ or $1$ and rejoins it at $τ^*_1=(3-\sqrt5)/2$; the rest of the edge lies on $\partialΛ_5$. In computations for $n\le8$, a cap returns to its edge smoothly at $τ^*_m$, at a corner at $τ^*_m$, or at a corner beyond $τ^*_m$.

papers.title: Direct and Indirect Competition in a Two-Prey-One-Predator System : Global Dynamics, Chaos, and the Paine Conjecture
papers.abstract: This paper studies the global dynamics of a three-dimensional Lotka-Volterra system of two prey, with direct competition between them, and one predator. Under a symmetry assumption, the rescaled parameter space is sorted into four generic categories, which yield a complete classification of the global dynamics into 56 meaningful subcases. We determine the existence and stability of the boundary and positive equilibria, including global asymptotic stability and bistability of boundary equilibria, and necessary and sufficient conditions for local asymptotic stability of the positive equilibrium. We identify regimes of periodic solutions and chaos, including a period-doubling route to chaos. We further show that the parameters of Gilpin's chaotic dynamics fall within some cases. Biologically, we introduce the notion of extensive negative competition, which, together with trade-off competition and apparent competition, interprets the interactions among the three species. Our classification shows that the full system largely tracks the dynamics of the prey-only subsystem, and these competition mechanisms explain the differences between them, clarifying how predator-mediated interactions alter competitive outcomes and facilitate prey persistence, thereby providing mathematical support for Paine conjecture.

papers.title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $σ$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.

papers.title: Separating the Polar of Sets of Uniqueness from the Polars of All $H^{(d)}$-Sets
papers.abstract: We construct a perfect set of uniqueness on the circle carrying a continuous probability measure which annihilates every $H^{(d)}$-set, simultaneously for all finite dimensions d. This gives a strict inclusion between the polar of the compact sets of uniqueness and the polar of the union of the classes $H^{(d)}$, answering a question raised in earlier work on these polars. The construction uses random binary increments of size comparable to the reciprocal of a product of square roots. A Gaussian sampling estimate gives a uniform Fourier-tail bound for all pseudomeasures supported by the resulting set, and also bounded atomic approximation and spectral synthesis. A separate energy estimate, stable under deletion of a small number of increments, yields full support for every limiting quasi-independent image of every positive measure absolutely continuous with respect to the constructed measure.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal Spherical Attention and Retrieval: Sharp Coarsening Clocks and Certified Score Correction
papers.abstract: We develop nonreciprocal spherical attention as a mathematical framework for coarsening and compressed nearest-neighbor retrieval. For two shrinking acute blocks whose centers have zero skew pairing and whose total mass ratio is subexponential in inverse temperature, we prove $\lim_{β\to\infty}β^{-1}\log T_β=1-\cosφ$, without restricting particle-count growth. An explicit three-body flow has two rigorously separated metastable exponents. For finite compression, mass centering yields a sharp $O(r^2)$ attention-output error bound at fixed temperature, with an explicit spherical-normalization correction. We formulate skew query-side score calibration as a strictly convex moment problem and derive a unique normal equation, residual-based optimization certificates, and bounded low-rank projections. A norm-aware margin objective calibrates native squared-distance rankings. Experiments use semantic retrieval data, one million visual descriptors with three codebook seeds, and a ten-million-vector FAISS IVF-PQ index with recomputed exact cosine ground truth. On SIFT1M, skew margin calibration raises native-L2 hit@10 from 0.8926 to 0.8948; symmetric calibration reaches 0.8996. The ten-million-vector index reaches 0.8827 hit@10 at 0.1794 ms per query in a four-thread batch benchmark, while validation selects no skew update. Exact streamed attention over ten million keys evaluates compressed memory on 1,024 held-out queries. Independent matrix solves, automatic differentiation, finite differences, interval arithmetic, full-flow tests, and nine Rocq-checked algebra lemmas support reproducibility. Directionality alone does not establish retrieval superiority.

papers.title: Weak and Sharp Stretched-Exponential Flocking in the Kinetic Cucker-Smale Model with Noncompactly Supported Initial Data
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the kinetic Cucker-Smale model under initial data with unbounded support in both position and velocity. Such data invalidate classical diameter-based flocking arguments and make sustained spatial cohesion difficult to establish. We prove an estimate for spatial characteristics under a finite spatial second moment and a sufficiently high velocity moment, without any requirement on coupling strength. We also prove weak flocking, i.e. control of spatial variance and integrability of velocity fluctuations in time. Under stronger assumptions on the initial tails, we establish uniform propagation of spatial exponential moments of explicitly determined order, a substantially stronger conclusion than bounded spatial variance. These estimates lead to explicit stretched-exponential rates of velocity alignment and convergence of the centered spatial distribution toward a limiting profile. Another contribution is the construction of countably atomic solutions that show optimality of the decay exponent in the spatial-tail-limited class. Together, the results clarify how initial phase-space tails govern spatial confinement and quantitative flocking for kinetic distributions without compact support.

papers.title: Nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the Gross-Pitaevskii equation
papers.abstract: We prove a nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the repulsive Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation with a time-dependent trapping potential $V(x,t)$. If either (i) $V(\cdot,t)$ is smooth, subquadratic in space and with uniformly bounded spatial derivatives of order $\geq 2$, or (ii) $V(\cdot,t)$ is a uniformly bounded perturbation of a fixed non-negative potential which is asymptotically $|x|^m, m\geq 2$, then the GP equation has a global solution, which remains uniformly close to the instantaneous minimizer of the time-independent GP functional, provided the initial condition is a ground state. In fact, we show that the existence of a solution of the GP equation is the real bottleneck: If existence is assumed, then adiabaticity holds under very minimal assumptions.

papers.title: Generalized Quasi-Symmetric Nets: A Constructive Approach to the Equimodular Elliptic Type and to Flexible $m \times n$ Nets
papers.abstract: Quadrilateral meshes that flex with rigid planar faces are of interest to transformable architecture, rigid-foldable origami, and mechanical metamaterials. Their building blocks are flexible $3 \times 3$ nets, that is, Kokotsakis polyhedra with a quadrangular base, classified by Izmestiev. We study one of his types, the equimodular elliptic type, defined by three conditions on the flat angles, the third of them through Jacobi elliptic functions. We turn these conditions into equivalent algebraic ones, free of elliptic functions, which lead to the generalized quasi-symmetric nets (GQS-nets), polyhedra of this type that include the known elliptic quasi-symmetric nets. For every polyhedron of this type, we give a flexible polyhedron with the same flat angles and its flexion in closed form. From the simplest GQS-nets, we assemble arbitrarily large flexible $m \times n$ nets. Examples include nets that, at one position, form letters; further nets in the supplementary materials form digits or, seen along their rows, approximately follow the side silhouettes of a bunny and a fish. Unlike numerically computed mechanisms, these nets are exactly flexible. As an application, we design three such nets as transportable arch halls of 80 mm sandwich panels, which fold to fit through the door of a standard container or into the well of a low-bed semi-trailer, and we check them numerically under snow load and build a 1:20 model of one. Supplementary Mathematica notebooks verify the symbolic computations, a Python tool constructs the nets and checks them numerically, including for self-intersections, and further scripts recheck the halls.

papers.title: Integrating Data Center Flexibility into Power System Operations: A Framework for Temporal Redispatch
papers.abstract: Rapid growth in data center electricity demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) training and inference, is expected to increase stress conditions for power grids. Operational flexibility from data centers offers a near-term lever to relieve such stresses. Existing models of data center flexibility tend to bundle economic incentives with physical constraints, obscuring the tradeoff between economic willingness to shift load and technical limitations to do so. This paper proposes a temporal-redispatch focused framework that decouples data center demand flexibility into two independently parameterized dimensions: (1) systematic flexibility, capturing the economic environment through penalties for temporal shifting of data centers' scheduled demand, and (2) operational flexibility, capturing the physical envelope through the demand shifting time window and the limit on shifted data center demand. The framework relies on a direct current optimal power flow (DC-OPF) linear program which enables annual parametric analysis at hourly resolution. The framework is studied using a synthetic grid mimicking the Texas transmission system populated with the 2026 Adjusted Forecast from ERCOT (Electric Reliability Council of Texas). Results show that operational flexibility imposes a physical lower bound on unsatisfied demand that no economic incentive can overcome; longer shifting windows and higher limits on shifted data center demand reduce operational cost with different impacts on grid utilization; and, temporal redispatch shaves system-wide net load peaks while partially compensating for localized transmission bottlenecks that emerge under modeled coal retirement scenarios.

papers.title: On the probability that the integer parts of polynomials are coprime
papers.abstract: We prove that for any $s\ge 2$ and polynomials $f_{1}(x),\dots,f_{s-1}(x)\in \mathbb{R}[x]$ satisfying a certain equidistribution condition, the natural density of the numbers $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $n,\lfloor f_{1}(n)\rfloor,\dots,\lfloor f_{s-1}(n)\rfloor$ are mutually coprime is $1/ζ(s)$. This generalises a recent result of Champagne, in which this was proven under the assumption that $f_{1}$ is linear.

papers.title: A converse theorem for GL(2) over global fields without root numbers
papers.abstract: We prove a converse theorem for GL(2) over global fields in which the root numbers in the twisted functional equations need not be prescribed. Instead, we allow nonzero scalar factors that are invariant under unramified twists. We show that these scalars are independent of the twisting character and obtain a unique isobaric automorphic representation with the prescribed unramified local components.

papers.title: A Quasisymmetric Analogue of the Bruhat Order
papers.abstract: We define a quasisymmetric analogue of the Bruhat order on indexed binary forests using the multiplicity-free Monk rule for forest polynomials. For the finite window $\mathcal{P}_n$ of forests supported in $[1,n]$, we construct an explicit partition into saturated chains terminating at the top rank, proving that $\mathcal{P}_n$ is strongly Sperner. We also recover the known Catalan ballot formula for its rank numbers. For principal lower intervals, we prove that $[\varnothing,F]$ is a lattice if and only if it is Boolean, and characterize this property by the avoidance of a bent corner in $F$, a path of three internal vertices that changes direction. This gives a forest analogue of the pattern-avoidance characterization of Boolean principal Bruhat intervals. We also conjecture that every principal lower interval is shellable, providing computational evidence and proving the conjecture for a family of hook intervals.

papers.title: Hardy transitions on product lattices
papers.abstract: Boundary conditions can change the dimensional scale of a sharp functional inequality. We determine this change for inverse-square Hardy inequalities on the product lattices $\mathbb N^k\times\mathbb Z^{N-k}$. Their sharp constants satisfy $C_{N,k}\sim N^2Ψ(k/N)$ uniformly for $1\le k\le N$, where $Ψ(α)\sim2α$ at zero. The law gives linear growth for a fixed number of positive coordinates, every intermediate power for suitable sublinear choices, and quadratic growth for a positive proportion. We develop a method that connects exact uncertainty inequalities with Hardy inequalities through logarithmic localization, and combines this transfer with a block decomposition to cover all proportions. The transfer holds on weighted graphs with an explicit geometric error and controls the variational problem over arbitrary functions. A mixture of two Mathieu ground energies determines $Ψ$. At the fully positive endpoint, the variational problem defining $κ=Ψ(1)$ has a unique nondegenerate minimum and a unique positive energy--moment minimizing profile. We also prove strict comparison with the continuum coefficient in every sector for $N\ge9$, the optimal uniform dimension.

papers.title: Fisher--Hartwig asymptotics and critical moments for the circular beta ensemble
papers.abstract: We determine the joint moments of real powers of the absolute value of characteristic polynomials in the circular beta ensemble, for every $β>0$. At fixed distinct prescribed points, the Fisher--Hartwig formula holds for every exponent greater than $-1$, with explicit constants and a relative error bounded by a negative power of the matrix size $N$. For approaching points in the same integrable range, the error is bounded by a negative power of $Nδ_N$, provided that $Nδ_N\to\infty$ and the sum of the absolute values of the negative exponents is less than two. Here $δ_N$ is the minimum distance between the prescribed points; this range includes every integrable pair of root exponents. For $q>0$ at the critical relation $pq^2=2β$, we prove the Keating--Wong asymptotic for the $p$th moment of the integral of the $q$th absolute power of the characteristic polynomial, for every real $p>1$. The leading asymptotic extends to every complex spatial weight in $L^p$. The proofs combine the recursion for orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle with conditional expectation identities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos and quantitative estimates for approaching singularities.

papers.title: The multivariate Berry-Esseen theorem with an absolute constant
papers.abstract: We prove that the multivariate Berry--Esseen inequality for sums of independent random vectors holds with the same constant in every dimension. For independent centered random vectors $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ whose covariance matrices sum to $I_d$, we show that the distance between the distribution of their sum and $N(0,I_d)$, measured uniformly over convex sets, is at most $C_0\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{E}\|X_i\|_2^3$ for a universal constant $C_0$. The bound requires only finite third moments and holds uniformly in the dimension, the number of summands, and their distributions. It also yields the corresponding bound for independent and identically distributed vectors. In particular, $C_0$ can be chosen to be $980$.

papers.title: The real eigenvalues of the non-backtracking Laplacian
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $N$ nodes and $M$ edges, with minimum degree at least $2$. We prove that the non-backtracking Laplacian of $G$ has at least $2M-2N+2c+2b$ real eigenvalues, counted with algebraic multiplicity, where $c$ is the number of connected components of $G$ and $b$ is the number of bipartite ones. More precisely, at least $M-N+2c$ of them lie in $[0,1)$ and at least $M-N+2b$ lie in $(1,2]$. We show that the bound $2M-2N+2c+2b$ is sharp, and that a connected $d$-regular graph attains it if and only if it is strictly Ramanujan, i.e., every adjacency eigenvalue $μ\ne\pm d$ satisfies $|μ|<2\sqrt{d-1}$. For completeness, we also show that the non-backtracking Laplacian has at most $2M-2c-2b$ real eigenvalues.

papers.title: Graphs versus loopless digraphs with a given degree sequence, and convergence of uniformly random graphs at every density
papers.abstract: For a degree sequence d on n vertices with M edges, let G(d) be the number of simple graphs and D(d) the number of loopless digraphs with in-degree = out-degree = d. We conjecture that G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d, a single inequality across all densities, and prove it up to an extra factor log n: G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d. The proof compares pairs of graphs with Eulerian digraphs by alternately colouring closed trails; the failure of injectivity is measured exactly, shared edges cancel against 2-cycles, and parity is handled by merging trails and by a parity argument on Eulerian circuits of odd components. No asymptotic enumeration and no bound on the maximum-entropy multipliers is used. When the maximum-entropy edge probabilities lie in [delta, 1-delta], the same method gives the conjecture itself, G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n / delta). Combined with the exact identity G(d) = exp(g*(d)) pi(d), where pi(d) is the probability that the maximum-entropy beta-model has degrees exactly d, and a van der Waerden-type bound for D(d), this shows that uniformly random graphs with degree sequence d are close in the normalized cut metric to their beta-model whenever M >> n log n log(M/n), at every density, with no tameness and no cap on the degrees. We also record the conjecture in the sparse regime and, with constant 1/2+o(1), in the dense tame regime, from the asymptotic enumerations of McKay-Wormald and Barvinok-Hartigan.

papers.title: An $L\log L$ theory of sparse graph convergence
papers.abstract: Borgs, Chayes, Cohn and Zhao developed a limit theory for sparse graphs based on $L^p$ upper regularity with $p>1$, where Holder's inequality controls small sets. We develop the analogous theory in the Orlicz class $L\log L$, replacing Holder by the Young-Fenchel inequality for $Ψ(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u$ and $Ψ^*(v)=e^v-1-v$. We prove a weak regularity lemma for upper $Ψ$-regular graphons with $4^{O(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ parts, using the modular $\intΨ$ as the energy; that upper $Ψ$-regular sequences have cut-metric convergent subsequences; that convergent sequences with $L\log L$ limits are upper $Ψ$-regular; and that $L\log L$ balls are cut-metric compact. The class strictly contains every $L^p$ class with $p>1$, and we give sparse $W$-random graphs that are upper $Ψ$-regular but not upper $L^p$ regular for any $p>1$. For graphs with a given degree sequence we prove, by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs with switchings, that if the average degree tends to infinity, the density to zero and the degree profile converges in $L^1$ to $\varphi$, uniformly random graphs converge in the normalized cut metric to $\varphi\otimes\varphi$, with no condition on the maximum degree; the sequence is upper $Ψ$-regular when $\varphi\in L\log L$. We also show that the maximum-entropy $β$-model is entrywise Chung-Lu when $d_{\max}^2=o(M)$, and that cut-closeness to it follows from a lower bound $e^{-o(M)}$ on its probability of having the prescribed degrees. Finally, $Ψ$ is the large deviation rate function of sparse Erdos-Renyi graphs up to a factor $1+O(1/\log\frac1p)$.

papers.title: Recursive Reasoning Exploration: Mathematical Research through Evolving Reasoning Graphs : case study: An Exact Certificate-Degree Theorem for Two-Term Tensor Decompositions : Phase III of the Math Instruments Program
papers.abstract: Large collections of manuscripts and research notes offer ways to reuse arguments, while making it harder to retain hypotheses, check claims, and understand how results were obtained. We propose Recursive Reasoning Exploration (RRE), a framework for cumulative mathematical research through evolving reasoning graphs. RRE links claims and jointly required premises to research targets, attempted arguments, counterexamples, checks, and revisions. Each investigation can generate further targets, and its supported outcomes become available to subsequent investigations. This is Phase III of the Math Instruments program: identifying mathematical instruments, reconstructing reusable reasoning, and organizing recursive research from that reasoning. The framework supports human-directed, collaborative, and goal-directed autonomous exploration, with open-ended exploration as a further mode. Its records also provide material for learning how mathematical investigations develop. A complexity research case study establishes an exact theorem: for every complex tensor of order n >= 2 and rank greater than two, the minimum Nullstellensatz certificate degree for its original two-term decomposition equations is 3n. This includes an infinite family whose every flattening has rank at most two. The exploration develops an explicit boundary certificate, a balanced transfer lemma, and an exhaustive argument using classical rank-two geometry. A parallel branch gives bounds 3m + 3 <= delta_m(I_m, N) <= 3m + 6 for every nonzero nilpotent m by m matrix. Six graph revisions record the progression from inherited results to these theorems, with exact arithmetic checks and a replayable exploration history. We present the RRE representation and protocol, the mathematical proofs, visualizations of graph evolution, and a research agenda for shared human-AI exploration, cumulative reuse, and education.

papers.title: Sobolev spaces arising from the Stockwell transform on Gelfand pairs
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of Sobolev-type spaces on Gelfand pairs, built from the Stockwell transform: a function belongs to the space of a given smoothness when its Stockwell transform, multiplied by a weight that grows with the smoothness, is square integrable. We prove that these spaces are Hilbert spaces, that they form a decreasing scale under continuous embeddings, and that an interpolation inequality controls the norm at an intermediate smoothness by the norms at the two endpoints. Under integrability conditions on the weight and on the family of analysing windows, they embed continuously into Lebesgue spaces. Under a local domination condition on the window, we show that their elements have bounded continuous representatives.
