An ordered frequency factorization gives exact dyadic histograms, moments, total-variation distances, and extremal multiplicities. The limiting frequency generating function $z^3/(2-z)$ is universal, although the highest finite multiplicities depend on $p$. Finally, the summatory function has main terms $N^2/4+(N/2)\log_2N$, an explicit parameter-dependent log-periodic term of order $N$, and remainder $O_p(N/\sqrt{\log N})$.

papers.title: Improved first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We study the smoothed first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions for which every nontrivial power of the character remains primitive. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet and finite order Hecke $L$-functions occurring in the proof, we obtain asymptotic formulas with errors $O(Q^{\frac{49}{58}+\eps})$ and $O(Q^{\frac{23}{26}+\eps})$, respectively. We follow the double Dirichlet series approach of Gao and Zhao. The main ingredient is a joint estimate for the two sums arising from the removal of rational prime divisors, with the Möbius coefficients retained. This gives a quotient of Dirichlet $L$-functions. Under GRH, we bound both the Dirichlet $L$-functions and their reciprocals. Combining the joint estimate with estimates for the generating series of Gauss sums gives larger regions of meromorphic continuation. These regions do not separate the possible secondary terms.

papers.title: A secondary term in the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet L-functions
papers.abstract: P. Gao and L. Zhao obtained an asymptotic formula for the smoothed first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $Q$ with conductors coprime to $3$, with a main term of order $Q$ and error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{7}{8}+\eps}\right)\) under the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis. Building on their double Dirichlet series, we assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis and separate an explicit secondary term of order $Q^{\frac{5}{6}}$, with error $O\left(Q^{\frac{23}{28}+\eps}\right)$.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Full Multivariate Partial-Twuality Polynomials
papers.abstract: For each nonempty finite simple graph, we study five full multivariate partial-twuality polynomials defined using matrix ranks and coranks over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Over an arbitrary coefficient field $K$, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for nontrivial factorization in the Laurent polynomial ring by additive separation of the exponent function across a nontrivial vertex partition. For $\bullet\in\{τ,δτ,τδ,δτδ\}$, the full multivariate partial-$\langle\bullet\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z^{\pm1},\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected. For $δ$, we characterize the connected graphs whose polynomials are reducible by a condition on the parities of vertex degrees and of the numbers of common neighbors, and determine their irreducible factors. For each operation, the corresponding polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and at least one state has zero $z$-exponent. In particular, the full multivariate partial-$\langleδ\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and bipartite.

papers.title: Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers
papers.abstract: Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $π_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $p_k:\tilde{R}_n\rightarrow R_n$ be the standard $k$-sheeted regular cyclic cover of $R_n$ induced by a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action on $\tilde{R}_n$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $R_{n_k}$, where $n_k=k(n-1)+1$) generated by a free rotation through $2π/k$ of $\tilde{R}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ be the liftable outer automorphism group associated with a standard $k$-sheeted normal cover $p_k$. For $n\geq3$, we show that $\{\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)\}_{k\geq2}$ forms an infinite family of self-normalizing subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$. For $n\geq2$, these groups are maximal if and only if $k$ is prime. Furthermore, we derive explicit finite generating sets for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ for $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the infinite chain of roses, and let $q_n:\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow R_n$ be the standard infinite-sheeted cover induced by $\langle τ\rangle$, where $τ$ is the unit translation on $\mathcal{C}$. As a final application, we obtain a finite generating set for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_\infty}(F_n)$ when $n\geq 3$.

papers.title: $p$-Wasserstein distance and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cramér-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$. We also determine the covariance bias under the uncorrected normalization and establish the corresponding Wasserstein bounds, lower bounds and moderate deviation estimates. The dimension and the model parameters are fixed.

papers.title: Dual Path Following for an Aerial Manipulator Under State and Input Constraints via Transverse Feedback Linearization
papers.abstract: This paper studies dual path following for a quadrotor carrying a three-degree-of-freedom arm. The center of mass of the combined system must follow a vehicle path and the end effector must follow a second path, while the arm respects its joint limits and avoids its singular postures. The vehicle and the arm are mechanically coupled, so one controller must handle both paths. With the center of mass and the end-effector path coordinates as outputs, and a dynamic extension of the thrust, the system admits a normal form without internal dynamics. We characterize the states where this normal form fails. We formulate the transverse feedback linearizing controller as a quadratic program that relaxes only the speed of the end effector along its path and imposes safety and actuator limits as inequality constraints. The program reduces to a scalar problem with a closed-form solution. If it remains strictly feasible for all time, the feedback is locally Lipschitz, both paths are invariant and attractive, and every constraint holds. In the physics engine Drake, the controller resolves a conflict between the two speed references by slowing the end effector while both paths remain invariant. By contrast, a cascade with a safety filter leaves both paths. Code and animations are available at https://gradslab.github.io/am_dual_pf-/

papers.title: Precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with Weibull-type and lognormal-type random step sizes
papers.abstract: We prove precise large deviations for the symmetric elephant random walk with random step sizes. When the distribution of $|Z_1-1|$ is subexponential, we first show that, for each fixed$p\in[0,1]$, there exists a positive number sequence $b_n\to\infty$ such that \[ \mathbb P(S_n>x)\sim \mathbb P(S_n<-x)\sim \frac n2\overline F(x) \] uniformly for $x\ge b_n$, where $\overline F(x)=\mathbb P(|Z_1-1|>x)$. This existence result requires no moment assumptions and does not specify the growth rate of $b_n$. For $p\in[0,3/4]$, we further give explicit sufficient conditions on $b_n$ under Weibull-type and lognormal-type tail conditions with a regularly varying factor $x^γL(x)$, where $γ\in\mathbf R$ and $L$ is a positive measurable slowly varying function. Analogous results hold with $\mathbb P(|Z_1|>x)$ and non-strict tails.

papers.title: Parameters and lim CM sequences: the Q-sequence conjecture and Lech's formula
papers.abstract: We prove that if a local ring has a weakly lim Cohen-Macaulay sequence of modules, then it satisfies the conjecture that every system of parameters is a Q-sequence. We also give a generalization of Lech's formula for the multiplicity of a local ring $(R,m)$ with respect to a system of parameters that allows a very large class of sequences of $m$-primary ideals generated by monomials in the parameters to be used in the calculation. The cases where the sequence of ideals consists of the powers of the ideal generated by parameters, or where the ideals in the sequence are generated by varying powers of the individual parameters all of which tend to infinity, which is Lech's original formula, are included.

papers.title: Transport for Conditional Sampling: Foundations and Applications
papers.abstract: Conditional sampling is central to Bayesian inference, generative modeling, and causal inference: given a joint law for random variables $X$ and $Y$ and an observation $Y=y$, one seeks to sample from the conditional law of $X\mid Y=y$. Even when the joint distribution is accurately represented, this task can be computationally difficult as it may require evaluating intractable normalizing constants or solving a new inference problem for each observation. Measure transport provides an approach to this problem by identifying a map with triangular structure that directly pushes forward a reference to the conditional of a joint distribution for any observation. This article reviews the theoretical, methodological, and algorithmic foundations of triangular transports, with the Knothe-Rosenblatt rearrangement as a canonical construction. We discuss methods for estimating triangular maps from finite samples, as well as their use in simulation-based inference and causal inference. While our primary aim is to review existing formulations, we also present new ideas and open questions for conditional sampling using transport.

papers.title: $L^1$ amplification near a self-similar vortex collapse in 2D Navier-Stokes
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative $L^1$ instability for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse as viscosity tends to zero. For every $0<γ<\frac12$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, we construct solutions that are $O(ν^{1-γ})$-close in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ at $t_0$ but exhibit order-one $L^1$ separation in a shrinking neighborhood of the collapse point at times approaching collapse as $ν\to0$. By time translation, we also obtain pairs of solutions with initial $L^1$ distance $O(ν^{1-γ})$ that develop order-one separation at a fixed positive time. In both constructions, the solutions have the same viscosity and total circulation and are uniformly bounded in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The proof exploits the amplification of small time delays, the fast speed of the vortex centers near collapse, together with sharp inviscid approximation estimates for the Navier--Stokes equations established in~\cite{Ga11,NguyenCollapse}.

papers.title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
papers.abstract: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.

papers.title: Longest-Queue Policies in Dynamic Matching with Abandonments
papers.abstract: We study a dynamic two-way matching market in which agents of heterogeneous types arrive over time, wait to be matched according to a compatibility network, and abandon the system if their random patience expires. The decision maker collects match rewards and pays holding and abandonment costs, and seeks to maximize the expected net value over a finite horizon. We evaluate policies by their approximation ratio against a fluid benchmark, the optimal value of a linear-programming relaxation that upper bounds the expected net value of every policy. Under a general position gap (GPG) condition, which requires the unique optimal dual solution of this linear program to remain optimal under small perturbations of the arrival rates, we propose a longest-queue policy. The policy first uses this dual solution to identify a set of good match types and a set of critical agent types. Upon each arrival, it considers only good matches and matches the arrival to the critical partner with the longest queue subject to availabilities. In the high-volume regime, in which arrival rates are scaled by s, we prove that the policy attains an approximation ratio of at least 1-O(1/s) at every scale s >= 1 and every horizon T >= 1, so the ratio tends to 1 as s goes to infinity.

papers.title: Whittaker modules for the principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$ via free field realizations
papers.abstract: We study Whittaker and generalized Whittaker modules for the universal principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, using two free field realizations: one in the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank two and the other in the tensor product of the universal Virasoro vertex algebra with the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank one. Under explicit conditions on the parameters, we construct universal Whittaker modules, establish their ordered bases, and obtain explicit irreducibility criteria. Under an explicit nondegeneracy condition, we also show that the submodules of these tensor products correspond to the submodules of the Virasoro factor. We prove irreducibility of the universal Whittaker modules constructed in this paper.

papers.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
papers.abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.

papers.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
papers.abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.

papers.title: Effective Hausdorff dimension one is cofinal in the K-degrees
papers.abstract: Every K-degree has an upper bound of effective Hausdorff dimension one and Kurtz random sequences are cofinal in the K-degrees.

papers.title: Some variants of function domination
papers.abstract: We investigate whether classical recursion-theoretic notions defined by function domination remain unchanged when success is required only on sets of prescribed asymptotic density. We establish robustness for many such notions and uncover unexpected connections between familiar degree properties by comparing upper and lower density. In contrast, pdomination, as defined by Chong, Hoi, Stephan and Turetsky, is not robust under density weakenings. We also answer a question of Kjos-Hanssen and Nies by characterizing superhighness as domination with a threshold boundedly limit recursive in the oracle. As an application, we introduce supermaximal sets, a strengthening of maximality whose degrees are exactly the superhigh r.e. degrees.

papers.title: Degenerate neckpinches at the first $N$ singular times
papers.abstract: For every integer $N\ge1$, we construct a smooth closed connected strictly mean-convex rotationally symmetric surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose level set flow remains connected until extinction and has exactly one singular point at each of its first $N$ singular times. These singularities are degenerate neckpinches with the Angenent--Velázquez asymptotics: the leading deviation from the cylinder under parabolic rescaling is a cubic Hermite term.

papers.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.

papers.title: A short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality in dimension three
papers.abstract: We give a short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality with sharp constant $2$ for matrices of dimension at most three.

papers.title: The Yangian associated with the binary tree
papers.abstract: In this article, we give three candidates for a definition of the Yangian associated with the binary tree $X^*$ and the group $Aut(X^*)$ consisting of automorphisms of $X^*$ which preserve the tree structure. The first candidate has the Schur-Weyl duality with one kind of an extension of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra. The second and third ones have a homomorphism corresponding to the wreath recursion.

papers.title: The MZ-property for three-term differences
papers.abstract: We study the Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund property for finite differences. A difference \[ D(f,h)=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k f(b_kh) \] is said to have the MZ-property if, for every measurable function $f$, \[ D(f,h)=o(h) \quad\text{and}\quad f(h)=o(1) \] imply \[ f(h)=o(h). \] In this paper, we characterize all three-node differences \[ D(f,h)=af(qh)+bf(rh)+cf(sh) \] having the MZ-property. In particular, for irrational differences with distinct nodes, we obtain explicit necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients $a,b,c$ and the nodes $q,r,s$. As an application, our results resolve an open problem concerning a second-order Riemann difference.

papers.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for the sine-Gordon model in the subcritical regime
papers.abstract: We prove a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the massive two-dimensional sine-Gordon model throughout the subcritical range $0<β<8π$. For fixed mass, volume and arbitrary real coupling, the constant has a positive lower bound independent of the lattice spacing. When the dimensionless coupling is small, the lower bound is also uniform in volume and approaches the Gaussian constant as the coupling tends to zero. This extends the known range $β<6π$ and gives a rate of entropy decay for the reversible Langevin dynamics that remains positive as the cutoff is removed. The proof follows the Polchinski flow to a positive physical scale, where the Hamiltonian is a bounded perturbation of a uniformly convex one. For interactions invariant under constant field shifts, spatial differences bound their curvature by the gradient energy. For the oscillating part, we compare Gaussian integration with an average in which the original cosine phase fluctuates independently of the remaining variables. We estimate the comparison error at an intermediate scale, then differentiate the remaining Gaussian density. This preserves both phase damping and spatial decay without assuming bounds on second derivatives of the incoming local terms. The resulting strict gain between scales closes the estimates for every fixed $β<8π$.

papers.title: Perfectness of partial Christoffel transforms of Nikishin systems
papers.abstract: We study multiple orthogonal polynomial systems obtained from a Nikishin system of two measures by applying a Christoffel transform to one of the measures at a point $x=x_0$. We show that if $x_0$ separates the supports of the generating measures, then the modified systems remain perfect. As an application, we prove that the type I multiple orthogonal polynomials of a Nikishin system have no zeros in the gap between the supports of its generating measures.

papers.title: Continuity of Global Attractors under a Mass-Preserving Singular Memory Limit, with an Application to a Coupled Suspension Bridge System
papers.abstract: We study how the global attractor of a dissipative evolution equation with memory depends on the memory kernel when the kernel concentrates, while preserving its total mass, towards a Dirac mass at the origin. The mass-preserving rescaling is the structural feature that prevents the effective elastic coefficients from degenerating in the limit, so that the memory-dependent dynamics reduces formally to a memoryless damped system with unchanged elastic coefficients. For a coupled nonlinear suspension bridge system with past history, taken as a concrete model, we establish uniform-in-parameter dissipativity and uniform-in-parameter exponential stability of the associated linear semigroup. These uniform estimates yield uniform quasi-stability, uniform exponential attraction, finite-time convergence of the semigroups, and uniform Hölder continuity with respect to the perturbation parameter. We deduce upper semicontinuity of the global attractors, and, under an additional structural stability hypothesis on the limit attractor, lower semicontinuity as well. The analysis separates the general continuity mechanism, which applies to a broad class of memory kernels and dissipative systems, from the model-specific verification, which exploits the coupled bridge structure.

papers.title: Three-phase time minimization transportation problem with non-idle phases: a polynomial two-witness algorithm
papers.abstract: The three-phase time minimization transportation problem partitions the origin-terminal links into three sets used in consecutive phases and minimizes the sum of the phase shipment times. Optimal solutions may leave a phase idle, as in the main example of the original study. We require every phase to carry a positive integer quantity while leaving the split of the total requirement across phases free. Discarding idle solutions from the original algorithm does not, in general, solve this variant. We prove that the optimum is attained by fixing one witness link in each of two phases and deciding the third phase by a single network flow computation, with the optimal Phase-3 time of each witness pair located by binary search. The resulting exact algorithm is strongly polynomial. It extends to any fixed number of phases, whereas, when the number of phases is part of the input, even non-idle feasibility is strongly NP-complete; feasibility alone is fixed-parameter tractable in the number of phases via known rainbow-matching results. We also characterize the minimum time of each phase. On the main example, non-idleness raises the optimum from 38 to 41. On 3,650 random instances with up to $50\times50$ links the algorithm took at most 50.2 seconds, and non-idleness raised the optimal value in 41% of the 2,250 instances with equal phase sizes; on 90 sampled instances it was faster than a mixed integer programming solver on 80 with a direct formulation and on 65 with a tighter threshold formulation.

papers.title: Benign population landscapes do not transfer to empirical risk minimization in nonsmooth optimization
papers.abstract: Benign landscapes provide a geometric explanation for the success of iterative methods on nonconvex problems arising in data science. The landscape is benign if every local minimizer is global and every other critical point is a strict saddle. For methods that avoid strict saddles, convergence to a critical point therefore implies convergence to a global minimizer. For smooth stochastic optimization, a common strategy for establishing such landscapes proceeds in two steps: $(i)$ establish benign geometry for the population objective---which is often easier to analyze---and $(ii)$ transfer this geometry to the empirical objective using concentration of gradients and Hessians. Recent work has extended saddle-point avoidance guarantees to weakly convex nonsmooth optimization through the notion of active strict saddles. We show, however, that benign population geometry need not transfer to empirical objectives in this setting. Specifically, for robust phase retrieval with Gaussian measurements---a well-studied and highly structured problem---the population objective is benign. Nevertheless, the empirical objective has sharp spurious local minima with probability bounded away from zero as the sample size tends to infinity. This asymptotic probability lower bound is independent of the dimension.

papers.title: Exponential stability of the reduced Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin system with one temperature
papers.abstract: We consider the reduced Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin system with one temperature, obtained from the full Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin thermoelastic beam system by neglecting one of the two temperature variables. This system was left essentially open in a recent work of Dell'Oro, where only a conjecture on its exponential stability condition was formulated. By combining the spectral analysis recently developed by Dell'Oro, Pata and Vasylyeva for the abstract Gurtin--Pipkin heat equation with the resolvent estimate framework of Dell'Oro for Bresse systems, we prove that the associated contraction semigroup is exponentially stable if and only if two explicit stability numbers, depending on the structural constants of the beam, both vanish. The proof is based on a spectral characterization of the infinitesimal generator in a half-plane containing the imaginary axis, an analysis of its spectrum on the imaginary axis, sharp upper bounds for the resolvent, and the Gearhart--Prüss theorem. In particular, we confirm the conjecture of Dell'Oro and provide a rigorous spectral analysis of the reduced system. The same method yields the exponential stability characterization of the corresponding reduced Bresse--Maxwell--Cattaneo system, and can be adapted to other reduced Bresse-type models.

papers.title: Decay of Correlations for Multiplicative Functionals of Determinantal Point Processes
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is an upper bound on the correlations of multiplicative functionals of determinantal point processes. In particular, for the sine process, the correlations of a multiplicative functional associated with a rapidly decaying function decay quadratically. It follows that the spectral density of such functionals belongs to the Sobolev space $H_1$.

papers.title: Differentially Private Distributed Optimization via the Intrinsic Randomness of Zeroth-Order Estimators: Sampling Geometry, Convergence, and Privacy Guarantees
papers.abstract: Distributed zeroth-order optimization has gained increasing attention in applications where exact gradients are computationally expensive or unavailable. However, the iterative exchange of local decision variables makes distributed networks vulnerable to inference attacks. While differential privacy provides a rigorous framework for privacy protection, conventional approaches generally require additional random noise, which inevitably affects optimization accuracy. In this paper, we investigate whether the randomness inherent in zeroth-order estimation can itself provide privacy protection. We develop a distributed zeroth-order gradient descent method that integrates consensus updates with a ball-uniform two-point gradient estimator. Our theoretical analysis shows that our algorithm attains standard convergence guarantees in both online and offline optimization settings. We then characterize the relevant probability distributions of the associated privacy mechanism, and establish differential privacy guarantees for both the online and offline optimization settings. These results reveal the potential of intrinsic zeroth-order randomness for privacy protection.

papers.title: Sharper Bounds for Graphical Two-Choice Allocation
papers.abstract: In graphical two-choice allocation, vertices are bins, and each arriving ball must be placed irrevocably at one endpoint of a uniformly random edge. The objective is to keep the maximum-minus-minimum load gap small at every time. On cycles, endpoint-local monotone rules incur polynomial gaps at long time horizons, whereas global rules can achieve polylogarithmic gaps. We prove a joint exponential-moment inequality for the orthogonal contrasts of a binary partition tree, controlling all contrasts along a root-to-leaf path simultaneously. Applied to the Bansal--Feldheim strategy, it improves the gap on every $κ$-edge-connected $d$-regular graph from $O((d/κ)\log^4 n\log\log n)$ to $O((d/κ)\log^3 n\log\log n)$. We give an explicit strategy on the $n$-cycle with expected gap $O(\log^2 n)$ uniformly over deterministic times and exponential tails at each such time. An Euler-tour projection yields $O(\bar d\log^2(2M))$ for every connected graph with $M$ edges and degree-proportional capacities. For lower bounds, we introduce a stochastic cut workload: the expected largest normalized overload forced by the requests, plus an indivisibility term. For every online integral strategy, the supremum over time of the expected gap is at least one sixth of this benchmark. Regular rings of cliques attain $Ω((d/κ)\log n)$ along an explicit family, improving the prior additive lower bound. With unequal capacities, the workload need not control the gap: one family has constant relative cut slack, bounded workload and gap $Ω(\log\log n)$; another has workload at most $20$ but forces gap $Ω(\log n)$ even for clairvoyant fractional allocations that remain irrevocable.

papers.title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
papers.abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm.

papers.title: Triple bubbles in the hyperbolic plane
papers.abstract: We prove that the standard triple bubble uniquely minimizes perimeter among clusters in the hyperbolic plane with three prescribed positive finite areas. The standard family admits global pressure coordinates, and its volume differential is the negative of a positive definite grounded weighted graph Laplacian. A normalized perimeter excess attains a comparison minimum under a perimeter bound and gives a strict comparison between actual and model pressures. Component relabeling reduces the possible topologies to an all-boundary network or a 4-daisy. Discrete comparisons exclude the 4-daisy; pressure-preserving face deletion reduces the remaining network to the standard tetrahedral configuration.

papers.title: Strict rearrangement inequalities for logarithmic p-Laplacians
papers.abstract: We establish cases of equality for the Polya-Szego inequality of the logarithmic p-Laplacian.

papers.title: A unified study of explosive processes with a root in the neighborhood of the unit circle
papers.abstract: This study is dedicated to autoregressive processes with stable and explosive time-varying coefficients, with a particular emphasis on a root located inside or outside the unit circle but converging towards the unit circle as the sample size increases (so that the limit process is integrated). Our objective is to develop a unified asymptotic theory that connects the classical stable, unstable and explosive regimes. By considering roots approaching the unit circle from both the stationary and explosive sides, we investigate how the corresponding asymptotic behaviors (of the process and the OLS) interact, and we try to build bridges between the rates associated with these regimes. This perspective provides a framework for understanding mixed autoregressive dynamics having a root in the neighborhood of the unit circle, provided a fairly general set of conditions.

papers.title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
papers.abstract: Bérczi, Gehér, Imolay, Lovász, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,α}$, $0<α<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.

papers.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
papers.abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.

papers.title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
papers.abstract: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.

papers.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the \emph{abstract group problem} for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is \emph{universal} and \emph{finitely universal}, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.

papers.title: Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Structural Reductions, Transverse Products, and Fixed-Codimension Stability
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, product constructions, and fixed-codimension stability. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy. Connected Nash decomposition and an analytic diagonal argument yield an explicit bound \[ \mathcal{N}(k,n)\leqslant 2^{\,2^{\,3(k+1)(n-k)}}. \] For configurations whose direction sums have dimension at most $k+1$, we prove the exact reduction $\mathcal{N}_{\leqslant k+1}(k,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,n-k+1)$. Every codimension-two configuration splits off a common linear factor, so $\mathcal{N}(n-2,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,3)$. A transverse product construction gives multiplicative inequalities. We further prove that for every fixed codimension $c$, the sequence $\mathcal{N}(k,k+c)$ is eventually constant. In codimension three, a sharper normal-span argument gives \[ \mathcal{N}(k,k+3)=\mathcal{N}(7,10)\qquad(k\geqslant7), \] where the numerical threshold uses the computer-assisted theorem $\mathcal{N}(1,3)=7$. The structural and stability results are otherwise independent of that numerical input.

papers.title: Setting Things Straight: On the Straightness and Non-Straightness of Two-Step Rectified Flow
papers.abstract: Rectified flow (RF) is an ODE-based generative modeling framework that has achieved remarkable success in practice over the past few years. By design, RF seeks to produce flows that have a high degree of straightness, in the sense that the resulting ODE trajectories can be obtained with relatively few (ideally, one) sampling steps. However, a rigorous analysis of straightness or near-straightness of RF flows remains missing in the literature. In this paper, we study settings in which the coupling generated by two-step RF is provably straight at the population level. We provide a complete characterization in two popular classes of data distributions: (i) smooth, strongly log-concave densities and (ii) Gaussian mixture models. Our main results yield sharp conditions for the coupling generated by two-step RF to be straight. Non-straight couplings are constructed when these conditions fail, which demonstrate the sharpness of these conditions. Using the theory developed on the straightness of two-step RF, we propose a notion of approximate straightness that measures the straightness of the learned couplings and can be estimated from the data. We introduce a procedure for constructing asymptotic confidence intervals for our proposed notion of approximate straightness and propose a data-driven method for selecting the number of reflow rounds in multiple iterations of RF.

papers.title: Critical measures and coefficient limits for non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
papers.abstract: We study critical holomorphic multiplicative chaos with circular iid inputs of unit variance. Writing \(R=|X_1|\), the radially normalized boundary measures converge in probability to a finite measure with almost surely positive mass exactly when \(\mathbb{E}[R^2\log(2+R)]<\infty\); otherwise they converge to zero. Radial and Fourier--radial approximations have distinct sharp \(L^q\) convergence criteria at each \(0<q<1\); convergence at every such order holds for both families exactly when \(\mathbb{E}e^{sR}<\infty\) for every \(0<s<2\). In the positive-limit class, coefficient vectors multiplied by \((\log n)^{1/4}\) and their analytic windows converge stably to Gaussian mixtures determined by the same critical measure. A uniformly bounded input family gives uncountably many coefficient-limit laws inequivalent under nonzero deterministic complex rescaling. We distinguish these laws using exact weighted tails under \(\mathbb{E}I_0(2R)<\infty\), where \(I_0\) is the modified Bessel function, and negative mass moments. For \(\log\mathbb{P}(R>u)\sim-λu^α\), \(0<α<1\) and \(λ>0\), the normalization and Gaussian-mixture form persist, while every positive limit moment diverges; we determine the logarithmic tails. Finite limiting moments need not imply convergence of the original coefficient moments. In the positive-limit class, coefficient periodograms recover the critical measure and energy normalization gives Gaussian limits. Hardy nonmembership holds under finite variance alone; the positive-limit class has sharp weighted Bergman criteria for \(0<p\le2\) and boundary Sobolev threshold \(s=-1/2\).

papers.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincaré prior that neither test decides
papers.abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $δ_F$ with bounded drift is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincaré inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincaré, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincaré class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.

papers.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
papers.abstract: We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -Δu=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that the equation admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove the compactness of the solution set for this equation by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is non-degenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set is finite. Our results also give a definite answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

papers.title: An improved upper bound on the chromatic number of the n-dimensional sphere
papers.abstract: In this short note, we obtain upper bounds on the chromatic numbers of spheres using recent improvements in bounds for Euclidean space. We show that $χ(S^n_{R}) \leq (ξ_R + o(1))^n$, where $ξ_R = \frac{3\sqrt 3}{2}(1-\frac{1}{4R^2}) $ and $χ(S^n_R)$ denotes the chromatic number of the $n$-dimensional sphere of a fixed radius $R$.

papers.title: Bipartite solutions of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxer equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of unitary set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions, called \emph{bipartite} solutions. This class, which is purely combinatorial in nature, forms a full subcategory of $\mathcal{LYB}$, the category of Lyubashenko type solutions of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, and is particularly amenable to explicit classification results. We give an intrinsic necessary and sufficient condition for a solution of the Yang--Baxter equation to be isomorphic to a bipartite solution, we settle the isomorphism problem within this class and, as an application, we determine their automorphism groups. If $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, the number of isomorphism classes of bipartite solutions on $X$ is $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 + \sum_{m=2}^{n} \bigl( o(m, n-m) - 1 \bigr)$, where $o(m, k)$ denotes the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$ acting by conjugation on the $k$-element multisets of elements of $S_m$. The paper also offers a comparative study: for small $|X| = n$ we count, up to isomorphism, all set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions on $X$, together with five distinguished families of solutions. Throughout the range we were able to compute, the class $\mathcal{LYB}$ accounts for a large share of all bijective and of all non-degenerate solutions, strikingly close to the total.

papers.title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity. Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.

papers.title: Time-Uniform Dependent Central Limit Theory
papers.abstract: We establish a near-optimal almost sure invariance principle for nonstationary time series under the functional dependence measure (FDM) framework. This result yields a universal time-uniform dependent central limit theorem, which serves as the basis for anytime-valid inference. In particular, we instantiate the theorem through asymptotic confidence sequences (AsympCSs), time-uniform counterparts of asymptotic confidence intervals obtained via central limit theorems, extending those originally proposed in Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) to time series with serial dependence. We further refine the original definition because, as we show, it can admit AsympCSs that fail to achieve asymptotic time-uniform coverage even for independent and identically distributed settings. We address this issue by adding a simple eventual-inclusion condition, which in turn permits more flexible variance estimation. In time-series settings, this relaxation can substantially ease restrictions on bandwidth and kernel selection. For feasible implementation of AsympCSs, we establish strong consistency of HAC variance estimators under the FDM framework, accommodating a wider range of commonly used bandwidth choices than existing results under mixing conditions. As illustrations, we construct AsympCSs for algorithms with Markovian structure and time-series-based causal estimands.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.

papers.title: Rotations, Shears, and Two-Generation on Spheres
papers.abstract: For every round sphere $S^n$, $n\ge2$, we exhibit two explicit smooth vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $Diff_0(S^n)$. By deleting one gradient component from the second generator, we obtain two explicit divergence-free vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $SDiff_0(S^n)$. In both cases two generators are minimal. The proof first generates the divergence-free vector fields using rotations, a linearly modulated rotational shear, and transverse vector spherical harmonics. On $S^2$ this reduces to the Hamiltonian/Poisson formalism; for $n\ge4$ irreducibility of the transverse harmonic spaces completes the degree-raising argument, while $S^3$ requires a separate treatment of its two curl eigenspaces. Adding one gradient field and using the divergence map then generates all smooth vector fields. Finally, a Casimir operator for a recovered copy of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ separates the components of the generating fields and compresses the natural finite generating families to two.

papers.title: Linear Preservers of Semipositivity and Minimal Semipositivity
papers.abstract: We classify all real linear into preservers of semipositivity on $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$, $m,n\ge2$, relative to arbitrary source and target pairs of proper cones, without assuming invertibility or a prescribed form. The classification consists of product maps $L(A)=XAY$ and rank-$n$ degenerate maps $L(A)=Ψ(u^TA)$, subject to explicit cone and matrix-pencil conditions. For square minimal semipositivity with respect to the standard nonnegative orthant, preservation forces the operator to be invertible: for $n\ge2$, the linear into preservers are precisely the maps $L(A)=XAY$ and $L(A)=XA^TY$ with $X,Y\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ satisfying $X^{-1},Y^{-1}\ge0$. We also classify all linear preservers of orthant semipositivity from $M_{2,2}(\mathbb{R})$ to $M_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ into three disjoint classes, two of which consist of maps of rank three outside product form.

papers.title: Quantum algorithms for optimal control: large-scale finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation
papers.abstract: We develop quantum algorithms for optimal control over a prescribed finite time interval (finite horizon), focusing on continuous-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR). This foundational control problem often requires solving a nonlinear matrix Riccati equation, which can be costly for large systems and long control durations on conventional classical solvers. We instead work directly with the state-costate optimality equations, reformulating the LQR problem as a multiple-shooting linear system. Importantly, we prove a condition-number bound for the system that is independent of the horizon, under stabilizability and detectability assumptions. By incorporating the initial and final conditions into a single linear system, we can solve the subsequent linear system more efficiently with a quantum linear systems subroutine. For a given initial state, our quantum algorithms return classical estimates of the optimal cost and the optimal control inputs at a selected time, without constructing a Riccati solution operator. Given sparse-matrix block-encodings, an initial-state preparation oracle and a fixed number of control inputs, the query and gate complexities scale polylogarithmically with system size and control duration, provided that sparsity, relevant norms, and stability parameters are bounded. The dependence on the target error is inverse-linear up to logarithmic factors. We establish the required bounds uniformly in system size and duration for a family of damped mass-spring chains with two endpoint controls. Numerical experiments support the analysis.

papers.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.

papers.title: Non-existence of Negative Weight Derivations of the Moduli Algebras of Isolated Weighted Homogeneous Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: Mather and Yau proved that the analytic isomorphism class of an isolated complex hypersurface singularity is determined by its dimension and its moduli algebra. Yau's conjecture asserts that the moduli algebra of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity over $\C$ has no nonzero derivation of negative degree. We prove this conjecture.

papers.title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
papers.abstract: For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, we prove that integrating one coordinate of the truncated correlation of order $k$ for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF) gives $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. The integral converges absolutely, and the identity holds pointwise, including at coincident fixed coordinates by continuous extension. This answers the marginal-identity part of Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran's question for the planar GEF. We also prove a general criterion for simple point processes: under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions, the identities hold almost everywhere if there are compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one, eventually equal to one on each compact set, whose linear statistics have variances tending to zero. For GEF zeros, strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions. The proof combines a mixed-cumulant estimate with the partition formula for ordinary and factorial cumulants.

papers.title: A Criterion for Finite Hypergeometric Reductions of Lauricella's $F_C$ with Arguments Related by Cube Roots of Unity
papers.abstract: We consider the germ at the origin of Lauricella's function $F_C^{(3)}(a,b;c_0,c_1,c_2;κ,ωκ,ω^2κ)$, where $ω=\exp(2π\sqrt{-1}/3)$. We assume that $a,b,c_0,c_1,c_2$ avoid nonpositive integers and that $c_0,c_1,c_2$ also avoid half-integers. We consider finite linear combinations of ordinary generalized hypergeometric series with arguments $ακ^3$, where $α$ is a nonzero complex constant that may vary between summands, each multiplied by a nonnegative integer power of $κ$. Every target series has lower parameters outside the nonpositive integers and converges near the origin or terminates. We prove that such a representation exists if and only if, for each $j=0,1,2$, either $c_j-c_0$ or $c_j+c_0$ is an integer, and construct finite sums of ordinary ${}_9F_8$ functions when this condition holds. We prove necessity from irreducible differential equations of order $24$ for the generating functions of the three coefficient subsequences and from their formal solutions at infinity.

papers.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of Kähler geometry: the classical Kähler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Ampère energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics.

papers.title: Graph and Hypergraph Counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation Conjecture Beyond $n^{k-1}$
papers.abstract: For a fixed $k$-graph $F$, let $h_F(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $F$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\text{ex}(n,F)+q$ edges. Let $c(n,F)$ be the minimum number created by adding one edge to an extremal $F$-free $k$-graph. We construct stable counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture for every $k\ge2$. The ratio $h_F(n,q)/(q c(n,F))$ tends to zero over ranges extending beyond $n^{k-1}$. For graphs, we give examples of every chromatic number at least three. In particular, there is a graph $F$ for which this ratio tends to zero for $1\le q=o(n^{4/3})$. For $k\ge3$, we use connected linear expansions of $G=(M_a\cup K_{1,b}\cup I_h)\vee K_{m_1,\ldots,m_{k-1}}$. Under explicit parameter conditions, the ratio tends to zero for $1\le q=o(n^{k-1+(b-1)/(a+b-1)})$ when $b\ge k+1$. We prove the exact Turán theorems for both constructions and determine their unique extremal graphs and hypergraphs. Keywords: supersaturation; extremal graph; linear hypergraph; graph expansion; stability.

papers.title: Global Extendability of Local Atoms in Sparse Moment Relaxations
papers.abstract: Moment relaxations provide lower bounds for polynomial optimization problems, while their moment matrices can also carry information about solutions. We study whether atomic candidates extracted from clique blocks reveal part of a global minimizer in moment relaxations with correlative sparsity. We give sufficient conditions for global extendability. If the relaxation is value-exact and the moment matrix of a selected clique has maximum rank over the optimal face and satisfies simplicial regularity, then at least one of its atomic candidates is globally extendable. When this maximum rank is one, we derive a direct certificate for global extendability. Further examples demonstrate the necessity of value exactness for global extendability. Numerical experiments on unicycle trajectory optimization successfully yield near-optimal solutions through progressive extraction and fixing, demonstrating the practical effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
papers.abstract: We study weighted Fourier extension estimates for the truncated cone. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we introduce a more refined trilinear estimate. We obtain this estimate by applying weighted bilinear restriction on half-scale cubes and combining tube traversal with trilinear Kakeya to sum the local packet energies. Together with Lorentz rescaling, it yields improved weighted extension estimates.

papers.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
papers.abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.

papers.title: Additive complements to the primes and large gaps between Romanoff numbers
papers.abstract: We prove that every set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains all sufficiently large integers satisfies $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This proves a quantitative form of Ruzsa's Conjecture 2 and gives a negative answer to the $O(\log X)$ question in Erdős Problem 32. The bound follows from a more general result: for an arbitrary set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and sufficiently large $X$, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers in $[X/2,X]$ outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$, provided this length is positive. As an application, we obtain $G_{\mathcal R}(X)\gg\log\log X$ for the longest block in $[1,X]$ containing no Romanoff number $p+2^n$, improving the bound $G_{\mathcal R}(X)\gg\log\log X/\log\log\log X$ of Kalmynin and Konyagin. The argument also applies to $p+a^n$ for every fixed integer $a\ge2$. The key step is a lemma on large shifts, proved using truncated products of divisor sums and the removal of auxiliary primes dividing differences of shifts.

papers.title: Negatively Curved Minimal Surfaces in the Round Four-Sphere
papers.abstract: We construct smooth closed embedded minimal surfaces with everywhere negative Gaussian curvature in the unit round four-sphere. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $m$, our construction gives a minimal surface $Σ_m$ of genus $m^2+1$ such that $\operatorname{Area}(Σ_m)\to 4π^2$ as $m\to+\infty$. This result yields a complete solution to Problem 101 in Yau's 1982 list of open problems.

papers.title: Hodge and Hodge-Witt polygons under specialization
papers.abstract: We show that, in equal characteristic $p$, the Hodge-Witt polygon can only move down and domino numbers can only increase under specialization in smooth proper families. We also show that the Hodge polygon of the generic fiber of a proper smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\mathcal{O}_C$ lies on or above the Hodge-Witt polygon of its special fiber, where $C$ is a complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We further show that, in this mixed-characteristic setting, if the crystalline cohomology of the special fiber is torsion-free in degrees $n$ and $n+1$, then the degree-$n$ Hodge polygon of the generic fiber lies on or below the abstract Hodge polygon of the special fiber. We illustrate these comparisons with explicit examples.

papers.title: Improved dimension bounds for Falconer's distance problem in the plane
papers.abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbb R^2$ be analytic with $t=\dim_{\mathrm H}E>1$. We prove $\dim_{\mathrm H}ΔE\ge 4/5+η_0$ for an absolute, non-explicit constant $η_0>0$, and \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}ΔE\ge \frac{t^2-2t+5}{2t^2-7t+10} \quad\text{for }1<t\le\frac{11-\sqrt{41}}{4}, \] which reaches $7/8$ at the right endpoint. For pinned distances, $\dim_{\mathrm H}Δ_xE\ge q_*=0.7813\ldots$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^2$ outside an exceptional set of Hausdorff dimension at most one, with stronger bounds depending on $t$ and further exceptional-set estimates. If $E$ is compact and supports an $s$-Frostman measure $μ$, $s>1$, then \[ \underline{\dim}_{\mathrm B}Δ_xE\ge \max\left\{\frac45+η_0,\min\left\{\frac{3s+1}{5},\frac78\right\}\right\} \] for $μ$-almost every $x$. The same bound holds for pinned Hausdorff dimension under a common dyadic mass law, allowing oscillation with scale. We retain information about both endpoints in the Kolmogorov complexity estimates of Stull and Fiedler--Stull. Applying the partition estimates with the endpoints reversed yields $4/5$ and the rational bound. Equality forces both information profiles to have excess information on a common interval of scales. Encoding one source measure for all pins converts this constraint into a configuration of points and circles with many rich perpendicular bisectors. Lower bounds of Katz--Tardos and Ren--Wang contradict the upper bound of Fu--Gan--Ren; compactness then gives $η_0>0$. This rigidity argument has a precedent in the work of Héra, Shmerkin and Yavicoli on Furstenberg sets, using Bourgain's projection theorem. A separate finite-scale selection proves the pinned lower box bound.

papers.title: Measuring the roughness of a signal
papers.abstract: We study the non-parametric estimation of the roughness of a path from discretely sampled observations. Our approach is based on the concept of normalized power variation of a path. The estimator identifies a variation index by comparing coarse increments with local sums of fine increments. We prove pathwise consistency under Hölder regularity, nondegenerate coarse critical power sums, uniform local bounds on fine critical power sums, and separation of the two sampling scales and obtain a convergence rate for the estimator. Neither convergence of critical variation nor monotonicity of the finite-sample statistic is required. The result applies to fractional Brownian motion under dyadic sampling and to Schauder series with bounded coefficients bounded away from zero. For signed Takagi--Landsberg functions we obtain a uniform asymptotic formula and a quantitative bound for every root of the estimating equation in a fixed parameter interval. For fractional Brownian motion, we obtain asymptotic uniqueness of the estimating root and a polynomial almost-sure error bound. We illustrate the results with numerical experiments for Takagi-Landsberg functions, fractional Brownian motion and the stochastic heat equation.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Stochastic First-Order Algorithms with Variance Reduction in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We establish complexity lower bounds for stochastic first-order algorithms in nonconvex--concave minimax optimization, allowing algorithms to use variance reduction. Our main contribution is a lower bound for a zero-respecting algorithm class that permits variance reduction, extending beyond the algorithmic restrictions imposed by some existing lower bounds. We consider objectives with an $L$-Lipschitz continuous joint gradient, a compact convex dual domain of Euclidean radius at most $D_Y$, and a primal value function, defined by maximizing the objective over the dual variable, with initial suboptimality at most $Δ$. The target accuracy $\varepsilon$ is measured by the gradient norm of the Moreau envelope of the constrained primal value function with parameter $1/(2L)$. Under an unbiased stochastic first-order oracle with variance at most $σ^2$ and mean-squared smoothness, we prove the lower bound $Ω\!\left(L^2D_YΔ\varepsilon^{-3}+L^3D_Y^2Δσ^2\varepsilon^{-6}\right)$. This result quantifies the dependence on accuracy, dual-domain radius, and oracle noise even when variance reduction is allowed. We also establish complementary lower bounds for nonconvex--strongly-concave minimax optimization. With dual strong-concavity parameter $μ>0$ and condition number $κ:=L/μ$, we obtain $Ω\!\left(LΔ\sqrtκ\,\varepsilon^{-2}+LΔκσ^2\varepsilon^{-4}\right)$ under the bounded-variance oracle model. Under the additional mean-squared smoothness condition with constant $\bar L$, we obtain $Ω\!\left(LΔ\sqrtκ\,\varepsilon^{-2}+Δ\bar Lσκ^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-3}\right)$. Together, these results identify complexity barriers across the concave and strongly concave regimes, with the main nonconvex--concave bound remaining valid for algorithms that use variance reduction.

papers.title: Upper bounds on the Turán density of projective hypergraphs over a finite field
papers.abstract: For a prime power $q\geq2$ and an integer $m\geq2$, let $PG(m,q)$ denote the $m-$dimensional projective hypergraph over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Employing the $\mathsf{L}^p-$method and using the incidence structure, we establish the Turán density of $PG(m,q)$ \begin{equation*} π(PG(m,q))\leq\begin{cases} \left(1-\frac{1}{q+1}\right)^{\frac{1}{q}} & \text{ if } m=2, \left(1-\frac{1}{(q+1)|E(PG(m-1,q))|}\right)^{\frac{1}{1+q^{m-1}}} & \text{ if } m\geq3. \end{cases} \end{equation*} The previously known upper bound on its Turán density was $1-\binom{q^m}{q}^{-1}$. As a consequence of our estimate, this upper bound is improved for each prime power $q\geq3$ and for each dimension index $m\geq2$. For a positive integer $t$, let $B_{t}[PG(2,q)]$ be the $(q+1)-$graph formed by taking $t$ copies of the $PG(2,q)$ that shares a common edge. Using the $\mathsf{L}^p-$method, we establish that the upper bound of the Turán density of $B_{t}[PG(2,q)]$ is $\left(1-\frac{1}{q+1}\right)^{\frac{1}{qt}}$.

papers.title: Smooth perturbation theory and generic Cantor spectrum for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic operators
papers.abstract: We consider multi-dimensional quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators with monotone sawtooth-type potentials in the perturbative localization regime. We prove that a given gap is closed iff a corresponding (via a natural gap labeling) eigenfunction vanishes at the origin. Using this, we show that for a generic choice of the sampling function $f$, the spectrum of such an operator is a Cantor set, with all possible gaps being open. We also provide a class of functions $f$ for which some gaps are closed. Finally, we observe that certain gaps are more difficult to close than the others.

papers.title: Invariant Shape Analysis of Surfaces with Spherical Topology
papers.abstract: Every real spherical harmonic of even degree is congruent to its mirror image. We prove that a real spherical harmonic of odd degree $n\ge3$ with distinct Maxwell axes is congruent to its mirror image if and only if the hyperelliptic curve of genus $n-1$ defined by its binary form has a reduced automorphism of even order whose lift acts on the form by $-1$. We then determine the locus of these curves: it is the locus of curves with an extra involution if and only if $n-1$ is a power of two, and otherwise it also contains, for each even divisor $k$ of $n-1$ with odd cofactor $d\ge3$, an irreducible family $y^2=x K(x^{2k})$, $°K=d$, with generic reduced automorphism group $\Z/2k$. For $n=3$ the condition is the vanishing of the skew invariant of the binary sextic. As an application, the invariants of the truncated spherical harmonic expansion of a genus-zero surface, in a conformal parameterization normalized by its conformal barycenter, give a descriptor that is exactly invariant under parameterization, position and scale, records handedness, and is stable in the orbit distance.

papers.title: Sublinear Markov Semigroups Beyond Uniqueness
papers.abstract: To what extent does a local operator on smooth test functions determine a sub-Markov semigroup and its underlying structure of laws? Many existing approaches work with Feller semigroups on the space \(C_b\) of bounded continuous functions and rely on uniqueness, often established through a comparison principle for the associated evolution equation. However, even when the local operator is linear, uniqueness may fail and a \(C_b\)-Feller restriction may exclude the associated canonical semigroup. We discover that the space \(\operatorname{USC}_b\) of bounded upper semicontinuous functions offers a natural setting for this study. Within this framework, a complete description of the relationships among sublinear local operators, sublinear sub-Markov semigroups, and their underlying structures of laws is achieved without assuming uniqueness. Under suitable regularity and Lyapunov conditions, we construct the greatest semigroup compatible with a prescribed sublinear local operator and obtain a stochastic representation in terms of a Markov process under sublinear expectations. We characterize all sublinear sub-Markov semigroups dominated by this greatest semigroup in two ways: through a one-to-one correspondence with stable subfamilies of its representing laws, and through an order relation between their infinitesimal generators and the prescribed local operator. We further characterize the greatest semigroup via the greatest viscosity subsolution of the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation. These results clarify what information about global stochastic evolution can be recovered from local infinitesimal descriptions and what freedom remains in the absence of uniqueness. The resulting characterizations are new even when the local operator is linear.

papers.title: Proofs Without Nominals: Gödel's Ontological Argument, its Shallow Embedding, and the Open Questions of the Monatshefte Notes
papers.abstract: The shallow embedding of higher-order modal logic in classical higher-order logic, used in Benzmüller and Scott's Notes on Gödel's and Scott's variants of the ontological argument, reaches beyond the modal object language: its quantifiers range over domains containing the nominals and satisfaction operators of hybrid logic. A proof using one proves a theorem of the embedding, not necessarily of the modal logic. Whether a result is one of the modal logic can be settled by replaying it in an explicit calculus, or, more cheaply and for all results at once, by analysing what the embedding's proofs substitute. Every statement the Notes prove has a proof in the embedding substituting nothing outside the object language, 294 of them explicit. The Notes' own proofs substitute none either; what it flags are terms a prover introduced. A soundness theorem over general models closed under the object language, and a sentence of that language the embedding proves but which fails in such a model, fix what the certificate says. The Notes' three open questions are settled too, without nominals, but by the empty instance of the conjunction axiom, too cheaply to convince. Generalised to Gödel's "any number of summands", the axiom covers the empty conjunction and the singleton. This article restricts it to at least two different conjuncts, a non-degenerate reading of Gödel's footnote, and settles them again without nominals. In effect only the empty conjunction is excluded; the singleton comes back with the other axioms. In one variant the restriction refutes the possible existence of a God-like being; the answers return, with no side condition, once the Notes' non-emptiness clause is confined to Gödel's essence. Every theorem here is verified in Isabelle/HOL and independently in Lean 4, the separating model in its propositional part; the countermodels are Nitpick's, checked by the build.

papers.title: Determination of all diffeomorphism invariant tensor fields on the space of smooth positive densities on a compact manifold with corners
papers.abstract: It was proved in [3] that on a closed manifold of dimension greater than one, every smooth weak Riemannian metric on the space of smooth positive probability densities that is invariant under the action of the diffeomorphism group is a multiple of the Fisher--Rao metric. Here we describe all purely covariant tensor fields of arbitrary order on the space of positive densities of a compact manifold with corners which are invariant under the action of the connected component of the diffeomorphism group. Finally, we classify the considerably fewer purely contravariant invariant tensor fields, describe the basic mixed contraction, and indicate the expected form of general invariant tensor fields.

papers.title: Matching algebras and their Dunkl subalgebras
papers.abstract: For a finite simple graph $G = (V, E)$, we consider the quotient algebra $\mathcal M(G)$ of the polynomial ring in the variables $u_e$ (for $e \in E$) by the ideal generated by all products $u_e u_f$ for non-disjoint edges $e$ and $f$ (including all squares $u_e^2$). This quotient is called the matching algebra of $G$, since it has a basis indexed by the matchings of $G$. In this quotient, we define a subalgebra $\mathcal D(G)$ generated by the signed incidence sums $θ_v=\sum_{e=(v,w)}u_e-\sum_{e=(w,v)}u_e$ for all $v \in V$ (where all edges of $G$ are oriented arbitrarily); we call this the Dunkl matching algebra. We show that, as a graded vector space, $\mathcal D(G)$ is dual to the span of all polynomials $p_M = \prod_{(i,j) \in M} (x_i - x_j)$, where $M$ ranges over all matchings of $G$. For the complete graph $K_n$, the latter span is a direct sum of two-row Specht modules (one in each degree); thus its Hilbert series is that of the Catalan triangle, and, in characteristic zero, the Dunkl matching algebra can be presented by linear and quadratic relations. For arbitrary graphs, we formulate the saturation problem of deciding when the selected matching Specht generators $p_M$ in a given degree $k$ span the full two-row Specht module $S^{(n-k,k)}$. We show that saturation in degree $k$ forces $k$-connectivity, that saturation in degree $2$ is equivalent to $2$-connectivity, and that $k$-linked graphs are saturated in degree $k$. We also prove saturation in every possible degree whenever the complement of $G$ is a matching. We show that the Dunkl matching algebra equals the full matching algebra exactly for forests, and give an explicit Hilbert series formula for unicyclic graphs.

papers.title: A quasipolynomial inverse theorem for the $\mathsf{U}^k(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ norm in the high characteristic
papers.abstract: We prove an inverse theorem for the Gowers uniformity norm $\mathsf{U}^k(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ with quasipolynomial bounds in the case when $p \geq k$. The inverse theorem follows from a quasipolynomial structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms, which are a natural generalization of Freiman homomorphisms to maps of several variables. The proof of the structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms is the central result of the paper and rests on three main ingredients: algebraic regularity method, abstract Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers theorem and the theory of multilinear maps defined on multilinear varieties. The last ingredient originates from an earlier work of Gowers and the author, and is significantly expanded in this paper. In particular, once the theory of such maps is in place, the proof of the structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms is relatively short, especially compared to the previous quantitative results in the inverse theory of Gowers norms.

papers.title: Effective atom-dimer bands of three-body lattice systems at strong coupling: exact critical mass ratios and a statistics-quasimomentum duality
