papers.abstract: We study three particles on the two-dimensional square lattice with contact interactions of infinite strength, in every sector of total quasimomentum, for three statistics: identical bosons, two identical fermions with a distinguishable third particle, and two identical bosons with a distinguishable third particle. The atom-dimer sector associated with the infinitely degenerate eigenvalue of the pair-contact operator is analysed on the whole Brillouin zone. A Feshbach-Schur reduction gives explicit effective Hamiltonians built from the Dirichlet Laplacian and a rank-four exchange operator, and a spectral transfer theorem with explicit error bounds identifies the atom-dimer threshold of the three-body operator with that of the effective one; the eigenvalue counting function below the threshold is squeezed between those of the effective operator, so that the number of atom-dimer states bound uniformly in the coupling equals the number of bound states of the effective Hamiltonian. The threshold problem reduces to a four-by-four Hermitian matrix whose zero-energy limit is built from the two-point resistances of the square lattice and hence to a quartic polynomial. This yields the complete atom-dimer zones in closed form; the critical hopping ratio as an explicit function on the whole Brillouin zone with two-sided bounds and closed forms at all symmetry points; at most two atom-dimer states per sector with an explicit second threshold; exact onset laws of infinite order at the corner point and linear-over-logarithmic in the pure p-wave channel; and two exact dualities relating a change of statistics to a shift of quasimomentum by half a reciprocal-lattice vector. The reduction of the three-body eigenvalue problem to the lattice Skornyakov-Ter-Martirosyan equation is proved with an explicit isomorphism of eigenspaces.

papers.title: The lattice covering density of the regular octahedron
papers.abstract: We prove that the lattice covering density of the regular octahedron is $9/8$, establishing the optimality of the classical body-centered cubic covering. A hypothetical lattice covering of smaller density would yield a lattice basis whose six Kuhn tetrahedra each fit in a translate of the octahedron. A sharp determinant bound then gives a contradiction. As a consequence, the maximum order of an undirected Abelian Cayley graph with three generators and their inverses and diameter at most $k$ is $\frac{32}{27}k^3+O(k^2)$ as $k\to\infty$.

papers.title: Four collinear points or six visible points
papers.abstract: Every finite planar set of at least $880$ points contains four collinear points or six pairwise visible points.

papers.title: Thermodynamic formalism and multifractal analysis of Birkhoff averages for parabolic rational maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the multifractal analysis of Birkhoff averages for parabolic rational maps. We establish a conditional variational principle and prove the real analyticity and strict monotonicity of the Birkhoff spectrum, as well as the existence and uniqueness of the measure attaining the supremum in the conditional variational principle, on a certain region. To this end, we prove the existence and uniqueness of an expanding equilibrium measure and the real analyticity of the pressure function on a suitable domain. For parabolic systems, our approach using thermodynamic formalism provides a unified framework for establishing the conditional variational principle and investigating finer properties of the Birkhoff spectrum, including its real analyticity, strict monotonicity, and the existence and uniqueness of a measure attaining the supremum on a certain region.

papers.title: Characteristic Mapping Method for Vlasov-Poisson with BGK-collisions
papers.abstract: This work presents the first steps for simulating kinetic plasmas with collisions using the characteristic mapping method (CMM). The CMM is a semi-Lagrangian method that uses the group structure of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms to efficiently represent the flow-maps of transport problems. Individual submaps can be composed to follow the flow backward in time to its initial foot point, numerically establishing the back-to-label symmetry. The novelty of the presented work is the handling of the source term by storing the Duhamel integrals of each time sub-interval, allowing efficient temporal-integration. Furthermore, we use the Lagrangian structure to avoid implicit time-stepping in the hydrodynamic regime, which is known to be stiff. We benchmark our method on the Boltzmann-BGK and Vlasov-Poisson-BGK equations and consider different test cases, the Sod shock tube problem and nonlinear Landau damping for different Knudsen numbers. We show third-order spatial and temporal convergence and illustrate the fine-scale zoom property of CMM for the bump-on-tail instability.

papers.title: MOE-DGSCND: Multi-Objective Enterprise Green Supply Chain Network Design
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies the Multi-Objective Enterprise Doubly-Green Supply Chain Network Design (MOE-DGSCND) problem, an extension of Multi-Objective Supply Chain Network Design. The problem studied here is a three-objective combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes total cost f1, carbon dioxide emissions f2 and customer dissatisfaction f3 over binary decisions regarding which distribution centers to open and how to assign customer zones to open facilities. The problem generalizes the capacitated facility location problem (CFLP) and is known to be NP-hard (Garey and Johnson, 1979). This paper formally specifies the decision variables, objective functions and constraints and investigates three solution approaches using a single numerical instance: (A) an exact weighted-sum integer linear programming (ILP) formulation solved with Python combinatorially and via PuLP, (B) three Fully Polynomial-Time Approximation Schemes (FPTAS) providing (1 + $ε$)-approximate solutions for $ε$ := 0.15 and (C) two baseline heuristics for comparison. On an instance with eight customers and five candidate distribution centers, the exact solver certifies the optimal (sampled) supported solutions across eight weight combinations, while the FPTAS-based approaches complete within milliseconds, compared to centiseconds for the exact ILP on this tiny non-stochastic instance.

papers.title: Removable matchings in $2$-connected graphs
papers.abstract: A matching $M$ of a $2$-connected graph $G$ is \emph{removable} if $G-M$ is $2$-connected. We prove that, for every integer $d\ge4$, every $2$-connected graph with at least $2d$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$ has a removable matching of size $d$. This improves the previously known lower bound $d-2$ for $d\ge5$ to the optimal value $d$, answering a question of Li, Zhou, Fujita, and Mao. We also show that a $2$-connected graph on at least six vertices with minimum degree at least $3$ has a removable matching of size $3$ if and only if it is not a wheel. Our proofs use edge contraction and the structure of \emph{minimal non-removable matchings}.

papers.title: A Probability Model for Pentagonal Prism Dice Rolls
papers.abstract: In the realm of probability theory and game design, the study of dice probabilities plays a crucial role. The featured dice are usually fair, so their probabilities can be predicted without rolling the dice. Pentagonal prismatic dice are not fair. Hence, the probabilities are more complicated. Our mathematical model is naturally derived from both the geometric properties of the dice and empirical evidence. Dice of varying sizes but with constant volume were designed. Using a 3D printer with 100 percent infill, the dice were printed and prepared. A machine that simulates dropping dice through a dice tower onto a hard surface was used to obtain about 41,000 results. From these data, a statistical model was constructed that gives probabilities of dice with varying height-to-radius ratios. The formula for the model is based on the centroid solid angle, but with two adjustment parameters due to varying energy and other requirements to transition between different resting aspects. Within the range of height-to-radius ratios tested, the data are within reasonable statistical error of the model.

papers.title: A Two-regime Khintchine Inequality and an Improved Bound on the Degree-1 Fourier Weight for Linear Threshold Functions
papers.abstract: The Khintchine inequality provides a lower bound on the expected absolute value of a weighted sum of independent Rademacher random variables. In the classical setting, when the coefficient vector has unit Euclidean norm, this lower bound is a constant, with equality attained only by a simple family of extremal configurations. A refinement due to De, Diakonikolas, and Servedio, referred to as the \emph{linear Khintchine inequality} in this work, strengthens this estimate by establishing a lower bound that depends linearly on the distance of the coefficient vector from the extremal set. In this paper, we present a refined analysis of this dependence on the weight vector. Our results reveal a phase transition in the rate of improvement: when the dimension exceeds six, the lower bound undergoes an abrupt change as the weight vector deviates from the minimizer. Additionally, we improve the slope constant in linear Khintchine inequality. As a consequence, we establish an improved lower bound on the degree-1 Fourier weight for linear threshold functions $\mathbf W^{\leq1}[f]\geq0.55100929$, marking progress towards a conjecture of Benjamini, Kalai, and Schramm.

papers.title: Optimal Condition Numbers in Low-Rank Positive Semidefinite Matrix Sensing
papers.abstract: In this paper we focus on the stability of positive semidefinite matrix sensing maps $Φ_{\mathcal{A}}=(\langle A_i,X\rangle)_{i=1}^m$ where $A_i\succeq 0$, $X\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r$. We introduce the bi-Lipschitz constants of $Φ_{\mathcal{A}}$ and define the global condition numbers as the ratio of upper and lower Lipschitz constants. We give deterministic universal lower bounds for these condition numbers that depend only on the rank $r$ and on the underlying field. We then show that rank-one Gaussian measurements asymptotically attain these bounds, except for the operator-norm condition number over $\mathbb R$ when $r=1$. For this exceptional case, we establish a sharper universal lower bound and prove its asymptotic sharpness. As an application, we derive stability guarantees for an $\ell_1$-residual PhaseLift-type estimator at the optimal sampling scale. These results identify the intrinsic limits of conditioning in positive semidefinite matrix sensing and connect these limits to stable low-rank recovery.

papers.title: Extending Goldberg's Exact Sequence to Braid Groups of Graphs and Simplicial Complexes
papers.abstract: For a finite connected simplicial complex $X$, the strand map $ι_\ast$, from $\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ to $\prod_{i=1}^nπ_1(X,x_i^0)$, sends a pure braid to the homotopy classes of its strands. A theorem of Goldberg (1973) computes its kernel when $X$ is a closed surface other than $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$: the kernel is the normal closure of the pure braids supported in an embedded disc. We extend this picture to arbitrary finite connected simplicial complexes. Call $X$ $\textit{weakly Goldberg}$ if some contractible subcomplex $X_0\subseteq X$ realises Goldberg's description, $\kerι_\ast=\left\langle \operatorname{im}(\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)) \right\rangle$, and $\textit{Goldberg}$ if $X_0$ can moreover be chosen so that $\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ is injective. We prove that the strand map is surjective if and only if $X\not\cong S^1$; that $X$ is weakly Goldberg if and only if its free part is a forest; and that $X$ is Goldberg if and only if it admits an $\textit{admissible tree}$ -- a maximal tree of a scaffold, compatible with the boundary and interior types of the attachments of the free part to the thick components. We also classify the complexes for which the kernel is trivial, settle the exceptional surfaces $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$, and obtain complete answers for manifolds and for graphs. The main tools are a graph-of-spaces decomposition of the configuration space at a point of $X$ and a resolution procedure reducing an arbitrary complex to a simple model.

papers.title: Adaptive Schauder Stochastic Mirror Descent in Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we solve risk functional minimization problems with general losses in Banach spaces within the framework of stochastic approximation. We introduce an adaptive regularization strategy for stochastic mirror descent (SMD). Specifically, using a Schauder basis, we construct nested finite-dimensional subspaces whose dimensions adapt to the sample size $n$ to balance approximation and optimization errors. We solve each SMD subproblem over the corresponding subspace and project the stochastic subgradient onto its dual space. This yields closed-form solutions and coordinate-wise coefficient updates with low computational and storage complexity. For risk minimization in $\mathcal{L}^p$ spaces with $1<p<\infty$, we construct Bregman distances adapted to the uniform convexity of the underlying Banach space using $\max\{2,p\}$-convex functionals. At the $\mathcal{L}^1$ endpoint, we instead construct a locally strongly convex functional based on the entropy function. By developing a new analytical framework, we show that the risk functional values converge to the minimum at a rate of $\mathcal{O}\left(n^{-\min\{\frac12,\frac1p\}}\right)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the misspecified setting, we prove convergence under weaker regularity assumptions and derive explicit polynomial rates under suitable regularity conditions. Finally, we apply the method to statistical inverse problems and illustrate its empirical performance through numerical experiments in both settings.

papers.title: Generalizations of the groups $G_{n}^{k}$: graphs, moduli spaces, algebraic geometry, spherical braids
papers.abstract: In this work, we construct a generalization of the $G_n^k$-theory to the case of an arbitrary hypergraph. The case of spherical braids is considered separately, using the stratification of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_n(S^2)$ and the hypergraph $Γ_n^{\mathrm{sph}}$ encoding projective constraints. In contrast to the original $G_{n}^{k}$ theory, where codimension-one properties are determined by exactly $k$ particles, the present work considers various cases corresponding to strata of codimension~$1$. These groups admit nice maps to free products of cyclic groups. Among unsolved problems, we emphasize the question how the above construction works for abelian varieties and, in particular, for elliptic curves.

papers.title: Dirichlet symbols and the nonlinear wave equation
papers.abstract: We develop the geometry of conformal mappings through Dirichlet operator symbols and the nonlinear wave equation. These symbols, introduced in the work of Hedenmalm and Shimorin (2020), are holomorphic functions on the bidisk associated with contractions on $L^2(\mathbb{D})$. For Grunsky operators, the nonlinear wave equation and the related Riccati equation induce a hierarchy of of differential relations along the diagonal. We use this jet hierachy to obtain alternative coordinates and a characterization of the manifold $Σ/\mathbb{C}$ of normalized exterior univalent functions modulo translations, without an explicit univalence test. This manifold may be viewed as an extension of the universal Teichmüller space beyond the quasicircle boundary setting. The diagonal jets also give rise to a hierarchy of \emph{diagonal series Schwarzian derivatives}. Already the fourth Schwarzian $S_4(ψ)$ leads to differential equations connected with the Weierstrass elliptic $\wp$ function and Painlevé I, revealing a comparison between the geometry of conformal mappings and that of complex tori. As a quantitative application of the framework, we interpret asymptotic variance through the Littlewood-Paley formula as an asymptotic density of quadratic nonlinearity energy under logarithmic averaging. We introduce Schwarzian asymptotic variance and obtain the upper bound $12.566563\ldots$ for its averaged squared hyperbolically normalized amplitude, in comparison with the classical pointwise bound $36$.

papers.title: Kernel Ridge Regression over Hölder Classes: Function and Derivative Losses
papers.abstract: We study ordinary kernel ridge regression over full Hölder-Zygmund balls, measuring errors in Sobolev norms and in pointwise and uniform losses for mixed derivatives. For targets of smoothness $s$, every RKHS norm equivalent to $H^{s+d/2}$ gives the optimal $H^r$ risk for $0\le r<s$; integer choices of $r$ include integrated squared derivative losses. Pointwise and uniform guarantees require additional kernel structure. A localized wavelet kernel attains the sharp derivative rates with the same regularization orders as for function estimation, whereas equivalent changes of the RKHS norm can destroy the population bias rates. For the ordinary Gaussian kernel with a shrinking bandwidth, we prove a uniform derivative risk bound with the optimal polynomial rate and an explicit, unoptimized logarithmic factor. The results allow bounded measurable design densities bounded away from zero and conditionally sub-Gaussian noise.

papers.title: Random unitary circuits with constant spectral gap
papers.abstract: We prove constant lower bounds for the spectral gap of the following random walks on unitary groups $\mathsf{SU}(2^n)$ on $n$ qubits. (i) Random Pauli Rotation: choose an $n$-qubit Pauli operator $P$ and an angle $θ\in [0,2π)$, both uniformly at random, and apply $e^{\mathrm i θP}$. (ii) Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit: choose $n-1$ unitaries $U_{i}$ uniformly at random from $\mathsf{SU}(4)$ (including central phases of the parent group) independently, and apply $U_{2j-1}$ on two qubits $2j-1, 2j$ and then $U_{2j}$ on two qubits $2j, 2j+1$. Importantly, the gap bounds are independent of $n$ and apply for all finite dimensional unitary representations of $\mathsf{SU}(2^n)$ uniformly. Our results immediately imply that the Random Pauli Rotation and Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit converge to approximate unitary $t$-designs after $\mathcal{O}(nt)$ steps. As a consequence, we improve implications for the complexity growth of random unitary circuits as a function of the depth. The existing argument can be applied almost verbatim, but previously the depth had to be $\mathcal{O}(2^{cn})$ for some $c < 1$. Our unconditional constant spectral gap removes this restriction. We prove analogous constant-gap results for orthogonal and Clifford groups; the latter is indispensable for our result on the Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit. The former implies convergence to approximate orthogonal $t$-designs. In this case, the implied mixing time with respect to a constant additive and multiplicative error is optimal (up to an absolute constant factor) for $t=2$.

papers.title: A Geometric Derivation of the Einstein Equations from the Causal Action Principle
papers.abstract: The causal action principle for causal fermion systems is analyzed for a minimizing measure whose support is assumed to have the structure of a smooth manifold $\tilde{M}$. The concept of osculating vacua is introduced. It is shown that the Lagrangian induces on $\tilde{M}$ a Lorentzian metric. Moreover, the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action imply that the Ricci tensor must satisfy the Einstein equations of General Relativity for an energy-momentum tensor given in terms of a power expansion in the regularization length. The gravitational coupling constant is found to be the square of the regularization length. Our methods provide a systematic procedure for deriving corrections to the Einstein equations. The paper includes a self-contained introduction to causal variational principles and the causal action principle. Most geometric structures (connection, Riemannian metric and curvature) are introduced and analyzed in the general setting of causal variational principles for an arbitrary dimension of $\tilde{M}$. The Lorentzian setting works only for causal fermion systems and is worked out only in four spacetime dimensions.

papers.title: Mean Field Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Algorithms for Mean Field Control
papers.abstract: This monograph provides an introduction to mean field reinforcement learning through the lens of Markov decision processes arising from large-population stochastic control with mean field interactions and common noise. Starting from the connection between multi-agent reinforcement learning and mean field control, it develops the probabilistic, mathematical, and control-theoretic framework needed to formulate representative-agent learning problems, analyze their relationship with finite-population systems, and study both general and linear-quadratic models. The presentation includes dynamic programming principles, propagation-of-chaos limits, and theoretical analyses of tabular Q-learning and policy-gradient methods. It also discusses numerical implementations, including tabular schemes and deep reinforcement learning methods such as deep deterministic policy gradient. The goal is to give readers a coherent bridge between mean field control theory and reinforcement learning methodology, emphasizing the mathematical structure of the problems and the design of tractable learning approaches for large stochastic populations.

papers.title: Lumping of reaction networks: Generic and critical parameters
papers.abstract: We investigate linear lumping for parameter-dependent mass action reaction networks, distinguishing between generic and critical parameter regimes. For generic parameters -- those ranging in some non-empty open subset of parameter space -- we prove that exact linear lumping yields only "obvious" reductions: elimination of non-reactant species or projections along stoichiometric first integrals. This characterization extends to reaction networks with product-form kinetics, including Michaelis-Menten and Hill-type rate laws. For mass action systems we proceed to develop an algorithmic approach to identify critical parameter sets -- algebraic subvarieties in parameter space where non-trivial lumpings become available. This procedure reduces the determination of lumping maps to a system of finitely many polynomial equations. It also applies to constrained lumping scenarios (which are frequently motivated by chemical considerations). We then review and extend results about proper lumpings. Finally, we discuss lumpings of a self-replicator system, and of a two-pathway enzyme mechanism, to document the viability of our methods in relevant scenarios. Our results clarify the relationship between structural (parameter-independent) and fine-tuned (parameter-dependent) reductions, with implications for approximate lumping when system parameters lie near critical values

papers.title: Korovkin type theorems for operators acting on functions of polynomial and exponential growth on $[0,\infty)$
papers.abstract: We establish two Korovkin-type approximation theorems for sequences of positive linear operators acting on continuous functions on $[0,\infty)$. The first result shows that pointwise convergence on all polynomial test functions implies pointwise convergence for every function in the domain that is dominated by a polynomial. The second result provides an analogous criterion for functions of exponential growth, where the test functions are the exponentials $e^{λx}$, $λ\in\mathbb{R}$. The results are applied to several classical and modified positive linear operators, including Baskakov, Szász--Mirakjan, Phillips, Post--Widder, Gamma, and Durrmeyer-type operators. Further applications are given to operators associated with modified Bessel functions and hyperbolic functions. The approach provides a unified framework for deriving pointwise convergence on unbounded intervals from convergence on suitable test functions.

papers.title: The Calderón problem for near-Euclidean metrics
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider the anisotropic Calderón problem of determining the potential from boundary measurements of the time-independent Schrödinger equation on compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary. We prove a global uniqueness theorem for small perturbations of the Euclidean metric.

papers.title: The partial data Calderón problem in dimension three
papers.abstract: We consider an inverse boundary value problem for the time-independent Schrödinger equation in dimension three. We prove that the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map defined near a boundary point uniquely determines the potential in a neighborhood of the boundary point in the interior. In particular, we show that the uniqueness question can be reduced to the injectivity of a weighted X-ray transform, which links inverse boundary value problems to integral geometry.

papers.title: Khayyam's Choices of Conics
papers.abstract: In the late eleventh century, Omar Khayyam gave a systematic classification of, and solutions to, cubic equations by means of intersecting conic sections. His work is often retold in modern Cartesian language, where each cubic is reduced to equations of certain curves whose intersection determines solutions in the Cartesian plane. In this paper, we retain the first part of the standard modern treatment of Khayyam: translating his verbal algebra into modern symbolic algebra. But instead of interpreting the resulting equations as curves in a Cartesian plane, we interpret them as Khayyam himself did, as relations between positive geometrical magnitudes represented by conics in the Apollonian sense. On this basis, and using a purpose-designed colour scheme, we reconstruct, in a compact treatment, his solutions to all the cubic equations treated by Khayyam. The reconstruction brings to light a hidden feature of the treatise and draws a sharp line between the geometrization of algebra as practised by Khayyam, on the one hand, and the geometrization of algebra developed by Fermat and Descartes, on the other.

papers.title: Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves: from tents to houses
papers.abstract: One of the classical results of mathematical population genetics states that the frequency of a beneficial mutant's offspring, on its way to fixation in a large population, looks like a logistic curve. A logarithmic scaling (both in height and time) of these selective sweep curves leads (in the case of strong selection) to a tent-like shape in the large population limit: First the logarithmic frequency of the mutant increases linearly from 0 to 1, then that of the former resident decreases from 1 to 0. For moderate selection the logarithmic frequencies develop (in the large population limit) a jump at the beginning/the end of the sweep, which takes the shape of the tent into that of a house. Our main result (proved for the Moran model) assesses the regularity of this convergence in the large population limit: It is uniform in the house's roof (phases of linear growth and decline) and "Skorokhod $M_1$" in the house's walls (closely around the jumps). Apart from interest in its own right, we anticipate that this result and the proof techniques will be instrumental for extending the description of clonal interference by Poissonian interacting trajectories (as it was done in Hermann et al. (2024) for strong selection) also to moderate selection.

papers.title: Muon with Nesterov Momentum: Heavy-Tailed Noise and (Randomized) Inexact Polar Decomposition
papers.abstract: Most first-order optimizers treat matrix-valued parameters as vectors, ignoring the intrinsic geometry of hidden-layer weights in neural networks. Muon addresses this mismatch by updating along the polar factor of a momentum matrix, but its theoretical understanding has lagged behind practice. In particular, practical implementations incorporate Nesterov momentum, compute the polar factor only approximately, and operate with stochastic gradients that may be heavy-tailed. We close this gap by developing a convergence theory for Muon with Nesterov momentum and inexact polar decomposition in non-convex matrix optimization under heavy-tailed noise. Our analysis builds on a unified framework for inexact polar decomposition that captures practical iterative approximations such as Newton-Schulz and quantifies how their errors propagate through the optimization dynamics. Under uniform bounds on polar errors, we establish an optimal iteration and sample complexity of $O \left(\varepsilon^{\frac{-(3α-2)}{(α-1)}} \right)$ for finding an $\varepsilon$-stationary point, where $α\in(1,2]$~denotes the heavy-tail index. For the inexact-polar setting with $σ_1=0$, we also provide guarantees that do not require prior knowledge of $α$. We analyze a randomized low-rank polar decomposition that is substantially more efficient than full-space methods while remaining compatible with our theory. Numerical experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed inexact and randomized~variants.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning with Markov Risk Measures and Multipattern Risk Approximation
papers.abstract: For a risk-averse finite-horizon Markov Decision Process, we introduce a special class of Markov coherent risk measures, called mini-batch measures. We also define the class of multipattern risk-averse problems that reduce to linear MDPs in the risk-neutral case. We use both concepts in a feature-based $Q$-learning method with multipattern $Q$-factor approximation and we prove a high-probability regret bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(d^{3/2}HN^{H-1}\sqrt{K}\big)$, where $d$ is the number of features, $H$ is the horizon, $N\ge2$ is the mini-batch size, $K$ is the number of episodes, and $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}$ hides logarithmic factors. We also propose an economical version of the $Q$-learning method that streamlines the policy evaluation (backward) step. The theoretical results are illustrated on a stochastic assignment problem and a short-horizon multi-armed bandit problem.

papers.title: Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the variational problems associated with the $L^2$-norms of the normal and tangent curvature tensors for submanifolds immersed in a unit sphere. We define the critical points of these functionals under normal variations as Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds, for which we explicitly establish the Euler-Lagrange equations in terms of the second fundamental form. Furthermore, by investigating the focal submanifolds of OT-FKM isoparametric hypersurfaces, we construct infinitely many non-trivial examples of both Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds. Notably, the curvature tensors of these examples generally do not satisfy the classical Yang-Mills equations.

papers.title: A Thin Sheet Volume Integral Equation Solver for Simulation of Bianisotropic Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: A thin-sheet (TS) volume integral equation (VIE) formulation incorporating generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) is presented for the simulation of three-dimensional (3D) bianisotropic metasurfaces. The metasurface is represented as an equivalent thin sheet, with its constitutive tensors derived from the GSTC susceptibility tensors. Invoking the thin-sheet approximation, the governing VIEs are reduced to surface integral equations (SIEs), in which tangential and normal flux density components are treated as distinct sets of unknowns and discretized using Rao-Wilton-Glisson and pulse basis functions, respectively. In contrast to conventional GSTC approaches based on conventional SIEs, which represent only tangential fields, the proposed framework rigorously enforces the bianisotropic GSTCs, including normal field interactions, while retaining the flux-based VIE character of the formulation. Numerical examples, including a comparison with an SIE-GSTC solver that neglects the normal susceptibility components, demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed TS-VIE-GSTC solver for polarization rotation on planar and curved sheets, perfect reflection, beam steering with spatially varying susceptibilities, multi-directional attenuation, and oblique phase-shift transformation.

papers.title: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
papers.abstract: Let \(Λ\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(Λ^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\), without imposing finiteness conditions on \(Λ^!\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_λ)\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, thereby closing a gap left open in the work of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

papers.title: Wave number dynamics in the real and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the large-scale dynamics of the one-dimensional real and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations using a scalar equation for the local wave number derived by a Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) expansion. For the real equation, the reduction has a conserved gradient structure. With higher-order regularization, we obtain families of exact stationary solutions and show that all nonuniform steady states are linearly unstable. These include localized holes distinct from the classical Langer-Ambegaokar hole. In the Eckhaus-unstable regime, the reduced equation develops finite-time singularities associated with phase slips. We derive a universal self-similar description of this process, with parameter-independent scaling exponents in good agreement with direct numerical simulations. The similarity profile satisfies a nonlinear fourth-order boundary-value problem admitting multiple numerically identified solutions. For the complex equation with nearly real coefficients, an additional Burgers-type nonlinearity produces wave steepening and traveling shocks connecting plane waves of different wave numbers. We derive the shock profile exactly and show numerically that the full complex Ginzburg-Landau equation converges to this prediction in the appropriate asymptotic limit. Outside this regime, the wave number profile becomes nonmonotonic, as explained in terms of spatial dynamics. These shocks differ qualitatively from classical Nozaki-Bekki solutions. The reduced equation thus unifies stationary holes, self-similar collapse toward phase slips, and propagating shocks within a common description of pattern-forming systems.

papers.title: A Linear Temporal Logic of Frequencies on Series of Events
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LTLFS, a linear temporal logic for reasoning about frequencies in finite series of probabilistic events. The logic conservatively extends linear temporal logic over finite traces with measure-sensitive operators that compare the empirical distribution observed at any point in a series with an independently specified target distribution. Its semantics integrates the actual sequence of events, the probability distribution governing individual outcomes, and the set of finite assignments compatible with the target frequency. This supports two complementary tasks: verifying whether an observed partial distribution is compatible with the benchmark, and predicting whether and with what probability the completed series can still satisfy it. The language can express observed and attainable frequencies, the probability of realizing a desired final distribution, and conditional probabilities for subsequent outcomes under the assumption that the benchmark is met. We establish formal properties of the operators and characterize their interaction with the temporal structure. A running example concerning representational fairness in sequential outputs from a generative AI system illustrates how the framework can distinguish temporary deviations from irrecoverable violations and support early, logically interpretable intervention. LTLFS thereby provides a symbolic foundation for runtime monitoring of evolving quantitative requirements, with applications to explainable and responsible AI.

papers.title: Galois representation of the product of two Drinfeld modules of generic characteristic
papers.abstract: We study the adelic Galois representations attached to products of two Drinfeld modules of generic characteristic. As a function-field analogue of Serre's open image theorem for products of elliptic curves, we show that the image of the joint adelic representation is commensurable with the subgroup defined by the natural determinant compatibility conditions if and only if at least one of the two Drinfeld modules has potential complex multiplication, or the two modules are not geometrically isogenous up to any Frobenius twist. Our proof combines Pink's theory of minimal quasi-models, explicit reciprocity laws from global class field theory, and an analysis of residual Galois representations. As an arithmetic application, we prove a torsion finiteness result: if one of the Drinfeld modules has no potential complex multiplication and the two are not geometrically isogenous up to any Frobenius twist, then that Drinfeld module has only finitely many torsion points over the compositum of the maximal abelian extension of the base field and the torsion field of the other module. This is an analogue of the classical results of Ribet and Zarhin for abelian varieties.

papers.title: On a stable partnership problem with integer choice functions
papers.abstract: We consider a far generalization of the well-known stable roommates and non-bipartite stable allocation problems. In its setting, one is given a finite non-bipartite graph $G=(V,E)$ with nonnegative integer edge capacities $b(e)\in{\mathbb Z}_+$, $e\in E$, in which for each vertex (``agent'') $v\in V$, the preferences on the set $E_v$ of its incident edges are given via a choice function $C_v$ acting on the vectors in ${\mathbb Z}_+^{E_v}$ bounded by the capacities and obeying the standard axioms of substitutability and size monotonicity. We refer to the related stability problem as the stable partnership problem with integer choice functions, or SPPIC for short. Extending well-known results for particular cases, we give a solvability criterion for SPPIC and develop an algorithm of finding a stable solution, called a stable partnership, or establishing that there is none. Moreover, in general the algorithm constructs a pair $(x,{\cal K})$ such that $x\in {\mathbb Z}_+^E$ and ${\cal K}$ is a set of pairwise edge-disjoint odd cycles in $G$ satisfying the following properties: if ${\cal K}=\emptyset$, then $x$ is a stable partnership, whereas if ${\cal K}$ is nonempty, then a stable partnership does not exist, and in this case, the set ${\cal K}$ is determined canonically. Our constructions essentially use earlier author's results on the corresponding bipartite counterpart of SPPIC. Keywords: stable marriage problem, stable roommates problem, stable partition, stable allocation, choice function

papers.title: Residual Recombination Methods as Anderson-like Acceleration: An Algebraic Interpretation of BoostConv
papers.abstract: BoostConv has been introduced in earlier works as an effective acceleration technique for nonlinear iterative processes and has been successfully employed in a variety of applications to enhance convergence rates or to compute unstable fixed points that are otherwise inaccessible through standard approaches. Despite its demonstrated practical effectiveness, the theoretical properties of the method have not yet been fully characterized. In this work, we present a more robust formulation of the BoostConv algorithm and, for the first time, provide a rigorous proof of its local convergence. The proposed analysis places BoostConv within a precise mathematical framework, clarifying its interpretation as a nonlinear convergence accelerator and establishing sufficient conditions under which convergence to a fixed point is guaranteed. The theoretical findings are illustrated through several numerical examples, spanning from a linear problem to a low-dimensional benchmark and a large-scale incompressible Navier-Stokes simulation. These results demonstrate the robustness and practical relevance of the proposed method and bridge the gap between empirical performance and rigorous analysis, paving the way for further developments and applications to complex nonlinear problems.

papers.title: Fixed-Point Delayed Subgradient Methods for Nonsmooth Convex Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the nonsmooth convex optimization problems over the fixed point constraint sets of firmly nonexpansive operators. To find an optimal solution of the problem, we present an iterative method based on the hybrid steepest descent method and the idea of a delayed subgradient scheme in which allows the use of staled subgradients from the earlier iteration when updating the next iteration. We start the convergence part by deriving an upper bound for the difference of the best-achieved function values and the optimal value. After that, to ensure the convergence in iterations, we prove that there exists a subsequence of the generated sequence by the proposed method which converges to an optimal solution. Moreover, we subsequently show that the whole generated sequence converges to an optimal solution when the strict convexity of the objective function is imposed. Further, we extend the presented results to the inexact version and the centralized network system consisting of a finite number of workers and a central server. Finally, we apply the proposed method to image inpainting problems. The numerical results describe the effect of delay in many cases of objective functions.

papers.title: Discrete Gaussian Free Field via Hadamard's formula
papers.abstract: We establish a discrete Hadamard variational formula for Green operators on weighted graphs along an increasing family of subgraphs. The increment of the Green operator factors through harmonic extension from the newly added layer and the positive square root of its boundary Green operator. This gives a dimension-free decomposition of the Green kernel and an associated isometric Hadamard operator. As an application, the discrete Gaussian free field is constructed by successively adding independent harmonically extended Gaussian contributions. The formulation uses only the graph structure and its conductances, without smoothness assumptions. For nested square-lattice approximations of smooth planar domains, we also prove convergence of the growing fields in finite-dimensional distributions and convergence of the integrated Hadamard increments as Green-operator forms.

papers.title: Convexity of Radial Mean Bodies via an Extension of Ball's Bodies
papers.abstract: In this work, we extend a classical theorem of Keith Ball on integrals of log-concave functions along rays against the weight $r^{p-1}$ to the previously inaccessible regime $p\in (-1,0)$: if $g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+$ is an integrable, upper semi-continuous, log-concave function which attains its maximum at the origin and has the origin in the interior of its support, then \[ x\mapsto \left(\frac{p}{g(o)}\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{p-1}(g(rx)-g(o))\mathrm{d}\,r\right)^{-\frac{1}{p}} \] is a gauge on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Our approach also provides a new proof of the original regime $p> 0$. The argument is based on a reduction to a two-dimensional inequality derived from Prékopa's theorem, which may be of independent interest. As a consequence of this extension, we resolve a nearly 30-year-old question of Richard Gardner and Gaoyong Zhang in the affirmative. In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_p K$ of a convex body $K\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ for $p>-1$. Furthermore, they established that $R_p K$ is convex for $p\geq 0$, but the convexity of $R_p K$ for $p\in (-1,0)$ remained open. We prove that $R_p K$ is convex for all $p>-1$.

papers.title: On problems of Erdős and Baumann-Briggs on minimising the density of $s$-cliques in graphs with forbidden subgraphs
papers.abstract: Using flag algebras, we prove that the minimum density of $8$-cliques in a large graph without an independent set of size $3$ is $491411/268435456+o(1)$, thus resolving a new case of an old problem of Erdős [Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. 7 (1962) 459-464]. Also, we establish some other results of this type; for example, we show that the minimum $s$-clique density in a large graph with no independent set of size 3 nor an induced 5-cycle is $2^{1-s}+o(1)$ when $s=4,5,6$. For each of these results, we also describe the structure of all extremal and almost extremal graphs of large order $n$. These results are applied to give an asymptotic solution to a number of cases of the problem of Baumann and Briggs [Electron. J. Combin. 32 (2025) P1.22] which asks for the minimum number of $s$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph in which every $k$-set spans a $t$-clique.

papers.title: An assortment of problems in permutation patterns: unimodality, equivalence, derangements, and sorting
papers.abstract: We collect open problems in permutation patterns on four themes: rank-unimodality in the permutation pattern poset and log-convexity of principal classes, Wilf-equivalence and shape-Wilf-equivalence, the enumeration of derangements in permutation classes, and sorting by stacks in series, generalized stacks, and restricted containers (C-machines).

papers.title: On Fujita's conjecture for a general hyperkähler manifold in the standard series of examples
papers.abstract: For the moduli spaces $\mathcal{V}(K3)_{d,t}^n$ and $\mathcal{V}(\text{Kum})_{d,t}^n$ of polarized hyperkähler manifolds of $\text{Hilb}^n(K3)$-type and $\text{Kum}^n$-type respectively, with polarization with square $2d$ and divisibility $t$, we study general base point freeness and very ampleness of the polarization. We provide conditions, in terms of $n, d, t$ that guarantee that the general polarization, in any connected component of these moduli spaces, to be base point free or very ample.

papers.title: Base Change Of Fundamental Group Schemes
papers.abstract: Let $K/k$ be a field extension, $X$ a connected quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over $k$ with a rational point $x$, $p:X_K\to X$ the natural projection, $\mathcal{C}_X$ and $\mathcal{C}_{X_K}$ the Tannakian categories whose objects consist of vector bundles on $X$ and $X_K$ respectively. We give criteria for the natural homomorphism $π(\mathcal C_{X_K},x_K)\toπ(\mathcal C_X,x)_K$ to be an isomorphism. Suppose further $X$ is geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$. As applications, we prove base change isomorphisms for $π^{\acute{e}t},π^{E\acute{e}t}$ under arbitrary extensions and for $π^S,π^N,π^{EN}$ under arbitrary algebraic extensions; a cuspidal cubic curve example shows that it can fail for purely transcendental extensions. In positive characteristic, base change isomorphism holds for $π^{Loc}$ and $π^{ELoc}$ under separable algebraic extensions; an elliptic curve example shows that it can fail for finite purely inseparable extensions.

papers.title: Taylor-Accelerated Neural Network Interpolation Operators on Irregular Grids: Higher-Order Approximation and Derivative-Informed Field Reconstruction
papers.abstract: In this paper, a new class of Taylor-accelerated neural-network interpolation operators is introduced for quasi-uniform, irregularly distributed grids to reconstruct derivative-informed physical fields in both univariate and multivariate settings. The framework incorporates Taylor expansions within the neural network operators framework, allowing operators to efficiently utilize the smoothness of the target function. We determine the analytical properties of the proposed operators, including well-posedness, uniform boundedness, and exact interpolation at the sampling nodes. Additionally, we establish polynomial reproduction to a specified degree and provide Jackson-type error estimates based on higher-order moduli of smoothness, thereby improving convergence rates on quasi-uniform, irregular grids. The applicability of the method is demonstrated by reconstructing physical fields such as temperature, electromagnetic fields, and fluid properties, including pressure and velocity. The numerical results show that the proposed operators provide reliable, accurate estimates in the presence of noise and irregular sampling. The enhanced accuracy of the proposed method is validated by comparing it with current interpolation systems on irregular grids, including Lagrange-type methods.

papers.title: Normalized solutions for a critical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg equation: the effect of the weights on the coupling range
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions of $-\mathrm{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) = λ|x|^{-2a}u + β|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u + |x|^{-b2^\sharp}|u|^{2^\sharp-2}u$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx = ρ^2$, where $0 < a < \frac{N-2}{2}$, $a < b < a+1$, $2 < q < 2^\sharp$, and $2^\sharp$ is the critical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg exponent. Let $q_c$ denote the mass-critical exponent. For $2 < q < q_c$ and small $β> 0$, we obtain two positive radial solutions: a local minimizer with negative energy and a solution of mountain-pass type. For $q_c \le q < 2^\sharp$, there is a number $β_0 \ge 0$, defined through the energy level below which compactness holds, such that a positive radial ground state exists for every $β> β_0$. In the mass-critical case $q = q_c$, this holds for $β_0 < β< β^*$, where $β^*$ is explicit, and for $β\ge β^*$ the ground state level is zero and is not attained. Our main result is a necessary and sufficient condition on $N$, $a$, $b$ and $q$ for $β_0 > 0$. The condition holds only when $a$ is close to $\frac{N-2}{2}$, and it fails in the formal unweighted limit $a = b = 0$. When $β_0 > 0$, the ground state level is not attained for $0 < β< β_0$, and every normalized solution has energy above the compactness level. When $β_0 = 0$, we describe the behavior of ground states as $β\to 0$. The proofs combine the Pohozaev constraint, sharp estimates for the extremals of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, and a blow-up analysis in Emden-Fowler variables.

papers.title: On noncontinuous bisymmetric strictly monotone operations
papers.abstract: We construct bisymmetric, partially strictly increasing binary operations on real intervals which are not continuous. This shows that continuity cannot be removed from the classical characterization of bisymmetric quasi-sums due to Aczél and Dhombres. Our examples are operations of the form \[ F(x,y)=f^{-1}(αf(x)+βf(y)), \] where $α,β>0$ and $α+β\neq1$. The generating map $f$ is chosen as a strictly increasing bijection from an interval onto a two-component subset of $\mathbb{R}$ separated by a gap. The range is directly invariant under the relevant weighted sums, while the gap produces a jump of $f$ and hence discontinuity of every one-variable section. As a consequence, we obtain discontinuous associative and strictly increasing operations on intervals, and we extend the construction to the multivariate case. In the opposite direction, we prove that if a symmetric bisymmetric strictly increasing operation is reflexive at two points of an interval, then it is automatically continuous on the segment between them and coincides there with a quasi-arithmetic mean.

papers.title: On the dimension drop for harmonic measure on uniformly non-flat Ahlfors-David regular boundaries
papers.abstract: We extend earlier results of Azzam on the dimension drop of the harmonic measure for a domain $Ω\subset \R^{n}$ with $n\geq 3$, with dimensional Ahlfors regular boundary $\partialΩ$ of dimension $s$ with $n-1-δ_0 \leq s\leq n-1$, that is uniformly non flat. Here $δ_0$ is a small positive constant dependent on the parameters of the problem. Our novel construction relies on elementary geometric and potential theoretic considerations. We avoid the use of Riesz transforms and compactness arguments, and also give quantitative bounds on the $δ_0$ parameter.

papers.title: Low-Dimensional Adaptation of Rectified Flow: A Diffusion and Stochastic Localization Perspective
papers.abstract: In recent years, Rectified flow (RF) has gained considerable popularity largely due to its generation efficiency and state-of-the-art performance. In this paper, we investigate how well RF automatically adapts to the intrinsic low dimensionality of the support of the target distribution to accelerate sampling. We show that, using a carefully designed \blue{end-point adapted} time-discretization scheme and with sufficiently accurate drift estimates, the RF sampler enjoys an iteration complexity of order $O(k/\varepsilon)$ (up to log factors), where $\varepsilon$ is the precision in total variation distance and $k$ is the intrinsic dimension of the target distribution. In addition, we show that the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) procedure is equivalent to a stochastic version of RF by establishing a novel connection between these processes and stochastic localization. Building on this connection, we further design a stochastic RF sampler that also adapts to the low-dimensionality of the target distribution under mild requirements on the accuracy of the drift estimates, and also with a specific time schedule. We illustrate the efficacy of newly designed time-discretization schedules with simulations on the synthetic data and text-to-image (T2I) data experiments.

papers.title: Inverse Iterations for Phase-Invariant Nonlinear Eigenvalue Problems
papers.abstract: We study the local convergence of nonlinear inverse iterations for eigenvalue problems arising from variational energies that are invariant under global phase rotations. This symmetry introduces an inherent degeneracy of the target eigenvalue, preventing the direct application of existing convergence results that require a simple eigenvalue. Within an abstract variational framework, we investigate a shifted Jacobian-based inverse iteration, known as the J-method, and establish its local convergence to quasi-isolated ground states. Our analysis shows that the target eigenvalue of the J-operator has algebraic and geometric multiplicity exactly two. By introducing an auxiliary iteration that fixes the global phase, we prove local linear convergence of the iterates modulo phase rotations and derive sharp convergence rates in terms of the spectrum of the J-operator. In particular, these rates can be improved through spectral shifting. We apply the abstract theory to a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation that models spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates, verify the relevant structural assumptions and numerically examine the quasi-isolation of the computed ground states. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the shifted J-method, particularly in regimes with slowly converging conventional inverse iterations.

papers.title: Finite-sample Valid Permutation Inference under Multi-way Clustering
papers.abstract: Econometric applications with multi-way clustering often feature a small number of effective clusters or heavy-tailed data, making standard cluster-robust and bootstrap inference unreliable in finite samples. In this paper, we develop a framework for finite-sample valid permutation inference in linear regression with multi-way clustering under an assumption of conditional exchangeability of the errors. Our assumption is closely related to the notion of separate exchangeability studied in earlier work, but can be more realistic in many economic settings as it imposes minimal restrictions on the covariate distribution. We construct permutation tests of significance that are valid in finite samples and establish theoretical power guarantees, in contrast to existing methods that are justified only asymptotically. While our main presentation is under exchangeable errors, our framework encompasses invariance-based tests that remain valid under general forms of heteroskedastic errors. We also extend our methodology to settings with missing data and derive power results that reveal phase transitions in detectability. Through simulation studies, we demonstrate that the proposed tests maintain correct size and competitive power, while standard cluster-robust and bootstrap procedures can exhibit substantial size distortions.

papers.title: Derivation of a nonlinear, history-dependent tissue-level current law for an electropermeabilization model via homogenization
papers.abstract: We study a phenomenological electropermeabilization model in a periodic medium representing biological tissue. Starting from a cell-level model describing the electric potential and the degree of poration, we perform dimensional analysis to identify a relevant scaling in terms of a small parameter $\varepsilon$ - the ratio between the cell and the tissue size. The electric potential satisfies electrostatic equations in the extra- and intracellular domains, while its jump across the cell membrane evolves according to a nonlinear law coupled with an ordinary differential equation for the poration degree. We prove the well-posedness of the microscopic problem, derive a priori estimates, obtain formal asymptotics, and rigorously justify the expansion by combining two-scale convergence with monotonicity arguments. The resulting macroscopic model exhibits memory effects and a nonlinear, time-dependent effective current. It captures the nontrivial evolution of effective conductivity, including a characteristic drop reflecting the capacitive behavior of the lipid bilayer, in agreement with experimental data. Numerical computations of the effective conductivity confirm that, although the intracellular and extracellular bulk conductivities are constant, tissue conductivity varies nonlinearly with electric field strength, showing a sigmoid trend.

papers.title: Totient-based Identities for Integer Pairs with Equal Divisor Sums
papers.abstract: A pair of integers is called amicable if each number equals the sum of the proper divisors of the other. In this paper, we investigate a broader class of integer pairs $(A, B)$ that satisfy the weaker condition $σ(A) = σ(B)$, where $σ$ is the sum-of-divisors function. We focus on pairs whose greatest common divisor is a power of two and analyze their distinct prime factorizations. Specifically, we consider configurations of the forms $(A=2^n ab,\ B=2^n cd)$, $(A=2^n abc,\ B=2^n de)$, and $(A=2^n abc,\ B=2^n def)$, where the factors are odd primes. For each configuration, we derive explicit symmetric identities that must be satisfied. These identities relate the odd prime factors of $A$ and $B$ to the quantity $\varphi(A)+\varphi(B)$, where $\varphi$ denotes Euler's totient function. As a consequence, these relations provide necessary structural constraints for amicable pairs of these specific forms, while also revealing an underlying algebraic symmetry for any pair with equal divisor sums.

papers.title: Pathwise uniqueness by noise for singular stochastic PDEs
papers.abstract: Uniqueness for stochastic PDEs with drift in differential form is a main open problem in the recent literature on regularisation by noise. This paper establishes a self-contained theory in the framework of stochastic evolution equations on separable Hilbert spaces and provides a first result to address such an issue, in the direction of both pathwise and weak uniqueness, as well as continuous dependence on the initial data. The singularity of the drift allows to achieve novel uniqueness results for several classes of examples, ranging from fluid-dynamics to phase-separation models.

papers.title: Groupoid graded rings and their categories of graded modules
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a groupoid acting on a set $X$ and let $R$ be a $G$-graded ring with graded local units. We study the main properties of the category $gr-(R,G,X)$ of $X$-graded $R$-modules and adjoint functors between categories of this kind. We characterize the latter in terms of tensor-like and hom-like functors. As an application we obtain a characterization of equivalences between such categories in the spirit of Morita theory. Then we introduce restriction and induction functors between categories of type $gr-(R,G,X)$ and show that many functors between such categories can be realized naturally as a restriction or induction functor. This includes the forgetful functor, the functor associating a $G$ graded $R$-module with the $H$-graded module formed by the sum of the homogeneous components of degree in subgroupoid $H$, and the one associating it with the collapsing of homogeneous components in cosets modulo $H$ for $H$ a wide subgrupoid. We characterize when a restriction or induction functor is an equivalence of categories. Finally, we prove that $gr-(R,G,X)$ is always equivalent to the category of modules over a ring with local units and, generalizing a result of Menini and Năstăsescu, we characterize when $gr-(R,G,X)$ is equivalent to the category of modules over a unital ring.

papers.title: Convergence rate of empirical measures in the subspace robust Wasserstein distance
papers.abstract: We obtain an estimate for the expected subspace robust 2-Wasserstein distance between any probability measure with a finite q-th moment (q>2) defined on a separable Hilbert space, and its empirical distribution from $n$ i.i.d. samples.

papers.title: Structural and Spectral Properties of Strictly Interval Graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper we deal with a subclass of chordal graphs, which are simultaneously strictly chordal and interval, the strictly interval graphs. We present a new characterization of the class that leads to a simple linear recognition algorithm. Next we introduce a new subclass of strictly interval graphs, the $SI$-core graphs, that are non-split and non-cograph graphs and show that several elements of the new class are Laplacian integral

papers.title: $k$-path graphs: experiments and conjectures about algebraic connectivity and $α$-index
papers.abstract: This work presents conjectures about eigenvalues of matrices associated with $k$-path graphs, the algebraic connectivity, defined as the second smallest eigenvalue of the Laplacian matrix, and the $α$-index, as the largest eigenvalue of the $A_α$-matrix. For this purpose, a process based on [Discrete Applied Mathematics 164 (2014) 297-303] is presented to generate lists of $k$-path graphs containing all non-isomorphic 2-paths, 3-paths, and 4-paths of order $n$, for $6 \leq n \leq 26, 8 \leq n \leq 19$, and $10 \leq n \leq 18$, respectively. Using these lists, exhaustive searches for extremal graphs of fixed order for the mentioned eigenvalues were performed. Based on the empirical results, conjectures are suggested about the structure of extremal $k$-path graphs for these eigenvalues.

papers.title: Morita Rigidity for Kleene Algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce Morita equivalence to the study of Kleene algebras and modules. Classical characterizations of Morita-equivalent semirings such as having equivalent categories of modules and one semiring being a full idempotent corner of a finite matrix semiring over the other transfer easily to this new context. We also observe that Morita equivalence can be applied to extending and restricting scalars in Lindenbaum--Tarski algebras of propositional dynamic logics, and that an appropriately-defined category of generalized finite automata satisfies the property that when the underlying Kleene algebras are Morita equivalent then the corresponding categories of generalized automata are equivalent. But the signature results which we obtain relate to rigidity of Kleene algebras in this context. Specifically, every semiring that is Morita-equivalent to the semiring reduct of a Kleene algebra has a unique expansion to a Kleene algebra, and semiring bimodules witnessing Morita-equivalence of semirings which are reducts of Kleene algebras are already Kleene bimodules.

papers.title: Wave packet decompositions and sharp bilinear estimates for rough Hamiltonian flows
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to prove bilinear $L^p$ estimates for rough dispersive evolutions satisfying non-degeneracy and transversality assumptions. The estimates generalize the sharp Fourier extension estimates for the cone and the paraboloid. We obtain the sharp dependence on transversality and sharp up to endpoints $L^p$ range. To this end, we combine an axiomatic induction-on-scales with the construction of a wave packet parametrix for dispersive equations with $C^{1,1}$-coefficients by using the FBI transform.

papers.title: The Derived Auslander--Iyama Correspondence II: Bimodule Calabi--Yau Structures
papers.abstract: Let $d$ be a positive integer. In a previous article we established a bijective correspondence between the following classes of objects, considered up to the appropriate notion of equivalence: differential graded algebras (dg) with finite-dimensional $0$-th cohomology such that the canonical generator of their perfect derived category is a basic $d\ZZ$-cluster tilting object, and basic Frobenius algebras that are twisted $(d+2)$-periodic as bimodules. In this article, we prove a variant of our general correspondence for bimodule right Calabi--Yau dg algebras. A novel ingredient is a new cohomology theory which contains obstructions to the existence and uniqueness of minimal $A_\infty$-bimodule structures on a graded bimodule. As an application of our results, we obtain, to our knowledge, the first example of an algebraic triangulated category with a triangulated Calabi--Yau structure that cannot be lifted to a bimodule right Calabi--Yau structure on any of its dg enhancements.

papers.title: Genericity of ergodic measures on non-positively curved manifolds with flat strips
papers.abstract: We study the geodesic flow defined on the unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold with non-positive curvature. In the case of surfaces, Coudène and Schapira proved that the existence of a flat strip prevents the set of ergodic measures from being generic in the space of invariant probability measures. We show the existence of a three-dimensional manifold that contains an embedded flat torus and where ergodicity is a generic property. More generally, Coudène and Schapira proved that ergodicity is a generic property within the space of invariant probability measures defined on $Ω_{NF}$, the set of non-wandering vectors whose orbits do not bound a flat strip. We introduce a larger set $\mathcal{R}_w$ where the same property holds, and we illustrate the extent of our findings using a famous example of a rank-one manifold attributed to Gromov.

papers.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
papers.abstract: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.

papers.title: Radial Epiderivative Based Fritz John and KKT Conditions in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: In this study, we examine Fritz John (FJ) and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) type optimality conditions for a class of nonsmooth and nonconvex optimization problems with inequality constraints, where the objective and constraint functions all are assumed to be radially epidifferentiable. The concept of the radial epiderivative constitutes a distinct generalization of classical derivative notions, as it replaces the conventional limit operation with an infimum-based construction. This formulation permits the analysis of directional behavior without invoking standard neighborhood-based assumptions and constructions commonly required in generalized differentiation. This leads to one of the key advantages of the radial epiderivative which lies in its applicability even to discrete domains, where classical and generalized derivatives are often inapplicable or undefined. The other advantage of this concept is that it provides a possibility to inverstigate KKT conditions for global minimums. Consequently, this approach necessitates a reformulation of fundamental analytical tools such as gradient vectors, feasible direction sets, constraint qualifications and other concepts which are central to the derivation of optimality conditions in smooth optimization theory. The primary contribution of this paper is the development of a comprehensive theoretical framework for KKT conditions tailored to the radially epidifferentiable setting. We introduce novel definitions of the radial gradient vector, of the set of feasible directions, and examine how classical constraint qualifications may be interpreted and extended within this new framework.

papers.title: Homotopy lifting, asymptotic homomorphisms, and traces
papers.abstract: The following homotopy lifting theorem is proved: Let $φ, ψ: B \to D/I$ be homotopic $\ast$-homomorphisms and suppose $ψ$ lifts to a (discrete) asymptotic homomorphism. Then $φ$ lifts to a (discrete) asymptotic homomorphism. Moreover the whole homotopy lifts. \noindent We also prove a completely positive version of this theorem and a version where $φ$ is replaced by an asymptotic homomorphism. These are the first homotopy lifting theorems that hold for all separable C*-algebras. We obtain a lifting characterization of several important properties of C*-algebras and use them together with our homotopy lifting theorems to get the following applications: MF-property is homotopy invariant; If either $A$ or $B$ is exact, $A$ is homotopy dominated by $B$ and all amenable traces on $B$ are quasidiagonal, then all amenable traces on $A$ are quasidiagonal; If a C*-algebra $A$ is homotopy dominated by a nuclear C*-algebra $B$ and all (hyperlinear) traces on $B$ are MF, then all hyperlinear traces on $A$ are MF. Some of the extension groups introduced by Manuilov and Thomsen coincide. The C*-algebra $qA$ from Cuntz's picture of KK-theory is always quasidiagonal. Every homotopy symmetric C*-algebra is MF.

papers.title: Scalar and Mean Curvature Comparison on Compact Cylinder
papers.abstract: Let $ X $ be a closed, oriented Riemannian manifold. Denote by $ (M = X \times I = X \times [0, 1], \partial M = X \times \lbrace 0 \rbrace \cup X \times \lbrace 1 \rbrace, g) $ a compact cylinder with smooth boundary, $ \dim M \geqslant 3 $. In this article, we address the following question: If $ g $ is a Riemannian metric having (i) positive scalar curvature (PSC metric) on $ M $ and nonnegative mean curvature on $ \partial M $; and (ii) $ χ(X) = 0 $ and $ \dim X \geq 5 $, then there exists a PSC metric on $ X $. This generalizes a result of Gromov and Lawson for $ X = \mathbb{T}^{n} $. Our result also implies an infinite band width consequence complementary to Gromov's band width conjecture, which roughly says no additional obstruction or flexibility for the existence of PSC on $ X $ is gained by passing to $ X \times [0, 1] $. Our result relies on geometric PDE analysis with respect to a new conformal invariance---the $ g $-angle condition between normal vector field along $ \partial M $ and the global vector field tangential to the $ I $-direction.

papers.title: Pontryagin-Weiss classes and a rational decomposition of spaces of homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We construct a rational homotopy pullback decomposition for variants of the classifying space of the group of homeomorphisms for a large class of manifolds. This has various applications, including a rational section of the stabilisation map ${\rm Top}(d)\rightarrow {\rm Top}$ of the space of homeomorphisms of ${\bf R}^d$ for $d\ge 6$, or a new method to construct topological bundles and detect characteristic classes thereof. Some steps in the proofs may be of independent interest, such as the construction of a nullhomotopy of the twice-iterated stabilisation map for the space of orientation-preserving derived automorphisms of the rational $E_d$-operad, results on recovering boundaries of manifolds from their interior in the context of embedding calculus, or a treatment of tensor products of truncated $\infty$-operads.

papers.title: From semi-total to equitable total colorings, and their induced partitions into perfect and total perfect codes
papers.abstract: Independently posed by Behzad and Vizing, the Total Coloring Conjecture asserts that the total chromatic number $χ''(G)$ of a connected simple graph $G$ is either $Δ(G)+1$ or $Δ(G)+2$, where $Δ(G)$ is the largest degree of a vertex of $G$. Deciding whether a cubic graph $G$ has $χ''(G)=Δ(G)+1$, even if $G$ is bipartite, is NP-hard. The problem persists even for equitable total colorings. Williams and Holroyd gave a condition for total colorings via the introduction of semi-total colorings. In the present work, focus is set mainly on obtaining, by means of a variation of Kempe's 1879 graph-coloring algorithm, equitable total colorings out of semi-total colorings of: symmetric cubic graphs (3-cube, Petersen, Heawood, Pappus, Desargues, etc., graphs) and cage graphs (Robertson graph, etc.) Moreover, total colorings of the 3-cube and subsequent $4k$-polygon prisms ($k>1$) are shown to exist that have perfect codes as their vertex color classes, as well as semi-total colorings of Möbius ladders that have total-perfect codes as their vertex color classes, only $K_{3,3}$ of which equitable. In addition, a semi-total coloring of the 90-vertex Foster graph is shown to have a vertex color class being a total-perfect code. On the other hand, a semi-total coloring of the 42-vertex $(5,6)$-cage yields a decomposition into 3 copies of the Heawood graph, by the edges of same color endvertices, and 7 6-cycles. Among other cases, non-equitable total colorings of cubic graph expansions are taken to equitable semi-total colorings.

papers.title: Horizontality of partially hyperbolic foliations
papers.abstract: We show exactly which Seifert manifolds support partially hyperbolic dynamical systems. In particular, a circle bundle over a higher-genus surface supports a partially hyperbolic system if and only if it supports an Anosov flow. We also show for these systems that the center-stable and center-unstable foliations can be isotoped so that their leaves are transverse to the circle fibering. As a consequence, every partially hyperbolic system defined on the unit tangent bundle of a higher-genus surface is a collapsed Anosov flow.

papers.title: Black holes in the Dynnikov Coordinate Plane
papers.abstract: This work gives an application of Dynnikov coordinates in geometric group theory. We present a new approach to the study of subgroups of the mapping class group of a disc with $3$ marked points, $\mathbb{D}_3$, using Dynnikov coordinates.

papers.title: Structures preserved by primitive actions of $S_ω$
papers.abstract: We present a dichotomy for structures $A$ that are preserved by primitive actions of $S_ω = \text{Sym}({\mathbb N})$: such a structure primitively positively constructs all finite structures and the constraint satisfaction problem is NP-complete, or the constraint satisfaction problem for $A$ is in P. To prove our result, we study the first-order reducts of the Johnson graph $J(k)$, for $k \geq 2$, whose automorphism group $G$ equals the action of $\text{Sym}({\mathbb N})$ on the set $V$ of $k$-element subsets of $\mathbb N$. We use the fact that $J(k)$ has a finitely bounded homogeneous Ramsey expansion and that $G$ is a maximal closed subgroup of $\text{Sym}(V)$.

papers.title: Second order regularity of solutions of elliptic equations in divergence form with Sobolev coefficients
papers.abstract:
We give $L^p$ estimates for the second derivatives of weak solutions to the Dirichlet problem for equation $\operatorname{div}(\mathbf{A}
abla u) = f$ in $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with Sobolev coefficients. In particular, for $f\in L^2(Ω)  igcap L^s(Ω)$ $$\|Δu\|_{2} \leq  egin{cases} c_1\|f\|_2 + c_2 \|
abla \mathbf{A}\|_q^2\|f\|_s, & 	ext{if } 1 < s < d/2,  rac{1}{2}= rac{2}{q}+  rac{1}{s} -  rac{2}{d}\ c_1\|f\|_2 + c_2 \|
abla \mathbf{A}\|_4^2\|f\|_s, & 	ext{if } s > d/2 \end{cases}.$$

papers.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
papers.abstract: Cellular automata find applications in cryptography, error correction, theoretical computer science, and the simulation of physical and biological processes. We say that a Boolean function is a proper lifting if its induced cellular automaton is reversible. This paper introduces new classes of proper liftings, constructed through compositions of landscape functions, and explores their cryptographic potential by computing indicators relevant to differential and linear cryptanalysis. We combine theoretical and computational methods to obtain a complete classification of proper liftings for diameters up to $6$. Several open problems and conjectures are posed along the way.

papers.title: Sliced Wasserstein Geodesics and Equivalence Wasserstein and Sliced Wasserstein metrics
papers.abstract: This paper will introduce a family of sliced Wasserstein geodesics which are not standard Wasserstein geodesics, objects yet to be discovered in the literature.
