These objects exhibit how the geometric structure of the Sliced Wasserstein space differs from the Wasserstein space, and provides a simple example of how solving the barycenter and gradient flow problems change when moving between these metrics. Some of these geodesics will only be Hölder continuous with respect to the Wasserstein metric and thus will provide a direct proof that Sliced-Wasserstein and regular Wasserstein metrics are not equivalent. Previous proofs of this were done for various cases in [2] and [5]. This paper, not only provides a direct proof, but also fills in gaps showing these metrics not equivalent in dimensions greater than 2.

papers.title: Effective eigenvalue approximation from moments for self-adjoint trace-class operators
papers.abstract: Spectral properties of bounded linear operators play a crucial role in several areas of mathematics and physics. For each self-adjoint, trace-class operator $O$ we define a set $Λ_n\subset \mathbb{R}$, and we show that it converges to the spectrum of $O$ in the Hausdorff metric under mild conditions. Our set $Λ_n$ only depends on the first $n$ moments of $O$. We show that it can be effectively calculated for physically relevant operators, and it approximates the spectrum well without diagonalization. We prove that using the above method we can converge to the minimal and maximal eigenvalues with super-exponential speed. We also construct monotone increasing lower bounds $q_n$ for the minimal eigenvalue (or decreasing upper bounds for the maximal eigenvalue). This sequence only depends on the moments of $O$ and a concrete upper estimate of its $1$-norm; we also demonstrate that $q_n$ can be effectively calculated for a large class of physically relevant operators. This rigorous lower bound $q_n$ tends to the minimal eigenvalue with super-exponential speed provided that $O$ is not positive semidefinite. As a by-product, we obtain computable upper bounds for the $1$-norm of $O$, too. Numerical examples demonstrate the relevance of our approximation in estimating entropy and negativity, which is useful, among others, in quantum optical and in open quantum system models. The results can be directly applicable to problems in quantum information, statistical mechanics, and quantum thermodynamics, where using traditional techniques based on diagonalization is impractical.

papers.title: Veronese sections and interlacing matrices of polynomials and formal power series
papers.abstract: The concept of a fully interlacing matrix of formal power series with real coefficients is introduced. This concept extends and strengthens that of an interlacing sequence of real-rooted polynomials with nonnegative coefficients, in the special case of row and column matrices. The fully interlacing property is shown to be preserved under matrix products, flips across the reverse diagonal and Veronese sections of the power series involved. These results and their corollaries generalize, unify and simplify several results which have previously appeared in the literature. An application to the theory of uniform triangulations of simplicial complexes is included.

papers.title: Theoretical Guarantees for the Subspace-Constrained Tyler's Estimator
papers.abstract: We study the subspace-constrained Tyler's estimator (STE) for recovering a low-dimensional linear subspace from data contaminated by outliers. Under deterministic conditions on inlier spread and outlier alignment, we prove linear convergence to the true subspace from a sufficiently accurate initialization. The guarantee also applies when the dimension-scaled signal-to-noise ratio is below one, where general robust subspace recovery is SSE-hard. When initializing STE from a candidate subspace, we provide a sufficient recovery condition based on the initial angular error and the size of the identity shift applied to the subspace projector. For noisy inliers, we prove a subspace error proportional to the noise level within an explicit iteration bound. Finally, under an asymptotic, anisotropic Gaussian inlier--outlier model, we show that Tyler's M-estimator (TME) provides a successful STE initialization even when TME's own leading eigenspace differs from the target subspace.

papers.title: Large N instantons, BPS states, and the replica limit
papers.abstract: We study the relation between large N instantons and conventional instantons, focusing on matrix models and topological strings. We show that the resurgent properties of the perturbative series at fixed but arbitrary N, including the replica limit N = 0, can be obtained from large N instantons. In the case of topological strings, it has been conjectured that the resurgent structure encoded by large N instantons is closely related to the spectrum of BPS states. We give direct evidence for this connection in the case of Seiberg-Witten theory and other topological string models, and we show in detail how the resurgent properties at fixed N follow from the large N theory, and therefore can be used to obtain information on BPS invariants.

papers.title: Interval Replacements of Persistence Modules
papers.abstract: Persistence modules indexed by finite posets arise in topological data analysis. Unlike in the one-parameter case, they need not decompose into interval modules. Interval replacements approximate them by formal differences of interval decomposable modules. Extending earlier work on 2D-grids, we study these replacements for arbitrary compression systems. Different choices can give different interval rank invariants and replacements, including those related to interval resolutions on commutative ladders. Our main results are an explicit formula for interval ranks and an essential-cover theorem. Using Auslander--Reiten theory, we express interval ranks in terms of ranks of matrices formed from the structure maps of the module. The essential-cover theorem recovers each interval rank from a suitable restriction of the module. The replacement construction preserves the corresponding interval rank invariant, which recovers the usual rank invariant on segments. Essential covers also give a sufficient condition for two compression systems to yield the same invariant. For total compression, the invariant coincides with the generalized rank invariant of Kim and Mémoli. On 2D-grids, essential covers recover the zigzag formula of Dey, Kim, and Mémoli for this invariant.

papers.title: Kähler Solitons, Contact Structures, and Isoparametric Functions
papers.abstract: Many known examples of simply-connected gradient Kähler-Ricci solitons in real dimension four are toric, and the symmetry is intrinsically related to the potential function $f$ and the scalar curvature $\SS$. In this article, we consider the case that $f$ and $\SS$ are functionally dependent and deduce a complete classification, while the independence case is addressed elsewhere. The main theorem recovers all known examples of cohomogeneity one symmetry. We also discover a connection to the theory of isoparametric functions and contact geometry. Indeed, a key ingredient is a new characterization for a deformed Sasakian structure generalizing a classical result.

papers.title: Optimal Control of Stationary Doubly Diffusive Flows in Bounded Lipschitz Domains: Analysis and Numerical Approximation
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the control constrained distributed optimal control of a stationary doubly diffusive flow model. For the control problem, we use a well-posedness analysis based on minimal assumptions on data and domain. We show the existence of an optimal control with quadratic type cost functional, study the Fréchet differentiability properties of the control-to-state map and establish the first-order necessary optimality conditions corresponding to the optimal control problem. Expanding on this we prove the local optimality of a reference control using second-order sufficient optimality condition for the control problem. Then, following the \textit{optimize-then-discretize} approach, we propose a fully non-conforming, locally exactly divergence-free discretization of the control problem based on the lowest order $(\texttt{CR}_0, \mathbb{P}_0)$ finite element spaces for the state and adjoint variables, and explicit and implicit discretizations for the control variable. Optimal \textit{a priori} error estimates are established for the state, adjoint and control variables in suitable norms up to the regularity of the solution. Finally, the optimal control is computed using a primal-dual active set strategy as a semi-smooth Newton method and numerical experiments are performed to validate the theoretical findings, and it's applicability to optimal control of thermal and solutal convection in a porous medium.

papers.title: Learning Decision-Focused Uncertainty Sets in Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a data-driven technique to automatically learn tractable contextual uncertainty sets in robust optimization, for a family of problems with both objective and constraint uncertainty. This decision-focused method reshapes the uncertainty sets by optimizing for both worst-case and average-case performance while guaranteeing constraint satisfaction with high probability via a conditional value-at-risk constraint. We solve the resultant constrained learning problem using a stochastic augmented Lagrangian method that relies on differentiating the solutions of the robust optimization problems with respect to the parameters of the uncertainty set. Due to the nonsmooth and nonconvex nature of the augmented Lagrangian function, we apply the nonsmooth conservative implicit function theorem to establish that, under regularity and boundedness assumptions, the accumulation points of the resulting algorithm are feasible solutions of the constrained learning problem when the penalty parameters remain bounded, and stationary points of the constraint violation otherwise. Using a covering argument with Hoeffding's inequality, we show both marginal and conditional finite-sample probabilistic guarantees of constraint satisfaction for any approximately feasible solution. We also characterize when a decision-focused set is worth learning. In the proposed settings, numerical experiments show that our method outperforms traditional approaches in data-driven robust optimization in terms of out-of-sample performance.

papers.title: Complements of discriminants of real singularities of type $X_{10}$
papers.abstract: Conjecturally complete lists of connected components of the complements of the discriminant varieties (aka wave fronts) of smooth function singularities of types $X_{10}^3$ and $X_{10}^1$ are provided. The combinatorial invariants of these components are defined and calculated. It is shown that the one-dimensional homology group of the complement of the discriminant of any versal deformation of any singularity of class $X_{10}^1$ contains a subgroup isomorphic to $\Z^3$.

papers.title: Affine and cyclic affine equivalence of rotation-symmetric S-boxes
papers.abstract: A rotation-symmetric S-box on $n$ bits is a vectorial Boolean function that commutes with the right cyclic shift and is therefore determined by a single Boolean function. The map $χ$ used in Keccak is a well-known example. Ordinary affine equivalence allows arbitrary invertible affine transformations, which need not preserve rotation symmetry. We introduce \emph{cyclic affine equivalence}, in which the implementing transformations each have an invertible $k$-circulant linear part with $\gcd(k,n)=1$ and a translation vector fixed by the shift. For $n\ge3$, the two relations give the same classes of rotation-symmetric permutations exactly when $n$ is an odd prime for which $2$ is a primitive root. In every other dimension $n\ge3$, explicit constructions exhibit affine classes containing several cyclic affine classes. We derive exact class-size formulas, count cyclic affine classes for $3\le n\le9$, and classify a four-bit family of $χ$-siblings under both relations. Finally, we characterize when a permutation is affinely equivalent to a rotation-symmetric one and apply the criterion to the Ascon S-box.

papers.title: On the Bounds of Stopping and Cycle Numbers in the Collatz Process
papers.abstract: We study the stopping time and cycle structure of the normalized Collatz iteration using a binary sequence formalism. By introducing a recursive rooted sequence tree by Winkler (2017), we establish a bijection between admissible binary sequences and integers $m \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$, showing that every such integer arises uniquely in this construction. Within this framework, we derive sharp lower and upper bounds for the weighted digit-sum $\sum_{i=1}^{r} 3^{r-i} 2^{\mathbf{1}(i)-1}$, namely \[ 3^r - 2^r \;\leq\; \sum_{i=1}^{r} 3^{r-i}\, 2^{\mathbf{1}(i)-1} \;\leq\; r \cdot 3^{r-1}, \] the upper bound being strictly tighter than the bound $s \cdot 3^r$ previously established by Luca (2005). These bounds yield corresponding sharp bounds on any hypothetical cycle number $m_c$, and imply that the ratio $F_q(m)/m$ satisfies \[ 1 - \varepsilon_1 \;<\; \frac{F_q(m)}{m} \;<\; 1 + \varepsilon_2, \] with $F_q(m)/m \to 1$ as $r \to \infty$, while the ratio $3^r/2^s$ approaches but never reaches $1$ for any finite admissible sequence. We further show that the ratio of the maximum to minimum summation satisfies $α(r) \sim r/3$ as $r \to \infty$, providing a theoretical basis for the empirically observed scaling $α\approx \max(r)/3$. Together, these results imply that any nontrivial cycle number, if one exists, must grow without bound and satisfy increasingly stringent arithmetic constraints, consistent with all known computational and theoretical bounds on the Collatz conjecture.

papers.title: The model theory of the curve graph
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop a bridge between model theory, geometric topology, and geometric group theory. In particular, we investigate the Ivanov Metaconjecture from the point of view of model theory, and more broadly we seek to answer the general question: why does the curve graph of a surface play such a central role in the study of surfaces and mapping class groups? More specifically, we consider a surface $Σ$ of finite type and its curve graph $\mathcal C(Σ)$, and we investigate its first-order theory in the language of graph theory. Crucially, $\mathcal C(Σ)$ is bi-interpretable with a certain object called the augmented Cayley graph of the mapping class group of the surface. We use this bi-interpretation to prove that the theory of the curve graph is $ω$--stable, to compute its Morley rank, and to show that it has quantifier elimination with respect to the class of $\forall\exists$--formulae. We also show that many of the complexes which are naturally associated to a surface are interpretable in $\mathcal C(Σ)$. This shows that these complexes are all $ω$--stable and admit certain a priori bounds on their Morley ranks. We are able to use Morley ranks to prove that various complexes are not bi--interpretable with the curve graph. As a consequence of quantifier elimination, we show that algebraic intersection number is not definable in the first order theory of the curve graph. Finally, we prove that the curve graph of a surface enjoys a novel phenomenon that we call interpretation rigidity. That is, if surfaces $Σ_1$ and $Σ_2$ admits curve graphs that are mutually interpretable, then $Σ_1$ and $Σ_2$ are homeomorphic to each other. Along the way, numerous technical results are obtained.

papers.title: An inverse theorem for Freiman multi-homomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $G_1, \dots, G_k$ and $H$ be vector spaces over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$ of prime order. Let $A \subset G_1 \times\dots\times G_k$ be a set of size $δ|G_1| \cdots |G_k|$. Let a map $φ\colon A \to H$ be a multi-homomorphism, meaning that for each direction $d \in [k]$, and each element $(x_1, \dots, x_{d-1}, x_{d+1}, \dots, x_k)$ of $G_1\times\dots\times G_{d-1}\times G_{d+1}\times \dots\times G_k$, the map that sends each $y_d$ such that $(x_1, \dots,$ $x_{d-1},$ $y_d,$ $x_{d+1}, \dots,$ $x_k) \in A$ to $φ(x_1, \dots,$ $x_{d-1},$ $y_d,$ $x_{d+1}, \dots,$ $x_k)$ is a Freiman homomorphism (of order 2). In this paper, we prove that for each such map, there is a multiaffine map $Φ\colon G_1 \times\dots\times G_k \to H$ such that $φ= Φ$ on a set of density $\Big(\exp^{(O_k(1))}(O_{k,p}(δ^{-1}))\Big)^{-1}$, where $\exp^{(t)}$ denotes the $t$-fold exponential. Applications of this theorem include: $\bullet$ a quantitative inverse theorem for approximate polynomials mapping $G$ to $H$, for finite-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector spaces $G$ and $H$, in the high-characteristic case, $\bullet$ a quantitative inverse theorem for uniformity norms over finite fields in the high-characteristic case, and $\bullet$ a quantitative structure theorem for dense subsets of $G_1 \times\dots\times G_k$ that are subspaces in the principal directions (without additional characteristic assumptions).

papers.title: Intersection theory on derived stacks
papers.abstract: We define integral cycle complexes and Chow homology of derived Artin stacks. To any quasi-smooth family of derived Artin stacks we associate a bivariant fundamental class, encoding the virtual fundamental classes of its fibres and their deformation invariance up to coherent homotopy. We extend the Riemann-Roch theorem of Baum-Fulton-MacPherson from quasi-projective schemes to derived Artin stacks, and thereby obtain a virtual Riemann-Roch formula for quasi-smooth derived Artin stacks. As another application of the formalism, we construct intersection products on regular Artin stacks locally of finite type over a field. Finally, we prove an integral comparison of our Chow homology with the cycle-theoretic Chow groups of Kresch.

papers.title: $q$-Bernstein functions and applications
papers.abstract: We characterize q-Bernstein functions by exponential tests and, on a geometric lattice, by a well-defined spectral q-Laplace convolution semigroup. We also establish results on q-completely monotonic, q-log-completely monotonic, and q-Bernstein functions and give applications to q-gamma functions.

papers.title: Gromov hyperbolicity and uniformity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first exhibit an example which answers negatively to a question posed by Herron et al. in 2008. That is, there is a rectifiably connected open set in a proper geodesic metric space so that it is Gromov hyperbolic with respect to the quasihyperbolic metric, and its Gromov boundary endowed with a visual metric is naturally bilipschitz equivalent to its metric boundary, but it is not uniform. Moreover, two positive answers are given under additional hypotheses. It is shown that a metric space is uniform if and only if it is Gromov hyperbolic and the natural map between its Gromov closure and its metric completion exists and satisfies a relatively quasisymmetric condition. Both bounded and unbounded cases are in our considerations via two different uniformization theorems developed recently by Bonk et al. and the first author, respectively. Finally, we characterize uniform metric spaces with uniformly perfect boundaries in terms of Gromov hyperbolicity and Teichmüller's displacement property.

papers.title: How Does One Cut a 30-60-90 Triangle?
papers.abstract: We enumerate dissections of a 30-60-90 triangle into smaller triangles similar to itself, counting unlabeled arrangements up to similarity and reflection. There are 18 four-piece, 121 five-piece, and 844 six-piece arrangements, corresponding to 11, 47, and 235 distinct multisets of piece areas. We present illustrated catalogs organized by these area multisets and distinguish layouts obtained by subdivision and local rotations or reflections from independent layouts. A separately implemented computational search reproduces every arrangement up to nine pieces, finding 460404 arrangements. Counts through nine pieces for five other classes of triangles are included for comparison.

papers.title: Hyperrigidity and convexity in two variables
papers.abstract: We extend Brown's one-variable rigidity theorem to strictly convex functions of two variables under a regularity assumption. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let $f$ be real-valued, strictly convex on $K$, and of class $C^2$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. We prove that the generating set $\{x_1,x_2,f\}$ is hyperrigid in $C(K)$.

papers.title: Equational theories of min-plus semirings
papers.abstract: We study the equational theory and subvarieties of the variety $\mathcal V$ generated by $(\mathbb N_0,\min,+)$. We prove that a subvariety of $\mathcal V$ is proper if and only if it is locally finite, equivalently, if and only if it satisfies a power-stabilization identity. Every finite member generates a hereditarily finitely based variety with a finite subvariety lattice. In contrast, the periodic subvarieties defined by $x^m=x^{m+1}$ are nonfinitely based for $m\geq2$. We construct a strictly descending chain of nonfinitely based subvarieties and three varieties generated by explicit reduced products, each with a decidable equational theory. The smallest is a limit variety: it is nonfinitely based, and every proper subvariety has an absolute finite identity basis. The subvariety lattice of $\mathcal V$ has cardinality continuum. In fact, the interval between the first reduced-product variety and the subvariety defined by $x^2=x^3$ already has this cardinality, and all its members are nonfinitely based. We also give a hereditarily finitely based example with an infinite subvariety lattice. The constructions use finite convex models and recognition quotients.

papers.title: Grid triples, link cobordisms in $\CPbar$ and the computation of Heegaard-Floer TQFT
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial description of the Heegaard--Floer link-cobordism maps associated with pointed triple grid diagrams in the complement of three $4$-balls in complex projective plane with reverse orientation. Every contributing index-zero holomorphic triangle decomposes into Euclidean triangular sheets. We characterize the compatible collections of sheets that contribute by an explicit geometric separation criterion, expressed as a lattice-point test, and prove that each has mod-\(2\) count one. Individual sheets may wrap around the torus in the unblocked theory, whereas they are embedded in the blocked theory. In each fixed \(\SpinC\) structure, the map is determined by a finite enumeration. A difference number computed from the triangular regions determines the \(\SpinC\) structure of a Whitney triangle. Together with the topology of the associated surface, this gives an explicit formula for the absolute bigrading of each summand of the cobordism map. After basepoint reduction, the formula determines the Laurent monomial representing any nonzero map on the rank-one torsion-free two-variable knot Floer modules, yielding vanishing and ideal-containment criteria. We apply the construction to an affine family of grid links \(K(n;p,s)\), obtaining explicit cobordisms involving infinite families of torus knots and links, together with closed formulas for the bigradings of their distinguished grid states.

papers.title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum. We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_σ\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $σ\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.

papers.title: An Introduction to Financial Derivatives: Open Lecture Notes
papers.abstract: These lecture notes give a broad introduction to financial derivatives at the level of a Masters program in quantitative finance. Topics include forward and futures contracts, no-arbitrage bounds and put-call parity, the binomial model, the fundamental theorems of asset pricing, Brownian motion and Itô calculus, the Black-Scholes model, the Greeks, variance swaps, local and stochastic volatility models including Heston, and static hedging of barrier options. Each chapter ends with exercises, and complete solutions, including Python code for the computational exercises, are provided in an appendix. The notes are open source: the LaTeX source is available at https://github.com/mattlorig/intro-financial-derivatives, and readers are invited to submit corrections and additions.

papers.title: Lehmer's number is not an orientable stretch factor in genus six
papers.abstract: Let $λ_L \approx 1.17628$ be Lehmer's number. We prove that no pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus six with orientable invariant foliations has stretch factor $λ_L$. This gives a negative answer to a question of Lanneau and Thiffeault on the minimal stretch factor in even genus. As a consequence, the minimal stretch factor $δ_6^{+}$ of such maps is the largest root of $x^{12}-x^{9}-x^{7}+x^{6}-x^{5}-x^{3}+1$, approximately $1.20189$. The proof combines the Lefschetz method of Lanneau and Thiffeault, the standardly embedded train tracks of Hironaka and Tsang, an elementary analysis of the transition digraph, and an obstruction from periodic conjugacy classes in the fundamental group.

papers.title: Stochastic Euler Products in the Paley-Wiener Space
papers.abstract: General sufficient conditions, in terms of stochastic Euler products, are given for a realization of a point process to have finite excess or finite deficiency in the Paley-Wiener space.

papers.title: Graceful supertrees with at most $2m-\mathrm{diam}(T)$ edges
papers.abstract: A graceful labeling of a tree with $m$ edges is a bijection from its vertices to $\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$ whose edge differences are pairwise distinct. The Graceful Tree Conjecture asserts that every tree admits such a labeling; equivalently, the smallest graceful tree containing a given $m$-edge tree has $m$ edges. For this embedding problem, Sethuraman, Ragukumar and Slater proved that fewer than $4m$ edges suffice, while Sethuraman and Ragukumar observed that in practice fewer than $2m$ appear to suffice. We prove the latter bound for every tree. For any root of height $h$ with $t_h$ vertices at maximum distance, we construct a graceful tree containing the original tree with exactly $M=2m-h-t_h+1$ edges; in particular, $2m-\operatorname{diam}(T)$ edges suffice. The construction completes a cyclic reflection of van Bussel's level labeling without increasing its span; each original edge difference $d$ is replaced by $M+1-d$. Unused vertex labels and missing edge differences are indexed by the same intermediate-level positions, allowing an explicit attachment rule that preserves the tree property. The best root for this construction is computable in linear time. Because every graceful supertree labeling restricts to a range-relaxed labeling, a uniform supertree bound of $(2-\varepsilon)m+O(1)$ would imply such a range-relaxed bound for all trees.

papers.title: Threshold existence for random NAE-$k$-SAT and random hypergraph $2$-colourability
papers.abstract: The existence of limiting threshold densities for random hypergraph $2$-colourability and random NAE-$k$-SAT was conjectured in earlier work, including Achlioptas and Moore [RANDOM 2002] and Coja-Oghlan and Panagiotou [STOC 2012]. We prove these conjectures for all $k\geq 3$. We also show that $α^{\mathrm{2-col}}_k \leq α^{\mathrm{NAE}}_k$ for each $k\geq 3$.

papers.title: Heat flow and the fundamental solution of the Baouendi-Grushin operator
papers.abstract: For the Baouendi-Grushin operator $\mathscr L_γ= Δ_x + |x|^{2γ}Δ_y$ in $\R^{m+k}$, with $γ>0$, we prove that the time integral of the heat kernel with pole at the origin equals $C_{γ,Q}\, N_γ^{2-Q}$, where $N_γ$ is the gauge and $Q$ the homogeneous dimension. When $γ\not=1$ no closed form of the heat kernel is known. After a partial Fourier transform in $y$, the time integral of the heat kernel becomes the Green function of an anharmonic oscillator, which solves a generalized modified Bessel equation, and the gauge appears when the inverse Fourier transform is computed as a Hankel transform. In particular, the heat flow provides a new proof that $C_{γ,Q}\, N_γ^{2-Q}$ is a fundamental solution of $-\mathscr L_γ$ with pole at the origin.

papers.title: Optimal Certified Multiple Testing with E-values
papers.abstract: We study randomized multiple testing with e-values under arbitrary dependence and introduce a conditional certification constraint: Given the observed evidence, each coordinate's expected rejection certificate must not exceed its e-value. Existing randomized e-BH improvements satisfy this constraint but have no established optimality guarantee. We prove that the maximum conditional inclusion probability for hypothesis $i$, given e-values~$x$, is $1 \wedge (α/ K) \sum_j \min(x_i, x_j)$, and construct one rule attaining these bounds simultaneously. The rule uses a single independent uniform variable, rejects a prefix of the ordered e-values, and has a unique conditional rejection-set law among rules attaining all the bounds. It therefore maximizes every nonnegative weighted sum of inclusion probabilities, including expected true discoveries under any truth configuration. Under a shared uniform draw, its rejection set contains those of e-BH and U-eBH. The construction extends to BY-calibrated p-values, and simulations under positive and negative dependence show power gains over existing randomized procedures.

papers.title: The sharp Stein-Tomas inequality on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove that constant functions are global maximizers for the endpoint Stein--Tomas inequality on $\mathbb{S}^1$, thereby determining its sharp constant. By the known characterization of the phases of maximizers, every nonzero maximizer then has the form $f(ω)=c e^{ix_0\cdotω}$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: Optimal lengths of commutators of idempotents and similarity of nilpotent operators to their negatives
papers.abstract: Let $\HH$ be a complex separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We prove that every operator in $\BH$ is a sum of three commutators of idempotents and a product of two such commutators. Both numbers are best possible. The same is true for differences of idempotents, for operators similar to their negatives, and for operators anticommuting with an involution. Each of these four classes therefore has additive length three and multiplicative length two. We also construct nilpotent operators of order three that are similar to their negatives but cannot be conjugated to their negatives by any bounded involution. These results answer Question~7.22(a)--(c), the question in Remark~7.17, and the question about involutions in Section~2.9 of Marcoux, Radjavi and Zhang, \emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{284} (2023), 109854.

papers.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schrödinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-ηp_n})$, where $η>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.

papers.title: Accelerating posterior sampling in Bayesian inverse problems with diffusion models: an online-offline perspective
papers.abstract: Bayesian inverse problems require both informative prior models and computationally feasible posterior inference. Score-based diffusion models provide expressive learned priors, but their use for inversion introduces a conditioning problem: the score of a noised posterior is generally unavailable from a prior score alone. This selective survey reviews the principal approaches to that problem, including likelihood guidance, spectral and projection methods, sequential Monte Carlo corrections, and amortized conditional training. We organize methods by how they split cost between offline preparation and online inference, and compare their assumptions, advantages and limitations, with emphasis on computational speedups. Some ongoing directions and open questions are gathered at the end.

papers.title: Similarity cancellation and primitive operator roots
papers.abstract: Kaplansky's second test problem for similarity asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$ for bounded operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We answer this question in the negative, even for compact operators whose singular values satisfy any prescribed positive upper bounds tending to zero. We also show that cancellation can fail under the stronger hypothesis $J_2(T)\sim J_2(S)$ considered by Marcoux, Radjavi, Troscheit, and Zhang \cite{MRTZ}. For these operators, finite amplifications and primitive roots are similar exactly at even multiplicities and even orders, respectively. In contrast, cancellation in fixed matrix size admits a uniform bound on the condition number. This extends the finite type~$I$ results of Jiang, Ma, Shi, and Zhang \cite{JMSZ}. The bound also holds for simultaneous similarity of arbitrary families of matrices and can be chosen to tend to one as the amplified bound tends to one. We conclude that, in a finite type~$I$ von Neumann algebra, cancellation of doubles and cancellation of primitive square roots are each equivalent to boundedness of the orders of its nonzero homogeneous summands.

papers.title: Counterexamples to uniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform under quadratic decay
papers.abstract: We show nonuniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform on $\mathbb Z^2$ under quadratic decay. We construct an explicit nonzero function in $\ell^1(\mathbb Z^2)$ with pointwise decay $O(|z|^{-2})$ whose sums over integer lines vanish. We also obtain an infinite-dimensional null space with the same decay assumption. Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.

papers.title: Contact multiplicity and a sharp six-map bound for collinear self-similar dendrites
papers.abstract: Let $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the attractor of $n\ge2$ similarities $z\mapstoλz+b_k$, $0<|λ|<1$, whose fixed points are evenly spaced on a line, and suppose that $K$ does not lie in a line. We prove that $K$ can be a dendrite only if $n\le6$, and that such dendrites exist for every $2\le n\le6$; no separation or finite-intersection hypothesis is imposed. Hence, for $n\ge7$, every connected $K$ of this kind has interior points or separates the plane. Neighboring pieces of $K$ meet in similar copies of a single contact set. In a dendrite exactly one first-level piece meets this set, whereas for $n\ge7$ at least $n-\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil\ge2$ do, a bound attained by explicit quadratic parameters. The proof combines a planar translation obstruction for replicated contact arcs with an estimate based on Jensen's formula. After normalizing to $z\mapsto t+z/c$, $t\in\{-n+1,-n+3,\ldots,n-1\}$, the connectedness locus is the closure, outside the unit disk, of the roots of monic integer polynomials of height at most $n-1$. The same estimate shows that, for $n\ge7$, every such polynomial with a non-real root $c$ satisfying $|c|^2\ge\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil+1$ has subleading coefficient of absolute value at most $\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$, and that this bound is sharp. Accordingly, for $n\ge7$, at every non-real boundary point $c$ of the locus with $|c|>1$, each expansion $c=\sum_{j\ge0}d_jc^{-j}$ with integer digits $|d_j|\le n-1$ has $|d_0|\le\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$.

papers.title: Minimax estimation of linear functionals in the Darcy inverse problem
papers.abstract: We study estimation of linear functionals $\int fψ$ of the conductivity $f$ in the Darcy problem $\nabla\cdot(f\nabla u)=g$ from observations of $u$ in Gaussian white noise of level $N^{-1/2}$. When the potential has a single nondegenerate minimum, we determine the minimax rates over Sobolev balls in the linearised experiment. Unless a compatibility condition along the gradient flow holds, the rate is governed by an effective dimension $T$ of the Hessian at the minimum, not by the ambient dimension: it is $N^{-(2s+T)/(4s+8)}$ for $T<4$, has an elbow at $T=4$ with an extra logarithmic factor, and is parametric for $T>4$. In the nonlinear experiment we show that these lower bounds persist when compatibility fails at the reference and $T\le4$, and we prove the minimax rate on classes with isotropic critical Hessians, and the parametric rate near references with $T>4$. In dimension at most four, no nonzero linear functional is uniformly $\sqrt N$-estimable on a Sobolev neighbourhood of the constant conductivity, even when it is regular there.

papers.title: Sharp Critical Rates for Locally Private Distribution Estimation
papers.abstract: We determine sharp minimax rates for distribution estimation under pure local differential privacy at critical query smoothness. For the integral probability metric generated by the unit ball of $B^d_{2,q}$, $1\le q\le\infty$, over fixed periodic Sobolev density balls with positive smoothness and interior slack at the uniform density, the expected risk is of order $N^{-1/2}(\log N)^{3/2-1/q}$, where $N=n\varepsilon^2$; expected squared risk has the squared order. The fine index governs aggregation across resolutions that share one private information budget. A single noninteractive release with a measurable proper density output attains these rates, and matching lower bounds allow finite public blackboard interaction and repeated participation under each user's total privacy budget. A known $L^2$ radius permits the same rates without using density smoothness, with output in the $L^2$ density ball. Separately, for positive smooth densities on $[0,1]$, integrated squared CDF risk has minimax order $(\log N)^2/N$, with sharp quantile, Wasserstein, and transport map consequences. The rates hold uniformly for $0<\varepsilon\le1$ as $N\to\infty$, with class parameters fixed.

papers.title: Small-LCM Distinct Covering Systems via Segmented Local Search
papers.abstract: We construct distinct covering systems with minimum moduli 8, 9, 10, 11 and least common multiples 20160, 75600, 302400, 3326400, respectively, and conjecture that these values are minimal. For minimum modulus 8, the exclusion computations leave only 10080 and 15120 unresolved below our construction. The constructions use segmented local search: moduli are introduced in increasing blocks, followed by joint reoptimization of selected blocks. We give complete residue lists and an independent integer-arithmetic verifier. Two computational studies, comprising 180 initial runs and 130 follow-up runs, compare initialization orders, revisit rules and seed-bank capacities under fixed scan limits.

papers.title: The Prodigal Elephant Returns: Last-Return Laws in the Superdiffusive Regime
papers.abstract: Let $(S_n)$ be the one-dimensional elephant random walk with memory parameter $p\in(3/4,1)$ and first-step probability $q=\mathbb{P}(S_1=1)\in[0,1]$. Set $a=2p-1$, and let $f_{q,a}$ denote the density of the almost-sure limit of $S_n/n^a$. We prove that the last return time $T_0=\sup\{m\geq0:S_m=0\}$ satisfies: $\mathbb{P}(T_0\geq n)\sim f_{q,a}(0)\sqrt{\frac{8}{π(2a-1)}}n^{-(a-1/2)}$. Reflection gives $f_{q,a}(0)=f_{1,a}(0)$, so the constant is independent of $q$. For future walks started from admissible states $(n,x_n)$ with $x_n/\sqrt n\to z$, we establish functional convergence of the centered martingale-normalized paths to a time-changed Brownian motion. Uniform control of late hitting times then gives the eventual-return kernel $2Φ(-\sqrt{2a-1}|z|)$, uniformly on bounded scaled windows, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The same last-visit asymptotic holds uniformly for nonempty deterministic targets $F_n\subseteq[-r_n,r_n]\cap\mathbb{Z}$, $r_n=o(\sqrt n)$, held fixed during each trajectory. Conditionally on $T_0\geq n$, we identify the joint limit of $S_n/\sqrt n$, the next return divided by $n$, and the last return divided by the next return. The last ratio converges to $A^{-1/(2a-1)}$, independently of the other two limiting coordinates, where $A$ has the arcsine distribution on $(0,1)$.

papers.title: Artinian reduction applied to the Largest Intersection Problem
papers.abstract: Suppose we have $r$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^m$ of degree $d$, whose defining polynomials are linearly independent and whose intersection is zero-dimensional. What is the maximum number of points in their intersection? This problem is motivated by computing the generalized Hamming weights of projective Reed-Muller codes, and a conjectured formula for this maximum was given in [21]. We prove the conjectured formula for arbitrary $m$ when $\binom{m+d}{d}-\binom{d+2}{2}<r\leq\binom{m+d}{d}$. We use the notion of Artinian reduction to reformulate the problem in terms of graded Artinian algebras and then apply combinatorial tools to bound their Hilbert functions.

papers.title: Mixed-Integer Programming for Causal Discovery with Unknown Hard-Intervention Targets
papers.abstract: When intervention targets are uncertain, learning causal relationships and identifying directly perturbed variables become a joint task. We develop an exact mixed-integer program based on optimized parent-set scores (PS-MIP) for joint graph and intervention-target estimation in linear Gaussian structural equation models under stochastic hard interventions. The method can incorporate candidate-edge restrictions and partial target knowledge when available. For each random variable, PS-MIP evaluates candidate sets of direct causes, or parent sets, by optimizing the likelihood parameters and compatible target patterns, retaining both the score and a minimizing target pattern. A global mixed-integer program then selects parent sets subject to acyclicity. Under stated conditions, this reduction preserves the joint objective and reconstructs the graph, targets, and likelihood parameters. Because the local scores are precomputed, PS-MIP replaces a direct large bilinear mixed-integer program with a linear selection problem; empirically it certifies global optimality on far more instances than the direct formulation (126 of 180 versus 34) and is often orders of magnitude faster. On synthetic data, PS-MIP achieves favorable false-discovery--true-discovery trade-offs relative to several benchmark algorithms for causal discovery with unknown intervention targets, along with strong intervention-target recovery in denser settings. An exploratory study on real data from a controlled physical system further demonstrates recovery beyond simulation.

papers.title: Singular Perturbations for Control Systems Safety
papers.abstract: Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) offer a powerful theory for enforcing safety in dynamical systems. Yet, applying this framework to complex systems is challenging when subsystems are feedback-interconnected and operate at different timescales. Such structures arise naturally in multiphysics systems and in control architectures where physical plants interact with optimization, estimation, and control algorithms. In many of these settings, safety involves only part of the system, motivating the design of reduced-order certificates. Inspired by singular perturbation theory, we establish sufficient conditions, involving separation between slow and fast dynamics, under which a reduced-order safety certificate can be lifted to the full interconnected system. Specifically, we construct a composite CBF ensuring forward invariance of a lifted subset of the original safe set. We also show that the certified safe set expands monotonically as the tuning parameter accelerating the fast dynamics is reduced. Numerical results validate the approach on two robotic systems: a planar 2-DoF manipulator with motor dynamics and a 6-DoF UR10e manipulator controlled by a suboptimal optimization algorithm.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop
papers.abstract: We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman reconstruction. In the second, we obtain a closed-form evaluation of the generating series from which the conjecture follows. For $n=3$, the resulting closed formula establishes a special case of a Gopakumar-Vafa-type conjecture for Calabi-Yau fivefolds.

papers.title: Clique counts under degree and matching constraints
papers.abstract: We study the maximum number of $t$-cliques in graphs with maximum degree at most $D$ and matching number at most $M$, with no restriction on the number of vertices. For $t\ge 3$, we determine this maximum whenever $D\ge 2M-1$ and characterize all extremal graphs when the maximum is positive. Up to isolated vertices, these are complete or complete split graphs for $D\ge 2M$, while $K_{2M}$ is uniquely extremal when $D=2M-1$. We also derive a general upper bound from the Chvátal-Hanson edge theorem and refine it for even $D$. For fixed even $D$ and $3\le t\le D+1$, every extremal graph consists, apart from isolated vertices, of copies of $K_{D+1}$ together with a remainder whose order is bounded independently of $M$. When $D/2$ divides $M$, this remainder is empty and the extremal graph is unique. This structure yields an eventual recurrence, reducing the determination of all extremal values and graphs to finitely many matching bounds.

papers.title: $a$-contraction applied to the time-asymptotic stability of weak shocks for a general 1-D viscous system
papers.abstract: The method of $a$-contraction with shifts builds on the relative entropy method of Dafermos and DiPerna and allows both viscous shocks and rarefaction waves to be studied directly at the level of the solution. This unified framework led to the resolution of Matsumura's long-standing conjecture on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous shock in composition with a rarefaction. Kang, Vasseur, and Wang established this stability for the one-dimensional compressible barotropic Navier-Stokes system. Their result was subsequently extended to composite planar waves for general $n\times n$ viscous systems in arbitrary spatial dimensions. The present paper is a companion to that work. Here we prove the estimates on viscous shock profiles needed to apply $a$-contraction with shifts, including derivative estimates that go beyond the standard bounds. We also give a streamlined account of the main ideas of the method by focusing on a single viscous shock for a general one-dimensional system.

papers.title: Entropic Column Generation and Lehmer Branch-and-Price for Bin Packing Problem
papers.abstract: We introduce Lehmer branch-and-price, an exact algorithm for bin packing and cutting stock problems built on the Lehmer transform, the ratio of Mellin transforms of item weights at consecutive orders. The transform maps each bin, a finite multiset of item weights, to a smooth increasing curve, and so gives the discrete problem a continuous representation on which the tools of analysis, such as convexity, exponential families and smoothing, can act. Read along this curve, the problem yields an explicit dual solution, a monotone representation of the dominance order, a family of constructive heuristics with first fit decreasing as its limit, and an integer identity that tells when the linear relaxation can decide an instance and when only a perfect packing can improve the best solution known. Lifted from items to patterns, the transform gives entropic column generation, a new form of column generation that bounds the relaxation from both sides at every iteration without solving the pricing problem exactly, maximizes a smoothed dual at an explicit rate, and measures by an entropy how much the relaxation leaves undecided. We show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the standard benchmark in both the number of instances solved and the computational time.

papers.title: Modular proof analysis and cut elimination for the Reflection Calculi $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$
papers.abstract: The reflection calculus with one modality is denoted by $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and its quantified generalization is known as $\mathsf{QRC}_1$. These decidable calculi are of interest since they generate the strictly positive fragments of the (quantified) provability logic for theories like Peano Arithmetic and Heyting Arithmetic. We introduce analytic cut-free calculi ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ for $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The new calculi derive sequents of the form $A\Longrightarrow B$ with $A,B$ strictly positive formulas. In particular, the new calculi do not use (multi)sets nor nested sequents. For both ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ it is shown that the cut-rule is admissible. As a consequence, it is proven that the calculi are deductively equivalent to $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The cutfree systems are used to prove uniform interpolation for the two reflection calculi. In addition, ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ is used to give a syntactic proof of Dashkov's Theorem to the extent that $\mathsf{RC}_1$ is the strictly positive fragment of the provability logic ${\mathsf{GL}}$. The paper also introduces non-analytic calculi that are conceptually easier but proof-theoretically behave badly. It is shown that even those systems allow direct cut-elimination: the benefits of the strict positivity outweigh the draw-backs of a non-analytic calculus in these cases.

papers.title: When Pedal Shapes Come Back: a Complex Story
papers.abstract: Under the usual nondegeneracy assumptions, repeatedly projecting a fixed point onto the side lines of an $n$-gon returns its shape after $n$ steps. We explain this classical theorem through a short complex-number identity: the multipliers of one step move cyclically around the polygon. The same calculation allows a different common angle of projection at each step. A sharp angle-dependent contraction bound identifies the incircle centre as the maximiser for tangential polygons. In space, even a regular tetrahedron can fail to recover its shape after four steps. We give an exact example, then show how concentric inscribed and circumscribed spheres restore a two-step return. Rectangular boxes provide a further four-step family.

papers.title: Resonance varieties of Schubert arrangements
papers.abstract: We compute the resonance varieties of the Orlik--Solomon algebras of Schubert matroids. Previously known results have been largely confined to matroids of rank $3$, and the Schubert matroids give a family of nontrivial examples of arbitrary rank. We give an expression for the cohomology of the Orlik--Solomon algebra that we show holds for Schubert matroids as well as for simple, complex-realizable rank-$3$ matroids that do not support multinets. Our proof introduces a family of matroids for which the Orlik--Solomon algebra is isomorphic to an exterior Stanley--Reisner algebra.

papers.title: Varieties of associative algebras with slow central codimension growth
papers.abstract: Central codimensions measure the dimensions of spaces of multilinear polynomials modulo those taking values in the center of an algebra. We classify associative algebras over a field of characteristic zero whose central codimensions grow at most linearly. The classification is given up to equality of polynomial identities, in terms of explicit generating algebras and an equivalent finite exclusion criterion. We also give a direct structural characterization of the bounded case. As a consequence, we determine the five varieties of quadratic central codimension growth whose proper subvarieties all have at most linear central growth. As an application of the bounded-growth classification, we characterize algebras graded by an arbitrary finite group whose graded central codimensions are bounded. Up to graded PI-equivalence, these are direct sums of commutative and nilpotent graded algebras, possibly together with the Grassmann algebra on two generators endowed with the trivial grading.

papers.title: Halving Partitions and Hyperbinary Expansions
papers.abstract: Starting from a positive integer, repeatedly halve the current value, rounding up or down. Which resulting sequences have terms that add to the starting integer? A simple balance identity turns the rounding choices into hyperbinary expansions, in which each power of two occurs at most twice. This correspondence gives exact counts by length and an injection into the expansions counted by Stern's diatomic sequence. We characterize equality in the resulting bound by the binary digits of the odd part of the integer. We also determine the unique longest partition and give a short recursive counting algorithm. When the required total is allowed to vary, the chain counts eventually equal Stern's number, and we determine the exact threshold. A direct proof shows that the counts of hyperbinary expansions in the three length classes modulo three differ by at most one. For sufficiently long halving partitions, the counts by length first weakly increase and then weakly decrease, although the full sequence need not do so.

papers.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. III
papers.abstract: This paper is the third in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices of size $n\times k$ with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. In this part we study the remaining case where $k = 3$ and $n \ge k + 2 = 5$ and prove that every linear map preserving the Cullis' determinant admits the same description as for the case where $k \ge 4$ and $n \ge k + 2$ obtained previously.

papers.title: Representability of Graphical Symplectic Matroids
papers.abstract: Chow associated with every finite multigraph $G$ a symplectic matroid $\GraphS{G}$ on the signed edge set $E\sqcup E^{*}$, whose restrictions to transversals are frame matroids of signed graphs, and Sarvepalli asked which of these matroids are representable. For a connected graph containing a cycle, we show that every isotropic representation of $S(G)$ admits an incidence-flow normal form. The remaining representation conditions are expressed through its admissible minors. Consequently, if $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable, then the bridgeless part of $G$ has a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow. In characteristic other than two, $\GraphS{G}$ is representable if and only if every non-loop edge on a cycle has a parallel mate. In characteristic two, we characterize the loopless graphs without two vertex-disjoint cycles by the existence of a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow, and we show that rigidly linked short cycles, and hence subdivisions of the prism, are obstructions. For $3$-connected simple graphs this gives a complete answer: $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable if and only if $\F$ has characteristic two, $G$ has no two vertex-disjoint cycles, and either $|\F|>2$ or $G\cong K_5$. In particular, the matroid of the Petersen graph is representable over no field. Finally, the admissible corank--nullity polynomial of an arbitrary symplectic matroid is intrinsic and satisfies a three-term contraction identity. For graphical symplectic matroids, this becomes a deletion-contraction recursion that closes up once marked vertices are allowed, and polynomials built from enveloping matroids agree with it exactly for sheltering envelopes.

papers.title: How Much Can Approximate Equilibria Change the Social Cost of Selfish Routing?
papers.abstract: We study approximate Nash equilibria in nonatomic congestion games, with the goal of understanding how much the social cost can change when the equilibrium condition is relaxed. We consider $ε$-approximate Nash equilibria ($ε$-NE), in which each player uses a strategy whose cost is at most $1 + ε$ times the minimum available cost. We compare the social costs of $ε$-NE and exact Nash equilibria. This lets us quantify, for example, how much a navigation app can reduce total travel time when drivers tolerate routes slightly slower than the fastest available route. For degree-$d$ polynomial latencies in both general nonatomic congestion games and single-commodity routing games on series-parallel networks, we give tight lower and upper bounds on the relative change in social cost from an exact Nash equilibrium to any $ε$-NE, with matching instances for every $ε$. For small $ε$, the largest possible relative reduction and increase in general congestion games are both $Θ(\sqrt{dε})$, independently of the number of resources and populations. In contrast, on series-parallel networks of depth $h$, the largest possible relative reduction is $Θ(hε)$, while the largest possible relative increase is known to be $ε$. For the classes of games we study, these results give a tight and quantitative characterization of the possible changes in social cost and establish a separation between general and series-parallel networks.

papers.title: The Lorentz Threshold in Fourier Restriction
papers.abstract: Classical Stein--Tomas restriction controls a Fourier transform on a curved surface, but the estimate changes when its values lie in a Banach space. We determine the sharp Lorentz threshold at the critical exponent $4/3$: for coefficients in $\ell_D^{4/3,q}$, the optimal Gaussian restriction constant grows like $(1+\log D)^{|3/4-1/q|}$. A multiscale wave-packet construction proves sharpness, including the delicate index $q=2$. The same threshold holds for fractional Gaussian noise, while Gaussian type and cotype alone do not distinguish the positive and negative cases. As a dispersive consequence, we establish a sharp Lorentz-channel spacetime estimate for linear capillary waves.

papers.title: Partial coactions of Hopf algebras on nonunital algebras and categories
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate partial coactions of a Hopf algebra on an associative, possibly nonunital algebra and on $\Bbbk$-linear categories. We prove that every partial coaction has a globalization in a broad sense. We study in detail the case of a partial coaction on an algebra with local units; we prove that such a coaction is always induced from a global coaction, and we show that there exists a naturally associated $\Bbbk$-linear category endowed with a partial coaction.

papers.title: Quadratic and Koszul Licci Ideals
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of all Koszul licci ideals, including a complete description of the defining equations and graded Betti tables for these ideals, showing that they exactly correspond to quadratic licci ideals that are at most two links away from a complete intersection. More generally, we show how to uniquely associate the Hilbert function of a quadratic licci ideal to a partition of its codimension, and use it to prove that the Hilbert function of a quadratic ideal determines whether or not it is licci. This provides a strong affirmative answer in the quadratic case to a question of Huneke, Polini, and Ulrich asking whether graded Betti tables determine the licci property of graded ideals.

papers.title: Bochner-Riesz means for Laguerre expansions
papers.abstract: We investigate the $L^p$ norm convergence of Bochner-Riesz means $S_R^δf$, $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^+,dμ_β)$ associated to Laguerre expansions of type $β\geq -1/2$. For any given $1 < p < \infty$ and $β> -1/2$, we provide a complete characterisation of the order $δ$ for which these means are uniformly bounded on $L^p$ spaces. A particularly noteworthy phenomenon arises for $-1/3 <β<0$, where the admissible $(p, δ)$ region differs substantially from those for $ -1/2 \leq β\leq -1/3$ or $β\geq 0$. Interestingly, the convergence for $-1/3 < β<0$ is an interaction between the ranges $ -1/2 \leq β\leq -1/3$ and $β\geq 0$.

papers.title: Optimal Conversion from Zero-Concentrated to Gaussian Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Gaussian differential privacy (GDP) and zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP) are two competing privacy accounting frameworks, but they share similar minimax lower bounds in various estimation problems. Moreover, it is known that a mechanism satisfying $μ$-GDP satisfies $(μ^2/2)$-zCDP, whereas the converse fails to hold at the same calibration. In this paper, we establish the optimal reverse conversion, showing that every $ρ$-zCDP mechanism satisfies $μ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)$-GDP, where $μ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)=2Φ^{-1}((1+e^{-t_ρ})^{-1})$ and $t_ρ$ uniquely solves the equation $ρ=t_ρ\tanh(t_ρ/2)$. We also obtain simplified bounds $\sqrt{πρ}\leqμ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)\leq\sqrt{8ρ}$, with sharp constants, which imply equivalence of the two frameworks up to constants. This explains why their minimax risks agree up to a constant rescaling of the privacy budget. We show that the squared conversion is strictly convex, which implies that converting zCDP to GDP before applying composition or group privacy yields a tighter GDP guarantee than converting afterward. We also derive the sharp conversion from bounded-range and logistic DP mechanisms (e.g., exponential mechanism) to GDP, where converting before composition but after group privacy gives the tighter guarantee.

papers.title: Adaptive Optimizers Can Get a Policy Ranking Wrong: Momentum, Dependent Data, and a Two-Run Remedy
papers.abstract: Operators choosing among decision rules, such as when a battery charges or where an idle taxi goes, rank them by estimated long-run value. A standard estimator, linear temporal-difference (TD) learning, fits values from one stream of correlated observations. Large fits often use an adaptive optimizer, such as adaptive moment estimation (Adam), with fixed averaging rates. We show that these rates can change what is estimated, not just how fast: the same observations drive the updates and the optimizer's step-size scaling, moving the fit away from the intended TD value. The shift differs across rules, so it need not cancel in a comparison, and more data only makes a wrong ranking look more certain. Our remedy refits the same data at a second averaging rate that halves the effective gain, the number to which the leading shift is proportional. Twice the new fit minus the original removes that shift. In New York taxi and battery models calibrated to real data, common optimizer settings leave the selected rule unchanged but order close rules wrongly and misstate its value. Our remedy corrects nearly every wrong ordering, with one extra fit when the shift is moderate and two when it is larger.

papers.title: Hodge theory and topology of Bogomolov--Guan manifolds
papers.abstract: Bogomolov--Guan manifolds are simply connected, irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds that are not Kähler, yet they echo hyperkähler geometry in striking ways. We show that their Frölicher spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ and that their Hodge numbers are stable under small deformations. The general fibers of their natural Lagrangian fibration are rationally null-homologous, and the Beauville--Bogomolov--Fujiki form is degenerate. Despite this, in every dimension, the Euler characteristics agree with those of generalized Kummer manifolds. In dimensions four and six, we compute the full Hodge diamonds and all Chern and Pontryagin numbers. Surprisingly, these characteristic numbers are the same as the generalized Kummer ones, even though the Betti numbers differ and the Hodge diamonds are asymmetric.

papers.title: Entanglement for elliptic curve group orders
papers.abstract: For an elliptic curve $E$ defined over a number field $K$ and $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime of good reduction of $E/K$, we let $n_\mathfrak{p}=\#E(k_\mathfrak{p})$ be the order of the group of points over the residue class field $k_\mathfrak{p}$. Divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by a prime $\ell$ depends on the splitting behavior of $\mathfrak{p}$ in the $\ell$-division field $K(E[\ell](\bar{K}))$ of $E$ and, generically, divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by different primes $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ are `independent events' on the set of primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of good reduction. However, there do exist elliptic curves with `entangled division fields' for which infinitely many $n_\mathfrak{p}$ are coprime to $\ell_1$ and infinitely many $n_\mathfrak{p}$ are coprime to $\ell_2$, but no $n_\mathfrak{p}$ is coprime to to $\ell_1 \ell_2$. For $\ell_1=2$, we classify in group theoretical terms the entanglement giving rise to this behavior, and count up to isomorphism the number of `special $2\ell$-division groups' exhibiting the phenomenon. A final section shows how such groups may be realized as the Galois group of $2\ell$ division fields for elliptic curves $E/\mathbf{Q}$.

papers.title: On the growth of weak regular partitions in k-uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: This paper classifies hereditary properties of k-uniform hypergraphs according to bounds in the weak hypergraph regularity lemma first developed by Chung. Specifically, we prove the bounds must grow at a constant, polynomial, exponential, or tower rate. This generalizes work in the 3-uniform case by the second author.

papers.title: Fermat curves and explicit class field theory for real quadratic number fields
papers.abstract: We use Fermat curves with real multiplication and classical CM theory to construct an explicit class field theory for arbitrary real quadratic number fields. The underlying strategy is well-established in computational class field theory, our main contribution is a geometric model to realize this strategy explicitly. This approach complements the recent breakthrough works solving conjectures by Brumer, Stark and Shintani and gives an alternative constructive solution to Hilbert's 12th problem for real quadratic fields.

papers.title: Online Autotuning of Algebraic Multigrid via Contextual Bandits and Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are widely used for solving large sparse linear systems, but their efficiency depends strongly on interacting setup and solve parameters. Effective parameter choices typically depend on the problem. We develop a phase-aware online autotuning method for hypre's BoomerAMG to reduce cumulative time-to-solution over sequences of related linear systems. A LinUCB-based contextual bandit selects mixed-type parameters for AMG hierarchy construction using a shared cost model over PDE descriptors and configuration encodings. A recursive LSTDQ controller uses residual and timing observations to estimate the AMG solve time within each attempt and adapt relaxation weights between multigrid cycles. Both learners update from ongoing solves without offline pretraining. Across grids of sizes $40^3$, $60^3$, and $80^3$, the joint autotuning method reduces total runtime, including recurring learner computation, by 36.1-43.3% for diffusion problems and 19.8-31.0% for diffusion-advection problems over sequences of 5000 linear systems, relative to the reference BoomerAMG default configuration. On a variable-flow diffusion-advection benchmark comprising 30,000 systems on a $60^3$ grid, 2 systems fail to converge with joint autotuning, compared with 1677 for the reference configuration, under their respective attempt budgets.

papers.title: Casson invariant of knots defined by random braids
papers.abstract: We investigate the expectation $E(v_2)$ of the Casson invariant $v_2$ for knots represented by two similar types of braids, the rosette $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $\prod_{1\leq 2i\leq s}σ_{2i}^{\pm 1}\prod_{1\leq 2i+\leq s}σ_{2i+1}^{\pm 1}$ and the quasitoric $s$-braids which are products of $k$ factors $σ_{1}^{\pm 1}σ_{2}^{\pm 1}...σ_{s-1}^{\pm 1}$. If $k$ is of the form $ns+1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{s+1}{24}$ where $c$ is the number of crossing points of braid; if $k$ is of the form $ns-1$, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{5-s}{24}$.\\ If we go through all $3$-braids, regardless of the shape of their diagram, we get $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{8}$. \\ For knots with a checkerboard diagram, $\dfrac{E(v_2)}{c}\sim \dfrac{1}{16}$.

papers.title: Lyapunov functions for the Langevin equation with dissipative damping
papers.abstract: We study the well-posedness and the large time stability of the Langevin equation in the presence of potentials and dissipative damping together with additive white noise. While the confining potential is assumed to be smooth, the nonlinear damping is allowed to have either polynomial growth or singular behaviors. We construct novel Lyapunov functions and determine the corresponding parameter regimes that lead to global well-posedness or finite-time explosion. These Lyapunov functions also allow for deriving quantitative mixing rates toward equilibrium. Our results extend existing ergodic theory established for the instance of nonlinear damping satisfying suitable integrability conditions.

papers.title: Cartesian closedness of lax comma categories
papers.abstract: For a finitely complete category X, we prove that the lax comma category Cat//X is cartesian closed if and only if its free coproduct completion Fam(X) is cartesian closed. The proof uses a change-of-base theorem: postcomposition with a functor induces a left adjoint between lax comma categories precisely when that functor is a left multiadjoint. We describe the exponentials and derive examples from known results on family categories.

papers.title: Fluid Limits and Upper Bounds for Randomized Greedy Matching
papers.abstract: The Modified Randomized Greedy (MRG) algorithm [Tinhofer (1984), Aronson-Dyer-Frieze-Suen (1995)] is a classical greedy algorithm for finding approximate maximum matchings. MRG repeatedly picks a uniformly random unmatched vertex and matches it to a uniformly random unmatched neighbor, if one exists. Since 1991, the best upper bound on its approximation ratio has been $2/3$, given by the Bomb graphs of [Dyer and Frieze (1991)]. We improve this bound to $0.6569$ on general graphs and $0.6607$ on bipartite graphs. Our constructions consist of copies of small gadgets, with specified vertex classes joined completely. We track each algorithm by counting gadget copies with each possible configuration of remaining vertices. Wormald's differential equation method [Wormald (1995)] shows that these counts, scaled by the size parameter of the construction, converge to a deterministic trajectory known as the \textit{fluid limit}, which is described by ordinary differential equations. This fluid limit approximation holds while the relevant vertex classes have positive density, and so we devise a separate counting argument determines the contribution from the end of the run. Furthermore, we apply our framework to Random Decision Order (RDO), in which vertices are processed in uniformly random order and choose unmatched neighbors according to fixed adversarial preferences. On bipartite graphs, we determine the exact limiting ratio on the Double-Bomb family of [Tang-Wu-Zhang (2020)]. Its minimum is $31/48$, confirming their numerical estimate of about $0.646$.On general graphs, we improve their upper bound of $5/8$, given by the paw graph, to $0.5946$ on a new family. Finally, we give one possible explanation for why $2/3$ seemed to be optimal for MRG in the concluding remarks.

papers.title: An Incidence-Based Edge-Averaged Method for Convection-Diffusion Problems on Polytopal Meshes
papers.abstract: We develop an incidence-based edge-averaged method for scalar convection-diffusion problems on convex polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimensions. The proposed method extends the classical edge-averaged finite-element scheme through a graph-theoretic formulation based on vertex-edge incidence matrices. We first establish this formulation on simplices in arbitrary dimensions and then extend it to convex polytopes by introducing complementary edges and generalized barycentric coordinates. A key ingredient is a matrix identity that relates the generalized Whitney edge mass matrix to a diagonal representation of the Poisson stiffness matrix, enabling an exponentially-fitted discretization expressed entirely in terms of nodal values and edge weights. We prove that the resulting stiffness matrix is a nonsingular $M$-matrix under suitable positivity and connectivity conditions, ensuring monotonicity and the discrete maximum principle. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional simplicial and nonsimplicial meshes demonstrate first-order convergence in the $H^1$ semi-norm and stable, nonoscillatory solutions in convection-dominated regimes.

papers.title: Coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity from a universal cumulant lifting
papers.abstract: Using probabilistic methods, we establish universal cumulant lifting criteria for Stieltjes and Hamburger moment sequences. In the Stieltjes case, we characterize coefficientwise Hankel total positivity after convolution with every initial moment sequence by requiring each once-shifted cumulant sequence to be Stieltjes. We also prove equivalence with the numerical moment property at every nonnegative intensity. In the Hamburger case, we use twice-shifted cumulants to obtain coefficientwise-positive leading Hankel determinants, a degree bound, an explicit highest-degree component, and drift invariance. We work with formal series and require neither exponential moments nor moment determinacy. We establish composition, binomial-convolution, and substitution results, and apply them to implicit equations and autonomous differential equations, tree and forest families, and lognormal compound-Poisson moments in a unified approach. From known moment sequences, we obtain general coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive families containing the classical Bessel, Lah, and Laguerre polynomials. We not only give new proofs of coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity of many combinatorial polynomials, but also prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity for the component polynomials of functional digraphs confirming a conjecture of Sokal and establish fixed-shape Schläfli--Gessel--Seo polynomials positivity supporting another conjecture of Sokal.

papers.title: On Wagstaff primes in the $k$-Pell number sequence
papers.abstract: A Wagstaff prime is a prime number of the form $(2^{\mathfrak{p}}+1)/3$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is an odd prime. For an integer $k\ge 2$, the sequence of $k$-generalized Pell numbers $\bigl(P_n^{(k)}\bigr)_{n\ge 2-k}$ is the linear recurrence of order $k$ given by $P_n^{(k)}=2P_{n-1}^{(k)}+P_{n-2}^{(k)}+\cdots+P_{n-k}^{(k)}$ for $n\ge 2$, with initial values $P_{2-k}^{(k)}=\cdots=P_{0}^{(k)}=0$ and $P_1^{(k)}=1$. For $k=2$ this is the classical Pell sequence. Motivated by the recent determination of the Wagstaff primes in the $k$-Fibonacci and $k$-Lucas sequences, we study the exponential Diophantine equation $P_n^{(k)}=(2^{\mathfrak{p}}+1)/3$ in positive integers $n,k$ and an odd prime $\mathfrak{p}\geq 3$, with $k\ge 2$. We show that this equation has no solutions, that is no $k$-Pell number is a Wagstaff prime. The proof combines linear forms in logarithms of algebraic numbers with reduction based on the theory of continued fractions, together with a computational verification in the remaining finite range.

papers.title: Optimal AB-program for Poincaré--Sobolev and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that we can subtract the full spectral gap $\left(\frac{N-1}{p}\right)^{p}$ of the $p$-Laplacian and keep the sharp Sobolev constant $S(N,p)$ of $\mathbb{R}^N$ at the same time in a large family of $p$. For $p=2$, this was proved by Benguria, Frank and Loss in dimension three, and it was shown by Hebey to be false in dimensions $N\geq4$. For $p\neq2$, it was proved by Nguyen for $N\geq4$ and $\frac{2N}{N-1}\leq p<N$. By employing, among other tools, a suitable conjugation that maps the radial $p$-Dirichlet integral on $\mathbb{H}^N$ onto its Euclidean counterpart on $\mathbb{R}^N$ while preserving the $L^p$ norm, together with a one-dimensional tangent line inequality, we establish such sharp Poincaré--Sobolev inequalities for $N=3$ and $2\leq p<3$, for $N=4$ and $\frac{1+\sqrt{13}}{2}\leq p<4$, and for $N\geq5$ and $\min\{3,\frac{1+\sqrt{4N-3}}{2}\}\leq p<N$. In particular, in all cases we also obtain an explicit remainder term. Moreover, since the change of function keeps the $L^p$ norm, we prove the sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with the full spectral gap and the sharp Euclidean constant for $N=3$ and $2\leq p\leq3$, and for $N\geq4$ on an explicit interval of $p$. For $p\geq3$, we also use the change of variable $t=\sinhρ$ and the Hardy inequality, which give a second remainder term. At the endpoint $p=N$, this remainder gives a Hardy--Trudinger--Moser inequality on $\mathbb{H}^N$ under a weaker constraint than the one of Liang, Lu, Wang and Yang, in every dimension $N\geq3$.
