Finally, we show that for $1<p<\frac{1+\sqrt{4N-3}}{2}$, which includes all $1<p<2$, the full spectral gap can still be subtracted with some positive constant in front of the Sobolev term, and that this constant is smaller than $S(N,p)^{p}$ when $p<\min\{2,\sqrt N\}$. Together with our other results, this shows that the full spectral gap can be subtracted for every $1<p<N$.

papers.title: A study on v-numbers of $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(L,M/I^nN)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(L,M/I^nN)$
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian $\mathbb{N}$-graded ring. Assume that $L$ and $M$ are finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}$-graded $R$-module, and $I$ a homogeneous ideal of $R$. Let $N$ be a graded submodule of $M$. Fix $k\in \mathbb{N}$. Denote $H:=\operatorname{Ext}^k_R(L,M)$ (or $\operatorname{Tor}_k^R(L,M)$) and $H_n:=\operatorname{Ext}^k_R(L, M/I^nN)$ (or $\operatorname{Tor}_k^R(L,M/I^nN)$). When $I$ is generated by elements of positive degree, we show that the local $v$-number of $H_n$ either coincides with that of colon submodule $(0:_H I)$ or is a polynomial in $n$ of degree one whose leading coefficient is one of the degrees of the generators of $I$. This extends the main result of Ghosh-Pramanik [J. Algebra 671 (2025), 61-74], where asymptotic linearity was shown under the assumption that $(0:_H I)=0$.

papers.title: Lower Bounds on Inference Complexity for Polyak-Ruppert Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp lower bounds for Gaussian approximation of Polyak-Ruppert averaged stochastic gradient descent with polynomially decreasing step sizes. For every fixed exponent $γ\in(1/2,1)$, a single one-dimensional smooth, strongly convex example has approximation error with the limiting variance of order $n^{1/2-γ}+n^{γ-1}$ in Kolmogorov and convex distances. This matches the existing upper bound throughout the range of $γ$. The nonlinear bias contributes $n^{1/2-γ}$ even when the Gaussian reference uses the finite linearized variance. We also derive a lower bound of order $n^{-(1-γ)/2}$ for the relative mean error of estimating the limiting variance from one SGD trajectory, uniformly over a scalar quadratic family. With the limiting variance known, achieving approximation error $\varepsilon$ on this example takes order $\varepsilon^{-4}$ iterations for the best choice $γ=3/4$. Achieving both Gaussian approximation and relative mean variance-estimation errors at most $\varepsilon$ uniformly over the model class requires at least order $\varepsilon^{-6}$ iterations for every fixed $γ$.

papers.title: Robust Optimization in Stochastic Games
papers.abstract: A player's impatient valuation of an infinite stream of stage payoffs is a weighted average with nonincreasing weights. Such valuations generalize geometric discounting and allow imprecise or heterogeneous time preferences. For a stochastic game \(Γ\) and a profile \(u\) of impatient valuations, let \(Γ_u\) be the induced game. We ask when approximately optimal or equilibrium behavior can be chosen to vary continuously and stably with \(u\). We show that this robustness is governed by the corresponding uniform long-run payoff property: the uniform value in the adversary case, and uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs in the equilibrium case. In finite state spaces, the latter is equivalent to the usual existence of a uniform equilibrium payoff. In the two-player zero-sum case, if \(Γ\) has a uniform value, then the value of \(Γ_u\) varies uniformly continuously with \(u\), and for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a uniformly continuous mapping assigning to each \(u\) an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal strategy in \(Γ_u\). Hence this holds for every finite two-player zero-sum stochastic game. In the non-zero-sum case, uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs imply a finite cover of the valuation-profile space by neighborhoods on each of which a single strategy profile is a robust \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium. For sunspot, correlated, and extensive-form correlated equilibria, uniform approximate equilibrium payoffs are equivalent to the existence, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), of a uniformly continuous mapping assigning to each valuation profile a robust \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium on a neighborhood of that profile. Consequently, every finite stochastic game admits uniformly continuous robust extensive-form correlated \(\varepsilon\)-equilibrium selections.

papers.title: Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
papers.abstract: In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.

papers.title: Enumeration of plane hypermaps with a mixed boundary II
papers.abstract: A plane hypermap with a boundary is a connected graph embedded in the plane with a distinguished face, and whose inner faces are properly face-bicolored. We say that such hypermaps are k-alternating if the colors of the faces adjacent to the distinguished face alternate at most 2k times when going counterclockwise. Eynard and Orantin, in [EO2005], have found a universal expression for the generating functions of k-alternating hypermaps as a surprisingly simple function of the generating function of 1-alternating hypermaps. In this article, we will provide combinatorial formulas for k-alternating hypermaps using specific subclasses of hypermaps in which each vertex can either be connected to a previously marked vertex, called accessible, or connected to all other vertices in what we call a blob. In particular, this method will allow us to derive the results from [EO2005] from a combinatorial perspective, and we anticipate that it will lead to the computation of asymptotics for hypermaps in future work. This article is naturally a sequel to, and most importantly a generalization of, the results in [BEL26], which deals essentially with the case of 1- and 2-alternating hypermaps.

papers.title: A Game of Scales
papers.abstract: These notes cover the material of two courses given at SISSA, Trieste, in the academic years 2023-2024 and 2025-2026, together with some material from courses taught in other recent years. The original idea behind these courses emerged from conversations with Andrea Causin and Margherita Solci about the somewhat elusive notion of `multiscale behaviour', which arises in the study of variational problems involving one or more small parameters. Two main mechanisms govern their asymptotic behaviour: concentration and oscillations. Their description is often associated with the emergence of a characteristic `scale', quantifying either the speed of concentration or the period of an optimal oscillation. These mechanisms may originate from different variational principles and may occur separately, coexist, compete, or interact, thus providing a natural interpretation of the term `multiscale'. This perspective inspired the informal title of the courses, which also became the title of these notes. The natural framework for these analyses is $Γ$-convergence. However, these notes are not intended as a general introduction to this now well-established theory. We provide only a brief account of the techniques relevant to our purposes, referring the reader to the author's book chapter {\em A Handbook of $Γ$-convergence}. For a broader introduction to $Γ$-convergence, and in particular to its topological properties, the standard reference is Dal Maso's monograph {\em An Introduction to $Γ$-convergence}.

papers.title: Seshadri functions on surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the Seshadri function on the ample cone of a smooth complex projective surface at a fixed point. At a submaximal class, we show that the function is differentiable if and only if there is a unique Seshadri curve. At a maximal class $L$, differentiability is equivalent to every curve $C$ computing the Seshadri constant satisfying $\frac{[C]}{{\rm mult}_x C}=\frac{[L]}{\sqrt{L^{2}}}$. We also prove that the non-differentiability locus is nowhere dense. For the blow-up of $\mathbb P^{2}$ at $r\ge 9$ very general points, assuming the $(-1)$-curves conjecture for the blow-up at $r+1$ very general points, we construct a non-empty open subset of the ample cone on which the Seshadri function at a very general point equals $\sqrt{L^{2}}$. Consequently, this function is not piecewise linear. Under the assumption of the Strong SHGH conjecture, we obtain a common non-empty open subset on which maximality holds at every point when $r\ge36$.

papers.title: Local superderivations of Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$
papers.abstract: We prove that every even or odd local superderivation of the Block Lie superalgebra $S(q)$ is a superderivation for every $q\in\mathbb{C}$, with both basis indices ranging over $\mathbb{Z}$. The superderivations used in the local condition have the same parity as the map. The proofs use the known description of homogeneous superderivations, bracket computations, and coefficient comparisons.

papers.title: Local and global conservation laws of partial differential equations on moving domains in three dimensions
papers.abstract: For PDE systems in three spatial dimensions, firstly, a review of the various types of global conservation laws --- volumetric, surface-flux, circulatory --- is given using vector calculus, and their corresponding local forms --- divergence, curl, gradient --- are explained. Secondly, an extension of each type of conservation law to moving domains is presented, where the domain --- volume, surface, curve --- is transported by a prescribed velocity field. This provides a generalization of Reynolds' transport theorem known for material domains in which the velocity field is the fluid velocity. The main results are illustrated by numerous physical examples taken from gas dynamics, fluid flow, nonlinear acoustics, chemotaxis, plasma dynamics, and also Maxwell's equations, which do not involve any physically specified velocity field. As an additional main result, an extension of the multiplier method for finding local conservation laws of divergence-type is presented for local curl-type and gradient-type conservation laws on both static and moving domains.

papers.title: Magnetic norm inflation below the velocity regularity threshold for viscous non-resistive MHD
papers.abstract: We study viscous, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamics on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. For every fixed magnetic exponent $s>d/2$ and every velocity exponent $q<s-1$, we prove norm inflation at the origin in $H^q\times H^s$. Arbitrarily small divergence-free Schwartz data generate classical solutions whose magnetic $H^s$ norm becomes arbitrarily large at arbitrarily small positive times, while the velocity remains arbitrarily small in $H^q$ throughout the observation interval. Together with endpoint local well-posedness, this identifies $q=s-1$ as the sharp lower velocity threshold for fixed $s>d/2$. The construction uses a symmetric pair of high-frequency velocity packets and a fixed low-frequency magnetic profile. A Fourier component of their stretching interaction has a fixed sign and gains the power $K^{s-1-q}$ on a short diffusive time scale. Subtracting an exact reference flow and using endpoint Besov estimates controls the full nonlinear remainder. Quantitative higher-order estimates ensure existence through the observation time and yield the uniform smallness of the velocity in the target norm.

papers.title: Non-backtracking Laplacian for hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We extend the non-backtracking Laplacian for graphs, introduced by Jost, Mulas and Torres, to hypergraphs. The operator is defined on the permutations of the edges and is normalized by the number of edges through which a non-backtracking walk can continue. We show that it satisfies a symmetry that generalizes the graph case, and that it can be obtained from the random walk Laplacian of a directed graph by rescaling if and only if all edges have the same cardinality. Moreover, we show that, up to copies of the eigenvalue $1$, its spectrum can be computed from a much smaller matrix indexed by the incidences of the hypergraph, and we use this reduction to bound the remaining eigenvalues away from $1$.

papers.title: The Value of Steiner Hubs in Two-Hop Distance Labeling
papers.abstract: Two-hop distance labelings were introduced in 2002 by Cohen, Halperin, Kaplan, and Zwick with hubs of two kinds: vertices of the graph, or, in their Steiner variant, arbitrary objects carrying arbitrary real values. On no family is the value of that freedom known. We determine it on $\ell_1$ products of betweenness-free metrics, those with no point between two others, a class containing every Hamming graph. The freedom is worth nothing when the factors have at most three letters, while from four letters on the largest saving is polynomial in the size of the product, attained on products of positively weighted stars. The $d$-dimensional hypercube is the two-letter case, and labeling it takes $(5/2+o(1))^d$ entries even with arbitrary hubs, matching the vertex-hub optimum of Goldberg, Razenshteyn, and Savchenko. Every lower bound here comes from one semidefinite program on a single factor, whose value $Λ$ never exceeds the rate that vertex hubs already achieve on the Hamming graph; where $Λ$ meets that ceiling, the freedom is worth nothing, and the ceiling is met exactly up to three letters.

papers.title: Minimum-Norm Interpolation in Weighted Variation Spaces: Direct and Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: We study minimum-norm interpolation in weighted variation spaces generated by ReLU$^s$ ridge functions on the unit ball, where $s$ is a positive integer. For a target $f$ in the weighted variation space and a node set with sufficiently small fill distance $h$, every minimum-norm interpolant satisfies the direct bound $\|f-\mathscr{I}_{X_h}f\|_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}h^{(2s+1)/4}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$. Under a boundary separation condition on the nodes, we construct a matching lower bound for the worst-case interpolation error. For the inverse problem, we introduce dual certificates and derive an estimate analogous to a Bernstein inequality. Under suitable upper bounds on dictionary size and spectral lower bounds for the atomic Gram matrices, sufficiently fast $L_2$ convergence of minimum-norm interpolants along geometrically decreasing fill distances implies that the target belongs to $\mathcal{V}_s$. As a byproduct, the best $L_2$ approximation error $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}$ for shallow ReLU$^s$ networks of width at most $n$ satisfies $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}n^{-1/2-(2s+1)/(2d)}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, with the weighted atomic cost of an approximating network bounded by a constant multiple of $\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, independently of $n$.

papers.title: Secant dimensions and bilinear decomposition widths for finite Heisenberg groups
papers.abstract: Let $G=UT_3(\F_q)$ be the finite Heisenberg group. We study the image closures and secant varieties of a family of equivariant bilinear maps between representations induced from central characters. Evaluation at a basepoint identifies the ambient space with $M_{q^2}(\C)$. A single channel is represented by $A^T\operatorname{diag}(d)B$, with $A$ and $B$ in prescribed twisted-convolution algebras. We prove that its affine image closure has dimension $3q^2-2$ for every central-character pair and that its affine second-secant closure has the expected dimension for every prime power $q$. For $q\ge3$, the proof constructs two differential images with zero intersection. We also prove a subgroup-lifting theorem for channel parameterizations on finite abelian groups with bicharacter coefficients: a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|H|-2)$ on a subgroup $H$ extends by zero to a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|K|-2)$ on the ambient group $K$, provided that every parameter vector is nonzero. Exact Jacobian certificates determine all secant dimensions for $q=2,3,4,5$, with generic widths $2,4,6,9$. The lifting theorem yields specified higher-secant dimensions on infinite families of extension fields. Attainment of the dimension lower bound for arbitrary $q$ remains a conjecture.

papers.title: A matroid characterization of the combinatorially symmetric maximum nullity of a graph
papers.abstract: The graph parameter ${\mathrm N}(G)$ is the maximum nullity among all combinatorially symmetric matrices associated to a graph $G$. The zero forcing number ${\mathrm Z}(G)$ is a well-known upper bound for ${\mathrm N}(G)$, and a zero forcing set of $G$ is exactly a set that intersects each fort of the graph. So the zero forcing number can be defined as the size of a minimum set that intersects every fort of $G$. This paper provides a similar characterization of ${\mathrm N}(G)$ that is purely combinatorial, using a connection to matroid theory and collections of forts that are compatible in a certain sense. We provide several examples highlighting subtle differences among compatible collections of forts and how they relate to full spark matrices and matroids associated to $G$.

papers.title: A localized packing lemma for sets of bounded $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension
papers.abstract: In the setting of abelian groups, Haussler's packing lemma implies that any subset of bounded $\operatorname{VC}$-dimension can be approximated by one of a small number of representative translates. While this exact statement is provably false under the weaker hypothesis that $A$ has bounded $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension, we show that in $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ a similar statement does hold after localization to cosets of subspaces depending on the individual translates. More precisely, given $ε>0$ and $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p^n$ with $\operatorname{VC}_2(A)<k$, we show that there exist $r\leq ε^{-O_{k,p}(1)}$ and $g_1,\ldots, g_r\in \mathbb{F}_p^n$ with the property that for every $x\in \mathbb{F}_p^n$, there is a partition $\mathcal{C}_x$ of $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ into cosets of (possibly distinct) subgroups, each of index at most $\exp(ε^{-O_{k,p}(1)})$, and a subcollection $Ω_x\subseteq \mathcal{C}_x$ whose union has size at least $(1-ε)|\mathbb{F}_p^n|$, such that on each $C\in Ω_x$, the translate $A-x$ looks like one of $A-g_1,\ldots, A-g_r$, in the sense that $|((A-x)Δ(A-g_{i_{x,C}}))\cap C|<ε|C|$ for some $1\leq i_{x,C}\leq r$. We also prove a second version of this result in which each partition $\mathcal{C}_x$ is the set of cosets of a single subgroup $H_x$ of quasipolynomial index but where the bound on $r$ is a quadruple exponential.

papers.title: From Gaussian to stable and back: Non-Pareto points in growing dimension
papers.abstract: We study the number of non-Pareto points in two high-dimensional models: a homogeneous Poisson point process and a fixed-size sample of independent uniform points in the unit cube. A point is non-Pareto if some other sample point is coordinatewise less than or equal to it. As the dimension grows on the logarithmic scale of the intensity or sample size, the asymptotic behavior exhibits a surprising sequence of transitions: from Gaussian to stable fluctuations, back to Gaussian, then to a Poisson limit at the sparsity threshold, followed by the eventual disappearance of non-Pareto points. We identify the critical thresholds, normalizations, and limiting laws in both models. Notably, the return to Gaussianity occurs while the stability index remains strictly below $2$ and is driven by a change in the dominant fluctuation mechanism. Moreover, in part of the returning Gaussian regime, the natural normalization is the square root of the expected count rather than its standard deviation. At the stable--Gaussian transition, the two mechanisms can coexist, giving rise to a sum of independent stable and Gaussian random variables.

papers.title: Profile decomposition, strict binding and global compactness for a critical Grushin embedding
papers.abstract: We study attainment of the best constant in \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^{m+n}} \bigl(|\nabla_xu|^2+|x|^2|\nabla_yu|^2+a|u|^2\bigr) \geq S_a\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{m+n}} (1+|x|^2)^{n/(Q-2)}|u|^q\right)^{2/q}, \end{equation*} where \(m,n\geq1\), \(Q=m+2n\), \(q=2Q/(Q-2)\), and \(a>0\). Using annular interpolation and a transverse-average recurrence with \(L^q\) contraction \(2^{-m/q}\), we decompose bounded sequences into finite, Grushin and Euclidean profiles. Energy and critical mass split, with a power bound in the number of profiles on the remaining mass. We prove compactness of normalized minimizing sequences modulo \(y\)-translations under \(S_a<\min\{S_G,a^{n/Q}S_E(1)\}\), where \(S_G\) and \(S_E(1)\) are the tangent constants. The strict-binding set is empty or an open interval; we prove nonemptiness for \(n=1\) and even \(m\geq6\). At finite positive endpoints of a nonempty binding interval, we characterize attainment by first-order binding gaps. We obtain a finite critical-profile decomposition of Palais--Smale sequences with a remainder vanishing in energy.

papers.title: Understanding Work/Life Balance Through Mathematical Model
papers.abstract: Work/life balance (WLB) remains a central yet elusive concept in social and organizational sciences, often described qualitatively without a unified quantitative framework. To address this gap, a novel compartmental mathematical model is proposed that formalizes WLB as a dynamic population-level phenomenon. The individuals are categorized into 4 compartments, namely, regularly employed, temporarily employed, imbalanced (infected), and balanced (recovered), representing balanced and imbalanced states. Role-based complaints govern the transitions between states, the conflict conversion rates of these complaints, and the recovery rate. The model, structured as a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations, is analyzed for the existence of the equilibrium and its stability. In the analysis, the stable disease-free equilibrium is found to exist, representing complete societal balance. The other endemic equilibrium is shown to be infeasible through simulations and thus requires certain parameter constraints, which represent a specific scenario that may occur in the population. However, it is found that the endemic equilibrium always remains unstable. The model's ability to quantify how micro-level stressors spread into macro-level imbalance is demonstrated by numerical simulations, which also validate the analytical results. This work establishes a rigorous mathematical foundation for WLB, enabling future empirical and mathematical calibrations.

papers.title: The Eleven Questions : March 2016 - October 2026
papers.abstract: We review the eleven open questions in Appendix H of Farina's manuscript on entire solutions of the Allen-Cahn equation (dated March 9, 2016).

papers.title: A relative version of Weinstein's morphism
papers.abstract: We introduce a relative version of Weinstein's morphism associated to a Lagrangian submanifold \(L\) of a closed symplectic manifold \((M,ω)\). We construct a homomorphism \[ \mathcal{A}^{(L,α)}\colon π_{1}\bigl(\operatorname{Ham}_0(M,L)\bigr) \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}/\mathcal{P}_{2}(M,ω), \] and establish its basic properties. We compute the invariant in several examples, including latitude circles in \(S^2\), and more generally, Lagrangian fibers in toric manifolds. These computations provide obstructions to Ha\-mil\-to\-nian isotopy of Lagrangian submanifolds and detect nontrivial, and in some cases infinite-order, elements in the homotopy groups of their Hamiltonian stabilizers.

papers.title: Massively parallel Schwarz methods for the high-frequency Helmholtz equation with O(k) convergence
papers.abstract: We develop a one-level restricted additive Schwarz solver with perfectly matched layer transmission conditions (RAS--PML) for high-frequency Helmholtz systems. For problems with ${O}(k^d)$ unknowns, $d=2,3$, the solver uses Cartesian decompositions and ${O}(k^d)$ concurrent local solves for a single right-hand side, where $k$ is the wavenumber. Starting from the convergence theory for fixed decompositions established in~\texttt{arXiv:2404.02156}, we address the growing cost {as $k$ increases} of local solves through a nested RAS--PML construction. Under suitable stability and contraction assumptions, we prove that sufficiently accurate recursive local solves preserve convergence of the outer iteration. We also prove that a single inner iteration at each non-terminal level yields a correction algebraically equivalent to one-level RAS--PML, provided that the hierarchy-induced finest local problems and composite restriction and weighted extension operators are retained. This equivalence provides a hierarchical interpretation and permits a direct implementation without recursive transfers. We assess the one-level solver using PML and overlap widths of order ${O}(k^{-1}\log k)$. Constant-coefficient experiments cover $300\leq k\leq19200$ in two dimensions and $60\leq k\leq780$ in three dimensions, reaching $1.47\times10^9$ and $4.75\times10^8$ complex unknowns, respectively. Richardson iteration counts grow approximately linearly with $k$ over these ranges, while total parallel runtime, including setup and solution, exhibits near-linear growth at the larger tested wavenumbers. Further experiments assess the effects of mesh refinement and heterogeneous media.

papers.title: On Sparse Graph Limits for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
papers.abstract: Graph neural networks are often trained on small graphs and deployed on larger ones, raising the question of which graph information must be preserved for combinatorial optimization values to transfer across sizes. We establish size-transfer guarantees for normalized graph optimization values using finite collections of energy features. For affine objectives, including MAX-CUT, coloring defect, and independent-set density, differences in task value are controlled by discrepancies in normalized scalar energy probes on all bounded-degree graphs. For general Lipschitz objectives, such as those with balance penalties, an additional representation error appears; this error vanishes on hyperfinite graph families but can remain bounded away from zero on expanders. Thus, at fixed degree bound, state space, Lipschitz constant, and target accuracy, a finite energy representation independent of graph size suffices universally for affine tasks and asymptotically for general Lipschitz tasks on hyperfinite families. These results yield prediction guarantees under explicit conditions on encoder accuracy, readout stability, and representation coverage, together with statistical generalization bounds. Theoretically, we prove Shapley-Folkman bounds with sharp parameter dependence, including a dimension-free $\ell_2$ regime, and realize the resulting energy features with a fixed-weight message-passing network using random node initialization on bounded-treewidth graphs. Experiments with exact solvers and trained models test the resulting transfer guarantees.

papers.title: Claw-free perfect graphs are chromatic-choosable
papers.abstract: We prove that every claw-free perfect graph $G$ satisfies $\ch(G)=χ(G)=ω(G)$. More strongly, if $S$ is a clique of simplicial vertices of $G$ and $k\geω(G)$, every proper precoloring of $S$ extends to a proper coloring of $G$ from arbitrary lists of size $k$ on $V(G)\setminus S$. The proof has three coloring steps: a mixed-list theorem for cobipartite graphs, a precoloring-extension theorem for elementary graphs built on Galvin's kernel method and a homogeneous-pair exchange argument, and a polynomial method (Combinatorial Nullstellensatz) argument for graphs of interval type in which a Vandermonde factor is transferred across each incomplete pair. The three coloring steps are assembled along the structure theorems of Chvátal--Sbihi, Maffray--Reed and Chudnovsky--Seymour, using double clique cutsets for composition. As a consequence, every perfect line graph is chromatic-choosable, recovering the theorem of Peterson and Woodall. Our precoloring extension theorem also resolves a conjecture posed by Chudnovsky and Seymour.

papers.title: Uniform cubic bounds for irrational values of the dilogarithm
papers.abstract: We study explicit denominator conditions ensuring the irrationality of the dilogarithm at positive and negative rational points. We prove that $\operatorname{Li}_2(p/q)$ is irrational whenever $q>(4e^4/27)p^3$, and obtain an explicit, slightly smaller threshold for $\operatorname{Li}_2(-p/q)$. The positive argument specializes the Rhin--Viola integral family and uses a uniform estimate for a restricted prime divisor. The negative argument combines the same arithmetic construction with three adjacent integral moments and an explicit maximization. We also give finite-numerator refinements by interpolating certified partition bounds and by introducing a comparison measure with a quadratic tail. In particular, $\operatorname{Li}_2(5/q)$ is irrational for every integer $q\ge418$. The proof separates the established integral and determinant constructions from the parameter estimates and finite certificates used here.

papers.title: Maximal input entropy for binary two-deletion and two-insertion channels
papers.abstract: Under uniform transmission, we determine the received binary words that maximize input entropy for two-deletion and two-insertion channels. For two deletions the maximizers are exactly the two alternating words at every positive received length. For two insertions the same conclusion holds from received length five onward; we give all smaller cases and exact maximal values. The proof combines an embedding-count identity organized by runs with strict convexity estimates, and a grouping of two-position deletion masks. For every insertion radius we give the complete positive embedding histogram of an alternating received word. We also determine its three-deletion histogram for every length, and certify all three-deletion maximizers through received length twelve and all three-insertion maximizers through length eighteen by exact integer comparison. These computations give precise three-error conjectures with their small-length exceptions.

papers.title: A local limit theorem for singularity visits on translation surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X,ω)$ be a translation surface with at least one singularity. We investigate the distribution of the number of singularity encounters along prime closed geodesics on $X$. Writing $\ell(γ)$ for the geometric length of a closed geodesic and $m(γ)$ for the number of singularities it encounters, we establish a uniform counting local limit theorem for the values of $m(γ)$ sampled over $\ell(γ)<T$. The key technical step is to introduce and study a trace-class operator whose spectral data encodes the Fourier transform of our counting distribution. Our results hold for every translation surface, without genericity assumptions.

papers.title: A characterization and closure property of Thorin's class
papers.abstract: Thorin's class coincides with the smallest class of probability laws on $\mathbb{R}$ that contains all gamma laws and their reflections, while being closed under convolution and weak convergence. In particular, all Thorin laws are self-decomposable. This paper proves an alternative characterization of Thorin's class in terms of what we call the hyperbolic Bochner-Bernstein property. This property corresponds to the notion of hyperbolically completely monotone Laplace transforms on the positive half line, but extended to the real-valued setting. Using the new characterization, it is shown that Thorin's class is closed under multiplication with independent random variables admitting hyperbolically completely monotone densities, which partly settles an open question raised by Bondesson and allows for proving that a large class of possibly skewed real-valued distributions is in Thorin's class. As particular examples, we apply the closure property to show that Johnson's S\textsubscript{U} distribution and the Pearson type IV distribution are in Thorin's class for all parameter choices.

papers.title: Finite-Time Tracking Success or Failure in the Pursuer--Evader Model
papers.abstract: We investigate a sufficient framework for determining the success or failure of finite-time tracking in pursuer--evader dynamics. To this end, we design a nonsmooth coupled multi-agent system by adopting a previously established pursuer--evader model from the existing literature, which characterizes asymptotic tracking success and failure, as the backbone. We then provide appropriate sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of initial data, system parameters, and kernel functionals, under which some pursuers can successfully track evaders within a finite time, while others fail to do so. In particular, we show that the pursuer--evader subsystem associated with the pursuers that successfully track the evader, together with the corresponding evaders, exhibits finite-time stability.

papers.title: Two types of averaging principles for multiplicative stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equations with fast oscillations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study averaging principles for stochastic KdV equations perturbed by a fast oscillating term generated by a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, $ s\geq 0$. When dealing with multilinear estimates of the nonlinear terms in the stochastic KdV type equation, two kinds of workspace are both effective. The classical workspace can help us prove the averaging principle in the $L_ω^2$ sense, but it has more restrictions on the noise kernel and the conservation structures. When we use a new workspace without homogeneous low frequency restrictions, only the regularity conditions and the $L_x^2$ conservation structure is needed. Correspondingly, because there is no moment estimate of the solution, we can only prove the perturbed equations converge to an averaging equation in the probability sense. Our works may have important reference value, because it not only provides a new perspective to handle dynamical problems of stochastic dispersive model, but also compare it with the classical method.

papers.title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for the Regime-Switching Consumption-Investment Problem
papers.abstract: This paper establishes an entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) framework for the continuous-time consumption-investment problem under a regime-switching market model with general utility functions. By incorporating randomized exploratory policies and Shannon entropy regularization into the stochastic optimal control formulation, we derive closed-form representations for the optimal exploratory consumption and investment strategies. Specifically, the optimal investment strategy follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution, whereas the optimal consumption strategy takes the form of a Gibbs measure---which specializes to a Gamma distribution under logarithmic utility and a non-standard exponential distribution under power utility. Crucially, our theoretical analysis reveals that the classical deterministic optimal decisions correspond to the mode---rather than the mean---of these exploratory distributions. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of the exploratory value function to its classical unregularized counterpart as the temperature parameter vanishes. For algorithmic design, we develop a continuous-time q-learning framework grounded in a novel continuous-time q-function, prove the policy improvement theorem, and establish martingale characterizations for both on-policy and off-policy learning. We find that parameterizing the actor network based on theoretical distribution families can help accelerate convergence and enhance numerical stability. Furthermore, numerical experiments across regime-switching environments provide empirical support for our theoretical findings, demonstrating stable loss convergence as well as the monotonicity and concavity of the learned value functions.

papers.title: Impact Mechanism of a Point Interaction in the Cubic Half-Wave Equation: Well-Posedness, Constrained Energy Levels and Near-Critical Rigidity
papers.abstract: We study the one-dimensional nonlinear half-wave equation with a logarithmically renormalized point interaction. The nonlinearity is focusing and cubic, which is mass-critical. We establish well-posedness in the energy space using a new method for unconditional uniqueness that requires no auxiliary Strichartz assumption. We reveal the mechanism by which the point interaction affects ground states. The free critical mass is the sharp threshold: fixed-mass ground states exist and are orbitally stable below it, whereas at and above it the constrained energy is unbounded from below. We also prove a near-critical rigidity result showing that bounded energy concentrating sequences converge to free ground states after rescaling.

papers.title: Nonlinear kink modes for nonisentropic supersonic vortex sheets
papers.abstract: In this paper, planar nonisentropic vortex sheets of the two-dimensional Euler equations under the stability condition are studied via nonlinear geometric optics, focusing on the interaction induced by a small-amplitude, high-frequency incident wave impinging on a planar vortex sheet. It is found that there exist three asymmetric critical incident angles at which resonance occurs, leading to a significant amplification of the reflected and refracted oscillatory waves. Moreover, by refining the asymptotic expansion, we deduce that the leading profiles of the highly oscillatory waves are described by initial-boundary value problems for Burgers transport equations, while the leading profile of the contact discontinuity front satisfies an initial value problem for a Hamilton--Jacobi-type equation, which reduces to a forced linear transport equation on one resonant branch. These results extend the resonant amplification mechanism from the isentropic setting to the nonisentropic Euler flow and reveal the asymmetric influence of entropy variations on the nonlinear evolution of compressible vortex sheets.

papers.title: Alternative Tikhonov-Type Regularization for the Calderón Inverse Conductivity Problem
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the application of two regularization methods, classical Tikhonov and Alternative Tikhonov regularization, to the Calderón inverse conductivity problem. We develop an iterative reconstruction scheme based on linearizing the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and approximating conductivity updates using Gaussian basis functions. The resulting linear systems are solved using both regularization methods, with particular attention given to the derivation and numerical implementation of Alternative Tikhonov regularization. We compare the performance of these methods through numerical experiments on a synthetic conductivity containing two localized regions of differing conductivity. A total of 666 reconstruction tests are performed across varying regularization parameters, damping factors, and iteration counts. The lowest relative reconstruction errors obtained are 0.064730 for Alternative Tikhonov and 0.065173 for classical Tikhonov regularization. Although both methods produce comparable reconstructions, Alternative Tikhonov achieves the lowest observed error. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of both approaches within the proposed reconstruction scheme and motivate further investigation into parameter selection, numerical stability, and reconstruction accuracy.

papers.title: Almost Gorenstein edge rings of bipartite graphs and their $h$-vectors
papers.abstract: We characterize bipartite graphs whose edge rings are almost Gorenstein. Using this characterization, we recover known results for two families of graphs. In addition, we show that if the edge ring of a bipartite graph is almost Gorenstein and its $h$-polynomial has degree at least two, then the $h$-polynomial is palindromic except possibly for the linear and next-to-leading coefficients. Moreover, we construct two bipartite graphs whose edge rings have the same $h$-vector, although only one of the rings is almost Gorenstein.

papers.title: Unlikely likelihoods: likelihood analysis for the triangular and random histogram models
papers.abstract: This paper concerns certain parametric models for densities on the unit interval which lead to nonsmooth and nonregular likelihood functions. (i) The first is the simple triangular model on the unit interval, characterised by a density linearly increasing from zero to the mode position $θ$ and then linearly decreasing to zero from the mode to one. With data from this model the likelihood function is a sum of individually log-convex terms, and with the derivative having discontinuities at each data point. (ii) The second is the one-parameter two-box density which is flat on $[0,θ]$ and $(θ,1]$, with $θ$ the median. The likelihood has jumps at each datapoint. Here the maximum likelihood estimator is sharper than usual, with convergence in distribution of $n(\hatθ-θ)$ to a nonnormal limit. We also study the $k$-box extension of this model, with density being flat on $k$ boxes determined by $k$ quantiles. (iii) This second model is extended to the two-parameter two-box model, with areas $γ$ and $1-γ$ for boxes $[0,θ]$ and $(θ,1]$. Again the likelihood is nonregular, and the maximum likelihood estimators exhibit different rates of convergence for the breakpoints and the density values. The model generalises to the $2(k-1)$ parameter density piecewise flat over $k$ boxes. For each of these models we tend to the delicate task of sorting out the large-sample behaviour of the log-likelihoods, then leading to precise and partly nonstandard limit distributions for the maximum likelihood and Bayes estimators.

papers.title: Two-point Padé approximation and patterns in continued fractions for $(F_{n+1}/F_n)^k$
papers.abstract: We explore the simple continued fraction expansion for the $k$th power of the Fibonacci convergent $F_{n+1}/F_n$, as $n$ grows. For most $k$, this continued fraction consists of $k$ linearly growing \emph{patches} of infinite periodic continued fractions separated by \emph{junctions} that vary periodically in $n$. But under special conditions, two patches merge or, more strikingly, an exponentially growing \emph{monster term} replaces two patches and the junction between them. We trace these phenomena to properties of the Padé approximants that approximate $x^k$ near $x = φ$ and $x = \barφ$ simultaneously. We prove the patterns for second-order unimodular recurrences and compute several more instances of this rare and apparently previously unnoticed monster term.

papers.title: Far-field Layers of Steady State for Viscous and Heat-conductive Gas
papers.abstract: We study the vanishing heat conductivity limit of radially symmetric stationary solutions to the non-isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the exterior of a ball under an inflow boundary condition. A distinctive feature of this singular limit is the formation of a far-field layer whose transition region moves toward spatial infinity as the heat conductivity tends to zero. We establish the existence and uniqueness of stationary solutions with the uniform estimates with respect to the heat conductivity and analyze the corresponding limiting problem. The limiting solution generally fails to attain the prescribed far-field density and temperature separately, although its pressure at infinity agrees with the prescribed far-field pressure. We show that this discrepancy gives rise to a far-field layer, derive its explicit representation, and identify its characteristic spatial scale. Finally, we prove that the stationary solution is uniformly approximated over the entire exterior domain by the superposition of the limiting solution and the far-field layer.

papers.title: On the classification of entire solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation in any dimension
papers.abstract: The mathematical content that follows dates from 9 March 2016. I began writing it in early December 2014, whilst I was visiting Scuola Normale Superiore in Pisa, Italy. I would like to thank Luigi Ambrosio, Andrea Malchiodi, Carlo Mantegazza e Gérard Tronel who, between January 2015 and March 2016, read this version of the manuscript and some earlier drafts. Their feedback and constant support have been a source of encouragement. The manuscript has been at rest since March 2016. Neither its content nor its status will undergo changes in the future; it asks merely to be considered through the eyes of that moment. Paris, October 23, 2026, Alberto Farina

papers.title: Stability of least-energy solutions of the harmonic map flow from the plane into the 2-sphere
papers.abstract: We prove the asymptotic stability of the least-energy harmonic map $W:\mathbb R^2\to S^2$ for the harmonic map flow under small, sufficiently decaying, non-symmetric perturbations. Solutions exist globally and are asymptotically described by a modulation of $W$ plus a remainder that converges to zero as $t\to\infty$. The modulation parameters associated with scaling, rotation, and translation remain close to their initial values and converge to finite limits. The proof relies on an inner-outer gluing decomposition and the analysis of a non-local equation governing the modulation parameters.

papers.title: Spanning tree with bounded degree sum of two adjacent vertices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first give a sharp sufficient condition on degree sum for a connected graph to have a spanning tree whose maximum of degree sum of two adjacent vertices are bounded. These improve some previous results on the spanning tree with bounded maximum degree. Next, we also use our main result to study the generalized rainbow connection of graphs. In particular, we give some degree sum conditions for a connected graphs to have a bounded (1,2)- rainbow connection number.

papers.title: Inverse source problem of variable-exponent time-fractional diffusion equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates an inverse temporal source problem for a variable-exponent time-fractional diffusion equation with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. By the perturbation method, the model is equivalently transformed into a constant-order fractional diffusion equation with a convolution perturbation term. Existence, uniqueness, and energy estimates of strong and weak solutions to the forward problem are established, and for a separable source term the uniqueness and Lipschitz stability of the temporal source function are proved using local integral observations. A numerical reconstruction algorithm combining Tikhonov regularization with the conjugate gradient method is developed with a convergence error estimate, and numerical experiments verify its effectiveness and stability for different variable-exponent functions, noise levels and source functions. Since fractional advection--diffusion models describe the turbulent transport of airborne pollutants, the method is also applicable in atmospheric science for recovering the emission history of a pollution source from sparse measurements.

papers.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. Our approach treats the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gröbli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.

papers.title: Ground state uniqueness and quantitative stability for the mass-critical Hartree equation
papers.abstract: We prove that the ground state of the mass-critical Hartree equation is unique up to phase rotations and translations and nondegenerate in every dimension $d\ge3$. This makes the recent conditional $L^2$ classification of minimal-mass blow-up and non-scattering solutions unconditional; we also give a direct $H^1$ proof of the finite-time blow-up classification. We further establish a global quadratic stability estimate for the sharp Hartree interpolation inequality. For the optimal stability constant, we rule out vanishing of minimizing sequences and describe their possible loss of compactness.

papers.title: Mutual-visibility colouring with two colours is NP-complete for every fixed diameter
papers.abstract: A mutual-visibility set in a graph $G$ is a set $S$ of vertices such that any two vertices of $S$ are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $χ_μ(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition $V(G)$. Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $χ_μ(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter $d$, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial. The proof rests on a reformulation of $χ_μ(G)\le 2$ for diameter-two graphs as the $2$-colourability of an associated hypergraph, and on a reduction from $2$-colourability of $3$-uniform hypergraphs without short cycles.

papers.title: On motivic multiplicativity of cyclic covers
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a smooth projective complex variety of dimension $n$ with trivial Chow groups, and let $f: X\rightarrow Y$ be a cyclic cover of degree $d$ branched over a smooth ample divisor $D\in |dL|$. We show that a naturally constructed Chow--Künneth decomposition of $X$ is $m$-fold $mn$-multiplicative for each integer $m\geq2$ and that its stable motivic multiplicativity defect satisfies $\mathfrak{sd}(X)\leq 2dn$. If, in addition, each positive-codimension cycle class on $Y$ is supported on $D$, then a double cover admits motivic $0$-multiplicativity. As a further application, we show that any smooth Gushel--Mukai sixfold admits motivic 0-multiplicativity. Moreover, we establish the sharp modified-diagonal property for all smooth double EPW sextics, confirming a conjecture of O'Grady for these varieties.

papers.title: A Computational Verification of the Markov Uniqueness Conjecture for $z\leq 10^{500000}$
papers.abstract: We describe a finite computational verification of Markov Uniqueness Conjecture for normalized positive integer solutions of $x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz$ with $z \leq 10^{500000}$. The archived run reports $239\,536\,376\,556$ triples with distinct maximal coordinates.The method combines a disjoint tree decomposition, certified fixed-point range bounds, a deterministic 48-bit candidate screen,and replay modulo $2^{128}$. We give the mathematical justification and a reproducibility procedure covering package checks,retained-data auditing, and a full rerun. The conclusion depends on correct execution of the exhaustive screen and replay; the retained audit does not regenerate the deleted screening buckets.

papers.title: Positive expansiveness of operator semigroups: orbit growth and spectral criteria
papers.abstract: This paper studies positive expansiveness and positive kinematic expansiveness for strongly continuous semigroups of bounded linear operators on complex Banach spaces. We prove that positive kinematic expansiveness is equivalent to the unboundedness of every nonzero orbit, while positive expansiveness additionally requires the generator to be bounded from below. We also show that continuous changes of time can be replaced by increasing homeomorphisms without changing positive expansiveness. Uniform exponential expansion implies positive expansiveness without any surjectivity assumption; we characterize it through the minimum modulus, the lower growth bound, and the approximate point spectrum of a single semigroup operator. Under a uniform positive lower bound on the semigroup, positive expansiveness is equivalent to positive kinematic expansiveness together with boundedness below of the generator. Diagonal semigroups on $\ell_p$ then show that uniform exponential expansion, positive expansiveness and its kinematic version form a strictly decreasing hierarchy. Finally, we derive necessary spectral conditions for bounded generators and show that all three properties coincide in finite dimensions.

papers.title: Global classical solutions of the repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system
papers.abstract: Global classical existence for general large data in the three-dimensional repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system has long been an open problem. We give an affirmative answer: every nonnegative $C^1$ initial datum satisfying \[ f_0(x,p)+|\nabla_{x,p}f_0(x,p)|\lesssim\langle x\rangle^{-a}\langle p\rangle^{-b},\qquad a>1,\quad b>3, \] generates a unique global classical solution. No smallness or symmetry is assumed. The result covers finite and infinite mass and energy, including infinite kinetic energy density. The power thresholds are sharp for general pure-power bounds ensuring finite density and an absolutely convergent Coulomb field. The proof rests on two new mechanisms: local energy recovery for a population selected by energy growth, and a corrected moment--action closure based on nonnegative transverse interactions. The argument also yields global classical solutions of the nonrelativistic equation in the same initial class, allowing infinite mass with polynomial velocity tails of any order $b>3$.

papers.title: Robust distortion riskmetrics under symmetry, unimodality, and Wasserstein constraints
papers.abstract: We study worst-case distortion riskmetrics over symmetric distributions with prescribed mean and variance in a Wasserstein ball around a reference distribution. Our key contribution is the construction of a reference-dependent auxiliary distortion that encodes the Wasserstein constraint while preserving symmetry under the concave-envelope operation. Under suitable regularity and nondegeneracy conditions, this construction yields sharp upper bounds for distortions of bounded variation, allowing nonmonotonicity and interior discontinuities, and identifies extremal distributions when the bounds are attained. An approximation preserving symmetry and the prescribed moments exactly shows that upper semicontinuous relaxation of the symmetrized distortion leaves the supremum unchanged for budgets strictly above the feasibility threshold. With additional unimodality, symmetry fixes the quantile's concavity-convexity transition at the midpoint, yielding a characterization via $L^2$-projection onto a fixed closed convex cone for absolutely continuous distortions with square-integrable derivatives. Numerical examples for ES, RVaR, and VaR illustrate how shape restrictions and the reference distribution affect feasibility and worst-case risk. Simulations with data-dependent Wasserstein radii examine worst-case ES and feasibility under correctly specified and misspecified shape restrictions.

papers.title: Stratified Superintegrability of Spin Calogero-Moser-Sutherland Systems
papers.abstract: We study the Poisson chain of the compact spin Calogero-Moser-Sutherland system obtained by conjugation reduction of $T^*\mathrm{SU}(n)$ at a fixed coadjoint orbit. We give a Horn-type condition ensuring that the spectral torus acts freely on the full fiber over a simple spectrum; for each orbit, the admissible spectra form a nonempty open dense set, and the restricted chain is strongly superintegrable of rank $n-1$ on every orbit-type stratum. We also construct, across certain affine spectral walls, a proper quotient map onto a Hausdorff stratified Poisson space with a finite Whitney stratification. For $\mathrm{SU}(3)$, we compute the free spectral domain and the quotient near two intersecting walls, and a zero-orbit example shows that the analogous quotient need not be Hausdorff on the unrestricted reduced phase space.

papers.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system in the half-space with localized boundary data
papers.abstract: We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and localized boundary data $ψ(x')φ(t)\mathbf e_j$, $1\le j\le n$, where $ψ$ is supported in the closed unit ball. A separation point is a boundary point outside $\operatorname{supp}ψ$ where a component takes both signs on positive-measure sets in every sufficiently small adjoining space-time neighborhood. By evaluating the spatial convolutions appearing in the solution formula of the Stokes system via confluent hypergeometric functions, we obtain explicit formulas for the first normal derivatives of tangential components, the second normal derivative of the normal component, and tangential pressure derivatives at the boundary. For normal data, suitable Hölder regularity and strict log-concavity of $φ$ yield a unique separation point for each tangential component at every point of its coordinate axis outside the ball, and exactly two for the normal component at each sufficiently distant boundary point. We prove monotonicity and large-distance asymptotics of their temporal coordinates and quantitative temporal vanishing estimates for the normal derivatives. For tangential data in $n\ge3$, we prove the existence and uniqueness of separation points of tangential and normal components, including at fixed spatial points while $φ$ is positive. We derive spatial asymptotics at large distance and time from data moments and, under a geometric condition, supporting faces of $\operatorname{supp}ψ$. We characterize tangential pressure-gradient signs for both tangential and normal data, locating favorable and adverse regions near the boundary. For radial $ψ$, additional assumptions yield existence, uniqueness, and asymptotics of pressure-gradient zeros and zero curves, including those governed by the zero of the Caputo half-derivative of $φ$.

papers.title: Canonical quantum curve I
papers.abstract: We formulate a canonical quantum curve conjecture $\widehat HΨ_*=0$ for spectral curves of positive genus. Here $Ψ_*$ is the non-perturbative wave function associated with Eynard--Orantin topological recursion, specialized at the \emph{canonical vanishing point}, a distinguished zero of the closed non-perturbative partition function. The operator $\widehat H$ is obtained by Weyl quantization of $H(x,y)$, with $\widehat x=x\cdot$ and $\widehat y=\hbar\partial_x$, together with quantum corrections to its coefficients. These corrections depend only on closed moduli and $\hbar$ and vanish classically. Whenever a geometric definition is available, we conjecture that the corrected coefficients are suitably normalized Wilson-loop expectation values. When a corresponding refined theory exists, we conjecture a relation between the canonical vanishing point and the closed Nekrasov--Shatashvili free energy. We prove the quantum curve conjecture for Weierstrass curves and the mirror curves of canonical bundles of smooth projective toric weak del Pezzo surfaces, including local $\mathbb P^2$. For the local surfaces considered here, we relate the canonical vanishing point to a derivative of the closed NS free energy. For local $\mathbb P^2$, we also identify the corrected coefficient with a suitably normalized, geometrically defined NS Wilson-loop expectation value.

papers.title: Equivariant $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for amenable actions
papers.abstract: We prove that every amenable action of a countable discrete group on a separable, simple, unital, nuclear, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra absorbs the trivial action on $\mathcal{Z}$ up to cocycle conjugacy. The group may be nonamenable, as in Suzuki's recent examples, and no assumptions on outerness or on the tracial state space are needed. This extends OpenAI's result for amenable groups to amenable actions. Amenability of the action cannot be omitted in general, as examples of the author and Lupini show. More generally, we show that every tracially amenable action on a separable, unital, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra with traces admits invariant central copies of all matrix algebras, without simplicity or nuclearity. For amenable actions on simple nuclear algebras, equivariant property (SI) allows one to deduce $\mathcal{Z}$-stability from this. As applications, we obtain absorption of $\mathcal{Z}$ for intermediate subalgebras in the crossed product, and also pure infiniteness for outer amenable actions of nonamenable groups. The basic techniques involving Gaussian variables originate in OpenAI's preprint, and are also the main new tool in its proposed solution to the Toms--Winter conjecture. We extend these techniques in order to deal with the weight functions coming from amenability, and one of the main new ingredients is the fact that one can replace an amenable action by an auxiliary one for which the amenability weights are central. In order to make the probabilistic tools accessible to the community beyond what is used here, we include an appendix where the theory is developed assuming only an elementary background, and where the relevant estimates are proved in detail.

papers.title: A note on the product of holomorphic correspondences
papers.abstract: In this article we study the concept of product of two holomorphic correspondences which was introduced in our previous work. Beginning with some basic results regarding the orbit space associated with the product correspondence, we then move on to a detailed analysis on the thermodynamic formalism of the same. Some of the results look at the behaviour of the product correspondence with respect to the individual correspondences. Finally, we explore different families of correspondences with expanding nature.

papers.title: Quantum Generalized Cluster Algebras from Scattering Diagrams: Positivity and Mutation
papers.abstract: We construct generalized quantum cluster scattering diagrams over a ring of formal reciprocal exchange coefficients, for compatible seeds satisfying \(\widetilde B^TΛ=[I_n\mid0].\) A central lattice extension records the roots of the exchange polynomials as independent degrees. Applying Davison--Mandel positivity in this extension and proving a positive cylinder projection theorem yields positive wall factorizations and theta coefficients in the root variables. Their regular classical limits recover generalized cluster scattering diagrams. Nonvanishing under classical specialization, together with control of the mutated positive monoids, gives quantum mutation compatibility. The resulting scattering atlas has the generalized cluster fan, and every reachable cluster monomial is a theta function. Classical detection of theta coefficients gives a geometric proof of the Laurent phenomenon, with positivity after adjoining the polynomial roots. Evaluation of the exchange coefficients recovers the generalized quantum cluster algebras with this normalization. The Fock--Goncharov mutation product becomes a wall-crossing action, identifying extended \(g\)-vectors with leading theta exponents and \(F\)-polynomials with the coefficient factors on their right. Constructing these polynomials before evaluation gives the separation formula for arbitrary prescribed reciprocal Laurent polynomial coefficients, without requiring positivity at \(t=1.\) Positivity in the roots is distinguished throughout from positivity in the exchange coefficients.

papers.title: Galois Actions on Energy-Harmonic Functions
papers.abstract: We study the action of $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ on the solutions to the discrete Dirichlet problem for a graph with fixed edge energies. We establish transitivity of the Galois action outside a thin set in the parameter space and demonstrate that the exceptional thin set may be Zariski dense, so the conclusion cannot in general be replaced by one that holds on a Zariski-open set. Identifying the parameter locus where the Galois action is transitive constrains the possibilities for linking combinatorial and arithmetic properties of the discrete energy-harmonic Laplace equations and other systems of the same form.

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Hamiltonian Descent for Radiation Therapy Treatment Planning
papers.abstract: Direct incorporation of dose-volume constraints into inverse radiotherapy planning leads to large mixed-integer optimization problems that accurately represent clinical requirements but are computationally challenging. We develop and evaluate a quantum-inspired approach for automated dose-volume-constrained intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) and intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) planning. Clinical requirements are formulated as mixed-integer optimization problems, with binary variables representing dose-volume constraint violations. Patient-specific dose-influence matrices are generated at the photon control-point and proton spot levels, and intensities are optimized using Quantum-Inspired Hamiltonian Descent (QIHD). We evaluate QIHD on eight clinical cases: four IMRT (two prostate, one head-and-neck, and one liver) and four IMPT (two lung, one prostate, and one liver). The IMRT formulations contain 27,621 to 112,565 variables and are solved in 5 to 32 minutes, while the IMPT formulations contain 69,861 to 221,342 variables and are solved in 11 to 35 minutes on an NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU. QIHD produces dose distributions satisfying clinical protocols without manual intervention. In comparison, a CPU implementation of Gurobi fails to solve most tested mixed-integer formulations within several hours. These results demonstrate the computational feasibility of GPU-accelerated QIHD for automated photon and proton treatment planning. Prospective clinical validation and implementation of decomposed subproblems on quantum hardware remain future directions.

papers.title: Common-Source Assembly for Spherical Minimal Immersions
papers.abstract: We develop a matching principle for assembling maps from a common manifold into spherical minimal immersions. The equations couple the coefficients to the induced metric and yield examples with nonminimal constituent immersions. We establish existence and uniqueness of matching coefficients under suitable hypotheses and sharp rigidity for complete harmonic assemblies over $\mathbb S^2$. For a Clifford family, the first eigenspace determines the underlying fibration. The principle also produces weighted minimal profiles that generate minimal products in round spheres, with examples formed from finitely many Lawson--Osserman blocks of different degrees over a common Hopf source.

papers.title: Locally Conformal Analysis of Non-Degenerate Odd Pairs
papers.abstract: We study the locally conformal geometry of cosymplectic and coorientable contact manifolds within a common algebraic framework based on a non-degenerate odd pair: a one-form and a two-form whose appropriate wedge product defines a nowhere-vanishing top-degree form on an odd-dimensional manifold. We consider conformally compatible local geometric and Hamiltonian data and encode their gluing through a closed Lee form and the Lichnerowicz-de Rham differential. For locally conformal cosymplectic geometry, we introduce an equal-weight formulation in which the defining forms carry the same conformal weight. This formulation allows compatible local Hamiltonian vector fields to glue directly into a global Hamiltonian vector field without additional rescaling, thereby preserving the local dynamics. For contact geometry, we develop a twisted odd-pair formulation in which the Lee form records the conformal gluing of local Hamiltonian data, while the global one-form remains an ordinary contact form. We illustrate these constructions through time-dependent mass dynamics in the cosymplectic setting and dissipative particle dynamics in the contact setting.

papers.title: Invariant universal averages and Bertrand's paradox: a response to Shackel
papers.abstract: In 2014, with D. Aerts we proposed a solution to the hard problem of Bertrand's paradox by means of a universal average over different ways of randomizing an entity. In his recent monograph, N. Shackel raises objections concerning the approximation by cellular densities, the restrictions used in their construction, the apparently trivial limit of their averages, the choice of a second-order probability law, and the dependence of the result on the naming of chords. We revisit these objections using the invariance-based formulation of the universal average. The first objection is well taken, and the approximation argument is repaired: an explicit sequence of bivalent cellular densities provides weak approximation of any prescribed probability measure, with an error bound for intervals. We show that any second-order selection law invariant under rearrangements of equal-length cells has the same uniform barycenter, independently of the particular densities and weights employed. For cellular densities, this conclusion holds exactly at every finite resolution. Thus, non-uniqueness of the second-order law does not prevent uniqueness of the resulting average within the indifferent class. Finally, we prove that no probability measure can be invariant under both these rearrangements and arbitrary changes of interval lengths. The reference geometry therefore cannot be obtained by averaging alone: it must be supplied by the physical modelization of the randomized entity. These results clarify the scope, and the limitations, of our original distinction between the easy and hard problems of Bertrand's paradox.

papers.title: Optimal Learning in Fairness-Aware Contextual Bandits
papers.abstract: Mitigating unfair disparities in sequential decision-making is a growing concern in machine learning. We study contextual bandits under a global covariate-based Lipschitz fairness constraint, pioneered by \cite{dwork2012fairness}, requiring individuals with similar contexts to receive similar action distributions. We show that this constraint induces a randomisation region near the decision boundary and explicitly quantify the population level cost of fairness. We further establish a canonical representation of the optimal fair policy, which reduces the fair policy design to a lower-dimensional boundary optimisation problem. We develop a lazy fair greedy algorithm that exploits fairness-induced covariate diversity under continuous contexts, with policy updates computed via finite-dimensional linear programming. For general context distributions, including discrete and mixed contexts, we propose a lazy polyhedral upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm, whose optimistic optimisation reduces to finitely many linear programs over confidence-set vertices. Both methods satisfy fairness at every round and achieve regret of order $O(\sqrt{T} + T^{(d-2)/(d-1)}{\indc\{d\geq 4\}})$ up to poly-logarithmic factors, where $d$ is the dimension of the contexts. A matching minimax lower bound for $\ell_1$-based fairness establishes optimality, and reveals an unavoidable nonparametric cost of learning the decision boundary, which dominates the parametric learning cost when $d \geq 4$. Experiments on synthetic and real data support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.

papers.title: There is only one transitive Anosov flow (in dimension 3, with orientable foliations, up to bicontact padding and Goodman surgeries)
papers.abstract: We introduce a new surgical operation on Anosov flows, which we call bicontact padding surgery. The operation is defined using the machinery of strongly adapted bicontact structures, and involves inserting a 'padding' layer where one of the contact structures rotates many times around the Reeb flow of the other. We show that every skew Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a finite cover of a geodesic flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. Together with previous results, this implies that every transitive Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a suspension flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. This gives some progress towards the Christy-Fried-Ghys conjecture, which predicts that the same statement is true using only Goodman surgery.

papers.title: Curvature pinching for minimal Tangent-Yang-Mills hypersurfaces in spheres
papers.abstract: We prove a rigidity theorem for closed connected minimal Tangent-Yang-Mills hypersurfaces in the unit sphere. In every dimension $n\geqslant 3$, such a hypersurface is totally geodesic if the squared norm of its Riemannian curvature tensor is at most $2n(n-1)$.

papers.title: Convergence of non-symmetric forms with changing reference measures
papers.abstract: We develop a functional-analytic theory of convergence for non-symmetric generalized Dirichlet forms defined on a sequence of Hilbert spaces $H_n$ converging to a limit space $H$ in the sense of Kuwae-Shioya, with the principal applications concerning $L^2$-spaces over varying reference measures $μ_n \to μ$. Extending Mosco's variational convergence for Dirichlet forms to the non-symmetric setting via a functional controlling the off diagonal values of the forms, we introduce a notion of generalized convergence of non-symmetric Dirichlet forms and show it to be equivalent to strong convergence of the associated resolvents, to weak convergence of the co-resolvents, and to strong graph convergence of the infinitesimal generators. A version of the Trotter-Kato theorem in the Kuwae-Shioya framework yields the corresponding equivalence for $C_0$-contraction semigroups. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for the generalized convergence of elliptic and sectorial $a_{i,j}$-forms with changing speed measures, both on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and in infinite dimensions over a Gelfand triple, and deduce weak convergence of the laws of the associated right processes under tightness of the path measures.

papers.title: Decay Rate toward the Rarefaction Wave and the Viscous Contact Wave for Jin--Xin Relaxation Model
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the time-decay rates toward the rarefaction wave and the viscous contact wave for the one-dimensional Jin--Xin relaxation system under the $L^1$ integrability condition of the initial perturbation. In the case of a strictly convex flux, we employ a decomposition method to derive a logarithmic $L^1$ estimate related to a conjecture proposed by Liu\cite{liu2001lp}. Furthermore, a time-weighted $L^2$ method yields the optimal decay rate toward the rarefaction wave. Regarding the case where the flux is partially linearly degenerate, by employing a similar \(L^1\) estimate and time-weighted \(L^2\) method, along with a refined estimate of the nonlinear wave interactions, we obtain the corresponding decay rate toward the composite wave. The decay estimates are obtained without smallness assumptions on the initial perturbations or the wave strength.

papers.title: Categorifications of noncrossing partitions of type B and affine type A
papers.abstract: The lattice of wide subcategories of a tube is isomorphic to the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B. We prove that through this categorification of noncrossing partitions, Kreweras complement is taking left perpendicular categories. With the help of this categorification and weighted projective lines, we obtain an inclusion from the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B_n to a lattice of affine type A_n which preserves Kreweras complement.

papers.title: High-Frequency Estimation of the Leverage Effect under Rough Volatility with Microstructure Noise
papers.abstract: This paper develops feasible high-frequency inference for the leverage effect when the spot variance follows rough Volterra dynamics, leverage loadings depend on endogenous rough states, and observed prices may be contaminated by microstructure noise. We define an integrated leverage parameter through a scaled covariation between log prices and spot variance that accounts for their different local fluctuation scales. The scaled realized covariation admits a stable functional central limit theorem with an explicit pathwise centering correction arising from within-interval variation in the leverage loading. A loading regularity condition renders this correction asymptotically negligible, and we verify the condition for direct Volterra loadings and for smooth functions of closed rough states for every Hurst index below one half. We construct a block-based estimator with an exact finite-window correction for the leading proportional bias, together with a nonnegative single-scale estimator of its asymptotic variance. Pre-averaging extends feasible inference to observations with independent and identically distributed microstructure noise. Simulations under the rough Heston model demonstrate accurate finite-sample calibration with and without noise. An empirical application to fifteen years of one-second data on nine U.S. equities and ETFs finds negative median leverage estimates for every asset at weekly and monthly horizons.

papers.title: Markov-driven self-similar measures and non-homogeneous slicing
papers.abstract: We introduce the concept of Markov-driven self-similar measures, a notion that simultaneously generalizes classical self-similar measures, self-conformal measures, dynamically driven self-similar measures and many random measures. This class is also closed under Cartesian products and linear projections. We initiate the study of this class of measures and investigate the $L^q$ dimension of Markov-driven self-similar measures under certain Diophantine conditions. As an application, we obtain the first Furstenberg slicing type results for intersections of Cantor sets in non-homogeneous settings.

papers.title: Linear resolutions of powers of edge ideals of gap-free graphs with matching number four
papers.abstract: For a finite simple gap-free graph $G$, let $B(G)$ denote the vertices $v$ for which $G-N_G[v]$ is not co-chordal, and put $C(G)=V(G)\setminus B(G)$. We prove a sufficient condition for all ordinary powers of its edge ideal to have linear resolutions from the second power onward: every induced anticycle of length at least five must contain an edge with both endpoints in $C(G)$. The argument uses variable generators of augmented colon ideals to eliminate anticycles that may persist in the ordinary quadratic colons. It yields linear resolutions for all powers $I(G)^q$, $q\ge2$, whenever the ordinary matching number is at most four, which answers the first part of a question of Erey, Hà, Hibi, Kara and Morey. The criterion also applies to certain graphs with adjacent exceptional vertices and matching number five. The proofs are theoretical and valid over arbitrary fields.
