The proof uses discharging; the case $Δ=6$ is computer-assisted.

papers.title: Sharpness transitions for weighted Triebel--Lizorkin Hardy inequalities with p < q
papers.abstract: For two-weight fractional difference energies with inner and outer exponents $1<p<q$, we study the optimality of the Hardy constant generated by a homogeneous power. We prove nontrivial sharpness intervals for every sign of $D=d+2β-sp$, including a two-sided interval when $D=0$, and strict loss of optimality near both finite-energy endpoints. For $q\ge2$, sharpness extends beyond the elementary pointwise scalar criterion through an integrated remainder estimate: after opposite logarithmic displacements are combined, a positive contribution at bounded displacements absorbs the negative contribution at larger displacements. A single quadratic reference energy controls this comparison and the angular fluctuations of near-extremizers. When $1<p<q<2$, optimization of the scalar supporting-line inequality gives the exact power exponent for that criterion and a larger explicit sharpness interval. Angular variations provide explicit strict-loss examples. The method extends to flat singular sets and regional half-space energies, with separate finiteness ranges for test energies and the homogeneous candidate. Complementary results for $p>q$ include flat-subspace inequalities. The constants are optimal on the stated smooth test classes and extend unchanged to their difference-norm completions whenever they are positive.

papers.title: Profinite groups whose closed subgroups are subnormal of defect at most two
papers.abstract: In this paper, we classify profinite groups whose closed subgroups are subnormal of defect at most two, providing profinite versions of theorems due to Heineken and to Mahdavianary. We also establish that if G is a finitely generated periodic pro-π group, where π is a finite set of odd primes, and all its procyclic subgroups are subnormal of defect at most 2, then G is a finite π-group in which every abelian subgroup is subnormal of defect at most 2.

papers.title: Dispersive Tree Agreements for Multi-Robot Coordination
papers.abstract: Multi-robot coordination of nonlinear systems is naturally formulated as joint-space optimal control subject to joint constraints. Existing methods that approach joint optimality remain largely centralized and offline, while decentralized, real-time counterparts target safe navigation without pursuing the joint optimum. This paper develops a decentralized, real-time planner that approaches the joint optimum as an anytime process. We extend a recent single-robot framework that searches dispersive trees of forward-propagated commands to coordinate a multi-robot team near-optimally. We first show that the inter-robot coupling can be effectively replaced by some local constraints, under which locally grown dispersive trees contain a near-optimal agreement. It is this structure that the robots pursue by a negotiation driven by decentralized column generation. In the quiescent limit, this negotiation is shown to settle on a near-optimal agreement. Our real-time protocol, WarpWeaver, runs the negotiation asynchronously over a receding horizon and closes on quiesced agreements even when deadlines cut it short. In simulation, WarpWeaver reduces total travel time by up to 22% against centralized offline planners on the Dynobench suite and by up to 16% against a decentralized real-time baseline, and outperforms a task-specific planner on networked navigation. Hardware experiments on six robots planning onboard demonstrate real-world implementability.

papers.title: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets
papers.abstract: A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.

papers.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
papers.abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2πi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).

papers.title: Triangulation, Volume, and Symmetries of a Dihedral Group Analogue of the Permutohedron
papers.abstract: We study an analogue of the permutohedron for the dihedral group, which we call the dihedral permutohedron. We determine the facet structure of the dihedral permutohedron, use the facet structure to construct a triangulation, and determine a nice combinatorial formula for the volume of the dihedral permutohedron. Lastly, we find a family of interesting unimodular affine symmetries of the odd dihedral permutohedron.

papers.title: On Nonlocal Equations under Symmetries
papers.abstract: In this work, we establishes results of existence and regularity for solutions to nonlocal equations of the form $f(Δ)u = U(x,u(x)) ~\text{and}~f(Δ_{g})u=U(x,u(x))$ in the Euclidean context and Riemannian context respectively. We extend the results of \cite{Gorka 6} for the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ under cylindrically symmetry and compact Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ under action of a closed Lie subgroup $G \leq \text{Isom}_{g}(M)$. Our approach combines spectral theory, complex interpolation and fixed-point methods.

papers.title: Simple Strategy-Iteration with Dantzig's Rule is not Strongly Polynomial on Turn-Based Deterministic Games
papers.abstract: We study turn-based deterministic zero-sum games with discounted and long-run average costs. For discounted costs, we establish exponential and superpolynomial iteration lower bounds for the simple strategy-iteration method with Dantzig's rule under unrestricted costs and unit weights, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, we establish for the first time that the method is not strongly polynomial, and this remains true even when all action costs belong to $\{-1,0,1\}$. For long-run average costs, we extend the Dantzig counterpart in~\cite{zhongye2026} to the two-player setting and prove that it terminates at an optimal strategy profile. However, a similar counterexample construction establishes an exponential iteration lower bound for termination with unrestricted costs. This construction does not extend to unit weights, for which we prove that the algorithm admits a strongly polynomial implementation.

papers.title: Mutually touching cylinders: Littlewood's seven, and at most ten in general
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that at most seven congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ can touch pairwise. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968. For cylinders of arbitrary radii we prove the upper bound ten. Whether ten can be attained remains open.

papers.title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern-Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux-charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov-Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel-Watts theory.

papers.title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
papers.abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $dγ_n=π^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12Δ+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_γ=DL^{-1/2}Π_0$, where $Π_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_γ$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(γ_n)$ and $a>\int F\,dγ_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/π$ for complex-valued inputs.

papers.title: The Yau Geometric Conjecture for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: This paper presents a proof of the long-standing Yau Geometric Conjecture.

papers.title: The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in real quadratic function fields
papers.abstract: In the thirties of the last century, I.\,M. Vinogradov proved that the inequality $\|pα\|\le p^{-1/5+\varepsilon}$ has infinitely many prime solutions $p$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the distance to a nearest integer. This result has subsequently been improved by many authors. In particular, Vaughan (1978) replaced the exponent $1/5$ by $1/4$, using his celebrated identity for the von Mangoldt function and a refinement of Fourier analytic arguments. The current record is due to Matomäki (2009), who showed that the inequality $\|pα\|\le p^{-1/3+\varepsilon}$ has infinitely many prime solutions. This exponent $1/3$ is considered the limit of current technology. Baier and the author established an analogue of Matomäki's result for the function field $k=\Fq(T)$ and its imaginary quadratic extensions. Moreover, for real quadratic extensions of $k$ of class number one, they obtained an analogue of Vaughan's result (exponent $1/4$). In this paper, we establish the analogue of Matomäki's result for all real quadratic extensions of $k$ without any restriction on the class number.

papers.title: A general recipe for data-adaptive anytime-valid envelopes for iterative algorithms
papers.abstract: Most convergence guarantees for iterative stochastic algorithms are stated at a fixed iteration count and do not justify stopping at a data-dependent time. Recent anytime-valid envelopes do, but deterministic ones are typically too conservative for practical stopping, and existing data-adaptive ones are derived case-by-case, each concerned with a specific algorithm and a specific noise model and boundary construction. This paper provides a general recipe for sharp, data-adaptive anytime-valid envelopes for a large class of iterative algorithms. Our approach has two key steps: an optimization module derives a one-step recursion that performance measures of many such algorithms satisfy, reducing the error analysis to time-uniform concentration for predictably weighted sums of noise. Then, a statistical module ports the sub-$ψ$ condition to vector-valued processes, uniformly over predictable weights, and derives off-the-shelf boundaries via mixtures, stitching, and product betting martingales. Combining the two yields readymade envelopes for many iterative algoithms including but not limited to stochastic gradient descent (SGD), Oja's algorithm, temporal difference learning, Q-learning, and Bures-Wasserstein SGD, many with no prior data-adaptive anytime-valid guarantees. Specifically, for SGD, our framework recovers, often under weaker conditions, or significantly sharpens every existing envelope we are aware of. Our constructions come with explicit implementation details and are substantiated by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Event-Triggered Funnel Control for Output Reference Tracking of Unknown Nonlinear Systems
papers.abstract: We propose an event-triggered zero-order hold implementation of the funnel controller for output reference tracking of unknown nonlinear systems. The control input is updated only when the deviation between the current and the last transmitted input exceeds a prescribed threshold, reducing the number of input updates while maintaining closed-loop performance guarantees by incorporating an auxiliary integral state to compensate for the error introduced by the zero-order-hold input. We establish a uniform lower bound on the inter-event intervals excluding Zeno behavior, and derive a growth condition on the nonlinear dynamics that ensures global existence of the solution for arbitrary, predefined sampling schedules. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical simulations.

papers.title: Gaps between roots in ballistic deposition on a strip: linear variance, Gaussian limits and a Poisson regime
papers.abstract: Mansour, Rastegar and Roitershtein studied the \emph{roots} of ballistic deposition on a cyclic strip of $K$ sites, namely the sites that receive a particle at height one, and the number $D_{i,K}$ of pairs of consecutive roots at distance $i+1$. They computed the first two moments of $D_{i,K}$ for $i\le7$. They conjectured that for every $i$ the mean and the variance are exactly linear in $K$, that $D_{i,K}$ satisfies a central limit theorem, and that the standardized vector $(D_{i,K})_{i\ge1}$ converges to a Gaussian process. We prove these conjectures. The key observation is that the roots are exactly the valleys of a uniformly random circular arrangement, so that $D_{i,K}$ counts occurrences of a family of consecutive patterns. We determine sizes from which the moments are exactly linear; the size for the mean is sharp for every $i$, and those for the second moments cannot be lowered in any case we checked. We give closed forms for the variance constants and for the limiting covariance; the mean constants agree with a known distribution of distances between surface peaks. The reduction and the exact moment formulas are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib. We also prove a Wasserstein bound of order $(\mathbb{E} D_{i,K})^{-1/2}$ that is uniform in $i$, and a local limit theorem. Finally we describe the limit completely when $i$ grows with $K$: it is degenerate, Poisson or Gaussian according as $\mathbb{E} D_{i,K}$ tends to zero, to a positive constant, or to infinity.

papers.title: The Big Match under translation-invariant charges
papers.abstract: We study finite two-player zero-sum stochastic games in which the stream of expected stage payoffs is evaluated by a translation-invariant charge on the set of stages. Every patient valuation, that is, every diffuse charge that obeys the time value of money principle, is translation-invariant. By Mertens and Neyman (1981), every finite two-player zero-sum stochastic game has a value; in particular, each player has, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a strategy that is $\varepsilon$-optimal for all patient valuations simultaneously. We show that this robustness breaks down for translation-invariant charges, even when the charge is fixed in advance. In the Big Match with $0$--$1$ payoffs, for every charge, Player~2 can guarantee that Player~1's payoff is at most $1/2$, but cannot guarantee any smaller bound. Nevertheless, we construct a fixed translation-invariant charge such that, for every strategy of Player~1 and every $δ>0$, Player~2 has a pure reply yielding payoff less than $δ$. Consequently, the Big Match has no value under this charge. More generally, the supremum of the payoffs that Player~1 can guarantee ranges over $[0,1/2]$ as the translation-invariant charge varies. This contrasts with finite Markov decision processes, where every stationary Blackwell optimal strategy is optimal for every translation-invariant charge.

papers.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $Σ$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,Φ)$ with $(E,Φ)\cong(E,-Φ)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,Φ)$ corresponds to a representation $ρ$ of $π_1(Σ)$, then $(E,-Φ)$ corresponds to $(\overlineρ^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $η\mapsto-η$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.

papers.title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
papers.abstract: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{ξ_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{ξ_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^α}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ α=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ α=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ α>-1/2 $ is also obtained.

papers.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
papers.abstract: We study Galois coinvariants of the geometric étale fundamental group and étale cohomology of varieties over a finitely generated field $k$. We establish finiteness properties of these coinvariants for (possibly infinite) Galois extensions $L/k$ such that $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As applications, we obtain finiteness results for $L$-rational torsion points on abelian varieties and étale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over number fields.

papers.title: Hölder regularity for metric Anosov flows
papers.abstract: We define a class of flows on compact metric spaces that we call $C^α$ metric Anosov flows, $0 < α< 1$ or $α= \mathrm{Lip}$. We give verifiable criteria for a metric Anosov flow to be $C^α$. We show that $C^α$ metric Anosov flows have Hölder continuous local product structure, and in particular Hölder continuous holonomies. We deduce that topological conjugacies between $C^α$ metric Anosov flows are automatically Hölder continuous. We show that any $C^α$ metric Anosov flow admits a strong (i.e. Hölder continuous) Markov coding. This yields strong ergodic properties for equilibrium states for Hölder potentials for transitive $C^α$ metric Anosov flows. The regularity of the local product structure is proved in a non-compact setting which applies for the geodesic flow on the universal cover of a locally CAT(-1) space. This allows us to obtain Hölder regularity results for the holonomy maps for pinched negative curvature manifolds with respect to the Sasaki metric. This contrasts with the result of Ballmann, Brin and Burns that there are examples in this class for which the dynamical distributions are not Hölder.

papers.title: Quasiconformal uniformization and extension for planar trees
papers.abstract: A quasiconformal uniformization theorem of Rickman from 1966 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane. We prove an analogous uniformization theorem for planar trees by showing that every planar quasiconformal tree with uniform branch separation is quasiconformally equivalent to a quasiconvex planar tree with uniform branch separation and Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to 1. Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipschitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: Local Fan-type obstructions and Ore-type conditions for rainbow Hamiltonicity in graph systems
papers.abstract: Let $G=(G_1,...,G_n)$ be a graph system on a common $n$-vertex set $V$. For $v\in V$, set \[ δ(v)=\min_{i\in[n]}d_{G_i}(v), \qquad E_{\cap}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n E(G_i), \] and let $d^c(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest rainbow $u$--$v$ path. We study Hamiltonicity conditions imposed only on pairs at small rainbow distance. Suppose that every $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that \[ δ(u),δ(v)<\frac n2, \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad uv\in E_{\cap}. \] Our main result shows that any system satisfying this local Fan-type condition but containing no rainbow Hamilton cycle must satisfy \[ E_{\cap}=\varnothing, \qquad \sum_{v\in V}δ(v)\le\frac{n^2-1}{2}. \] Consequently, either $E_{\cap}\ne\varnothing$ or $\sum_{v\in V}δ(v)\ge\lceil n^2/2\rceil$ guarantees a rainbow Hamilton cycle. We further prove that the local Ore-type condition \[ δ(u)+δ(v)<n, \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad uv\in E_{\cap} \] already forces a rainbow Hamilton cycle. Along the way, the Fan-type hypothesis yields a rainbow Hamilton path and a rainbow $(n-1)$-cycle. For diagonal systems, our conditions reduce to the classical Fan and local Ore conditions. The proofs combine rainbow rotation--extension with a double-counting argument in an auxiliary digraph. Keywords: graph system; rainbow Hamilton cycle; rainbow distance; Fan-type condition; Ore-type condition; rotation--extension.

papers.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
papers.abstract: Given an integer $k \geq 2$, there are integers $M_k$ and $P_k$ so that for all $A \subseteq \mathbb F^n_p$ does not contain a restricted polynomial progression of the form \begin{align*} x, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n \end{pmatrix}, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^2 \\ y_2^2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n^2 \end{pmatrix}, \ldots, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^{k-1} \\ y_2^{k-1} \\ \vdots \\ y_n^{k-1} \end{pmatrix}, \end{align*} where $x \in \mathbb F^n_p$, with $p>P_k$, and $y \in \{0,2, 3, \ldots, M_k\}^n \backslash \{\vec{0} \}$, for some fixed $M_k$, then $A$ must have density bounded above by $\frac{C}{(\log^{(k^{O(k)})} n)^c}$, where $C, c>0$ only depend on $k$ and $p$. For $k\geq 4$, the best previously known bound came from the density Hales--Jewett theorem and was of inverse Ackermann type. The proof uses a recent inverse theorem for noise stability of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer, which arose in the study of constraint satisfaction problems. The main new ingredient is a proof that the underlying distribution counting restricted polynomial progressions does not admit a nontrivial abelian embedding, by way of an involved algebraic argument. Reasonable bounds are provided for $P_k$ and $M_k$.

papers.title: Terminal Blocks of Primes in Pisot Numeration Systems
papers.abstract: We prove a prime number theorem for fixed terminal block words in a family of Pisot integer numeration systems defined by canonical block expansions. Suppose that the dominant root $\varphi$ is a Pisot number and that the characteristic polynomial $P_h$ is its minimal polynomial. Then every terminal block word of total digit-length $m$ occurs among the primes with asymptotic frequency $\varphi^{-m}$. The result recovers the known Zeckendorf and generalized Fibonacci cases and extends the terminal-prime problem to irreducible Pisot-unit systems without assuming that the recurrence coefficients are monotone, that the canonical expansions are greedy, or that the finiteness property (F) holds. Explicit non-$β$ families and Pisot units failing (F) illustrate this extension. The main structural ingredient is a canonical block language whose expansion of the companion substitution fixed word records the corresponding integer expansions in natural order. This connects terminal conditions with Rauzy cylinder windows and then with a linear orbit on a compact torus. The required multiplicity-one geometry follows from Barge's pure-discreteness theorem after reversal of the substitution words. The same toral model yields prime genericity for finite factors of the substitution fixed word, polynomial sampling laws, asymptotic independence from fixed congruence classes, fixed-shift correlation formulas, and Möbius orthogonality. Combined with established prime theorems, it also gives a terminal refinement of Chebotarev and arithmetic progressions inside fixed terminal prime classes.

papers.title: Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations and Mixed-Type Chebyshev Multiple Orthogonal Polynomials
papers.abstract: We characterize when a semi-infinite banded totally positive matrix admits a positive bidiagonal factorization, without assuming boundedness, and establish criteria for stability under perturbations. These criteria distinguish whether the initial factor entries are fixed or allowed to vary. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, such factorizations always exist; a factorization can be chosen to depend analytically on all sufficiently small perturbations within the same band if and only if the polynomial symbol has distinct roots. Explicit root formulas determine the associated mixed-type multiple orthogonal polynomials and their matrix of positive measures. They also yield scalar linear forms independent of the chosen factorization, from which we obtain asymptotic zero spacing and sine-kernel limits. We further treat finite boundary modifications and limiting zero distributions for matrices with convergent diagonals.

papers.title: A New Upper Bound for 7-Universal Tournaments
papers.abstract: A tournament is $k$-universal if it contains every tournament on $k$ vertices as a subtournament. We give a 7-universal tournament on 14 vertices, improving the upper bound of 15 due to Zhang and Szeider. Together with their lower bound, it follows that the smallest 7-universal tournament has 13 or 14 vertices.

papers.title: A natural Chow lemma for smooth threefolds and fourfolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth proper integral variety of dimension at most four over a field of characteristic zero. We construct a finite sequence of blowups along smooth centers with projective endpoint, preserving the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective opens of $X$. The construction depends only on a fixed functorial principalization procedure and is natural under isomorphisms, including those over different ground fields. The proof has two parts. A colength argument on regular local surfaces gives, in every dimension, a finite preparation after which some maximal quasi-projective open has complement mapping into codimension at least three in $X$. In dimensions at most four these images are points or curves. Ample numerical classes on the normalized components of that complement give finite bounds for summing base ideals of linear systems. The resulting ideal descends to the original field; geometric integrality is not required.

papers.title: Sharp Convergence and Sample Complexity of Policy Mirror Descent for Average-Reward MDPs
papers.abstract: Policy mirror descent (PMD) has a mature finite-time theory in discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs), but less is known in the average-reward setting, a more natural objective for many control applications. We give a finite-time, finite-sample analysis of PMD in ergodic average-reward MDPs built around a single master recursion that governs convergence for any critic, without external regularization. Its specializations yield linear rates for exact, inexact-tabular, and linear function approximation (LFA) updates. For exact PMD, the rate is tight in the worst case, and convergence can become superlinear. We complement these convergence results with critics whose end-to-end sample complexities improve the prior best policy-gradient dependence from $|S||A|\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^3$ to $|S|\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^3+|S||A|\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^2$ in the tabular setting and from $|S||A|\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^5$ to $d\,t_{\mathrm{mix}}^3$ under LFA. Matching information-theoretic lower bounds establish that both critics are optimal up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: A power-commutator presentation for the group of truncated polynomials under substitution
papers.abstract: Given a prime $p$, the Nottingham group $G(p)$ is the group of formal power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots$, $a_i\in{\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}$, under substitution. For $n\geq 1$, we write $G_n(p)$ for the quotient of $G(p)$ by its normal subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in {\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}\}$, namely the group of truncated polynomials $x+a_2x^2+\cdots+a_nx^n$, $a_i\in {\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}$, under substitution, which is a $p$-group of order $p^{n-1}$ generated by $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^n$. In this paper, we determine the power-commutator presentation of $G_{15}(p)$ relative to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{15}$. This, in turn, automatically gives the power-commutator presentation of $G_{n}(p)$ relative to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{n}$ for any $1\leq n<15$, as well as the initial segments of the power and commutator relations in $G_{n}(p)$ corresponding to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{15}$ for any $n>15$.

papers.title: The edge case of the Hilbert matrix operator between weighted Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: The Hilbert matrix operator $H$ is bounded on the standard weighted Bergman spaces $A^p_α,\, p>α+2>1$. We examine the limiting case when $α=p-2$, and for $p\leq 2$, we characterize the logarithmic modification of the standard weight needed for the domain $A^p_{v_{γ,p}}$ and codomain $A^p_{v_{β,p}}$ to ensure boundedness. In particular, we prove that $H:A^2_{\log^γ} \to A^2_{\log^β}$ is bounded if and only if $γ-β\geq 2$ and $γ>1$, solving an open problem posed by B. Karapetrović and M. Jevtić. We also settle the situation for $p>2$ in all cases, except when the logarithmic exponents $γ$ and $β$ satisfy $γ-β=p$. Moreover, we completely solve the same problem when the domain and codomain are certain weighted reflexive $\ell^p$ spaces. All results are extended to the generalized Hilbert operator $H_g$.

papers.title: Integrating Learning and Optimization for Open Transport Capacity Pooling under Disruption
papers.abstract: Disruptions can leave logistics networks short of capacity, yet outside capacity is hard to use: incumbent models are private, provider records are incomplete, and offers stay hidden until a costly request for quotation (RFQ). We introduce open capacity pooling as a budgeted provider-discovery problem that links which capacity need to pursue, whom to contact, and which verified offer to admit. The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) coordinates incumbents without sharing models, and the resulting capacity gaps direct discovery. A machine-learning layer fitted before search ranks providers by predicted capability and a fleet-size proxy from directory records and large language model (LLM) readings of self-descriptions. Verification reveals offers, reduced-cost screening admits them, and re-optimization updates the gaps and prices. Under fixed offers and exact coordination, a full-revelation reference reaches the finite-universe optimum, while budgeted discovery remains heuristic. We evaluate the mechanism on 4,509 real firms in three US regions excluded from predictor training, using scenarios calibrated to seven historical disruptions and simulated availability, offered quantities, and prices. With 80 RFQs, about 1% of exhaustive search, the mechanism recovers 19-43% of the full-information value of outside transport, against 2-6% for random search, and saves USD 73,000-104,000 per event before search and contracting costs. At tight RFQ budgets, gap-guided need selection and learned ranking are complements in these testbeds. LLM reading helps rank capabilities that records omit, such as refrigerated service, but its operating value varies by region. The results support combining record-based learning with coordination-derived gaps under limited search budgets.

papers.title: Stanley-Reisner Theory in Mixed Characteristic
papers.abstract: We discuss a class of mixed characteristic rings defined analogously to Stanley-Reisner rings by replacing one variable with a uniformizing parameter for a discrete valuation ring. We adapt Hochster's formula for Tor and Ext modules, Hochster's formula for local cohomology, and Terai's criterion for Serre conditions to this new setting; one of the tools needed is cellular sheaf cohomology, for which we give a brief treatment.

papers.title: No infinite spin in the $n$-body problem in all dimensions
papers.abstract: In the planar $n$-body problem, Moeckel and Montgomery \cite{MM25} showed that there is no infinite spin for total collision solutions, when the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Following their approach, generalizations have been obtained for partial collision solutions and parabolic solutions in the planar case, and for total collision solutions in the spatial cases by various authors, all under the same assumption that the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Here we prove there is no infinite spin for any collision or parabolic solution in all dimensions without such an assumption.

papers.title: A Nearly Quadratic Lower Bound for Linear Optimization over Convex Bodies in the Membership Oracle Model
papers.abstract: We prove nearly quadratic lower bounds for randomized algorithms for linear optimization and uniform sampling over convex bodies in the membership oracle model. For linear optimization, this matches the known nearly quadratic upper bound up to a polylog factor in the dimension. For uniform sampling, this improves on the previous linear lower bound. Our construction also implies the same lower bound for volume estimation.

papers.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
papers.abstract: We prove that a compact Brody-hyperbolic manifold carrying a strictly positive quasi-closed plurinegative $(1,1)$-current has nef canonical bundle, which is ample if every positive Lelong level set has complex dimension at most two. We also establish Kähler rigidity of the prescribed Hermitian metric for nonpositive constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature on compact manifolds in Fujiki's class and for nonzero constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature on compact complex threefolds. In complex dimension four, we prove that every balanced Hermitian metric with nonzero constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature is Kähler, without assuming compactness or completeness. Under the same curvature assumption, dimension inequalities for the subspaces spanned by the image of the $(1,0)$ covariant derivative of the Chern torsion and its iterated images under Chern curvature endomorphisms imply Kählerness in dimensions at least five for balanced metrics and at least four without balancedness. At zero Chern holomorphic sectional curvature, we construct compact balanced examples in every complex dimension at least seven that are not Chern flat. However, on a compact connected Hermitian manifold with zero Chern holomorphic sectional curvature and vanishing first Chern--Ricci tensor, the prescribed metric is Kähler flat whenever the manifold admits a smooth semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form positive definite at some point.

papers.title: A Quaternary Legendre Pair of Length 64
papers.abstract: A quaternary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ is a pair of sequences over $\{\pm 1, \pm \mathrm{i}\}$ whose periodic autocorrelations sum to $-2$ at every nonzero shift. We give a quaternary Legendre pair of length $64$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported construction at this length.

papers.title: Evaluations of Series Using the Beta Function
papers.abstract: This article presents proofs of seven conjectural series identities for $π$ proposed by Z.-W. Sun. Our proofs rely mainly on transformations involving the Beta function. We also use symbolic integration with the software \texttt{Mathematica} to reduce the amount of computational work.

papers.title: Jordan-Hölder theory for complementary polyhedra and moduli of parahoric Higgs torsors
papers.abstract: We extend Behrend's theory of complementary polyhedra to include Jordan-Hölder theory by introducing the notion of Jordan-Hölder facets. As a consequence, we can construct Jordan-Hölder parabolic subgroup schemes for reductive group schemes over a smooth projective curve. We use these results to provide a uniform approach to describing Jordan-Hölder filtrations and S-equivalence of moduli stacks of semistable bundles, including vector bundles, principal bundles, parabolic bundles, parahoric torsors, and parahoric Higgs torsors, following Zhang. We explicitly give a description of Jordan-Hölder filtrations and S-equivalence in the semistable locus of parahoric torsors and parahoric Higgs torsors, coming from their good moduli spaces, as constructed by Alper-Halpern-Leistner-Heinloth and Réga. This application uses the Rees construction, as given by Heinloth, to identify filtrations of moduli stacks of parahoric torsors with reductions of parahoric torsors to parabolic subgroups, inducing Jordan-Hölder stratifications of the moduli stacks.

papers.title: A Sharp Sobolev Inequality on Compact CR Manifolds
papers.abstract: For any \(n\geq 1\), let \((M,θ)\) be a compact strictly pseudoconvex hypersurface type CR manifold with dimension \(2n+1\), \(Q=2n+2\) be its homogeneous dimension. We prove the sharp Folland--Stein Sobolev inequality on \(M\): if \(Q^*=2Q/(Q-2)\), then there exists a constant \(A>0\), depending only on \((M,θ)\), such that \[ \|u\|_{L^{Q^*}(M)}^2 \le K(n)^2\|\nabla_b u\|_{L^2(M)}^2 + A\|u\|_{L^2(M)}^2, \qquad u\in S^{1,2}(M). \] Here \(K(n)\) is the sharp constant in the Folland--Stein Sobolev inequality on the Heisenberg group \(\mathbb H^n\).

papers.title: Local Well-Posedness of the Unsteady Boundary Layer System for Dilatant Power-Law Fluids
papers.abstract: We establish local-in-time existence and uniqueness of monotone classical solutions to the two-dimensional nonstationary boundary layer equations for dilatant power-law fluids in a periodic half-space, for every fixed exponent $n>1$. The result holds under Oleinik's monotonicity condition and suitable weighted Sobolev, algebraic decay, and compatibility assumptions. The main difficulties are the tangential derivative loss caused by the normal velocity and the degeneracy at infinity of the principal coefficient $nω^{n-1}$ in the nonlinear vorticity diffusion $\partial_y^2(ω^n)$, where $ω=\partial_y u$. We adapt the Masmoudi-Wong energy method and use a good unknown to control the tangential derivative loss. For the nonlinear diffusion, we separate the estimates near the boundary from the treatment of degeneracy in the far field. Nonlinear boundary reduction and localized trace estimates control the boundary terms, while weighted estimates exploit the compensating decay of vorticity derivatives to control the diffusion commutators. Together with tangential regularization and weighted maximum and minimum principles, these estimates yield bounds uniform in the regularization parameter and preserve weighted monotonicity. Under these assumptions, the result provides an affirmative local-in-time answer to the existence and uniqueness question in Open Problem~11 of Oleinik and Samokhin.

papers.title: Ramanujan Transforms and Maximum Energy of Odd-Total-Exponent Integral Circulants
papers.abstract: For a finite graph, its energy is the sum of the absolute values of its adjacency eigenvalues. Let n be the product of powers of distinct odd primes, where all exponents are positive integers, the sum of the exponents is odd, and every prime whose exponent is odd is at least five. Among all nonempty sets of proper divisors of n, the energy of the corresponding integral circulant graph is uniquely maximised by the checkerboard divisor set consisting of those divisors for which the sum of the prime-power exponents is even. The maximum energy is one half of the sum of n and the product, over all prime factors, of explicit polynomial quantities. For exponent k and parameter x, the corresponding polynomial is given by two k plus one times x to the k-th power, together with four times the sum from zero to k minus one of j plus one times x to the j-th power with alternating sign determined by the parity of k minus j. For the proof, we use weighted prime-power Ramanujan transforms, which give an exact energy model in tensor form and extend to a polynomial matrix family for real parameters greater than one. A semidefinite parity theorem shows that the matrix obtained from this polynomial family by an explicit positive diagonal normalisation is a real symmetric contraction whose unique eigenvalue of modulus one is the simple eigenvalue determined by the parity of the exponent; this holds for even exponents at least two and parameters at least three, and for odd exponents at least one and parameters at least five. Tensorising this spectral structure and centring the binary divisor tensor yield a sharp one-norm bound for the corresponding tensor operator on sign vectors. In particular, for n equal to p squared times q cubed, with distinct odd primes p and q and with q at least five, this proves Roldan's conjectured maximality in this range.

papers.title: Waveguiding in systems of high contrast resonators: Theory and fast computations
papers.abstract: In this work, we study guided modes in systems of high-contrast resonators near nonzero interior Neumann frequencies, beyond the subwavelength regime. In the regular exterior regime, where the exterior Dirichlet problem is well-posed at the reference wavenumber, we introduce an infinite-dimensional frequency-dependent capacitance operator obtained by compressing the exterior Helmholtz Dirichlet-to-Neumann map to the traces of the interior resonant Neumann eigenspaces. We prove the norm-resolvent convergence of the continuous problem to this discrete effective operator as the contrast $δ\to0$, and derive first-order asymptotic formulas for compact-defect frequencies and line-defect band functions. We then establish exponential off-diagonal decay of the capacitance coefficients by a Combes--Thomas argument, yielding an exponentially accurate truncation of the discrete operator, and show that its retained coefficients can be computed from local Helmholtz problems. At the physical frequency, this local approximation converges exponentially under a uniform stability assumption for the growing finite-cluster problems. The stability assumption can be removed by introducing a vanishing complex absorption together with a Hermitian symmetrization. In particular, an absorption parameter of order $\sqrtδ$, together with interaction truncation and patch radii of order $|\logδ|$, suffices to preserve the $O(δ^2)$ accuracy of the first-order high-contrast expansion of the defect eigenfrequencies, yielding a fast computational method. Numerical experiments for dipole and quadrupole resonances illustrate the accuracy, exponential locality, and applicability of the discrete model to straight and bent waveguides generated by material or geometric detuning.

papers.title: Wave Selection at an $O(2)$-Hopf Bifurcation in Conservative Two-Component PDE Systems
papers.abstract: At an $O(2)$-equivariant Hopf bifurcation a spatially periodic system selects between traveling waves and standing waves, and which branch appears and whether it is stable is decided by two cubic normal form coefficients. Obtaining these coefficients for a given PDE has required a derivation carried out afresh for each model. We remove that step for two-component systems with conservative polynomial differential nonlinearities on a one-dimensional periodic domain, deriving closed form formulas for both coefficients. They are expressed directly in terms of the array of nonlinear PDE coefficients and the spectral data of the linearization, its critical eigenvectors, adjoint eigenvectors, and non-critical resolvents. We give verifiable conditions under which the underlying center manifold reduction is valid. A structural condition on the principal part of the linearization, together with sign conditions on the trace and determinant of its Fourier symbol, yields the resolvent estimate and the spectral gap that the reduction requires. A companion implementation evaluates the two normal form coefficients from the coefficient array and verifies the assumptions for a given system. We specialize the formulas to two applications: a strain-gradient regularization of the nonlinear $p$-system, whose quadratic case contains a previously studied model as a special case, and a first order conservative bilinear family, not previously analyzed, in which every bifurcation scenario allowed by the general classification is realized.

papers.title: A Sharp Refinement of Samuels' Inequality via Cap Moves
papers.abstract: Let $0\le μ_1\le μ_2 \le \cdots \le μ_n$ and $δ> 0$. Samuels' conjecture states that if $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are independent non-negative random variables with $\mathbb{E}[X_i] = μ_i$, then $$ \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^n X_i < δ+ \sum_{i=1}^n μ_i \right) \ge \min_{1\le i\le n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left(1-\frac{μ_j}{δ+ \sum_{k=i}^n μ_k}\right).$$ This conjecture was recently proved by Ling. In this note, we prove a refinement of Samuels' inequality via an operation called the \emph{cap move}. Our refined inequality is sharp, with equality attained for a strictly larger class of distributions than in the original inequality.

papers.title: When more data become less informative: Finite-precision periodicization and collapse of forecast-error Lyapunov estimates
papers.abstract: Equation-free forecast-error analysis is useful when governing equations, Jacobians, tangent dynamics, or full state vectors are unavailable and only scalar time series are observed. In this setting, the multi-horizon forecast-error curve can provide both an instability estimate and nonlinear predictive features, making its numerical reliability important. We show that long finite-precision chaotic records can enter an information-saturation regime in which increasing record length N (the total number of analyzed samples) adds repeated histories rather than new dynamical information. For the float32 logistic map, exact recurrence progressively fills the training catalogue with duplicate histories and identical futures, suppressing forecast-error growth and driving the estimated Lyapunov slope toward zero. Across 10,000 initial conditions, exact recurrence occurred by iteration 7612; across 28 stratified seeds, collapse onset strongly followed the recurrence-occupancy scale. A two-dimensional Hénon-map control confirms that recurrence and estimator failure are separate events: the float32 trajectory enters an exact machine-state cycle after a transient of $μ= 103,039$ samples, with cycle period P = 12,268, yet the forecast-error estimate remains close to the positive Jacobian/QR reference until catalogue saturation near N = 200,000. Casting an already generated float32 record to float64 does not restore lost information, whereas genuine float64 generation, restarted short trajectories, and one-ULP perturbations prevent collapse over the tested range. A recursive local-linear predictor exhibits the same endpoint at a later, predictor-dependent threshold. The results identify a recurrence-to-catalogue-saturation failure mode specific to forecast-error/analogue inference rather than Lyapunov estimation in general.

papers.title: A new strong rigidity phenomenon for the Bergman metric
papers.abstract: We establish a new local-to-global rigidity phenomenon for the Bergman metric. Namely, under natural geometric hypotheses, a local conformal identification of Bergman metrics determines the underlying complex manifold globally, up to the unavoidable ambiguity of removing Bergman-negligible subsets. More precisely, let $Ω\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain with a complete Bergman metric, and suppose that the Bergman metric of a complex manifold $M$ is locally conformal, via a holomorphic map $f$, to that of $Ω$, with a constant conformal factor when $n=1$. We prove that the given local map $f$ extends to a biholomorphism $F\colon M\to D$ onto a subdomain $D\subseteqΩ$ in two complementary settings. If $M$ is Stein, then $Ω\setminus D$ is a closed pluripolar set. If $M$ is a bounded domain and $Ω$ satisfies a natural symmetry condition expressed in terms of its automorphism orbits, then $Ω\setminus D$ is Bergman-negligible. In particular, this applies when $Ω$ is a bounded homogeneous domain and yields a characterization, up to Bergman-negligible sets, of a class of bounded domains with locally symmetric Bergman metrics, addressing a question raised by Loi--Palmieri and Zimmer. A key ingredient in the proofs is a new Calabi-type extension theorem tailored to Bergman metrics.

papers.title: Brauer graph algebras are closed under stable equivalence of Morita type
papers.abstract: We study stable equivalences of Brauer graph algebras. We prove that a basic symmetric algebra without semisimple summands which is stably equivalent to a Brauer graph algebra is again a Brauer graph algebra. In particular, Brauer graph algebras are closed up to semisimple summands under stable equivalence of Morita type. As consequences, we reprove the closure under derived equivalence established by Antipov and Zvonareva and obtain a solution of the reconstruction problem posed by Rickard and Rouquier for algebras stably equivalent of Morita type to Brauer graph algebras.

papers.title: Pure dimension and counterexamples to the maximality of purely-primes
papers.abstract: In analogy with the notion of Krull dimension, for every commutative ring $R$, we introduce the notion of pure dimension $\pdim(R)$ by considering chains of purely-prime ideals. Then we see that the inequality $\pdim(R)\leqslant\dim(R)$ holds for a very broad class of rings $R$, including pseudo-Noetherian rings (e.g., Noetherian rings), Gelfand rings (e.g., local rings), mp-rings (e.g., integral domains), and rings with finitely many maximal ideals or finitely many minimal primes. In fact, for all of these rings $R$, we always have $\pdim(R)=0$, i.e., every purely-prime ideal of $R$ is purely-maximal. \\ However, we prove a classification theorem which states for each ordinal number $Ω$ the proper pure ideals of the commutative ring $$R_Ω=k[X_α : α<Ω]/\big(X_α(1-X_β) : α<β<Ω\big)$$ are exactly of the form $I_λ=(x_α: α<λ)$ with $λ=0$ or $λ\leqslantΩ$ a limit ordinal (we write $x_α$ for the image of $X_α$ in $R_Ω$). In addition, all of them are purely-prime ideals and form the following unique strictly ascending chain: $$I_{0}=0\subset I_ω\subset I_{ω\cdot2}\subset I_{ω\cdot 3}\subset\ldots\subset I_{ω\cdotα}$$ where $α$ is a unique ordinal with $Ω=ω\cdotα+n$ and $n\inω$. To prove this theorem, we use the full strength of ...

papers.title: Critical $p$-Laplace equations with monotone coefficients: Liouville classification and a Schoen-type Harnack inequality
papers.abstract: We investigate positive weak solutions of the critical $p$-Laplace equation $$ -Δ_p u = u^{p^*-1} h(u), \qquad 1 < p < n, $$ where $h$ is a positive, bounded, continuous, and nonincreasing function. Our first main result is a complete classification of normalized, bounded, positive entire solutions for every equation in a compact family determined by $h$: Any such solution must coincide with an Aubin--Talenti profile. Moreover, the existence of an Aubin--Talenti profile as a solution implies that $h$ is constant on the entire interval of values attained by that profile. Subsequently, applying this classification result, we establish the following scale-invariant Schoen-type estimate $$ \left(\sup_{B_R} u\right)\left(\inf_{B_{2R}} u\right)^{p-1} \le C R^{p-n} $$ for nonnegative weak solutions defined in $B_{3R}$. As a direct corollary, we apply the profound result of Ciraolo--Gatti \cite{CG2026} to obtain a fully unrestricted Liouville theorem: Every positive entire solution must coincide with an Aubin--Talenti profile. For the purely critical equation, we also show that the corresponding Liouville classification is equivalent to a Schoen-type Harnack inequality. The arguments in this work give quasilinear versions of the Kelvin transform and the method of moving spheres, which was previously available only in the semilinear setting, and also yield alternative proofs of the classical results. The technique developed here can likely be extended to a wider class of Liouville-type problems for critical equations.

papers.title: On the Column Number of Delta-Modular Matrices: an $O(m^2 Δ)$ Bound via the Shifted Heller Constant
papers.abstract: In this paper, we build on the analysis initiated by Averkov and Schymura (2022) and prove that the shifted Heller constant for matrices with $m$ rows is at most $m^2 + m$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Consequently, the number of distinct columns of a $Δ$-modular matrix $A \in Z^{m \times n}$ of rank $m$ is at most $O(m^2 Δ)$. This improves upon the earlier bounds of $O(m^4 Δ)$ and $O(m^2 Δ^2)$.

papers.title: Disconnected Stab(X) and infinitely many braid group orbits
papers.abstract: We show that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions Stab(Y) on a very general quintic threefold Y has infinitely many connected components. Using similar methods, we also prove that for a particular smooth projective (weak Fano) threefold X the braid group action on the set of full exceptional collections in Dscr^b(X) has infinitely many orbits, in particular, it is not transitive. This provides a counterexample to a conjecture of Bondal and Polishchuk from 1993. The conjecture was first disproved by Chang, Haiden, and Schroll, who constructed a family of partially wrapped Fukaya categories for which the transitivity fails. However, no counterexample of the form Dscr^b(X) for X a smooth projective variety was previously known. In addition, we show that Stab(X) also has infinitely many connected components. These are the first known examples of a smooth projective varieties whose spaces of Bridgeland stability conditions are disconnected.

papers.title: Densities of arithmetic Hecke triangle group orbits
papers.abstract: We give new proofs computing the asymptotic densities for orbits of the arithmetic Hecke triangle groups $Γ_q$ when $q=4$ and $q=6$. We use elementary number theory techniques along with basic properties of the Möbius function and Riemann zeta function with additional congruence conditions. This note actually came about by observing that, in the $q=4$ case, the underlying congruence condition partitions the set of coprime integer pairs into three classes of equal density.

papers.title: Non-Clifford quantum cellular automata from invertible topological quantum field theories
papers.abstract: Quantum cellular automata (QCAs) describe locality-preserving quantum dynamics and link quantum information, many-body physics, and topological quantum field theory (TQFT). Constructing a QCA from a TQFT, however, remains challenging: although a topological action yields a Hamiltonian with commuting terms that realizes the desired ground state, it does not by itself specify an automorphism of the full operator algebra. We develop a unified algebraic construction that extends such Hamiltonians to complete separator-flipper algebras on the full tensor-product Hilbert space, thereby defining the corresponding QCAs microscopically. In 3 spatial dimensions, our framework unifies all previously known QCA constructions associated with the $\mathbb{Z}_8\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ subgroup of the Witt group, including the $U(1)_2$ and $U(1)_4$ QCAs. The same algebraic structure yields new infinite families of generalized $U(1)_2$ and $U(1)_4$ non-Clifford QCAs in spatial dimensions $d=4k-1$. We also reformulate the 4-dimensional $w_2w_3$ QCA and use it to construct QCAs from TQFTs associated with arbitrary products of Stiefel--Whitney classes. For example, we explicitly construct two infinite families: $w_2^nw_3^m$ QCAs in dimension $d=2n+3m-1$ and $w_2w_{4k-1}$ QCAs in dimension $d=4k$. For the 5-dimensional $w_3^2$ and $w_2^3$ QCAs, our construction gives finite-depth quantum circuits, consistent with the cobordism classification. More generally, we show that our construction yields a finite-depth quantum circuit whenever the corresponding Stiefel-Whitney number vanishes on every closed oriented manifold. Overall, these results convert invertible TQFTs into microscopic QCAs, provide higher-dimensional constructions beyond the Clifford setting, and open a systematic route to characterizing their stable structures and boundary anomalies.

papers.title: Asymptotic Resurgence of Facet and Stanley-Reisner ideals of Matroids
papers.abstract: Matroid configurations -- introduced by Geramita, Harbourne, Migliore, and Nagel -- are projective varieties which generalize so-called \textit{star configurations} and whose defining ideals are obtained by appropriately specializing the Stanley-Reisner ideal of a matroid. Motivated by this connection, we study the asymptotic resurgence of the Stanley-Reisner ideals of matroids. A result of Villareal shows that it is equivalent to study the asymptotic resurgence of facet ideals. We prove a formula for the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a matroid in terms of the Waldschmidt constant of facet ideals of the contractions of the matroid. As a consequence, we show that asymptotic resurgence respects the weak order on matroids of the same rank. Therefore, the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a given matroid is bounded above by the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a so-called \textit{almost-uniform} matroid of the same rank, which we compute explicitly. Guardo, Harbourne, and Van Tuyl showed that the asymptotic resurgence of an ideal is bounded below by the ratio of the initial degree of the ideal by its Waldschmidt constant. We prove that this lower bound is an equality for facet ideals of many classes of matroids, including matroids of rank $k$ on a ground set of size $n\ge 2k$ whose dual is paving, perfect matroid designs, and sparse paving matroids arising from Steiner systems. For the latter two classes, we explicitly compute the asymptotic resurgence.

papers.title: Quantum error-correcting codes from aperiodic monotiles: the Hat and the Spectre
papers.abstract: Li and Boyle showed that the Penrose tiling defines a quantum error-correcting code: superpositions of tilings over isometry orbits protect quantum information against erasure of any bounded region. We extend the construction to the aperiodic monotiles discovered by Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss. For the Hat, we prove strong local indistinguishability for all Hat tilings, and we prove local recoverability unconditionally for all nonsingular Hat tilings via the torus parametrization of the underlying cut-and-project scheme. The remaining singular case reduces to one sharply posed geometric question -- can a region that is a union of hats be retiled a second way? -- which we verify computationally has no counterexample up to a substantial scale: a certified $2490$-tile patch admits precisely one tiling by hats, so all $2^{2490}$ of its tile-subregions retile uniquely. Unlike the Penrose, Ammann-Beenker and Fibonacci tilings, both monotiles form two local-indistinguishability classes, so their code spaces split into two erasure-correcting sectors carrying a superselected classical label. Whether the label survives depends on which isometries are gauged: the Spectre's classes are exchanged by a $30^{\circ}$ rotation and merge once all proper isometries are gauged, whereas the Hat's are exchanged only by reflections. Under the physically natural gauge group $SE(2)$, the Hat code therefore stores one robust classical bit -- the handedness of its long-range order, readable in any bounded window with separation $Δ= |K|\sqrt{5}/3$ -- alongside its protected quantum sectors. It is the reflexible monotile, not the chiral one, that carries the chirality bit. We give the exact Perron-Frobenius data of both codes, including the per-class reflected-Hat frequencies $(3\mp\sqrt{5})/6$ and the Spectre orientation-class frequencies $(5\pm\sqrt{15})/10$.

papers.title: Heilbronn's Problem in the Unit Triangle: Computational Optimality Certificates for $n \le 8$
papers.abstract: We study Heilbronn's triangle problem in the unit right triangle, where $n$ points are placed to maximize the smallest of the $\binom{n}{3}$ triangle areas they span. We prove a boundary-structure result: unless all three vertices are occupied, some optimal configuration with $n \ge 5$ has at least four points on the boundary, one edge containing two of them. With the affine $S_3$ symmetry this fixes four boundary points and $n$ orientation variables in a mixed-integer model that certifies global optimality for all $n \le 8$ up to a relative gap of $10^{-4}$. For $n \le 7$ this independently confirms the known exact optima, the case $n = 7$ having been proved by Zeng and Chen with symbolic computation. For $n = 8$, where only bounds were known, it narrows the gap to Cantrell's configuration fourfold in 39 minutes on one machine. The optimum there is conjectured to be the real root of a septic obtained by Chen, Zeng and Zhou, which our reconstruction confirms to 250 digits. We show its Galois group is $S_7$, so on that conjecture no expression in radicals exists.

papers.title: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
papers.abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3213 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.4813e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic numbers. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.

papers.title: A Twin gradient method for unconstrained optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a new strategy for gradient-based unconstrained optimization, involving two parallel sequences of iterates that cooperate to determine their stepsizes via a \textit{Twin-Step} principle. Rather than minimizing the objective function individually, the algorithm selects steplengths that minimize the Euclidean distance between the two gradient based processes occurring simultaneously at each iteration. The theoretical analysis shows that the convergence of the mutual distance is governed by the angle between the search directions. In particular the effectiveness of the overall process degrades as the directions approach parallelism. To ensure robustness against collinearity, we introduce a hybrid framework, Twin-ABB$_{\min}$, which switches to the Adaptive Barzilai--Borwein method when the geometric cooperation becomes ineffective. Extensive and very promising numerical results evidence that the Twin phase creates favorable initial conditions for subsequent BB-type iterations.

papers.title: Periodicity in Banach algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider operators that are compositions of an isometric isomorphism and a left multiplier on a Banach algebra, and we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for these operators to have a dense set of periodic elements. As an application of this result, we characterize generalized weighted shifts with a dense set of periodic elements on the standard Hilbert module over C*-algebra of compact operators on a separable Hilbert space. As another application, we characterize generalized weighted shifts with a dense set of periodic elements on the standard Hilbert module over commutative non-unital C*-algebra. Finally, in the last section of the paper, we provide extensions of these results from the case of a sequence generated by powers of a single operator to families of operators indexed over a countable set.

papers.title: Strongly Primitive Salem Growth Polynomials for Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
papers.abstract: We study standard spherical growth rates of right-angled Coxeter groups through the clique polynomial of the defining graph. We prove that every even degree at least four occurs as the degree of a strongly primitive Salem growth rate: for each $d\geq2$, there are infinitely many connected $K_{2d+1}$-free defining graphs whose full reciprocal-radius polynomial is an irreducible Salem polynomial of degree $2d$. We also establish independence-polynomial obstructions for prescribed Salem polynomials, including a sharp first-coefficient bound $a_1\leq-5$. Finally, an elementary golden-ratio growth gap excludes Lehmer's number from the standard spherical growth rates of right-angled Coxeter groups.

papers.title: A characterization of edge-chromatic 3-critical graphs
papers.abstract: A graph with maximum degree $Δ$ is \emph{$Δ$-critical} if it is connected, has chromatic index $Δ+1$, and the deletion of any edge reduces its chromatic index to $Δ$; it is \emph{nontrivial} if it has no subgraph $H$ with $|E(H)|>Δ\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. We prove a characterization of all nontrivial $3$-critical graphs: every such graph is obtained either from smaller $3$-critical graphs by replacing a vertex with a triangle, by a Hajós-join, or by replacing a vertex with a suitable class~$1$ graph, or from a snark by deleting at most one vertex and some independent edges. The third operation, which we call a Meredith-type extension, generalizes the Meredith extension by allowing other class~$1$ graphs in place of $K_{2,3}$, and we give a sufficient condition under which it produces new nontrivial $3$-critical graphs from smaller ones. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first characterization of this kind for edge-chromatic $3$-critical graphs, and the Meredith-type extension has not previously been considered in this generality. The characterization was found by analyzing the output of an exhaustive computer search for nontrivial $3$-critical graphs of orders $13$ to $24$, and we make the resulting data publicly available. Based on these data, we also propose two conjectures that are closely related to the case $Δ=3$ of Seymour's exact conjecture and to Grötzsch's conjecture on the $3$-edge-colorability of planar graphs.

papers.title: Finite difference methods for a continuous-time heterogeneous agent model with recursive utility
papers.abstract: We propose, analyze and test computational methods for solving a continuous-time heterogenous agent model with Epstein-Zin utility. Such recursive utilities allow the model to disentangle between risk aversion and intertemporal substitution. Having discretized the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation arising in the model, we propose a Howard-Newton algorithm for the late resolution preference case, and a Howard-Tarski-Kantorovich algorithm for the early resolution preference case. We prove the convergence of the iterative algorithms. We obtain as a consequence the existence of solutions to the discretized HJB equations. In the late resolution case, we supply a priori estimates between the unique solutions of the continuous and discretized HJB equations.

papers.title: Bounded Bruhat intervals and affine Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: Dyer (1991) proved that, for each fixed length $k$, only finitely many isomorphism types of Bruhat intervals occur in finite Coxeter groups. In this short paper, we prove that this result holds also for affine Coxeter groups, and moreover that this characterizes the affine groups among all infinite Coxeter groups. We also show that the coefficients of $q$ in the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of a Coxeter group are bounded if and only if the group is finite or affine.

papers.title: The functoriality of moves on graphs and extended path homomorphisms
papers.abstract: Combinatorics of graphs is a very powerful tool to unravel various properties of graph algebras. In particular, isomorphisms between graph algebras are often implemented by moves between their graphs. In this paper, we make these combinatorial methods functorial. Our categorical approach not only reveals the relationship between moves, but also leads to unexpected extensions of known moves (shifts and reductions) and the characterization of out-splits as admissible epimorphisms admitting a lifting of the source map. The former allowed us to go beyond isomorphisms and Morita equivalences, and the latter yielded a factorization lemma for out-splits. Better still, the functorial understanding of maximal out-splits permitted combining them with the derived-graph construction, which resulted in computing new proper endomorphisms of Cuntz algebras. Finally, the functorial implementation of balanced in-splits required the construction of a new category of graphs, where morphisms are given as homomorphisms of graph inverse semigroups. Thus, the combinatorics of moves brought a new tool to the realm of noncommutative topology where directed graphs are viewed as quantum spaces.

papers.title: Topology of isometric classes and flows of geometric structures
papers.abstract: We study the topology of isometric classes of tensorial $H$-structures for closed and connected subgroups $H\leqslant\mathrm{SO}(n)$. The map assigning an $H$-structure its induced metric admits a global trivialization; consequently, the space of $H$-structures is homotopy equivalent to any fixed isometric class. On flat tori, these classes are mapping spaces into $\mathrm{SO}(n)/H$. We give examples with infinitely many connected components for $\mathrm{G}_2$, $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$, and almost Hermitian structures, determine the number of components for $\mathrm{SU}(m)$-structures on flat tori, and study the corresponding moduli spaces. For closed manifolds of dimension $n>2$, the intrinsic torsion energy on the full space of $H$-structures has infimum zero on every nonempty path component, and its critical points are precisely the torsion-free structures. In fixed isometric classes, we contrast the concentration phenomena underlying finite-time singularities with cohomological classes admitting positive energy lower bounds and harmonic representatives. Finally, we establish a lifting principle for metric-dependent flows, derive an evolution identity for isometric flows, and extend harmonic-flow estimates to general $H$-structures.

papers.title: Substitution groups of formal power series
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots\in R[[x]]$ under substitution, where $R$ is a commutative ring with $1\neq 0$ of prime characteristic $p$. Given any $n\geq 1$, the subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in R\}$ is normal in $G$, and the quotient $G_n=G/K_n$ is the group of truncated polynomials over $R$ of degree $\leq n$ under substitution. In this paper, we compute the exponent of the image of $K_r$ in $G_n$, for all $r,n\geq 1$, indicating in every case a family of elements realizing this exponent.

papers.title: A stacky resolution of singularities for orders by Azumaya algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a stacky resolution of singularities for certain noncommutative spaces which can be viewed as 'finite noncommutative extensions' of schemes. More precisely, we show that any order over a reduced separated finite type scheme over a field of characteristic zero can be resolved by an Azumaya algebra over a smooth Deligne--Mumford stack by a sequence of stacky blow-ups.

papers.title: On Local Finiteness of Modal K4 Algebras
papers.abstract: We study local finiteness for modal $K4$ algebras via the tunability of their dual general frames. In particular, we provide a sufficient condition for modal $K4$ algebras to be locally finite by identifying a structure which must be present in non-locally finite modal $K4$ algebras. We then show that this condition becomes both necessary and sufficient for $σ$-complete modal $K4$ algebras. Next, we translate this condition into a pair of order-theoretic conditions on transitive Kripke frames, providing a classification of local finiteness on their dual modal algebras. We further show that the logic of any class of well-founded transitive relations with no infinite antichains has the finite model property, and conclude that the logic of the class of well-quasi orderings has the finite model property.

papers.title: Accelerating Min-Max Optimization via Power-Law Stepsizes
papers.abstract: We revisit the convergence guarantees of the Extragradient (EG) method for unconstrained biaffine min-max optimization. It is known that EG with a fixed stepsize achieves a $Θ(T^{-1/2})$ last-iterate convergence rate, which is slower than the optimal $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ rate attainable by incorporating additional mechanisms such as anchoring. Motivated by recent advances showing that dynamic stepsizes alone can significantly accelerate gradient descent, we ask whether dynamic stepsizes can similarly accelerate the last-iterate convergence of EG. We present the first positive result in this direction. Specifically, we provide a deterministic dynamic stepsize schedule that accelerates the convergence rate of EG to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2/3+\varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon > 0$. We also show that this rate is nearly tight when the extrapolation and update steps of EG use the same stepsize. We then show that allowing different stepsizes for the extrapolation and update steps further improves the convergence rate to the near-optimal $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1+\varepsilon})$. Our analysis reduces stepsize scheduling to an optimization problem, whose solution leads to a stepsize schedule that follows (a discretization of) a power-law distribution. Our proposed stepsize schedules and analysis extend to other methods, such as Optimistic Gradient (OG), and suggest broader applicability to general min-max optimization problems.

papers.title: On Star operation and some ideals on the Baire space
papers.abstract: We investigate several $σ$-ideals on the Baire space $ω^ω$ $(\mathbb{Z}^ω)$, introducing and studying the ideals $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{SMZ}^+$, alongside the classical ideals of meager sets, strong measure zero sets, the eventually different ideal and infinitely equal ideal We establish structural relationships and proper inclusions among these ideals. Also we compute the cardinal invariants of $\mathcal{M}_-$, proving that they are same as invariants of $σ$-ideal of meager sets. We further analyze the operation $^*$ on families of sets, establishing dual relationships such as $\mathcal{ED}^* = \mathcal{IE}$, $\mathcal{IE}^*=\mathcal{ED}$, $\mathcal{M}_-^*=\mathcal{SMZ}^+$ and $\mathcal{H}^* = \mathcal{G}$, and derive separations between ideals under additional set-theoretic assumptions. Finally, we prove a tree dichotomy theorem for the ideal $\mathcal{M}_-$ and we study the associated forcing notion.

papers.title: Strong log-concavity in probit regression
papers.abstract: We show that strong log-concavity emerges in probit regression likelihoods without ridge penalization (i.e. Gaussian priors), unlike for the logistic case. Specifically, we provide: (a) a non-asymptotic characterization of strong log-concavity for fixed designs, similar to that for the existence of the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) and (b) an asymptotic analysis for random designs, in the proportional regime when the sample size $n$ and the number of covariates $d$ grow proportionally $d/n\rightarrow r\in[0,1)$. In the latter case we show that, provided $r$ is small enough, the resulting condition number is finite and bounded independently of $n,d,r$ with high-probability. Numerically tractable estimates are given in case $r=0$. Thus, probit regression provides a non-trivial example of a high-dimensional, well-conditioned log-concave objective.

papers.title: Eigenvalue bounds for quantum dot Dirac operators
