We call such sequences {\em satisfying}. Kiselev and the first author showed that $f_1 = \ldots = f_s=(s-1)n^{k-1}$ is satisfying for $s>470$, verifying the conjecture by Aharoni and Howard. This is the best possible if we insist that the families are of the same size. However, it turns out that much more can be said about asymmetric restrictions. In this paper, we investigate this question in several regimes and in particular answer the questions asked by Kiselev and Kupavskii. We use a variety of methods, including concentration and anticoncentration results, spread approximations, and the Combinatorial Nullstellenzatz.

papers.title: Learning to Select Between LP and SDP Relaxations for Nonconvex Quadratically Constrained Quadratic Programs
papers.abstract: Quadratically constrained quadratic programs (QCQPs) are ubiquitous in optimization: Such problems arise in applications from operations research, power systems, signal processing, chemical engineering, and portfolio theory, among others. Despite their flexibility in modeling real-life situations and the recent effort to understand their properties, nonconvex QCQPs are hard to solve in practice. Most of the approaches in the literature are based on either Linear Programming (LP) or Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations, each of which works very well for some problem subclasses but perform poorly on others. In this paper, we develop a relaxation selection procedure for nonconvex QCQPs that can adaptively decide whether an LP- or SDP-based approach is expected to be more beneficial by considering the instance structure. The proposed methodology relies on utilizing machine learning methods that involve features derived from spectral properties and sparsity patterns of data matrices, and once trained appropriately within a dimension-independent setup, the prediction model applies to any instance with an arbitrary number of variables and constraints. We develop classification and regression models under different feature-design setups, including a dimension-independent representation, and evaluate them on synthetically generated instances and a combined benchmark dataset consisting of MINLPLib and QPLIB instances. We further investigate relaxation selection within a spatial branch-and-bound framework, evaluating the trade-off between lower bound quality and computational time.

papers.title: Control of Human-Induced Seismicity in Underground Reservoirs Governed by a Nonlinear PDE-ODE System
papers.abstract: Induced seismicity caused by fluid extraction or injection in underground reservoirs is a major challenge for safe energy production and storage. This paper presents a robust output-feedback controller for induced seismicity mitigation in geological reservoirs described by a coupled 3D PDE-ODE model. The controller is nonlinear and robust (MIMO Super-Twisting design), producing a continuous control signal and requiring minimal model information, while accommodating parameter uncertainties and spatial heterogeneity. Two operational outputs are regulated simultaneously: regional pressures and seismicity rates computed over reservoir sub-regions. Closed-loop properties are established via explicit bounds on the solution and its time derivative for both the infinite-dimensional dynamics and the nonlinear ODE system, yielding finite-time or exponential convergence of the tracking errors. The method is evaluated on the Groningen gas-field case study in two scenarios: gas production while not exceeding the intrinsic seismicity of the region, and combined production with CO$_2$ injection toward net-zero carbon operation. Simulations demonstrate accurate tracking of pressure and seismicity targets across regions under significant parameter uncertainty, supporting safer reservoir operation while preserving production objectives.

papers.title: Curved $\infty$-Local Systems And Projectively Flat Riemann-Hilbert Correspondence
papers.abstract: We generalize the higher Riemann-Hilbert correspondence in the presence of scalar curvature for a (possibly non-compact) smooth manifold $M$. We show that the dg-category of curved $\infty$-local systems, the dg-category of graded vector bundles with projectively flat $\mathbb Z$-graded connections and the dg-category of curved representations of the singular simplicial set of the based loop space of $M$ are all $A_\infty$-quasi equivalent. They provide dg-enhancements of the subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant and have finite-dimensional fibers. In the ungraded case, we reduce to an equivalence between projectively flat vector bundles and a subcategory of projective representations of $π_1(M; x_0)$. As an application of our general framework, we also prove that the category of cohesive modules over the curved Dolbeault algebra of a complex manifold $X$ is equivalent to a subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules which generalizes a theorem due to Block to possibly non-compact complex manifolds.

papers.title: Automorphic form twisted Shintani zeta functions over number fields
papers.abstract: Automorphic twists of Shintani zeta functions encode spectral information about binary cubic forms and the shapes of cubic rings. We study their adelic integrals over an arbitrary number field, allowing ramified data, nonspherical vectors, and arbitrary unitary central character. For cuspidal twists the zeta function is meromorphic on the whole plane and holomorphic for $\Re s>1/4$.

papers.title: On the Lottery Problem: Tracing Stefan Mandel's Combinatorial Condensation
papers.abstract: Stefan Mandel is said to have won the lottery 14 times. He never disclosed the recipe he called combinatorial condensation, which enabled him to hit the Romanian lottery jackpot in the early phase of his betting career. Combinatorial condensation is frequently mixed up with another strategy known as buying the pot, which Stefan Mandel was pursuing later on. On occasion, he dropped a few hints on combinatorial condensation. The hints are applied in this work to narrow down and assess his initial recipe. The underlying theory resembles what a weekend mathematician, as he once referred to himself, may have encountered in the 1960s. The cardinality of the (15, 6, 6, 5) and (49, 6, 6, 5) lottery schemes shows that Stefan Mandel probably wasn't aware of lottery designs. First concepts on such topics had been available at that time, but coherent theories on combinatorial designs took off only in later decades. There is no absolute evidence beyond doubt, but the size of actual covering designs and the associated efforts allow the following hypothesis: Stefan Mandel most likely pioneered in constructing a (15, 6, 5) covering design many years before others published about it, which he applied in the Romanian lottery. Calculations indicate that he took considerable risks that his method might fail, because he limited himself to a subset of 15 numbers out of 49 numbers. The risks explain why he later changed his strategy from combinatorial condensation to buying the pot.

papers.title: Asymptotic geometry of non-abelian Hodge theory and Riemann--Hilbert correspondence, rank three $\widetilde{E}_6$ case
papers.abstract: We prove the Geometric P=W conjecture in rank 3 on the three-punctured sphere. We describe the topology at infinity of the related character variety. We use asymptotic abelianization of harmonic bundles away from the ramification divisor and an equivariant approach near the branch points to find the WKB (also known as Liouville--Green or phase-integral) expansion of the involved maps. We analyze the Stokes phenomenon governing their behavior.

papers.title: Transport-Free Lower Bounds for Ollivier--Ricci Curvature in Higher-Order Networks: Scope, Tightness, and Computational Applications
papers.abstract: We study how the Bauer--Jost--Liu curvature bound applies to hypergraph Ollivier--Ricci curvature (ORC) and how its accuracy depends on local mass and geometry. An explicit weighted-graph representation shows how the graph theorem applies. A transport construction transfers the bounds to monotone pairwise hyperedge aggregations. We analyze endpoint cancellation under laziness, quantify the exact improvement over the earlier mixture bound, and characterize the extremal geometry at fixed endpoint and overlap statistics. Further results quantify worst-case slack, stability, and exactness on isolated hyperedges. A capacity-constrained short-detour refinement uses additional geometric information and improves monotonically as the query budget increases. As a computational application, a threshold cascade preserves exact transport decisions. Numerical verification and public-hypergraph experiments examine tightness, walk dependence, and aggregation, including evaluations on 42,940 finite pairwise comparisons and 64,620 public-data instances. Together, the results specify the scope, equality mechanisms, and computational uses of BJL-type hypergraph bounds.

papers.title: Turning non-smooth points into rational points
papers.abstract: In a recent paper, the author and Stöhr established a bound on the number of iterated Frobenius pullbacks needed to transform a non-smooth purely inseparable point on a regular geometrically integral curve into a rational point. In this paper we improve this result, by establishing a new bound that is sharp in every characteristic $p>0$.

papers.title: Maximal Inequalities for Empirical Processes under General Mixing Conditions
papers.abstract: This paper provides a bound for the supremum of sample averages over a class of functions for a general class of mixing stochastic processes with arbitrary mixing rates. Regardless of the speed of mixing, the bound is comprised of a concentration rate and a novel measure of complexity. The speed of mixing, however, affects the former quantity implying a phase transition. Fast mixing leads to the standard root-n concentration rate, while slow mixing leads to a slower concentration rate whose speed depends on the mixing structure. Our findings are applied to obtain new Glivenko-Cantelli type results.

papers.title: Periodic Tunnel Systems: Reeb Graph Representations and Circular Max-Flow
papers.abstract: Inspired by the study of transport properties in materials science, we investigate the Reeb graph of a map \(f:X\to\Ss\), interpreting \(X\) as a periodic tunnel system in which transport takes place. The map \(f\) encodes a chosen periodic direction and induces a directed structure on the graph. Under constructibility, we establish a lifting result for directed paths that makes precise how the graph represents tunnel segments in \(X\). To turn this representation into a numerical transport descriptor, we equip the graph with cross-sectional capacities defined, in a Riemannian setting, by weighted Hausdorff-measure integrals. Under boundary regularity and Morse assumptions in dimension \(d\ge2\), we establish continuity over regular Reeb values and continuity of the total capacity across fibers. Taking edgewise infima gives the bottleneck capacities for a circular max-flow formulation, which measures flow through fibers of the map to the circle without choosing an arbitrary inlet or outlet. The resulting descriptor is computable by linear optimization and is related to minimum-cost circulations. For nonnegative real capacities, we prove that the max-flow value is invariant under periodic unrolling: the same descriptor is obtained whether the medium is modeled by a toroidal cell or by its periodic replication along the chosen direction. Simulations on periodic point clouds illustrate the construction and the effects of imposing source--target cuts.

papers.title: Characteristic polynomials and eigenvalues of tensors
papers.abstract: We lay the geometric foundations for the study of the characteristic polynomial of tensors. For symmetric tensors of order $d \geq 3$ and dimension $2$, and symmetric tensors of order $3$ and dimension $3$, we prove that only finitely many tensors share any given characteristic polynomial, unlike the case of symmetric matrices and the case of non-symmetric tensors. We propose precise conjectures for the dimension of the variety of tensors sharing the same characteristic polynomial, in the symmetric and non-symmetric settings.

papers.title: The Geometry of Latent Spaces: Projective Invariants, Structural Identification, and Ratio-Scale Measurement
papers.abstract: Latent variable modeling of discrete ordinal data typically relies on Euclidean priors or continuous divergence bounds, inducing a topological mismatch that leaves models vulnerable to factor score indeterminacy, rotational unidentifiability, and Neyman-Scott incidental parameter bias. We introduce an axiomatic, coordinate-free framework that constructs continuous latent coordinate spaces directly from empirical partial orders without extrinsic probability measures. By parameterizing ordinal choice topologies via a regularized log-odds field on a continuous projective product manifold $(\mathbb{P}^1)^Q$, pairwise field differences preserve the invariants of the projective linear group $\mathrm{PGL}(2, \mathbb{R})^Q$. Spectral decomposition of the integrated invariant Gramian matrix reduces the identification fiber strictly to the one-dimensional dilation group $\mathbb{R}_{>0}^Q$. This establishes ratio-scale measurement with generalized specific objectivity, transcending the restrictive uniform-discrimination assumptions of the Rasch model, identically resolving both classical rotational ambiguity and Guttman's factor score indeterminacy. We prove that an indicator array $P \ge 2Q+2$ is topologically necessary and sufficient to anchor a $Q$-dimensional metric space and structurally resolves incidental item parameters without joint, marginal, or conditional estimation. Finally, leveraging Hadamard differentiability and Hanson-Wright operator concentration, we establish that the projective spectral estimator is strongly consistent, asymptotically normal, and achieves optimal parametric concentration at rate $\mathcal{O}_P(P^{-1/2})$.

papers.title: The Fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra over nontrivially valued fields and the radius of convergence of nonarchimedean differential equations
papers.abstract: We prove a fundamental theorem for tropical partial differential equations, analogous to the fundamental theorem of tropical geometry in this context. We extend results from Aroca et al., Falkensteiner et al. and from Fink and Toghani for the case of trivial valuation as introduced by Grigoriev to differential equations with power series coefficients over any valued field. Crucial ingredients are the framework for tropical partial differential equations introduced by Giansiracusa and Mereta and a result on infinite intersections of projections of fibers of tropicalizations, which we prove using Hrushovski and Loeser's model-theoretic interpretation of Berkovich analytification. As a corollary of the fundamental theorem, we show that the radius of convergence of solutions of an ordinary differential equation over a nontrivially valued field can be computed tropically.

papers.title: Six equations in search of a finite-fold-ness proof
papers.abstract: By following the same construction pattern which Martin Davis proposed in a 1968 paper of his, we have obtained six quaternary quartic Diophantine equations that candidate as `rule-them-all' equations: proving that one of them has only a finite number of integer solutions would suffice to ensure that each recursively enumerable set admits a finite-fold polynomial Diophantine representation.

papers.title: A proof of Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that an $n\times n$ circulant Hadamard matrix must satisfy a family of congruence equations that have solutions only when $n \leq 4$, proving Ryser's 1963 conjecture that no such matrices exist for $n>4$.

papers.title: Distinction and quadratic base change for regular supercuspidal representations
papers.abstract: In this article, we study Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations based on the machinery developed by Hakim and Murnaghan to study distinguished representations, and the fundamental work of Kaletha on parameterization of regular supercuspidal representations. For regular supercuspidal representations, we give some new interpretations of the numerical quantities appearing in Prasad's formula, and reduce the proof to the case of tori. The proof of Prasad's conjecture then reduces to a comparison of various quadratic characters appearing naturally in the above process. We also have some new observations on these characters and study the relation between them in detail. For some particular examples, we show the coincidence of these characters, which gives a new purely local proof of Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of these groups. We also prove Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of G(E), when E/F is unramified and G is a general tamely ramified quasi-split reductive group.

papers.title: Quasitoposes as elementary quotient completions
papers.abstract: We characterise when the elementary quotient completion of an elementary doctrine, introduced in previous work by the first and third authors, is a quasitopos. Since the elementary quotient completion generalises the notion of exact completion of a cartesian category with weak equalisers to the setting of elementary doctrines, as proposed by F.W. Lawvere, the characterisation established in this paper, generalises previous results on exact completions, which include A. Carboni and E. Vitale's characterisation in terms of projective objects, Carboni and G. Rosolini's characterisation of locally cartesian closed exact completions, as revised by J. Emmenegger, and M. Menni's characterisation of exact completions that are toposes.

papers.title: Functional Data Representation with Merge Trees
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of representing functional data using tools from algebraic topology. We model functions through merge trees, which, like the more widely used persistence diagrams, are invariant under homeomorphic reparameterizations of their domain. This invariance allows statistical analyses that are robust to functional misalignment. We study a recently introduced metric for merge trees, establish its stability properties, and prove the consistency and convergence rates of a corresponding class of estimators. To illustrate the advantages of our topological approach to functional data analysis, we apply it to the AneuRisk65 dataset, replicating a well-known supervised classification task that made this dataset a benchmark for misaligned functional data. We also compare our results with those obtained using the Fisher-Rao metric, which further supports the effectiveness of the proposed method. The supplementary material includes an extensive comparison between merge trees and persistence diagrams, outlining their similarities and differences to help analysts choose the most suitable representation for a given application.

papers.title: Frames generated by the functional calculus and function frames of a normal operator
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that sequences generated by the functional calculus $(f(T)(e_n))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ can be equivalently written as function sequences $(f_n(T) g)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, when $T$ is normal and $g$ a cyclic vector for $T$. Here, $(e_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of vectors, $T$ is a bounded normal operator, $f$ and $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ are functions defined on a neighborhood of the spectrum $σ(T)$, and $g$ is a cyclic vector for $T$. After that, we characterize the frame property of such sequences in terms of the approximate point spectrum of $T^*$. Examples include certain operators (normal operators, compact operators, unilateral shifts, multiplication operators on Hardy spaces, etc.) that either generate only Riesz bases or allow redundancy. Our bridge theorem makes explicit the structural equivalence between frames generated by the functional calculus and function frames.

papers.title: Intersections of translates of finite-dimensionally valued frame spaces are conditionally slice-full and almost slice-full
papers.abstract: In recent work, the topology of frame spaces $\mathcal{F}_{(X,μ),n}$ has been studied via Stiefel manifolds, revealing in particular a connectedness property for intersections of their translates when $\operatorname{span}(\{a_j\}_{j \in J}$ is not too large, in fact when $\operatorname{codim}(\operatorname{span}\{a_j^l\}_{(j,l) \in J \times [\![1,n]\!]}) \geq 3n$, where $\{a_j\}_{j \in J}$ is the translating family \cite{ElIdrissiKabbajMoalige2023}. The investigation of the connectedness of the intersections of translates of the frame space can be extended to questions about the algebro-geometric and measure-theoretic structure of such intersections. The present article addresses these questions by uncovering an almost-linear structure within intersections of translated frame spaces. We show that the set of non-frames in finite-dimensional Hilbert $C^*$-modules inherits the structure of a slice-wise real affine algebraic subvariety. As a consequence, it is a small subset in a precise measure-theoretic sense. In particular, we prove that for any finite-dimensional Hilbert $C^*$-module $\mathcal{H}$ and any countable collection of translates of the frame space $\mathcal{F}_{(X,μ),\mathcal{H}}$, the intersection is conditionally slice-full in $L^2(X,μ;\mathcal{H})$ and almost surely slice-full. We inform the reader that the notions of slice-wise real affine algebraic subvarieties (although related to ind-varieties), conditionally slice-full subsets and slice-full subsets (although related to shy sets) of a Hausdorff topological vector space are, to our knowledge, both new.

papers.title: Remarks on some maximal subgroups of $F$ and on the $\vec{F}$-index of knots
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that three maximal subgroups of infinite index in the rectangular subgroup \( K_{(2,2)} \) of the Thompson group \( F \), each containing Jones's \( 3 \)-colorable subgroup \( \mathcal{F} \), can be characterized as stabilizer subgroups. Additionally, we show that the \( \vec{F} \)-index, an elementary knot invariant introduced thanks to Jones's construction of knots from Thompson groups, may increase at most by $4$ after changing the orientation of a knot.

papers.title: Hecke Algebra-valued Poincaré Series and Geometric Factorization of Affine Weyl Groups
papers.abstract: This paper studies affine Weyl groups through the geometry of geodesic tubes and their hyperbolic stabilizers. We introduce a geometric framework relating affine Weyl group factorizations to Hecke-algebra-valued Poincaré series and zeta functions on quotient complexes. Using this framework, we prove a conjecture describing the connection between geodesic tubes and factorizations of Poincaré series for affine Weyl groups. We also establish partial results toward a Hecke-algebra-valued zeta identity for simply connected groups, including the cases of types $\widetilde{A}_{n-1}$ and $\widetilde{C}_n$. These results highlight the interaction between affine Weyl group geometry, Hecke algebras, and zeta functions arising from Bruhat--Tits buildings.

papers.title: Infinite periodic groups of even exponents
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that free Burnside groups of sufficiently large even exponents are infinite. The method is very flexible and can also be used to study (partially) periodic quotients of any group which admits an action on a hyperbolic space satisfying a weak form of acylindricity.

papers.title: Asymptotics of principal evaluations of Schubert polynomials for layered permutations
papers.abstract: Denote by $u(n)$ the largest principal specialization of the Schubert polynomial: $ u(n) := \max_{w \in S_n} \mathfrak{S}_w(1,\ldots,1) $ Stanley conjectured in [arXiv:1704.00851] that there is a limit $\lim_{n\to \infty} \, \frac{1}{n^2} \log u(n), $ and asked for a limiting description of permutations achieving the maximum $u(n)$. Merzon and Smirnov conjectured in [arXiv:1410.6857] that this maximum is achieved on layered permutations. We resolve both Stanley's problems restricted to layered permutations.

papers.title: On kernel Mengerian orientations of line multigraphs
papers.abstract: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set $K$ such that every vertex outside $K$ has an arc to a vertex in $K$. We present a polyhedral description of kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of line multigraphs. Given a digraph $D$, let $FK(D)$ denote its fractional kernel polytope, and let $σ(D)$ denote the linear system defining $FK(D)$. A digraph $D$ is called kernel perfect if every induced subdigraph has a kernel, called kernel ideal if the fractional kernel polytope of every induced subdigraph is integral, and called kernel Mengerian if the defining system of every induced subdigraph is totally dual integral. We show that a clique-acyclic orientation of a line multigraph is kernel ideal if and only if it is kernel Mengerian. These equivalent properties hold precisely when the orientation is kernel perfect and has no even-cycle obstruction.

papers.title: Site Percolation on Multi-dimensional Lattice
papers.abstract: Sites in an infinite d-dimensional lattice, open with probability greater or equal to 1/d, form an infinite open path.

papers.title: Naturalization of Vinti's intermediary orbit---or how to get rid of small divisors in Brouwer's satellite solution
papers.abstract: A naturalization, in the sense of Deprit, of Vinti's dynamical system makes the construction of a first order analytical satellite perturbation solution without critical divisors possible. The process gives hints on how to recast Brouwer's classical solution in a form that is free from small divisors too. The functionality of classical perturbation solutions is in this way extended to the close vicinity of the critical inclination. The new analytical solution bears terms that may grow unbounded, but their negative effects do not disclose in time intervals in which this kind of solution may be useful in practice.

papers.title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
papers.abstract: We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense: (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton. (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first singularity modeled on the soliton is $C^{14}$-open. It is nonempty if and only if the manifold contains a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (4) The soliton is strongly rigid among shrinking Ricci solitons. As applications, we construct $C^{14}$-open sets of initial data whose Ricci flows perform any prescribed ordered sequence of blowdowns. (1) Every closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, including spin and exotic examples, can be reached by Ricci flow from a standard $k\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2$, through finitely many blowdown singularities. (2) On the standard $2\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#9\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$, there are infinitely many open sets of initial metrics whose Ricci flows, after a single blowdown, reach pairwise nondiffeomorphic manifolds. The proof uses the spectral analysis of Naff and the second author and deals with the gauge-fixing problem along Ricci flow through a Ważewski argument inspired by Stolarski. We also use Bamler-Lai's PDE-ODI principle. Except for continuation (requiring nonnegative curvature of the asymptotic cone), all results apply to linearly stable nonflat asymptotically conical shrinkers in all dimensions.

papers.title: Partial $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2, VMO}$ regularity for nondifferentiable fully nonlinear elliptic equations and Isaacs equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the partial regularity of viscosity solutions to fully nonlinear elliptic equations of the form $F(D^2u, x) = f(x)$ in previously unexplored settings: (i) When $F$ is non-differentiable with respect to $D^2u$. (ii) When either $F$ or $f$ lacks Dini continuity in $x$. In the first scenario, we introduce a tangent operator property for $F$ such that, for a fixed point $x_0$ and a given matrix $M_0$, $F(M, x_0)$ is tangential to a convex or concave operator at $M_0$. We establish partial $C^{2,α}$ regularity for equations exhibiting this property. In the second scenario, we establish new partial $W^{2, \text{VMO}}$ regularity provided that the oscillation of $F$ in $x$ under the $L^n$-norm is of order $o(\log^{-1}(1/r))$. We address the Hausdorff dimensions of the singular sets of solutions for equations of the form $F(D^2u)=f(x)$ with data $f$ in $W^{1,n}$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the tangent operator property holds for various classes of equations, including nondifferentiable twisted elliptic equations, infimum of $C^1$ equations, semiconvex equations, and piecewise differentiable equations. Finally, we tackle the issue of smooth enveloping and obtain partial regularity of solutions for three subclasses of Isaacs equations.

papers.title: On the lower bound of the refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture: proof of the cases S_{6,3} and S_{7,3} for 3x3 matrices
papers.abstract: For Hermitian matrices $α,β$ let $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)$ be the average of the traces of all words with $n$ letters $e^α$ and $m$ letters $e^β$. The refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture contains the lower bound $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)\ge\Tr e^{nα+mβ}$ (Tr denotes the trace), which for $n=m=1$ is the Golden--Thompson inequality. We prove this lower bound for all $n+m\le7$ when the matrices have size at most three, and for $\min(n,m)\le2$ in every dimension. In all these cases we prove the stronger inequality $\A_{n,m}(A,B)\ge\Tr(A^{n/m}B)^m$ for positive semidefinite $A,B$, or its mirror image with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged; the lower bound of the refined conjecture follows from the Araki--Lieb--Thirring inequality. The cases with three letters $B$ in dimension three, $(n,m)=(3,3)$ and $(4,3)$, are reduced by an exact identity and the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means to a polynomial inequality in two variables, which is certified in exact rational arithmetic by Bernstein expansion on three boxes. The certificate is a short program in the ancillary files.

papers.title: Graphs with three distinct distance eigenvalues, one of which is zero
papers.abstract: Koolen, Hayat and Iqbal asked for the connected graphs whose distance matrix has exactly three distinct eigenvalues, the middle one being $0$. The examples they gave, namely the Johnson graphs, the Hamming graphs and the halved cubes, are distance-regular. In this note, we show that the distance spectrum of such a graph is $\{ρ,0,-c\}$ with integers $c\ge2$ and $c\midρ$. For $c=2$ the graphs are exactly the cocktail party graphs, and for $c=3$ they are exactly the Cartesian product $K_3\,\square\,K_3$ of two triangles, the Petersen graph and its complement. We also show that such a graph need not be transmission-regular: Seidel switching the lattice graph $K_6\,\square\,K_6$ with respect to a line and the triangular graph $T(11)$ with respect to a maximal clique of size $10$ gives graphs on $36$ and $55$ vertices with distance spectra $\{54,0^{(26)},(-6)^{(9)}\}$ and $\{81,0^{(45)},(-9)^{(9)}\}$. Among the graphs of diameter $2$ obtained by switching a strongly regular graph with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ with respect to one part of an equitable partition, these two are the only ones that have exactly three distance eigenvalues and are not transmission-regular. We also observe that the transmission-regular graphs with exactly three distinct distance eigenvalues, the smallest one being $-3$, are exactly the complements of the strongly regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue $-2$ other than the cocktail party graphs.

papers.title: Letter to a Young Black Mathematician: History, Storytelling, and Belonging in Mathematics
papers.abstract: What does it mean to tell the story of a mathematician? Written as a letter to a young Black mathematician, this article reflects on how stories shape our understanding of mathematics and our sense of belonging within the mathematical community. Through the lens of Hidden Figures Revealed, a project documenting Black mathematicians at The Ohio State University, I discuss humanity, mathematics, and context as three guiding principles for mathematical storytelling. In particular, I reflect on how this framework emerged through archival research, shaped historical narratives, and informed mathematical learning experiences.

papers.title: Uniform duplication-divergence random graphs I: Degrees and Local Limits
papers.abstract: We study a growing random graph in which each new vertex chooses a uniformly random parent, joins that parent with probability $r\in(0,1]$, and independently joins each of the parent's current neighbors with probability $p\in(0,1)$. Let $p_c$ be the unique solution of $p_c e^{p_c}=1$. For $0<p<p_c$, we prove that the empirical degree distribution converges in probability to the stationary distribution $π$ of an explicit reset-and-growth Markov chain. Its upper tail satisfies $π((y,\infty))\sim C_{p,r}y^{-κ}$, where $C_{p,r}>0$ and $κ>0$ solves $p^κ+pκ=1$. This confirms predictions from physics (Lambiotte, Krapivsky, Bhat and Redner, \textit{Physical Review Letters}, 2016). We further show that for every fixed radius $\ell$ and $p<p_c$, the empirical distribution of induced rooted $\ell$-neighborhoods converges to the invariant law of a graph-valued reset-and-growth Markov process. We give an explicit construction of the limiting graph using a marked ancestral genealogy. Its root component is almost surely finite for $r<1$, and infinite with exactly one end for $r=1$. Moreover, for every $0<p<1$, both the fixed-vertex degrees and the maximum degree grow on the scale $t^p$, and the vertex of maximum degree is eventually unique and persistent.

papers.title: Stochastic and Noisy Oracles in Smooth Continuous Optimization
papers.abstract: We review models of inexact computational oracles in smooth continuous optimization and their implications for the convergence, computational complexity, and attainable accuracy of optimization algorithms. We adopt a framework in which zeroth-,first-, and second-order oracles are characterized by quantitative error bounds and may accept additional control parameters that influence both their accuracy and computational cost. We introduce deterministic and stochastic oracle models and illustrate their properties through a variety of examples, including finite-difference approximations, stochastic gradients, and randomized derivative estimators. Particular attention is given to the distinction between absolute and relative errors, bias and variance, and stochastic function evaluations with independent or coupled randomness. A central theme of the review is the use of common analytical tools to recover and compare convergence and complexity guarantees under different oracle models. For deterministic and stochastic first-order methods, we show how a general descent inequality leads to complexity bounds under various assumptions on the objective function and all proposed oracle models. In the stochastic setting, we develop bounds on expected stopping times and the accuracy that can be guaranteed under different oracle conditions. We also examine the total computational complexity of algorithms relying on specific oracle constructions and briefly review models of inexact second- order information and their use in optimization algorithms.

papers.title: Initial Subcategories via Free Presentations of the Constant Functor
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category. We characterize the full initial subcategories of $\mathcal{C}$ as precisely those whose representables give a free presentation of the constant functor $Δ_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbb{K}:\mathcal{C}\to\mathrm{Vect}$. Such a presentation yields a formula for the limit of any functor $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}$ as the kernel of a morphism between products of evaluations. When the linearized endomorphism ring of every object is local, we show that a minimal free presentation, whenever one exists, determines the unique minimal full initial subcategory, up to equivalence. Bass's characterization of perfect rings gives a sufficient condition for the existence of such presentations. In particular, every finite category with no nonidentity endomorphisms, such as a finite poset, contains a unique minimal initial full subcategory. In the poset case, our results recover the minimal initial subposet constructed in [BDL27] and [DL26]. When $\mathcal{C}$ is the free category on a finite quiver, we give an explicit construction of its minimal initial full subcategories, show that every such subcategory arises from this construction, and provide algorithms with time-complexity bounds.

papers.title: Stochastic Linesearch Methods for Stochastic Variational Inequality Problems: Parameter-Free Schemes and Non-Monotone Variants
papers.abstract: Much of the existing convergence guarantees and rate statements for stochastic variational inequality (SVI) problems are limited to stochastic approximation schemes that employ constant or diminishing steplength sequences bounded by some reciprocal of the Lipschitz constant $L$ of the map. This requires both knowing such constants and may lead to debilitatingly small steplengths, afflicting the scheme with potentially poor performance. We propose a parameter-free stochastic extragradient method with periodically restarted linesearch (\textbf{SEG-LS}) for solving pseudomonotone and monotone SVI problems. The resulting stepsize sequence is neither monotone nor requires prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant $L$. We show that the iteration and sample complexities for computing a point whose residual has norm at most $ε$ in expectation are $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$, respectively. These results improve to $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-1})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ in the monotone setting. In addition, we propose a periodically restarted biased stochastic linesearch method (\textbf{B-SLAM}) for solving non-monotone SVIs under strict copositivity. The resulting iteration and sample complexities are $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$, respectively. Preliminary numerics support these findings and display promise.

papers.title: The complexity of tilting
papers.abstract: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $φ$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $φ^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $φ^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $φ$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the Lévy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.

papers.title: String-averaging bargaining in solidarity cooperative games
papers.abstract: We consider the situation that the grand set of all players, in a cooperative game in characteristic function form with a nonempty core, consists of recognizable subsets of players. The underlying assumption is that the players of each subset have something in common between themselves which is not shared by the players of other subsets. For example, the members of these subsets are distinguishable by their nationalities or by their geographic locations or by some other market-related economic or social property. In addition to the agreement of all players to play the game to reach a point in the core, the members of each subset want to steer the iterative orbit of the bargaining process to a point in the core that will reflect the strength of their solidarity within their subset. This is why we call such subsets solidarity sets. The solidarity means that players of a solidarity set are willing to participate in coalitions that include only members of their solidarity set and are not willing to participate in coalitions of other solidarity sets. The question is how can such a game be played? Is there an iterative bargaining scheme that will generate a sequence of payoffs that converges to a point in the core which reflects the solidarity of the members of the solidarity sets? We propose bargaining schemes that allow the members of each solidarity set to perform, independently from other solidarity sets and, therefore, simultaneously in time, a full but finite sweep of intercoalitional collaboration. Then the end-points of all these sweeps are combined into a single payoff vector via a convex combination wherein the coefficients of the convex combination may reflect some a priori knowledge about the relative strengths of the different solidarity sets. These bargaining schemes are applied to a new type of cooperative game that we call solidarity cooperative game (SCG).

papers.title: An explicit bound on the extremal function for complete graph minors
papers.abstract: Kostochka and Thomason independently proved that every graph with density at least $β\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor, for some constant $β$. Thomason later proved that the least such density is $(0.319\ldots+o(1))\,t\sqrt{\log t}$. However, the $o(1)$ term in this formula is not explicit, so the formula gives no bound for any specific value of $t$. The goal of this paper is a bound of the form $β\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ that holds for every $t$, with $β$ small. We prove that, for every integer $t\geqslant2$, every graph with density at least $4.5\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor.

papers.title: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Equivariant linear maps cannot mix non-isomorphic irreducible representations, whereas nonlinear activations can. We develop a degree-resolved version of this nonlinear interaction picture and use the resulting block inventory to construct Specht Triple, a residual on unordered graph triples. On a synthetic structural benchmark with a frozen GIN backbone, Specht Triple reduces aggregate standardised test MSE by 11.05% relative to a parameter-matched Projector Control using the same irreducible projectors and complete linear equivariant space. The results support irreducible decomposition as an inductive bias for nonlinear higher-order equivariant processing.

papers.title: Box-Cone Representations of Bound-Factor RLT Constraints in Semidefinite Relaxations
papers.abstract: Linear inequalities can generate large constraint systems in semidefinite relaxations of binary quadratic programs, making the quadratic subproblems of splitting methods expensive to solve. We develop a box-cone representation of bound-factor reformulation-linearization technique (RLT) constraints in semidefinite relaxations of binary quadratic programs. These constraints arise by multiplying each original linear inequality by every binary variable and its complement and linearizing the resulting products. Our key observation is that all products generated by one inequality share a common slack and admit an exact representation in the standard cone over the unit box. This box-cone representation processes the inequalities through independent explicit projections, without introducing a separate nonnegative slack for each scalar RLT inequality. We illustrate the computational use of the representation within standard two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). The resulting subproblems require linear solves with a reusable factorization and explicit cone projections, without enlarging the semidefinite matrix. Experiments on 257 binary quadratic programs compare this implementation with SDPNAL+. A second application groups Max-Cut triangle inequalities into box cones and uses the resulting bounds within an existing branch-and-bound framework. Tests on 220 graphs show competitive performance with MADAM using only triangle cuts. Together, these applications illustrate the representation's usefulness as a building block for first-order methods.

papers.title: On kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernel
papers.abstract: We prove the weak maximum principle and the Cucker-Smale flocking theorem for a general class of kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernels. This includes the classical Cucker-Smale and Motsch-Tadmor systems with defining kernel $φ$ assumed to be merely continuous or even $φ\in L^\infty$ for solutions in the Lebesgue class $f\in L^1$. For such models the characteristic flow-map is not well-defined and therefore the classical approaches of Cucker-Smale \cite{CS2007a,CS2007b} or Ha-Liu-Tadmor \cite{HL2009,HT2008} break down. We develop a new method adopted to rough settings based on Ambrossio's probabilistic representation of solutions and construction of dynamic barriers. All proofs are performed in the framework of so called bounded communication protocols, a non-smooth variant of regular protocols introduced in \cite{Shv-CPAM, Shv-EA} and representing a broad range of models of collective dynamics.

papers.title: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models for Model Order Reduction of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Latent dynamics learning has emerged as a prominent approach for Model Order Reduction (MOR) of time-dependent, parameterized Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). Traditional autoencoder-based approaches are intrinsically tied to fixed spatial discretizations during both training and inference, motivating the development of meshless methodologies. In this context, conditioning provides a natural mechanism for representing temporal evolution through spatially continuous functions, enabling mesh-agnostic Latent Dynamics Models (LDMs). In this work, we introduce a unified mathematical framework for mesh-agnostic LDMs based on conditioning in Neural Fields (NeFs). Leveraging a taxonomy of conditioning mechanisms (weak, strong, and pure), we formulate meshless LDMs as NeFs conditioned on a latent state. We establish a Universal Approximation Theorem (UAT) for this class of models and analyze their stability by deriving Lipschitz bounds for different conditioning mechanisms. Our analysis reveals an expressivity--stability trade-off, providing insight into why more expressive conditioning, despite its higher representational capacity, can potentially degrade performance during temporal extrapolation. Finally, we provide a comprehensive comparison of meshless and mesh-based architectures in the continuous limit of the spatial discretization, showing that meshless models guarantee grid-independent Lipschitz bounds, unlike mesh-based counterparts. Our experiments across Burgers' equation, Navier--Stokes flow past a cylinder, and linear advection show that meshless LDMs can achieve predictive accuracy comparable to or better than their mesh-based counterparts while using only 2% of the trainable parameters and exhibiting nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.

papers.title: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token Prediction for non-Markovian Data?
papers.abstract: There exists little mathematical theory explaining why Transformer architectures are empirically successful even for non-Markovian data. To this end, this paper studies next-token prediction via stochastic optimal control theoretically trained Transformers for such sources, where we consider either stationary and ergodic non-Markovian sources or those which are hidden Markov models of some finite order (possibly non-stationary). In either case, we first obtain error bounds via finite models with finite window approximations. For stationary ergodic sources, the resulting error is bounded by an entropy gap; for $N$th order Markovian sources, it decays at an exponential rate $α^{\lfloor M/N\rfloor}$, where $M$ is the window length and $α$ is determined by filter stability (and the Dobrushin coefficients of the transition and measurement kernels). We then construct a Transformer of depth $M+1$, one head per layer, realizing the truncated filter, and we optimally train it with stochastic control developed in earlier work, which rigorously returns a near optimal Transformer. In particular, we show that for a non-Markovian source, either under stationarity and ergodicity for general models or under filter stability for hidden Markov models, an optimally trained Transformer has arbitrarily small performance error with increasing context length, data, and approximation refinement. Numerical studies accompany the theory.

papers.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
papers.abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $κ$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tildeΔ$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $κ$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--Göttsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tildeΔ}^κ|$ of $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $κ$.

papers.title: Erdős--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
papers.abstract: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erdős--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff.

papers.title: CuPIQP: A Batched and Differentiable QP Solver on GPUs for Robot Learning and Control
papers.abstract: Quadratic programs (QPs) are fundamental building blocks of many robotic tasks such as inverse kinematics, whole-body control, and model predictive control. Extending these methods to large-scale robot learning and control requires solving many QPs concurrently and, for end-to-end learning, differentiating through their solutions. Efficient batched optimization is therefore essential to bringing established model-based methods into GPU-based robotics pipelines. We present \textsc{cuPIQP}, a batched and differentiable QP solver on GPUs based on a proximal interior-point method, with unified support for dense, sparse, and multistage problems. The solver exploits parallelism across independent QPs and their internal structure while preserving per-problem numerical updates and termination decisions. Benchmarks with up to 16384 QPs per batch demonstrate solve-time speedups of up to $18.8\times$ over \textsc{Moreau} and $4.26\times$ over eight-core \textsc{PIQP}. In an end-to-end learning task, \textsc{cuPIQP} accelerates training by $4.6\times$ over \textsc{QPAX} and $7.8\times$ over \textsc{Moreau}. By reducing the computational cost, \textsc{cuPIQP} provides efficient, reusable infrastructure for integrating model-based optimization into large-scale robot learning and control.

papers.title: Neural Network Methods in the 2BSDE Formalism for Solving the High-Dimensional Black--Scholes Equation with Transaction Costs
papers.abstract: A 2BSDE system is written down for a $(D+1)$-dimensional Black--Scholes partial differential equation (PDE) with the Leland transaction cost model which incorporates the sign of the curvature. The 2BSDE system takes input from the ``speed'' (derivative of the curvature). This system is solved using a single ResNet neural network which learns both the solution to the PDE as well as the degrees of freedom in the curvature matrix. The network is used to learn the price of derivatives such as call options and butterfly spreads on geometric baskets for $D=10,100$ achieving a time-averaged RMSE of less than $0.1$ in each case.

papers.title: Functorial Analysis of Group-Alphabet Cellular Automata
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $n\in\mathbb N$. We consider one-dimensional cellular automata of length $n$ over the alphabet $G$, with periodic boundary conditions and with local rules $φ$ given by words. We construct a functor $F$ from $\mathbf{Grp}$, the category of groups (or any similar algebraic structure), to the category of pointed digraphs, and show its faithfulness. We introduce the image category $\mathcal C_{n,φ}$ of state transition graphs of all such group-alphabet cellular automata, and show $F$ is an equivalence onto this category. Consequently we investigate the translation of categorical structures in $\mathbf{Grp}$ in terms of automata, and give examples of how standard methods of homological algebra may now be applied to automata. Additionally, a graph-theoretical construction of the product in $\mathcal C_{n,φ}$ is given, together with a formula for cycle lengths and multiplicities in this product. When $G$ is abelian, further structural properties of state transition graphs follow, and we contrast these results with non-abelian counterexamples.

papers.title: The Table Problem for Convex Domains
papers.abstract: We prove a generalized Table Theorem for bounded convex domains in the plane. Then we prove a variation of the Table Problem for compactly supported functions on the plane. Our method is based on relating the table problem on a surface to the square peg problem for a configuration of star-shaped curves in the tangent bundle of the surface.

papers.title: Conformal geodesics and gauged Killing-Yano forms in dimension four
papers.abstract: We study the relation between conformal geodesics and conformal Killing-Yano (CKY) 2-forms on anti-self-dual conformal manifolds of dimension 4. In the flat case, twistor quadrics determine self-dual CKY forms whose zero loci contain conformal geodesics. To extend this construction to curved manifolds, we consider self-dual 2-forms with values in a line bundle and satisfying the gauged CKY equation, coupled to connections with anti-self-dual curvature. In this way we provide a local ambient characterization of non-null conformal geodesics as zero curves of gauged CKY forms, with the curvature vanishing along these curves.

papers.title: The Berger conjecture for three dimensional manifolds
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Berger says that on a simply connected manifold all of whose geodesics are closed, all unit speed geodesics have the same shortest period. In this paper we will show that the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow is free. We use symplectic geometry to investigate the topology of the quotient of the unit tangent bundle T^1M/S^1 by the S^1 action that comes from the geodesic flow. We show that this quotient admits the structure of a smooth symplectic manifold and that this symplectic manifold is symplectomorphic to S^2 \times S^2 equipped with a split form. This will enable a computation involving the Euler class of the orbibundle T^1M\rightarrow T^1M/S^1 which will lead to a solution of Berger's conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds.

papers.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.

papers.title: Optimal design problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian at prescribed energy level
papers.abstract: In this work we study two optimal design problems, of hard and soft obstacle type, in fractional Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. We also establish the connection between these problems, and finally we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the quotients $Λ_{s,μ}(α)/μ$ with respect to the energy level $μ$ at the endpoints $0$ and $+\infty$.

papers.title: Linear Rank Nonincreasing and Preserving Maps between Matrix Spaces
papers.abstract: We classify linear maps $φ$ between possibly different rectangular matrix spaces over a field $\mathbb F$ with $|\mathbb F|\ge5$ such that $\operatorname{rank} φ(A)\le2$ whenever $\operatorname{rank} A\le2$. Every such map has one of six forms. If its image contains a matrix of rank greater than two, then $φ(A)=MAN$ or $φ(A)=MA^{\top}N$ for fixed matrices $M,N$. The remaining forms have images consisting entirely of matrices of rank at most two, including an exceptional form arising from $3\times3$ alternating matrices. As a consequence, we characterize linear maps preserving rank exactly two. We also prove that rank-$k$ preservation implies rank-$k$ nonincrease when $|\mathbb F|>k+2$, and that rank-$k$ nonincrease implies rank-$\ell$ nonincrease for every admissible $\ell\ge k$ when $|\mathbb F|>k+1$. The classification uses the fact that the Chow rank of the generic $3\times3$ determinant is five, connecting the rank preserver problem with product decompositions of polynomials.

papers.title: Steady conformally Kähler Ricci solitons with isoparametric potential
papers.abstract: We classify complete, non-compact, simply connected, irreducible four-dimensional steady gradient Ricci solitons that are globally conformally Kähler and have an isoparametric potential. The steady Ricci solitons are $U(2)$-invariant nuts on $\mathbb R^4$, including the Bryant and Cao solitons, and bolts on $\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb R^2$ and on $\mathcal O(-m)\to\mathbb{CP}^1$. For each $m\ge3$ there is exactly one non-collapsed bolt. A key step, valid for Ricci solitons of every sign, is that away from the locally conformally flat case, the conformal factor is aligned with the potential function, which yields cohomogeneity-one symmetry.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$
papers.abstract: Bryan, Oberdieck, Pandharipande and Yin predicted the number of hyperelliptic curves on general abelian surfaces under a transversality condition. Some of the numbers have already been confirmed. In this paper we construct singular hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ polarised abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$ confirming a few predicted numbers, namely of (geometric) genus $g=d$ and of geometric genus $k+3$ on $(1,2k)$ and $(1,2k+1)$ polarised surfaces. Moreover, we have found that all genus 7 hyperelliptic curves on general $(1,8)$ polarised surfaces are double coverings of curves locally embedded into $(1,4)$ polarised surfaces. More interestingly, there is a unique genus 9 hyperelliptic curve (up to translation) locally embedded into a general $(1,12)$ polarised surface and it is a Klein covering of a curve locally embedded into a $(1,3)$ polarised surface.

papers.title: Handlebodies separate elements of surface groups
papers.abstract: In this note I prove that every non-trivial element of the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface X is non-trivial in the fundamental group of some handlebody with boundary X. This result appears to be folklore. I have uploaded a proof as the result is needed in a joint project with Clement Dupont on mapping class group actions on configuration spaces.

papers.title: RC Prediction: A Python Package for Parameter-Aware Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: A nonlinear dynamical system can be characterized by the autonomous evolution of its state in time and its dependence on system parameters. As a parameter varies, the dynamics can change quantitatively and, at bifurcation points, qualitatively. When the governing equations are unknown, a data-driven model should therefore capture both elements from observational data, rather than reproduce the dynamics at a single operating condition only. Parameter-aware reservoir computing (PARC) is a model-free framework for this purpose, where the parameter is supplied to a reservoir computer through an additional input channel. PARC is trained on time series recorded at several parameter values, and the trained reservoir, run in closed loop as an autonomous dynamical system, generates trajectories at parameter values that were never observed. rc_prediction is an open-source Python package that implements this workflow. It provides multi-parameter training of a reservoir, autonomous closed-loop prediction at user-specified parameter values, parameter scans, and a standard echo state network for forecasting at a fixed parameter. Hyperparameter optimization and optional GPU acceleration through PyTorch are also provided. We use three benchmark dynamical systems as examples to demonstrate its usage. As one of the featured applications, here we illustrate the prediction of critical transitions and system collapse: trained only on pre-critical data, the model is queried beyond the training range to predict whether the system collapses, to estimate the critical parameter $p_c^{*}$, and to characterize transient lifetimes.

papers.title: Martingale Representation in Counting-Process Filtrations via Poisson Embedding
papers.abstract: We revisit martingale representation for counting processes using the Poisson embedding, deriving the representation in their natural filtration from that of the underlying Poisson random measure. Our approach combines Poisson Malliavin calculus with the Clark-Ocone and Mecke formulas. We first characterize measurability with respect to the counting-process filtration through the structure of the Malliavin derivative. We show that any random variable measurable in the counting-process filtration is invariant with respect to the auxiliary mark on the acceptance region obtained from the Poisson embedding method and vanishes on the rejection region. We then prove that every square-integrable martingale in this smaller filtration consequently admits a unique stochastic integral representation with respect to the compensated counting process: the integrand is explicitly characterized as the conditional expectation of the Malliavin derivative, which identifies as the conditional effect of an additional accepted event on the terminal functional. Additionally, we define the mirroring counting process which counts the rejected events in the Poisson embedding procedure and we then provide an orthogonal decomposition of any martingale in the joint filtration of the accepted and rejected counting processes as a sum of a martingale in the counting filtration obtained by Poisson embedding and its mirroring martingale part on the rejected domain. Finally, we apply these results to general Hawkes processes constructed by Poisson embedding, obtaining a martingale representation and an explicit integrand formula in their natural filtration.

papers.title: Isometric Embeddings of Asymptotically Hyperbolic Manifolds into Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: The Nash Embedding theorem asserts that every closed Riemannian manifold can be isometrically embedded into a Euclidean space of sufficiently high dimension. In this paper, we address the asymptotically hyperbolic version of the problem. We prove that an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold $\left(M,g\right)$ can be realized as a submanifold of a sufficiently high-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathrm{H}^{N+1}$, intersecting the sphere at infinity transversely, if and only if $g$ is asymptotically Poincaré-Einstein to second order.

papers.title: Nondegeneracy of low-energy nodal solutions to the Yamabe equation
papers.abstract: We study the linearized Yamabe equation in $\R^n$, or equivalently on $\s^n$, at a low-energy sign-changing solution with two nodal domains. We consider odd dimensions $n=2k-1$ and a solution invariant under $Γ=O(k)\times O(k)$. Its regular level sets are isoparametric hypersurfaces, which foliate the sphere away from the two focal submanifolds. This symmetry reduces the equation for the solution to a singular ODE. In the balanced case, we choose a single-node profile that is odd under reflection across the midpoint. We prove nondegeneracy in the $Γ$-invariant subspace for every $k\ge2$, and in the full space $H^1(\s^n)$ for sufficiently large $k$: every kernel element is generated by a conformal invariance of the equation. The proof uses separation of variables, Wronskian identities and comparison functions adapted to the singular equations for the angular modes.

papers.title: On lens spaces which may embed in the complex projective plane
papers.abstract: Using an obstruction derived by Owens and relying on Donaldson's Diagonalisation Theorem, we obtain a complete classification of lens spaces of Lisca type $(2)$ or $(3)$ that are unobstructed from embedding in a homology complex projective plane. This classification is further refined for lens spaces $L(p,q)$ with $p$ even, using an obstruction due to Lidman--Moore--Vazquez based on work of Lin. This article is extracted from the author's PhD thesis.

papers.title: Scientist Mothers Working in Childcare Deserts Are Less Likely to Attain Tenure
papers.abstract: Childcare shortages have limited families' access to quality care, with consequences for children's development and parents' careers. We link two decades of childcare supply data to longitudinal surveys of U.S. scientists. We find workplace childcare deserts are widespread: more than half of scientists at universities and research institutions work in deserts, where supply falls significantly short of demand. We further find mothers working in deserts are less likely to attain tenure. They are also more likely to move to industry and part-time positions. Reduced work time partly accounts for the tenure association but other reasons remain. Expanding childcare availability near workplaces may help retain scientific talent.

papers.title: Uniformization of compact Kähler Threefolds of Zero Kodaira Dimension
papers.abstract: Given two smooth compact Kähler threefolds $X$ and $Y$ whose universal covers are biholomorphic, we show that $κ(X) = 0$ if and only if $κ(Y) =0$.

papers.title: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms
papers.abstract: The bottleneck of attention mechanisms, which are the fundamental building block of modern language models, is their quadratic complexity in terms of context size. There has thus been an increasing interest in the compression of the context, also called KV-cache compression. In this article, we consider the problem of compressing the context of attention mechanisms by first formulating it in the Hilbert space associated with its kernel. In this formalism, attention can be represented as the ratio of two linear maps whose interpolant is also the ratio of interpolants, this allows us to consider the interpolation of the linear maps directly. We thus introduce two novel KV-cache compression methods which we call GAIM and Q-DAIM, based on the Generalized Empirical Interpolation Method (GEIM) and the Q-Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method (Q-DEIM), respectively. As the cost of these methods is quadratic in terms of context length, we propose surrogate models based on the Taylor series, the Performer and the Random Fourier Features method which allow the compression to be done in linear time. Finally, we extend this result to the streaming attention setting, providing new methods which allow one to penalize the selection of interpolation nodes based on the previously interpolated context and to update the previous interpolation based on new information. We then provide numerical results on the convergence of the residuals and the output error in future queries and preliminary results on the LongBench-E benchmark showing performance comparable to the state-of-the-art methods. These experiments suggest that the range revealed by our Q-DAIM method could help identify where information is concentrated in the KV cache, thus enabling an efficient compression.

papers.title: Immersed Boundary Electrodiffusion in the Wasserstein Gradient Flow Formalism: Global Well-Posedness, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics, and Singular Asymptotics
papers.abstract: We introduce a unified optimal transport framework for the Immersed Boundary (IB) electrodiffusion active pump model. By representing membrane chemical potential barriers and active pump potentials via smoothed Eulerian kernels ($Ψ_w, \mathcal{H}_w$), we formulate the passive dynamics as an $L^2$-Wasserstein ($W_2$) gradient flow coupled to non-conservative active pushing fields representing ATP-driven $3:2$ $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$ exchangers. We establish global weak existence of solutions to the continuous Poisson--Nernst--Planck--IB system via a split-step Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational scheme, backed by Calderón--Zygmund bounds for non-local Poisson drift and $H^3(\mathbb{S}^1)$ interface regularity under Stokes flow. We prove the continuous Rayleighian energy balance and establish exponential $W_2$-stability of Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) under a quantitative Bakry--Émery curvature threshold. Furthermore, we analyze the dual singular limits of kernel smoothing width $w \to 0$ and dimensionless Debye length $g = λ_D / L \to 0$. We establish the precise asymptotic regime connecting regularized and sharp models, prove the $Γ$-convergence of regularized energy functionals, derive distributional interface flux jump conditions, and resolve $O(λ_D)$ Debye space-charge boundary layers to confirm bulk electroneutrality.

papers.title: Learning Stabilizing Latent Feedback Controllers via Multi-Step Backward Losses
papers.abstract: Can learned latent dynamics models support the design of feedback controllers that provably stabilize the original system? For linear time-invariant systems, we show that learning linear autoencoders and latent dynamics with multi-step prediction-reconstruction losses $\unicode{x2014}$ which we term "backward losses" as they encourage latent trajectories to reconstruct full state trajectories $\unicode{x2014}$ provably recovers the structure needed for stabilization. Specifically, a sufficiently long reconstruction horizon ensures that a minimum ${H}_\infty$-norm controller designed using the learned latent model stabilizes the original system through output-feedback via the corresponding encoder, provided the latent dimension is large enough to capture all non-stable modes of the underlying system. We also show why both reconstruction and a multi-step horizon are essential: forward prediction losses that require only low prediction error along latent trajectories admit global loss minimizers that discard unstable modes regardless of horizon length, while single-step reconstruction losses can yield latent models whose stabilizing controllers fail to stabilize the original system. Finally, experiments on a non-linear flexible-arm system illustrate the practical implications of our results for learning non-linear autoencoders and latent dynamics.

papers.title: Scaling Limits as Extensions of Continuous Bundles of C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We analyze scaling limits in algebraic quantum field theory using continuous bundles of C*-algebras. Different conditions of continuity on such bundles encode different strengths of approximation of the theory by its scaling limit. As a proof of concept, we consider the small-distance scaling limit of the theory of a massive free scalar field, which corresponds to a massless free scalar field. We provide a number of examples of local algebras of observables for which the corresponding bundle of C*-algebras representing the scaling limit is merely lower semicontinuous. Further, we construct an algebra of nonlocal observables for which the corresponding bundle of C*-algebras representing the scaling limit is uniformly continuous.

papers.title: Spectral Convergence of the Discrete Steklov Problem
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Schur complement $\textbf{S}$ of the graph Laplacian, defined on vertices sampled from a domain with $C^2$ boundary. We use a thin boundary layer to approximate the continuum boundary as the number of vertices increases and rely on transportation theory to justify the consistency of a discrete Steklov problem. In particular, $\textbf{S}$ acts on vectors defined over the shrinking boundary layer but behaves asymptotically like a known operator. In this paper, we use a variational argument to determine conditions for which the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $\textbf{S}$ converge to the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, and we provide evidence of this spectral convergence through a numerical example.

papers.title: Fast and Accurate Hydro Unit Commitment
papers.abstract: We introduce a fast novel algorithm to commit hydro-generators. We show that our algorithm can commit 56 generators for 200 days 10,000 times faster than Hexaly, the leading commercial solver for scheduling problems, without sacrificing solution quality. Our method can commit 1792 generators for an entire year in approximately 20 seconds on commodity hardware. Hexaly is unable to solve problems of this size in reasonable time. We attain this runtime improvement by introducing a greedy-heuristic tailored for hydro units. We provide a direction for a possible proof that the error our solver makes decreases with the problem size. This is supported by our experimental results. We prove that our solver's runtime scales log-linearly in the number of generators and time periods.

papers.title: Higher limits over the fusion orbit category via subgroup complexes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a saturated fusion system over a finite $p$-group $S$, and $\mathcal{O}^c (\mathcal{F})$ denote the centric orbit category of $\mathcal{F}$. Suppose that $G$ is a discrete group realizing $\mathcal{F}$, and $\mathcal{C}$ is the collection of all $p$-centric subgroups in $G$. We prove that for every $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)} \mathcal{O} ^c (\mathcal{F})$-module $M$, the higher limits $\lim ^* _{\mathcal{O}^c (\mathcal{F})} M$ are isomorphic to the equivariant cohomology $H_ G ^* (|\mathcal{C}| ; \mathcal{M} )$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is the $G$-equivariant coefficient system on $|\mathcal{C}|$ induced by $M$. This is the fusion system version of a theorem by Grodal for higher limits over the $p$-orbit category $\mathcal{O}_p(G)$ of a finite group $G$. As a consequence, for every fusion system $\mathcal{F}$, we obtain a finite sequence of cohomology groups, involving the cohomology of $\mathcal{F}$, which is exact if and only if the mod-$p$ subgroup decomposition for $\mathcal{F}$ over $\mathcal{F}$-centric subgroups is sharp.

papers.title: Global Testing of Gaussian Means by Combining Marginal and Conditional Evidence
papers.abstract: We propose a test of the global null hypothesis of zero means in correlated multivariate Gaussian data by combining marginal and conditional evidence at each coordinate. The conditional tests are based on the distribution of each coordinate given the remaining coordinates. At each coordinate, the corresponding two-sided $p$-values are combined using the Simes method, followed by a Bonferroni correction across coordinates. Because conditioning can either strengthen or weaken evidence against the null, neither marginal nor conditional testing is uniformly preferable. The proposed procedure adapts to their relative strengths while retaining the simplicity of minimum-type global testing. We establish finite-sample control of the global Type-I error under both known covariance and covariance estimated from an independent sample. The latter setting requires a careful analysis of the dependence between studentized marginal and conditional statistics. We evaluate the power of the proposed test through simulations, compare its performance with existing global tests, and illustrate its practical utility using a TCGA carcinoma dataset.

papers.title: Global strong solutions of the three-dimensional Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system via finite-dimensional scalar forcing
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish global existence of strong solutions for the three-dimensional Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system on the torus through finite-dimensional scalar modifications of a prescribed external force. For arbitrary initial data in $H^1\times H^2$ and any force that is locally bounded in time, we construct two smooth scalar corrections, one added to the third component of the fluid force and the other to the phase source. These corrections involve three fixed Fourier frequencies in the fluid equation and one in the phase equation, and act only on a set of times of arbitrarily small total measure. The proof combines a quantitative local theory with repeated returns of the solution to a fixed ball around zero. These returns rely on small-time asymptotic limits that balance the different scales of the two equations, together with a saturation procedure carefully adapted to the structure of the coupled system. Fluid transport generates the phase frequencies that the chosen phase forcing cannot produce on its own. As a consequence, we also obtain global strong solutions for the three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with a single smooth scalar correction acting on one component of the force at three fixed Fourier frequencies.

papers.title: Incremental Stability of Gradient Flows under Generalized Polyak-Łojasiewicz Inequalities and Its Implications for General Systems
papers.abstract: Gradient flows of twice continuously differentiable strongly convex and convex objectives are, respectively, incrementally exponentially stable and non-expansive in the Euclidean metric. In this work, we investigate to what extent these properties extend to nonconvex objectives satisfying generalized Polyak-Łojasiewicz inequalities. For objectives with a unique minimizer, we establish conditions under which the gradient flow is contracting in a state-dependent Riemannian metric and incrementally exponentially stable.
