For objectives with nonunique minimizers, we generalize the non-expansivity of convex objectives to incremental stability for more general nonconvex objectives. We focus on incremental stability due to its implication to convergence to equilibrium points; when paired with a Lyapunov function it implies pointwise convergence to a minimizer and continuity of the endpoint map. Along the way, we derive new structural results for incrementally stable nonlinear systems and extend the analysis to Heavy-Ball and Dynamical Inertial Newton flows.

papers.title: Equivariant Gradient Degree Comparison via Clarke Duality for Strongly Indefinite Hamiltonian Systems
papers.abstract: We study equivariant gradient degree comparisons for strongly indefinite Hamiltonian systems through Clarke duality. Under suitable convexity and compactness assumptions, we establish a correspondence between the primal and dual equations that preserves the symmetries of their solutions. We derive an identity relating their negative spectral representations and show that the Galerkin-normalized local index of the primal linearization coincides with the equivariant gradient degree determined by the dual Hessian. This comparison extends to infinite-dimensional settings through stabilized Galerkin approximations. We also establish relations between primal and dual crossing forms, equivariant spectral flow, and local equivariant gradient degrees at nondegenerate fixed solutions. The results provide a framework for studying equivariant bifurcation in strongly indefinite systems. As an application, we consider periodic Hamiltonian ring equations with dihedral symmetry and illustrate the computation of equivariant gradient degrees and bifurcation invariants.

papers.title: Basis statistics for phylogenetic tree shape: tree balance formulas beyond expectations
papers.abstract: Summary statistics that measure the shapes of phylogenetic trees contributed to quantitatively understanding evolutionary processes. Among phylogenetic summary statistics, the tree balance indices have been designed to capture intuitive notions of balance or imbalance in trees. Here, we characterize the tree balance indices in terms of basis statistics, mapping the exponentially large space of rooted, binary, unlabeled trees to lower-dimensional spaces. We observe that many tree balance indices can be represented in terms of linear functions of these low-dimensional spaces, enabling us to compute exact formulas for the means, variances, and covariances of many balance indices under the Yule--Harding model. The new framework recapitulates existing formulas for the expectations of 8 indices: Sackin index, average leaf depth, total cophenetic index, $\hat{s}$-shape statistic, Colless index, corrected Colless index, quadratic Colless index, and rooted quartet index for binary trees. It produces new formulas for the expectations of 9 additional indices: equal weights Colless index, total $I$ index, total $I'$ index, Rogers $J$ index, total internal path length, total path length, average vertex depth, stairs1 index, and stairs2 index. Moreover, the framework also allows us to calculate the exact variance of all 17 indices that are represented by the bases as well as the covariance and correlation for all $\binom{17}{2} = 136$ pairs among the 17 indices.

papers.title: Truncated Grassmannians: polytopes, representations, and Cauchy formulas
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to develop algebraic and combinatorial techniques for studying the geometric properties of truncated Grassmannians, a class of algebraic varieties obtained via certain projections of classical Grassmannians within their Plücker embeddings. We introduce a class of cyclic representations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of the general linear Lie algebra, which are proved to serve as duals of the homogeneous components of coordinate rings of truncated Grassmannians. We prove that the characters of these representations are computed via truncated Cauchy formulas and establish a connection with coordinate rings of complete collineations. We also construct monomial bases of these representations in terms of certain generalized chain polytopes and use the RSK correspondence to establish connections with Cauchy-type formulas and with Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.

papers.title: Some properties of completely convex functions
papers.abstract: We study the class $CC_α$ of completely convex functions of order $α$, defined through a two-point analogous of the classical convexity condition. We give several equivalent characterizations of $CC_α$, together with representation formulas in terms of two auxiliary Schwarz functions linked by a compatibility equation. From these representations, we derive coefficient bounds, a subordination result $zf'/f$, and a two-point Taylor expansion in which the Schwarzian derivative $S_f$ arises naturally as the coefficient of the linear term. This yields a pointwise bound for $S_f$ and a bound for the pre-Schwarzian norm $\|P_f\|_{CC_α}$, improving the classical Yamashita bound when $α\leq 1-1/\sqrt2 $. We also show that, unlike the class $C_α$ of convex functions of order $α$, every $f\in CC_α$ is bounded when $α>0$.

papers.title: Addendum to "Optimal Steering of a Linear Stochastic System to a Final Probability Distribution, Part II"
papers.abstract: We hereby fill in a gap in an induction argument used in the proof of a theorem on state-covariance controllability of linear stochastic systems in an earlier paper by the authors. The mathematical statement is true. The missing point in the proof concerns the assertion that, in the canonical single-input case, the control can be assigned arbitrary endpoint values. We amend the argument by proving a slightly stronger induction statement that permits arbitrary finite endpoint jets of the control. An independent approach to homogeneous state-covariance controllability was provided in a paper by Abdelgalil and Georgiou (2025) as a corollary of strong controllability results on $\GLp(n,\mathbb R)$, and shown herein that it extends to the case of additive noise as well.

papers.title: Foatic Homomesy
papers.abstract: Using a unified method of identifying a telescoping function for each statistic-action pair, we prove conjectures of La Croix and Roby, and of Sheridan-Rossi that various permutation statistics, such as the number of fixed points, are homomesic under Foatic actions: compositions of the Foata bijection and dihedral symmetries of one-line notation. Underlying these results is a family of bijective identities relating permutation statistics across the Foata bijection; one of them --- an unexpected invariance of the number of right-to-left minima under reverse-complement, proved by an explicit bijection --- may be of independent interest. The telescoping functions also turn out to be shared among some Foatic actions, implying that mixing certain actions still yields a constant average on closed walks.

papers.title: Quantitative Stability for Anisotropic Gaussian Isoperimetric Inequality
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp, dimension-free quantitative stability theorem for the Gaussian isoperimetric inequality in general Gauss spaces $(\mathbb{R}^n,γ_A)$, where $A$ is an arbitrary positive-definite matrix. More precisely, we show that the anisotropic Gaussian perimeter deficit controls the square of the anisotropic Gaussian asymmetry with a dimension-free constant, recovering the sharp quadratic stability behavior known in the isotropic setting. The central difficulties are the loss of rotational symmetry and the lack of compactness of the isoperimetric sets. The main novelty of our work is a new symmetrization-based reduction to the small-perturbation regime, together with effective Fuglede-type estimates derived from the weighted constant mean curvature equation. These ingredients overcome the principal obstructions created by anisotropy and extend the proof-from-regularity approach to quantitative isoperimetric stability in the anisotropic setting.

papers.title: On the estimation of the Gromov-Hausdorff distance
papers.abstract: The paper investigates the Gromov--Hausdorff distance using a new tool, the so-called $\varkappa$-traces of metric spaces. A general lower bound for the Gromov--Hausdorff distance is obtained in terms of $\varkappa$-traces. Using this bound, exact estimates for the distance between an arbitrary metric space and its Hausdorff hyperspace are derived, and the behavior of the metric on transfinite towers (inductive limits) of hyperspaces is studied. In the final part of the paper, the trace machinery is applied to $l^p$-products of metric spaces. A connection is established between computing the Gromov--Hausdorff distance for infinite $l^\infty$-products and partition calculus. Using methods from Ramsey theory (in particular, the Erdos--Rado theorem), $\varkappa$-traces for $l^\infty$-products are computed, and sufficient conditions are obtained under which the Gromov--Hausdorff distance between infinite Cartesian products can be computed exactly. The final section also provides a general estimate for the Gromov--Hausdorff distance between $l^\infty$-products of metric spaces using the Erdos--Rado theorem.

papers.title: Simple Cuts, Simple Landscape: Dimension-Free Rank Bounds for Burer-Monteiro Factorizations via Rank-Width
papers.abstract: In this work, we study Burer-Monteiro factorizations of semidefinite programs with unit diagonal constraints. For a real symmetric cost matrix whose rank-width over $\mathbb{R}$ is at most $k$, we prove that every non-flat second-order stationary point of the factorized problem is globally optimal whenever the factorization rank is at least $2k$, independently of the matrix size.

papers.title: A phenotype-structured Cahn-Hilliard model
papers.abstract: We propose a phenotype-structure form of the Cahn-Hilliard equation with degenerate mobility and analyze the existence of weak solutions for this new variant. This model is motivated by tumor modeling as multiple phenotypes co-exist within the same tumor and are believed to constitute a continuum of phenotypes. The originality of the model lies in its ability to consider an infinite number of phases and it allows for spatial interactions between phenotypes as well as transport in the phenotypic space, i.e., mutations.

papers.title: Short Jennings series and the modular isomorphism problem
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $G$ a finite $p$-group whose Jennings series has length at most $p$, that is, $D_{p+1}(G)=1$; when $D_p(G)\ne1$ assume also that $G/D_p(G)$ has nilpotency class at most $p-2$. We prove that $G$ is determined up to isomorphism by its modular group algebra $\mathbb{F}_p G$, and indeed by the quotient $\mathbb{F}_p G/\mathrm{I}^{\,ν+1}$, where $\mathrm{I}$ is the augmentation ideal and $ν$ the length of the Jennings series; for an arbitrary finite $p$-group $G$, the quotient $\mathbb{F}_p G/\mathrm{I}^{\,p}$ determines $G/D_p(G)$; and that every automorphism of $\mathbb{F}_p G$ is the product of an automorphism of $G$ and an automorphism inducing the identity on $\mathrm{I}/\mathrm{I}^2$. In particular the modular isomorphism problem has a positive answer for all $p$-groups of exponent $p$ and class less than $p$, and for all $p$-groups of class at most $p-2$ and exponent dividing $p^2$ whose derived subgroup has exponent $p$. Consequently every counterexample in odd characteristic has class at least $p-1$, or a derived subgroup of exponent at least $p^2$, or an element of order $p^3$. The proof combines a descent theorem in the truncated group algebra of a free group, valid for every prime, with a relative rigidity theorem for the unipotent automorphisms of truncated group algebras of groups of exponent $p$, proved through the Lazard correspondence. The bound $p$ is the range in which the logarithm of the group algebra exists.

papers.title: Analysis of Triggered Packet Streams: Stochastic Bounds on System Time under General Triggering Delays
papers.abstract: Many emerging communication systems increasingly involve devices that transmit packets in multiple causally dependent stages as part of an internal workflow, rather than waiting for receiver feedback. To analyze such systems, we recently introduced the $\mathrm{M^T/G/1}$ queue, in which primary customers arrive according to an exogenous Poisson process, and each triggers a secondary customer to join the queue after an independent random delay, called the \textit{triggering delay}. Our prior heuristic approximations assume identical exponential service times, and our matrix-analytic framework assumes exponential triggering delays. However, no exact analysis is available when both distributions are general. In this paper, we derive stochastic bounds, in the usual stochastic order, on the system-time distribution of each customer class under general triggering-delay and service-time distributions. The service times within each primary--secondary pair may be generally dependent. Using sample-path coupling and level-crossing arguments, we show that the stationary workload is stochastically sandwiched between those of two classical queues: a two-class $\mathrm{M/G/1}$ queue with independent Poisson arrivals (lower bound), and a batch-arrival $\mathrm{M^{[2]}/G/1}$ queue where each primary--secondary pair arrives simultaneously (upper bound). Notably, these bounds do not depend on the triggering-delay distribution, and they are asymptotically tight in the sense that the stationary workload converges in distribution to that of the lower- and upper-bound queues as the triggering delays diverge to infinity and converge to zero in probability, respectively. We translate these workload bounds into system-time bounds for each customer class. Simulation experiments support these bounds.

papers.title: The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture is true
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group. A nowhere-zero $A$-flow of a graph gives every edge a direction and a non-zero value in $A$, so that at every vertex the sum of the values on the entering edges equals the sum on the leaving edges. Such a flow can be changed along a cycle: going around the cycle, add a fixed non-zero element of $A$ to the value of every edge that points forward and subtract it from the value of every edge that points backward. The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture states that if $A$ has at least four elements, then in every graph in which all degrees are even, any two nowhere-zero $A$-flows are joined by a chain of such changes through nowhere-zero $A$-flows. It also states that, for every integer $k\ge 4$, the same holds for integer flows whose values are between $1$ and $k-1$ in absolute value, where each change adds a non-zero integer. We prove this conjecture. The core of the proof is an induction on the number of edges: if a flow enters a vertex $v$ along an edge $uv$ and leaves $v$ along an edge $vw$ with the same value, the two edges can be replaced by one edge $uw$, and the induction hypothesis applies to the smaller graph. So the main task is to change every flow into a flow with such a pair of edges. For nowhere-zero $A$-flows with $|A|\ge 4$, replacing vertices of degree more than $4$ by triangles reduces the problem to graphs with all degrees at most $4$. For integer flows, a counting argument joins any two nowhere-zero flows with values in the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_k$, $k\ge 4$, by changes that add $1$, $-1$, $2$ or $-2$; every such chain gives a chain of integer flows with values between $1$ and $k-1$ in absolute value, and every integer flow of this chain reduces modulo $k$ to a flow of the given chain. All results of this paper are also proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant, from Lean's standard axioms alone.

papers.title: On the factorization graph of finite groups
papers.abstract: Given a finite group $G$, the factorization graph $Γ(G)$ has as vertices the nontrivial proper subgroups of $G$, with two distinct vertices $H$ and $K$ adjacent if and only if $HK = G$. In this paper, we study structural and combinatorial properties of $Γ(G)$ for three families of groups: cyclic groups of square-free order, generalized quaternion groups, and dicyclic groups. For cyclic groups $C_{p_1\cdots p_r}$, we describe the global structure of $Γ(G)$ and determine its order, degree sequence, center, girth, and diameter. We also characterize completely when $Γ(G)$ is claw-free, show that it is non-planar for $r \geq 4$, and prove that after removing all pendant vertices, the resulting induced subgraph is 2-connected; we further compute its exact circumference for small $r$, showing it is Hamiltonian precisely when $r=4, 5$. For generalized quaternion groups, we classify all isolated vertices and prove that the reduced factorization graph has diameter two and a unique central vertex. Moreover, we show that it is planar, has chromatic number~$3$, is Eulerian, and non-Hamiltonian, and that it contains maximal induced stars and triangular book subgraphs. Finally, we analyze the dicyclic case and show that the reduced factorization graph is a complete bipartite graph, from which all main invariants follow directly. An explicit SageMath algorithm for constructing $Γ(G)$ is included.
authors: Yesneri Zuleta y E. J. García-Claro

papers.title: Generic properties of the Laplace spectrum and eigenfunctions
papers.abstract: We prove that the spectrum of the Laplace--Beltrami operator on compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary is generically linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Furthermore, we prove that pointwise products of eigenfunctions generically are linearly independent. The proof is based on conformal perturbations of the metric. The result implies in particular that generically the truncation of the continuous functions on $M$ by spectral projections of the Laplace operator is given by symmetric matrices.

papers.title: Modules with unbalanced support
papers.abstract: A finitely generated module has unbalanced support if its support has positive dimension but meets a top-dimensional component of the spectrum only at the closed point. We ask what homological signals are left behind by this geometry. Separating the spectrum into two wings, we prove first Tor nonvanishing for positive-depth modules and give criteria for second Tor nonvanishing. In depth zero, we obtain a structural sequence describing the finite-length torsion under a first Tor vanishing. A recent counterexample to the Peskine--Szpiro dimension inequality conjecture establishes the existence of modules of finite projective dimension and unbalanced support \cite{Ma}. We apply our framework to these modules and establish a numerical torsion--spine balance for linked Cohen--Macaulay wings. We also construct such modules over a reduced Gorenstein ring with exactly two irreducible components.

papers.title: Simple proofs of a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality and their extensions
papers.abstract: We revisit the one-dimensional Gagliardo-Nirenberg interpolation inequality $$\|u'\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R})}\leq C\|u\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R})}^{1-a}\|u''\|_{L^r(\mathbb{R})}^{a},\qquad u\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}),\quad \tfrac12\leq a\leq 1,$$ and recall how its general form follows from the case $a=\frac12$ by interpolation with an endpoint estimate. For $a=\frac12$ and $p=q=r$, we give four alternative proofs, based on integration by parts (two proofs), on an ODE, and on the $L^p$ theory of singular integrals. The two proofs by integration by parts also cover most of the other admissible exponents. In $\mathbb{R}^N$, the integration by parts arguments give the inequality with explicit constants and, for $p\leq 2$, with the Laplacian in place of the Hessian and a constant independent of the dimension. For weighted measures $w(x)\,dx$, a pointwise version of the ODE argument gives the pointwise inequality $|\nabla u|^2\leq C_N\,Mu\,M(Δu)$, where $M$ is the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function, and hence the inequality for Muckenhoupt weights, with the Laplacian and an explicit constant. The integration by parts arguments give it for homogeneous weights of large degree and for superharmonic weights. These results apply, in particular, to power weights and to monomial weights.

papers.title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
papers.abstract: Estimating biased finite-memory sources from a single trajectory is a fundamental problem with practical impact, for example in estimating entropy for cryptography. We study order-$d$ binary sources whose conditional probabilities have bias at most $ε$, and establish *sharp* sample complexity bounds: relative accuracy $γ$ with confidence $1-δ$ needs $γ^{-2}\,(\tfrac12-ε)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\tfrac1δ)$ samples up to constants depending on $ε$, with matching upper and lower bounds and no dependence on mixing time or spectral gap. The proof rests on a sharp bound on expected hitting times of the sliding-window (de Bruijn) chain, which stay of order $1/π(w)$ uniformly in $d$ exactly when $ε<\tfrac3{10}$, and on majorization of the window masses by those of independent biased coins. Applied to published entropy-source validations, the bounds show that their trace lengths may be underpowered: $10^6$ bits cannot resolve all transitions of an $8$-bit model to better than about $4.5\%$ relative error.

papers.title: The full shadow of a polynomial II. Vanishing root masses and holes
papers.abstract: For a complex polynomial $P$, its full shadow is the closure of the set of zeros of all derivatives of all powers $P^n$, and its limiting core is the Hausdorff limit, as $n\to\infty$, of the set of zeros of all derivatives of $P^n$. These sets retain geometric information that weak limits of root-counting measures discard. We determine complete zero-set limits for arrays of polynomials whose roots approach finitely many locations. A cluster containing $o(D)$ roots of a degree-$D$ polynomial can survive outside the limiting support of the derivative zeros, which depends only on the positive limiting masses: under repeated differentiation, the zeros it produces follow a straight path, selected by an explicit min--max condition, and preserve the cluster's exact multiplicity. When such a location instead carries a small positive mass $\varepsilon$, the support of the limiting zero distribution at a fixed ratio of derivative order to degree develops an arc on the $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ scale with a universal local semicircle profile. We use these mechanisms to prove that polynomial shadows can have robust and arbitrarily complicated topology. For every $k\ge2$, there are polynomials with $k+2$ distinct root locations whose limiting cores and full shadows have at least $\binom{k}{2}$ holes; this persists under coefficient perturbations and among square-free polynomials without a reflection axis. In a four-location family, the core and full-shadow areas tend to zero while one hole has area tending to $8/1221$.

papers.title: The nodally bound-preserving finite element method for the transport equation
papers.abstract: Numerical approximations of transport problems, even when stabilised, often violate the bounds respected by the exact solution. Depending on the problem being solved, this can produce non-physical results, such as negative densities or higher-than-unity concentrations. Various bound-preserving numerical methods exist, yet they are usually either conditionally stable or only first-order accurate. In this context, the present work extends the nodally bound-preserving finite element method to the linear transport equation. As a baseline discretisation we use the least-squares finite element method, which is instrumental in achieving unconditional stability for second-order time stepping. It also leads to symmetric algebraic systems, thereby enabling simple, efficient solvers, which we further enhance through Anderson acceleration. Unconditional stability is proved for the backward Euler and Crank--Nicolson discretisations. We also derive error estimates for the fully discrete second-order scheme and provide various numerical examples, including two-phase incompressible flows.

papers.title: Kupershmidt--Nijenhuis structures on pre-Leibniz algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first construct the dual of a representation of a pre-Leibniz algebra and study infinitesimal deformations of a pre-Leibniz algebra with a representation, which lead to Nijenhuis pairs, characterizing trivial deformations, and to dual-Nijenhuis pairs. Building on these notions, we introduce Kupershmidt-(dual-)Nijenhuis structures and show that they give rise to hierarchies of pairwise compatible Kupershmidt operators, the converse holding under an invertibility condition. Finally, we show that Rota--Baxter--Nijenhuis structures, $r$-$n$ structures and BN-structures all arise as particular cases, and that the first two correspond to each other on quadratic pre-Leibniz algebras.

papers.title: An infinite family of conservation laws for perfect compressible fluids
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of an infinite family of conservation laws and, more generally, balance laws, satisfied by plane-symmetric flows of perfect compressible fluids, allowing all components of the velocity vector to be possibly non-vanishing. We cover general pressure laws satisfying solely hyperbolicity and asymptotic conditions. We exhibit an almost quadratic formulation of the Euler equations, which we refer to as the J-formulation, and introduce a reduced Euler system based on an effective mass-energy density and an effective pressure law which account for transverse velocities. We establish the existence of a fundamental kernel which we use to generate all spacetime (quasi-)currents, also called mathematical entropy pairs. We derive explicit formulas for their density and flux components, together with the source-terms of the corresponding balance laws. Furthermore, we establish regularity and asymptotic estimates covering the whole range of physical variables, including vacuum. We prove that the kernel is positive on the interior of its support provided the pressure law satisfies a genuine nonlinearity condition, and we also investigate the future-convexity of the spacetime currents. Throughout, the fluid momentum parallel to the orbits of plane-symmetry is kept arbitrary. In turn, this family of spacetime quasi-currents provides a key ingredient in our companion study of torus-symmetric Einstein-Euler flows with weak regularity.

papers.title: Sharp convex body sparse bounds and quantitative matrix weighted estimates for Hilbert transforms along curves
papers.abstract: We prove convex body sparse bounds for coordinatewise Hilbert transforms along monomial curves and local $C^d$ curves with uniformly nonvanishing torsion on the closed integration interval. Adapting the scalar estimates of Cladek--Ou \cite{CladekOu2018} and the lifting method of Laukkarinen--Lorist \cite{LaukkarinenLorist2026} to the anisotropic geometry, we obtain one sparse family of genuine curve-adapted boxes and quantitative $L^p(W)$ bounds for matrix weights. The convex body sparse exponent range is sharp up to its boundary: estimates hold in the interior of $Ω_d$, while any fixed finite number of sparse families fails outside $\overline{Ω_d}$ when $1/r+1/s>1$. We also establish an explicit endpoint-contact obstruction. For every interior planar exponent pair, a polynomial curve with positive torsion on the open integration interval violates the full-interval sparse estimate.

papers.title: A Local Fourier-Transform Proof of Offen's Spherical Transfer Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $E/F$ be an unramified quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic zero and odd residual characteristic. Offen proved that, on the full spherical space of nondegenerate Hermitian matrices, equality of the Hironaka and Satake transforms implies Jacquet--Ye matching. We give a purely local proof of this theorem. The argument combines Jacquet's compatibility of matching with Fourier transform, the Godement--Jacquet functional equation, and Hironaka's scalar functional equation for Hermitian zeta integrals. The local proof recovers Jacquet's spherical-Hecke fundamental lemma from the unit case.

papers.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
papers.abstract: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.

papers.title: Integral Hodge structures and atoms of fourfolds
papers.abstract: Following the recent work by OpenAI on the irrationality of very general cubic fourfolds in Hassett divisors, we prove some compatibility of Iritani's blow-up formula with the classical blow-up decomposition of integral Hodge structures. As a consequence, we express OpenAI's birational invariant in terms of the theory of atoms developped by Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu. We also show that, for every smooth complex rational cubic fourfold, the primitive cohomology is isometric as an integral Hodge structure to the twisted middle cohomology of a K3 surface and we prove irrationality of the very general Verra fourfold.

papers.title: Tate and Artin--Tate Motivic Tensor-Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: We compute the Balmer spectra of geometric Tate and Artin--Tate motives with $\mathbb{F}_p$-coefficients over any field whose characteristic differs from $p$. For Tate motives, we find the bigraded comparison map to be a homeomorphism to the homogeneous spectrum of the motivic cohomology of the base field. For Artin--Tate motives, we describe the spectrum as a gluing of the spectrum of Artin motives computed by Balmer--Gallauer with the punctured Tate spectrum. We determine all specialisations between these pieces and the resulting topology. Under the hypothesis that the spectrum of rational Tate motives is a singleton, we also compute the integral Tate spectrum after inverting the exponential characteristic of the base field. As a consequence of our results, we identify the punctured Tate spectrum as an open subspace of the spectrum of the category of geometric Voevodsky motives, and draw some conclusions concerning the latter. Finally, we include an appendix where we define generalised periodicity in the context of tensor-triangular geometry, and explore its applications in motivic settings.

papers.title: Heat trace and Riesz means with a large Robin parameter
papers.abstract: We consider the Laplacian with Robin boundary conditions on a smooth Riemannian manifold with boundary and investigate the behavior of various spectral quantities as the Robin parameter approaches infinity. Although the spectrum, heat trace, and Riesz means converge pointwise to their Dirichlet analogues, the asymptotics of these quantities as the spectral parameter approaches infinity, or as time approaches zero, do not. The remainders in the usual asymptotic expansions are not bounded as the Robin parameter approaches infinity. Our main result is a two-term asymptotic expansion for the Robin heat trace that depends jointly on the time variable and the Robin parameter, with a remainder that satisfies a uniform bound independent of the Robin parameter. We apply this result to obtain a similar two-term asymptotic expansion for Riesz means of order at least one, again with a remainder bound independent of the Robin parameter.

papers.title: Exotic involutions on irreducible 4-manifolds from Real Seiberg--Witten theory
papers.abstract: Using Real Seiberg--Witten theory, Miyazawa constructed infinitely many exotic involutions on ${\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$, and Baraglia extended this construction to $X\#{\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$ for a broad class of $4$-manifolds $X$ equipped with an involution $c$. We show that, under suitable Real Seiberg--Witten hypotheses, the ${\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$ summand can be omitted when $X$ is non-spin and the complement of the fixed locus is simply-connected. Our construction also yields infinite families of topologically isotopic but smoothly non-isotopic embeddings of the branch surface in the quotient $X/\langle c\rangle$. As applications, we construct anti-holomorphic involutions on irreducible, simply-connected projective surfaces of general type with infinitely many exotic copies, none of which is anti-symplectic with respect to any orientation-compatible symplectic form. These surfaces include cyclic branched covers of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ and complete intersections of multidegree $(2,4k)$ in $\mathbb{CP}^4$.

papers.title: Monopole-Fermion Scattering from Twisted Conformal Boundary States
papers.abstract: We derive monopole-fermion scattering correlators from conformal boundary states in twisted sectors. The key ingredient is that symmetry-preserving boundary conditions contain sectors twisted by topological symmetry lines. Their overlaps determine correlators of operators attached to these lines, including the outgoing excitations required by charge conservation in the Callan-Rubakov effect. We construct the twisted boundary states of $N$ free Dirac fermions with $U(1)^N$-preserving boundary conditions, extending the familiar description in terms of charge lattices to shifted lattices describing twisted sectors. Using cluster decomposition and open-closed duality, we determine their coefficients and fix their normalization relative to the untwisted boundary state. We find that the Callan-Rubakov boundary condition yields a two-point function between an incoming fermion and an outgoing defect operator with a coefficient of unit modulus, even when the corresponding correlators of ordinary local fermions vanish. Finally, we relate these correlators to four-dimensional partial-wave scattering using gauge-covariant asymptotic states. We identify the missing $s$-wave contribution to the unitarity relation and argue that the twisted channel supplies it with precisely the required normalization.

papers.title: On Boundary State Screening via Solitons
papers.abstract: We present a coarse classification scheme for the boundary data of massive QFTs based on transitions of boundary states via soliton / kink profiles. Starting from the lattice of boundary states, we introduce the boundary screening group $\mathbb{B}$: the equivalence classes of boundary states which cannot be connected by such transitions. In string theory backgrounds which geometrically engineer an interacting QFT in the target space, $\mathbb{B}$ computes the worldsheet analog of the target space defect group $\mathbb{D}$. When $\mathbb{B}$ is non-zero, it provides a diagnostic for having a target space with non-normalizable modes. For interfaces between QFTs, similar considerations imply the existence of a non-trivial conserved charge associated with soliton absorption / transmission, which means that the interface cannot fully dissolve / disappear. Similar considerations hold for junctions of QFTs, which in the special case of string worldsheet CFTs translate to junctions of string theories. We illustrate these general considerations with a number of non-geometric 2D $\mathcal{N} = (2,2)$ Landau-Ginzburg models, as well as their natural lifts to 4D $\mathcal{N} = 1$ Wess-Zumino models.

papers.title: Systolic Geometry and Combinatorics of Surfaces
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates two themes. The first studies systolic embeddings of graph on translation surfaces, proving existence results for essential and cellular systolic embeddings and determining extremal genera for certain graph families. The second examines hyperbolic surfaces in the Thurston set, constructing a one-parameter deformation that increases the sys- tole length and produces Bolza-like surfaces, i.e., surfaces whose systolic geodesics decompose the surfaces into triangles, for infinitely many genera. A symmetry property of geodesic inter- sections on these surfaces is also established, together with an application of these Bolza-like surfaces.

papers.title: Homotopy in enriched functor categories: Frobenius exact structures and weak Serre functors
papers.abstract: Let $(\V, \otimes, I,[-,-])$ be a closed symmetric monoidal category with finite (co)limits. Assume that $\V$ is weakly idempotent complete and additive. For a given small $\V$-category $\A$, we investigate sufficient conditions on $\A$ under which the ordinary category $[\A, \V]_0$ of $\V$-functors from $\A$ to $\V$, equipped with the exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$, is a Frobenius exact category,and hence, induces a triangulated stable category. The exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$ encompasses the degre-wise trivial exact structure on categories of $N$-chain complexes and $m$-periodic chain complexes, with terms in a variety of settings, including left $R$-modules, quasi-coherent sheaves on a scheme, and Banach spaces. We subsequently address the question of describing abstract left and right homotopy relations in $([\A, \V]_0;\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}})$ in terms of families of morphisms defined objectwise, as in the cases of chain-homotopy and relative homotopy relations. To this end, we introduce the notion of left/right-weak Serre $\V$-functors on $\A$, and investigate their relationships with the classical Serre functor relative to a commutative ring $k$.

papers.title: Sharp Nonlocal Poincaré Inequalities and Liminf Lower Bounds for Sobolev and BV Energies on Metric Measure Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $p\in[1,\infty)$, and let $(X,ρ,μ)$ be a complete doubling $q$-Poincaré space for some $q\in[1,p]$ with a lower dimension $d$ and an upper dimension $D$. In this article, we establish Poincaré inequalities for two families of nonlocal nonconvex functionals defined using distances or volumes. More precisely, for any ball $B$ with its radius $r_B\in(0,\operatorname{diam} X)$, any $λ\in(0,\infty)$, and any measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\frac{1}{μ(B)^2}\int_B\int_B|f(x)-f(y)|^p\,dμ(x)\,dμ(y)\\ &\quad\lesssimλ^pr_B^pφ(B)^{γp}+\frac{λ^pr_B^p}{μ(B)}\mathop{\int_{ΛB}\int_{ΛB}}\limits_{\genfrac{}{}{}{2}{|f(x)-f(y)|}{ρ(x,y)φ(x,y)^γ}>λ}\frac{φ(x,y)^{γp}}{V(x,y)}\,dμ(x)\,dμ(y), \end{align*} where $V(x,y):=μ(B(x,ρ(x,y)))$ and either $φ=ρ$ with $φ(B)=r_B$ and $γ\in(-\infty,-\frac{\min\{q,D\}}{p}]$ or $φ=V$ with $φ(B)=μ(B)$ and $γ\in(-\infty,-\frac{q}{p\max\{q,d\}}]$. Here both ranges of $γ$ are sharp over the class of $q$-Poincaré spaces with the prescribed lower and upper dimensions, and the constant $Λ\in[1,\infty)$ and the implicit positive constant depend only on $p$, $γ$, and the geometric constants of $X$. We also obtain lower bounds for Sobolev energy and total variation in terms of the limit inferior of these functionals, for $γ$ in either the above negative ranges or $(0,\infty)$. Our proofs use the curve characterization of Poincaré spaces and an adaptive dyadic refinement argument based on medians.

papers.title: On Some Special Cases of the Weber-Schafheitlin Integral
papers.abstract: We consider special cases of the discontinuous Weber--Schafheitlin integral in which the orders $μ$ and $ν$ of the Bessel functions differ by an integer and the exponent $λ$ equals $0$ or $\pm1$, with $μ-ν+λ$ odd. Explicit closed-form results are obtained in terms of Jacobi polynomials.

papers.title: Harborth's theorem p(5)=18 revisited
papers.abstract: Let $p(n)$ be the minimum cardinality of a finite planar point set in which each point has exactly $n$ unit-distance neighbours. Harborth proved $p(5)=18$ in work presented in 1985 and published in 1987, using a detailed case analysis. We revisit the proof using convex-hull arguments, incidence counts, and elementary properties of intersections of unit circles. These tools give an alternative treatment of configurations with $14$ and $16$ points and organize the final case distinction by a common vector-sum structure. We also treat a configuration not explicitly covered by the case analysis in the online PDF copy of Harborth's paper available to us, and give an explicit justification of the six-point classification used in the argument. No result subsequent to Harborth's proof is required.

papers.title: Bernstein and Stieltjes properties of some functions involving logarithmic functions
papers.abstract: We show that $\frac1{g(x)}$, with $g(x)=\frac{x-1}{x\ln x}$, is a complete Bernstein function and give its Lévy measure explicitly. For $h(x)=\frac{(x^2-1)\ln(x+1)}{x^2\ln x}$, we prove that $h$ is not a Stieltjes function, so $\frac1h$ is not a complete Bernstein function, but $\frac1h$ is a Bernstein function. The latter rests on the positivity of a function built from the convolution of the exponential integrals $E_1$ and $E_2$. We also give a related completely monotonic function that is not a Stieltjes function.

papers.title: The Geometry of Multitask Learning: Sharp Rates for Shared Subspace Estimation
papers.abstract: Learning a shared subspace in multitask learning is an important statistical problem, yet exact rates remain poorly understood in many of the formal settings considered in the literature. To address this gap, which arises from limitations of existing upper-bound techniques, we propose a general multitask lemma. The lemma provides sufficient conditions for fast subspace estimation in generic multitask settings, in the form of geometric conditions on the task regression functions and their estimators. We subsequently show that the multitask lemma yields sharp minimax rates---previously unknown---for linear regression and classification in the regimes considered, and rates matching up to logarithmic factors for additive-noise regression.

papers.title: Anti-concentration and Graham's rearrangement problem in finite abelian groups
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a subset of $n$ elements of a group $G$. An ordering $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of its elements is valid if the partial sums $x_1,x_1+x_2,\ldots,x_1+\cdots+x_n$ are pairwise distinct. This notion has a long history in combinatorial group theory, dated back to Gordon's works in early 1960. Alspach-Liversidge conjecture asserts that any subset of the nonzero elements of a finite abelian group $G$ has a valid ordering. This generalizes Graham's conjecture, which considers the case when the group $G$ is $\mathbb{F}_p$, the cyclic group of prime order. Graham's conjecture has been solved recently, as a combination of results by Kravitz, Bedert and Kravitz, Müyesser and Pokrovskiy, Bedert, Bucić, Kravitz, Montgomery, and Müyesser, and Pham and Sauermann. Beside this, the only other case where Alspach-Liversidge conjecture has been confirmed is $G=\mathbb{F}_2^k$, thanks to a recent result by Bedert, Bucić, Kravitz, Montgomery, and Müyesser. We prove the Alspach-Liversidge conjecture in its full generality. Our proof combines ideas from many previous papers. In particular, we will use the probabilistic approach and the absorption method. Our new main technical ingredient is a Fourier-moment estimate, which is of independent interest. In particular, we can use it to show that the distribution of certain kinds of random sums in an abelian group has an almost uniform distribution.

papers.title: JT gravity as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks
papers.abstract: We prove that flat Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity arises as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks. We give a clean criterion, formulated in terms of branching explorations, for a discrete model to converge to this conjecturally universal limit. For simplicity, we apply this criterion to a Boltzmann ensemble of disks with rectilinear boundary, defined by summing over combinatorial types and integrating over lengths. As the length of a distinguished side tends to infinity, the rescaled surface converges in law to a continuum random surface prescribed by Ferrari's path-integral formulation of JT gravity. Convergence is in the topology of smooth convergence of the conformal factors on compact subsets of the interior when uniformizing in a fixed domain; the limiting conformal factor is described by a harmonic Gaussian field closely related to holomorphic multiplicative chaos. The crux is a branching exploration of flat JT gravity whose lengths evolve as conditioned Cauchy processes and whose unexplored components are conditionally independent. We construct this exploration using a conformal welding theorem proved in a companion paper, and show that it is the scaling limit of Budd's row-by-row exploration of the discrete disks, analogous to the peeling of random planar maps. Under a tightness condition, our criterion upgrades this convergence to a conformal scaling limit for the discrete disks. Other natural combinatorial disk models admit analogous first-row recursions, providing a route to their scaling limits.

papers.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact Kähler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.

papers.title: Central Limit Theorems and Network-Free Inference for Heterogeneous Spatial Autoregressions on Sparse Graphons
papers.abstract: Network dependence is widely regarded as a fundamental obstacle to inference: outcomes linked through a graph are not independent, the graph is rarely observed in full, and models for how dependence propagates are easily misspecified. We show that for a broad class of responses generated through a random network, the obstacle is smaller than it appears. We study a heterogeneous spatial autoregression on a sparse graphon, in which each node's response is a weighted average of its neighbors' responses with a node-specific, nonparametric coefficient plus a node-specific input, and we prove that sample means and smooth functions of vector means are asymptotically Gaussian down to average degree nearly logarithmic in the population size, allowing unbounded graphons with hubs and heavy-tailed inputs. The limiting variance interpolates exactly between two regimes according to the sampling fraction. When the observed nodes are a vanishing fraction of the population, the variance is the marginal variance of the response, the ordinary sample variance is consistent, and the usual $t$-interval is valid with no knowledge of the network. The proof averages over the graph rather than conditioning on it, isolating the behavior of the response through an exact identity for resolvents of Markov kernels and controlling the network noise by an Efron-Stein inequality; neither step requires the walk-by-walk covariance bounds of fixed-network analyses. Consequences for regression with node-level and network-derived covariates are derived.

papers.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
papers.abstract: We investigate counting problems for discrete (geometric) structures in tropical settings, motivated by the comparison of the expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games. First, we give an upper bound on the number of coherent matching fields of type $(n,r)$ and a lower bound on the number of combinatorial types of $n$-hyperplane sequences in the max-plus tropical space of dimension $r-1$. These structures are closely related, and our bounds establish that as $n \to \infty$, for every fixed $r$ their number equals $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$. This in turn implies that the number of regular triangulations of the products of simplices $Δ^{n-1}\timesΔ^{r-1}$ is also $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$, thereby answering a question of Santos. Second, we obtain that the number of labeled order types over the reals and over the signed tropical numbers coincide at first order, establishing a comparison of the expressivity of mean-payoff games and linear programs as measured by labeled order types. Last, the subclass of mean-payoff games known as parity games arise from linear programs by a ``double tropicalization.'' We show that the number of labeled order types obtained after this double tropicalization collapses.

papers.title: Improved Gradient Complexity for Quasi-Newton Proximal Extragradient Methods via Certified Curvature Reuse
papers.abstract: We study how curvature estimated from gradient differences can accelerate proximal-extragradient quasi-Newton methods. Existing global guarantees for QNPE, A-QNPE, and OL-OQN learn Hessian approximations online and incur dimension dependence through regret bounds. We introduce certified curvature reuse: one finite-difference probe per iteration refreshes a group of Hessian columns, while a path-length certificate controls the error of stale columns and determines the step. Each iteration uses at most three gradient queries and one regularized linear solve (or trust-region step), without a gradient line search or an inner oracle-querying loop. In the convex and strongly convex settings, bisection on stored scalar quantities selects a near-maximal certified stepsize; in the nonconvex setting, a uniform certificate gives an explicit learning rate. With other problem parameters fixed, the convex method attains $O(\min\{k^{-2},dk^{-3}\})$ in a single run, with no logarithmic factor or additive dimension term, matching accelerated gradient descent (AGD) for $k\lesssim d$ and improving on A-QNPE thereafter. In the strongly convex setting with condition number $κ$, a single run matches AGD's $(1-Θ(κ^{-1/2}))^k$ rate for $k\lesssim d\logκ$ and achieves a superlinear upper envelope, eventually scaling as $(1+k^2/B^2)^{-k}$ with $B=\tilde O(dκ)$, improving on QNPE. In the nonconvex setting, the method finds an $\varepsilon$-stationary point in $O(\min\{d^{1/3}\varepsilon^{-3/2},\varepsilon^{-7/4}\})$ gradient queries, improving on OL-OQN's $O(d^{1/4}\varepsilon^{-13/8})$. For sparse Hessians, $d$ is replaced by an effective dimension $χ\le d$. We also compare our bounds with lazy-Hessian, double-loop, and cutting-plane methods.

papers.title: A self-normalized law of the iterated logarithm for Rademacher random multiplicative functions
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers, and let $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}f(n)$. We prove a two-sided law of the iterated logarithm normalized by the full predictable quadratic variation \[ Q(x)=\sum_{p\le x}\bigg(\sum_{\substack{m\le x/p\\ P(m)<p}}f(m)\bigg)^2 \] of the martingale obtained by revealing the prime signs. Almost surely, \[ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{M(x)}{\sqrt{2Q(x)\log\log x}}=1, \qquad \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{M(x)}{\sqrt{2Q(x)\log\log x}}=-1. \] The same equalities hold with $\log\log Q(x)$ in the denominator. The almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$. This gives a self-normalized version of the questions of Wintner and Erdős on almost sure fluctuations. We also prove that $Q(x)/q(x)$ cannot converge in probability to $1$ for any positive deterministic function $q$. Moreover, \[ \limsup_{x\to\infty} \frac{|M(x)|}{\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4}} \] is either an almost surely finite and positive random variable with nondegenerate distribution or infinite almost surely. We do not determine which alternative holds.

papers.title: Some remarks on robust features of surfaces in 4-space
papers.abstract: We study robust features of smooth surfaces in 4-space associated with contact with lines and hyperplanes. We investigate the local and multi-local singularities of orthogonal projections and height functions that describe these contacts and their corresponding geometric loci on the surface. At an $A_4$-singularity of a height function, we show that the $A_3$-curve and the $A_1A_2$-curve are generically tangent with contact of order $2$. We further establish criteria for the versality of the families of height functions and orthogonal projections in terms of the regularity of the $B_2$-curve and $S_2$-curve, respectively. Finally, we obtain the $[A_2]$- and $(A_0S_0)_2$-curves arising from multi-local singularities of orthogonal projections and describe their tangency properties at the $B_3$- and $H_3$-singularities.

papers.title: Critical Robin Problems on Manifolds with Noncompact Boundary
papers.abstract: We work on connected, noncompact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds $(\mathcal{M}, g), n \geq 3$, that are complete with respect to $d_g$ and have noncompact boundary and bounded geometry. We study the existence of positive solutions in $C^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{\infty}(\mathcal{M})$ to the Yamabe problem: $$ \left\{\begin{aligned} -Δ_g u+\frac{n-2}{4(n-1)} R_g u & =\mathscr{C}_0 u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} \quad \text { in } \mathcal{M}, \\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial ν}+\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)} H_g u & =\mathscr{C}_1 u^{\frac{n}{n-2}} \quad \text { on } \partial \mathcal{M}, \end{aligned}\right. $$ where $\mathscr{C}_0=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}), \mathscr{C}_1=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}) \mathscr{C} \bar{d}^{\frac{2}{n-2}}$, the parameter $\mathscr{C} \geq 0$ is fixed, and $$ Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}):=\inf _{u \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \backslash\{0\}} \frac{E_g(u)}{\left(\|u\|_{L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M})}^{2^*}+\mathscr{C}\|u\|_{L^{2^{\#}}(\partial \mathcal{M})}^{2^*}\right)^{2 / 2^*}} . $$ Here $E_g$ is the associated quadratic energy. We assume $Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M})<Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})$ and $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})>0$, where $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}$ is the corresponding variational level at infinity. We approach this problem using nonnegative solutions $u_j \in W_{\partial}^{1,2}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j)\right), j \in \mathbb{N}, j \geq j_0$, for which we prove that $$ \sup _{j \geq j_0}\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^{\infty}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j-1)\right)}<\infty . $$ For $\mathscr{C}>0$, we also prove that, along a subsequence, $\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^2{ }_{\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j) \cap \partial \mathcal{M}\right)}} \rightarrow \bar{d}$, with $0<\bar{d} \leq \mathscr{C}^{-1 / 2^*}$. For $\mathscr{C}=0$, we set $\bar{d}=0$.

papers.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, reduced and immersed
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a `reduced' form of permutation twisted cohomology as introduced by Balmer--Gallauer and further developed by Miller. This ring is bigraded by a well-chosen choice of endotrivial complex, rather than multigraded by a family of endotrivial complexes. The Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules openly immerses into the homogeneous spectrum of this ring. We also show that for $p$-groups, Miller's `remixed' twisted cohomology ring also admits the Balmer spectrum as an open subspace, and confirm in both cases it can be upgraded to have Dirac scheme structure; furthermore, we prove that the two open covers witnessing this are in general different.

papers.title: Almost Homogeneity Characterizes Almost Bi-Lipschitz Euclidean Embeddability
papers.abstract: A metric space admits an almost bi-Lipschitz embedding into a Euclidean space if and only if it is almost homogeneous. We prove the sufficient direction, complementing the known necessary condition. More quantitatively, we bound the target dimension and the embedding constants for every logarithmic exponent $γ>1$. The bounds depend only on the covering parameters in the almost homogeneity condition. In particular every doubling metric space admits such an embedding. This answers a question of Margaris and Robinson and the almost bi-Lipschitz part of a question of Olson and Robinson. As a consequence, the difference set of the image is doubling, which answers the difference-set questions of Olson and Robinson and of Margaris.

papers.title: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten-Stigum
papers.abstract: We give the first polynomial-time algorithm to estimate the partition function of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the uniformly random $d$-regular graph to arbitrarily high accuracy for all inverse temperatures up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold. This is the entire regime in which the model is "replica symmetric," and is conjectured to be optimal for polynomial-time counting and sampling. To achieve our algorithmic result, we establish the absence of Fisher zeros for the partition function in a constant-width strip around the interval from $0$ up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, with high probability over the randomness of the input graph. AI Disclosure: The overarching vision and proof architecture were developed solely by the authors without AI input. GPT 5.5 Pro was used, with extensive guidance from the authors, for only a few minor technical aspects of the proof. The authors independently verified correctness and wrote everything by hand. We take full responsibility for its contents. A more detailed statement can be found in Section 1.2.

papers.title: An Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs
papers.abstract: Given a graph $G$, does it have quantum symmetries, or in other words, is the algebra of the quantum automorphism group non-commutative? In the world of ordinary groups, determining whether a finitely presented group is commutative is undecidable. This is an immediate consequence of the Adian-Rabin theorem, which shows that many natural properties of finitely presented groups are undecidable. In this paper, we prove an Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs, showing that many natural properties of the quantum automorphism group of a graph (including having quantum symmetries) are undecidable. We also show that it's undecidable to determine if the discrete quantum automorphism group is non-trivial. Our methods are based on solution groups of linear system nonlocal games, and we also prove an Adian-Rabin theorem in this context.

papers.title: Early career researcher responses to AI in math
papers.abstract: We've heard a lot about AI in math from Fields medalists, AI labs, and established professors. However, the personal stakes are highest for early career researchers. Hoping to provide a platform for graduate students and postdocs to voice their opinions, concerns, and experiences, we wrote and distributed a survey on AI in math. In this article, we share the responses to our survey. All responses are anonymous, and respondents came from almost $60$ institutions and at least $5$ countries. Our survey included both multiple choice questions and more open-ended free response questions. If you are a senior mathematician or university administrator reading these survey results, our goal is for you to understand the concerns of the younger generations and use your authority to take action accordingly. If you are an early career mathematician reading these survey results, we hope you find comfort in the knowledge that your experiences are shared by many others. If you are not a mathematician, we hope you come away from this article with a deeper understanding of the goals, values, and concerns of the community.

papers.title: Asymptotic GIT-stability of KSB-stable varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that KSB-stable varieties introduced by Kollár and Shepherd-Barron as a generalization of Deligne-Mumford's stable curves are stable in the sense of geometric invariant theory (GIT). More precisely, we show that KSB-stable varieties are asymptotically GIT-stable with respect to a sequence of linearizations defined by the Hodge bundle.

papers.title: Supersaturation: Cliques and Positive Square Energy
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n$ and let $k_r$ denote the number of unlabeled copies of $K_r$ in $G$. Let $s^+$ denote the sum of the squares of the positive adjacency eigenvalues of $G$. For every fixed integer $r\geq2$, we prove that, as $n \to \infty$ \[ \sqrt{s^+}>\left(1-\frac1r\right)n \quad\Longrightarrow\quad k_{r+1}\geq \left(\frac1{r^{r-1}}-o_r(1)\right)n^{r-1}. \] The coefficient $r^{-(r-1)}$ is asymptotically best possible; in particular, the triangle case gives $k_3\geq n/2-o(n)$. The proof combines positive square energy stability, the clique removal lemma, and a sharp clique count around a maximum $r$-cut. The triangle case requires an additional block-matrix argument.

papers.title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
papers.abstract: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. As an application, we give presentations for the so-called \textit{sisters} of the standard Picard modular groups for $d=3, 7,$ and $11$. In particular, this shows that the sister of $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_7)$ is a perfect group.

papers.title: Self-regularization and structural adaptation of NPMLE for Gaussian mixture models in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish structural properties of the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) for $d$-dimensional Gaussian mixtures whose means lie in a hypercube. We show that, with high probability, the NPMLE based on $n$ independent observations self-regularizes by fitting a mixture model with $O((\frac{\log n}{\log\log n})^d)$ components, achieving the optimal model complexity without explicit model selection. Furthermore, the NPMLE exhibits a structural adaptation property: For data drawn from a finite mixture, the number of fitted components is bounded in probability as $n\to\infty$. Our proof applies a multivariate Jensen-type bound to control the typical number of critical points of the KKT function associated with the first-order optimality conditions. The key step is to lower bound its gradient norm uniformly on complex spheres. We establish this lower bound by decomposing the KKT function into an empirical fluctuation term and a relative density estimation error term, combining small-ball probability estimates for the former with polynomial approximation and Hellinger error bounds for the latter.

papers.title: Power Adjusting Games Under Block-Dependent Pool Payout Schemes
papers.abstract: Advanced power adjusting block withholding attacks such as PAW and T-PAW have been analyzed so far under a global-reset version of the proportional scheme (GRP), which is rarely used in practice. In this paper, we analyze T-PAW, which contains FAW and PAW as special cases, under the block-dependent payout schemes deployed in practice: Pay-Per-Last-N-Shares (PPLNS), round-based Proportional (PROP) and exponential-decay (EXP). We derive the revenue ratios analytically, by renewal arguments for PPLNS and through the stationary carry process of an open round for PROP and EXP. We further introduce Power Adjusting Hopping (PAH), where an adversary of any size adjusts its power allocation towards the pool according to the blockwork age of the round without withholding any block, and derive its revenue ratios under PROP and EXP. We show that GRP misestimates the T-PAW gain in a scheme-dependent direction: it overstates the gain under PROP up to an order of magnitude and understates it under EXP for the original slush decay rate. PROP is highly vulnerable to PAH, while EXP faces a trade-off: a slow decay invites PAH and a fast decay invites T-PAW. PPLNS is the least vulnerable scheme: it is immune to PAH and it mitigates, but does not eliminate, T-PAW. All analytical results are verified by Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: The Value of Experiments in Assortment Optimization
papers.abstract: Retailers can learn customer preferences by experimenting with different assortments. However, the cost of each experiment and the operational burden of repeatedly changing product offerings can make extensive experimentation impractical. We study how much a retailer can improve its final assortment decision using customer observations from one (or a very small number of) fixed experimental assortments. We consider the multinomial logit model, where product revenues are known but customer preferences are unknown. In this setting, we jointly design the experimental assortment and the rule for selecting a final assortment from observed customer choices to minimize worst-case regret: the expected revenue loss of the final assortment relative to an optimal assortment under the true preferences, maximized over possible customer preferences. We first characterize exactly the minimax regret and an optimal assortment when no experimentation is possible. We then show, surprisingly, that offering a single experimental assortment to just one customer can already substantially reduce regret, depending on how the products' revenues compare. We derive the exact minimax regret and an optimal experimental policy in this setting. When a single fixed experimental assortment is offered to many customers, we give a geometric characterization of the limiting minimax regret and construct an asymptotically optimal policy. Depending on product revenues, this single experiment can yield no improvement over no experimentation or nearly complete regret reduction. Finally, we extend our analysis to multiple experimental assortments chosen in advance, characterizing the limiting minimax regret, constructing asymptotically optimal policies, and identifying which collections of assortments allow worst-case regret to vanish as the number of customer observations grows.

papers.title: Convergence of a drainage network model with branching to the Brownian net
papers.abstract: We consider a drainage network model represented by a system of coalescing random walks exhibiting long range dependence before coalescence. This model was introduced by Gangopadhyay et. al. [GRS04] and Coletti et. al. [CFD09] proved its convergence to the Brownian web under diffusive scaling. Santos et. al. [SVZ24] considered a branching version of this model where branching occurs with low probabilities varying with the scaling parameter and showed that any sub-sequential limit contains a copy of the Brownian net. It was conjectured that the limit is indeed the Brownian net. In this work we prove this conjecture. Further, compared to [SVZ24], we explore the question of scaling limit in a wider spectrum of scaling regime. This work contributes to the broader understanding of the basin of attraction of the Brownian net.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness of the $2$D Euler Evolutions with $L^1\cap L^p$ Vorticity
papers.abstract: For each prescribed $1<p<\infty$, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\cap L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)$ that admits two distinct evolutions under the unforced two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on $[0,1]$. Both vorticities are strongly continuous in $L^1\cap L^p$ and are transported exactly by their respective almost-everywhere invertible, measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flows. The construction couples unstable four-vortex configurations across increasingly small spatial scales, realizing them through concentrated signed vortex patches. At each finite cutoff, a prepared reference evolution remains close to rotating configurations, while a second evolution differs initially only at the finest scale. In the second evolution, the finest configuration consists of separating dipoles whose remote strain activates the instability of the next larger configuration. This process propagates through successive scales with summable transition times. As the cutoff tends to infinity, the two families of initial data converge strongly, along a subsequence, to the same datum, while a nonzero difference survives at a fixed larger scale and is detected by a fixed smooth observable at a positive limiting time. Quantitative concentration and relative comparison estimates establish this cascade for exact Euler patch solutions. Strong compactness through inverse-flow stability then preserves both exact vorticity transport and the positive-time distinction between the two limiting evolutions. The initial datum and construction parameters may depend on $p$.

papers.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in $2$D Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp uniqueness--nonuniqueness criterion for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations within a class of stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices. Let $Θ$ be any finite nondecreasing envelope for the vorticity $L^p$ norms, and set $I_Θ=\int_{p_0}^\infty Θ(p)^{-1}\,dp$. If $I_Θ=\infty$, every array in the corresponding class admits a unique Euler evolution, even among bounded energy-admissible weak velocity solutions. If $I_Θ<\infty$, there exists a compactly supported array in the same class admitting two distinct unforced Lagrangian Euler evolutions from the same initial datum. The criterion holds for arbitrary nondecreasing envelopes $Θ$.

papers.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
papers.abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.

papers.title: Sharp lifespan estimates for heat equations with Hörmander operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem $u_t-\mathcal L u=h(t)u^p$, $u(0)=\varepsilon u_0\ge0$, where $p>1$, $h\ge0$ is only locally integrable, and $\mathcal L=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j^2$ is a homogeneous Hörmander sum of squares on $\mathbb R^n$ of homogeneous dimension $q$. Diffusion spreads the solution out and weakens the nonlinearity, while the reaction $h(t)u^p$ may force blow-up. We prove that the outcome is decided by the single quantity $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T)=\int_0^Th(t)(1+t)^{-\frac q2(p-1)}\,d t$, in which the reaction at time $t$ is weighted by the factor by which diffusion has weakened the solution: small data are global if $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(\infty)<\infty$, while otherwise the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ satisfies $c\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}\le\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T_\varepsilon)\le C\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for small $\varepsilon$. Our technique of proof is based on a backward-semigroup functional combined with a Gaussian-envelope energy and an ODE cap telescoped along interlaced geometric grids. The result contains the Euclidean, Heisenberg, Carnot and Grushin cases, yields explicit lifespan laws for power, logarithmic, exponential, periodic and intermittent coefficients, and exhibits effects with no autonomous counterpart, such as a lifespan with no power law in $\varepsilon$. We also prove regularity and a priori estimates for classical solutions and discuss what remains true for a general nonlinearity $f(u)$.

papers.title: Willmore inequalities beyond the injectivity radius
papers.abstract: We generalize a method first introduced by Li, Yau, Simon, and Topping (for closed surfaces immersed in the flat Euclidean space), and we establish a global-in-nature estimate, with an explicit cut-locus contribution, on the Willmore energy of closed surfaces that are immersed in a complete Riemannian three-manifold and need not be embedded. Our estimate applies to ambient spaces whose sectional curvature is bounded above and whose injectivity radius may be finite. For positive upper curvature bounds, the global weighted estimates require an explicit radius restriction. The Willmore energy is bounded below by a functional involving the self-intersection number of the surface and the injectivity radius of the ambient space. Furthermore, by investigating in what sense our inequalities are optimal and realized by geodesic spheres in constant curvature spaces, we are led to introduce a weighted version of the Willmore functional, which is adapted to geodesic spheres in the model spaces and takes the sectional curvature of the ambient space into account. As a corollary, we obtain sufficient conditions for an immersed surface in a curved space to be embedded.

papers.title: A Behavioral approach to Constrained Linear Quadratic Control: Feasibility and Optimality
papers.abstract: This paper develops a constrained linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control framework within the behavioral approach. Unlike classical formulations that rely on state-input representations, our method treats both the system dynamics and the constraints as trajectory-level objects. The system is modeled through a kernel representation, while inequality constraints are captured using behavioral inequalities defined over infinite-dimensional convex cones. Using quadratic differential forms (QDFs) to encode performance indices, we formulate the constrained LQ problem as a convex variational optimization over trajectories. By employing Gateaux differentials, we derive the stationarity and complementarity conditions and show that they admit a representation as an augmented behavioral system whose unique decomposition into autonomous and controllable sub-behaviors yields a complete parameterization of all optimal constrained trajectories. The resulting conditions constitute a behavioral analogue of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) framework. A numerical example illustrates the effect of inequality constraints on the optimal behavior. The framework provides a general, trajectory-level representation for constrained optimal control and opens avenues for closed-loop and data-driven extensions.

papers.title: A DG algebra structure for the edge ideal of any split graph
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit DG algebra structure on the minimal free resolution of the quotient of a polynomial ring by the edge ideal of any split graph (that is, a graph whose vertex set is a disjoint union of a clique and an independent set). The algebra structure is based on a simple combinatorial notion, which we call the fixing edge of a pair of edges, that directly captures the structure of the underlying graph. Our construction involves an explicit description of the minimal free resolution of the edge ideal of such a graph, including formulas for both the Betti numbers and the differentials.

papers.title: Rate-Optimal Spectral Likelihood-Ratio Clustering in Stochastic Block Models
papers.abstract: Spectral clustering commonly assigns communities by clustering a low-dimensional representation, whereas likelihood refinement can improve an initial assignment using the observed edges. We ask whether sharp community-recovery accuracy can be retained when the refinement no longer accesses individual edges. We develop spectral likelihood-ratio clustering for stochastic block models using one regularized adjacency eigensystem and the original vertex degrees. The method estimates connection probabilities and updates each vertex's label by a likelihood-ratio classifier on reconstructed rows. The refinement accepts any sufficiently accurate initialization, including one computed from the same graph. Its expected misclassification proportion is bounded by a constant times the error of a raw-edge oracle classifier, plus the probability that initialization misses the required accuracy. Repeated k-means++ on the retained spectral coordinates supplies one complete procedure with a constant-factor oracle guarantee. The oracle knows the model parameters and the other labels. The guarantee holds for a fixed number of communities, comparable positive block probabilities and community sizes, and a nondegenerate normalized block matrix. It allows arbitrarily slowly diverging expected degrees under the stated upper sparsity condition. We explain the likelihood-ratio construction first, then the regularization and exact-degree correction required by the general result. The proof combines sharp local testing, truncated spectral-row estimates and leave-one-out comparisons.

papers.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
papers.abstract: We introduce NEOPIC, a framework for learning the field operator in particle-based methods applied to kinetic plasma simulations. Its key novelty is a neural operator that acts directly on the empirical measure of the particles, rather than on a grid, and is evaluated at the particle positions. No mesh or tree is needed and, unlike grid-based neural operators, no deposition onto a mesh takes place, so the particle noise that dominates the inputs of particle simulations is not aliased. Since it replaces only the field solve, it serves as a plug-and-play field solver for particle-based methods: it can be trained on data from particle-in-cell, particle-in-Fourier or tree codes, and combined with any time integrator, including implicit schemes. We prove that the discrete evaluation coincides with the continuous operator at any number of particles (representation equivalence) and derive an error analysis that separates sampling, learning and time-stepping errors: up to the learning error, NEOPIC has the error structure of standard Monte Carlo particle methods. We show that the particle noise in the training data acts as an implicit regularizer, which gives guidance on the number of training particles in relation to the particle numbers used at inference. A complexity analysis shows that NEOPIC is an $O(N_p)$ method whose constants are set by the architecture alone, independently of any mesh or tree. Numerical experiments on electrostatic benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including Landau damping, two-stream and bump-on-tail instabilities, a cyclotron mini-app and a Penning trap, confirm the theoretical findings. A single model trained on several mini-apps generated by different reference methods captures all of them and remains stable up to twice the training time window, which points towards foundation models for fields in particle-based methods.
