We show that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges admits a balanced partition $V_1,\ldots,V_k$ such that \begin{equation*} \max_{\substack{A\in\binom{[k]}{\ell}}}e_G\left(\bigcup_{i\in A}V_i\right)\le\frac{\ell^2}{k^2}m+\frac{\ell^2(k-\ell)}{k^2}(n-1)+\frac{\ell(k-\ell)}{k(k-1)}\sqrt{\left(\binom{k}{\ell}-1\right)m}. \end{equation*} In the case $\ell=2$, our result confirms a conjecture of Bollobás and Scott in a stronger form.

papers.title: Exact Traces for Vector-Valued Morrey Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish an exact trace theorem for vector-valued time-Morrey spaces and complementary continuity theorems for time-BMO evolution classes. For a Banach couple $X_1\hookrightarrow X_0$, $1<p<\infty$ and $0<λ<1$, we prove that the trace of the class $u\in\mathcal M^{p,λ}(X_1)$, $u_t\in\mathcal M^{p,λ}(X_0)$ is exactly $(X_0,X_1)_{θ,\infty}$, where $θ=1-(1-λ)/p$. A constructive extension realizes every admissible trace, and counterexamples establish optimality of both the smoothness exponent and the weak fine index. Time-BMO control yields continuous finite-index interpolation traces and, under a mixed boundedness hypothesis, a logarithmic time modulus whose base-space logarithm is necessary. For the quadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation on the torus, we characterize the bounded initial data generating Morrey-regular solutions by the exact Besov condition $u_0\in B_{2,\infty}^{2θ}$. The proof uses Hopf--Cole linearization and a direct composition argument, and requires no smallness assumption. Lacunary nonlinear solutions realize the sharp trace threshold. A forced Hamilton--Jacobi example exhibits genuinely logarithmic time regularity, and a forward--backward mean-field-game system illustrates initial and terminal trace compatibility. \par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} Morrey spaces; trace spaces; real interpolation; Hamilton--Jacobi equations; bounded mean oscillation.

papers.title: Affine reflection transforms of convex polygons with parallel opposite sides
papers.abstract: We study affine reflection transforms of convex polygons with parallel opposite sides. An opposite-side involution sends a pencil through an interior point to a piecewise smooth family of lines. Its completed envelope consists of conic arcs and transition segments. The completed transform has non-positive oriented area. Maximising the negative oriented area and dividing by the polygonal area gives an affine invariant that vanishes precisely for centrally symmetric polygons. Combining an identity for reflected chord vectors with the Rogers--Shephard inequality shows that this invariant is strictly less than $1$, with optimal universal constant $1$. The energy extends continuously to the boundary and vanishes there. We also compare chord counts under compatible smoothing and prove Hausdorff convergence to the smooth transform.

papers.title: Bounds on non-hermite Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information
papers.abstract: We obtain the relation between non-hermite skew information $NI_{ρ,α}(A)$, $NU_{ρ,α}(A)$, variance $NV_ρ(A)$ and $NJ_{ρ,α}(A)$ by using the maximal eigenvalue and the minimal eigenvalue of density $ρ$. And also we obtain their refinements.

papers.title: A Functional Central Limit Theorem for Locally Stationary Time Series in Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a functional central limit theorem for locally stationary time series in a separable Banach space $B$. The result requires no type-2 or cotype assumptions and thus covers spaces central to functional data analysis, such as $C([0,1])$ and $L^p([0,1])$. Under moment conditions, summable physical dependence coefficients and a bracketing entropy condition controlling the infinite-dimensional tails, the centered partial sum process converges weakly in $D([0,1],B)$ to a centered Gaussian process, whose covariance is the integrated local long-run covariance, an element of the projective tensor product. We also obtain a stochastic integral representation with respect to a cylindrical Brownian motion. As the limit depends on the unknown long-run covariance, we prove consistency of a block multiplier bootstrap for the partial sum process. This yields CUSUM tests for a constant mean of the full process, based on arbitrary continuous seminorms and valid under a time-varying long-run covariance. For linear projections, we derive a self-normalized test with a pivotal limit. In simulations, the supremum norm test detects localized changes that its $L^2$ counterpart largely misses, and applications to EEG and temperature data illustrate the methodology. Examples in $C([0,1])$ and $W^{1,p}_0([0,1])$ show how the entropy condition can be verified.

papers.title: Minimal Products via Weighted Spheres
papers.abstract: We establish an exact composition principle for spherical immersions coupled through coefficient profiles and norm-preserving bilinear maps. Under explicit mixed orthogonality, the spherical mean curvature vector splits into orthogonal input and profile contributions. The composition is minimal if and only if every input is minimal and the profile is $W$-minimal for the induced monomial weight. Tensor iteration allows weighted profiles to serve as inputs in further compositions. At fixed weights, Hsiang--Lawson reduction and Kapouleas--McGrath doubling yield closed embedded $W$-minimal profiles. When the effective exponents tend to infinity in positive limiting proportions, Gaussian transfer produces interior coefficient profiles from closed embedded self-shrinkers that are nondegenerate modulo rotations. The number of distinct corresponding profiles is bounded below by the Lusternik--Schnirelmann category of the rotation orbit.

papers.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
papers.abstract: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group. This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.

papers.title: The Hibi-Li Face-Number Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the face-number conjecture of Hibi and Li: for every finite poset, the order polytope has no more faces of any given dimension than the chain polytope. More generally, the face numbers increase weakly along the admissible family of chain--order polytopes when one order coordinate is replaced by a chain coordinate. We also prove that, unless the order and chain polytopes are unimodularly equivalent, all face-number inequalities in dimensions $2,\ldots,|P|-1$ are strict.

papers.title: Two-disjoint-cycle-cover edge bipancyclicity in Cartesian products
papers.abstract: For two even integers $r_1\leq r_2$, a graph $G$ of even order is \emph{2-DCC edge $[r_1,r_2]$-bipancyclic} if for every ordered pair $(e,f)$ of independent edges and every even integer $\ell\in[r_1,r_2]$, there exist two vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1$ and $C_2$ with $V(C_1)\cup V(C_2)=V(G)$, $|C_1|=\ell$, $|C_2|=|V(G)|-\ell$, $e\in E(C_1)$, and $f\in E(C_2)$. We study this property for Cartesian products $G=H_1\square\cdots\square H_d$ with $d\geq2$, where each factor is $K_2$ or an even-order bipartite edge-Hamiltonian graph. We prove that $G$ is 2-DCC edge $[4,|V(G)|/2]$-bipancyclic whenever $d\geq4$, and also for $d\in\{2,3\}$ under explicit Hamiltonian-cycle conditions on $H_i$. Here $1\leq i\leq d$. As applications, we give sharp characterizations for undirected toroidal meshes, star-cube networks, and hyperstar networks.

papers.title: Regularity of the Value Function in Multi-Asset Portfolio Selection with Proportional Transaction Costs
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the variational inequality arising from a specific singular control problem: portfolio selection under proportional transaction costs. This variational inequality is a gradient-constrained partial differential equation (PDE). Generally, the literature only guarantees the W^{2, \infty} regularity of the solution to such a PDE, and counterexamples exist for higher regularity. In this paper, by exploiting the concavity of the value function, we connect this gradient-constrained problem to an obstacle problem, and finally show that the solution is C^{2,α} except at the corner points where multiple gradient constraints bind. Especially, if there are two assets, then a global C^{2,α} solution can be guaranteed.

papers.title: Bad Reduction of Genus Two Curves with complex multiplication
papers.abstract: We study genus two curves whose Jacobians have complex multiplication by a biquadratic CM field. In this setting the Jacobian decomposes as a product of two elliptic curves with complex multiplication by orders in the same imaginary quadratic field. We derive upper bounds for the primes of stable bad reduction of such curves in terms of the discriminants of the CM orders. To do so, we give an explicit description of principally polarized abelian surfaces with CM by a biquadratic field via small CM cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety of signature (3,2). We use it to prove an arithmetic intersection formula between such CM cycles with Humbert surfaces in terms of coefficients of incoherent Eisenstein series and representation numbers of ternary positive definite quadratic forms. Finally, employing the arithmetic properties of higher Green functions, we show that primes of stable bad reduction always exist.

papers.title: Limit shape, avalanches, and stabilisation of abelian sandpiles on comb lattices
papers.abstract: We study two aspects of the abelian sandpile model on comb lattices. First, we prove that the infinite-volume limit of the stationary measures is supported on the saturated configuration. We then investigate the shape of avalanches induced by adding a particle at the origin in finite boxes of size $(2n+1)\times(2n+1)$ around the origin. In the stationary distribution on these finite boxes, we show that avalanches reach the boundary along the vertical teeth with probability tending to $1$, while the horizontal spread is of order $\sqrt{n}$. Finally, we establish that the single-source limit shape for abelian sandpiles on the comb lattice agrees with the corresponding limit shapes for the divisible sandpile, internal diffusion-limited aggregation (IDLA), and rotor-router aggregation models. This establishes limit shape universality on the comb lattice.

papers.title: A Note on a Result of Chen Li: the Thinning Problem via the Kernel Method
papers.abstract: Recently, C. Li posted a preprint that resolves the fractional version of Talagrand's discrete convexity problem. In this note, we use the method of C. Li to answer another problem of Talagrand.

papers.title: Existence and Regularity of Stable Resonant Spectral Submanifolds and Linearization Maps
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of $C^{r_{*},α}$-regular sub-stable invariant manifolds and conjugacies for analytic maps near a fixed point in the presence of resonances, assuming an invertible semisimple linearization. The regularity order $r$ and the admissible Hölder exponents $α$ depend on the resonant indices and the relative rates of contraction. Our approach uses functional expansions based on logarithmic polynomials, which allow the invariance equation to be solved explicitly and algorithmically to arbitrary order. The existence results are obtained via a fixed-point argument in a suitable Banach space. We further present several analytic examples that illustrate the theorem and demonstrate the loss of regularity caused by resonances.

papers.title: Iterative Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) distillation can propagate teacher bias under covariate shift when target reward feedback is unavailable. We propose Iterative Calibration and Learning (IterCaL), which alternates source-reward teacher calibration through token-level branching with student learning on target prompts. We prove polynomial convergence in expected average KL to the oracle student, the reference-regularized target-reward maximizer within a potentially misspecified student class; a quantified source-to-target calibration discrepancy gives an explicit additive true-return term. Our separation shows that regularized direct teacher matching retains positive oracle-KL error at its population optimum for every shared reference penalty, even when the teacher is stronger than every student. On the same instance, IterCaL converges to the oracle using source rewards alone.

papers.title: On the largest prime factors less than $y$ of consecutive shifted primes
papers.abstract: For an integer $n > 1$, let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$, and let $P_y^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$ not exceeding $y$. One of Erdős and Turán's conjectures asserts that the asymptotic density of integers $n$ satisfying $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ is $1/2$. Furthermore, Wang conjectures that for $x\rightarrow\infty$, one has $\#\{p\leq x:P^+(p-1)<P^+(p+1)\}\sim π(x)/2$. In this paper, we show the following results. For any $3\leq y\ll x^{o(1)}$, for $x\rightarrow\infty$, we have \begin{align*} &\#\{n\leq x:P^+_y(n)<P^+_y(n+1)\}\sim \frac{1}{2}x, \\&\#\{p\leq x:P^+_y(p-1)<P^+_y(p+1)\}\sim \frac{1}{2}π(x), \end{align*} where the first result extends a previous range $3\leq y\ll \exp(\log x/(100\log\log x))$ due to Rivat (2001). For any $0<α<17/32$, let $y=x^α$. Then there exists $h(α)>0$ such that \begin{align*} \#\{p\leq x:P_y^+(p-1)<P_y^+(p+1)\}\geq(h(α)+o(1))π(x). \end{align*} In particular, the function $h$ satisfies $\lim_{α\rightarrow 0^+}h(α)=1/2$. Similar result also holds for $\#\{n\leq x:P_y^+(n)<P_y^+(n+1)\}$, which improves a previous result $\lim_{α\rightarrow 0^+} h(α)=1/4$ due to Wang (2019).

papers.title: First-Derivative Chromatic Symmetric Reconstruction For Proper Trees
papers.abstract: Richard Stanley asked whether every tree $T$ is determined up to isomorphism by its chromatic symmetric function $X_T$. We approach this open problem by regarding $X_T$ as a polynomial in the power-sum symmetric functions $p_1, p_2, \dots$ and studying the invariant $Φ_T = \left.\frac{\partial {X_T}}{\partial p_1}\right\rvert_{p_1 = 0}$. We prove that $Φ_T$ distinguishes, among proper trees, every proper tree in which any non-leaf vertex with two or more non-leaf neighbors has a number of leaf neighbors occurring at no other non-leaf vertex. We give an equivalent formulation of Stanley's question in terms of $Φ_T$. Finally, we show that counts of spanning forests with at most $t$ edges cannot distinguish all $k$-vertex trees when $t<\left\lfloor k/2\right\rfloor$, for every $k\ge4$.

papers.title: Verified Linear Programming via Tolerance-Aware Precision Boosting
papers.abstract: Linear programming plays a fundamental role in computer science, with applications in optimization, formal verification, SMT solving, and numerous other domains. When exactness guarantees are required, numerical inaccuracies arising from floating-point arithmetic can compromise soundness, whereas exact rational arithmetic often incurs significant computational overhead. In this paper, we investigate the numerical stability of the simplex algorithm and establish conditions under which a precision-boosting floating-point implementation provably produces the same pivot decisions and final basis as an exact rational implementation, from which the final result is reconstructed and certified exactly. Our analysis shows that correctness depends on both arithmetic precision and a careful handling of numerical tolerances. Based on these results, we develop a tolerance-aware, precision-boosting simplex algorithm with formal correctness guarantees. Finally, we introduce a delta-complete termination criterion that allows the algorithm to terminate once certified upper and lower bounds on the optimal objective differ by at most a user-specified threshold delta, providing a certified, user-controlled optimality gap.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2$ is invertible requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $π\colon S \to R$ with $π(1) = 1$. In particular, over $\mathbb{R}$ and every finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ of odd characteristic, a quadratic field extension contains a square root of every possible doubling parameter, so the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over these fields, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over them is at most $(9n-21)2^n+28$ when $n\ge2$. When the top doubling parameter is a non-square, as in the standard real tower, the bound is $(9n-15)2^{n-1}+10$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. When $R=\mathbb{R}$ with every doubling parameter equal to $-1$, the real quasilinear schedule uses fewer total arithmetic operations than both direct multiplication and a uniform algorithm of Cariow-Cariowa for $n\ge4$. An implementation for the standard real tower is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$, for both single and batched products, and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

papers.title: Unimodality shenanigans in Ehrhart theory
papers.abstract: We construct counterexamples to a four-decade-old conjecture attributed to Stanley concerning the unimodality of $h^*$-polynomials of IDP polytopes. As additional applications of our main constructions, we also disprove a conjecture by Brenti on the log-concavity of $h^*$-polynomials of Gorenstein IDP polytopes, and a conjecture by Ferroni and Higashitani concerning the log-concavity of the Ehrhart series of IDP polytopes. We also answer their question about the existence of very ample polytopes with non-log-concave interior Ehrhart series. Our class of examples arises by taking Cayley sums of rectangular prisms, and hence they possess regular unimodular flag triangulations by a result of Haase, Paffenholz, Piechnik and Santos. Remarkably, for the unimodality conjecture we can even find smooth counterexamples.

papers.title: Links and singularities of stable maps from $3$-manifolds to surfaces
papers.abstract: For any two links in the $3$-sphere, we provide a visual construction of a stable map $f$ from the $3$-sphere to the Euclidean plane such that $f$ has no cusp points, the set of definite (resp. indefinite) fold points of $f$ is isotopic to the first (resp. second) given link, and $f$ does not have a certain type of singular fibers. Moreover, we obtain a similar result for any $3$-manifold by setting the target space to the $2$-sphere.

papers.title: The derived length of subgroups of the Cremona group
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal derived length of a solvable subgroup of the plane Cremona group over $\mathbb C$ is equal to $5$. The main difficulty is the case of subgroups containing loxodromic elements. To treat this case, we prove that the maximal derived length of a finite solvable subgroup is $4$ and establish a centraliser theorem: the centraliser of a finite solvable subgroup of derived length $4$ contains no loxodromic element. The proof of the centraliser theorem relies on Blanc's classification of maximal algebraic subgroups and then uses equivariant Sarkisov theory, orbit estimates, superrigidity, and fixed curves of genus at least two.

papers.title: On a Brunn-Minkowski principle for first-order information functionals
papers.abstract: In this work we present the following general principle: every positive homogeneous functional on an abstract convex cone satisfying a suitable Brunn-Minkowski inequality gives rise to an information functional -defined as the quotient of the functional by its relative surface area- that satisfies a linear Brunn-Minkowski inequality. We also establish the dual counterpart of this principle for functionals satisfying an analogous convexity property, yielding reverse linear Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for the associated information functionals. Furthermore, we show that homogeneity is necessary within this principle by providing a counterexample to the expected result for the information functional associated to the standard Gaussian measure. As applications, we recover, via an alternative first-order argument, a classical result by Giannopoulos, Hartzoulaki and Paouris (2002) for the ratio of two consecutive quermassintegrals, together with a characterization of the equality case. The same argument extends to the setting of mixed discriminants of symmetric positive definite matrices. Finally, our approach yields new extensions of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Dembo, Cover and Thomas, for the classical information functional, both to the $L_p$ setting ($p \geq 1$), where the relative surface area is expressed in terms of Lutwak's first $L_p$ quermassintegral, and to the measure-theoretic framework, for measures with homogeneous densities satisfying some concavity. Moreover, we prove that our principle applies also in the context of the Blaschke addition, both in the volume and in the (mixed) affine surface area cases, obtaining new inequalities as an application of it.

papers.title: On the real-rootedness of Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of $(132,213)$-avoiding permutahedra
papers.abstract: Let $P_d$ be the convex hull of the permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ that avoid the patterns $132$ and $213$, and let $H_d(t)$ be its Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial. We prove that all zeros of $H_d(t)$ are real and negative for $3\le d\le1000$ and for every $d\ge2^{62}$; for $d\le2$ the polynomial is constant. Expanding $H_d(t)$ in refined Eulerian polynomials does not suffice, since a coordinate is already negative at $d=7$. Let $A_{d,i}(t)$ enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with first entry $i$ by number of descents. For $c\ge0$, we prove that every nonnegative linear combination of $A_{d,1},\ldots,A_{d,d}$ and the adjacent differences $A_{d,r+1}-cA_{d,r}$, $2\le r\le d-2$, is real-rooted for all $d\ge4$ simultaneously if and only if $c\le2-\sqrt3$. This reduces real-rootedness to the positivity of explicit weighted tails of the coordinates. An exact certificate checks these inequalities for $d\le1000$, and coefficient estimates based on Darroch's theorem on the mode of a sum of Bernoulli variables prove them for $d\ge2^{62}$; the range $1001\le d<2^{62}$ remains open. Along the way we identify $P_d$, up to lattice equivalence, with twice a chain-poset permutahedron and with the Newton polytope of a discriminant, which transfers the known cube structure and volume of these models to $P_d$. We also show that the coefficient of $t^{d-1}$ in $H_d(t)$ counts strong tournament score sequences for $d\ge3$, confirming a conjecture of Rehberg in this range.

papers.title: Transformation of Adaptive Multistage Sampling for Solving Finite-Horizon Markov Decision Processes with Unknown Model
papers.abstract: This work provides a learning approach to solving finite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs) when the underlying model of a given finite MDP is unknown to the decision maker. We transform the adaptive multistage sampling (AMS) algorithm into a sampling-free algorithm, called "adaptive multistage rollout (AMR)," for estimating the optimal value at an initial state when only the state set and the action set are known. AMR emulates the backward induction as in AMS but in a reinforcement learning (RL) setting. At each iteration, AMR generates a non-stationary policy to be used for exploration and rolls out the policy in order to obtain a single trajectory of experiences and traces it backwards in a non-recursive way while doing relevant updates only at visited states and for actions taken at the visited states. We show that AMR is asymptotically optimal such that the sequence of the expected absolute errors approaches zero and its convergence rate depends on the number of visits to each reachable state at each stage from the initial state, essentially transforming the result of AMS into the RL setting.

papers.title: A class of port-Hamiltonian systems with general time delays
papers.abstract: We define a class of infinite dimensional linear port-Hamiltonian delay systems, give a characterization for such systems, and provide an easily verifiable sufficient condition to belong to this class, thereby extending the study by Breiten, Hinsen and Unger in [IEEE Trans. Autom. Control vol. 69, no. 12 (2024), pp. 8924-8930, doi: 10.1109/TAC.2024.3464332]. The results rely on the operator semigroup theoretic treatment of linear delay PDEs.

papers.title: On Decay of the Local Mean Oscillations of the Vorticity Direction in Critical Navier-Stokes Flows
papers.abstract: We isolate and analyze the geometric PDE governing the evolution of the vorticity direction in the 3D incompressible (unforced) Navier-Stokes equations (NSE), restricted to the case of a critical spatial point singularity where the vorticity magnitude concentrates as $O(|x|^{-2})$, inhabiting the critical Lorentz space $L^{3/2, \infty}$. The PDE consists of the Harmonic Map Heat Flow (HMHF) into the sphere supplemented with the fluid transport, cross-diffusion and tangential strain. The question is whether the NSE mechanics can propagate logarithmic decay of the local mean oscillations of the direction -- the condition $ξ\in \mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ -- which (in this setting) was shown in the companion paper to prevent finite time blow-up. A key observation is that the $O(|x|^{-2})$ concentration, factored out of the viscous cross-diffusion, generates an outward radial drift $4ν\, x/|x|^2$ at the core. Under a suitable condition we prove a barrier lemma for the total drift-diffusion operator and show that the HMHF nonlinearity is harmless for the quantity $\frac12|ξ- e|^2$ which is a subsolution on any hemisphere. This yields a transfer theorem: the $\mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ regularity of the direction at the core, uniformly up to the singular time, is controlled by a logarithmic modulus in time of the direction at the inner scale, together with the physical strain. Crucially, the strain enters the direction equation only through its tangential component which vanishes precisely when the direction is an eigenvector of the strain tensor. Since this includes the eigenvector carrying the maximal stretching, the result is in contrast to the classical geometric regularity theory which is built on depleting the full vortex-stretching term and thus confined to configurations of weak stretching.

papers.title: A GPU-Accelerated Blocked Adaptive Randomized Range Finder Based on an Implicit Householder QR Decomposition
papers.abstract: Low-rank methods can reduce the memory and computational requirements of deep neural network training in approaches such as GaLore. Randomized range finders offer an attractive alternative to singular value decompositions, particularly when the required rank is determined adaptively from a prescribed approximation tolerance. We introduce a blocked adaptive randomized range finder based on a Householder QR decomposition and an optimized hybrid CPU--GPU implementation. Numerical experiments show that it preserves orthogonality and approximation accuracy in regimes where block Gram--Schmidt without reorthogonalization becomes unstable. The blocked formulation exposes matrix--matrix operations and enables overlap of CPU panel factorization with GPU updates. On an NVIDIA GH200, the overlapped implementation reduces the runtime for the largest tested matrix from 9.91 s on the CPU to 0.407 s. The method provides a stable and efficient building block for low-rank approximation on heterogeneous systems with applications in computational science and engineering.

papers.title: Generalized Fermat equation over number fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $A,B,C\in\mathcal{O}_K\setminus\{0\}$. Put $S_K=\{\mathfrak{P}:\mathfrak{P}\mid2\}$ and $S_K'=\{\mathfrak{q}:\mathfrak{q}\mid2ABC\}$. We establish two criteria for the non-existence of non-trivial solutions of $Ax^p+By^p=Cz^p$ over $K$ for sufficiently large prime exponents $p$. Both criteria use a valuation bound on the $S_K'$-unit equation at a fixed $\mathfrak{P}\in S_K$. The first excludes all non-trivial solutions in $K^3$ when $v_{\mathfrak{P}}(A)=v_{\mathfrak{P}}(B)=m$ and $v_{\mathfrak{P}}(C)=m+k$, with $k>4v_{\mathfrak{P}}(2)$. The second, under an explicit nonvanishing condition on the coefficient valuations, excludes solutions $(a,b,c)\in(K^\times)^3$ whose $\mathfrak{P}$-valuations are not all equal. In particular, it excludes non-trivial primitive integral solutions with $\mathfrak{P}\mid abc$. Neither criterion restricts the residue degree of $\mathfrak{P}$. Both criteria hold unconditionally over every totally real field; over general number fields, we assume residual modularity and Eichler--Shimura-type conjectures. The first criterion covers a new coefficient range. In particular, under the corresponding $S_K$-unit bound, $x^p+y^p=2^rz^p$ has no non-trivial solutions in $K^3$ for each fixed $r\geq5$ and sufficiently large prime $p$. This bound holds for a set of real quadratic fields of relative density $1$. For a family of imaginary quadratic fields of relative density $5/6$, we explicitly determine the $S_K$-unit solutions and verify the valuation bound for both criteria when $A,B,C\in\{\pm2^r:r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}\}$, including the same $r\geq5$ conclusion.

papers.title: An approximate zero bias transformation for random sums: Applications to sampling with outliers, auto insurance, and generative AI
papers.abstract: We develop $L^1$ bounds for the difference between a test function of a random sum and a standard normal random variable, where the summands are assumed to be independent but not necessarily identically distributed. The bounds are obtained through a new version of the approximate zero bias transformation specifically developed for random sums. Although the identical distribution assumption is relaxed, the bounds are of order $1/\sqrt{n}$, matching the order of existing bounds in the literature under the same distributional assumption on the number of summands. The main results are then applied to three real-world settings: random sums obtained from simple random sampling with outliers, total insurance claims, and generative AI response times.

papers.title: Two-point correlations of multiplicative functions with dense orbits
papers.abstract: Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{T}$ be completely multiplicative functions with dense images in the complex unit circle $\mathbb{T}$. We prove that, for every non-empty open set $U \subset \mathbb{T}^2$, the set of integers $n$ such that $(f(n),g(n+1)) \in U$ has positive upper logarithmic density, unless the pair $(f,g)$ is of a special form. This result strengthens earlier theorems of Klurman and Mangerel, as well as of Charamaras, Mountakis, and Tsinas, and yields simpler proofs.

papers.title: The Multivariable Strong Monodromy Conjecture for Plane Curves
papers.abstract: We prove the multivariable Strong Monodromy Conjecture for the local topological zeta function of arbitrary tuples of nonzero nonunit plane curve germs. The entries may be nonreduced and may have common irreducible factors. We also prove that the non-equivariant local motivic and topological zeta functions have the same polar locus and generic pole orders, using a multivariable extension of the Nicaise--Xu definition of motivic pole order. Our arguments combine twisted Poincaré residues with resolution formulas and specialization to one variable. In arbitrary dimension, we prove that a nonzero iterated residue class on a stratum of a log resolution implies the vanishing of the Bernstein--Sato ideal at the corresponding parameter. In particular, every topological polar hyperplane whose order equals the ambient dimension is contained in this zero locus. For algebraic germs, the topological pole order is at most the motivic pole order, and the two attain maximal order simultaneously.

papers.title: Three omitted values and non-Blaschke point divisors in half-planes
papers.abstract: We construct a real meromorphic function $F$ on $\mathbb C$ such that $F^{-1}(\{0,1,\infty\})\subset\mathbb R$, while $F$ is not of bounded type in either half-plane. More strongly, for every $a\in\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, the $a$-point divisor in either half-plane fails the Blaschke condition. Thus the construction gives a negative answer to the half-plane bounded-type question arising from Nevanlinna's 1925 work. Postcomposition gives the analogous counterexample for any prescribed triple of distinct values in the Riemann sphere. The core construction and proof were generated during an autonomous run of GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.

papers.title: Degeneracies of Lagrange functions and geometric interpretations of Lagrange multipliers
papers.abstract: We introduce Lagrange functions associated with height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves. We show that degeneracies of these functions characterize geometric properties of the curves, such as inflections and vertices, and give geometric interpretations of the corresponding Lagrange multipliers in terms of contact with lines and circles.

papers.title: Activation-Keyed Momentum: An Anisotropic Momentum Update via the Delta Rule
papers.abstract: Most modern optimizers form their momentum as an exponential moving average (EMA) of past gradients, forgetting every direction at one fixed rate. However, the inputs a deep network sees during training can be highly anisotropic, with a few directions queried frequently while most are seen rarely. Preconditioning methods address this anisotropy by wrapping extra processing around this buffer and leave the momentum update itself unchanged. We propose Activation-Keyed Momentum (AK-Momentum), which builds direction-awareness into the momentum update rule. The gradient of a linear layer splits into an input activation that acts as a $\textit{key}$ and an output-side error that acts as a $\textit{value}$. Keying on that activation, AK-Momentum updates the momentum buffer by the canonical delta rule, so each direction is forgotten at a rate set by how often it appears. We prove that it is a valid momentum, that it applies the input-side curvature correction without matrix inversion, and that it clears stale directions faster than EMA under both a fixed and a drifting optimum. It is a drop-in replacement for the momentum buffer of any optimizer, its coefficient transfers across widths under $μ$P, and its extra compute stays between $22.2\%$ and $25.0\%$ of a gated-MLP block's linear cost with no persistent memory. In FineWeb-Edu pretraining, AdamW with AK-Momentum (AK-AdamW) reaches AdamW's validation loss in up to $46.64 \pm 4.52\%$ fewer steps at 67M and $22.14 \pm 0.81\%$ at 370M over three seeds, and the gain persists at 1B on a Chinchilla-optimal budget. A Muon baseline tuned under the same protocol sits above AK-AdamW at both language-model scales, and the gain holds for SGD, ResNet-18, and ViT-Tiny on CIFAR-10. Training-time diagnostics confirm the predicted mechanism, better gradient tracking and healthier input directions. Code is available at https://github.com/euijinh/AK-Momentum.

papers.title: The minimum of the graph likelihood
papers.abstract: The likelihood of a finite simple undirected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is the probability that the uniform sequential attachment process, which at each step joins a new vertex to a uniformly random subset of uniformly random size of the vertices already present, outputs a graph isomorphic to $G$. Dervovic, Mocherla and Severini conjectured that the likelihood is minimised by the balanced complete bipartite graph. We prove that, among complete bipartite graphs of a given order, the balanced one uniquely minimises the likelihood. Exact computation shows that it also minimises over all graphs for every order from $6$ through $14$. At $n=15$, the exact global minimisers are $C_5[\bar K_3]$ and its complement, giving the first counterexample. Completed exact searches show that the global minimisers at order $16$ are $K_{8,8}$ and its complement. At order $17$, the unique minimiser is a self-complementary mixed blow-up of $C_5$. At order $18$, the minimisers are $K_{9,9}$ and its complement. We show that the failure is not sporadic by proving that the likelihood of the balanced complete bipartite graph is $2^{-(1/2-1/(8\ln 2)+o(1))n^2}$, whereas the minimum over all graphs of order $n$ is $2^{-(1/2+o(1))n^2}$, so the conjectured minimiser exceeds the minimum by a factor exponential in $n^2$. We also determine the Shannon entropy of the process to leading order, namely $n^2/(4\ln 2)$ bits, which shows that the conjectured minimiser is in fact more likely than a typical output of the process. The proofs rest on a vertex deletion recurrence which evaluates the likelihood in time $O(2^n n)$ and which closes on the blow-ups of any fixed base graph.

papers.title: A Sharp Joint Bias-Energy Envelope for Radial Clipping
papers.abstract: Radial clipping does two things at once: it cuts off the part of a vector outside a ball and leaves a bounded vector inside the ball. The part cut off defines the residual. For a random vector, we study the magnitude of the bias in the mean and the energy, defined as the centered second moment of the clipped vector. Controlling these effects is important in stochastic optimization with heavy tails, where the choice of the clipping threshold affects convergence bounds for algorithms. In the deterministic problem, for a fixed threshold $τ>0$, $1\le p\le2$, and nonnegative coefficients $α,β$, we find the smallest constant that simultaneously bounds the residual and energy in terms of $\lVert x\rVert^p$. This same constant remains sharp in the stochastic counterpart for random vectors in a Hilbert space. We also find the exact supremum of the corresponding linear combination of normalized bias and energy for arbitrary $α,β\in\mathbb R$. We then give a geometric picture in the energy-bias plane. Varying the weights, we describe the smallest closed convex region containing all normalized pairs and the attainable set itself, identifying unattainable boundary values. Every attainable pair at a fixed threshold can be realized by a real-valued random variable taking at most two values. We also consider all thresholds simultaneously. For any integrable random vector in a Hilbert space, we construct a single $\mathbb R^3$-valued random vector preserving its norm distribution, bias magnitude, and energy simultaneously at every threshold $τ>0$. Finally, we apply the joint bound to risk-adjusted reinsurance costs for a prescribed retention threshold and to the logarithmic shortfall of a clipped portfolio strategy relative to any constant-fraction strategy. AI was used in preparing this paper (see Section 8).

papers.title: Gradient Hölder regularity for singular fractional $p$-Laplace equations
papers.abstract: We prove interior $C^{1,α}$ regularity for globally bounded weak solutions to the fractional $p$-Laplace equation $(-Δ_p)^s u=0$ under the assumptions $n\ge2$, $1<p<2$, $0<s<1$, and $sp>p-1$, where $α=α(n,p,s)>0$. This resolves the open problem of gradient Hölder continuity for globally bounded solutions in the singular range $sp>p-1$. The proof is based on affine approximation and estimates independent of the normalized affine slope. When these slopes tend to infinity, we prove convergence to a solution of a linear nonlocal equation of order $sp-p+2$, together with convergence of the normalized energies to the corresponding quadratic energy. The regularity of the limiting equation yields an improved affine approximation. For bounded slopes, we prove that every globally Lipschitz weak solution of $(-Δ_p)^s u=0$ in $\mathbb R^n$ is affine and use this result in a compactness argument. The two estimates are combined in an iteration that preserves the required energy and tail bounds and gives Hölder continuity of the gradient.

papers.title: Equilateral Completion in Floretion Triangular Coordinates: Locality, Product Points, and Reflection Symmetry
papers.abstract: We study nondegenerate equilateral triangles whose vertices are centroids of the $4^n$ order-$n$ floretion tiles. Scaled integer triangular coordinates give exact equilateral completions and, by an obstruction modulo $3$, show that all three vertices have the same tile orientation. In particular, the complete triangle family and its synchronized local cyclic subfamily have respective sizes $|E_n|=\frac{4^n(4^n-1)}{12},\quad |L_n|=\frac{7^n-4^n}{3},$ so the local proportion tends to zero. Our principal new result answers the radial-homogeneity question left open in the preceding revision: for every order, the number of triangles containing a given tile is given by an exact affine formula in its squared scaled centroid radius. Although the two tile orientations have different formulas, their attainable squared radii belong to disjoint residue classes modulo $3$, yielding a single radial-incidence law on the full centroid set. We also determine local and nonlocal vertex incidences and obtain circular-shell and squared-radius moment identities. The unsigned vertex product defines an algebraic product point. By a rigidity theorem of Ma and Zhang, the multiplication-generated triangles are precisely the nontrivial global cyclic orbits; combining this with our geometric shell classification, we show that the product point is the origin exactly when the Euclidean triangle center is the origin. Further results enumerate central-vertex, no-$e$, and main-axis families, derive Fibonacci and finite-state recurrences for product-centered and reflection-restricted classes, and characterize pairwise anticommutation.

papers.title: Generalized Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence and Weil-Petersson current
papers.abstract: In this paper we extend Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence along holomorphic fibre space and we show that there exists a generalized Hermitian-Einstein metric which is twisted with Weil-Petersson current.In fact we generalise Song-Tian program for vector bundles

papers.title: Generic Spectral Determination of Semiclassical Schrödinger Operators with $\mathbb Z_2$-Symmetry
papers.abstract: Consider the two-dimensional semiclassical Schrödinger operator $P_\hbar=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2}Δ+V$ on $\mathbb R^2$, where $V$ has a nondegenerate well at the origin, its harmonic frequencies are rationally independent, and $V$ is $\mathbb Z_2$-symmetric. We prove that, generically, the first three layers of the quantum Birkhoff normal form (QBNF) determine the full Taylor series of $V$ at the origin, up to the unavoidable spatial inversion $V(x)\mapsto V(-x)$. The generic condition depends only on the jet of $V$ through order ten. Consequently, for real analytic potentials with a unique isolated global well at the origin, the low-lying semiclassical spectrum generically determines $V$ up to spatial inversion.

papers.title: Eventual polynomiality and dualities of relative Ehrhart functions
papers.abstract: Classical Ehrhart theory measures the discrete capacity of a convex rational (or integral) polytope $P$ by counting the number of lattice points in the $t$-th dilate $tP$ of $P$. In this paper, we extend this paradigm by replacing a lattice point with a geometric object $Q$ of dimension at most $\dim P$. We show that the counting function $\mathrm{ehr}(P,Q;t)$ of such valid translations of $Q$ into $tP$ inherits eventual quasi-polynomiality (or eventual polynomiality) with leading term $\mathrm{vol}(P)t^d$, where $d = \dim P$. This result is naturally derived by induction on the dimension, based on the classical quasi-polynomiality (or polynomiality) of Ehrhart functions. Similarly, replacing $P$ with its relative interior $P^\circ$ defines $\mathrm{ehr}^\circ(P,Q;t)$, which is also shown to be an eventual quasi-polynomial (or eventual polynomial). Furthermore, we prove several formulas for relative Ehrhart functions under the condition that $P = kP_0$ and $Q = lQ_0$ for some integers $k$, $l > 0$, and polytopes $P_0$ and $Q_0$ with $\dim Q_0 > 0$ such that $Q_0$ is inscribed in $P_0$. In particular, we prove that under this condition, $\mathrm{ehr}(P,Q;-t) = (-1)^{d}\mathrm{ehr}^\circ (P,Q;t+ρ)$ $(t \gg 0)$ holds for some integer $ρ> 0$ if and only if $k \mid 2l$ via the classical Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity law. We also prove that under the same condition, $\mathrm{ehr}(P,Q;t) = \mathrm{ehr}^\circ (P,Q;t+σ)$ $(t \gg 0)$ holds for some integer $σ> 0$ if and only if $\mathrm{ehr}^\circ (P_0;\mathrm{codeg}\,P_0) = 1$ and $k \mid \mathrm{codeg}\,P_0$.

papers.title: A simple acylindrical recipe for non-split characteristic $2$ sharply $k$-transitive actions and their generalizations
papers.abstract: We provide a fairly simple list of conditions on a group $G$ acting acylindrically on a $δ$-hyperbolic metric space sufficient for the group to admit an action on a set that is $k$-sharp, transitive on $k$-sets and has the property that for any $k$-set $A$ the setwise stabilizer of $A$ acts on $A$ as prescribed by some fixed subgroup of the group of permutations of $k$ elements. In particular, this yields a large class of non-split sharply $2$ and $3$-transitive actions containing many finitely presented groups, and allows us to characterize sharp $2$-transitivity within the class of hyperbolic groups that do not contain a copy of $C_{2}\times C_{2}$.

papers.title: Caged subsequences in permutations
papers.abstract: Given a sequence $\mathfrak{a}:=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ of reals, a subsequence $\mathfrak{b}=(a_{i_1},\ldots,a_{i_k})$ is said to be "caged" if the largest and smallest among the members of $\mathfrak{b}$ are $a_{i_1}$ and $a_{i_k}$, though not necessarily in that order. In this paper, we consider the problem of maximal caged sequences in permutations $π\in S_n$. We also consider the same problem for a random permutation, both when the permutation is chosen uniformly at random and also when it is picked uniformly at random from among the permutations of rectangular shape, via the RSK correspondence. We also give a $O(n\log n)$ time algorithm to obtain these maximal caged sequences. In addition, we propose a randomized linear time algorithm that gives the length of the maximal caged sequence up to the factor of $(1-o(1))$.

papers.title: Essential $p$-dimension and Chern numbers
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth, projective, connected variety over a field $k$ containing a root of unity of order $p$. If $X$ has a Chern number prime to $p$, we show that every finite $p$-group acting on $X$ acts through a subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_n(k)$, where $n=\dim X$. This allows one to transfer properties of representations of finite $p$-groups to their actions on $X$. We deduce a fixed-point theorem which, unlike earlier results of this kind, is sensitive to the arithmetic of the base field, and whose dimensional bound is sharp for each individual group (apart from one low-dimensional case when $p=2$). We also obtain restrictions on finite $p$-groups of birational automorphisms of rationally connected varieties; for instance the Cremona group $\operatorname{Cr}_n(\mathbb{Q})$ contains no element of order $p^2$ when $p \ge n+2$. More generally, we prove variants of these results in the presence of a Chern number not divisible by a given power of $p$. The method is based on the following observation about the essential $p$-dimension $\operatorname{ed}_p(G)$ of an affine algebraic group $G$: over a field of characteristic zero, the number $\operatorname{ed}_p(G) + \dim G$ is the least dimension of a smooth projective variety $Y$ with a generically free $G$-action such that the degree map $\operatorname{CH}_G(Y) \to \mathbb{F}_p$ from the equivariant Chow group is nonzero. The Chern numbers modulo $p$ of $Y$ lie in the image of this map; combined with Karpenko and Merkurjev's computation of the essential $p$-dimension of finite $p$-groups, this yields our results.

papers.title: Infinite and finite series involving central binomial coefficients and closed forms of generalized hypergeometric functions
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{Z}^-=\{-1,-2,\dotsc\}$ and $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,\dotsc\}$. In 2023, Qi and Lim gave two claims for summing the infinite series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\binom{2k}{k}\frac{1}{α+k}\bigl(\frac{\pm1}{4}\bigr)^k$ for $α\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{Z}^-$. In this paper, we confirm these claims by expressing the infinite series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\binom{2k}{k}\frac{1}{α+k}\bigl(\frac{z}{4}\bigr)^k$ and the finite series $\sum_{k=1}^{n}\binom{2k}{k}\frac{1}{α+k}\bigl(\frac{z}{4}\bigr)^k$ in terms of the Gauss hypergeometric function ${}_2F_1\bigl[\tfrac12,α;1+α;z\bigr]$ and a generalized hypergeometric function ${}_3F_2$, for $|z|\le1$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Using the Euler integral representation, we derive closed forms, in terms of finite sums of sines and cosines of $\arcsin\sqrt{z}\,$, for ${}_2F_1\bigl[\tfrac12,\tfrac12+n;\tfrac32+n;z\bigr]$, ${}_2F_1\bigl[\tfrac12,1+n;2+n;z\bigr]$, two related ${}_3F_2$ functions, and the incomplete beta functions $B_z\bigl(\frac12+n,\frac12\bigr)$ and $B_z\bigl(1+n,\frac12\bigr)$. By the Pfaff transformation, we obtain closed forms of several further Gauss hypergeometric functions with parameters shifted by $n$. We also give a closed form of $\bigl[(1-z)\frac{\operatorname{d}}{\operatorname{d}z}(1-z)\bigr]^n\frac{\arcsin\sqrt{z}\,}{\sqrt{z(1-z)}\,}$ and a combinatorial identity.

papers.title: Hyperstructures as complete atomic Boolean algebras
papers.abstract: We show that several categories of hyperstructures, including the mosaics of Nakamura and Reyes and the hypergroups of Marty, are realizable as categories of objects with extra structure within the category of complete atomic Boolean algebras (CABAs) and atom-preserving morphisms.

papers.title: Arithmetic Landscape Functions of a Discrete Cat Map
papers.abstract: For a permutation of a finite set, we define a landscape by summing a discounted weight over the times each point returns to itself. The landscape value is determined by the point's least period. We relate the trace of the associated resolvent to fixed-point and exact-period counts, and show that the associated determinant is the reciprocal of the Artin-Mazur dynamical zeta function. We apply this framework to the discrete cat map modulo $N$. For every prime $p\ne5$, all nonzero points have period equal to the order of the cat-map matrix modulo $p$, yielding explicit formulas for the landscape trace and determinant. We prove a period-lifting formula at odd primes $p\ne5$, derive exact fixed-point and period counts modulo $5^a$, and combine prime-power results for composite moduli using the Chinese remainder theorem.

papers.title: A cube complex for virtual Artin groups
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a Coxeter graph, and let $S$ be its vertex set. An elemental complex over $Γ$ is an abstract simplicial complex $\mathcal D$ on $S$ that contains every pair $\{s, t\}$ with $s \neq t$ and $m_{s,t} \neq \infty$. To each elemental complex $\mathcal D$, we associate a cube complex $Ξ_{\mathcal D}$ on which the virtual Artin group ${\rm VA} [Γ]$ acts. We prove that $Ξ_{\mathcal D}$ is connected, simply connected, and locally regular; that the action of ${\rm VA}[Γ]$ on $Ξ_{\mathcal D}$ is regular, cocompact, and by isometries; and that the stabilizers of cells are parabolic subgroups. We finally prove that $Ξ_{\mathcal D}$ is CAT(0) if and only if ${\mathcal D}$ is a flag complex.

papers.title: Blow up and Concentration without Quantization: sharp Harnack type inequalities
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Onsager statistical mechanics description of turbulent Euler flows with point singularities, we refine the blow up analysis for sequences of solutions of a class of perturbed singular Liouville equations which share the phenomenon of ``blow up and concentration without quantization". The problem is delicate because we are dealing with the exact threshold value above which one meets the well known ``concentration without quantization" phenomenon, as recently pushed forward in [C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris} (2016)] and in [Y. Lee, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, W. Yang, {\em Comm. PDE.} (2017)]. We overcome these difficulties by developing different strategies for ``fast" and ``slow" blow up, combining refined Pohozaev identities, elliptic estimates and ``Sup+CInf" inequalities in the same spirit of [C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, {\em Comm. An. Geom.} (1998)]. In the process, we also derive a new sharp Harnack type inequality by using a moving-plane method, following the ideas in [D. Bartolucci, C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em Comm. P.D.E.} (2002)].

papers.title: Explicit and logarithmically improved chromatic bounds for $(P_2\cup P_3)$-free graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every $(P_2\cup P_3)$-free graph $G$, with $k=ω(G)$, satisfies \[ χ(G)=O\!\left(k^3\frac{\ln\ln k}{\ln k}\right). \] Thus the class admits an $o(k^3)$ binding function. We also prove the explicit bound \[ χ(G)\le \frac{k^3}{8}+\frac{5k^2}{4}-4k+8 \qquad(k\ge8), \] with a sharper formula for odd $k$. A further refinement gives an explicit cubic bound with leading coefficient $104/837<1/8$.

papers.title: Derived Azumaya Algebras on Compact Derived Smooth Manifolds
papers.abstract: We extend Toën's derived Brauer theory to the open site of Spivak's derived smooth manifolds. For a compact derived smooth manifold $X$, we define a spectralized structure sheaf $\mathbb{O}_{X}$ and prove that every Picard twist can be represented by a derived Azumaya algebra, whose Morita equivalence class is uniquely determined by the twist. In the open locally Morita trivial setting, this gives a natural bijection \begin{align*} Φ_{X}:\mathbf{dBr}^{\mathrm{open}}(X) \xrightarrow{\cong} H^{1}(|X|;\underline{\mathbb {Z}}) \times π_0Γ(|X|,\mathrm B^2GL_1(\mathbb O_X)). \end{align*} If we consider $C^\infty_X(\mathbb C)$ on ordinary smooth manifolds, the second factor is $H^3(|X|;\underline{\mathbb Z})$, which recovers the Dixmier-Douady invariant. If we consider $C^\infty_X(\mathbb R)$, the second factor is $H^2(|X|;\underline{\mathbb Z/2})$, which recovers the corresponding invariant of Donovan and Karoubi.

papers.title: Characterization of the boundedness of the segment multiplier on rearrangement-invariant spaces
papers.abstract: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.

papers.title: The mean-field limit of non-exchangeable particle systems with non-conservative dynamics and adaptive weights
papers.abstract: In the paper we introduce vector-valued dynamic extended graphons in order to obtain the mean-filed limit for certain class of problems with adaptive weights. We impose fairly general assumptions on the matrix of initial connections, which allows us to cover the case of sparse graphs.

papers.title: A note on application of mean-field limit to non-exchangeable non-conservative systems
papers.abstract: In this paper we apply the newly developed theory of extended graphons to a certain class of non-exchangeable, non-conservative problems. We establish the mean-field limit by proving the convergence of the associated generalized weighted empirical measures.

papers.title: Riemannian Deep Learning: Modules, Networks, and Geometries
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks on manifold-valued representations have attracted growing interest, but many basic components remain tied to specific manifolds, rely on Euclidean approximations, or require costly and numerically fragile geometric operations. This thesis develops a unified framework for Riemannian deep learning from three complementary perspectives: reusable neural modules, manifold-specific network architectures, and the design of underlying geometries. It generalizes batch normalization from Euclidean spaces and individual manifolds to broad classes of Lie groups and gyrogroups, and extends multinomial logistic regression from Euclidean space to SPD manifolds and then to general Riemannian manifolds. It further develops neural networks for several important geometric representations, including an unconstrained model of hyperbolic space, Busemann-based hyperbolic learning, and full-rank correlation matrices. Finally, it introduces adaptive and computationally efficient Riemannian metrics on SPD manifolds, including learnable Log-Euclidean geometries and fast, stable Cholesky-based geometries. The proposed methods are supported by theoretical analysis and validated through numerical experiments and applications in vision, signal processing, graph learning, and genomics.

papers.title: Archimedean Modular Symbols for Rankin-Selberg Convolutions of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$
papers.abstract: We explicit calculate the archimedean modular symbol for Rankin-Selberg convolutions of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$, for all generic cohomological representations.

papers.title: On two counterexamples in the geometry of numbers
papers.abstract: We give counterexamples to two optimization problems in dimensions eight and nine. 1. The Cartesian-product problem posed by Cassels for critical determinants and later formulated by Zong for lattice packings and for packings allowing translations but not rotations: whether the corresponding product inequalities are always equalities. The counterexample also disproves the natural product formula for unrestricted congruent packings. 2. A question raised by Sarnak and formulated as a conjecture in Chiu: whether, among unit-volume flat tori, height is minimized by a lattice maximizing the length of its shortest nonzero vector.

papers.title: Combinatorial identities derived from explicit formulas of Gauss hypergeometric functions
papers.abstract: In the present paper, with the help of the Faà di Bruno formula and several identities of partial Bell polynomials, the author establishes explicit formulas of the Gauss hypergeometric functions \begin{gather*} {\,}_2F_1\biggl(\frac{1-n}{2},\frac{2-n}{2};\frac{3}{2}-m;z^2\biggr), \quad {\,}_2F_1\biggl(-\frac{n}{2},\frac{1-n}{2};\frac{1}{2}-m;z^2\biggr),\\ {\,}_2F_1\biggl(a,a+\frac{1}{2};\frac{3}{2}-m;z^2\biggr), \quad {\,}_2F_1\biggl(a,a+\frac{1}{2};\frac{1}{2}-m;z^2\biggr) \end{gather*} for $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $a\in\mathbb{C}$, and then derives two combinatorial identities \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=0}^{m}\frac{2^k}{k!} \binom{2m-2k}{m-k} \sum_{\ell=0}^{k} \frac{(-1)^\ell}{2^\ell} \frac{(2k-2\ell-1)!!}{(n-\ell)!} \binom{2k-\ell-1}{\ell-1} =\frac{1}{n!}\binom{2m-n}{m} \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=1}^{m}\frac{1}{(k!)^2}\binom{2m-2k}{m-k} \sum_{\ell=1}^{k} \binom{k}{\ell}\ell(2k-\ell-1)! (2a)_\ell =\binom{2m+2a}{m}-\binom{2m}{m}, \end{equation*} where $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $a\in\mathbb{C}$. These newly-established identities extend and generalize the beautiful combinatorial identity \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{2^{k}}{k!}\binom{2n-2k}{n-k} \sum_{j=0}^{k}\frac{(-1)^{j}}{2^j} \frac{(2k-2j-1)!!}{(n-j)!} \binom{2k-j-1}{j-1} =\frac{1}{n!}, \quad n\in\mathbb{N}_0, \end{equation*} which was obtained in Theorem 4 of the paper "F. Qi, C.-Y. He, and D. Lim, Explicit formulas of two Gauss hypergeometric functions and several combinatorial identities, Discrete Appl. Math. Vol. 393 (2026), 215--229. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dam.2026.06.023."

papers.title: Diffeological Riemannian orbifolds
papers.abstract: We show that the data of a Riemannian metric on a differentiable stack presented by an orbifold groupoid is equivalent to the data of a Riemannian metric on its diffeological orbit space. As a consequence, we conclude that the classical notion of Riemannian orbifold is equivalent to that of a Riemannian diffeological orbifold. We use the framework for Riemannian diffeology introduced by Kuribayashi, Sakai, and Shiobara, and our result answers a problem they posed in the affirmative. More generally, we show that a Riemannian metric on a Lie groupoid, namely a 2-metric in the sense of del Hoyo and Fernandes, induces a Riemannian metric on its diffeological orbit space only if the Lie groupoid is regular, and that properness is a sufficient but not necessary condition.

papers.title: Equation-Free Screening of Mittag-Leffler-Compatible Dynamics from Scalar Time Series via kNN Multi-Horizon Profiles
papers.abstract: We study an equation-free screen for finite-window Mittag-Leffler compatibility, in which multihorizon relaxation profiles are constructed out of sample by k-nearest-neighbor prediction from ensembles of scalar trajectories and compared with candidate temporal laws. The screen assesses compatibility, not the generating mechanism. In a matched, noise-free calibration, it reproduces the generating Mittag-Leffler behavior to numerical precision, while relaxation-rate heterogeneity shifts the fitted Mittag-Leffler order toward lower values. For noise-free classical distributed-rate ensembles, a Mittag-Leffler preference over a single exponential disappears when a biexponential alternative is included. Under observational noise, this recovery is incomplete: with three candidate families, the Mittag-Leffler law is still selected in 60% of runs for a classical ensemble, against 72% for a fractional reference. In the tested noise-free settings, simpler profile constructions reproduce the screening decisions, whereas kNN predicts individual trajectories far more accurately than a constant predictor. The screening interpretation of a single-record example, initially investigated as a chaotic test case, is withdrawn as evidence about the continuous system after numerical verification revealed a nonrobust simulated regime. Mittag-Leffler compatibility is therefore a comparative, condition-dependent screening outcome, not identification of fractional origin.

papers.title: Strictly stable solutions in uniformly convex planar domains may have nonconvex superlevel sets
papers.abstract: We construct smooth, uniformly convex planar domains that admit minimal, strictly stable solutions of a semilinear Dirichlet problem whose superlevel sets are nonetheless nonconvex. The class of admissible nonlinearities includes, in particular, two prototypical cases: the Gelfand-type nonlinearity $e^u$ and the family of shifted power-type nonlinearities $(a+u)^p$, where $a>0$ and $p>1$. By applying the elementary scaling properties of the Dirichlet problem, we also show that the same lack of convexity of superlevel sets holds for the corresponding parameter-dependent equations. These results provide a negative answer to a question posed by Brezis, who inquired whether the stability of a solution necessarily entails quasiconcavity for these prototypical stable configurations.

papers.title: Coloring t-perfect graphs with fewer colors
papers.abstract: Recently, Chudnovsky, Cook, Davies, Oum, and Tan obtained the first finite bound on the chromatic number of t-perfect graphs, showing that they are 199053-colorable. We improve this bound to 130 by refining their proof. The original proof establishes that every graph with large odd girth and large chromatic number contains a certain structure called an r-arithmetic rope, and that its existence in a certain leveling of a graph with large odd girth would imply an odd wheel as a t-minor, a known obstruction to t-perfectness. While their technique requires a lower bound on the chromatic number that is exponential in r, we show that the existence of an r-arithmetic rope can already be guaranteed under a linear bound. Using a slightly weakened notion of arithmetic ropes allows us to reduce the bound even further.

papers.title: Spectrum of Complete Kähler Metrics on Bounded Hyperconvex Domains
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ be a bounded domain, and let $ρ:Ω\to[-1,0)$ be a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion function. We consider the logarithmic potential $g=-\log(-ρ)$ and the associated complete Kähler metric $ω=dd^{c} g$. We prove that if $ρ$ satisfies the finite weighted Monge-Ampère mass condition with weight $(-ρ)^{\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, then the spectrum and the essential spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator of $(Ω,ω)$ both coincide with $[n^{2},\infty)$. In particular, the bottom of the spectrum satisfies $λ_{0}(Δ_ω,Ω)=n^{2}$, and $n^{2}$ is not an $L^{2}$-eigenvalue. For each $α> \frac{n}{2}$, we set $f=(-ρ)^α$ and prove that $f$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(Ω,ω)$ if and only if the Monge-Ampère mass of $ρ$ weighted by $(-ρ)^{2α-n}$ is finite. The integral identities underlying this equivalence, applied to the complex powers $(-ρ)^{α+it}$, give, after normalization, a singular Weyl sequence at every $n^{2}+4t^{2}$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$, as $α\downarrow\frac{n}{2}$. Combining our theorem with Cegrell's finite-mass exhaustion theorem, we obtain a complete Kähler metric with spectrum and essential spectrum equal to $[n^{2},\infty)$ on every bounded hyperconvex domain.

papers.title: Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces
papers.abstract: A Minkowski normed space is the Euclidean space equipped with a (possibly asymmetric) uniformly convex and smooth norm, forming a particular class of Finsler manifolds. We construct a stochastic process with one-dimensional time marginal densities given by the fundamental solution to the nonlinear Finsler heat equation in Minkowski normed spaces. This process is constructed as a solution to a singular McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and constitutes a nonlinear Markov process in the sense of McKean. We show that solutions to this stochastic differential equation are pathwise unique, and, thus, probabilistically strong solutions, though the equation has singular coefficients beyond the subcritical regime. Since our construction is a natural extension of the construction of standard Brownian motion from the standard heat kernel, we call this process \emph{Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces.} Furthermore, we obtain a universality property, namely that whichever Minkowski norm is chosen, the radial part of this process is the standard Bessel process. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of stochastic processes associated with nonlinear heat equation in Finslerian spaces.

papers.title: Montel's theorem and tautness in calibrated geometry
papers.abstract: We relate the hyperbolicity of a calibrated manifold $(X, φ)$ to the analytic properties of the space of Smith immersions $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ from the Poincare $k$-ball into $X$. In particular, we establish the following calibrated analogue of a theorem of Royden: if $X$ is $φ$-saturated, then $R_φ$- and $K_φ$-hyperbolicity coincide, and either implies the equicontinuity of $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ with respect to the $φ$-distance. This yields a Montel theorem for compact $φ$-saturated calibrated manifolds as an immediate corollary. Our primary technical tool is a new Schwarz lemma for Smith immersions from $B^k$ into $X$, which is of independent interest. In a similar spirit, we also prove a calibrated analogue of Kiernan's theorem to the effect that the $K_φ$-hyperbolicity of $X$ is almost equivalent to $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ being a normal family. Finally, we prove that bounded domains in flat euclidean space are $R_φ$-hyperbolic for any calibration $φ$, and we investigate the hyperbolicity of products and discrete quotients.

papers.title: Hypocoercivity-preserving space-time Galerkin methods for kinetic Fokker-Planck equations
papers.abstract: We design and analyse a family of hypocoercivity-preserving fully discrete Galerkin methods for the kinetic Fokker--Planck (kFP) equations, a class of evolution partial differential equations (PDE) with \emph{degenerate} diffusion. The key idea in the method design is to mimic the framework of enhanced quadratic forms of Villani \cite{villani} to obtain a coercive bilinear form in a sufficiently strong exponentially weighted norm admitting a spectral gap/Poincaré inequality, despite the degeneracy. The problem is posed as a fourth-order evolution PDE on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^d$. The spatial discretization employs continuous piecewise polynomial approximation spaces on simplicial and/or box-type meshes comprising finite and infinite elements. Nonconformity is treated by constructing appropriate numerical fluxes in the spirit of $C^0$-interior penalty ($C^0$-IP) methods for fourth-order elliptic problems. The proof of coercivity requires new trace inverse inequalities for exponentially weighted norms on $d$-dimensional simplicial and box-type domains, and prismatic domains with infinite length. We prove these inequalities for a variety of exponential weights. Once coercivity is established, exponential convergence to equilibrium follows from an exponentially weighted Poincaré inequality. A fully discrete extension is obtained by coupling the spatial discretization with an $hp$-version discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping scheme. Exponential convergence to equilibrium is also proven for the fully discrete scheme. The proposed methods preserve total mass and exhibit \emph{provably} exponential convergence to equilibrium, a manifestation of `numerical hypocoercivity,' making them well suited for long-time kFP simulations. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results and investigate the convergence behaviour of the proposed method.

papers.title: Equilibria in Motion: Stability, Tracking, and Convergence
papers.abstract: {We study nonautonomous systems whose equilibrium sets are nonisolated and move with time. Their motion is measured on each ball by a localized Attouch--Wets distance, which yields an equilibrium speed that may depend on the radius. The distance from a trajectory to the current equilibrium set is estimated in two ways: through a composite Lyapunov function compared with a power of this distance, and, without any Lyapunov function, through a decay condition on the frozen vector fields. In the first setting, we prove practical stability, and Lyapunov stability when the dissipation has no residual, a case that forces the equilibrium sets to be nested. In the second, we obtain, in the region where the decay condition holds, an explicit tracking estimate driven by the equilibrium speed and the inputs, and we prove asymptotic tracking whenever their averages over unit time intervals vanish, a condition that cannot be weakened among conditions on the speed alone. We also derive input-to-state stability bounds and explicit convergence rates. When the equilibrium speeds are integrable, the equilibrium sets converge in the Attouch--Wets sense to a limiting set at an explicit rate. If, moreover, the velocity is bounded by a multiple of the distance to the current equilibrium set, every trajectory remaining in the region considered has finite length and converges to a point of the limiting set; for a fixed equilibrium set, this yields semistability. The results are illustrated on a scalar example and on resource-allocation models with time-varying demand and with rotating weights.

papers.title: Abelian Orbifolds for Brane Brick Models
papers.abstract: We present a systematic procedure for constructing brane brick models corresponding to abelian orbifolds of toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds, extending the orbifold construction beyond the well-studied case of abelian orbifolds of C^4. Given a parent brane brick model corresponding to a toric Calabi-Yau 4-fold M, we show that the action of an abelian orbifold group Gamma on the generators of M induces an action on the chiral and Fermi fields as well as the J- and E-terms of the associated 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theory. The requirement that the orbifolded brane brick model remains consistent with the closed paths associated with the J- and E-terms, together with the chiral cycles formed by their products, precisely reproduces the Calabi-Yau condition on the orbifold action. This procedure yields an explicit formula for the J- and E-terms of the orbifolded brane brick model in terms of those of the parent theory. We apply our construction to the brane brick models corresponding to Q^{1,1,1} and D_3, and present the resulting families of 2d (0,2) quiver gauge theories. We also present explicit expressions for generating functions that count distinct abelian orbifolds of Q^{1,1,1} and D_3.

papers.title: Discovery of connectivity-trainability trade-off of IQP circuits for Hamiltonian optimization
papers.abstract: Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time (IQP) circuits are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing due to the conjectured classical hardness of their sampling task and their shallow, highly parallelizable structure. Despite extensive studies of their complexity-theoretic properties, the role of circuit connectivity in their trainability as variational ansatze remains poorly understood. In this work, we present an investigation of IQP circuits for Hamiltonian optimization that traces a mechanistic chain linking circuit connectivity, entanglement generation, and gradient scaling: increasing connectivity drives the circuit output toward Haar-like statistics and volume-law entanglement, and this increase in entanglement is consistently associated with an exponential decay of the gradient variance and degraded optimization performance, while sparser architectures retain stable gradients at the cost of global expressibility and entanglement capacity. This connectivity-entanglement-gradient mechanism produces a nontrivial connectivity-trainability trade-off, demonstrating that effective IQP-based Hamiltonian optimization requires a balance between global expressibility and trainability rather than maximal expressivity alone. In particular, on our benchmarks, a circuit generating no entanglement already matches the optimization performance of more highly connected circuits, and a circular topology retains entanglement capacity while preserving trainability, making it a broadly effective choice among the architectures considered.

papers.title: Connecting Quantum Tomography and Quantum Retrodiction
papers.abstract: Quantum tomography and quantum retrodiction are traditionally viewed as separate inference tasks. We show that the two are manifestations of the same underlying principle. We prove that the Petz recovery map of a measurement channel is a gradient of the log-likelihood used in maximum-likelihood tomography, and we derive its extension to arbitrary quantum channels. Consequently, for measurement channels, repeated applications of the Petz map monotonically increase the likelihood, naturally yielding a method for quantum tomography.

papers.title: The Ornstein$-$Uhlenbeck process on $\mathscr P_2$ with a volatility operator
papers.abstract: We analyze diffusion processes ${(μ_t)}_{t\geq 0}$ on the $2$-Wasserstein space $\mathscr P_2$ over $\mathbb R^d$, which can be classified as Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes by means of their Fukushima decomposition. Characteristically for this class, $ | μ_t|_2^2-|μ_0|_2^2-2ct+2\int_0 ^t|μ_s|_2^2\,d s,\, t\geq 0,$ is a martingale, where $c\in(0,\infty)$ is a constant and $|μ_t|_2:=(\int_{\mathbb R^d}x^{\text{T}} xμ_t(d x ))^{1/2}$ denotes the second moment. Making a particular choice from this class, we obtain a process ${(μ_t)}_{t\geq 0}$ such that all moments exist and ${μ_t(θ)}-{μ_0(θ)}-\int_0 ^tμ_s\big(Δθ-\langle \text{id}_{\mathbb R^d},\nabla θ\rangle\big)d s$, $t\geq 0$, is a martingale for each multivariate polynomial $θ:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$.

papers.title: Continuous stochastic flows driven by white noise and their duals
papers.abstract: We study a class of continuous stochastic flows driven by a space-time white noise and characterize their dual flows by explicit stochastic differential equations. A key ingredient of the proof is the convergence of solutions under coefficient approximations. As an application, we derive the dual flows in two illustrative examples, the squared Bessel flow and the Jacobi flow. We also introduce a new model of polynomially self-repelling (PSR) flow and show that it enjoys a self-duality property.

papers.title: Express Language Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.

papers.title: Floating-point autotuning with customized precisions
papers.abstract: Reduced-precision arithmetic offers significant opportunities to improve performance, memory usage, and energy efficiency in numerical applications, provided that numerical accuracy is preserved.
